      "html": "<h1>ADR: AgentCore Runtime Backend</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-10</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Motivation</h2>\n<p>Today, OpenAB dispatches messages exclusively via ACP (Agent Client Protocol) — JSON-RPC over stdio to a co-located subprocess:</p>\n<pre><code>Discord/Slack msg ──► OpenAB ──stdio──► coding CLI (kiro, claude, codex…)\n</code></pre>\n<p>This means:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>One agent per container.</strong> The coding CLI binary must be bundled inside the same pod as OpenAB.</li>\n<li><strong>No parallelism across agents.</strong> Running Claude Code <em>and</em> Kiro simultaneously requires deploying two full OpenAB stacks.</li>\n<li><strong>Pod-bound lifecycle.</strong> If the pod restarts, the agent process (and any in-flight work) dies with it.</li>\n<li><strong>Resource coupling.</strong> The agent shares CPU/memory/disk with OpenAB — a 90-minute refactor starves the broker.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>AWS recently launched <strong>Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime</strong>, which hosts coding agents (Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, etc.) in isolated Firecracker microVMs with persistent filesystems, session management, and streaming invoke APIs. This creates an opportunity: OpenAB can route messages to remote AgentCore sessions, decoupling the agent lifecycle from the broker.</p>\n<h3>What this unlocks</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Dynamic multi-agent routing</strong> — one OpenAB instance routes to N different AgentCore runtimes based on @mention or config.</li>\n<li><strong>True isolation</strong> — each agent runs in its own microVM; no shared localhost, no credential leakage.</li>\n<li><strong>Background execution</strong> — agents survive pod restarts, laptop lid closures, and network drops.</li>\n<li><strong>Cost efficiency</strong> — microVMs spin down when idle (pay per use), no always-on pod per agent.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Integration Approaches</h2>\n<p>Two viable approaches exist. We recommend <strong>Option B</strong>.</p>\n<h3>Option A: OAB native SDK backend</h3>\n<p>Add a new <code>backend = &quot;agentcore&quot;</code> inside OAB that calls <code>InvokeAgentRuntime</code> directly via the AWS SDK.</p>\n<pre><code>Discord → OAB ──AWS SDK──► AgentCore Runtime (microVM)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Option B: <code>agentcore-acp</code> adapter (recommended)</h3>\n<p>Write a standalone ACP-compatible adapter binary that bridges ACP stdio to AgentCore SDK calls. OAB treats it like any other coding CLI — zero OAB changes.</p>\n<pre><code>Discord → OAB ──ACP stdio──► agentcore-acp ──AWS SDK──► AgentCore Runtime (microVM)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Why Option B wins</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Dimension</th>\n<th>A. OAB native SDK</th>\n<th>B. agentcore-acp adapter</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>OAB code changes</td>\n<td>Large — new trait, new backend, AWS SDK dep</td>\n<td><strong>Zero</strong></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Thin bridge philosophy</td>\n<td>Violated — OAB learns AWS specifics</td>\n<td><strong>Preserved</strong> — OAB only speaks ACP</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Onboarding pattern</td>\n<td>New pattern for operators</td>\n<td><strong>Same as kiro/claude/codex</strong></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Independent dev/test</td>\n<td>Coupled to OAB release cycle</td>\n<td><strong>Standalone binary</strong>, own repo/release</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Language flexibility</td>\n<td>Must be Rust (inside OAB)</td>\n<td><strong>Any language</strong> — Python PoC in hours</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-runtime routing</td>\n<td>Requires OAB routing logic</td>\n<td>Multiple OAB instances or adapter-level routing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Deployment</td>\n<td>OAB pod needs IRSA for AgentCore</td>\n<td>Adapter subprocess needs IRSA (same pod, same SA)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Streaming fidelity</td>\n<td>Direct event-stream consumption</td>\n<td>Adapter translates to ACP notifications (tiny overhead)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Option A remains viable for future consideration if we find the ACP translation layer adds unacceptable latency or loses information. But given that every other agent integration (kiro-cli, claude-agent-acp, codex --acp, gemini --acp, opencode acp) follows the adapter pattern, Option B is the natural extension.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Design: <code>agentcore-acp</code></h2>\n<h3>Architecture</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─ agentcore-acp (subprocess, started by OAB) ─────────────────────┐\n│                                                                   │\n│  stdin ◄── ACP JSON-RPC from OAB                                  │\n│  stdout ──► ACP JSON-RPC notifications to OAB                     │\n│                                                                   │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  ACP Server Layer                                           │  │\n│  │  - session/new → create/resume AgentCore session            │  │\n│  │  - session/prompt → InvokeAgentRuntime (streaming)          │  │\n│  │  - cancel → StopRuntimeSession (best-effort)               │  │\n│  └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                         │                                         │\n│  ┌──────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  AgentCore Client                                           │  │\n│  │  - boto3 / aws-sdk-rust / JS SDK                            │  │\n│  │  - invoke_agent_runtime(runtimeArn, sessionId, payload)     │  │\n│  │  - Stream text/event-stream → ACP content notifications     │  │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                                   │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                              │\n                              ▼\n                ┌──────────────────────────┐\n                │  AgentCore Runtime (AWS)  │\n                │  ┌────────────────────┐  │\n                │  │ microVM            │  │\n                │  │ Kiro / Claude /    │  │\n                │  │ Codex / etc.       │  │\n                │  │ /mnt/workspace     │  │\n                │  └────────────────────┘  │\n                └──────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>ACP Protocol Mapping</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>ACP Method (from OAB)</th>\n<th>agentcore-acp Action</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>session/new</code></td>\n<td>Generate <code>runtimeSessionId</code> from thread key, return session_id</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>session/prompt</code></td>\n<td><code>invoke_agent_runtime(payload={&quot;prompt&quot;: text})</code> → stream response → emit ACP <code>notifications/content</code> blocks on stdout</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>session/load</code></td>\n<td>Resume with same <code>runtimeSessionId</code>. If session was idle-terminated (404 <code>ResourceNotFoundException</code>), transparently invoke as new — AgentCore auto-provisions a new microVM and mounts the persisted filesystem. Return success either way.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cancel</code></td>\n<td><strong>Known limitation:</strong> see §Known Limitations. Default: call <code>StopRuntimeSession</code>. Configurable via `--cancel-strategy=noop</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Concurrency Control</h3>\n<p>AgentCore's behavior with concurrent <code>InvokeAgentRuntime</code> calls to the same session is undefined. The adapter <strong>must</strong> serialize invocations per session:</p>\n<pre><code>Thread A prompt arrives → acquire per-session mutex → invoke → release\nThread A prompt 2 arrives (while invoke in-flight) → wait for mutex → invoke\n</code></pre>\n<p>This matches OAB's existing invariant (I2: at most one in-flight ACP turn per thread), so in practice the mutex is a safety net, not a bottleneck.</p>\n<h3>Error Code Mapping</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>AgentCore Error</th>\n<th>ACP Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ThrottlingException</code> (429)</td>\n<td>ACP error response <code>{&quot;code&quot;: -32000, &quot;message&quot;: &quot;rate limited, retry later&quot;}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ResourceNotFoundException</code> (404)</td>\n<td>ACP error <code>{&quot;code&quot;: -32001, &quot;message&quot;: &quot;session not found&quot;}</code> → OAB shows error to user</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ValidationException</code> (400)</td>\n<td>ACP error <code>{&quot;code&quot;: -32602, &quot;message&quot;: &quot;invalid params: ...&quot;}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ServiceQuotaExceededException</code> (402)</td>\n<td>ACP error <code>{&quot;code&quot;: -32000, &quot;message&quot;: &quot;quota exceeded&quot;}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>RuntimeClientError</code> (424)</td>\n<td>ACP error <code>{&quot;code&quot;: -32603, &quot;message&quot;: &quot;agent runtime error: ...&quot;}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Network timeout / connection drop</td>\n<td>Adapter emits ACP error, does NOT crash (OAB sees error, not a dead process)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Streaming Translation</h3>\n<p>AgentCore returns <code>text/event-stream</code> (SSE). The adapter <strong>must</strong> use a proper SSE parser (e.g., <code>httpx-sse</code>, <code>aiohttp</code> SSE support) — not naive <code>iter_lines()</code> — because:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>SSE chunks may split across TCP packets (partial <code>data:</code> lines)</li>\n<li>Multiple events may arrive in a single chunk</li>\n<li>Keep-alive comments (<code>:</code>) must be filtered</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Parsed SSE events are translated to ACP JSON-RPC notifications:</p>\n<pre><code>SSE:  data: I'll analyze the code...\nACP:  {&quot;jsonrpc&quot;:&quot;2.0&quot;,&quot;method&quot;:&quot;notifications/content&quot;,&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;type&quot;:&quot;text&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;I'll analyze the code...&quot;}}\n\nSSE:  data: The issue is in line 42...\nACP:  {&quot;jsonrpc&quot;:&quot;2.0&quot;,&quot;method&quot;:&quot;notifications/content&quot;,&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;type&quot;:&quot;text&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;The issue is in line 42...&quot;}}\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is the same format OAB already consumes from kiro-cli, claude-agent-acp, etc. — zero changes needed in OAB's streaming/edit logic.</p>\n<h3>Session ID Mapping</h3>\n<p>AgentCore requires <code>runtimeSessionId</code> ≥ 33 characters. The adapter builds this deterministically from the <strong>sender context embedded in each prompt</strong>.</p>\n<p><strong>How the adapter gets the thread ID (no OAB changes needed):</strong></p>\n<p>OAB wraps every prompt with a <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> block containing the full routing metadata:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">&lt;sender_context&gt;\n{&quot;schema&quot;:&quot;openab.sender.v1&quot;,&quot;channel_id&quot;:&quot;1490282656913559673&quot;,&quot;thread_id&quot;:&quot;1514294613853208667&quot;,...}\n&lt;/sender_context&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<p>The adapter parses this on the first <code>session/prompt</code> to extract <code>thread_id</code> (or <code>channel_id</code> if no thread). This is the same sender context that all ACP agents already receive — no protocol changes needed.</p>\n<p><strong>Mapping examples (guaranteed ≥33 chars):</strong></p>\n<pre><code>Discord thread 1514294613853208667\n  → runtimeSessionId = &quot;oab-discord-thread-1514294613853208667&quot;  (38 chars ✓)\n\nSlack thread C0123456789.1234567890.123456\n  → runtimeSessionId = &quot;oab-slack-thread-C0123456789-1234567890-123456&quot;  (47 chars ✓)\n\nShort/missing thread ID (edge case): channel_id only &quot;1490282656913559673&quot;\n  → runtimeSessionId = &quot;oab-discord-channel-1490282656913559673&quot;  (39 chars ✓)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Length guarantee:</strong> If the constructed ID is &lt; 33 chars, the adapter pads with zero suffix. Alternatively, use a UUID v5 namespace hash of the thread key (always 36 chars).</p>\n<p><strong>Fallback:</strong> If <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> is absent (e.g., non-OAB usage), the adapter falls back to a per-process monotonic session ID. This loses cross-restart resume but still functions.</p>\n<p>Deterministic mapping means:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>No persistent state file needed in the adapter</li>\n<li>Resume works automatically after adapter restart</li>\n<li>Multiple adapter instances can share the same AgentCore sessions</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Configuration</h2>\n<p>From the OAB operator's perspective, <code>agentcore-acp</code> is just another agent command:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;agentcore-acp&quot;\nargs = [&quot;--runtime-arn&quot;, &quot;arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:123456789012:runtime/kiro-agent&quot;, &quot;--region&quot;, &quot;us-west-2&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n# IAM credentials come from pod's service account (IRSA) — no env vars needed\n</code></pre>\n<p>For multi-agent setups, deploy multiple OAB instances each pointing to a different runtime:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Instance 1: Kiro\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;agentcore-acp&quot;\nargs = [&quot;--runtime-arn&quot;, &quot;arn:aws:...:runtime/kiro-agent&quot;]\n\n# Instance 2: Claude Code\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;agentcore-acp&quot;\nargs = [&quot;--runtime-arn&quot;, &quot;arn:aws:...:runtime/claude-agent&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Or, if the adapter supports it, a single adapter could route based on hints in the prompt/sender context (future enhancement).</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. AgentCore Runtime Characteristics</h2>\n<p>Key properties that the adapter must handle:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Property</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n<th>Implication</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Session idle timeout</td>\n<td>15 min (configurable, up to 8hr)</td>\n<td>Each invoke resets the timer; long gaps = cold start</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Max session lifetime</td>\n<td>8 hours</td>\n<td>Long-running work needs session rotation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cold start</td>\n<td>~5-15s (microVM boot)</td>\n<td>First invoke per session has visible latency</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Filesystem persistence</td>\n<td>14 days after last use</td>\n<td>Agent state survives across session restarts</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Streaming response</td>\n<td><code>text/event-stream</code> over HTTP/2</td>\n<td>Real-time token delivery, translatable to ACP</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Parallelism</td>\n<td>Independent microVM per session</td>\n<td>No resource contention between sessions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cost model</td>\n<td>CPU-seconds + peak memory</td>\n<td>Idle sessions cost nothing after termination</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Comparison with local ACP</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Concern</th>\n<th>ACP (local subprocess)</th>\n<th>agentcore-acp (remote)</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent location</td>\n<td>Same container</td>\n<td>Remote microVM</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Startup</td>\n<td>Already running</td>\n<td>Cold start on first invoke (~5-15s)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Session state</td>\n<td>In-memory (process)</td>\n<td>Persistent filesystem (/mnt/workspace)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Credential isolation</td>\n<td>Shared pod env</td>\n<td>Fully isolated (IAM + AgentCore Gateway)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Tool permission prompt</td>\n<td>Supported (mid-turn)</td>\n<td>Not supported — agents run autonomously</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Max session duration</td>\n<td>Unlimited (until pod dies)</td>\n<td>8 hours (configurable)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Resume after restart</td>\n<td>Lost (unless session/save)</td>\n<td>Automatic (filesystem persists)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Parallelism</td>\n<td>Shared CPU per pod</td>\n<td>One microVM per session</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Implementation Plan</h2>\n<h3>Phase 1: Python PoC</h3>\n<p>Minimal <code>agentcore-acp</code> in Python (fastest path to validation):</p>\n<ol>\n<li>ACP stdio server (read JSON-RPC from stdin, write to stdout)</li>\n<li><code>session/new</code> → generate runtimeSessionId</li>\n<li><code>session/prompt</code> → <code>boto3.client('bedrock-agentcore').invoke_agent_runtime()</code> with streaming</li>\n<li>Parse <code>response[&quot;response&quot;].iter_lines()</code> → emit ACP content notifications</li>\n<li>Package as a single script or small pip package</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Deliverable:</strong> Working end-to-end demo: Discord message → OAB → agentcore-acp → AgentCore → streaming reply in Discord.</p>\n<h3>Phase 2: Production hardening</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Proper error handling (throttling, session terminated, cold start detection)</li>\n<li>Cold start UX: emit a &quot;⏳ Starting agent environment...&quot; notification before streaming begins</li>\n<li>Session resume logic (detect if session was idle-terminated, re-invoke transparently)</li>\n<li>Config file support (runtime ARN, region, payload template, timeout)</li>\n<li>Logging and observability (structured logs, latency metrics)</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Phase 3: Advanced features</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Multi-runtime routing within a single adapter instance</li>\n<li><code>InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand</code> support for deterministic operations (exposed as an ACP tool?)</li>\n<li>Rust rewrite for performance/single-binary distribution (if Python overhead is measurable)</li>\n<li>Integration with AgentCore Gateway MCP for tool access</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Known Limitations</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Cancel is safe for filesystem, destructive for in-memory state.</strong> AgentCore has no mid-invoke cancel API. When OAB sends <code>cancel</code>, the adapter can call <code>StopRuntimeSession</code> which terminates the microVM. <strong>Filesystem (<code>/mnt/workspace</code>) persists for 14 days</strong> — files, git history, installed packages are all safe. What is lost: in-memory agent state (conversation context, running processes, partial computations). The next invoke on the same session ID mounts the same filesystem on a fresh microVM. This makes cancel = stop session a reasonable default for most coding workflows.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Cold start latency (~5-15s).</strong> First invoke per session requires microVM boot. The adapter handles this proactively: if no SSE event arrives within 3 seconds of invoking, the adapter emits an early ACP notification:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{&quot;jsonrpc&quot;:&quot;2.0&quot;,&quot;method&quot;:&quot;notifications/content&quot;,&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;type&quot;:&quot;text&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;⏳ Starting agent environment...&quot;}}\n</code></pre>\n<p>OAB displays this immediately, so the user knows the system is working. Once streaming begins, normal content flow takes over. This is defined behavior, not dependent on OAB's stall detection.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>8-hour max lifetime.</strong> Sessions cannot exceed <code>maxLifetime</code> (default 8hr). Long-running work needs the adapter to transparently rotate to a new session and re-mount the same filesystem.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Open Questions</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Payload format</strong> — Different AgentCore runtimes may expect different payload schemas (<code>{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;...&quot;}</code> vs raw text vs MCP). Do we need a <code>--payload-template</code> flag?</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Session context passthrough</strong> — Should the adapter forward OAB's sender context (user name, channel, etc.) in the payload so the remote agent knows who's asking?</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Human-in-the-loop</strong> — ACP supports mid-turn tool permission prompts. AgentCore agents run autonomously. Is this acceptable, or do we need a callback mechanism via the adapter?</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Multi-agent routing</strong> — Single adapter routing to multiple runtimes, or multiple adapter instances? Former is more convenient, latter is simpler.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Language choice for production</strong> — Python (fast to write, boto3 native), Rust (single binary, matches OAB ecosystem), or Node.js (middle ground)?</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Alternatives Considered</h2>\n<h3>A. OAB native SDK backend (not recommended for now)</h3>\n<p>Add <code>backend = &quot;agentcore&quot;</code> directly inside OAB with AWS SDK calls. This works but:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Violates the &quot;thin bridge&quot; philosophy — OAB shouldn't understand AWS specifics</li>\n<li>Adds <code>aws-sdk-bedrockagentcore</code> as a compile-time dependency to OAB</li>\n<li>Different release cycle (AgentCore API changes shouldn't require OAB rebuild)</li>\n<li>Breaks the consistent &quot;all agents are ACP subprocesses&quot; mental model</li>\n</ul>\n<p>May revisit if the ACP translation layer proves to be a bottleneck.</p>\n<h3>B. Deploy OAB itself on AgentCore</h3>\n<p>Run the entire OpenAB + agent container on AgentCore Runtime. This works but:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Still couples agent to container</li>\n<li>Doesn't leverage AgentCore's multi-session isolation</li>\n<li>Doesn't enable dynamic routing from one OAB instance</li>\n<li>Loses the thin bridge role</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>C. WebSocket relay to AgentCore</h3>\n<p>Persistent WebSocket between OAB and a custom proxy. Rejected:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Adds another service to deploy</li>\n<li><code>InvokeAgentRuntime</code> already streams; no intermediary needed</li>\n<li>More moving parts, same result</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>D. MCP-based integration via AgentCore Gateway</h3>\n<p>Use Gateway's MCP endpoint as a tool layer for local agents. Complementary (could add for tools) but doesn't solve the agent lifecycle coupling problem.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/its-safe-to-close-your-laptop-now-hosting-coding-agents-on-amazon-bedrock-agentcore/\">AWS Blog: Hosting Coding Agents on AgentCore</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/APIReference/API_InvokeAgentRuntime.html\">InvokeAgentRuntime API Reference</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/APIReference/API_InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand.html\">InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand API Reference</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-lifecycle-settings.html\">AgentCore Runtime Lifecycle Settings</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/bedrock-agentcore-runtime-session-storage/\">AgentCore Session Storage (Preview)</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-long-run.html\">Handle Long-Running Agents</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/linyiru/openab/blob/6ad4ef419dd131e3f718dfd9b224f3967387da94/DESIGN.md\">OpenAB DESIGN.md</a> — &quot;Thin Bridge&quot; philosophy</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/openab-agent\">ADR: openab-agent</a> — Native agent pattern (similar standalone approach)</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: AgentCore Runtime Backend"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/ambient",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Ambient Mode</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-26</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> chaodu-agent</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Context</h2>\n<p>Today, OpenAB only dispatches messages to an agent when the agent is explicitly\nmentioned (or the message is in a thread the agent participates in). This means\nagents are deaf to surrounding conversation unless invoked — they cannot\nproactively contribute context, answer questions addressed to no one in\nparticular, or notice when a discussion touches their area of expertise.</p>\n<p>We want agents to behave more like attentive team members who listen to the room\nand speak up when they have something valuable to add, without requiring an\nexplicit <code>@mention</code> every time.</p>\n<h2>Prior Art</h2>\n<h3>OpenClaw — <code>/activation always</code></h3>\n<p>OpenClaw supports an <code>always</code> activation mode as a cross-platform group chat\nfeature (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, iMessage — configured via\n<code>agents.list[].groupChat.mentionPatterns</code> and <code>channels.*.groups</code>):</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Every message is dispatched to the agent (no mention required).</li>\n<li>Agent returns the sentinel token <code>NO_REPLY</code> when it has nothing to add;\nthe gateway discards silently.</li>\n<li>Pending messages (up to 50) are accumulated as context and injected as\n<code>[Chat messages since your last reply - for context]</code>.</li>\n<li>Per-group toggle via <code>/activation always</code> or <code>/activation mention</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Limitation:</strong> messages are dispatched one-by-one — each message triggers a\nseparate LLM invocation, even if it results in <code>NO_REPLY</code>. No batching.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Hermes Agent — <code>free_response_channels</code></h3>\n<p>Hermes provides <code>DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS</code> and\n<code>DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION=false</code>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>The bot responds to <strong>every</strong> message in designated channels without mention.</li>\n<li>Free-response channels skip auto-threading (replies inline) and isolate\nsessions per user (<code>group_sessions_per_user: true</code> by default).</li>\n<li>History backfill (<code>DISCORD_HISTORY_BACKFILL</code>) recovers missed channel context\non <code>@mention</code> — only triggered when <code>require_mention: true</code> and skipped in\nfree-response channels and DMs where the transcript is already complete.\nScans up to 50 messages backwards, stopping at the bot's own last message.</li>\n<li><strong>Limitation:</strong> no autonomous decision-making — the bot always replies. There\nis no <code>NO_REPLY</code> equivalent; it's either &quot;respond to everything&quot; or\n&quot;respond only on mention.&quot;</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Research — &quot;Controlling AI Agent Participation in Group Conversations&quot;</h3>\n<p>(arXiv 2501.17258, Jan 2025) — studies user preferences for AI agent behavior\nin group settings. Key finding: users benefited from having the AI in the group,\nbut disliked when the agent dominated the conversation and desired controls\nover its interactive behaviors.</p>\n<h3>Gap Our Design Fills</h3>\n<p>Neither OpenClaw nor Hermes implements <strong>batch flush</strong> — they dispatch per\nmessage. Our design accumulates messages and flushes them as a batch, which:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Reduces LLM invocations (one call per batch instead of N).</li>\n<li>Gives the agent fuller conversational context for better judgment.</li>\n<li>Provides natural rate-limiting without additional cooldown mechanisms.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Decision</h2>\n<p>Introduce an <strong>Ambient Mode</strong> using a <strong>batch flush</strong> strategy.</p>\n<h3>Architecture Overview</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                          Discord Gateway (events)                            │\n└───────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                    │ MESSAGE_CREATE\n                                    ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Handler::message()                                                         │\n│                                                                             │\n│  ┌─────────────┐    YES    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐     │\n│  │ Own bot msg?├──────────►│ DROP (echo prevention)                   │     │\n│  └──────┬──────┘           └──────────────────────────────────────────┘     │\n│         │ NO                                                                │\n│         ▼                                                                   │\n│  ┌─────────────┐    YES    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐     │\n│  │ @mention?   ├──────────►│ Normal Mention Dispatch Path             │     │\n│  │             │           │ • Discard ambient buffer for this channel│     │\n│  └──────┬──────┘           │ • Cancel in-flight ambient flush         │     │\n│         │ NO               │ • Thread + reactions + full session       │     │\n│         ▼                  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘     │\n│  ┌──────────────────┐ NO   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐    │\n│  │ Ambient channel?  ├────►│ IGNORE (not ambient-enabled)             │    │\n│  └──────┬────────────┘     └──────────────────────────────────────────┘    │\n│         │ YES                                                               │\n│         ▼                                                                   │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │\n│  │              Ambient Dispatcher::submit(msg)                      │      │\n│  └──────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘      │\n└─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                  │ mpsc::channel (bounded)\n                                  ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Ambient Consumer Loop (per-channel)                                        │\n│                                                                             │\n│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ Buffer Phase                                                          │  │\n│  │                                                                       │  │\n│  │   msg ──► [  buffer  ] ◄── accumulate until trigger                   │  │\n│  │                                                                       │  │\n│  │   Flush triggers (whichever first):                                   │  │\n│  │     • Timer expired (flush_interval ± 20% jitter)                     │  │\n│  │     • Count reached (flush_max_messages = 10)                         │  │\n│  │     • Hard cap hit  (flush_hard_cap = 50)                             │  │\n│  └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                  │ swap-and-drain                            │\n│                                  ▼                                           │\n│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ Flush Phase                                                           │  │\n│  │                                                                       │  │\n│  │   1. Acquire global semaphore (max_concurrent_flushes = 3)            │  │\n│  │   2. Set channel_flushing = true                                      │  │\n│  │   3. Fetch context_window (20 msgs) from Discord API                  │  │\n│  │   4. Build payload:                                                   │  │\n│  │      ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐         │  │\n│  │      │ System: &quot;You are in ambient mode...&quot;                 │         │  │\n│  │      │ [Ambient context — channel history]                  │         │  │\n│  │      │ [Ambient batch — N new messages]                     │         │  │\n│  │      │ [End of batch — reply [NO_REPLY] if nothing to add]  │         │  │\n│  │      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘         │  │\n│  │   5. Send to LLM (ambient session pool)                               │  │\n│  │   6. Set channel_flushing = false                                     │  │\n│  │   7. Release semaphore                                                │  │\n│  └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n└──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                   │\n                                   ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Response Router                                                            │\n│                                                                             │\n│   LLM Response ──► trim + lowercase                                         │\n│                        │                                                    │\n│              ┌─────────┴─────────┐                                          │\n│              ▼                   ▼                                           │\n│   &quot;[no_reply]&quot;              Actual content                                  │\n│        │                         │                                          │\n│        ▼                         ▼                                          │\n│   🗑️ Discard silently      📤 Post to channel                              │\n│   (no reactions,           (no 👀🤔🔥 reactions,                            │\n│    no threading)            direct message post)                            │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Dual-Path Concurrency (Mention vs Ambient)</h3>\n<pre><code>Channel #general (ambient-enabled)\n━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\n\nTimeline:\n  t=0s   UserA: &quot;how do I deploy?&quot;        ──► ambient buffer\n  t=3s   UserB: &quot;check the wiki&quot;          ──► ambient buffer\n  t=8s   UserA: &quot;wiki is outdated&quot;        ──► ambient buffer\n  t=15s  UserC: &quot;@bot help me deploy&quot;     ──► MENTION PATH\n                                               │\n         ┌─────────────────────────────────────┘\n         ▼\n  ┌────────────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────────┐\n  │ Mention Dispatch               │    │ Ambient Buffer             │\n  │                                │    │                            │\n  │ Session: discord:&lt;thread_id&gt;   │    │ [msg1, msg2, msg3]         │\n  │ Pool: Main                     │    │         │                  │\n  │ Reactions: 👀🤔🔥🆗            │    │         ▼                  │\n  │ Response: in new thread        │    │   DISCARDED (not flushed)  │\n  └────────────────────────────────┘    └────────────────────────────┘\n\n  t=16s  (new buffer cycle starts fresh)\n  t=20s  UserD: &quot;anyone tried helm 3.15?&quot;  ──► new ambient buffer\n  ...\n  t=76s  flush_interval elapsed            ──► flush new buffer\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Mechanism</h3>\n<pre><code>Discord Channel\n────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  msg1 (t=0s)  │\n  msg2 (t=3s)  │  accumulate in buffer\n  msg3 (t=8s)  │\n  msg4 (t=12s) │\n               ▼\n         ┌─────────────────────────────┐\n         │ Flush trigger fired         │\n         │ (60s elapsed OR 10 msgs)    │\n         └─────────────┬───────────────┘\n                       │\n                       ▼\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  OpenAB Gateway                                                  │\n│                                                                  │\n│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ Ambient Dispatch (batch)                                   │  │\n│  │                                                            │  │\n│  │ • Drain messages from mpsc channel into batch              │  │\n│  │   (new messages queue for next flush cycle)                │  │\n│  │ • Prepend: channel history (context_window via API)        │  │\n│  │ • Prepend system instruction:                              │  │\n│  │   &quot;You are in ambient mode. Below is a batch of recent     │  │\n│  │    messages. If you have nothing valuable to add, reply    │  │\n│  │    exactly: [NO_REPLY]&quot;                                    │  │\n│  │ • Send batch to agent                                      │  │\n│  └────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                               │                                  │\n│                               ▼                                  │\n│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ Response Router                                            │  │\n│  │                                                            │  │\n│  │ • Agent replies &quot;[NO_REPLY]&quot; → discard silently            │  │\n│  │ • Agent replies with content  → post to Discord            │  │\n│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Buffer Lifecycle</h3>\n<p>Conceptually, the ambient buffer operates as a <strong>swap-and-drain</strong> model —\ningestion is decoupled from flush processing so neither blocks the other.</p>\n<p>In practice, this is implemented via the existing <code>Dispatcher</code> infrastructure\nusing a bounded <code>mpsc::channel</code> per ambient channel (see Implementation Notes).\nThe mpsc channel provides the same decoupling guarantees: <code>submit()</code> pushes\nmessages into the channel (non-blocking for senders), and the ambient consumer\nloop drains messages via <code>rx.recv()</code> with a deadline. The &quot;swap&quot; happens\nimplicitly — once the consumer drains and moves into flush processing, new\nmessages queue in the channel buffer for the next cycle.</p>\n<p>The key invariant: flush processing never blocks message ingestion.</p>\n<h3>Flush Triggers</h3>\n<p>Messages are accumulated in a per-channel buffer and flushed when <strong>any</strong>\ncondition is met (whichever comes first):</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Trigger</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Time</td>\n<td><code>flush_interval_seconds = 60</code></td>\n<td>Seconds since first buffered message</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Count</td>\n<td><code>flush_max_messages = 10</code></td>\n<td>Max messages to accumulate before flush</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Hard cap</td>\n<td><code>flush_hard_cap = 50</code></td>\n<td>Safety cap — force flush if <code>flush_max_messages</code> is set high or disabled</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Relationship between <code>flush_max_messages</code> and <code>flush_hard_cap</code>:</strong>\n<code>flush_max_messages</code> is the operational trigger (default 10). <code>flush_hard_cap</code>\nis a safety net for deployments where operators set <code>flush_max_messages</code> to a\nvery large value (or 0 to disable count-based flushing) to rely solely on\ntimer-based flushes. In that scenario, <code>flush_hard_cap</code> prevents unbounded\nbuffer growth during message spikes. With default values (10 and 50), the hard\ncap is effectively dormant — this is intentional.\n| Mention | immediate | @mention discards buffer, triggers normal mention dispatch (not a flush) |</p>\n<p><strong>Flush interval jitter:</strong> to prevent thundering herd when many channels flush\nsimultaneously, the actual interval is <code>flush_interval_seconds ± 20%</code> (random\nper-channel, recomputed each cycle).</p>\n<p><strong>@mention handling:</strong> when a <code>@mention</code> is detected at the Handler level\n(before the buffer), the system:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Discards the ambient buffer for that channel (messages are lost — not flushed).</li>\n<li>If an ambient flush is already in-flight, sets a <code>cancelled</code> flag to suppress\nthe ambient response before posting (see Concurrent reply prevention below).</li>\n<li>Dispatches the @mention via the normal mention-triggered path (with full\nreactions, threading, etc.).</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Rationale: the bot is about to reply directly via mention — flushing the ambient\nbuffer simultaneously would produce a redundant double-reply. The discarded\nmessages provided conversational context that the mention dispatch can retrieve\nvia <code>context_window</code> (Discord API history fetch) if needed.</p>\n<p><strong>Concurrent reply prevention:</strong> to prevent double-replying to the same channel:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>The ambient consumer holds a per-channel <code>AtomicBool</code> flag (<code>flushing</code>) with\na <strong>safety timeout</strong> (<code>flush_timeout_seconds = 120</code>). If the flag remains set\nbeyond the timeout (e.g., consumer panicked/OOM), it is automatically reset\nand the condition is logged as an error.</li>\n<li>When a @mention arrives on an ambient channel (detected at Handler level,\nbefore the buffer), the system:\n<ol>\n<li>If ambient consumer is idle (not flushing): discard buffer, dispatch\nmention normally.</li>\n<li>If ambient consumer is mid-flush: set a <code>cancelled</code> flag <strong>and</strong> suppress\nthe ambient response atomically using a <code>post_guard</code> — the guard is\nacquired before the <code>[NO_REPLY]</code> check and held through <code>post_response()</code>.\nThe mention dispatch path invalidates the guard, ensuring no ambient\nmessage is posted after cancellation.</li>\n</ol>\n</li>\n<li>Conversely, if a mention dispatch is already in-flight, the ambient consumer\nskips posting its response — the user already got a direct reply.</li>\n<li>This ensures at most one bot response is posted to a channel at any given\nmoment from the ambient + mention paths combined.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Message Filtering for Buffer</h3>\n<p>Not all messages enter the ambient buffer:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>✅ <strong>User messages</strong> in ambient-enabled channels (without @mention) → buffer</li>\n<li>✅ <strong>Bot messages from other bots</strong> (if <code>allow_bot_messages</code> permits) → buffer</li>\n<li>❌ <strong>Own bot messages</strong> → never buffered (prevents echo loops)</li>\n<li>❌ <strong>Messages that @mention the bot</strong> → bypass buffer, discard existing\nbuffer contents + normal mention dispatch</li>\n<li>❌ <strong>Messages in threads created by the bot</strong> → handled by existing\nthread-based session logic, not ambient</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Batch Payload</h3>\n<p>The flushed batch is formatted as a conversation block:</p>\n<pre><code>[Ambient context — recent channel history]\n[12:00:01] UserC: I pushed the helm fix yesterday\n[12:00:02] UserB: cool\n\n[Ambient batch — 4 new messages since last flush]\n[12:03:01] UserA: Anyone know how to fix the helm release?\n[12:03:04] UserB: Which chart version?\n[12:03:11] UserA: 0.8.5\n[12:03:15] UserC: Try rolling back first\n\n[End of batch — reply only if you can add meaningful value.\n Otherwise reply exactly: [NO_REPLY]]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Session Strategy</h3>\n<p>Ambient dispatches use a <strong>dedicated session pool</strong>, separate from the main\nmention-triggered pool:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Mention dispatch</th>\n<th>Ambient dispatch</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Session key</td>\n<td><code>discord:&lt;thread_id&gt;</code></td>\n<td><code>ambient:discord:&lt;channel_id&gt;</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Pool</td>\n<td>Main pool (<code>[pool]</code>)</td>\n<td>Ambient pool (<code>[pool.ambient]</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Lifetime</td>\n<td>Long-lived (session_ttl_hours)</td>\n<td>Short-lived (ambient_session_ttl_minutes)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cross-flush memory</td>\n<td>Full transcript</td>\n<td>Rolling window (last N flushes)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Reactions</td>\n<td>✅ Full (👀🤔🔥🆗)</td>\n<td>❌ Suppressed</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Why separate pools:</strong> prevents ambient traffic from exhausting the main pool\nand blocking normal @mention responses. The ambient pool has its own\n<code>max_sessions</code> cap.</p>\n<p><strong>Cross-flush context:</strong> the ambient session retains a rolling window of the\nlast <code>ambient_context_flushes</code> (default: 3) flush interactions, so the agent\nhas memory of what it said/declined recently. Sessions expire after\n<code>ambient_session_ttl_minutes</code> (default: 60) of inactivity.</p>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<p>All ambient settings are grouped under a top-level <code>[ambient]</code> section:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[ambient]\nenabled = false                       # master switch\nflush_interval_seconds = 60           # time-based flush trigger (±20% jitter applied)\nflush_max_messages = 10               # count-based flush trigger\nflush_hard_cap = 50                   # safety cap — force flush at this count\ncontext_window = 20                   # historical messages fetched via Discord API before batch\nmax_concurrent_flushes = 3            # max simultaneous LLM calls across all ambient channels\nflush_timeout_seconds = 120           # safety timeout — auto-reset flushing flag if exceeded\n\n[ambient.pool]\nmax_sessions = 5                      # separate pool for ambient dispatches\nsession_ttl_minutes = 60              # ambient session inactivity timeout\ncontext_flushes = 3                   # rolling window of retained flush history\n\n[ambient.discord]\nchannels = [&quot;1490282656913559673&quot;]    # required — explicit allowlist, empty = disabled\nallow_bot_messages = false            # whether other bots' messages enter ambient buffer\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Design rationale:</strong> flush parameters (<code>flush_interval_seconds</code>, <code>flush_max_messages</code>,\netc.) are platform-agnostic and live at the <code>[ambient]</code> level. Platform-specific\nsettings (channel allowlists) live under <code>[ambient.&lt;platform&gt;]</code>. This allows\nfuture multi-platform support (<code>[ambient.slack]</code>, <code>[ambient.telegram]</code>) without\nrestructuring.</p>\n<p><strong><code>channels</code> semantics:</strong> an explicit allowlist is <strong>required</strong>. If <code>channels</code>\nis empty or omitted while <code>enabled = true</code>, ambient mode is <strong>not activated</strong>\nfor any channel (fail-safe). This prevents accidental global ambient activation.</p>\n<p><strong><code>context_window</code>:</strong> fetches the N most recent messages from the Discord\nchannel history API (before the batch window) to provide additional context.\nThis is a Discord API call with standard rate limiting. If fewer than N messages\nexist, all available messages are included. These messages are <strong>not</strong> counted\ntoward <code>flush_max_messages</code>.</p>\n<h3>Error Handling</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>LLM timeout / network error</td>\n<td>Batch is <strong>discarded</strong> (not retried). Next flush cycle starts fresh. Logged as warning.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent returns tool calls</td>\n<td>Treated as normal response — if final output is not <code>[NO_REPLY]</code>, post it. Tool calls execute normally within the ambient session.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent returns empty response</td>\n<td>Treated as <code>[NO_REPLY]</code> (discard silently).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Buffer grows beyond <code>flush_hard_cap</code></td>\n<td>Force flush immediately, regardless of timer state.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Discord API rate limit on <code>context_window</code> fetch</td>\n<td>Skip context window, flush batch without historical context. Log warning.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Sentinel Value</h3>\n<p>The sentinel is <code>[NO_REPLY]</code> (case-insensitive, trimmed). Chosen because:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Unlikely to appear in natural agent output.</li>\n<li>Simple to detect with a string match (no regex needed).</li>\n<li>Easy for any LLM to produce reliably.</li>\n<li>Consistent with OpenClaw's established <code>NO_REPLY</code> convention.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Consequences</h2>\n<h3>Benefits</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Token efficient</strong> — one LLM call per batch instead of per message. A\nchannel with 10 messages in 60 seconds costs 1 invocation, not 10.</li>\n<li><strong>Better judgment</strong> — agent sees a complete conversational thread, making\nit far more likely to know when a question was already answered (→ NO_REPLY)\nvs. when it should contribute.</li>\n<li><strong>Natural rate limiting</strong> — the flush interval + jitter acts as inherent\nrate-limiting. Combined with <code>max_concurrent_flushes</code>, prevents cost spikes.</li>\n<li><strong>Agents behave like real team members</strong> — aware of context, able to\ncontribute organically.</li>\n<li><strong>User-configurable</strong> — operators decide the cost/intelligence trade-off.</li>\n<li><strong>Fail-safe defaults</strong> — disabled by default, requires explicit channel list,\nseparate session pool prevents impact on normal operations.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Trade-offs</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Latency</strong> — ambient replies are delayed by up to <code>flush_interval_seconds</code>.\nAcceptable because ambient replies are unsolicited; explicitly mentioned\nmessages bypass the buffer entirely via the normal dispatch path.</li>\n<li><strong>Token cost still increases</strong> — even with batching, each flush is an LLM\ncall. Mitigations: per-channel opt-in, tunable flush interval/count,\n<code>max_concurrent_flushes</code> cap.</li>\n<li><strong>Potential for noise</strong> — a poorly-tuned prompt or model may reply too\neagerly. The batch format and explicit instructions mitigate this.</li>\n<li><strong>No retry on failure</strong> — ambient batches are fire-and-forget. If a flush\nfails, those messages are lost context. Acceptable because ambient is\nbest-effort by nature.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Alternatives Considered</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Per-message dispatch (OpenClaw-style)</strong> — dispatch every message\nindividually. Rejected because it burns N invocations for N messages,\nmost of which return NO_REPLY. Batch flush achieves the same goal with\n~1/N the cost.</li>\n<li><strong>Keyword pre-filter</strong> — only dispatch if the message matches certain\nkeywords. Rejected as primary mechanism because it defeats the purpose of\nintelligent, context-aware participation. May be added later as a cost\noptimization layer.</li>\n<li><strong>Separate lightweight classifier</strong> — use a small/cheap model to decide\nwhether to invoke the main agent. Viable as a future enhancement but adds\ncomplexity for v1.</li>\n<li><strong>Periodic summary mode</strong> — batch N messages and summarize them before\nsending to agent. Rejected because the agent should see raw messages for\nfull context; summarization loses nuance.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Implementation Notes</h2>\n<h3>Reuse of Existing <code>Dispatcher</code> Infrastructure</h3>\n<p>OpenAB already has a <strong>turn-boundary batching</strong> system (PR #686,\n<code>message_processing_mode</code> config) with <code>Dispatcher</code>, per-thread <code>mpsc::channel</code>,\nand <code>consumer_loop</code>. Ambient Mode should extend this infrastructure rather than\nbuilding a parallel buffer system.</p>\n<p><strong>What we reuse:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>Dispatcher::submit()</code> — message ingestion into bounded mpsc channel</li>\n<li><code>BufferedMessage</code> struct — carries prompt, sender_context, attachments</li>\n<li><code>consumer_loop</code> — long-lived task that drains and dispatches</li>\n<li><code>dispatch_batch</code> → <code>pack_arrival_event</code> — packing N messages into\n<code>Vec&lt;ContentBlock&gt;</code> with repeated <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> delimiters</li>\n<li><code>ThreadHandle</code> lifecycle — idle eviction, SendError retry</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>What differs for ambient mode:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Turn-boundary (existing)</th>\n<th>Ambient consumer</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Drain trigger</td>\n<td>Turn completion (greedy drain when agent finishes)</td>\n<td>Timer (<code>flush_interval ± jitter</code>) OR count (<code>flush_max_messages</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Key</td>\n<td><code>(platform, thread_id)</code></td>\n<td><code>ambient:(platform, channel_id)</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Prerequisite</td>\n<td>Message already passed mention/involved gate</td>\n<td>Message has NO mention (new gate path)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Response handling</td>\n<td>Normal post</td>\n<td><code>[NO_REPLY]</code> check before posting</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Reactions</td>\n<td>Full (👀🤔🔥🆗)</td>\n<td>Suppressed</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Session pool</td>\n<td>Main pool</td>\n<td>Ambient pool (separate <code>max_sessions</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Not a new <code>message_processing_mode</code>:</strong> ambient mode is a <strong>parallel dispatch\npath</strong>, not a replacement for the primary processing mode. The existing\n<code>message_processing_mode</code> enum (<code>per-message</code>, <code>per-thread</code>, <code>per-lane</code>) is\nunchanged. Ambient mode is configured separately via <code>[ambient]</code> and runs as\na separate Dispatcher instance alongside the primary one.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Existing modes (unchanged) — applies to mention-triggered messages:\nmessage_processing_mode = &quot;per-message&quot;   # 1 msg → 1 turn\nmessage_processing_mode = &quot;per-thread&quot;    # batch at turn boundary\nmessage_processing_mode = &quot;per-lane&quot;      # batch at turn boundary, per-sender\n\n# Ambient mode is independent — configured in [ambient], not here.\n</code></pre>\n<p>Ambient mode runs as a <strong>separate Dispatcher instance</strong> alongside the primary\none. The primary Dispatcher handles mention-triggered messages (using whatever\n<code>message_processing_mode</code> is configured). The ambient Dispatcher handles\nnon-mentioned messages in ambient-enabled channels with a timer-based consumer.</p>\n<h3>Ambient Consumer Loop</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">// Pseudocode — ambient consumer differs from turn-boundary consumer:\nasync fn ambient_consumer_loop(rx, config, flush_semaphore, channel_flushing) {\n    loop {\n        let first = match rx.recv().await {\n            Some(msg) =&gt; msg,\n            None =&gt; return,                    // channel closed, exit consumer\n        };\n        let deadline = Instant::now() + config.flush_interval_jittered();\n        let mut batch = vec![first];\n\n        loop {\n            let remaining = deadline - Instant::now();\n            match timeout(remaining, rx.recv()).await {\n                Ok(Some(msg)) =&gt; {\n                    batch.push(msg);\n                    if batch.len() &gt;= config.flush_max_messages { break; }\n                    if batch.len() &gt;= config.flush_hard_cap { break; }\n                }\n                Ok(None) =&gt; break,             // channel closed\n                Err(_) =&gt; break,               // timer expired\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Acquire global concurrency permit (blocks if max_concurrent_flushes reached)\n        let _permit = flush_semaphore.acquire().await;\n\n        // Mark channel as flushing (with safety timeout for auto-reset)\n        let _flushing_guard = FlushingGuard::new(\n            channel_flushing,\n            config.flush_timeout_seconds,\n        ); // auto-resets on drop OR timeout\n\n        // Flush: dispatch batch with [NO_REPLY] system prompt\n        match dispatch_ambient_batch(batch).await {\n            Ok(response) =&gt; {\n                if !response.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(&quot;[NO_REPLY]&quot;) {\n                    // Atomic check-and-post: acquire post_guard to prevent\n                    // race with mention cancellation\n                    if let Some(_guard) = post_guard.try_acquire() {\n                        post_response(response).await;\n                    }\n                    // else: mention arrived, cancelled — skip posting\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) =&gt; {\n                warn!(&quot;ambient flush failed, discarding batch: {e}&quot;);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // _flushing_guard dropped here — resets channel_flushing\n        // _permit dropped here — releases semaphore slot\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Other Implementation Details</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No thinking message:</strong> ambient dispatches do NOT send a &quot;...&quot; placeholder\nmessage. Unlike normal mention dispatch, ambient responses are posted directly\nas a single message (or discarded). This eliminates visual flickering in\nthe channel.</li>\n<li><strong><code>[NO_REPLY]</code> check:</strong> applied after <code>stream_prompt</code> completes. If the\ntrimmed final content equals <code>[NO_REPLY]</code> (case-insensitive), no message is\nposted.</li>\n<li><strong>Bot-to-bot loop prevention:</strong> the bot's own messages never enter the buffer\n(existing <code>bot_id</code> check). <strong>For ambient channels, <code>allow_bot_messages</code>\ndefaults to <code>&quot;off&quot;</code></strong> regardless of the global setting — other bots' messages\nare excluded from the ambient buffer unless the operator explicitly opts in.\nEven if opted in, the existing <code>max_bot_turns</code> config (default 100, hard\ncap 1000 — applied at ingest, before <code>submit</code>) prevents infinite loops. The ambient system prompt\nalso explicitly instructs: &quot;Do not reply to other bot messages unless directly\nrelevant to a human's question.&quot;</li>\n<li><strong>Mention detection reuse:</strong> the existing <code>is_mentioned</code> logic in\n<code>Handler::message()</code> (src/discord.rs) fires <strong>before</strong> the buffer push.\nIf mentioned, the message takes the normal dispatch path; the ambient buffer\nfor that channel is discarded (not flushed).</li>\n<li><strong>Bot echo prevention:</strong> <code>msg.author.id == bot_id</code> check (already exists in\nHandler::message) ensures bot's own messages never enter the buffer.</li>\n<li><strong>Reactions suppressed:</strong> ambient dispatches skip <code>StatusReactionController</code>\nentirely — no 👀🤔🔥 on every channel message.</li>\n<li><strong>Serialization with normal dispatch:</strong> the ambient session key\n(<code>ambient:discord:&lt;channel_id&gt;</code>) is different from mention session keys\n(<code>discord:&lt;thread_id&gt;</code>), so they never contend on the same session lock.\nHowever, concurrent reply prevention (see above) ensures at most one response\nis posted per channel — if a @mention arrives mid-flush, the ambient response\nis cancelled via the <code>post_guard</code> mechanism.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Ambient Mode"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/basic-cronjob",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Basic CronJob Support (Config-Driven Scheduled Messages)</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-04-26</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n<li><strong>Related:</strong> <a href=\"/openab/refarch/cronjob_k8s_refarch\">K8s CronJob Reference Architecture</a></li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. User Story &amp; Requirements</h2>\n<p>As an OpenAB operator, I want to define scheduled messages in <code>config.toml</code> that are sent to the agent at specified times, so that I can automate recurring tasks (daily summaries, weekly reports, periodic scans) without external infrastructure.</p>\n<p>As a small-team user, I don't want to set up Kubernetes CronJobs or GitHub Actions just to send a daily prompt to my bot.</p>\n<p>Requirements:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Cron expressions defined declaratively in <code>config.toml</code></li>\n<li>Each cron entry specifies a target channel and a message payload</li>\n<li>OAB sends the message to the agent via the existing ACP session, as if a user typed it</li>\n<li>The scheduler is internal to OAB but <strong>does not</strong> allow the agent to configure or modify cron entries at runtime</li>\n<li>No coupling between scheduler failures and gateway stability — failed cron executions must not block or degrade normal chat traffic</li>\n<li>This is Phase 1 only — complex scheduling (conditional logic, retries, fan-out) remains the domain of external schedulers (K8s CronJob, GitHub Actions)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Context &amp; Decision Drivers</h2>\n<h3>Lessons from In-App CronJob (OpenClaw Pattern)</h3>\n<p>The &quot;in-app cronjob&quot; pattern — where the agent configures its own cron via natural language — has known issues:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Opacity</strong> — users cannot easily inspect what the agent configured</li>\n<li><strong>Reliability</strong> — continuous cron failures or too many in-flight jobs affect gateway stability</li>\n<li><strong>Unpredictability</strong> — agent-generated payloads may not match user intent</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Design Principle: Decouple Scheduler from Core</h3>\n<blockquote>\n<p>&quot;If you already have a good landlord doing scheduling, you don't need your own alarm clock in the room.&quot;</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>OAB's position: the scheduler should be <strong>external to the agent runtime</strong>. For Phase 1, &quot;external&quot; means config-driven (operator-controlled, not agent-controlled). For advanced use cases, truly external schedulers (K8s, GHA) are recommended.</p>\n<h3>Why Config-Driven First</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Covers the 80% use case: &quot;send this message at this time&quot;</li>\n<li>Zero additional infrastructure for simple deployments</li>\n<li>Operator has full visibility and control over what runs and when</li>\n<li>Aligns with OAB's &quot;keep it simple&quot; philosophy</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. High-Level Design</h2>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[cronjobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;                    # cron expression (UTC)\nchannel = &quot;123456789&quot;                        # target channel ID\nmessage = &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot; # message sent to agent\nplatform = &quot;discord&quot;                         # optional, defaults to first configured\nsender_name = &quot;CronScheduler&quot;               # optional, defaults to &quot;openab-cron&quot;\nthread_id = &quot;1234567890&quot;                     # optional, post to existing thread\n\n[[cronjobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 0 * * 0&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789&quot;\nmessage = &quot;generate weekly status report and post it here&quot;\nplatform = &quot;discord&quot;\n\n[[cronjobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 18 * * 1-5&quot;\nchannel = &quot;C0123456789&quot;\nmessage = &quot;check for any critical alerts in the last 8 hours&quot;\nplatform = &quot;slack&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;OpsBot&quot;\nthread_id = &quot;1714000000.000000&quot;              # Slack thread_ts\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Sender Identity</h3>\n<p>When a cron job fires, the message injected into the agent session includes a sender header so the agent knows who/what triggered it:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Default:</strong> <code>openab-cron</code> (if <code>sender_name</code> is not specified)</li>\n<li><strong>Customizable:</strong> operators can set <code>sender_name</code> per cron entry</li>\n</ul>\n<p>The agent sees this in the prompt context the same way it sees a Discord/Slack username, e.g.:</p>\n<pre><code>[openab-cron]: summarize yesterday's merged PRs\n</code></pre>\n<p>This helps the agent distinguish scheduled prompts from interactive users, and operators can use meaningful names like <code>&quot;DailyOps&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;WeeklyReport&quot;</code> for clarity in logs and thread titles.</p>\n<h3>Execution Flow</h3>\n<pre><code>┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  OAB Process                                                 │\n│                                                              │\n│  ┌────────────────┐    tick    ┌──────────────────────┐      │\n│  │  Cron Scheduler│──────────▶│  Session Pool        │      │\n│  │  (internal)    │           │  (existing)          │      │\n│  │                │           │                      │      │\n│  │  Evaluates     │  create   │  Spawns ACP session  │      │\n│  │  expressions   │──session─▶│  for target channel  │      │\n│  │  every minute  │           │                      │      │\n│  └────────────────┘           └──────────┬───────────┘      │\n│                                          │                   │\n│                                          ▼                   │\n│                               ┌──────────────────────┐      │\n│                               │  Agent (kiro-cli)    │      │\n│                               │  Receives message    │      │\n│                               │  as if user typed it │      │\n│                               └──────────┬───────────┘      │\n│                                          │                   │\n│                                          ▼                   │\n│                               ┌──────────────────────┐      │\n│                               │  Platform Adapter    │      │\n│                               │  Posts reply to      │      │\n│                               │  target channel      │      │\n│                               └──────────────────────┘      │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Key Behaviors</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Evaluation</strong> — a lightweight scheduler thread evaluates cron expressions once per minute</li>\n<li><strong>Session creation</strong> — when a cron fires, OAB creates (or reuses) a session for the target channel, identical to a user-initiated session</li>\n<li><strong>Message injection</strong> — the configured message is injected as if a user sent it in the channel</li>\n<li><strong>Reply delivery</strong> — agent response is posted to the target channel via the normal platform adapter</li>\n<li><strong>Thread creation</strong> — each cron execution creates a new thread (Discord) or thread reply (Slack), keeping cron outputs organized. If <code>thread_id</code> is specified, the reply is posted to that existing thread instead (useful for accumulating recurring results in one place).</li>\n<li><strong>Isolation</strong> — cron execution uses the same session pool with standard concurrency limits; a stuck cron job does not starve interactive sessions</li>\n<li><strong>Logging</strong> — each cron tick emits structured logs: <code>DEBUG</code> for expression evaluation, <code>INFO</code> for fired jobs (schedule, channel, message), <code>WARN</code>/<code>ERROR</code> for failures (session creation failed, channel not found, agent timeout)</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Failure Handling</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent session fails to start</td>\n<td>Log error, skip this tick, retry next schedule</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent times out</td>\n<td>Session TTL applies normally; cron does not retry</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Channel not found / bot not in channel</td>\n<td>Log error, skip; do not crash OAB</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Overlapping executions (previous still running)</td>\n<td>Skip if a session for the same cron entry is still active</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>OAB restart</td>\n<td>Cron state is stateless — re-evaluated from config on startup, no persistence needed</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Cron failures are <strong>fire-and-forget</strong> — they log but never block the main event loop or degrade interactive chat performance.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Helm Values Mapping</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># values.yaml\nagents:\n  kiro:\n    cronjobs:\n      - schedule: &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;\n        channel: &quot;123456789&quot;\n        message: &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot;\n        platform: &quot;discord&quot;\n      - schedule: &quot;0 0 * * 0&quot;\n        channel: &quot;123456789&quot;\n        message: &quot;generate weekly status report&quot;\n        platform: &quot;discord&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Rendered into <code>config.toml</code> via the existing Helm ConfigMap template.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Scope Boundaries</h2>\n<h3>In Scope (Phase 1)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Static cron expressions in <code>config.toml</code></li>\n<li>One-way message injection to agent</li>\n<li>Reply posted to configured channel</li>\n<li>Standard 5-field cron syntax (minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week) — same format as Linux crontab, Kubernetes CronJob, and GitHub Actions</li>\n<li>Timezone support via optional <code>timezone</code> field (defaults to UTC)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Cron Expression Format</h3>\n<p>The schedule field uses standard POSIX cron syntax, compatible with:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Linux <code>crontab -e</code></li>\n<li>Kubernetes <code>CronJob.spec.schedule</code></li>\n<li>GitHub Actions <code>cron:</code></li>\n<li>AWS EventBridge <code>cron()</code> (slightly different wrapper but same fields)</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code>┌───────────── minute (0–59)\n│ ┌───────────── hour (0–23)\n│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1–31)\n│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1–12)\n│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0–7, 0 and 7 = Sunday)\n│ │ │ │ │\n* * * * *\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Explicitly Out of Scope</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Feature</th>\n<th>Reason</th>\n<th>Alternative</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent self-configuring cron</td>\n<td>Opacity + reliability concerns (OpenClaw lesson)</td>\n<td>Operator edits config</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Conditional execution</td>\n<td>Complexity belongs in external schedulers</td>\n<td>K8s CronJob / GHA</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Retry with backoff</td>\n<td>Over-engineering for Phase 1</td>\n<td>External scheduler</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cron result persistence / history</td>\n<td>Adds state management to OAB</td>\n<td>External observability</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-step workflows / DAGs</td>\n<td>Not a scheduler's job</td>\n<td>GitHub Actions / Step Functions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Dynamic cron via API / Discord command</td>\n<td>Requires runtime state, auth, validation</td>\n<td>Future ADR if needed</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Comparison with External Scheduler Approaches</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Config-Driven (this ADR)</th>\n<th>K8s CronJob</th>\n<th>GitHub Actions</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Infrastructure needed</td>\n<td>None (built into OAB)</td>\n<td>K8s cluster</td>\n<td>GitHub repo</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Isolation</td>\n<td>Shared OAB process</td>\n<td>Separate Pod per execution</td>\n<td>Separate runner</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Scalability</td>\n<td>Bounded by session pool</td>\n<td>Unlimited (Pod per job)</td>\n<td>Unlimited (runner per job)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Complexity</td>\n<td>Minimal</td>\n<td>Medium (manifests, RBAC)</td>\n<td>Low-Medium (workflow YAML)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Visibility</td>\n<td>Config file + logs</td>\n<td>kubectl + Pod logs</td>\n<td>Actions UI + logs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Best for</td>\n<td>Simple recurring prompts</td>\n<td>Heavy/long-running jobs</td>\n<td>CI/CD-integrated tasks</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Recommendation:</strong> Use config-driven cron for simple &quot;send message at time X&quot; use cases. Graduate to K8s CronJob or GitHub Actions when you need isolation, retries, conditional logic, or long-running executions.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Rollout Plan</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n<th>Deliverable</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 1 (this ADR)</strong></td>\n<td>Config-driven <code>[[cronjobs]]</code> in <code>config.toml</code></td>\n<td>Scheduler module, Helm values, docs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 2</strong></td>\n<td>Observability</td>\n<td>Cron execution metrics, structured logs, optional webhook on failure</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 3</strong></td>\n<td>Enhanced expressions</td>\n<td><code>@daily</code>, <code>@weekly</code> shortcuts, second-precision (optional), jitter</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Consequences</h2>\n<h3>Positive</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Zero-infrastructure scheduled tasks for simple use cases</li>\n<li>Operator has full control and visibility — no agent-configured surprises</li>\n<li>Stateless design — no persistence, no migration, restart-safe</li>\n<li>Decoupled from gateway event loop — cron failures cannot degrade chat</li>\n<li>Natural upgrade path to external schedulers for complex needs</li>\n<li>Aligns with OAB's simplicity-first philosophy</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Negative</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Cannot be configured via natural language in conversation (by design)</li>\n<li>Requires config change + restart/reload to modify schedules</li>\n<li>Limited to what a single message prompt can express</li>\n<li>No built-in retry — transient failures are silently skipped until next tick</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Compliance</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>No agent self-configuration</strong>: the agent must not be able to create, modify, or delete cron entries. All scheduling is operator-controlled via config.</li>\n<li><strong>Isolation from chat traffic</strong>: cron execution must use the standard session pool with concurrency limits. A cron job must never starve interactive sessions.</li>\n<li><strong>Stateless scheduler</strong>: no persistent cron state. Schedule evaluation is purely derived from config + current time.</li>\n<li><strong>Standard cron syntax</strong>: expressions must follow the POSIX 5-field cron format. Non-standard extensions must be explicitly documented.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Version:</strong> 0.1</li>\n<li><strong>Changelog:</strong>\n<ul>\n<li>0.1 (2026-04-26): Initial proposed version</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/refarch/cronjob_k8s_refarch\">K8s CronJob Reference Architecture</a> — external scheduler approach for heavy workloads</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/config-reference\">OpenAB Configuration Reference</a> — existing config.toml structure</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway\">ADR: Custom Gateway</a> — gateway architecture context (scheduled triggers via webhook)</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/crontab.5.html\">cron(5) man page</a> — POSIX cron expression syntax</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Basic CronJob Support (Config-Driven Scheduled Messages)"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/context-aware-token",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Context-Aware Token for Agent-Initiated Platform Operations</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-03</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n<li><strong>Related:</strong> #339, PR #527 (superseded)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Problem</h2>\n<p>OAB agents today are <strong>passive receivers</strong> — they get a prompt from the adapter and return a response. But real-world usage reveals scenarios where agents need to <strong>actively interact</strong> with the platform:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Current State</th>\n<th>Desired State</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Update thread title to reflect task status</td>\n<td>Agent uses <code>curl</code> via steering doc hack</td>\n<td>Agent calls Discord API directly</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Fetch a specific historical message</td>\n<td>❌ Not possible — agent only sees conversation window</td>\n<td>Agent fetches any message by ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Notify a bot in another channel</td>\n<td>❌ Not possible — agent is confined to current channel</td>\n<td>Agent sends cross-channel messages</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Ping another bot to trigger a reaction</td>\n<td>❌ Not possible</td>\n<td>Agent mentions bot in target channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Why Not PR #527's Approach?</h3>\n<p>PR #527 proposed always prepending quoted message content to the agent prompt at the OAB transport layer. While well-implemented, this approach:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Always pays the cost</strong> (~500 tokens per reply) even when the agent already has the context from conversation history</li>\n<li><strong>Only solves one edge case</strong> (reply/quote context) out of the broader set of agent-initiated operations</li>\n<li><strong>Puts the decision in the wrong layer</strong> — OAB (transport) decides what context the agent needs, instead of the agent deciding for itself</li>\n</ul>\n<p>A context-aware token lets the agent <strong>pull context on demand</strong> — only when it determines the context is needed.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Prior Art &amp; Industry Research</h2>\n<h3>OpenClaw</h3>\n<p><strong>How it works:</strong> OpenClaw uses a <strong>mediated architecture</strong> — agents never get direct API tokens or raw platform access. All platform interactions flow through the Gateway + Channel Adapter layer:</p>\n<pre><code>Agent → Gateway (tool call / response) → Channel Outbound Adapter → Platform API\nPlatform API → Channel Monitor → Gateway (normalized MsgContext) → Agent\n</code></pre>\n<p>Key mechanisms:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>50-action message action system</strong> — agents invoke named actions (<code>send</code>, <code>thread-create</code>, <code>read</code>, <code>edit</code>, <code>delete</code>, <code>search</code>, <code>pin</code>, <code>role-add</code>, etc.) dispatched to channel plugins. Each action is gated by <code>supportsAction</code> checks against a <code>ChannelCapabilities</code> object declaring what each platform supports.</li>\n<li><strong>Session tools for cross-channel operations</strong> — <code>sessions_list</code>, <code>sessions_history</code>, <code>sessions_send</code>, <code>sessions_spawn</code> let agents discover sessions, fetch transcripts, send messages across channels, and spawn sub-agents. Inter-session messages are tagged with <code>message.provenance.kind = &quot;inter_session&quot;</code> for auditability.</li>\n<li><strong>Layered policy model</strong> — security enforced at multiple levels: Tool Profile → Provider Profile → Global Policy → Provider Policy → Agent Policy → Group Policy → Sandbox Policy. Later sources override earlier ones.</li>\n<li><strong>Send Policy</strong> — configurable deny/allow rules for agent-initiated messages by channel and chat type, enforced at the gateway level.</li>\n<li><strong>Session-based trust boundaries</strong> — <code>main</code> sessions (operator) get full host access; <code>dm</code> and <code>group</code> sessions are sandboxed in Docker containers by default.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Security lessons from advisories:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Advisory</th>\n<th>Risk</th>\n<th>Lesson for OpenAB</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-v3qc-wrwx-j3pw\">GHSA-v3qc-wrwx-j3pw</a> (High)</td>\n<td>LLM agent disabled exec approval via config.patch</td>\n<td>Behavioral constraints alone are insufficient — agents can modify their own config to bypass them</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-2rqg-gjgv-84jm\">GHSA-2rqg-gjgv-84jm</a> (High, CVSS 8.8)</td>\n<td>Workspace boundary override via attacker-controlled params</td>\n<td>Gateway must enforce boundaries regardless of caller overrides</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-7jx5-9fjg-hp4m\">GHSA-7jx5-9fjg-hp4m</a> (Moderate)</td>\n<td>ACP permission auto-approval bypass via untrusted metadata</td>\n<td>Auto-approval heuristics trusting untrusted metadata are dangerous</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Key insight:</strong> The mediated architecture IS the security boundary.
