Agents never touch platform APIs directly — the Gateway enforces what's allowed.</p>\n<p>References:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Channel plugin types: <a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw\"><code>src/channels/plugins/types.plugin.ts</code></a></li>\n<li>Session tools: <a href=\"https://molty.finna.ai/docs/concepts/session-tool\">docs/concepts/session-tool</a></li>\n<li>Security advisories: <a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security\">github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security</a></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Hermes Agent</h3>\n<p><strong>How it works:</strong> Hermes Agent uses a <strong>tool-based architecture</strong> — platform operations are exposed as LLM tools with OpenAI function-calling schemas. The agent decides when to call them.</p>\n<p>Key mechanisms:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Discord tool</strong> (<a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\"><code>tools/discord_tool.py</code></a>) — 14 actions split into two toolsets: <code>discord</code> (core: <code>fetch_messages</code>, <code>search_members</code>, <code>create_thread</code>) and <code>discord_admin</code> (server management). Uses Discord REST API directly with the bot token.</li>\n<li><strong>Cross-platform <code>send_message</code> tool</strong> (<a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\"><code>tools/send_message_tool.py</code></a>) — supports 17+ platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Matrix, etc.) with human-friendly name resolution via <code>gateway/channel_directory.py</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Dynamic schema based on capabilities</strong> — Discord tool detects bot intents via <code>GET /applications/@me</code> and hides unavailable actions from the schema (e.g., <code>search_members</code> hidden if GUILD_MEMBERS intent is missing). This prevents the LLM from hallucinating calls to tools it can't use.</li>\n<li><strong>Config-based action allowlist</strong> — <code>discord.server_actions</code> in config.yaml restricts which actions the agent can perform. Runtime re-checks the allowlist even if a stale cached schema exposes a disabled action.</li>\n<li><strong>Defense-in-depth</strong> — three layers: (1) schema filtering removes unavailable actions, (2) runtime allowlist check at dispatch, (3) platform-level permission errors (Discord 403) handled gracefully with actionable guidance.</li>\n<li><strong>Error redaction</strong> — <code>_sanitize_error_text()</code> strips secrets (GitHub PATs, Bearer tokens, API keys) from error messages before they reach the LLM.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Gaps relevant to OpenAB:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Only Discord has a comprehensive read tool (<code>fetch_messages</code>). Other platforms (Telegram, Slack, etc.) have no equivalent — agents can send to them but not read from them.</li>\n<li>No formal capability/scope system beyond the Discord config allowlist. The agent either has the tool or doesn't.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Key insight:</strong> Tools provide a structured, auditable interface vs raw API access. The schema itself acts as a capability declaration — the agent can only call what's in the schema.</p>\n<p>References:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Discord tool: <a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\"><code>tools/discord_tool.py</code></a></li>\n<li>Send message tool: <a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\"><code>tools/send_message_tool.py</code></a></li>\n<li>Tool registry: <a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\"><code>tools/registry.py</code></a></li>\n<li>Security docs: <a href=\"https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/security\">hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/security</a></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Comparison</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>OpenClaw</th>\n<th>Hermes Agent</th>\n<th>OpenAB (this ADR)</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent-to-platform interface</td>\n<td>Mediated — Gateway dispatches named actions</td>\n<td>Tool-based — LLM tools with function-calling schemas</td>\n<td>Direct — agent calls platform API with token</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Security enforcement</td>\n<td>Technical — Gateway enforces layered policy</td>\n<td>Technical — schema gating + runtime allowlist + platform permissions</td>\n<td>Behavioral — steering docs define allow/deny (see §5 for evolution path)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cross-channel operations</td>\n<td><code>sessions_send</code> with provenance tagging</td>\n<td><code>send_message</code> tool with 17+ platform support</td>\n<td>Agent uses token + <code>curl</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Message fetching</td>\n<td><code>sessions_history</code> + <code>read</code> action</td>\n<td><code>discord_tool.fetch_messages</code> (Discord only)</td>\n<td>Agent calls REST API directly</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Audit trail</td>\n<td>Inter-session provenance tags</td>\n<td>Tool call logs</td>\n<td>None built-in (see §5 for planned additions)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Why OpenAB Diverges</h3>\n<p>Both OpenClaw and Hermes use <strong>mediated architectures</strong> where the platform (Gateway or tool runtime) controls what agents can do. OpenAB's context-aware token takes a different path: <strong>direct agent access with behavioral constraints</strong>.</p>\n<p>This is a deliberate tradeoff:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>OAB's architecture</strong> — OAB is a passive transport layer by design. Adding a Gateway mediation layer or tool runtime would be a fundamental architecture change, not an incremental feature.</li>\n<li><strong>Agent diversity</strong> — OAB supports 4+ different agent runtimes (Kiro CLI, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini). A mediated approach would require each runtime to integrate with OAB's tool/action system. Direct token access works with any agent that has shell access.</li>\n<li><strong>Pragmatism</strong> — The pattern already works in production (超渡法師 uses <code>curl</code> + bot token for thread title updates). This ADR formalizes and hardens what's already happening.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>The security gap is real and acknowledged — §5 below describes the evolution path from behavioral-only to defense-in-depth.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Proposed Design</h2>\n<h3>Core Concept</h3>\n<p>Give the agent a <strong>scoped platform token</strong> (e.g., <code>DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN</code>) that it can use to perform platform API calls when it judges them necessary. The token is configured by the user in their steering/tools definition, not by OAB core.</p>\n<pre><code>OAB Layer (transport)              Agent Layer (intelligence)\n─────────────────────              ────────────────────────\nBOT_TOKEN                          DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN\nPassive: receive msg, send reply   Active: fetch, notify, update\nOAB doesn't change                 User defines allowed operations\nAdapter responsibility             Agent autonomy\n</code></pre>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>User sets <code>DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN</code> in the agent's environment (same bot token or a separate scoped token)</li>\n</ol>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ <strong>Security note:</strong> Using the same bot token as <code>DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN</code> grants the agent full bot permissions — this is a convenience shortcut suitable only for trusted, single-operator deployments. For production or multi-tenant environments, use a separate token with minimal scopes when the platform supports it. See §5 for the security evolution path.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<ol start=\"2\">\n<li>User defines allowed operations in <code>tools.md</code> or steering docs</li>\n<li>Agent decides at runtime when to use the token — e.g., &quot;user said 'why?' and I'm not sure what they're referring to, let me fetch the referenced message&quot;</li>\n<li>OAB core is unaware of this — it's purely an agent-side capability</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Scope Definition (User-Controlled)</h3>\n<p>The trust boundary is initially defined by the user in steering docs. <strong>This is a documentation convention, not a security boundary</strong> — the agent has the full token and is behaviorally constrained, not technically restricted. See §5 for the evolution path toward technical enforcement.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-markdown\"># Discord Context Tools\n\nYou have DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN for platform operations.\n\n## Allowed\n- Update current thread title\n- Fetch messages in current channel/thread\n- Send messages to specified channels (cross-channel notify)\n- Add reactions\n\n## Not Allowed\n- Delete messages\n- Modify server settings\n- Manage roles/permissions\n- Create/delete channels\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Use Cases</h2>\n<h3>4a. Smart Quote Resolution (Replaces PR #527)</h3>\n<p>Instead of always prepending quoted content:</p>\n<pre><code>User replies to a message: &quot;why?&quot;\n  │\n  ├─ Agent sees &quot;why?&quot; in prompt\n  ├─ Agent checks conversation history — enough context? → respond directly\n  ├─ Not enough context? → use token to fetch referenced message\n  └─ Now respond with full understanding\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Benefit:</strong> Zero extra tokens when context is already available. Only fetches when genuinely needed.</p>\n<h3>4b. Cross-Channel Bot Coordination</h3>\n<pre><code>User: &quot;ask 普渡法師 in #claude-room to review this code&quot;\n  │\n  ├─ Agent uses token to send message to #claude-room\n  ├─ Message mentions 普渡法師 bot\n  └─ 普渡法師 receives the message and starts working\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4c. Thread Title Management</h3>\n<pre><code>Agent finishes reviewing PR #527\n  │\n  ├─ Agent uses token to update thread title\n  └─ &quot;🔢 PR #527 reviewed&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is already happening today via steering doc + <code>curl</code>. The token formalizes it.</p>\n<h3>4d. Historical Context Retrieval</h3>\n<pre><code>User: &quot;what did Jack say about this yesterday?&quot;\n  │\n  ├─ Agent searches conversation history — not in window\n  ├─ Agent uses token to fetch recent messages from channel\n  └─ Finds Jack's message and responds\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Security Model</h2>\n<h3>Current State: Behavioral Constraints Only</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Concern</th>\n<th>Mitigation</th>\n<th>Limitation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Token is same as BOT_TOKEN — full permissions</td>\n<td>Steering docs define allow/deny list</td>\n<td>Agent can ignore steering docs (prompt injection, hallucination)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent could misuse token</td>\n<td>Steering docs define explicit scope</td>\n<td>No technical enforcement — relies on agent compliance</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Token leaked in logs</td>\n<td>Agent instructed to reference by env var name</td>\n<td>No redaction layer — agent could still echo the value</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cross-channel abuse</td>\n<td>Steering docs restrict target channels</td>\n<td>No runtime validation of target channels</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>This is insufficient for production use.</strong> OpenClaw's security advisories demonstrate that behavioral constraints alone fail — their <a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-v3qc-wrwx-j3pw\">GHSA-v3qc-wrwx-j3pw</a> showed an LLM agent disabling its own exec approval via config modification.</p>\n<h3>Evolution Path: Behavioral → Defense-in-Depth</h3>\n<p>The security model evolves across four maturity levels (distinct from the <a href=\"#10-rollout-plan\">Rollout Plan in §10</a>, which tracks implementation milestones):</p>\n<p><strong>Level 1 (Behavioral only — current):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Steering docs define allowed operations</li>\n<li>Suitable for trusted, operator-controlled agents only</li>\n<li>Acceptable risk: operator is the user AND the admin</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Level 2 (Audit logging):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>OAB logs all outbound HTTP calls from agent processes (network-level observation)</li>\n<li>No enforcement, but provides visibility for post-incident analysis</li>\n<li>Implementation: eBPF-based network monitoring or HTTP proxy with logging</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Level 3 (Proxy enforcement):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Agent's <code>DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN</code> routes through an OAB-controlled HTTP proxy</li>\n<li>Proxy validates each API call against a configured allowlist:\n<pre><code># Example proxy allowlist (config.toml)\n[agent_proxy]\nallowed_endpoints = [\n  &quot;GET /channels/*/messages&quot;,      # fetch messages\n  &quot;PATCH /channels/*&quot;,             # update thread title\n  &quot;POST /channels/*/messages&quot;,     # send messages\n  &quot;PUT /channels/*/messages/*/reactions/*&quot;,  # add reactions\n]\ndenied_endpoints = [\n  &quot;DELETE *&quot;,                      # no deletions\n  &quot;PUT /guilds/*&quot;,                 # no server modifications\n]\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>Denied calls return 403 with audit log entry</li>\n<li>Inspired by Hermes Agent's defense-in-depth (schema filtering + runtime allowlist + platform permissions)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Level 4 (True scoped tokens):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>If Discord (or other platforms) introduce fine-grained token scopes, swap the token</li>\n<li>The agent-side interface doesn't change — only the token's actual permissions narrow</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Comparison with Prior Art</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Layer</th>\n<th>OpenClaw</th>\n<th>Hermes Agent</th>\n<th>OpenAB Level 1</th>\n<th>OpenAB Level 3</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Schema/capability gating</td>\n<td>✅ <code>supportsAction</code></td>\n<td>✅ Dynamic schema</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Runtime allowlist</td>\n<td>✅ Send Policy</td>\n<td>✅ Config allowlist</td>\n<td>❌ Steering docs only</td>\n<td>✅ Proxy allowlist</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Platform permission errors</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅ Graceful 403 handling</td>\n<td>✅ (passthrough)</td>\n<td>✅ (passthrough)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Audit trail</td>\n<td>✅ Provenance tags</td>\n<td>✅ Tool call logs</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>✅ Proxy logs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Secret redaction</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>✅ <code>_sanitize_error_text()</code></td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>✅ Proxy strips tokens from errors</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Concrete Resolution Path for Issue #339</h2>\n<p>Issue <a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/339\">#339</a> requests reply/quote context in agent prompts. PR #527 implemented always-on prepending; this ADR supersedes that approach with on-demand fetching.</p>\n<h3>How #339 Gets Resolved</h3>\n<p>There are two distinct scenarios for context resolution. The token is only needed for the second.</p>\n<p><strong>Scenario A — Discord reply (user uses reply/quote feature):</strong></p>\n<p>Discord Gateway already sends <code>referenced_message</code> (full message object) and <code>message_reference</code> (with <code>message_id</code>, <code>channel_id</code>, <code>guild_id</code>) on reply messages (type 19). OAB's adapter receives this data and can passthrough it to the agent at near-zero cost.</p>\n<p><strong>Step 1 — OAB passthroughs reply metadata (minimal transport-layer change):</strong></p>\n<p>OAB already receives <code>referenced_message</code> from Discord's gateway. Instead of prepending the full quoted content (PR #527's approach), OAB injects only the metadata:</p>\n<pre><code>[Reply context: message_id=1234567890, channel_id=9876543210, author=Jack]\n</code></pre>\n<p>This costs ~20 tokens (vs ~500 for full content) and gives the agent enough information to decide whether to fetch.</p>\n<p><strong>Step 2 — Agent decides whether to fetch:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>If the conversation history already contains the referenced message → respond directly (zero extra cost)</li>\n<li>If the agent needs the full content of the referenced message → use <code>DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN</code> to call <code>GET /channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}</code> and fetch it</li>\n<li>If no token is configured → agent responds based on available context (graceful degradation)</li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Because Discord already provides <code>referenced_message</code> on reply messages, OAB could alternatively passthrough the full content directly (like PR #527). The metadata-only approach is preferred because it keeps the transport layer minimal and lets the agent decide. Either way, the token is not strictly required for this scenario.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p><strong>Scenario B — Non-reply historical lookup (no <code>referenced_message</code> available):</strong></p>\n<p>When a user asks about past messages without using Discord's reply feature (e.g., &quot;what did Jack say about this yesterday?&quot;), there is no <code>referenced_message</code> in the Gateway event. This is where the context-aware token provides unique value — the agent uses it to call <code>GET /channels/{channel_id}/messages</code> and search for relevant messages.</p>\n<p><strong>Step 3 — Steering doc template:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-markdown\"># Reply Context Resolution\n\nWhen you see `[Reply context: message_id=..., channel_id=..., author=...]`:\n1. Check if the referenced message is already in your conversation history\n2. If not, and you need it to respond accurately, fetch it:\n   curl -s -H &quot;Authorization: Bot $DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n     &quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}&quot;\n3. If DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN is not available, respond based on available context\n\n# Historical Context Retrieval (no reply metadata)\n\nWhen a user references past messages without using Discord reply:\n1. Use the token to fetch recent messages from the channel:\n   curl -s -H &quot;Authorization: Bot $DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n     &quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/{channel_id}/messages?limit=50&quot;\n2. Search the results for relevant context\n3. If DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN is not available, ask the user to quote or reply to the specific message\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Acceptance Criteria for #339</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> OAB injects reply metadata (<code>message_id</code>, <code>channel_id</code>, <code>author</code>) into agent prompt — small transport-layer PR</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Steering doc template published for agents to use the token for on-demand fetching</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> At least one agent (超渡法師) validated end-to-end: reply in Discord → agent fetches referenced message → responds with full context</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Issue #339 closed with reference to this ADR and the implementing PRs</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. What Changes in OAB?</h2>\n<p><strong>Minimal.</strong> The key design principle is preserved — OAB remains a passive transport layer:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Reply metadata injection</strong> (for #339): OAB adds <code>[Reply context: message_id=..., channel_id=..., author=...]</code> to the prompt when a Discord message has <code>referenced_message</code>. This is a small, targeted change in <code>discord.rs</code> (~10 lines).</li>\n<li><strong>Token passthrough</strong>: OAB already passes environment variables to agent processes. No change needed — user adds <code>DISCORD_CONTEXT_TOKEN</code> to their agent config.</li>\n<li><strong>Proxy (Level 3, optional)</strong>: If/when proxy enforcement is added, it would be a new optional component, not a change to OAB core.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Relationship to Existing Features</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Feature</th>\n<th>Relationship</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>PR #527 (reply context)</td>\n<td><strong>Superseded</strong> — context-aware token solves the same problem more efficiently (on-demand vs always-on)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Custom Gateway ADR</td>\n<td><strong>Complementary</strong> — gateway handles inbound webhooks; context-aware token handles agent-initiated outbound operations</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-Platform Adapters ADR</td>\n<td><strong>Complementary</strong> — each platform can have its own scoped token type</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Steering docs</td>\n<td><strong>Extended</strong> — steering docs gain a new responsibility: defining token scope (Level 1 only — Level 3 moves to proxy enforcement)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Open Questions</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Question</th>\n<th>Options</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><del>One token per platform or unified?</del></td>\n<td><strong>Decided: Per-platform</strong> — simpler and more secure</td>\n<td>Start with Discord, extend later</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Should OAB inject the token automatically?</td>\n<td>No — user configures it in agent env</td>\n<td>Keeps OAB uninvolved</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Rate limiting on agent-initiated calls?</td>\n<td>Level 1: rely on platform rate limits; Level 3: proxy-level rate limiting</td>\n<td>Proxy can enforce per-agent rate limits</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>How to handle platforms without API tokens?</td>\n<td>N/A until needed</td>\n<td>LINE, Telegram have different auth models</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Should OAB provide a proxy from Level 1?</td>\n<td>No — start with behavioral constraints for trusted operators, add proxy when multi-tenant or untrusted agents are needed</td>\n<td>Complexity should match the threat model</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. Rollout Plan</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n<th>Target</th>\n<th>Acceptance Criteria</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 1</strong></td>\n<td>Document the pattern — steering doc template for Discord context token</td>\n<td>v0.9.x</td>\n<td>Template published, validated with 超渡法師</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 2</strong></td>\n<td>Resolve #339 — OAB injects reply metadata, agent fetches on demand</td>\n<td>v0.9.x</td>\n<td>#339 closed, end-to-end validation with at least one agent</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 3</strong></td>\n<td>Formalize as <code>tools.md</code> convention across OpenAB agents</td>\n<td>v0.10.x</td>\n<td>All 4 agent runtimes have working steering doc templates</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 4</strong></td>\n<td>Add optional audit logging for agent-initiated API calls</td>\n<td>v0.10.x</td>\n<td>Operator can see what API calls agents make</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 5</strong></td>\n<td>Evaluate proxy enforcement for multi-tenant / untrusted agent scenarios</td>\n<td>v0.11.x+</td>\n<td>Design doc for proxy layer if demand exists</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Consequences</h2>\n<h3>Positive</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Agent gets platform awareness without OAB core changes</li>\n<li>On-demand context fetching is more token-efficient than always-on prepending</li>\n<li>Enables cross-channel coordination — a capability that was previously impossible</li>\n<li>User controls the scope — no one-size-fits-all behavior imposed by OAB</li>\n<li>Pattern extends naturally to other platforms</li>\n<li>Concrete path to resolve #339 with minimal OAB changes</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Negative</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Phase 1 trust boundary is behavioral (steering docs), not technical — relies on agent compliance. Acceptable for trusted operators; insufficient for multi-tenant deployments.</li>\n<li>Each user must configure the token and define scope — more setup burden</li>\n<li>Agent-initiated API calls add latency when they occur</li>\n<li>No centralized audit of what agents do with the token until Phase 4</li>\n<li>Diverges from industry standard (mediated architecture) — conscious tradeoff for OAB's passive transport philosophy</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/339\">Issue #339</a> — Original feature request for reply/quote context</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/pull/527\">PR #527</a> — Implementation of always-on quote prepending (superseded by this ADR)</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway\">ADR: Custom Gateway</a> — Complementary architecture for inbound webhook handling</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/multi-platform-adapters\">ADR: Multi-Platform Adapters</a> — Platform-agnostic adapter layer</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security\">OpenClaw Security Advisories</a> — Real-world security lessons for agent-platform interactions</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/tools-runtime\">Hermes Agent Tools Runtime</a> — Tool-based agent interaction architecture</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Context-Aware Token for Agent-Initiated Platform Operations"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/control-directives",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Control Directives</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-02</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> chaodu-agent</li>\n<li><strong>Related:</strong> <a href=\"/openab/output-directives\">Output Directives</a></li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context</h2>\n<h3>1.1 Problem</h3>\n<p>A single OAB bot instance may serve multiple projects, each with its own steering files, skills, and workspace context. Today, there is no mechanism for a user to specify session-level parameters (working directory, model) when initiating a conversation. The bot always starts with its default configuration, requiring manual reconfiguration or separate bot instances per project.</p>\n<h3>1.2 Why Workspace Selection Matters</h3>\n<p>Specifying a workspace at session start eliminates the manual warm-up cost. Without it, users spend the first several messages orienting the agent. With <code>[[ws:...]]</code>, the agent gains full project context immediately:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Steering rules</strong> — <code>AGENTS.md</code> and <code>.kiro/steering/</code> load automatically (coding style, architecture decisions, naming conventions). The agent knows how this project does things.</li>\n<li><strong>Skills</strong> — <code>.kiro/skills/</code> activate project-specific capabilities (e.g., review workflows, deployment helpers).</li>\n<li><strong>File scope</strong> — the agent's working directory is the project root; reads, searches, and writes target the correct codebase.</li>\n<li><strong>Git context</strong> — branch, remote, and commit history are correct for PR review, diff, and blame operations.</li>\n<li><strong>Session isolation</strong> — multiple projects served by one bot instance never leak context between sessions.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>In short: one directive replaces 3–5 round trips of &quot;here's the repo, here's how we work, here's what I need.&quot;</p>\n<h3>1.3 Existing Pattern</h3>\n<p>OAB already has <strong>output directives</strong> — <code>[[key:value]]</code> syntax that agents prepend to their responses to control delivery behavior (e.g., <code>[[reply_to:...]]</code>). This pattern is well-understood, parsed reliably, and invisible to end users after processing.</p>\n<h3>1.4 Opportunity</h3>\n<p>Extend the <code>[[key:value]]</code> convention to <strong>input</strong> (user → bot) messages, creating <strong>control directives</strong> that configure the session at creation time. This unifies the directive syntax across both directions and gives users declarative control over session initialization without requiring new slash commands or config files.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Decision</h2>\n<p>Introduce <strong>Control Directives</strong> — <code>[[key:value]]</code> patterns in user messages that configure session parameters. They share the double-bracket syntax with output directives but flow in the opposite direction (user → broker → agent runtime).</p>\n<h3>2.1 Syntax</h3>\n<pre><code>@Bot [[ws:~/workdir/foo]] [[title:PR review]]\ninvestigate this build failure\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2.2 Core Rules</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Rule</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Scope</strong></td>\n<td>Processed only on the session's first message (the one that mentions/triggers the bot)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Parsing</strong></td>\n<td>Extract a leading control header only: directives immediately after the trigger/mention and before normal prompt text</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Stop condition</strong></td>\n<td>The first non-directive token or line starts prompt content; later <code>[[key:value]]</code> text is preserved verbatim</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Stripping</strong></td>\n<td>Header directives are removed from the message; remaining text becomes the prompt</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Duplicate keys</strong></td>\n<td>Last value wins</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Unknown keys</strong></td>\n<td>Silently ignored (forward compatible)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Placement</strong></td>\n<td>Directives may be adjacent on the trigger line or on following header lines before prompt content begins</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Empty value</strong></td>\n<td>Behavior is directive-specific: empty <code>ws</code> and <code>model</code> are invalid; empty <code>title</code> means &quot;use generated title&quot;</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>2.3 Architecture Position</h3>\n<pre><code>User message\n     │\n     ▼\n┌─────────────────────┐\n│  Directive Parser    │  ← extracts leading [[key:value]] header, strips it\n│  (middleware)        │\n└─────────────────────┘\n     │\n     ├── structured SessionMetadata\n     │\n     ▼\n┌─────────────────────┐\n│  Agent Runtime       │  ← receives clean prompt + metadata\n└─────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>The directive parser runs <strong>before</strong> the message enters the agent pipeline. It outputs:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>prompt: String</code> — the message with directives stripped</li>\n<li><code>metadata: SessionMetadata</code> — parsed key-value pairs for runtime configuration</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Supported Directives (Phase 1)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Directive</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[ws:/path]]</code></td>\n<td>Set session working directory; loads steering/skills from that path</td>\n<td><code>[[ws:~/projects/myapp]]</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[title:...]]</code></td>\n<td>Set initial thread title</td>\n<td><code>[[title:Bug triage #42]]</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>3.1 <code>[[ws:/path]]</code> — Workspace</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Loads <code>AGENTS.md</code>, <code>.kiro/steering/</code>, and skill definitions from the target path</li>\n<li>If the path does not exist, session fails with user-visible error</li>\n<li><strong>Security boundary — bot home subtree only.</strong> Enforcement order:\n<ol>\n<li>Reject if path is relative (does not start with <code>~</code> or <code>/</code>)</li>\n<li>Expand <code>~</code> → bot home directory</li>\n<li>Canonicalize both the bot home root and target path (resolve symlinks, <code>..</code>, <code>.</code>) via <code>std::fs::canonicalize()</code> or equivalent</li>\n<li>Verify canonical path starts with bot home root (<code>canonical.starts_with(bot_home)</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Reject</strong> if outside bot home — session does not start, user-visible error returned</li>\n</ol>\n</li>\n<li>The canonical workspace is stored in <code>SessionMetadata</code> and reused for session creation, session load/resume, eviction rebuilds, and any persisted session mapping. A <code>[[ws:...]]</code> session must never resume in the configured default working directory unless that was the resolved workspace.</li>\n<li>Workspace steering defines repo context (remote URL, branch, etc.) — no separate repo binding needed in Phase 1</li>\n</ul>\n<h4>Workspace Aliases</h4>\n<p>Full paths are verbose for frequent use. The operator may define workspace aliases in <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[workspace.aliases]\nopenab = &quot;~/projects/openab&quot;\ninfra  = &quot;~/projects/infra-cdk&quot;\nweb    = &quot;~/projects/frontend&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Users reference aliases with an <code>@</code> prefix:</p>\n<pre><code>@Bot [[ws:@openab]] [[title:Fix CI]]\nhelp me debug the smoke test\n</code></pre>\n<p>Resolution order:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>If value starts with <code>@</code>, look up alias in <code>workspace.aliases</code></li>\n<li>If alias not found → reject with user-visible error listing available aliases</li>\n<li>If found → substitute the full path, then apply the same canonicalize + security check as raw paths</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Aliases are syntactic sugar — they resolve before any security validation and produce identical <code>SessionMetadata</code> to raw paths.</p>\n<h3>3.2 <code>[[title:...]]</code> — Thread Title</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Sets the initial thread/channel title</li>\n<li>Agent may override this later per its own SOP (e.g., status-based title updates)</li>\n<li>Max length: 100 characters (truncated silently)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3.3 <code>[[model:...]]</code> — Model Selection</h3>\n<p>Phase 2 adds <code>[[model:...]]</code> after the parser, workspace, and title path are implemented.</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Value must match a configured model identifier</li>\n<li>If the model is unavailable or unknown, the session is rejected after runtime config discovery but before the user's first prompt is sent. The user receives an error and no user task is executed in the wrong model.</li>\n<li>Does not persist beyond the session</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Design Decisions</h2>\n<h3>4.1 Why Session-First Only</h3>\n<p>Processing directives only on the first message keeps the mental model simple:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>No mid-conversation state mutations</li>\n<li>No need for &quot;directive acknowledged&quot; confirmation messages</li>\n<li>Session parameters are immutable once established</li>\n<li>Easier to reason about for both users and agents</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>4.2 Why Not Slash Commands</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Slash Commands</th>\n<th>Control Directives</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Discovery</td>\n<td>Platform UI autocomplete</td>\n<td>Docs / muscle memory</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Composability</td>\n<td>One command at a time</td>\n<td>Multiple directives in one message</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Platform dependency</td>\n<td>Requires registration per platform</td>\n<td>Platform-agnostic (just text)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Works with mention</td>\n<td>Awkward (<code>/command @bot</code>)</td>\n<td>Natural (<code>@bot [[...]] prompt</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Control directives are platform-agnostic text — they work on Discord, Slack, Telegram, or any adapter without platform-specific command registration.</p>\n<h3>4.3 Relationship to Output Directives</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Output Directives</th>\n<th>Control Directives</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Direction</td>\n<td>Agent → Platform</td>\n<td>User → Broker</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Processing layer</td>\n<td>Response post-processor</td>\n<td>Message pre-processor</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Timing</td>\n<td>Every response</td>\n<td>Session first message only</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Syntax</td>\n<td><code>[[key:value]]</code></td>\n<td><code>[[key:value]]</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Unknown keys</td>\n<td>Ignored</td>\n<td>Ignored</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Duplicate keys</td>\n<td>Last wins</td>\n<td>Last wins</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Shared syntax reduces cognitive load. The direction is unambiguous from context (who authored the message).</p>\n<p>Control directives intentionally do <strong>not</strong> scan the entire message body. This mirrors the output directive header concept and avoids corrupting normal prompts that quote code, issue templates, or examples containing <code>[[key:value]]</code>.</p>\n<h3>4.4 Security Considerations</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>[[ws:...]]</code> enforces bot home subtree only — canonicalize, reject symlink escapes (see §3.1)</li>\n<li><code>[[model:...]]</code> only selects from pre-configured models; cannot inject arbitrary API endpoints; unknown model = hard fail</li>\n<li>Directive values are sanitized (no newlines, no control characters beyond the value delimiter)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>4.5 No Mid-Session Reset</h3>\n<p>Control directives are immutable once the session starts. There is no mechanism to change <code>ws</code>, <code>title</code>, or <code>model</code> mid-conversation. To change parameters, start a new session. This eliminates state mutation complexity and keeps the session contract predictable.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Future Extensions</h2>\n<p>These are <strong>not</strong> in scope for Phase 1 but the design accommodates them:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Directive</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[repo:owner/repo]]</code></td>\n<td>Bind GitHub repository context (Phase 1 relies on <code>[[ws:...]]</code> steering to define repo context)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[timeout:300]]</code></td>\n<td>Session timeout in seconds</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[skill:review]]</code></td>\n<td>Activate a specific skill set</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[label:bug]]</code></td>\n<td>Tag the session/thread with labels (multi-value: array semantics)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Why <code>[[repo:...]]</code> is not in Phase 1:</strong> Workspace steering files already define repository context (remote URL, branch conventions, etc.). A standalone <code>[[repo:...]]</code> directive would need to specify what &quot;binding&quot; means (clone? set remote? just metadata?) — that design is deferred until usage patterns emerge from <code>[[ws:...]]</code> adoption.</p>\n<p>For multi-value keys (e.g., <code>[[label:a]] [[label:b]]</code>), a future revision may introduce array semantics where repeated keys accumulate rather than overwrite. Phase 1 uses last-wins for all keys.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Implementation Plan</h2>\n<h3>Phase 1: Parser + <code>ws</code> (with aliases) + <code>title</code></h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Implement directive parser as a middleware in the message ingestion pipeline</li>\n<li>Define <code>SessionMetadata</code> struct</li>\n<li>Persist <code>SessionMetadata</code> per session key so workspace survives reconnect, resume, and eviction rebuilds</li>\n<li>Add <code>[workspace.aliases]</code> table to <code>config.toml</code> schema</li>\n<li>Wire <code>[[ws:...]]</code> to workspace/context loading (raw paths and <code>@alias</code> resolution)</li>\n<li>Wire <code>[[title:...]]</code> to thread title initialization</li>\n<li>Unit tests for parser edge cases (nested brackets, escaped content, empty values, body text that contains directive-like literals, unknown alias error)</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Phase 2: <code>model</code></h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Wire <code>[[model:...]]</code> to model selection in agent runtime</li>\n<li>Validate against runtime config options before the first user prompt is sent; reject unknown values instead of falling back silently</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Phase 3: <code>/new</code> Slash Command</h3>\n<p>Platform-specific UX sugar that translates to control directives internally.</p>\n<pre><code>/new ws:~/projects/myapp model:claude-sonnet-4-20250514\ninvestigate the build failure\n</code></pre>\n<ol>\n<li>Register <code>/new</code> slash command on supported platforms (Discord, Slack)</li>\n<li>Command handler parses arguments into <code>[[key:value]]</code> directives</li>\n<li>Feeds through the same directive parser pipeline as inline directives</li>\n<li>Creates a new thread with the parsed session metadata</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Why <code>/new</code>:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Short, intuitive — matches &quot;new session/thread&quot; mental model</li>\n<li><strong>Typed arguments with platform UI</strong> — autocomplete for workspaces, dropdown for models, validation before submit. Users don't need to memorize exact model names or path syntax</li>\n<li>Does not conflict with other bots' commands</li>\n<li>Naturally implies &quot;session start&quot; — aligns with first-message-only rule</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Relationship to inline directives:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>/new</code> is <strong>transport sugar only</strong> — it MUST NOT introduce semantics beyond what <code>[[key:value]]</code> provides</li>\n<li>Users who prefer text-only (or are on platforms without slash commands) use <code>@Bot [[...]]</code> directly</li>\n<li>Both paths produce identical <code>SessionMetadata</code></li>\n<li><code>/new</code> and inline <code>[[...]]</code> cannot co-exist in the same message (a <code>/new</code> invocation IS the session's first message; there is no separate text body to embed inline directives)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Alternatives Considered</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Alternative</th>\n<th>Rejected Because</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>YAML front-matter in messages</td>\n<td>Visually heavy; unfamiliar to chat users</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Separate <code>/config</code> command before conversation</td>\n<td>Extra round-trip; breaks single-message session start</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Per-channel bot configuration</td>\n<td>Doesn't scale to ad-hoc project switching</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Environment variables per bot instance</td>\n<td>Requires multiple bot deployments</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/output-directives\">Output Directives</a> — existing <code>[[key:value]]</code> pattern for agent → platform</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/steering-design-guide\">Steering Design Guide</a> — how workspace steering files are structured</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Control Directives"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/custom-gateway",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Custom Gateway for Webhook-Based Platform Integration</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Superseded</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-04-22</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n<li><strong>Supersedes:</strong> Sections of <a href=\"/openab/adr/line-adapter\">ADR: LINE Adapter</a> (v2 Target Architecture)</li>\n<li><strong>Superseded by:</strong> <a href=\"/openab/adr/unified-binary\">ADR: Separate Binaries with Opt-In Unified Build</a></li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>⚠️ This ADR is partially superseded by the unified binary architecture.</strong>\nOpenAB now supports a single unified binary mode for simplified deployment\n(see <a href=\"/openab/adr/unified-binary\">ADR: Separate Binaries with Opt-In Unified Build</a>).\nWhile the unified binary is the recommended path for standard setups, the\nstandalone gateway architecture remains fully supported for deployments\nrequiring strict outbound-only network isolation for the OpenAB core.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. User Story &amp; Requirements</h2>\n<p>As an OpenAB operator, I want to connect webhook-based platforms (LINE, Telegram, WhatsApp, GitHub, CI/CD, monitoring, custom apps) to OAB without modifying OAB core, so that OAB remains a pure outbound-only agent runtime and new event sources are opt-in.</p>\n<p>As a platform integrator, I want to write a plugin/adapter for my platform and register it with the gateway, so that any webhook source can drive an OAB agent session without upstream code changes.</p>\n<p>Requirements:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>OAB core must remain outbound-only — no inbound ports, no TLS, no K8s Service</li>\n<li>The gateway is a separate, independently deployable service</li>\n<li>Adding a new webhook platform requires only a gateway plugin, zero OAB changes</li>\n<li>The gateway handles all platform-specific concerns: signature validation, payload parsing, credential management, reply delivery</li>\n<li>OAB connects to the gateway via WebSocket, same pattern as Discord/Slack</li>\n<li>The gateway is opt-in — Discord/Slack-only deployments don't need it</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. High-Level Design</h2>\n<h3>Architecture Overview</h3>\n<pre><code>                    External (inbound HTTPS)              Internal (cluster)\n                    ────────────────────────              ──────────────────\n\nLINE Platform ──POST──▶ ┌─────────────────────┐\nTelegram      ──POST──▶ │                     │\nGitHub Events ──POST──▶ │   Custom Gateway    │ ◀──WebSocket── OAB Pod\nCI/CD webhook ──POST──▶ │     :443/8080       │\nCustom app    ──POST──▶ │                     │\n                         └─────────────────────┘\n                                  │\nDiscord Gateway ◀──WebSocket───── OAB Pod  (unchanged, direct connection)\nSlack Socket    ◀──WebSocket───── OAB Pod  (unchanged, direct connection)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Inside the Gateway</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Custom Gateway                                     │\n│                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐          │\n│  │  LINE    │  │ Telegram │  │  GitHub  │  ...      │\n│  │ Adapter  │  │ Adapter  │  │ Adapter  │          │\n│  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘          │\n│       │              │              │               │\n│       ▼              ▼              ▼               │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐        │\n│  │         Event Normalizer                │        │\n│  │   platform payload → unified event      │        │\n│  └──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘        │\n│                     │                               │\n│                     ▼                               │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐        │\n│  │       WebSocket Server (:9090)          │        │\n│  │   OAB connects here as a client         │        │\n│  └──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘        │\n│                     │                               │\n│                     ▼                               │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐        │\n│  │         Reply Router                    │        │\n│  │   OAB reply → correct platform API      │        │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘        │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Message Flow</h3>\n<pre><code>Inbound (webhook → OAB):\n  1. External platform POSTs to gateway endpoint (e.g., /webhook/line)\n  2. Platform adapter validates signature, parses payload\n  3. Event Normalizer converts to unified event schema\n  4. Gateway pushes event to OAB over WebSocket\n  5. OAB routes to AdapterRouter → Session Pool → kiro-cli\n\nOutbound (OAB → platform):\n  1. Agent produces a response\n  2. OAB sends unified reply over WebSocket to gateway\n  3. Reply Router looks up platform + credentials for the target channel\n  4. Gateway calls the platform-specific API (LINE Push, Telegram sendMessage, etc.)\n  5. Delivery confirmation sent back to OAB over WebSocket\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Internal Event Schema</h2>\n<p>The contract between the gateway and OAB. All platform-specific details are normalized away before crossing this boundary.</p>\n<h3>Inbound Event (Gateway → OAB)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;schema&quot;: &quot;openab.gateway.event.v1&quot;,\n  &quot;event_id&quot;: &quot;evt_abc123&quot;,\n  &quot;timestamp&quot;: &quot;2026-04-22T08:00:00Z&quot;,\n  &quot;platform&quot;: &quot;line&quot;,\n  &quot;event_type&quot;: &quot;message&quot;,\n  &quot;channel&quot;: {\n    &quot;id&quot;: &quot;Cxyz789&quot;,\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;group&quot;,\n    &quot;thread_id&quot;: null\n  },\n  &quot;sender&quot;: {\n    &quot;id&quot;: &quot;Uabc123&quot;,\n    &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Alice&quot;,\n    &quot;display_name&quot;: &quot;Alice Chen&quot;,\n    &quot;is_bot&quot;: false\n  },\n  &quot;content&quot;: {\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot;,\n    &quot;text&quot;: &quot;explain VPC peering&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;mentions&quot;: [],\n  &quot;message_id&quot;: &quot;msg_456&quot;,\n  &quot;raw&quot;: {}\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Key fields in the base schema:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>channel.thread_id</code></strong>: thread identifier for platforms that support threads (Discord thread ID, Slack <code>thread_ts</code>). <code>null</code> for platforms without threads (LINE). OAB uses this for session key construction — without it, per-thread session isolation cannot work through the gateway.</li>\n<li><strong><code>mentions</code></strong>: array of mentioned entity IDs (users, bots). Required for @mention gating — the gateway adapter parses platform-specific mention formats and normalizes them here. Without it, OAB cannot determine whether the bot was mentioned, breaking the primary mitigation for LINE group chat noise and Discord/Slack trigger logic.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Outbound Reply (OAB → Gateway)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;schema&quot;: &quot;openab.gateway.reply.v1&quot;,\n  &quot;reply_to&quot;: &quot;evt_abc123&quot;,\n  &quot;platform&quot;: &quot;line&quot;,\n  &quot;channel&quot;: {\n    &quot;id&quot;: &quot;Cxyz789&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;content&quot;: {\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot;,\n    &quot;text&quot;: &quot;VPC peering is...&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Key fields in the outbound reply:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>reply_to</code></strong>: the <code>event_id</code> of the inbound <code>GatewayEvent</code> that triggered this reply. The gateway can use this for reply correlation — e.g., looking up a cached LINE reply token to prefer the free Reply API over the quota-consuming Push API. Empty string if the reply is not associated with a specific inbound event (e.g., cron-triggered messages).</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Design Principles for the Schema</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Platform field is metadata, not routing logic</strong> — OAB uses it for session key construction and sender context, but does not branch behavior on it</li>\n<li><strong>Content is polymorphic</strong> — <code>type</code> can be <code>text</code>, <code>image</code>, <code>file</code>, etc. Platforms that don't support a content type get a graceful fallback (e.g., image → URL link)</li>\n<li><strong><code>raw</code> is optional</strong> — the original platform payload, for adapters that need platform-specific fields. OAB core should never depend on <code>raw</code></li>\n<li><strong>Schema versioned</strong> — <code>openab.gateway.event.v1</code> allows backward-compatible evolution</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Schema Concerns Deferred to Protocol Spec</h3>\n<p>The following fields/concepts are known to be needed but are not fully defined in this ADR. They must be addressed in the protocol specification before v2 ships:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Concern</th>\n<th>Why It's Needed</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>conversation_key</code> / <code>session_hint</code></td>\n<td>Explicit session boundary signal from gateway, so OAB and GW don't independently derive session keys that drift apart. May generalize <code>thread_id</code> + <code>channel.id</code> into a single key.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>trace_id</code> / <code>correlation_id</code></td>\n<td>End-to-end tracing across inbound event → agent run → outbound reply → delivery ack</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>capabilities</code> / <code>delivery_constraints</code></td>\n<td>Platform feature flags (supports edit? reply? threads? attachments? max message length?) so OAB can do graceful fallback</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>reply_context</code></td>\n<td>Reply token, quote target, original message reference — not all platforms only need <code>channel.id</code> to deliver a reply</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>tenant</code> / <code>gateway_instance</code></td>\n<td>Multi-tenancy routing if a shared gateway serves multiple OAB instances</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Gateway Adapter Interface</h2>\n<p>Each platform adapter implements a common interface:</p>\n<pre><code>Adapter Interface:\n  validate(request)     → bool          # signature/auth check\n  parse(request)        → Event         # platform payload → unified event\n  send(reply)           → DeliveryAck   # unified reply → platform API call\n  health()              → Status        # platform connectivity check\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Adapter Registration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># gateway-config.yaml\nadapters:\n  line:\n    enabled: true\n    path: /webhook/line\n    credentials:\n      channel_secret: ${LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET}\n      channel_access_token: ${LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN}\n  telegram:\n    enabled: true\n    path: /webhook/telegram\n    credentials:\n      bot_token: ${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}\n  github:\n    enabled: true\n    path: /webhook/github\n    credentials:\n      webhook_secret: ${GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Adding a new platform = implement the adapter interface + add a config block. Zero OAB changes.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. What This Enables Beyond Chat</h2>\n<p>The gateway turns OAB from a &quot;chat bot&quot; into an <strong>event-driven agent platform</strong>:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Event Source</th>\n<th>Webhook Payload</th>\n<th>OAB Can Do</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>LINE / Telegram / WhatsApp</td>\n<td>User message</td>\n<td>AI coding assistant (existing)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>GitHub webhook</td>\n<td>PR opened, issue created</td>\n<td>Auto-triage, auto-review, auto-label</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>CI/CD (Actions, Jenkins)</td>\n<td>Build failed</td>\n<td>Analyze logs, suggest fix, notify</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Monitoring (PagerDuty, CloudWatch Alarm)</td>\n<td>Alert fired</td>\n<td>Runbook execution, incident response</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Custom application</td>\n<td>Any JSON payload</td>\n<td>User-defined agent workflows</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>The key insight: OAB's session pool and agent runtime are platform-agnostic. The only platform-specific code lives in gateway adapters. Once the gateway exists, any HTTP event source can drive an agent session.</p>\n<p>This also lowers the barrier to entry: triggering an agent no longer requires setting up a chat platform bot. A simple <code>curl -X POST https://gateway/webhook/custom -d '{&quot;text&quot;: &quot;run daily security scan&quot;}'</code> from a cron job is enough to start an agent session — no SDK, no bot token, no platform account needed.</p>\n<p>Scheduled triggers are supported natively via any external scheduler (K8s CronJob, EventBridge, GitHub Actions cron) — the gateway sees a regular HTTP POST with no knowledge of scheduling logic.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5a. Example Integrations</h2>\n<p>Two examples to illustrate how the gateway handles different event types — one chat platform, one non-chat event source.</p>\n<h3>Telegram: Chat-Style Webhook</h3>\n<pre><code>Telegram servers ──POST /webhook/telegram──▶ Gateway\n  │\n  ├─ Adapter: validate bot_token, parse Update JSON\n  ├─ Normalize: extract chat_id, sender, text, mentions\n  │\n  ▼\nGateway ──WebSocket──▶ OAB\n  event: { platform: &quot;telegram&quot;, channel.id: &quot;chat_12345&quot;,\n           sender.name: &quot;Bob&quot;, content.text: &quot;deploy to staging&quot; }\n  │\n  ▼\nOAB reply ──WebSocket──▶ Gateway\n  │\n  ├─ Reply Router: POST https://api.telegram.org/bot.../sendMessage\n  └─ { chat_id: &quot;chat_12345&quot;, text: &quot;Deploying now...&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p>Telegram is structurally similar to LINE — inbound webhook, no threads, push-style reply. The gateway adapter handles Telegram-specific auth and payload format; OAB sees the same unified event schema.</p>\n<h3>GitHub: Non-Chat Event Source</h3>\n<pre><code>GitHub ──POST /webhook/github──▶ Gateway\n  │  (X-Hub-Signature-256 header)\n  │\n  ├─ Adapter: validate HMAC signature, parse pull_request.opened event\n  ├─ Normalize: repo as channel, PR author as sender, PR title+body as content\n  │\n  ▼\nGateway ──WebSocket──▶ OAB\n  event: { platform: &quot;github&quot;, channel.id: &quot;openabdev/openab&quot;,\n           event_type: &quot;pull_request&quot;, sender.name: &quot;juntinyeh&quot;,\n           content.text: &quot;PR #521: Feature/line — adds LINE adapter...&quot; }\n  │\n  ▼\nOAB reply ──WebSocket──▶ Gateway\n  │\n  ├─ Reply Router: POST https://api.github.com/repos/.../issues/521/comments\n  └─ { body: &quot;Auto-triage: this PR adds a new adapter...&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p>GitHub shows the gateway handling a non-chat event. The adapter maps repo → channel, PR author → sender, and PR description → content. OAB processes it like any other message. The reply goes back as a PR comment via GitHub API.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Architectural Differences from v1</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>v1 (LINE in OAB)</th>\n<th>Custom Gateway</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>OAB inbound ports</td>\n<td>Yes (webhook :8080)</td>\n<td>None — pure outbound</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Platform-specific code in OAB</td>\n<td><code>line.rs</code>, <code>config.rs</code> changes</td>\n<td>Zero — all in gateway</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Adding a new platform</td>\n<td>Modify OAB core, new adapter in Rust</td>\n<td>Gateway plugin only, OAB untouched</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>TLS / K8s Service for OAB</td>\n<td>Required for LINE</td>\n<td>Not required — gateway handles it</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Deployment for DC/Slack-only users</td>\n<td>Carry LINE code even if unused</td>\n<td>Gateway not deployed, zero overhead</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Credential management</td>\n<td>OAB holds LINE tokens</td>\n<td>Gateway holds all webhook credentials</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Scaling webhook handling</td>\n<td>Coupled to OAB pod</td>\n<td>Gateway scales independently</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Open Design Questions</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Question</th>\n<th>Options</th>\n<th>Impact</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>WebSocket direction</strong></td>\n<td>OAB connects to GW (OAB is client) vs GW connects to OAB (GW is client)</td>\n<td>OAB-as-client is simpler — matches Discord/Slack pattern, OAB initiates all connections</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Multi-tenancy</strong></td>\n<td>One GW per OAB instance vs shared GW serving multiple OAB instances</td>\n<td>Shared GW needs routing table; per-instance is simpler for v2</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Reconnect / backpressure</strong></td>\n<td>What happens when OAB ↔ GW WebSocket drops?</td>\n<td>Need reconnect with event replay or at-least-once delivery</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Event ordering</strong></td>\n<td>Strict per-channel ordering vs best-effort</td>\n<td>Strict ordering requires per-channel queuing in GW</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Plugin distribution</strong></td>\n<td>Built-in adapters vs dynamic loading vs separate binaries</td>\n<td>Built-in for v2, plugin mechanism for v3</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Rollout Plan</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n<th>Deliverable</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v1 (now)</strong></td>\n<td>LINE adapter inside OAB</td>\n<td>PR #521 — unblocks LINE users</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v2</strong></td>\n<td>Standalone gateway + OAB generic gateway adapter + LINE migrated out</td>\n<td>Gateway service, LINE adapter, internal event schema, OAB connects via WebSocket</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v3</strong></td>\n<td>Multi-platform gateway</td>\n<td>Telegram, GitHub, custom adapters</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v4</strong></td>\n<td>Plugin / distribution model</td>\n<td>Third-party adapters without forking gateway</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Migration Path from v1 to v2</h3>\n<p>LINE only allows a single webhook URL per channel, so live dual-run (v1 and v2 receiving the same production traffic simultaneously) is not possible. Validation must use a separate test channel or synthetic replay.</p>\n<pre><code>Phase 1 — Deploy gateway alongside v1 OAB:\n  OAB Pod [LINE adapter built-in]  ◀──POST── LINE Platform   (v1, production traffic)\n  OAB Pod [gateway adapter]  ──WS──▶  Gateway Pod [LINE adapter]  (v2, deployed but idle)\n\nPhase 2 — Validate v2 path (staging / synthetic):\n  Use a separate LINE test channel (or synthetic HTTP replay) pointed at the gateway\n  Confirm: signature validation, session routing, reply delivery all work\n  Production traffic still flows through v1\n  Define go/no-go criteria before executing Phase 3\n  (e.g., N messages processed, zero signature failures, reply latency within threshold)\n\nPhase 3 — Cut over (atomic switch):\n  Disable v1 LINE adapter in OAB config\n  Point production LINE webhook URL to gateway endpoint\n  OAB now receives LINE events only through gateway WebSocket\n\nPhase 4 — Clean up:\n  Remove line.rs from OAB codebase\n  Remove LINE-specific config/secrets from OAB\n  OAB is back to outbound-only\n</code></pre>\n<p>Key constraint: Phase 3 (cut-over) must be atomic per platform — LINE's single webhook URL in the Developers Console is the routing switch. There is no gradual traffic split; it's all-v1 or all-v2.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Consequences</h2>\n<h3>Positive</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>OAB core permanently stays outbound-only — simpler security model, no attack surface</li>\n<li>New webhook platforms are opt-in and require zero OAB changes</li>\n<li>Gateway can be independently scaled, versioned, and deployed</li>\n<li>Opens OAB to non-chat event sources (GitHub, CI/CD, monitoring)</li>\n<li>Gateway is potentially useful as a standalone open-source project beyond OAB</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Negative</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Additional service to deploy and operate (gateway pod)</li>\n<li>Internal WebSocket protocol adds a layer of complexity and a potential failure point</li>\n<li>Reply path through gateway adds one network hop of latency (negligible in-cluster)</li>\n<li>Gateway becomes a credential store for all webhook platforms — single point of compromise if breached</li>\n<li>Event schema design is a long-term commitment — breaking changes affect all adapters</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Credential Store Security Risks</h3>\n<p>The gateway holding all platform credentials is the correct architectural choice (it keeps OAB platform-agnostic), but concentrates risk:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Credential concentration</strong>: a gateway breach exposes all platform tokens. Mitigate with per-adapter secret isolation (separate K8s Secrets, not one shared Secret).</li>\n<li><strong>Audit and rotation</strong>: all credential access must be auditable. Tokens must support rotation without gateway downtime.</li>\n<li><strong>Least privilege</strong>: each adapter should only have access to its own platform credentials, not other adapters'.</li>\n<li><strong>OAB ↔ GW transport security</strong>: the internal WebSocket connection must use mTLS or equivalent authentication. Without it, any pod in the cluster can impersonate OAB and send replies through the gateway.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Compliance</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>OAB outbound-only</strong>: after adoption of the custom gateway architecture, new platform integrations must not add inbound platform-traffic handling to OAB core unless explicitly approved by a superseding ADR.</li>\n<li><strong>Event schema stability</strong>: the <code>openab.gateway.event.v1</code> schema is currently a draft envelope for v2 development. The protocol spec must finalize all required fields (including deferred concerns in Section 3) before the schema is declared stable. Once declared stable, breaking changes require a version bump (<code>v2</code>) and a migration path.</li>\n<li><strong>Credential isolation</strong>: platform credentials (tokens, secrets) must reside in the gateway, not in OAB. OAB must not hold or access platform-specific authentication material.</li>\n<li><strong>Adapter interface compliance</strong>: all gateway adapters must implement <code>validate</code>, <code>parse</code>, <code>send</code>, and <code>health</code>. Adapters that skip signature validation must be explicitly flagged as insecure.</li>\n<li><strong>Webhook correctness</strong>: all adapters must validate signatures against exact raw request body bytes, per the constraints defined in <a href=\"/openab/adr/line-adapter\">ADR: LINE Adapter</a> Compliance #1.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Version:</strong> 0.2</li>\n<li><strong>Changelog:</strong>\n<ul>\n<li>0.2 (2026-06-29): Superseded — unified binary is now the recommended default; standalone gateway remains supported for strict outbound-only isolation</li>\n<li>0.1 (2026-04-22): Initial proposed version</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/line-adapter\">ADR: LINE Messaging API Adapter</a> — v1 LINE adapter design and v2 bridge concept that led to this ADR</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions.html\">Documenting Architecture Decisions</a> — Michael Nygard (2011)</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://adr.github.io/\">ADR GitHub Organization</a> — Community hub for ADR templates and tooling</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/architectural-decision-records/adr-process.html\">AWS Prescriptive Guidance — Using ADRs</a> — ADR lifecycle and compliance sections</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Custom Gateway for Webhook-Based Platform Integration"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/ecs-control-plane",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: ECS Control Plane (CRD + Operator Pattern on ECS)</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-18</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @pahud.hsieh</li>\n<li><strong>Related:</strong> <a href=\"/openab/adr/multi-platform-adapters\">Multi-Platform Adapters</a>, <a href=\"/openab/adr/basic-cronjob\">Basic CronJob</a></li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Motivation</h2>\n<p>OpenAB currently deploys on Kubernetes using Helm charts. While K8s provides a mature operator pattern (CRD + Controller), many teams prefer or require <strong>Amazon ECS</strong> for its operational simplicity and tighter AWS integration.</p>\n<p>We want to bring the same declarative, self-healing deployment model to ECS:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Operators declare desired state in YAML manifests (analogous to CRDs)</li>\n<li>A controller reconciles desired state against actual ECS resources</li>\n<li>OAB instances + arbitrary backends are deployed and maintained automatically</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This enables a &quot;GitOps for ECS&quot; workflow where pushing a YAML change triggers the controller to converge the cluster to the new desired state.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Design Overview</h2>\n<pre><code>┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  ECS Control Plane (runs as ECS Service)             │\n│                                                      │\n│  ┌────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  │\n│  │ State Store│  │  Reconciler  │  │  ECS API /  │  │\n│  │   (S3)     │◄─│  Controller  │─►│  CloudMap   │  │\n│  │            │  │              │  │             │  │\n│  └────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └─────────────┘  │\n│                        ▲                             │\n│                        │ events / poll               │\n│                        ▼                             │\n│                 ┌──────────────┐                     │\n│                 │ S3 Events /  │                     │\n│                 │ EventBridge  │                     │\n│                 └──────────────┘                     │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Core Loop (Reconciliation)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Load all YAML manifests from S3 (desired state)</li>\n<li>Describe current ECS services/tasks (observed state)</li>\n<li>Compute diff (compare <code>metadata.generation</code> vs <code>status.observedGeneration</code>)</li>\n<li>Apply changes: create, update, or delete ECS resources</li>\n<li>Write status back to S3 (separate prefix), set <code>status.observedGeneration = metadata.generation</code></li>\n<li>Sleep / wait for next event</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Manifest Schema</h2>\n<h3>API Identity (fixed)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>apiVersion</code></td>\n<td><code>oab.dev/v1</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>kind</code></td>\n<td><code>OABService</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>All examples in this ADR use this identity. No other combinations (<code>openab.dev/v1</code>, <code>AgentDeployment</code>) are valid.</p>\n<h3>Full Example</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: oab.dev/v1\nkind: OABService\nmetadata:\n  name: my-agent\n  namespace: prod\n  generation: 4                    # incremented by oabctl on each apply\nspec:\n  replicas: 1\n  capacityProvider: FARGATE        # FARGATE (default) or FARGATE_SPOT\n  cpu: 256                         # vCPU units (256 = 0.25 vCPU)\n  memory: 512                      # MB\n  taskDefinition:\n    image: 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/openab:latest\n  bootstrapFrom: s3://oab-state/agents/my-agent/latest.tar.gz\n  secrets:\n    - name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN\n      source: ssm\n      path: /oab/my-agent/discord-token\n    - name: LLM_API_KEY\n      source: secretsmanager\n      arn: arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123:secret:oab/my-agent/llm-key\n  networking:\n    subnets: [subnet-abc, subnet-def]\n    securityGroups: [sg-123]\n    assignPublicIp: false\n  config:\n    agent:\n      name: my-agent\n      backend: bedrock\n      model: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514\n    discord:\n      enabled: true\n      botId: &quot;123456789&quot;\n      guildId: &quot;987654321&quot;\n      channelIds: [&quot;111111111&quot;]\n    steering:\n      source: s3\n      bucket: oab-steering\n      prefix: agents/my-agent/\n    memory:\n      backend: s3\n      bucket: oab-memory\n      prefix: agents/my-agent/\n    tools:\n      github: { enabled: true }\n      web: { enabled: true }\nstatus:\n  phase: Running                   # Pending | Running | Failed | Terminating\n  observedGeneration: 4            # last generation the controller reconciled\n  taskArns:\n    - arn:aws:ecs:us-east-1:123456789012:task/cluster/abc123\n  lastReconciled: &quot;2026-05-18T22:50:00Z&quot;\n  conditions:\n    - type: Available\n      status: &quot;True&quot;\n      lastTransitionTime: &quot;2026-05-18T22:50:00Z&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Key Fields</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>metadata.generation</code></td>\n<td>Monotonically increasing counter, bumped by <code>oabctl apply</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.capacityProvider</code></td>\n<td><code>FARGATE</code> (on-demand) or <code>FARGATE_SPOT</code> (up to 70% savings, tolerates interruption)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.cpu</code> / <code>spec.memory</code></td>\n<td>Maps to ECS task definition (must be valid Fargate combination)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.taskDefinition.image</code></td>\n<td>Container image</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.bootstrapFrom</code></td>\n<td>S3 path to mutable state archive (memory, knowledge base — <strong>no secrets</strong>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.secrets</code></td>\n<td>Per-agent secret references (SSM / Secrets Manager)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.config</code></td>\n<td>Structured agent config; controller renders to <code>config.toml</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.networking</code></td>\n<td>ECS awsvpc configuration</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>status.observedGeneration</code></td>\n<td>Last generation the controller successfully reconciled</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Replicas Semantics</h3>\n<p>OAB agents are <strong>single-instance</strong> by design — each agent holds one adapter connection (WebSocket gateway for Discord/Telegram/Slack). There is no load balancing across agent replicas.</p>\n<p><strong>Rules:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>replicas: 1</code> — the only valid value</li>\n<li>Controller <strong>rejects</strong> <code>replicas &gt; 1</code> at validation time</li>\n<li>Scaling is horizontal by deploying <strong>more agents</strong> (each with its own bot token), not by replicating one agent</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Fleet Provisioning (<code>OABFleet</code>)</h3>\n<p>Enterprise scenario: provision 10-20 agents in one apply. Controller handles everything including Discord Bot registration.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: oab.dev/v1\nkind: OABFleet\nmetadata:\n  name: enterprise-team\n  namespace: prod\nspec:\n  defaults:\n    capacityProvider: FARGATE_SPOT\n    cpu: 512\n    memory: 1024\n    taskDefinition:\n      image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:latest\n    networking:\n      subnets: [subnet-abc, subnet-def]\n      securityGroups: [sg-oab]\n    discord:\n      enabled: true               # all agents use Discord\n  agents:\n    - name: kiro-01\n      config: { agent: { backend: kiro } }\n    - name: kiro-02\n      config: { agent: { backend: kiro } }\n    - name: kiro-03\n      config: { agent: { backend: kiro } }\n    - name: codex-01\n      config: { agent: { backend: codex } }\n      cpu: 1024\n      memory: 2048               # override defaults\n    - name: codex-02\n      config: { agent: { backend: codex } }\n      cpu: 1024\n      memory: 2048\n    - name: gemini-01\n      config: { agent: { backend: gemini } }\n    - name: gemini-02\n      config: { agent: { backend: gemini } }\n    - name: gemini-03\n      config: { agent: { backend: gemini } }\n    - name: gemini-04\n      config: { agent: { backend: gemini } }\n    - name: gemini-05\n      config: { agent: { backend: gemini } }\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Discord Bot Provisioning Flow</h3>\n<p>Since Discord does not offer a public API for Bot creation, the actual flow for fleet provisioning is:</p>\n<pre><code>Pre-requisite (manual, one-time per agent):\n  → Create Bot in Discord Developer Portal\n  → Store token in SSM: /oab/{namespace}/{name}/discord-token\n  → Note the OAuth2 invite URL\n\noabctl apply -f fleet.yaml\n  │\n  │  For each agent:\n  ├─ 1. Validate spec + verify secret exists in SSM\n  ├─ 2. Render config.toml → S3 artifact (immutable, per generation)\n  ├─ 3. Register ECS TaskDefinition (pinned to config artifact + secrets)\n  ├─ 4. Create ECS Service (desiredCount=1)\n  └─ 5. Write status (phase=Running)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Apply output:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">$ oabctl apply -f fleet.yaml\n\n✓ kiro-01   provisioned (ECS service created, task running)\n✓ kiro-02   provisioned (ECS service created, task running)\n✓ kiro-03   provisioned (ECS service created, task running)\n✓ codex-01  provisioned (ECS service created, task running)\n✓ codex-02  provisioned (ECS service created, task running)\n✓ gemini-01 provisioned (ECS service created, task running)\n...\n\n10 agents provisioned.\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>User's manual steps (one-time):</strong> create bots in Discord Developer Portal, store tokens, add bots to server via OAuth URL.</p>\n<h3>Responsibility Model</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Layer</th>\n<th>Responsibility</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>oabctl</code> / Controller</td>\n<td>Desired state: create ECS Services; <strong>observe</strong> ECS task/service status → write back to <code>status/</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>ECS</td>\n<td>Runtime health: task dies → auto-restart (desiredCount=1)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>User</td>\n<td>One-time: create bots in Discord Developer Portal, add to server via OAuth URL</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>The controller does <strong>not</strong> restart tasks — ECS handles that. But the controller <strong>does</strong> observe ECS service/task/deployment status on each reconcile cycle and writes it back to <code>status/{ns}/{name}.json</code>. This enables <code>oabctl get</code>, <code>oabctl wait --for=Available</code>, and <code>status.phase</code> / <code>status.conditions</code> to work.</p>\n<h3>Prerequisites for Auto-Registration</h3>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>⚠️ Note:</strong> Discord does not provide a public API to programmatically create Bot Applications. <code>autoRegister</code> is a <strong>future research item</strong> pending Discord API changes or partnership access. For now, bot credentials must be pre-created manually in the Discord Developer Portal.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p><strong>Phase 1/2 approach:</strong> Each agent's bot token is pre-created and stored in SSM/Secrets Manager. The <code>OABFleet</code> spec references existing credentials:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">spec:\n  agents:\n    - name: kiro-01\n      config: { agent: { backend: kiro } }\n      secrets:\n        - name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN\n          source: ssm\n          path: /oab/kiro-01/discord-token   # pre-created\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Future (if Discord API allows):</strong> <code>autoRegister: true</code> would automate Bot creation. This requires a separate research ADR.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Multi-Runtime Support (ECS + K8s)</h2>\n<p>The same YAML manifest can deploy to <strong>both ECS and Kubernetes</strong>. The spec is platform-agnostic; platform-specific details live in an optional <code>platform:</code> overlay.</p>\n<h3>Design Principle</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────┐\n│  oab.dev/v1 YAML    │  ← one spec, platform-agnostic core\n└──────────┬──────────┘\n           │\n    ┌──────┴──────┐\n    ▼             ▼\n┌────────┐   ┌────────┐\n│  ECS   │   │  K8s   │\n│Controller│   │Operator│\n└────┬───┘   └────┬───┘\n     ▼             ▼\n  ECS Service   Deployment + ConfigMap + ExternalSecret\n</code></pre>\n<p>Each controller reads the core spec and its own <code>platform:</code> overlay, ignoring the other.</p>\n<h3>Spec with Platform Overlay</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: oab.dev/v1\nkind: OABService\nmetadata:\n  name: chaodu\n  namespace: prod\nspec:\n  # Core (cross-platform)\n  cpu: 512\n  memory: 1024\n  config:\n    agent: { backend: kiro }\n    discord: { enabled: true, botId: &quot;123&quot;
