}\n  secrets:\n    - name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN\n      source: ssm\n      path: /oab/chaodu/discord-token\n\n  # Platform-specific (each controller reads only its own key)\n  platform:\n    ecs:\n      capacityProvider: FARGATE_SPOT\n      executionRole: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/oab-task-execution\n      taskRole: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/oab-chaodu-task\n      networking:\n        subnets: [subnet-abc, subnet-def]\n        securityGroups: [sg-oab]\n        assignPublicIp: false\n    k8s:\n      nodeSelector: { node.kubernetes.io/capacity-type: spot }\n      serviceAccount: oab-agent\n      storageClass: gp3\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Translation Table</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Core Spec</th>\n<th>ECS Controller</th>\n<th>K8s Operator</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cpu: 512</code></td>\n<td>TaskDef <code>cpu=512</code></td>\n<td><code>resources.requests.cpu: 500m</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>memory: 1024</code></td>\n<td>TaskDef <code>memory=1024</code></td>\n<td><code>resources.requests.memory: 1Gi</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.config</code></td>\n<td>Render → S3 artifact → startup wrapper</td>\n<td>Render → ConfigMap → volume mount</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>spec.secrets[].source: ssm</code></td>\n<td>ECS native <code>secrets</code> field</td>\n<td>ExternalSecret → K8s Secret</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform.ecs.capacityProvider</code></td>\n<td>Fargate capacity provider</td>\n<td><em>(ignored)</em></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform.ecs.executionRole</code></td>\n<td>ECS task execution role</td>\n<td><em>(ignored)</em></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform.ecs.taskRole</code></td>\n<td>ECS task role</td>\n<td><em>(ignored)</em></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform.k8s.nodeSelector</code></td>\n<td><em>(ignored)</em></td>\n<td>Pod nodeSelector</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Rules</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>platform:</code> is optional. If omitted, controller uses its own defaults.</li>\n<li>Controller <strong>strict-validates</strong> its own platform key (e.g., ECS controller rejects invalid <code>platform.ecs.*</code> fields with an error).</li>\n<li>Controller <strong>ignores</strong> other platform keys entirely (ECS controller skips <code>platform.k8s</code>, and vice versa).</li>\n<li>Core spec fields (<code>cpu</code>, <code>memory</code>, <code>config</code>, <code>secrets</code>) are mandatory and cross-platform.</li>\n<li><code>OABFleet</code> also supports <code>platform:</code> at both <code>defaults</code> and per-agent level.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Phase Plan</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Phase 1</strong>: ECS controller only. <code>platform.ecs</code> supported, <code>platform.k8s</code> ignored.</li>\n<li><strong>Phase 3</strong>: K8s operator reads same manifests (from S3 or as native CRD). Shared schema, different runtime.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Config Delivery Model</h2>\n<p>The controller does <strong>not</strong> mount config into containers (ECS/Fargate has no shared volume equivalent to K8s ConfigMap). Instead:</p>\n<h3>Flow</h3>\n<pre><code>oabctl apply -f agent.yaml\n  → writes manifest to S3 (manifests/{ns}/{name}.yaml, generation incremented)\n\nController reconcile:\n  → reads spec.config from manifest\n  → renders config.toml\n  → writes to s3://oab-control-plane/artifacts/{ns}/{name}/{generation}/config.toml (immutable)\n  → registers new ECS TaskDefinition with env CONFIG_ARTIFACT_PATH pinned to this generation\n  → updates ECS Service (rolling deployment)\n\nECS Task startup (entrypoint wrapper):\n  → s3:GetObject ${CONFIG_ARTIFACT_PATH} → /home/agent/config.toml\n  → s3:GetObject ${BOOTSTRAP_FROM} → tar xzf → /home/agent/ (mutable state only)\n  → exec openab\n</code></pre>\n<p>Config artifacts are <strong>immutable per generation</strong> — once written, never overwritten. During rolling updates, old tasks keep fetching their pinned generation while new tasks use the new one.</p>\n<h3>Entrypoint Wrapper</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">#!/bin/bash\nset -e\n# 1. Restore mutable state FIRST (memory, knowledge base)\nif [ -n &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_FROM&quot; ]; then\n  aws s3 cp &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_FROM&quot; /tmp/bootstrap.tar.gz\n  tar xzf /tmp/bootstrap.tar.gz -C /home/agent/\n  rm /tmp/bootstrap.tar.gz\nfi\n# 2. Download controller-rendered config LAST (overwrites any config.toml from archive)\naws s3 cp &quot;$CONFIG_ARTIFACT_PATH&quot; /home/agent/config.toml\nexec /usr/local/bin/openab\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Order matters:</strong> bootstrap archive is restored first, then the controller-rendered <code>config.toml</code> overwrites any stale config from the archive. <code>oabctl snapshot</code> must exclude <code>config.toml</code> from the archive (it's controller-managed, not user state).</p>\n<h3>What Goes Where</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Content</th>\n<th>Location</th>\n<th>Managed By</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>config.toml</code></td>\n<td>S3 artifact (controller renders)</td>\n<td><code>spec.config</code> in manifest</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Secrets (bot tokens, API keys)</td>\n<td>SSM / Secrets Manager</td>\n<td><code>spec.secrets</code> in manifest</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Memory / knowledge base</td>\n<td><code>bootstrapFrom</code> archive</td>\n<td><code>oabctl snapshot</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Steering files</td>\n<td>S3 (referenced in config.toml)</td>\n<td>Separate steering bucket</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Secrets never go in the bootstrap archive.</strong> The archive contains only mutable runtime state that the agent accumulates over time.</p>\n<h3>IAM Requirements (Task Execution Role)</h3>\n<p>The ECS task execution role (<code>platform.ecs.executionRole</code>) must have:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n  &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;s3:GetObject&quot;],\n  &quot;Resource&quot;: [\n    &quot;arn:aws:s3:::oab-control-plane/artifacts/${namespace}/${name}/*&quot;,\n    &quot;arn:aws:s3:::oab-state/agents/${name}/*&quot;\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>This allows the startup wrapper to download the controller-rendered <code>config.toml</code> and the bootstrap archive.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Per-Agent Secret Injection</h2>\n<p>Each agent/bot has its <strong>own</strong> credentials — no token sharing between agents.</p>\n<h3>Design Principles</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Each <code>OABService</code> owns its secrets (1:1 mapping)</li>\n<li>Controller never touches secret values — it only wires references into ECS Task Definitions</li>\n<li>ECS native <code>secrets</code> field handles injection at runtime</li>\n<li>IAM scoping ensures each task role can only read its own secret path</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Spec</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">spec:\n  secrets:\n    - name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN\n      source: ssm\n      path: /oab/chaodu/discord-token\n    - name: LLM_API_KEY\n      source: secretsmanager\n      arn: arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123:secret:oab/chaodu/llm-key\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Controller Behavior</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Deploy</strong> — maps <code>spec.secrets</code> to ECS TaskDefinition <code>secrets</code> field:\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;secrets&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot;, &quot;valueFrom&quot;: &quot;/oab/chaodu/discord-token&quot; },\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;LLM_API_KEY&quot;, &quot;valueFrom&quot;: &quot;arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123:secret:oab/chaodu/llm-key&quot; }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li><strong>IAM</strong> — task execution role scoped to the agent's secret path:\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n  &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;ssm:GetParameters&quot;, &quot;secretsmanager:GetSecretValue&quot;],\n  &quot;Resource&quot;: [\n    &quot;arn:aws:ssm:*:*:parameter/oab/chaodu/*&quot;,\n    &quot;arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:oab/chaodu/*&quot;\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Secret Rotation Lifecycle</h3>\n<pre><code>1. Operator rotates secret in SSM/Secrets Manager (manual or auto-rotation)\n2. Controller detects rotation:\n   - Option A: spec.secrets[].autoRestart: true → controller forces new deployment\n   - Option B: operator runs `oabctl restart my-agent`\n3. ECS launches new task → new task fetches fresh secret value at startup\n4. Old task drains and stops (ECS rolling update)\n5. Controller updates status:\n   - conditions[].type: SecretsRefreshed\n   - conditions[].lastTransitionTime: &lt;now&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Failure handling:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>If new task fails to start (bad secret value), ECS circuit breaker stops the rollout</li>\n<li>Controller sets <code>status.phase: Failed</code>, <code>conditions[].type: SecretInjectionFailed</code></li>\n<li>Old task remains running (ECS deployment circuit breaker preserves last healthy state)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. State Store Design (S3-Only)</h2>\n<pre><code>s3://oab-control-plane/\n  ├── manifests/{namespace}/{name}.yaml     ← desired state (oabctl writes)\n  ├── status/{namespace}/{name}.json        ← observed state (controller writes)\n  └── artifacts/{namespace}/{name}/{generation}/  ← immutable config per generation\n        └── config.toml\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Concern</th>\n<th>Mechanism</th>\n<th>Rationale</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Desired state</td>\n<td><code>manifests/</code> prefix</td>\n<td>Human-readable, git-syncable, versioned via S3 versioning</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Status</td>\n<td><code>status/</code> prefix</td>\n<td>Controller writes after each reconcile cycle</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Config artifacts</td>\n<td><code>artifacts/</code> prefix</td>\n<td>Controller-rendered config.toml for task startup</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Generation tracking</td>\n<td><code>metadata.generation</code> in manifest YAML</td>\n<td>Explicit counter, not tied to S3 VersionId</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Change detection</td>\n<td>S3 Event Notifications → EventBridge (Phase 2)</td>\n<td>Phase 1 uses polling</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Consistency</td>\n<td>S3 strong read-after-write</td>\n<td>Sufficient for single-controller</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Optimistic locking</td>\n<td>S3 conditional writes (If-None-Match / ETag)</td>\n<td>Prevents concurrent <code>oabctl apply</code> conflicts</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Generation vs S3 VersionId</h3>\n<p>S3 VersionId is an opaque string — not suitable for comparing &quot;which is newer.&quot; Instead:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>metadata.generation</code> is an explicit integer, incremented by <code>oabctl apply</code></li>\n<li><code>status.observedGeneration</code> records the last generation the controller reconciled</li>\n<li>Controller skips reconcile if <code>observedGeneration == generation</code> (no-op)</li>\n<li>Stale status writes are detected: if status.observedGeneration &lt; manifest.generation, the status is outdated</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Delete Semantics (Phase 2)</h3>\n<p>Phase 1: <code>oabctl delete</code> removes the manifest from S3; controller detects absence and tears down ECS resources.</p>\n<p>Phase 2: Proper deletion with finalizers:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>oabctl delete</code> sets <code>metadata.deletionTimestamp</code> in the manifest (tombstone)</li>\n<li>Controller runs finalizers (drain connections, cleanup CloudMap, remove artifacts)</li>\n<li>Controller removes manifest and status objects only after all finalizers complete</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Controller Upgrade Strategy</h2>\n<p>The controller runs as a single-replica ECS Service.</p>\n<h3>Phase 1 (acceptable brief gap)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Controller's own ECS Service config\ndeploymentConfiguration:\n  minimumHealthyPercent: 0      # allow old to stop before new starts\n  maximumPercent: 100\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>ECS rolling update: stop old → start new</li>\n<li>Brief reconciliation gap (30-60s) during upgrade</li>\n<li>No in-flight reconcile is lost — next cycle picks up any drift</li>\n<li>Acceptable for Phase 1 because reconcile is idempotent</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Phase 2 (zero-downtime)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>DynamoDB-based leader election (two controller replicas)</li>\n<li>Active/standby: standby takes over within seconds if active fails health check</li>\n<li>Version skew handling: new controller must handle manifests written by old <code>oabctl</code> versions (schema backward compatibility)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Rollback</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Controller image is pinned in its own ECS TaskDefinition</li>\n<li>Rollback = <code>aws ecs update-service --task-definition &lt;previous-revision&gt;</code></li>\n<li>Controller state is in S3 (stateless process), so rollback is safe</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. CLI UX (<code>oabctl</code>)</h2>\n<h3>Core Commands</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">oabctl apply -f agent.yaml          # declare/update desired state\noabctl get oabservice               # list all services + status\noabctl get oabservice my-agent      # single service detail\noabctl delete oabservice my-agent   # remove (Phase 1: immediate; Phase 2: finalizer)\noabctl diff -f agent.yaml           # show local vs remote diff\noabctl logs my-agent                # shortcut to ECS task logs (CloudWatch)\noabctl restart my-agent             # force new deployment (pick up rotated secrets)\noabctl snapshot my-agent            # capture runtime state → bootstrapFrom archive\noabctl wait my-agent --for=Available # block until condition met\n</code></pre>\n<h3><code>apply</code> Semantics</h3>\n<pre><code>$ oabctl apply -f prod/my-agent.yaml\n\n✓ Schema validated (oab.dev/v1 OABService)\n✓ Replicas check passed (replicas=1)\n✓ Uploaded to s3://oab-control-plane/manifests/prod/my-agent.yaml\n✓ Generation: 3 → 4\n⏳ Waiting for reconciliation...\n✓ Service my-agent reconciled (observedGeneration=4, 1/1 tasks running)\n</code></pre>\n<h3><code>diff</code> Granularity</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">oabctl diff -f agent.yaml              # spec-only: local YAML vs remote manifest\noabctl diff -f agent.yaml --rendered   # rendered: show generated config.toml diff\noabctl diff -f agent.yaml --status     # include status comparison\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Implementation</h3>\n<p><code>oabctl</code> talks directly to S3 via AWS SDK. No API server needed. Auth is standard IAM (role, profile, env vars). Config stored in <code>~/.oabctl/config</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[default]\nregion = &quot;us-east-1&quot;\nbucket = &quot;oab-control-plane&quot;\ncluster = &quot;oab-prod&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. Phase Scope</h2>\n<h3>Phase 1 — MVP (target)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>In Scope</th>\n<th>Out of Scope</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>S3 manifest store (versioning enabled)</td>\n<td>EventBridge triggers</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Single-instance controller (poll every 30s)</td>\n<td>Multi-replica controller / leader election</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>oabctl apply</code> / <code>oabctl get</code></td>\n<td><code>oabctl delete</code> with finalizers</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Controller renders config.toml → S3 artifact</td>\n<td>DynamoDB state store</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>ECS service create / update</td>\n<td>Rollback (<code>oabctl rollback</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Startup wrapper downloads config + bootstrap</td>\n<td>EFS / shared volumes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>metadata.generation</code> / <code>status.observedGeneration</code></td>\n<td>Multi-region</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Per-agent secrets via SSM/SM</td>\n<td>Auto-rotation detection</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Replicas validation (reject &gt;1)</td>\n<td>Auto-scaling policies</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Phase 2</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>OABFleet</code> kind + Discord <code>autoRegister</code> (batch Bot provisioning)</li>\n<li>Event-driven triggers (S3 → EventBridge → controller)</li>\n<li><code>oabctl delete</code> with tombstone + finalizers</li>\n<li><code>oabctl diff</code>, <code>oabctl logs</code>, <code>oabctl restart</code></li>\n<li>DynamoDB for leader election (active/standby controller)</li>\n<li>Secret auto-rotation detection + auto-restart</li>\n<li>Rollback via generation history</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Phase 3</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>K8s Operator</strong> — same <code>oab.dev/v1</code> schema consumed as native CRD; <code>platform.k8s</code> overlay</li>\n<li>Multi-region (controller per region, S3 cross-region replication)</li>\n<li>Dependency graph (service A depends on service B)</li>\n<li>Auto-scaling policies in manifest spec</li>\n<li>GitOps integration (GitHub Actions → <code>oabctl apply</code> on push)</li>\n<li>Schema versioning + migration tooling</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>11. Alternatives Considered</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Alternative</th>\n<th>Why not chosen</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>AWS Proton</td>\n<td>Opinionated, limited customization for OAB-specific logic</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>AWS Copilot</td>\n<td>Good for simple apps, no custom reconciliation loop</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>CDK Pipelines</td>\n<td>Deployment tool, not a runtime controller with drift detection</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Step Functions orchestrator</td>\n<td>Stateless execution model, no continuous reconciliation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Run K8s anyway (EKS)</td>\n<td>Valid but adds operational overhead for teams that chose ECS</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>DynamoDB as primary store</td>\n<td>Adds infra; S3 sufficient for single-controller Phase 1</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>12. Open Questions</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Multi-region</strong> — single controller per region, or global controller with regional reconcilers?</li>\n<li><strong>Observability</strong> — CloudWatch metrics from the controller, or push to a shared OAB dashboard?</li>\n<li><strong>Networking isolation</strong> — shared VPC with per-service SG rules, or per-namespace VPC?</li>\n<li><strong>Schema versioning</strong> — how to handle <code>oab.dev/v2</code> migration when spec evolves?</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>13. Decision</h2>\n<p>We adopt the CRD + Operator pattern on ECS with an <strong>S3-only state store</strong>, <strong>explicit generation tracking</strong>, and a <strong><code>oabctl</code> CLI</strong> for the operator interface. The controller runs as a single ECS service that reconciles <code>OABService</code> manifests against actual ECS state.</p>\n<p>Key design choices:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Config delivery</strong>: controller renders <code>config.toml</code> to S3 artifact; startup wrapper downloads it</li>\n<li><strong>Secrets</strong>: per-agent SSM/Secrets Manager references; never in bootstrap archive</li>\n<li><strong>Bootstrap</strong>: mutable runtime state only (memory, knowledge base)</li>\n<li><strong>Replicas</strong>: always 1; scale by deploying more agents, not replicating one</li>\n<li><strong>Generation</strong>: explicit <code>metadata.generation</code> / <code>status.observedGeneration</code> (not S3 VersionId)</li>\n<li><strong>Phase 1 scope</strong>: narrow (create/update only, poll-based, single controller)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>DynamoDB, EventBridge, finalizers, and multi-region are deferred to Phase 2+.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: ECS Control Plane (CRD + Operator Pattern on ECS)"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/hooks",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Lifecycle Hooks</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-27</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Problem Statement</h2>\n<p>When an OpenAB pod starts, the agent CLI needs more than just the binary — it needs <code>AGENTS.md</code>, <code>docs/*</code>, <code>bin/*</code>, skills, and potentially OAuth tokens to be fully operational on first message. Today, operators manually <code>kubectl exec</code> to set up these files or bake custom images, which is error-prone and not reproducible.</p>\n<p><strong>Goal:</strong> By the time the agent CLI receives its first JSON-RPC request, all required files and credentials are in place — zero manual intervention after deploy.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Approaches Considered</h2>\n<h3>A. Custom Dockerfile (ENTRYPOINT bake)</h3>\n<p>Operators build their own image layering content on top of the base openab image:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-dockerfile\">FROM ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:latest\nCOPY AGENTS.md /home/node/AGENTS.md\nCOPY bin/ /home/node/bin/\nCOPY .kiro/ /home/node/.kiro/\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Immutable, reproducible</li>\n<li>No startup latency</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Forces every operator to maintain a Dockerfile</li>\n<li>OAuth tokens cannot be baked in (expire, shouldn't be in images)</li>\n<li>Every content change requires image rebuild + push + rollout</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>B. initContainer + PVC</h3>\n<p>A Kubernetes init container populates the PVC before the main container starts:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">initContainers:\n  - name: bootstrap\n    image: alpine/git\n    command: [&quot;sh&quot;, &quot;-c&quot;, &quot;git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/org/agent-config /data/config &amp;&amp; cp -r /data/config/* /data/home/&quot;]\n    volumeMounts:\n      - name: data\n        mountPath: /data/home\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Separates content provisioning from runtime image</li>\n<li>PVC persists tokens across restarts (existing pattern)</li>\n<li>Helm chart can define init containers natively</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Startup latency (git clone, downloads)</li>\n<li>Kubernetes-only — doesn't help Docker Compose or bare-metal users</li>\n<li>Debugging init container failures is less visible</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>C. openab <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> in config.toml</h3>\n<p>openab executes a user-defined script before spawning the agent CLI:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\nscript = &quot;/data/pre-boot.sh&quot;\ntimeout_seconds = 60\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Works everywhere (Docker, k8s, bare metal, ECS)</li>\n<li>Configured in the same file operators already manage</li>\n<li>openab can log success/failure and abort cleanly</li>\n<li>Can be conditional (skip if files already exist)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Adds shell execution responsibility to openab</li>\n<li>Security surface if config is user-supplied (mitigated: config is operator-controlled)</li>\n<li>Logs mixed with openab startup output</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Decision</h2>\n<p><strong>Use a layered approach: initContainer for heavy provisioning + openab <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> for last-mile setup.</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Content Type</th>\n<th>Mechanism</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Static assets (AGENTS.md, docs, skills, bins)</td>\n<td>initContainer, ConfigMap, or custom image</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>OAuth tokens</td>\n<td>PVC (existing pattern, persists across restarts)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Dynamic/conditional setup</td>\n<td>openab <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>The <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> hook is the primary new feature openab needs to implement. The initContainer pattern is documented as a recommended practice but requires no openab code changes.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. <code>[hooks]</code> Specification</h2>\n<h3>Config Structure</h3>\n<p>Hooks are organized as 2-level TOML tables under <code>[hooks]</code>. Each hook is its own sub-table with independent configuration:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ntimeout_seconds = 60                  # max wall-clock time; 0 = no timeout\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;                  # &quot;abort&quot; (default) | &quot;warn&quot;\n\n# Script source — exactly ONE of the following three:\nscript = &quot;/etc/openab/pre-boot.sh&quot;    # Option A: path to executable file\n# inline = '''...'''                  # Option B: script content in config\n# url = &quot;https://...&quot;                 # Option C: remote script URL\n# sha256 = &quot;abc123...&quot;               #           (required with url)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Three Script Source Options</h3>\n<p><strong>Option A: <code>script</code> — file path</strong> (k8s ConfigMap, EFS, baked in image)</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\nscript = &quot;/etc/openab/pre-boot.sh&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Option B: <code>inline</code> — embedded in config.toml</strong> (ECS, Docker Compose, bare metal)</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\nset -e\naws s3 sync &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_URI&quot; &quot;$HOME/&quot;\n'''\n</code></pre>\n<p>openab writes the content to a temp file, <code>chmod +x</code>, executes it, then deletes it.</p>\n<p><strong>Option C: <code>url</code> + <code>sha256</code> — remote script</strong> (editable without redeploy, any platform)</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\nurl = &quot;https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/openab-config/main/pre-boot.sh&quot;\nsha256 = &quot;e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>openab fetches the URL, verifies the SHA-256 checksum, then executes. Fails hard on mismatch or network error.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Option</th>\n<th>Best for</th>\n<th>Requires redeploy?</th>\n<th>Network at boot?</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>script</code></td>\n<td>k8s (ConfigMap mount), EFS, image bake</td>\n<td>Only if image-baked</td>\n<td>No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>inline</code></td>\n<td>ECS, Docker Compose, bare metal</td>\n<td>Config change only</td>\n<td>No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code> + <code>sha256</code></td>\n<td>Central script repo, multi-cluster</td>\n<td>No (update sha256 to roll)</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Exactly one of <code>script</code>, <code>inline</code>, or <code>url</code> must be set. Setting multiple is a config error.</p>\n<h3>Common Fields</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>timeout_seconds</code> — max wall-clock time before kill. Default: 60.</li>\n<li><code>on_failure</code> — <code>&quot;abort&quot;</code> (default): openab exits non-zero (pod restarts). <code>&quot;warn&quot;</code>: log error, continue.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Hook Lifecycle</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Hook</th>\n<th>Timing</th>\n<th>Runs</th>\n<th>Phase 1</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_boot</code></td>\n<td>Before agent CLI spawns</td>\n<td>Once per process start</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_shutdown</code></td>\n<td>On SIGTERM, before exit</td>\n<td>Once per process stop</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>post_boot</code></td>\n<td>After first successful agent spawn</td>\n<td>Once per process start</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_session</code></td>\n<td>Before each ACP session creation</td>\n<td>Per session</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>post_session</code></td>\n<td>After ACP session teardown</td>\n<td>Per session</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Execution Semantics (<code>pre_boot</code>)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>openab starts, parses config.</li>\n<li>Resolves script source:\n<ul>\n<li><code>script</code> → use file directly</li>\n<li><code>inline</code> → write to temp file, chmod +x</li>\n<li><code>url</code> → fetch, verify sha256, write to temp file, chmod +x</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Spawns the resolved script as a child process.</li>\n<li>Waits for exit (respecting timeout).</li>\n<li>On exit 0 → proceed to spawn agent sessions normally.</li>\n<li>On non-zero exit, timeout, or sha256 mismatch → apply <code>on_failure</code> policy.</li>\n<li>Cleans up temp files (if <code>inline</code> or <code>url</code>).</li>\n<li>The script runs <strong>once per openab process start</strong>, not per session.</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Security</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>script</code> path must be absolute (no relative path traversal).</li>\n<li><code>url</code> requires <code>sha256</code> — openab refuses to execute unverified remote code.</li>\n<li>The script inherits the same sanitized environment as agent subprocesses (<code>env_clear()</code> + whitelist).</li>\n<li><code>DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code> and other openab secrets are NOT exposed to the bootstrap script.</li>\n<li>The script runs as the container's UID (not root, unless the container runs as root).</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Helm Chart Integration</h2>\n<p>The Helm chart adds optional support for:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Bootstrap script via ConfigMap:</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># values.yaml\nagents:\n  kiro:\n    hooks:\n      preBoot:\n        enabled: true\n        script: |\n          #!/bin/sh\n          set -e\n          # Clone agent config if not present\n          if [ ! -f &quot;$HOME/AGENTS.md&quot; ]; then\n            git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/org/config /tmp/cfg\n            cp /tmp/cfg/AGENTS.md &quot;$HOME/&quot;\n            cp -r /tmp/cfg/bin/ &quot;$HOME/bin/&quot;\n          fi\n</code></pre>\n<ol start=\"2\">\n<li><strong>initContainer (opt-in):</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    initContainers:\n      - name: fetch-config\n        image: alpine/git\n        command: [&quot;git&quot;, &quot;clone&quot;, &quot;--depth&quot;, &quot;1&quot;, &quot;https://github.com/org/config&quot;, &quot;/data/home/config&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Examples</h2>\n<h3>Minimal: just AGENTS.md from a ConfigMap</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># No [hooks] needed — mount AGENTS.md via ConfigMap volume\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Medium: clone a config repo on startup</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">#!/bin/sh\n# /etc/openab/pre-boot.sh\nset -e\nREPO=&quot;https://github.com/myorg/agent-config&quot;\nDEST=&quot;$HOME/.agent-config&quot;\n\nif [ ! -d &quot;$DEST/.git&quot; ]; then\n  git clone --depth 1 &quot;$REPO&quot; &quot;$DEST&quot;\nelse\n  git -C &quot;$DEST&quot; pull --ff-only 2&gt;/dev/null || true\nfi\n\nln -sf &quot;$DEST/AGENTS.md&quot; &quot;$HOME/AGENTS.md&quot;\nln -sf &quot;$DEST/bin&quot; &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Advanced: token refresh + conditional setup</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">#!/bin/sh\n# /etc/openab/pre-boot.sh\nset -e\n\n# Refresh OAuth if expired (token file on PVC)\nif [ -f &quot;$HOME/.kiro/auth.json&quot; ]; then\n  EXPIRES=$(jq -r '.expires' &quot;$HOME/.kiro/auth.json&quot;)\n  NOW=$(date +%s)\n  if [ &quot;$NOW&quot; -gt &quot;$EXPIRES&quot; ]; then\n    echo &quot;[pre_boot] OAuth token expired, attempting refresh...&quot;\n    kiro-cli auth refresh || echo &quot;[pre_boot] refresh failed, will use device flow on first request&quot;\n  fi\nfi\n\n# Ensure skills are present\ncp -rn /etc/openab/skills/ &quot;$HOME/.kiro/skills/&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null || true\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Enterprise Cloud Patterns</h2>\n<p>Enterprise deployments typically use a <strong>two-layer pull model</strong>: a shared org base followed by team/user personalization. The pod's cloud IAM identity (no secrets needed) authenticates to object storage.</p>\n<h3>Layering Model</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Layer 2: Personal/Team artifacts       │  ← s3 sync / gsutil rsync / azcopy sync\n│  (custom skills, steering, overrides)   │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  Layer 1: Org base tarball              │  ← s3 cp | tar xz (one-time)\n│  (AGENTS.md, shared bins, common docs)  │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  Container image (openab + agent CLI)   │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Cloud-Agnostic Auth</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Cloud</th>\n<th>Pod Identity Mechanism</th>\n<th>CLI</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>AWS</td>\n<td>IRSA / EKS Pod Identity</td>\n<td><code>aws s3 cp</code>, <code>aws s3 sync</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>GCP</td>\n<td>Workload Identity</td>\n<td><code>gcloud storage cp</code>, <code>gcloud storage rsync</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Azure</td>\n<td>Workload Identity Federation</td>\n<td><code>az storage blob download</code>, <code>azcopy sync</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>All three inject credentials via projected tokens or metadata — no secrets in config, no env vars to manage.</p>\n<h3>CLI Tooling: Self-Bootstrapping</h3>\n<p>The base openab image does NOT include cloud CLIs. The <code>pre_boot</code> script self-bootstraps using <code>curl</code> (which is in the base image):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Install AWS CLI to $HOME/bin (persists on PVC across restarts)\nif [ ! -x &quot;$HOME/bin/aws&quot; ]; then\n  mkdir -p &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n  curl -s &quot;https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip&quot; -o /tmp/awscli.zip\n  unzip -q /tmp/awscli.zip -d /tmp\n  /tmp/aws/install --install-dir &quot;$HOME/aws-cli&quot; --bin-dir &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n  rm -rf /tmp/awscli.zip /tmp/aws\nfi\nexport PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Since <code>$HOME</code> is on the PVC, the CLI install survives pod restarts — it only downloads once.</p>\n<h3>Canonical Enterprise Workflow</h3>\n<p>The enterprise platform team maintains a single <code>values-prod.yaml</code>. No custom Dockerfile, no custom chart — stock image, stock chart, all customization in values:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># values-prod.yaml\nagents:\n  kiro:\n    hooks:\n      preBoot:\n        enabled: true\n        timeoutSeconds: 120\n        onFailure: abort\n        env:\n          BOOTSTRAP_BASE_URI: &quot;s3://acme-openab/base.tar.gz&quot;\n          BOOTSTRAP_PERSONAL_URI: &quot;s3://acme-openab/teams/platform/alice/&quot;\n        script: |\n          #!/bin/sh\n          set -e\n\n          # Self-bootstrap AWS CLI (persists on PVC)\n          if [ ! -x &quot;$HOME/bin/aws&quot; ]; then\n            mkdir -p &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n            curl -s &quot;https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip&quot; -o /tmp/awscli.zip\n            unzip -q /tmp/awscli.zip -d /tmp\n            /tmp/aws/install --install-dir &quot;$HOME/aws-cli&quot; --bin-dir &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n            rm -rf /tmp/awscli.zip /tmp/aws\n          fi\n          export PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;\n\n          # Layer 1: org-wide base (one-time)\n          if [ ! -f &quot;$HOME/.bootstrapped&quot; ]; then\n            aws s3 cp &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_BASE_URI&quot; - | tar xz -C &quot;$HOME&quot;\n            touch &quot;$HOME/.bootstrapped&quot;\n          fi\n\n          # Layer 2: team/user personalization (always fresh)\n          aws s3 sync &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_PERSONAL_URI&quot; &quot;$HOME/&quot;\n    serviceAccount:\n      annotations:\n        eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/openab-agent\n</code></pre>\n<p>Deploy:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade openab openab/openab -f values-prod.yaml\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Alternatively, an initContainer can pre-install the cloud CLI into a shared <code>emptyDir</code> volume (mounted at <code>/tools</code> on both containers), eliminating the curl/install step from the script. This trades a simpler script for more Helm template complexity — use whichever fits your team's preference.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Design Principle</h3>\n<p>openab is cloud-agnostic — it doesn't know or care about AWS/GCP/Azure. The <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> script is the abstraction boundary. The Helm chart is unopinionated — it provides plumbing (ConfigMap mount, env pass-through) without prescribing cloud-specific logic. Enterprises write their script once in values, and every agent pod gets it.</p>\n<h3>ECS Fargate Workflow</h3>\n<p>ECS has no Helm, no ConfigMap, no initContainer. The <code>inline</code> option is the native fit — the script lives directly in <code>config.toml</code>, which is injected via environment variable, S3 fetch in entrypoint, or EFS mount.</p>\n<p><strong>config.toml with inline pre_boot:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\nset -e\n\n# Self-bootstrap AWS CLI (EFS or ephemeral — re-installs each cold start)\nif [ ! -x &quot;$HOME/bin/aws&quot; ]; then\n  mkdir -p &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n  curl -s &quot;https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip&quot; -o /tmp/awscli.zip\n  unzip -q /tmp/awscli.zip -d /tmp\n  /tmp/aws/install --install-dir &quot;$HOME/aws-cli&quot; --bin-dir &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n  rm -rf /tmp/awscli.zip /tmp/aws\nfi\nexport PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;\n\n# Pull artifacts (task role provides credentials automatically)\nif [ ! -f &quot;$HOME/.bootstrapped&quot; ]; then\n  aws s3 cp &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_BASE_URI&quot; - | tar xz -C &quot;$HOME&quot;\n  touch &quot;$HOME/.bootstrapped&quot;\nfi\naws s3 sync &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_PERSONAL_URI&quot; &quot;$HOME/&quot;\n'''\n\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;kiro-cli&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\nenv = { BOOTSTRAP_BASE_URI = &quot;s3://acme-openab/base.tar.gz&quot;, BOOTSTRAP_PERSONAL_URI = &quot;s3://acme-openab/teams/platform/alice/&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>ECS task definition highlights:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Task IAM role grants <code>s3:GetObject</code> / <code>s3:ListBucket</code> / <code>s3:PutObject</code> — no credentials in config</li>\n<li>Config.toml stored in S3 or Secrets Manager, fetched at container start via entrypoint wrapper</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Storage options:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mode</th>\n<th>Volume</th>\n<th>CLI install</th>\n<th>Artifacts</th>\n<th>OAuth tokens</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>EFS</td>\n<td>EFS mount at <code>$HOME</code></td>\n<td>Persists (install once)</td>\n<td>Persists</td>\n<td>Persists</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Ephemeral</td>\n<td>Task ephemeral storage</td>\n<td>Re-installs each cold start</td>\n<td>Re-pulls each start</td>\n<td>Requires S3 backup/restore</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Ephemeral mode with S3 backup/restore:</strong></p>\n<p>When no EFS is available, the <code>pre_boot</code> script restores state from S3 on start, and <code>pre_shutdown</code> backs up state before exit:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\nset -e\n\n# Install AWS CLI\nif [ ! -x &quot;$HOME/bin/aws&quot; ]; then\n  mkdir -p &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n  curl -s &quot;https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip&quot; -o /tmp/awscli.zip\n  unzip -q /tmp/awscli.zip -d /tmp\n  /tmp/aws/install --install-dir &quot;$HOME/aws-cli&quot; --bin-dir &quot;$HOME/bin&quot;\n  rm -rf /tmp/awscli.zip /tmp/aws\nfi\nexport PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;\n\n# Restore state from S3 (tokens, settings, cached artifacts)\naws s3 sync &quot;$STATE_BUCKET/$TASK_FAMILY/&quot; &quot;$HOME/&quot; --quiet\n\n# Pull org artifacts (always, in case base tarball updated)\naws s3 cp &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_BASE_URI&quot; - | tar xz -C &quot;$HOME&quot;\naws s3 sync &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_PERSONAL_URI&quot; &quot;$HOME/&quot;\n'''\n\n[hooks.pre_shutdown]\ntimeout_seconds = 30\non_failure = &quot;warn&quot;\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\nexport PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;\naws s3 sync &quot;$HOME/&quot; &quot;s3://$STATE_BUCKET/$TASK_FAMILY/&quot; \\\n  --exclude &quot;aws-cli/*&quot; --exclude &quot;bin/*&quot; --quiet\n'''\n\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;kiro-cli&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\nenv = { BOOTSTRAP_BASE_URI = &quot;s3://acme-openab/base.tar.gz&quot;, BOOTSTRAP_PERSONAL_URI = &quot;s3://acme-openab/teams/platform/alice/&quot;, STATE_BUCKET = &quot;s3://acme-openab/state&quot;, TASK_FAMILY = &quot;openab-kiro&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Lifecycle on Fargate Spot:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>Task starts → pre_boot (restore from S3) → agent ready → ... running ...\nSpot reclaim → SIGTERM → pre_shutdown (backup to S3) → exit\nTask restarts → pre_boot (restore from S3) → agent ready (as if nothing happened)\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Fargate Spot works fine since <code>pre_boot</code> is idempotent — worst case is a re-download on spot reclaim</li>\n<li>Ephemeral mode trades startup latency for simpler infra (no EFS to manage)</li>\n<li>EFS mode is preferred when OAuth tokens must survive task replacement without re-auth</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Migration</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Existing deployments:</strong> No change required. <code>[hooks]</code> is optional; omitting it preserves current behavior.</li>\n<li><strong>Operators with custom entrypoints:</strong> Can migrate their entrypoint logic into a <code>pre_boot</code> script and use the stock image.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Future Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Readiness integration:</strong> Expose readiness only after <code>pre_boot</code> completes (useful for k8s readiness probes).</li>\n<li><strong><code>post_boot</code> / <code>pre_session</code> / <code>post_session</code> hooks:</strong> Natural extensions under the same <code>[hooks]</code> namespace — each gets its own sub-table with the same field schema.</li>\n<li><strong>Caching for <code>url</code> mode:</strong> Cache the fetched script on PVC, only re-fetch if sha256 in config changes (avoids network dependency on routine restarts).</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Lifecycle Hooks"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/imessage-integration",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: iMessage Integration via macOS Gateway</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-18</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n<li><strong>Reviewers:</strong> @pahud</li>\n<li><strong>Tracking issues:</strong> (none yet)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Decision</h2>\n<p>Enable OAB agents to receive and respond to iMessage conversations, allowing users to interact with their agent team through Apple's native messaging platform. This extends OAB's multi-platform adapter architecture (see <a href=\"/openab/adr/multi-platform-adapters\">ADR: Multi-Platform Adapters</a>) to a platform that lacks an official API.</p>\n<p><strong>Decision:</strong> Implement iMessage as a built-in adapter within the Custom Gateway, running natively on macOS. The gateway polls <code>chat.db</code> for inbound messages and sends outbound via AppleScript, connecting to OAB core (running in OrbStack/containers) over WebSocket. This is an iMessage-only deployment — no separate bridge binary needed.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Motivation</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Users want to interact with OAB agents from iMessage — the default messaging app on iOS/macOS with 1B+ active users</li>\n<li>iMessage offers a more personal, low-friction interaction surface compared to Discord/Slack</li>\n<li>Apple provides <strong>no official iMessage API</strong> — all third-party integrations rely on macOS Messages.app as a bridge</li>\n<li>The existing <code>agy-acp</code> component already proves the &quot;poll SQLite DB&quot; pattern works reliably in OAB</li>\n<li>iMessage bridging requires macOS-native access (<code>chat.db</code> + AppleScript) — it <strong>cannot</strong> run inside a container</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Why iMessage Over Existing Channels</h3>\n<p>iMessage fills a gap that LINE, Telegram, and Slack cannot:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Advantage</th>\n<th>Detail</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>North America default</strong></td>\n<td>iPhone-to-iPhone messaging uses iMessage automatically — no app install required. Dominant in US/Canada market.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Zero-friction reach</strong></td>\n<td>Only requires a phone number. No &quot;add friend&quot; / &quot;find bot username&quot; step. Ideal for cold outreach: customer support, appointment reminders, order notifications.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>High trust signal</strong></td>\n<td>Conversations appear alongside friends/family in the native Messages.app. Users perceive it as personal communication, not &quot;yet another bot.&quot;</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Apple ecosystem integration</strong></td>\n<td>Siri dictation, Apple Watch, CarPlay, Focus Mode — notifications are not filtered as &quot;app push.&quot;</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>No new app required</strong></td>\n<td>Enterprise scenario: clients/employees already have iPhones; no need to mandate LINE/Telegram/Slack installation.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>When NOT to use iMessage:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Better choice</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Asia market (Taiwan/Japan/Thailand)</td>\n<td>LINE</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Developer/tech communities</td>\n<td>Discord / Telegram</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cross-platform users (Android + iPhone)</td>\n<td>Telegram / WhatsApp</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Rich UI (buttons, carousels)</td>\n<td>LINE / Slack</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Group bot interactions</td>\n<td>Discord / Slack</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Message editing / threading</td>\n<td>Discord / Slack</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Summary:</strong> iMessage's core value is <strong>North American market + zero-install barrier + high trust perception</strong>. For Asian markets or technical communities, LINE/Telegram remain more practical.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Architecture</h2>\n<h3>3.1 Primary: Custom Gateway on macOS Host + OAB in OrbStack</h3>\n<pre><code>┌────────────────┐\n│  iPhone User   │\n│  (iMessage)    │\n└───────┬────────┘\n        │\n        ▼\n═══════════════════\n║ Apple iMessage  ║\n║    Network      ║\n═══════════════════\n        │\n        ▼\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  macOS host (Mac mini / MacBook)         │\n│                                          │\n│  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  Messages.app                      │  │\n│  │  ~/Library/Messages/chat.db        │  │\n│  └──────────────┬─────────────────────┘  │\n│                 │ poll every 100-500ms    │\n│  ┌──────────────▼─────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  Custom Gateway (native binary)    │  │\n│  │                                    │  │\n│  │  ├── iMessage adapter (built-in)   │  │\n│  │  │   ├── poll chat.db (SQLite)     │  │\n│  │  │   └── send via osascript        │  │\n│  │  └── WebSocket client → OAB        │  │\n│  └──────────────┬─────────────────────┘  │\n│                 │                         │\n└─────────────────┼─────────────────────────┘\n                  │ WebSocket (outbound connection)\n                  ▼\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  OrbStack (Linux containers)             │\n│                                          │\n│  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  OAB Core                          │  │\n│  │  ├── AdapterRouter                 │  │\n│  │  ├── SessionPool                   │  │\n│  │  └── ACP agents                    │  │\n│  └────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                          │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Why the gateway must run on macOS host (not in a container):</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong><code>chat.db</code> access</strong> — macOS TCC (Transparency, Consent, Control) grants Full Disk Access per-app. A containerized process cannot inherit FDA permissions.</li>\n<li><strong>SQLite WAL locking</strong> — <code>chat.db</code> is held by Messages.app with WAL lock. A cross-VM mount risks lock contention.</li>\n<li><strong>AppleScript IPC</strong> — <code>osascript</code> communicates with Messages.app via macOS IPC (Apple Events). This only works from the same macOS session.</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>3.2 Alternative: Photon Spectrum (Cloud, No Mac Required)</h3>\n<pre><code>┌────────────────┐        ═══════════════        ┌──────────────────┐\n│  iPhone User   │───────║ Apple iMessage ║──────│  Photon Cloud     │\n│  (iMessage)    │        ═══════════════        │  (managed Mac群)  │\n└────────────────┘                               └────────┬─────────┘\n                                                          │ gRPC stream\n                                                          ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  OrbStack (Linux containers)                                        │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────────────┐     ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐ │\n│  │ Spectrum Sidecar  │────►│ OAB Core                             │ │\n│  │ (Node.js/Bun)    │     │                                       │ │\n│  └──────────────────┘     └───────────────────────────────────────┘ │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>Photon Spectrum manages the Mac infrastructure — no local Mac needed. Useful as fallback if Apple restricts local <code>chat.db</code> access.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. How iMessage Bridging Works</h2>\n<p>Apple does not provide an iMessage API. The gateway's iMessage adapter relies on two macOS-native mechanisms:</p>\n<h3>4.1 Receiving Messages (Inbound)</h3>\n<p>Messages.app writes all received messages to a local SQLite database at <code>~/Library/Messages/chat.db</code>. The adapter polls this DB for new rows:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-sql\">SELECT rowid, text, handle_id, date, is_from_me, cache_roomnames\nFROM message\nWHERE rowid &gt; ?last_seen_rowid\nORDER BY rowid ASC\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is the <strong>same pattern as <code>agy-acp</code></strong>, which polls <code>conversations/*.db</code> for new <code>step_payload</code> rows. Both use:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>SQLite read-only connection with WAL mode</li>\n<li>Polling interval (100-500ms)</li>\n<li>Monotonically increasing row ID as cursor</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>4.2 Sending Messages (Outbound)</h3>\n<p>Messages are sent by invoking AppleScript via <code>osascript</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-applescript\">tell application &quot;Messages&quot;\n    set targetService to 1st account whose service type = iMessage\n    set targetBuddy to participant &quot;+1234567890&quot; of targetService\n    send &quot;Hello from OAB&quot; to targetBuddy\nend tell\n</code></pre>\n<p>For group chats, send to a specific chat ID:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-applescript\">tell application &quot;Messages&quot;\n    set targetChat to chat id &quot;iMessage;+;chat123456&quot;\n    send &quot;Hello from OAB&quot; to targetChat\nend tell\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4.3 Comparison with agy-acp</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>agy-acp</th>\n<th>Custom Gateway (iMessage adapter)</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Monitored program</td>\n<td><code>agy</code> (Gemini CLI)</td>\n<td>Messages.app</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Data source</td>\n<td><code>conversations/*.db</code></td>\n<td><code>~/Library/Messages/chat.db</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Poll mechanism</td>\n<td><code>WHERE idx &gt; last</code> every 100ms</td>\n<td><code>WHERE rowid &gt; last</code> every 100-500ms</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Data format</td>\n<td>protobuf <code>step_payload</code> field 20.1</td>\n<td><code>attributedBody</code> blob / plain <code>text</code> column</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Send mechanism</td>\n<td>spawn <code>agy -p &quot;prompt&quot;</code></td>\n<td>spawn <code>osascript</code> (AppleScript)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Output</td>\n<td>JSON-RPC streaming notifications</td>\n<td>WebSocket to OAB core (direct)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Message Flow</h2>\n<h3>Inbound (User → Agent)</h3>\n<pre><code>1. User sends iMessage from iPhone\n2. Apple iMessage network delivers to Mac's Messages.app\n3. Messages.app writes row to chat.db\n4. Gateway's iMessage adapter detects new row (poll)\n5. Adapter formats as OpenAB inbound event:\n   { &quot;platform&quot;: &quot;imessage&quot;, &quot;sender&quot;: &quot;+1234567890&quot;,\n     &quot;text&quot;: &quot;...&quot;, &quot;channel_id&quot;: &quot;iMessage;-;+1234567890&quot; }\n6. Gateway sends event to OAB core via WebSocket\n7. AdapterRouter dispatches to SessionPool → agent\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Outbound (Agent → User)</h3>\n<pre><code>1. Agent produces response via ACP session\n2. OAB core sends outbound event via WebSocket to gateway\n3. Gateway's iMessage adapter invokes AppleScript\n4. Messages.app → Apple network → User's iPhone\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Platform Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>No message editing (iMessage supports &quot;edit&quot; natively on iOS 16+ but AppleScript cannot trigger it)</li>\n<li>No threading (conversations are flat)</li>\n<li>Reactions map to tapbacks (❤️, 👍, 👎, 😂, ‼️, ❓) — only 6 options</li>\n<li>No typing indicators via AppleScript (Spectrum Cloud supports this)</li>\n<li>No structured @mention field (see §6.1 below)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>6.1 @Mention Detection (Group Chat)</h3>\n<p>iMessage supports @mentions (iOS 14+, displayed as bold blue text), but <code>chat.db</code> does <strong>not</strong> expose them as a structured column. The mention data is embedded inside the <code>attributedBody</code> blob — a serialized <code>NSAttributedString</code> (NSKeyedArchiver / typedstream format).</p>\n<p><strong>To extract mentions, the adapter must:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li>Read <code>message.attributedBody</code> (binary blob)</li>\n<li>Decode NSKeyedArchiver binary plist</li>\n<li>Locate ranges where <code>__kIMMessagePartAttributeName</code> = 1 (indicates a mention)</li>\n<li>Extract the mentioned handle ID from <code>__kIMMentionConfirmedMention</code></li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Comparison with other platforms:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Mention detection</th>\n<th>Complexity</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Discord</td>\n<td><code>message.mentions</code> array</td>\n<td>Trivial — structured field</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>LINE</td>\n<td><code>mentionees</code> in webhook payload</td>\n<td>Trivial — structured field</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Slack</td>\n<td><code>&lt;@BOT_ID&gt;</code> in text + <code>app_mention</code> event type</td>\n<td>Easy — text pattern</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>iMessage</td>\n<td>Parse binary <code>attributedBody</code> blob</td>\n<td>Hard — undocumented binary format</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Implications for group chat:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>1:1 conversations (Phase 1):</strong> No mention detection needed — all messages are directed at the bot</li>\n<li><strong>Group chat (Phase 3):</strong> Adapter must parse <code>attributedBody</code> to know when the bot is mentioned, or fall back to keyword-prefix trigger (e.g. <code>/ask ...</code>)</li>\n<li>The <code>attributedBody</code> format is undocumented and may change across macOS versions — Rust <code>plist</code> crate can decode the binary plist, but the internal schema requires reverse-engineering</li>\n<li><strong>Outbound:</strong> AppleScript <code>send</code> does not support sending @mentions — bot replies are plain text only</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Config Design</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[gateway.imessage]\nenabled = true\npoll_interval_ms = 200\nchat_db_path = &quot;~/Library/Messages/chat.db&quot;  # default; override for testing\n\n# OAB core WebSocket endpoint (OrbStack container)\n[gateway]\noab_ws_url = &quot;ws://localhost:8080/ws&quot;  # OrbStack port-forwards to OAB\n\n# Spectrum mode (alternative — no local Mac needed)\n[gateway.imessage.spectrum]\nenabled = false\nproject_id = &quot;${PHOTON_PROJECT_ID}&quot;\nproject_secret = &quot;${PHOTON_PROJECT_SECRET}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Security Considerations</h2>\n<h3>8.1 macOS Host Risks</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Risk</th>\n<th>Mitigation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>No container isolation</td>\n<td>Dedicated macOS user account with minimal privileges</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Mac compromise → iMessage access</td>\n<td>Gateway is a thin adapter; all agent logic stays in OrbStack</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Apple account credential exposure</td>\n<td>Use a dedicated Apple ID, not personal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>AppleScript injection</td>\n<td>Sanitize all outbound text; no user input in script template</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Full Disk Access requirement</td>\n<td>Grant FDA only to the gateway binary, not the user shell</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>8.2 Photon Spectrum Risks</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Risk</th>\n<th>Mitigation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Third-party dependency</td>\n<td>Photon manages Apple infra; you trust their SLA</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Shared phone numbers (free tier)</td>\n<td>Upgrade to dedicated line ($250/mo) for consistent identity</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Apple ToS enforcement</td>\n<td>Photon assumes this risk; self-hosted is fallback</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>gRPC stream reliability</td>\n<td>SDK handles auto-reconnect; SMS/RCS fallback</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>8.3 General</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Messages contain PII — gateway and OAB must encrypt in transit (WebSocket over TLS)</li>\n<li>Rate limiting on outbound to avoid Apple throttling/blocking</li>\n<li>Gateway binary should be code-signed to satisfy macOS Gatekeeper</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Deployment</h2>\n<h3>Primary: macOS + OrbStack</h3>\n<pre><code>macOS host:\n  - Custom Gateway binary (Rust, native arm64/x86_64)\n  - Runs as launchd service (auto-restart, auto-start on boot)\n  - Requires: Full Disk Access for chat.db, Accessibility for AppleScript\n\nOrbStack (on same Mac):\n  - OAB Core container (Linux)\n  - Exposes WebSocket endpoint on localhost\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Why not containerize the gateway:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>chat.db</code> cannot be volume-mounted into Linux VMs (macOS TCC blocks cross-process FDA)</li>\n<li>AppleScript IPC (<code>osascript</code>) requires native macOS session — unavailable in containers</li>\n<li>SQLite WAL mode may conflict with cross-VM file locking</li>\n</ul>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Deployment</th>\n<th>Where</th>\n<th>Cost</th>\n<th>Complexity</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Primary (this ADR)</td>\n<td>Mac (gateway) + OrbStack (OAB)</td>\n<td>~$600 Mac mini</td>\n<td>Low</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Spectrum alternative</td>\n<td>OrbStack only (no Mac needed)</td>\n<td>$0-250/mo</td>\n<td>Low</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. Implementation Phases</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n<th>Dependencies</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 1</strong></td>\n<td>iMessage adapter in Custom Gateway: poll chat.db, send via AppleScript, WebSocket to OAB</td>\n<td>Custom Gateway (<a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway\">ADR</a>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 2</strong></td>\n<td>Spectrum sidecar adapter as alternative (no Mac required)</td>\n<td>Photon account</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 3</strong></td>\n<td>Rich features: tapback reactions, group chat support, @mention parsing, attachment handling</td>\n<td>Phase 1</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>11. Apple Compliance &amp; Risks</h2>\n<p>Apple does not provide an official iMessage API. All known approaches rely on:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>macOS Messages.app + SQLite</strong> — reading <code>chat.db</code> (requires Full Disk Access)</li>\n<li><strong>AppleScript automation</strong> — sending via <code>osascript</code> (uses public macOS APIs)</li>\n<li><strong>No protocol reverse-engineering</strong> — no private framework usage</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Current landscape (as of 2026-06):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>BlueBubbles, AirMessage have operated for years without Apple enforcement</li>\n<li>Photon Spectrum launched April 2026, commercially offering managed iMessage lines</li>\n<li>Apple has not issued cease-and-desist to any known project</li>\n<li>Risk: Apple could restrict <code>chat.db</code> access or AppleScript Messages automation in a future macOS update</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Mitigation:</strong> The adapter architecture is modular — if Apple blocks the self-hosted path, Spectrum Cloud remains as fallback (they absorb the compliance risk). If both paths are blocked, the adapter can be disabled without affecting other OAB platforms.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>12. Open Questions</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>#</th>\n<th>Question</th>\n<th>Options</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>1</td>\n<td>Poll interval default</td>\n<td>100ms vs 200ms vs 500ms</td>\n<td>Tradeoff: latency vs CPU. agy-acp uses 100ms</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2</td>\n<td>Group chat support in Phase 1?</td>\n<td>Yes / defer to Phase 3</td>\n<td>Recommend defer — no structured @mention field means bot can't reliably detect when addressed. 1:1 is the sweet spot.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3</td>\n<td>Should gateway run as launchd service?</td>\n<td>Yes (auto-restart) / manual</td>\n<td>launchd is macOS best practice for daemons</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>4</td>\n<td>Photon free tier shared numbers acceptable?</td>\n<td>Yes for POC / require dedicated</td>\n<td>Shared numbers may confuse recipients</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<p><em>This ADR was drafted based on research into Photon Spectrum (photon-hq/spectrum-ts), imessage-kit, and the existing agy-acp polling pattern in OAB.</em></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: iMessage Integration via macOS Gateway"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/line-adapter",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: LINE Messaging API Adapter</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted</li>\n<li><strong>Initial Date:</strong> 2026-04-22</li>\n<li><strong>Last Updated Date:</strong> 2026-04-28</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent, @iamninihuang</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. User Story &amp; Requirements</h2>\n<p>As a LINE user, I want to interact with an OpenAB agent directly in LINE — both in 1:1 DMs and group chats — so that I can use the same AI coding assistant without switching to Discord or Slack.</p>\n<p>Requirements:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Receive user messages from LINE and route them to an agent session</li>\n<li>Send agent responses back to the user via LINE</li>\n<li>Validate webhook signatures to ensure messages are authentically from LINE</li>\n<li>Support user/group allowlists for access control</li>\n<li>Integrate into the existing multi-adapter architecture (run alongside Discord/Slack)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>When to Use LINE</h3>\n<p>LINE is the right choice when:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Your users are primarily on LINE (common in Taiwan, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia)</li>\n<li>The primary use case is <strong>1:1 private conversations</strong> with the agent — each user gets a dedicated session, similar to Discord DM</li>\n<li>You need a mobile-first experience — LINE's mobile app is the dominant interface</li>\n<li>You want to reach users who don't have or use Discord/Slack</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>When to Use Discord or Slack Instead</h3>\n<p>LINE is not ideal when:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Multiple users need to collaborate with the agent simultaneously</strong> — Discord/Slack threads provide per-conversation isolation; LINE groups share a single session, leading to context pollution</li>\n<li><strong>You need long, multi-turn conversations in a team setting</strong> — thread-based platforms keep each conversation organized and searchable</li>\n<li><strong>You have many concurrent users (&gt;10)</strong> — LINE's always-on session model creates higher memory pressure; Discord/Slack's @mention-triggered sessions scale more efficiently</li>\n<li><strong>You need rich interaction patterns</strong> — Discord/Slack support reactions, file attachments with preview, and threaded discussions; LINE has a 5000-char message limit, no reactions, and no threads</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Summary: Best Fit by Scenario</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Recommended Platform</th>\n<th>Why</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Individual developer, mobile-first</td>\n<td><strong>LINE</strong></td>\n<td>1:1 DM works well, convenient on mobile</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Small team (2-5), async collaboration</td>\n<td><strong>Discord / Slack</strong></td>\n<td>Threads keep conversations organized</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Large team (10+), concurrent usage</td>\n<td><strong>Discord / Slack</strong></td>\n<td>On-demand sessions scale better</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Users in LINE-dominant regions</td>\n<td><strong>LINE</strong> (1:1) + <strong>Discord</strong> (team)</td>\n<td>Use LINE for personal, Discord for team</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Public-facing bot for community</td>\n<td><strong>Discord</strong></td>\n<td>Channels + threads + @mention gating</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. High-Level Design</h2>\n<h3>Architecture Overview</h3>\n<pre><code>┌──────────────┐\n│ LINE Platform │\n└──────┬───────┘\n       │ HTTPS POST (webhook)\n       ▼\n┌──────────────────┐\n│ TLS Termination  │  (CDN / Reverse Proxy / Ingress)\n└──────┬───────────┘\n       │ HTTP\n       ▼\n┌──────────────────┐\n│  Load Balancer   │\n└──────┬───────────┘\n       │\n       ▼\n┌──────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐\n│  K8s Service     │────▶│  OpenAB Pod                     │\n│  (ClusterIP)     │     │                                 │\n└──────────────────┘     │  ┌───────────┐  ┌────────────┐  │\n                         │  │ Webhook   │  │ Discord    │  │\n                         │  │ Handler   │  │ Adapter    │  │\n                         │  │ (:8080)   │  │ (WebSocket)│  │\n                         │  └─────┬─────┘  └─────┬──────┘  │\n                         │        │              │         │\n                         │        ▼              ▼         │\n                         │  ┌─────────────────────────┐    │\n                         │  │    Adapter Router        │    │\n                         │  └─────────┬───────────────┘    │\n                         │            │                    │\n                         │            ▼                    │\n                         │  ┌─────────────────────────┐    │\n                         │  │    ACP Session Pool      │    │\n                         │  │  ┌───────┐ ┌───────┐    │    │\n                         │  │  │kiro-cli│ │kiro-cli│...│    │\n                         │  │  └───────┘ └───────┘    │    │\n                         │  └─────────────────────────┘    │\n                         └─────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Message Flow</h3>\n<pre><code>1. LINE user sends message\n2. LINE Platform POSTs to webhook endpoint with JSON payload + HMAC signature\n3. Webhook handler validates signature using channel secret\n4. Handler extracts sender info, message text, and source (user/group/room)\n5. Handler determines session key:\n   - 1:1 DM  → line:{userId}\n   - Group   → line:{groupId}\n   - Room    → line:{roomId}\n6. Message is routed to AdapterRouter → ACP Session Pool → kiro-cli process\n7. Agent response is sent back via LINE Reply API (free) or Push Message API (fallback)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Hybrid Reply/Push Dispatch Flow</h3>\n<pre><code>LINE User                    Gateway                         OAB Core\n   │                            │                               │\n   │  message + replyToken      │                               │\n   │ ─────────────────────────▶ │                               │\n   │                            │  1. Verify HMAC signature     │\n   │                            │  2. Generate event_id (UUID)  │\n   │                            │  3. Cache:                    │\n   │                            │     event_id → replyToken     │\n   │                            │     (TTL 50s, max 10k)        │\n   │                            │                               │\n   │                            │  GatewayEvent { event_id }    │\n   │                            │ ─────────────────────────────▶│\n   │                            │                               │  Store event_id in\n   │                            │                               │  ChannelRef.origin_event_id\n   │                            │                               │\n   │                            │                               │  Agent processes...\n   │                            │                               │\n   │                            │  GatewayReply {               │\n   │                            │    reply_to: event_id         │\n   │                            │  }                            │\n   │                            │ ◀─────────────────────────────│\n   │                            │                               │\n   │                            │  4. Lookup cache(event_id)    │\n   │                            │     ├─ HIT + fresh            │\n   │     Reply API (FREE) ✅    │     │  → Reply API            │\n   │ ◀──────────────────────────│     │                         │\n   │                            │     ├─ HIT + expired          │\n   │     Push API (quota) 💰    │     │  → Push API fallback    │\n   │ ◀──────────────────────────│     │                         │\n   │                            │     └─ MISS                   │\n   │     Push API (quota) 💰    │        → Push API fallback    │\n   │ ◀──────────────────────────│                               │\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Reply Strategy: Hybrid Reply/Push Messages</h3>\n<p>LINE offers two reply mechanisms:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Reply message</strong>: uses a reply token, but the token expires in 1 minute (free).</li>\n<li><strong>Push message</strong>: no time limit, can send to any user/group at any time (consumes quota).</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Historically, OpenAB relied solely on <strong>push messages</strong> because agent processing can exceed the 1-minute reply token window. To optimize costs for free-tier accounts, OpenAB now uses a <strong>Hybrid Strategy</strong> implemented at the gateway level:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>The gateway caches incoming <code>replyToken</code>s keyed by <code>event_id</code> with a 50-second TTL.</li>\n<li>When OAB replies with a non-empty <code>reply_to</code> that matches a cached entry, the gateway routes the message via the free <strong>Reply API</strong>.</li>\n<li>If the token is expired, missing, or <code>reply_to</code> is empty, the gateway falls back to the <strong>Push API</strong>.</li>\n<li>A background task sweeps expired cache entries to prevent memory growth.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Architectural Differences from Discord/Slack</h2>\n<h3>Connectivity Model</h3>\n<p>Discord and Slack use <strong>outbound WebSocket</strong> — the bot connects out to the platform gateway. No inbound port, no public endpoint, no TLS termination needed.</p>\n<p>LINE uses <strong>inbound webhooks</strong> — the LINE platform sends HTTP POST requests to the bot. This flips the connectivity model:</p>\n<pre><code>Discord/Slack (outbound):\n  Pod ──WebSocket──▶ Platform Gateway\n  • No K8s Service needed\n  • No Ingress needed\n  • No TLS termination needed\n\nLINE (inbound):\n  Platform ──HTTPS POST──▶ TLS ──▶ LB ──▶ K8s Service ──▶ Pod :8080\n  • K8s Service required\n  • Ingress required\n  • TLS termination required (LINE mandates HTTPS with public CA cert)\n  • Pod has a publicly reachable attack surface\n</code></pre>\n<h3>What's Needed to Bridge the Gap</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Component</th>\n<th>Discord/Slack</th>\n<th>LINE</th>\n<th>Why</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>K8s Service</td>\n<td>Not needed</td>\n<td>Required</td>\n<td>Route inbound traffic to pod</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Ingress / Load Balancer</td>\n<td>Not needed</td>\n<td>Required</td>\n<td>Expose webhook endpoint externally</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>TLS termination</td>\n<td>Not needed</td>\n<td>Required</td>\n<td>LINE requires HTTPS with public CA cert</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Webhook signature validation</td>\n<td>N/A</td>\n<td>Required</td>\n<td>Verify requests are authentically from LINE (HMAC-SHA256)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>HTTP server in the pod</td>\n<td>Not needed</td>\n<td>Required</td>\n<td>Accept and parse incoming HTTP POST requests</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Webhook Server: LINE-Specific vs General-Purpose Gateway</h3>\n<p>Since LINE forces OpenAB to listen on an inbound port, a natural question arises: should this be a LINE-only handler, or a general-purpose webhook gateway that future platforms (Telegram, WhatsApp, etc.) can also use?</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Option</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Pros</th>\n<th>Cons</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>A. LINE-specific</strong></td>\n<td>Dedicated handler, only speaks LINE webhook format</td>\n<td>Simple, ships fast</td>\n<td>Not reusable for other platforms</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>B. General gateway</strong></td>\n<td>Shared HTTP server with <code>/webhook/{platform}</code> routing</td>\n<td>One listener, one TLS endpoint, extensible</td>\n<td>More upfront design</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>C. External queue</strong></td>\n<td>Webhook receiver → message queue → workers</td>\n<td>Horizontally scalable, decoupled</td>\n<td>Significant infra overhead</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Recommendation:</strong> Option A for v1 to unblock LINE support. Use a proper HTTP framework (e.g., <code>axum</code>) so that migrating to Option B is straightforward when a second webhook-based platform is added.</p>\n<h3>v2 Target Architecture: Independent Webhook Bridge Service</h3>\n<p>The preferred long-term direction is to extract the webhook handler into an <strong>independent service</strong> (separate container/pod), keeping OAB core outbound-only:</p>\n<pre><code>v2 architecture:\n\n  LINE Platform ──HTTPS POST──▶ [Webhook Bridge]  ──WebSocket──▶ OAB Pod\n  Discord Gateway ◀──WebSocket── OAB Pod\n  Telegram (future) ──HTTPS POST──▶ [Webhook Bridge] ──WebSocket──▶ OAB Pod\n\n  OAB only sees WebSocket connections — does not know or care about inbound HTTP.\n  Bridge acts as a &quot;platform gateway&quot; for webhook-based platforms, same role as\n  Discord Gateway or Slack Socket Mode server.\n</code></pre>\n<p>Benefits:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>OAB core stays pure outbound — no port to open, no TLS, no K8s Service</li>\n<li>Webhook platforms are fully opt-in — Discord/Slack-only users deploy nothing extra</li>\n<li>Bridge is independently scalable (stateless inbound path)</li>\n<li>Natural general-purpose gateway for LINE, Telegram, WhatsApp, etc.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Open design questions (require a follow-up ADR):</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>IPC protocol</strong>: WebSocket between bridge and OAB is the likely choice, but the event format and contract need to be defined</li>\n<li><strong>Reply path</strong>: does OAB call LINE Push API directly (OAB remains LINE-aware), or does OAB reply through the bridge (cleaner separation, but bridge becomes stateful with credentials)?</li>\n<li><strong>Session ownership</strong>: does the bridge or OAB own session routing?</li>\n<li><strong>Trust boundary, auth, reconnect, backpressure, dedup, ordering</strong></li>\n</ul>\n<p>This is scoped as a <strong>v2 initiative</strong>. v1 ships LINE support inside OAB (Option A) to unblock LINE users. The v2 bridge architecture will be designed with the benefit of real usage data from v1.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. ACP Session Model: Impact &amp; Mitigations</h2>\n<h3>How Sessions Map Across Platforms</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Session Key</th>\n<th>Trigger</th>\n<th>Isolation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Discord</td>\n<td><code>discord:{thread_id}</code></td>\n<td>@mention → new thread</td>\n<td>✅ Per-thread, fully isolated</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Slack</td>\n<td><code>slack:{thread_ts}</code></td>\n<td>@mention → new thread</td>\n<td>✅ Per-thread, fully isolated</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>LINE 1:1</td>\n<td><code>line:{userId}</code></td>\n<td>Any message</td>\n<td>⚠️ Per-user (similar to Discord DM)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>LINE Group</td>\n<td><code>line:{groupId}</code></td>\n<td>Any message</td>\n<td>❌ Shared across all group members</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>The fundamental difference: Discord/Slack have <strong>threads</strong> that provide natural per-conversation isolation. LINE has <strong>no thread primitive</strong> — all messages in a chat are a flat stream.</p>\n<h3>Why <code>line:{groupId}</code>, Not <code>line:{groupId}:{userId}</code></h3>\n<p>The session key for LINE groups is <code>line:{groupId}</code> (shared) rather than <code>line:{groupId}:{userId}</code> (per-user). This is a deliberate choice:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Bot replies are sent to the <strong>entire group</strong> via push message. The session boundary must match the <strong>visibility boundary</strong> — everyone in the group sees the same replies, so they should share the same context.</li>\n<li><code>line:{groupId}:{userId}</code> would create per-user isolation, but the bot's replies would still be visible to everyone. This creates a mismatch: private context driving public replies that make no sense to other group members.</li>\n<li>If per-conversation isolation is required, the correct answer is to use Discord or Slack, not to simulate threads within LINE.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Impact 1: Group Chat Context Pollution</h3>\n<p>In a LINE group, all members' messages feed into one shared agent session:</p>\n<pre><code>Alice: Review this Rust PR, focus on error handling\nBot:   [starts analyzing Rust code]\nBob:   Write me a Terraform module for EKS\nBot:   [context now has both Rust and Terraform — confused]\nCarol: What's for lunch?\nBot:   [context now includes lunch discussion — wasting tokens]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Effects:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Mixed intents from multiple users degrade agent response quality</li>\n<li>Context window fills with irrelevant messages, wasting tokens</li>\n<li>Bot replies are visible to everyone but may only make sense to one person</li>\n<li>No way to tell who the bot is responding to (no thread, no quote)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Impact 2: 1:1 DM Memory Pressure</h3>\n<p>Each session = one <code>kiro-cli</code> process (~350MB). Unlike Discord/Slack where sessions are <strong>on-demand</strong> (@mention triggers), LINE 1:1 sessions are <strong>always-on</strong> — every DM user has a persistent session.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> The ~350MB per-process figure is an observed estimate from typical kiro-cli usage. Actual memory varies by workload (context size, tool usage, file operations). Operators should profile their specific agent configuration before capacity planning.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Active Users</th>\n<th>Sessions</th>\n<th>Memory</th>\n<th>Pool (max_sessions=10)</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>5</td>\n<td>5</td>\n<td>~1.75 GB</td>\n<td>✅ Within limit</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>10</td>\n<td>10</td>\n<td>~3.5 GB</td>\n<td>⚠️ At limit</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>15</td>\n<td>15</td>\n<td>~5.25 GB</td>\n<td>❌ Eviction starts</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>30</td>\n<td>30</td>\n<td>~10.5 GB</td>\n<td>❌ Heavy thrashing</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>For comparison: a Discord server with 100 members might have 2-3 concurrent @mentions → 2-3 sessions. A LINE bot with 30 friends → potentially 30 concurrent sessions.</p>\n<p>When <code>max_sessions</code> is exceeded, the pool evicts the oldest idle session to make room.</p>\n<h4>What Happens When the Pool Is Full</h4>\n<p>With <code>max_sessions=10</code> and 10 active 1:1 DM users, the pool is at capacity (~3.5 GB memory):</p>\n<pre><code>Pool: [User1] [User2] [User3] ... [User10]   ← all 10 slots occupied\n\nUser11 sends a message:\n  1. Pool finds the oldest idle session (e.g., User3, idle for 20 min)\n  2.
