User3's session is suspended (session ID saved to disk)\n  3. A new kiro-cli process is spawned for User11\n  4. User11 gets a response — but with cold-start latency (~5-10s)\n\nUser3 comes back and sends a message:\n  1. Pool finds the oldest idle session again (e.g., User7)\n  2. User7 is suspended, User3's session is resumed from saved state\n  3. User3's conversation context is restored — but again with cold-start latency\n\nUser12 sends a message while User11 is still active:\n  1. Pool must evict someone — but fewer sessions are idle now\n  2. If all 10 sessions are actively processing, the new message queues\n     until a session becomes idle and can be evicted\n</code></pre>\n<p>Effects at scale:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>10 concurrent users</strong>: pool is full, no eviction yet. ~3.5 GB memory.</li>\n<li><strong>11-15 concurrent users</strong>: occasional eviction. Users experience intermittent cold-start delays (~5-10s). Context is preserved via session resume, but the swap adds latency.</li>\n<li><strong>20+ concurrent users</strong>: heavy thrashing. Most messages trigger an evict/resume cycle. The bot feels sluggish for everyone. Memory stays capped at ~3.5 GB but CPU spikes from constant process creation/teardown.</li>\n<li><strong>Worst case</strong>: all sessions are actively processing (no idle sessions to evict). New messages must wait until a session finishes its current task before it can be swapped out.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Impact 3: Always-On vs On-Demand</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th></th>\n<th>Discord/Slack</th>\n<th>LINE</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Trigger</td>\n<td>@mention required</td>\n<td>Every message triggers processing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Session creation</td>\n<td>Only when explicitly invoked</td>\n<td>Any DM or group message</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Concurrent sessions</td>\n<td>Few (most users aren't @mentioning)</td>\n<td>Many (every bot friend has a session)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Scaling characteristic</td>\n<td>Bounded by active @mentions</td>\n<td>Bounded by total bot users</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>This is the root cause of the scaling difference.</p>\n<h3>Mitigation Options</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>#</th>\n<th>Option</th>\n<th>Effect</th>\n<th>Trade-off</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>1</td>\n<td><strong>@mention gating</strong></td>\n<td>Only process messages that @mention the bot in groups; 1:1 DMs remain always-on</td>\n<td>Dramatically reduces group noise and session pressure; LINE API supports mention detection</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2</td>\n<td><strong>Lower session TTL</strong></td>\n<td><code>session_ttl_hours = 1</code> (default 24)</td>\n<td>Faster idle session reclaim, but returning users lose conversation context</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3</td>\n<td><strong>Larger node</strong></td>\n<td>More memory (e.g., 32GB) with higher <code>max_sessions</code></td>\n<td>Simple to implement; doesn't solve the fundamental scaling curve</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>4</td>\n<td><strong>Queue-based decoupling</strong></td>\n<td>Webhook → message queue → autoscaled worker pods</td>\n<td>Production-grade horizontal scaling; significant infrastructure investment</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>5</td>\n<td><strong>Lightweight agent mode</strong></td>\n<td>Reduce per-session memory footprint</td>\n<td>Fundamental fix, but out of scope for the LINE adapter</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>6</td>\n<td><strong>Session admission control</strong></td>\n<td>Reject or queue new sessions when pool is full and all sessions are active</td>\n<td>Protects active users from being evicted mid-conversation; see details below</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Session Admission Control (Option 6)</h4>\n<p>The current pool behavior is &quot;auto-evict oldest&quot; — the 11th user always gets in by kicking someone out. This creates unpredictable disruptions for active users.</p>\n<p><strong>Design goal:</strong> protect active sessions from disruptive eviction while giving overload behavior that is explicit and predictable.</p>\n<p>A more robust approach is a <strong>hybrid admission strategy</strong>:</p>\n<pre><code>New session request arrives:\n  1. Pool has free slot                          → open session immediately\n  2. Pool full, idle session exists (not processing\n     and idle_for &gt;= idle_threshold)             → evict oldest idle, open new\n  3. Pool full, ALL sessions active or below\n     idle_threshold                              → apply admission_policy\n       - evict_idle_then_reject: reply &quot;All agents are busy, please try again shortly&quot;\n       - evict_idle_then_queue:  add to waiting queue, notify when slot opens\n</code></pre>\n<p>Parameters:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Parameter</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Recommended v1 Default</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>idle_threshold</code></td>\n<td>Minimum idle time before a session is eligible for eviction. &quot;Idle&quot; means not currently processing an in-flight prompt — not just &quot;no recent message.&quot;</td>\n<td><code>10m</code></td>\n<td>LINE is mobile-first; users commonly pause 2-3 minutes between messages. <code>5m</code> is too aggressive for general use.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>admission_policy</code></td>\n<td>What to do when pool is full and no session meets <code>idle_threshold</code>. Three-state enum: <code>evict_idle_then_reject</code>, <code>evict_idle_then_queue</code>, <code>always_evict_idle</code> (current behavior).</td>\n<td><code>evict_idle_then_reject</code></td>\n<td>Start with deterministic reject. Queue adds scheduling/fairness/timeout/stale-response complexity — defer until usage data justifies it.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_queue_size</code></td>\n<td>Maximum waiting queue depth. Only applies when <code>admission_policy = evict_idle_then_queue</code>.</td>\n<td><code>0</code> (disabled)</td>\n<td>Queue is for short waits, not job backlogs. Keep small (<code>≤ 3</code>) if enabled. LINE's flat chat model means queued replies arrive late into a conversation that has moved on — poor UX at depth &gt; 3. Queuing also requires storing the original message and userId, then sending a push message to re-trigger processing when a slot opens — this is not a lightweight feature.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_wait_duration</code></td>\n<td>Maximum time a queued request waits before being rejected with a busy message. Only applies when queuing is enabled.</td>\n<td><code>0s</code> (disabled)</td>\n<td>Without this, queue has depth but no SLA. <code>30s</code>-<code>60s</code> is reasonable if queuing is enabled. Directly constrains user-perceived latency.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Recommended v1 defaults:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>idle_threshold       = 10m\nadmission_policy     = evict_idle_then_reject\nmax_queue_size       = 0\nmax_wait_duration    = 0s\n</code></pre>\n<p>v1 uses deterministic reject — no queuing. This keeps the behavior simple and predictable. Queuing can be enabled in a future iteration once real usage data is available to tune <code>max_queue_size</code> and <code>max_wait_duration</code>.</p>\n<p>Combined with existing mechanisms:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mechanism</th>\n<th>Trigger</th>\n<th>Effect</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>TTL expiry</strong></td>\n<td>Session idle &gt; <code>session_ttl_hours</code></td>\n<td>Auto-reclaim, frees slot</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Idle threshold eviction</strong></td>\n<td>Pool full + idle session exists (idle ≥ <code>idle_threshold</code>, no in-flight prompt)</td>\n<td>Reclaim oldest idle session for new user</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Hard cap reject</strong></td>\n<td>Pool full + all sessions active or below threshold</td>\n<td>New user gets &quot;busy&quot; message</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Queue</strong> (future)</td>\n<td>Pool full + queuing enabled</td>\n<td>New user waits up to <code>max_wait_duration</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Manual delete</strong></td>\n<td>Operator runs session delete command</td>\n<td>Force-free a specific slot</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Recommended Approach</h3>\n<p>For v1:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>1:1 DM</strong>: per-user session is the correct model, analogous to Discord DM</li>\n<li><strong>Group chat</strong>: per-group shared session is acceptable for v1. LINE group chat functions as a <strong>&quot;shared-room assistant&quot;</strong> — not a thread-equivalent collaboration tool. If the use case requires per-conversation isolation, the platform choice should be Discord or Slack, not LINE with simulated threads.</li>\n<li><strong>@mention gating</strong>: strongly recommended as a fast follow-up — converts LINE from always-on to on-demand, aligning its scaling characteristics with Discord/Slack</li>\n<li><strong>Capacity planning</strong>: document the memory math so operators can size their infrastructure appropriately. The default <code>max_sessions=10</code> is configurable via <code>pool.max_sessions</code> in <code>config.toml</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Summary</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Discord/Slack</th>\n<th>LINE</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Connectivity</td>\n<td>Outbound WebSocket</td>\n<td>Inbound webhook (HTTP POST)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>K8s Service / Ingress</td>\n<td>Not needed</td>\n<td>Required</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>TLS termination</td>\n<td>Not needed</td>\n<td>Required (public CA cert)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Thread support</td>\n<td>Yes → per-conversation isolation</td>\n<td>No → flat conversation stream</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Session isolation</td>\n<td>Per-thread</td>\n<td>Per-user (1:1) / Per-group (shared)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Trigger mechanism</td>\n<td>@mention (on-demand)</td>\n<td>All messages (always-on)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Session scaling</td>\n<td>~2-3 concurrent</td>\n<td>~N total bot users</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Memory pressure</td>\n<td>Low</td>\n<td>High (350MB × active users)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Consequences</h2>\n<h3>Positive</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>LINE users can interact with OpenAB agents without switching to Discord or Slack</li>\n<li>The inbound webhook pattern opens the door for future webhook-based platforms (Telegram, WhatsApp, etc.)</li>\n<li>Using <code>axum</code> for the HTTP server provides a solid foundation for a general-purpose webhook gateway</li>\n<li>Hybrid reply/push strategy optimizes cost: the gateway opportunistically uses the free Reply API when the agent responds within the token TTL, falling back to Push API for longer-running tasks</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Negative</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Deployment complexity increases: LINE requires K8s Service, Ingress, TLS termination, and a publicly reachable endpoint — none of which Discord/Slack need</li>\n<li>Group chats share a single session, leading to context pollution when multiple users interact simultaneously</li>\n<li>LINE's always-on trigger model creates higher memory pressure and session pool contention compared to Discord/Slack's on-demand @mention model</li>\n<li>Operators must perform capacity planning (memory per session × expected user count) that wasn't necessary for Discord/Slack-only deployments</li>\n<li>v1 couples inbound HTTP handling to the OAB process, breaking the outbound-only connectivity model of Discord/Slack. Planned extraction to an independent webhook bridge service in v2.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Compliance</h2>\n<p>To ensure this ADR is followed in implementation and future changes:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Webhook correctness</strong>: Webhook handling must validate the LINE signature against the exact raw request body bytes after the full HTTP body has been read according to protocol framing. Implementations must not use hand-rolled TCP parsing, lossy UTF-8 conversion, or reconstructed JSON for signature verification. A proper HTTP framework (e.g., <code>axum</code>) is the default acceptable implementation approach. Two specific failure modes make raw TCP handling unacceptable:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Partial read</strong>: a single <code>read()</code> call does not guarantee the full HTTP request arrives in one TCP segment. Truncated bodies cause HMAC validation to fail silently — messages are dropped with no error logged.</li>\n<li><strong>Lossy UTF-8 HMAC mismatch</strong>: if the raw buffer is converted to string via lossy UTF-8 before computing HMAC, any non-UTF-8 byte is replaced with <code>U+FFFD</code>, causing signature verification to fail on otherwise-valid requests.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Both are <strong>silent failures</strong> — no crash, no log, just dropped messages. The webhook signature is defined over the original request body bytes, so any lossy decoding or body reconstruction changes the verification surface and is architecturally invalid. PRs introducing raw TCP HTTP handling must be rejected with a reference to this ADR.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Session key convention</strong>: LINE sessions must use <code>line:{userId}</code> for 1:1 DMs and <code>line:{groupId}</code> for group chats. Deviations require a new ADR.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Documentation</strong>: any LINE adapter PR must include or update operator-facing documentation covering:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Group chat shared session behavior and its limitations</li>\n<li>Capacity planning guidance (memory math per session count)</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Group chat production use</strong>: @mention gating should be implemented before promoting group chat support to production-ready status.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Future webhook platforms</strong>: when adding a second webhook-based platform, evaluate migrating to a general-purpose webhook gateway (Section 3, Option B) before building another platform-specific handler.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Platform semantics</strong>: LINE group support must not be described or documented as thread-equivalent to Discord/Slack. LINE groups are &quot;shared-room assistants&quot; with fundamentally different isolation and scaling characteristics.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Version:</strong> 0.2</li>\n<li><strong>Changelog:</strong>\n<ul>\n<li>0.2 (2026-04-28): Hybrid Reply/Push strategy implemented (#608). Updated status to Accepted. Added dispatch flow diagram. Reply strategy section rewritten from Push-only to hybrid. Core propagates <code>event_id</code> via <code>ChannelRef.origin_event_id</code> (#619).</li>\n<li>0.1 (2026-04-22): Initial proposed version</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>References</h2>\n<p>This ADR follows the structure and process described in the following sources, adapted with project-specific sections (User Story, High-Level Design, Platform Comparison, Session Model Analysis) to fit OpenAB's needs.</p>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions.html\">Documenting Architecture Decisions</a> — Michael Nygard (2011). The original blog post that popularized ADRs. Defines the minimal template: Context, Decision, Status, Consequences.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://adr.github.io/\">ADR GitHub Organization</a> — Community hub for ADR templates, tooling, and academic references. Includes the Y-statement format from Zdun et al.'s &quot;Sustainable Architectural Decisions.&quot;</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.arc42.org/section-9/\">arc42 Section 9: Architecture Decisions</a> — European software architecture documentation standard. Emphasizes recording rejected alternatives and providing timestamps.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/architectural-decision-records/adr-process.html\">AWS Prescriptive Guidance — Using ADRs to streamline technical decision-making</a> — Extends Nygard's template with Compliance and Notes (version, changelog) sections, and defines the ADR lifecycle (Proposed → Accepted → Superseded).</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/architect-role/architecture-decision-record\">Azure Well-Architected Framework — Architecture Decision Record</a> — Microsoft's adoption of ADRs within the Azure Well-Architected Framework.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: LINE Messaging API Adapter"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/multi-platform-adapters",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Multi-Platform Adapter Architecture</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Partially Implemented — Phase 1+3 landed via #259 (Slack adapter)</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-04-06</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n<li><strong>Reviewers:</strong> @dogzzdogzz, @antigenius0910</li>\n<li><strong>Tracking issues:</strong> #86, #93</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Decision</h2>\n<p>Define a platform-agnostic adapter layer for agent-broker so it can serve Discord, Telegram, Slack, and future chat platforms through a single unified architecture. The ACP session pool and agent backend remain unchanged — only the &quot;front door&quot; becomes pluggable.</p>\n<p><strong>Primary contract: simultaneous multi-platform (Contract B).</strong> A single running instance can serve Discord + Slack (+ future adapters) concurrently, sharing one <code>SessionPool</code> with platform-namespaced session keys. This was validated by #259 which merged the Slack adapter with Discord + Slack running in one process.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Contract A (pluggable single-platform per deployment) is a subset of B and works automatically — deploy with only one <code>[platform]</code> section in config.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>2. Motivation</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>agent-broker was originally hard-wired to Discord via <code>serenity</code></li>\n<li>#86 proposes a Telegram adapter, #93 proposes Slack — both require similar abstractions</li>\n<li>Without a shared trait, each adapter will duplicate session routing, message splitting, reaction handling, and streaming logic</li>\n<li>A clean adapter boundary enables running multiple adapters simultaneously (e.g. Discord + Slack in one deployment, validated by #259)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Current Architecture (post-#259)</h2>\n<pre><code>                    ┌─────────────────┐\n                    │  Discord Users  │\n                    └────────┬────────┘\n                             │ Gateway WS (serenity)\n                             ▼\n                    ┌─────────────────┐\n                    │ DiscordAdapter  │──┐\n                    └─────────────────┘  │\n                                         │  impl ChatAdapter\n┌─────────────────┐                      │\n│  Slack Users    │                      ▼\n└────────┬────────┘             ┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐\n         │ Socket Mode (WS)     │   AdapterRouter  │────►│ SessionPool  │\n         ▼                      │                  │     │              │\n┌─────────────────┐             │  - route message │     └──────┬───────┘\n│  SlackAdapter   │────────────►│  - manage threads│            │ ACP stdio\n└─────────────────┘             │  - stream edits  │     ┌──────▼───────┐\n                                └─────────────────┘     │ AcpConnection │\n                                         ▲              └───────────────┘\n                                         │\n                                ┌─────────────────┐\n                                │ TelegramAdapter  │  (future — Phase 2)\n                                └─────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. ChatAdapter Trait</h2>\n<p>The core abstraction. Each platform implements this trait.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">#[async_trait]\npub trait ChatAdapter: Send + Sync + 'static {\n    /// Platform name for logging and config (&quot;discord&quot;, &quot;telegram&quot;, &quot;slack&quot;)\n    fn platform(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;'static str;\n\n    /// Maximum message length for this platform\n    fn message_limit(&amp;self) -&gt; usize;\n\n    /// Start listening for events. Blocks until shutdown.\n    async fn run(&amp;self, router: Arc&lt;AdapterRouter&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt;;\n\n    /// Send a new message, returns platform-specific message ID\n    async fn send_message(&amp;self, channel: &amp;ChannelRef, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;MessageRef&gt;;\n\n    /// Edit an existing message in-place\n    async fn edit_message(&amp;self, msg: &amp;MessageRef, content: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt;;\n\n    /// Create a thread/topic from a message, returns thread channel ref\n    async fn create_thread(&amp;self, channel: &amp;ChannelRef, trigger_msg: &amp;MessageRef, title: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;ChannelRef&gt;;\n\n    /// Add a reaction/emoji to a message\n    async fn add_reaction(&amp;self, msg: &amp;MessageRef, emoji: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt;;\n\n    /// Remove a reaction/emoji from a message\n    async fn remove_reaction(&amp;self, msg: &amp;MessageRef, emoji: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt;;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Design decisions:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>message_limit()</code> is on the trait (not hardcoded in router) so <code>AdapterRouter</code> can call <code>adapter.message_limit()</code> for <code>split_message</code> without matching on platform strings. (Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #1)</li>\n<li>Emoji handling: config stores Unicode emoji, each adapter converts internally to platform-specific format (e.g. Slack short names). (Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #6)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Platform-Agnostic References</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">/// Identifies a channel/thread/topic across platforms\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Hash, Eq, PartialEq)]\npub struct ChannelRef {\n    pub platform: String,           // &quot;discord&quot;, &quot;telegram&quot;, &quot;slack&quot;\n    pub channel_id: String,         // platform-native channel ID\n    pub thread_id: Option&lt;String&gt;,  // thread within channel (Slack thread_ts, Telegram topic_id)\n    pub parent_id: Option&lt;String&gt;,  // parent channel if thread-as-channel (Discord threads)\n}\n\nimpl ChannelRef {\n    /// Whether this ref points to a thread (either model)\n    pub fn is_thread(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {\n        self.thread_id.is_some() || self.parent_id.is_some()\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>ChannelRef</code> supports two threading models (Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #2):</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Thread-as-reply-chain</strong> (Slack, Telegram): same <code>channel_id</code>, identified by <code>thread_id</code></li>\n<li><strong>Thread-as-child-channel</strong> (Discord): separate <code>channel_id</code> with <code>parent_id</code> pointing to parent</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">/// Identifies a message across platforms\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct MessageRef {\n    pub platform: String,\n    pub channel: ChannelRef,\n    pub message_id: String,\n}\n\n/// Sender identity\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct SenderContext {\n    pub schema: String,        // &quot;openab.sender.v1&quot;\n    pub sender_id: String,\n    pub sender_name: String,\n    pub display_name: String,\n    pub channel: String,       // platform name\n    pub channel_id: String,\n    pub is_bot: bool,\n}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. AdapterRouter</h2>\n<p>Shared logic extracted from <code>discord.rs</code> that is platform-independent:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">pub struct AdapterRouter {\n    pool: Arc&lt;SessionPool&gt;,\n    reactions_config: ReactionsConfig,\n}\n\nimpl AdapterRouter {\n    /// Called by any adapter when a user message arrives.\n    /// Handles: session creation, prompt injection, streaming, reactions.\n    pub async fn handle_message(\n        &amp;self,\n        adapter: Arc&lt;dyn ChatAdapter&gt;,\n        channel: &amp;ChannelRef,\n        sender: &amp;SenderContext,\n        prompt: &amp;str,\n        trigger_msg: &amp;MessageRef,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt;;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Key design decisions:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>adapter</code> parameter is <code>Arc&lt;dyn ChatAdapter&gt;</code> (not <code>&amp;dyn</code>) so it can be moved into <code>tokio::spawn</code> for the edit-streaming background task. (Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #5)</li>\n<li>Thread creation decision (&quot;already in a thread?&quot;) lives in the router, using <code>ChannelRef::is_thread()</code>. Each adapter provides enough info in <code>ChannelRef</code> for the router to decide. (Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #3)</li>\n<li><code>StatusReactionController</code> is decoupled from Serenity types — it receives <code>Arc&lt;dyn ChatAdapter&gt;</code> and calls <code>add_reaction()</code> / <code>remove_reaction()</code> through the trait. (Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #4)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>The router owns:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Session pool interaction (<code>get_or_create</code>, <code>with_connection</code>)</li>\n<li>Sender context injection (<code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> XML wrapping)</li>\n<li>Edit-streaming loop (1.5s interval, message splitting via <code>adapter.message_limit()</code>)</li>\n<li>Reaction state machine (queued → thinking → tool → done/error)</li>\n<li>Thread creation decision (new thread vs. existing thread)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Each adapter only needs to:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Listen for platform events</li>\n<li>Determine if the message should be processed (allowed channels, @mention, thread check)</li>\n<li>Call <code>router.handle_message()</code></li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Platform Comparison</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Feature</th>\n<th>Discord</th>\n<th>Telegram</th>\n<th>Slack</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Connection</td>\n<td>Gateway WebSocket (<code>serenity</code>)</td>\n<td>Bot API polling / webhook (<code>teloxide</code>)</td>\n<td>Socket Mode WebSocket / Events API</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Threading model</td>\n<td>Thread-as-child-channel</td>\n<td>Forum topics (thread-as-reply)</td>\n<td>Thread-as-reply-chain (<code>thread_ts</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Message limit</td>\n<td>2000 chars</td>\n<td>4096 chars</td>\n<td>4000 chars (blocks: 3000)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Edit support</td>\n<td>✅ Full</td>\n<td>✅ Full</td>\n<td>✅ Full</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Reactions</td>\n<td>✅ Unicode + custom emoji</td>\n<td>✅ Unicode emoji</td>\n<td>✅ Unicode + custom emoji (short names)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Trigger</td>\n<td><code>@mention</code></td>\n<td><code>@mention</code> or any message (configurable)</td>\n<td><code>@mention</code> or app_mention event</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot message filtering</td>\n<td><code>msg.author.bot</code></td>\n<td><code>msg.from.is_bot</code></td>\n<td><code>event.bot_id</code> present</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Auth</td>\n<td>Bot token</td>\n<td>Bot token</td>\n<td>Bot token + App token (Socket Mode)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Config Design</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Enable one or more adapters. Multiple can run simultaneously.\n\n[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\nallowed_channels = [&quot;1234567890&quot;]\n\n[telegram]\nbot_token = &quot;${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\nmode = &quot;personal&quot;                    # &quot;personal&quot; or &quot;team&quot; (see #86)\nallowed_users = []                   # empty = deny all (secure by default, per #91)\n\n[slack]\nbot_token = &quot;${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\napp_token = &quot;${SLACK_APP_TOKEN}&quot;     # for Socket Mode\nallowed_channels = [&quot;C1234567890&quot;]\n\n# Agent and pool config remain unchanged\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;kiro-cli&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 10\nsession_ttl_hours = 24\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Startup Behavior</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>agent-broker reads config and starts an adapter for each <code>[platform]</code> section present</li>\n<li>If no adapter section is configured → error and exit</li>\n<li>Each adapter runs as a separate tokio task, sharing the same <code>SessionPool</code></li>\n<li>Session keys are namespaced: <code>discord:{thread_id}</code>, <code>telegram:{topic_id}</code>, <code>slack:{thread_ts}</code></li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Message Size Handling</h2>\n<p>Each platform has different message limits. The <code>format::split_message</code> function accepts a configurable limit, sourced from <code>adapter.message_limit()</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">pub fn split_message(content: &amp;str, max_len: usize) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt;;\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Max chars</th>\n<th><code>message_limit()</code></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Discord</td>\n<td>2000</td>\n<td>1900 (safety margin)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Telegram</td>\n<td>4096</td>\n<td>4000</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Slack</td>\n<td>4000</td>\n<td>3900</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Reaction Mapping</h2>\n<p>The <code>StatusReactionController</code> uses <code>Arc&lt;dyn ChatAdapter&gt;</code> to call <code>add_reaction()</code> / <code>remove_reaction()</code>, fully decoupled from any platform SDK.</p>\n<p>Config stores Unicode emoji. Each adapter converts internally:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Discord: Unicode passthrough</li>\n<li>Slack: Unicode → short name mapping (e.g. <code>👀</code> → <code>eyes</code>)</li>\n<li>Telegram: Unicode passthrough</li>\n</ul>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Action</th>\n<th>Discord</th>\n<th>Telegram</th>\n<th>Slack</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Add reaction</td>\n<td><code>create_reaction()</code></td>\n<td><code>set_message_reaction()</code></td>\n<td><code>reactions.add</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Remove reaction</td>\n<td><code>delete_reaction()</code></td>\n<td><code>set_message_reaction()</code> (empty)</td>\n<td><code>reactions.remove</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. Security Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Secure by default</strong> (#91): empty allowlist = deny all, for every platform</li>\n<li><strong>Bot message filtering</strong>: each adapter must ignore messages from bots to prevent loops</li>\n<li><strong>Token isolation</strong>: each platform's tokens are independent env vars</li>\n<li><strong>Session namespace isolation</strong>: <code>discord:123</code> and <code>slack:123</code> are separate sessions even if IDs collide</li>\n<li><strong>Rate limiting</strong>: platform-specific rate limits should be respected (Discord 5/5s, Slack 1/s per channel, Telegram 30/s)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>11. Implementation Phases</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n<th>Status</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 1</strong></td>\n<td>Extract <code>ChatAdapter</code> trait + <code>AdapterRouter</code>, refactor Discord to implement trait</td>\n<td>✅ Merged (#259)</td>\n<td>Pure refactor + Slack adapter landed together</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 2</strong></td>\n<td>Telegram adapter (<code>teloxide</code>), personal + team modes</td>\n<td>Not started</td>\n<td>Depends on #86</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 3</strong></td>\n<td>Slack adapter (Socket Mode), channel threading</td>\n<td>✅ Merged (#259)</td>\n<td>Includes simultaneous Discord + Slack</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 4</strong></td>\n<td>Per-adapter session soft limits, streaming timeout</td>\n<td>Not started</td>\n<td>See Known Limitations</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 5</strong></td>\n<td>Platform-specific features: Slack blocks, Telegram inline keyboards, Discord embeds</td>\n<td>Not started</td>\n<td>Text-only for v1; extend via <code>PlatformExt</code> traits later</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>12. Kubernetes / Helm Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Single image supports all adapters (all compiled in)</li>\n<li>Helm <code>values.yaml</code> gains <code>telegram.*</code> and <code>slack.*</code> sections</li>\n<li>Adapter selection is config-driven, not build-time</li>\n<li>PVC storage structure unchanged — auth tokens are per-agent, not per-platform</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>13. Testing Strategy</h2>\n<p>(Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #8)</p>\n<h3>MockAdapter</h3>\n<p>Define a <code>MockAdapter</code> (in-memory, no network) that implements <code>ChatAdapter</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">pub struct MockAdapter {\n    pub sent_messages: Arc&lt;Mutex&lt;Vec&lt;(ChannelRef, String)&gt;&gt;&gt;,\n    pub edited_messages: Arc&lt;Mutex&lt;Vec&lt;(MessageRef, String)&gt;&gt;&gt;,\n    pub reactions: Arc&lt;Mutex&lt;Vec&lt;(MessageRef, String)&gt;&gt;&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl ChatAdapter for MockAdapter {\n    fn platform(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;'static str { &quot;mock&quot; }\n    fn message_limit(&amp;self) -&gt; usize { 2000 }\n    // ... record calls for assertion\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Test coverage</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Layer</th>\n<th>What to test</th>\n<th>How</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AdapterRouter</code></td>\n<td>Session routing, streaming, reactions, thread creation</td>\n<td>Unit tests with <code>MockAdapter</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ChatAdapter</code> impls</td>\n<td>Platform-specific API calls, emoji mapping, error handling</td>\n<td>Integration tests per adapter (can mock HTTP)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ChannelRef</code></td>\n<td><code>is_thread()</code> logic for both threading models</td>\n<td>Unit tests</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>End-to-end</td>\n<td>Full message flow through router → pool → ACP</td>\n<td>Integration test with <code>MockAdapter</code> + real <code>SessionPool</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Phase 1 acceptance criteria (validated by #259)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>✅ Existing Discord behavior passes through the new trait boundary</li>\n<li>✅ <code>MockAdapter</code> can drive <code>AdapterRouter</code> in tests</li>\n<li>✅ No behavior change for Discord-only deployments</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>14. Resolved Questions</h2>\n<p>(Feedback: @dogzzdogzz #7, @antigenius0910)</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>#</th>\n<th>Question</th>\n<th>Decision</th>\n<th>Rationale</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>1</td>\n<td>Shared vs separate <code>SessionPool</code></td>\n<td><strong>Shared</strong></td>\n<td>Already namespaced by platform prefix; separate pools add complexity with no isolation benefit</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2</td>\n<td>Platform prefix in session keys</td>\n<td><strong>Yes, always prefix</strong></td>\n<td>IDs from different platforms can collide; prefix cost is negligible. Format: <code>{platform}:{thread_id}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3</td>\n<td>Global vs per-adapter <code>max_sessions</code></td>\n<td><strong>Global hard cap + per-adapter soft limit</strong></td>\n<td>Prevents one noisy platform from starving others. Global cap in <code>[pool]</code>, soft limits in each <code>[platform]</code> section</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>4</td>\n<td>Rich messages in v1</td>\n<td><strong>Text-only</strong></td>\n<td>Ship the abstraction first; rich messages are additive and platform-divergent</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>5</td>\n<td>Platform-specific features</td>\n<td><strong>Defer to Phase 5</strong></td>\n<td>Keep <code>ChatAdapter</code> minimal for v1; extend via <code>PlatformExt</code> traits or feature flags later</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>6</td>\n<td>Primary contract: A (single) vs B (simultaneous)</td>\n<td><strong>B — simultaneous multi-platform</strong></td>\n<td>Validated by #259. Contract A is a subset that works automatically</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>15. Known Limitations</h2>\n<p>(Feedback: @antigenius0910)</p>\n<h3>Resolved: SessionPool lock contention</h3>\n<p>@antigenius0910 raised that <code>SessionPool::with_connection()</code> held a write lock for the full prompt duration, which would serialize all sessions across platforms under Contract B.</p>\n<p><strong>Status: Resolved.</strong> The current implementation uses read lock + <code>Arc</code> clone + drop lock, then locks only the individual connection:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">pub async fn with_connection&lt;F, R&gt;(&amp;self, thread_id: &amp;str, f: F) -&gt; Result&lt;R&gt; {\n    let conn = {\n        let state = self.state.read().await;  // read lock, not write\n        state.active.get(thread_id).cloned()   // clone Arc\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(&quot;no connection&quot;))?\n    };  // state lock dropped here\n    let mut conn = conn.lock().await;  // lock individual connection\n    f(&amp;mut conn).await\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Multiple adapters' sessions can now execute concurrently without blocking each other.</p>\n<h3>Open: No streaming timeout</h3>\n<p>A hung ACP session (e.g. agent process stuck, infinite tool loop) will hold its connection <code>Mutex</code> indefinitely. Under Contract B, this doesn't block other sessions (each has its own <code>Mutex</code>), but it does permanently consume one session slot from the pool.</p>\n<p><strong>Suggested fix (follow-up issue):</strong> Add a configurable timeout to <code>with_connection</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">let mut conn = tokio::time::timeout(\n    Duration::from_secs(config.streaming_timeout_secs),\n    conn.lock()\n).await.map_err(|_| anyhow!(&quot;session timeout&quot;))??;\n</code></pre>\n<p>This would allow the pool to reclaim hung sessions and is especially important as the number of simultaneous adapters grows.</p>\n<hr />\n<p><em>This RFC was updated on 2026-04-21 to integrate review feedback from @dogzzdogzz (8 architectural points) and @antigenius0910 (Contract A vs B question), and to reflect the merge of #259 (Slack adapter implementing Phase 1+3).</em></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Multi-Platform Adapter Architecture"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/openab-agent",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: openab-agent — Native Rust Coding Agent with Built-in ACP</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-26</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @chaodu-agent</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Motivation</h2>\n<p>Today, every coding agent in OpenAB follows the same pattern:</p>\n<pre><code>openab (Rust) ──stdio JSON-RPC──► adapter (Node/Rust) ──spawns──► CLI agent ──HTTP──► LLM API\n</code></pre>\n<p>This introduces 3–4 layers of indirection, each with its own runtime, dependencies, and failure modes. Every agent requires:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>A separate Dockerfile (300–800MB images)</li>\n<li>A Node.js or Python runtime</li>\n<li>An ACP adapter wrapper (pi-acp, codex-acp, agy-acp, etc.)</li>\n<li>npm/pip supply-chain management</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Meanwhile, the actual work an agent does is simple:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Receive a prompt</li>\n<li>Call an LLM API (HTTP POST + SSE)</li>\n<li>Execute tool calls (read/write/edit/bash)</li>\n<li>Return the result</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Proposal:</strong> Build <code>openab-agent</code> — a single Rust binary that is both the ACP server and the coding agent, with no external runtime, no wrapper, and no adapter layer.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Design</h2>\n<h3>Architecture</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─ openab-agent (single Rust binary) ──────────────┐\n│                                                   │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  ACP Layer (stdin/stdout JSON-RPC)          │  │\n│  │  - session/new, session/prompt, cancel      │  │\n│  └──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘  │\n│                     │                             │\n│  ┌──────────────────▼──────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  Agent Core                                 │  │\n│  │  - Prompt assembly (system + user + tools)  │  │\n│  │  - Tool dispatch loop                       │  │\n│  │  - Session tree (branching history)         │  │\n│  └──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘  │\n│                     │                             │\n│  ┌──────────────────▼──────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  LLM Client (reqwest + SSE)                 │  │\n│  │  - OpenAI-compatible (GPT, Codex, DeepSeek) │  │\n│  │  - Anthropic (Claude)                       │  │\n│  │  - Google (Gemini)                          │  │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                   │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  Tools (4 only)                             │  │\n│  │  - read: file/directory reading             │  │\n│  │  - write: file creation                     │  │\n│  │  - edit: string replacement in files        │  │\n│  │  - bash: command execution (sandboxed)      │  │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                   │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Comparison with Existing Agents</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Existing (e.g. Pi, Codex)</th>\n<th>openab-agent</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Layers</td>\n<td>openab → adapter → CLI → LLM</td>\n<td>openab → <strong>agent</strong> → LLM</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Runtime</td>\n<td>Node.js / Python</td>\n<td>None (static binary)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Image size</td>\n<td>300–800MB</td>\n<td>~20MB (distroless)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cold start</td>\n<td>1–3s</td>\n<td>&lt;50ms</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>ACP support</td>\n<td>Requires wrapper</td>\n<td>Native, zero overhead</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Dependencies</td>\n<td>npm ecosystem</td>\n<td>Minimal crates</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Supply-chain risk</td>\n<td>High (node_modules)</td>\n<td>Low (cargo audit)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Required Crates</h3>\n<p>Only four crates are needed beyond what openab core already uses:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>reqwest</code> — HTTP client (LLM API calls)</li>\n<li><code>serde</code> / <code>serde_json</code> — JSON serialization</li>\n<li><code>tokio</code> — async runtime + process management (<code>tokio::process</code>) (already used in openab)</li>\n<li><code>futures</code> — <code>Stream</code> trait and <code>BoxStream</code> for async streaming</li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> <code>tokio-process</code> was merged into <code>tokio::process</code> in tokio 0.2 and the standalone crate is deprecated. All process spawning uses <code>tokio::process::Command</code> directly.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Nothing else. Can share code with openab core (ACP types, session pool logic).</p>\n<h3>Key Advantage: Deep Integration</h3>\n<p>Because we own the agent and it shares the same language as openab core, deep integration is possible — a future library mode can bypass stdio entirely, using in-process function calls to eliminate all IPC overhead.</p>\n<h3>Design Principles (inspired by Pi)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Minimal tool surface</strong> — 4 tools only (read, write, edit, bash). Maximizes context window for actual code.</li>\n<li><strong>Tiny system prompt</strong> — Agent instructions fit in ~500 tokens. No bloated tool descriptions.</li>\n<li><strong>Multi-model</strong> — Provider-agnostic. Switch models via config or mid-session command.</li>\n<li><strong>Session trees</strong> — Branching conversation history. Explore multiple approaches without losing context.</li>\n<li><strong>No SDK dependency</strong> — LLM APIs are just HTTP. A thin <code>reqwest</code> client (~300 lines) covers all providers.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. LLM Client Design</h2>\n<p>The LLM client is intentionally thin — no SDK, just HTTP:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">use futures::stream::BoxStream;\n\n// Unified trait for all providers\ntrait LlmProvider: Send + Sync {\n    fn chat&lt;'a&gt;(\n        &amp;'a self,\n        messages: &amp;'a [Message],\n        tools: &amp;'a [Tool],\n    ) -&gt; Pin&lt;Box&lt;dyn Future&lt;Output = Result&lt;BoxStream&lt;'a, Event&gt;&gt;&gt; + Send + 'a&gt;&gt;;\n}\n\n// Implementations are ~100 lines each\nstruct OpenAiProvider { base_url: String, api_key: String, model: String }\nstruct AnthropicProvider { api_key: String, model: String }\nstruct GoogleProvider { api_key: String, model: String }\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> <code>Stream</code> is a trait (from <code>futures</code>), not a concrete type. Returning it directly from a trait method would not compile. We use <code>BoxStream&lt;'a, Event&gt;</code> (i.e., <code>Pin&lt;Box&lt;dyn Stream&lt;Item = Event&gt; + Send + 'a&gt;&gt;</code>) to provide a type-erased, object-safe return type. The <code>async fn</code> in traits is similarly desugared to a boxed future for object safety.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>All three major APIs follow the same pattern:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>POST JSON body with messages + tool definitions</li>\n<li>Stream SSE events back</li>\n<li>Parse tool_use / function_call blocks</li>\n<li>Loop until stop</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Provider differences are minor (header format, JSON schema for tools, SSE event names) and well-contained in ~300 lines per provider.</p>\n<h3>API Change Tracking &amp; Version Pinning</h3>\n<p>Without an official SDK, API changes must be tracked deliberately. Strategy:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Pin API versions in headers</strong>: <code>anthropic-version: 2023-06-01</code>, <code>x-api-version</code> for OpenAI (when available)</li>\n<li><strong>Model version pinning</strong>: use dated model snapshots (e.g., <code>claude-sonnet-4-20250514</code>) not aliases (<code>claude-sonnet-4</code>) in default config</li>\n<li><strong>CI canary job</strong>: weekly integration test against each provider's API with a minimal prompt. Failures trigger alerts, not breakage.</li>\n<li><strong>Provider feature flags</strong>: new API features (extended thinking, computer use, etc.) are gated behind feature flags, not auto-enabled</li>\n<li><strong>Changelog tracking</strong>: maintain <code>PROVIDERS.md</code> documenting supported API versions, known breaking changes, and migration notes</li>\n<li><strong>OpenAI-compatible fallback</strong>: providers implementing the OpenAI chat completions spec (DeepSeek, Groq, Together, Ollama, etc.) require zero additional code — only <code>base_url</code> changes</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Tool Implementation</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tool</th>\n<th>Input</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>read</code></td>\n<td>path, optional line range</td>\n<td>Read file contents or list directory</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>write</code></td>\n<td>path, content</td>\n<td>Create or overwrite file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>edit</code></td>\n<td>path, old_str, new_str</td>\n<td>Replace exact string in file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bash</code></td>\n<td>command, optional working_dir</td>\n<td>Execute shell command, return stdout/stderr</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Path Security (read/write/edit tools)</h3>\n<p>All file tools enforce <strong>path confinement</strong> to prevent path traversal attacks:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>All paths are canonicalized (<code>std::fs::canonicalize</code>) before access</li>\n<li>Resolved path must be within <code>working_dir</code> or explicitly allowed directories</li>\n<li>Symlinks are resolved and checked against the boundary</li>\n<li>Attempts to escape (e.g., <code>../../etc/passwd</code>) return an error, not file contents</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">fn validate_path(path: &amp;Path, working_dir: &amp;Path) -&gt; Result&lt;PathBuf&gt; {\n    let canonical = path.canonicalize()?;\n    if !canonical.starts_with(working_dir) {\n        return Err(Error::PathTraversal(path.display().to_string()));\n    }\n    Ok(canonical)\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Sandboxing (bash tool)</h3>\n<p>The <code>bash</code> tool runs commands via <code>tokio::process::Command</code> with:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Configurable timeout (default: 120s)</li>\n<li><strong>Process group kill on timeout</strong> — uses <code>setsid</code> + <code>kill(-pgid)</code> to ensure all child/grandchild processes are terminated, preventing orphan process leaks</li>\n<li>Optional <code>bubblewrap</code> (bwrap) sandboxing on Linux; falls back to basic process isolation on macOS (see Cross-Platform Sandboxing below)</li>\n<li>Working directory scoped to agent's <code>working_dir</code></li>\n<li>No network access restriction by default (agent needs to call APIs, git, etc.)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Environment Variable Filtering</h3>\n<p>The <code>bash</code> tool does <strong>NOT</strong> inherit the agent's full environment. Instead:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Deny-list by default</strong>: sensitive variables are stripped before spawning child processes:\n<ul>\n<li><code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code>, <code>OPENAI_API_KEY</code>, <code>GOOGLE_API_KEY</code>, <code>OPENAB_AGENT_*</code> (all provider keys)</li>\n<li>Any variable matching <code>*_SECRET</code>, <code>*_TOKEN</code>, <code>*_KEY</code> patterns (configurable)</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Allow-list passthrough</strong>: only explicitly declared safe variables are inherited:\n<ul>\n<li><code>PATH</code>, <code>HOME</code>, <code>USER</code>, <code>LANG</code>, <code>TERM</code>, <code>SHELL</code></li>\n<li>Variables listed in <code>OPENAB_AGENT_BASH_ENV_ALLOW</code> (comma-separated)</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>This prevents prompt injection attacks from exfiltrating API keys via <code>curl</code>/<code>wget</code></li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">fn build_env(config: &amp;AgentConfig) -&gt; HashMap&lt;String, String&gt; {\n    let mut env = HashMap::new();\n    // Only pass safe defaults\n    for key in &amp;[&quot;PATH&quot;, &quot;HOME&quot;, &quot;USER&quot;, &quot;LANG&quot;, &quot;TERM&quot;, &quot;SHELL&quot;] {\n        if let Ok(val) = std::env::var(key) {\n            env.insert(key.to_string(), val);\n        }\n    }\n    // Add user-configured allow-list\n    for key in &amp;config.bash_env_allow {\n        if let Ok(val) = std::env::var(key) {\n            env.insert(key.to_string(), val);\n        }\n    }\n    env\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Cross-Platform Sandboxing</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Sandboxing</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Linux</td>\n<td><code>bubblewrap</code> (bwrap)</td>\n<td>Full filesystem/network namespace isolation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>macOS</td>\n<td>Process group isolation + env filtering</td>\n<td>Primary mechanism for local dev. <code>sandbox-exec</code> is deprecated by Apple and may be removed in future macOS versions — not relied upon.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Fallback</td>\n<td>Process group isolation + env filtering</td>\n<td>Minimum viable security without platform-specific tools</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>For production (Linux containers), <code>bubblewrap</code> is the primary mechanism. For local macOS development, the env filtering + path confinement provides baseline security without requiring bwrap.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Session Tree</h2>\n<p>Sessions are stored as a tree structure, not a flat list:</p>\n<pre><code>root\n├── turn-1 (user: &quot;explain this code&quot;)\n│   └── turn-2 (assistant: &quot;This code does...&quot;)\n│       ├── turn-3a (user: &quot;refactor it&quot;) ← branch A\n│       │   └── turn-4a (assistant: &quot;Here's the refactored...&quot;)\n│       └── turn-3b (user: &quot;add tests instead&quot;) ← branch B\n│           └── turn-4b (assistant: &quot;Here are the tests...&quot;)\n</code></pre>\n<p>Benefits:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Explore multiple approaches from a decision point</li>\n<li>Rollback without losing the exploration</li>\n<li>Persisted to disk as JSON for session resume</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Garbage Collection / Pruning</h3>\n<p>To prevent unbounded growth in long-running deployments:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Max tree depth</strong>: configurable (default: 200 turns per branch). Oldest turns are summarized when exceeded.</li>\n<li><strong>Max branches</strong>: configurable (default: 20 per session). Least-recently-used branches are pruned on overflow.</li>\n<li><strong>Inactive branch TTL</strong>: branches not accessed for N hours (default: 24h) are eligible for pruning.</li>\n<li><strong>Disk persistence cap</strong>: per-session JSON file capped at 10MB. Exceeding triggers forced summarization of oldest branches.</li>\n<li><strong>GC trigger</strong>: runs on every Nth turn (default: 10) or when memory pressure is detected.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>5a. Context Window Management</h2>\n<p>The agent must operate within LLM context limits (typically 128K–200K tokens). Strategy:</p>\n<h3>Token Counting</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Use <code>tiktoken-rs</code> for OpenAI models, character-based estimation (×0.3) for others</li>\n<li>Track cumulative token usage per session branch</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Window Overflow Strategy (ordered by priority)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Tool output truncation</strong> — large <code>bash</code> stdout or <code>read</code> results are truncated to configurable max (default: 30K tokens) with a &quot;truncated, showing first/last N lines&quot; indicator</li>\n<li><strong>Oldest turn summarization</strong> — when context exceeds 80% of model limit, oldest turns (excluding system prompt and last 4 turns) are replaced with a one-paragraph summary generated by the same LLM</li>\n<li><strong>Branch instead of truncate</strong> — if the user explicitly branches, the new branch starts with a compact summary of the parent path, preserving full context in the original branch</li>\n<li><strong>Hard cap rejection</strong> — if a single tool output exceeds 50% of context window, reject and ask the user to narrow the request</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent.context]\nmax_context_percent = 80          # trigger summarization at 80% of model limit\nmax_tool_output_tokens = 30000    # truncate individual tool outputs\nsummarize_after_turns = 20        # summarize turns older than the last 20\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;openab-agent&quot;\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n\n[agent.env]\n# Provider selection (one of):\nOPENAB_AGENT_PROVIDER = &quot;anthropic&quot;          # or &quot;openai&quot;, &quot;google&quot;, &quot;openai-compatible&quot;\nOPENAB_AGENT_MODEL = &quot;claude-sonnet-4-20250514&quot;\n\n# Auth (provider-specific):\nANTHROPIC_API_KEY = &quot;${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}&quot;\n# or: OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, etc.\n\n# Optional:\nOPENAB_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS = &quot;8192&quot;\nOPENAB_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECS = &quot;120&quot;\nOPENAB_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_LOOPS = &quot;50&quot;       # max tool-call iterations per prompt (default 50)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Steering Files</h3>\n<p>openab-agent reads steering files in the same pattern as other agents:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>AGENTS.md</code> in working directory (hot memory, always loaded)</li>\n<li><code>.openab-agent/system.md</code> — custom system prompt override</li>\n<li><code>.openab-agent/append.md</code> — append to default system prompt</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Future: Library Mode (Deferred — Not in v1 Scope)</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> This section documents a potential future optimization. It is explicitly <strong>out of scope</strong> for v0.1–v0.3 and will require its own ADR if pursued.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Because openab-agent is Rust (same as openab core), a future optimization is <strong>in-process mode</strong> — no stdio, no JSON-RPC serialization:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">// Current: IPC over stdio (v0.1–v0.3)\nopenab::spawn_process(&quot;openab-agent&quot;, &amp;[&quot;--acp&quot;]) // stdin/stdout JSON-RPC\n\n// Future: direct function call (requires separate ADR)\nlet agent = openab_agent::Agent::new(config);\nlet response = agent.prompt(session_id, messages).await; // zero-copy\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Known Risks (to be addressed in future ADR)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Panic propagation</strong>: an agent panic (e.g., malformed SSE parse) would crash the entire openab process. Mitigation: <code>catch_unwind</code> boundaries or <code>tokio::task::spawn</code> with panic hooks.</li>\n<li><strong>Resource isolation</strong>: in-process mode shares memory/threads with openab core. A runaway agent could starve the session pool.</li>\n<li><strong>Blast radius</strong>: process isolation (current design) provides natural fault containment. Library mode trades this for performance.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Decision</strong>: v1 ships as a standalone binary with stdio ACP. Library mode is a v2+ exploration only if IPC overhead proves to be a measurable bottleneck in production.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Rollout Plan</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n<th>Deliverable</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v0.1</strong></td>\n<td>Scaffold + ACP layer + single provider (Anthropic)</td>\n<td>Working agent, 4 tools, flat session</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v0.2</strong></td>\n<td>Multi-provider + session tree + steering files</td>\n<td>Feature parity with Pi's core</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v0.3</strong></td>\n<td>Dockerfile + Helm chart + CI</td>\n<td>Production-ready deployment</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>v0.4</strong></td>\n<td>Library mode exploration</td>\n<td>In-process integration with openab core</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Testing Strategy</h2>\n<h3>Unit Test Boundaries</h3>\n<p>Following the project's unit test ADR, operations involving network, filesystem, or subprocess are <strong>integration tests only</strong>. Unit tests cover pure logic:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Layer</th>\n<th>Unit-Testable</th>\n<th>How</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Prompt assembly</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Hand-written mock <code>LlmProvider</code> returning canned <code>BoxStream</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Tool dispatch routing</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Mock tool implementations (no real FS/process)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Session tree operations</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Pure data structure manipulation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Token counting / context management</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Pure computation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>SSE event parsing</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Feed raw bytes, assert parsed <code>Event</code> structs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>LLM HTTP calls</td>\n<td>❌ (integration)</td>\n<td>Real HTTP against provider or local mock server</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>File tools (read/write/edit)</td>\n<td>❌ (integration)</td>\n<td>Real filesystem in temp dirs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Bash tool</td>\n<td>❌ (integration)</td>\n<td>Real subprocess execution</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Hand-Written Mocks (no <code>mockall</code>)</h3>\n<p>Per team convention, all mocks are hand-written:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">struct MockLlmProvider {\n    responses: Vec&lt;Vec&lt;Event&gt;&gt;,\n    call_count: AtomicUsize,\n}\n\nimpl LlmProvider for MockLlmProvider {\n    fn chat&lt;'a&gt;(\n        &amp;'a self,\n        _messages: &amp;'a [Message],\n        _tools: &amp;'a [Tool],\n    ) -&gt; Pin&lt;Box&lt;dyn Future&lt;Output = Result&lt;BoxStream&lt;'a, Event&gt;&gt;&gt; + Send + 'a&gt;&gt; {\n        let idx = self.call_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let events = self.responses[idx].clone();\n        Box::pin(async move {\n            Ok(Box::pin(futures::stream::iter(events.into_iter())) as BoxStream&lt;'a, Event&gt;)\n        })\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Integration Tests</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Tagged with <code>#[cfg(test)]</code> + <code>#[ignore]</code> for CI gating</li>\n<li>LLM integration tests require <code>OPENAB_TEST_PROVIDER</code> env var</li>\n<li>File/bash tool tests use <code>tempdir</code> for isolation</li>\n<li>CI runs integration tests in a separate job with real credentials (not on every PR)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>CI Pipeline</h3>\n<pre><code>PR push → cargo fmt --check → cargo clippy → cargo test (unit only)\n                                                    ↓\nmerge to main → cargo test (unit + integration) → canary deploy\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. Open Questions</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Question</th>\n<th>Options</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Crate name</strong></td>\n<td><code>openab-agent</code> as a workspace member vs separate repo</td>\n<td>Workspace member keeps it close to openab core</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Subscription auth</strong></td>\n<td>Support OAuth flows (Claude Pro, ChatGPT Plus) or API-key only for v1?</td>\n<td>API-key only for v1; subscription auth adds complexity</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Permission model</strong></td>\n<td>Auto-approve all tool calls vs interactive approval?</td>\n<td>Auto-approve for v1 (matches OpenAB's <code>--trust-all-tools</code> pattern)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Context window management</strong></td>\n<td>Truncate old turns vs summarize vs session tree branching?</td>\n<td>Session tree branching for v1; summarization for v2</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Consequences</h2>\n<h3>Positive</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Zero external runtime</strong> — no Node.js, Python, or npm. Single static binary.</li>\n<li><strong>Minimal attack surface</strong> — no node_modules supply chain, no adapter layer vulnerabilities.</li>\n<li><strong>Fastest cold start</strong> — &lt;50ms vs 1–3s for Node-based agents.</li>\n<li><strong>Smallest image</strong> — ~20MB distroless vs 300–800MB for existing agents.</li>\n<li><strong>Native ACP</strong> — no wrapper overhead, no adapter bugs, no version mismatches.</li>\n<li><strong>Same language as openab</strong> — shared types, potential library mode, unified toolchain.</li>\n<li><strong>Full control</strong> — no upstream CLI breaking changes; we own the entire stack.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Negative</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>LLM API maintenance</strong> — must track API changes manually without official SDKs.</li>\n<li><strong>No subscription auth (v1)</strong> — API key only initially; users with Claude Pro/ChatGPT Plus subscriptions still need Pi or Codex.</li>\n<li><strong>Feature gap</strong> — v1 will lack features mature agents have (image support, MCP, web search tools).</li>\n<li><strong>Development effort</strong> — building from scratch vs leveraging existing open-source agents.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Risks</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>API instability</strong> — if providers make breaking changes frequently, maintenance burden grows. Mitigated by pinning API versions and weekly CI canary.</li>\n<li><strong>Scope creep</strong> — temptation to add more tools/features. Mitigated by the &quot;4 tools only&quot; design principle as a hard constraint for v1.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi\">Pi coding agent</a> — design inspiration (minimal tools, session trees, multi-model)</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/anthropics/agent-protocol\">Agent Client Protocol</a> — ACP spec</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab\">OpenAB</a> — host runtime</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: openab-agent — Native Rust Coding Agent with Built-in ACP"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "adr/openab-agent-mcp",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: openab-agent — MCP Client Support</h1>\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Motivation</h2>\n<p><code>openab-agent</code> is the native Rust coding agent shipped with OpenAB (Cargo workspace member <code>openab-agent/</code>, introduced 2026-05-26 via PR #924, targeted at the v0.8.4-beta series). Its <code>docs/adr/openab-agent.md</code> charter commits to a small surface: 4 built-in tools (<code>read</code>, <code>write</code>, <code>edit</code>, <code>bash</code>), a ~500-token system prompt, no LLM SDK dependency, multi-model via thin HTTP. PR #955 added <code>Skills</code> support (<code>openab-agent/src/skills.rs</code>, 224 LOC, zero new crate dependencies) as the first extension mechanism — descriptor-only injection plus on-demand load via the existing <code>read</code> tool.</p>\n<p>The agent currently has <strong>no MCP (Model Context Protocol) client</strong>. This ADR proposes one.</p>\n<h3>1.1 Why MCP for openab-agent</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Ecosystem leverage.</strong> Every Postgres/GitHub/Figma/Jira/Slack integration users will ask for already exists as an MCP server (mcpbundles.com tracks ~9k tools across ~1.4k providers as of 2026-Q2). Re-implementing each as a Skill or built-in tool is duplicative.</li>\n<li><strong>Parity with peer agents.</strong> Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Cline, Goose, opencode, OpenHands, Kiro, Junie, Roo Code all ship MCP clients. Users coming from any of these expect <code>mcpServers</code> config to &quot;just work&quot;.</li>\n<li><strong>Skills cannot replace MCP.</strong> Per Anthropic's framing — <strong>Skills = procedural (how to do); MCP = connectivity (where data/tools live)</strong>. Skills wrap CLI tools; MCP handles network, auth, streaming, server-side state.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>1.2 Why now</h3>\n<p>Skills landed in PR #955. The repo's design pattern for &quot;first-tier-but-tiny&quot; extension is now established. MCP is the natural next layer.</p>\n<h3>1.3 Prior internal attempts</h3>\n<p>Four MCP PRs to upstream <code>openabdev/openab</code> have closed without merging:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>PR</th>\n<th>Title</th>\n<th>State</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>#329, #330</td>\n<td><code>feat(mcp): inject per-user MCP servers from Discord profiles into ACP sessions</code></td>\n<td>CLOSED</td>\n<td>Broker forward</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>#345</td>\n<td><code>feat: inject per-user MCP servers into ACP sessions</code></td>\n<td>CLOSED</td>\n<td>Broker forward</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>#903</td>\n<td><code>feat(agent): forward configured MCP servers</code></td>\n<td>CLOSED</td>\n<td>Broker forward</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>All four targeted the broker layer — pass MCP server config through to the backing CLI (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor) and let that CLI handle MCP. <strong>None addressed native MCP support inside <code>openab-agent</code> itself.</strong> This ADR is scoped to the native agent.</p>\n<p>Issue #753 remains open and is broker-side (<code>[agent].inherit_cloud_mcp_servers</code> opt-out). This ADR does not change broker behavior.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Goals &amp; Non-Goals</h2>\n<h3>In scope</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>MCP <strong>client</strong> support inside <code>openab-agent</code></li>\n<li>Transports: stdio (local servers — Anthropic reference, npm/pypi community) and Streamable HTTP (vendor-hosted SaaS — Atlassian, Figma, Linear, Notion, Sentry, etc.). HTTP+SSE intentionally omitted — superseded by MCP spec 2025-11-25 and actively sunset by vendors (Atlassian deadline 2026-06-30). See §3.8 for landscape.</li>\n<li>OAuth login flow for MCP servers requiring it</li>\n<li>Per-session lifecycle with idle eviction</li>\n<li>Per-session config refresh — new ACP session re-reads <code>mcpServers</code> from disk (no file watcher, no mid-session reload; openab spawns short-lived sessions per thread so process restart is rarely needed)</li>\n<li>Progressive-disclosure tool surface (single meta-tool, not flat fan-out)</li>\n<li>Reuse of existing <code>src/auth.rs</code> PKCE / TokenStore where possible</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Out of scope</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>MCP <strong>server</strong> functionality (host only)</li>\n<li>WASM / cdylib plugin runtime</li>\n<li>Sidecar / out-of-process MCP bridge</li>\n<li>Per-thread MCP isolation (broker concern, not agent)</li>\n<li>Replacing Skills (Skills and MCP coexist)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Prior Art Survey</h2>\n<p>Per <code>docs/adr/pr-contribution-guidelines.md</code>, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are the mandatory references for architectural PRs. OpenClaw was evaluated and found <strong>not applicable to this ADR</strong>: it is a multi-channel messaging gateway (chat platforms ↔ MCP), not a coding agent. Its substantial MCP code (~2,900 LOC across <code>src/agents/mcp-*</code>, <code>src/config/mcp-*</code>, <code>src/mcp/</code>) addresses channel bridging rather than agent-side tool calling. The closer comparison for a coding-agent MCP client is <strong>opencode (§3.2)</strong>, included in addition to Hermes Agent.</p>\n<p>Five projects are surveyed below. Each contributes a design pattern the chosen architecture borrows from:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>§</th>\n<th>Project</th>\n<th>Borrowed pattern</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>3.1</td>\n<td>Hermes Agent</td>\n<td>Circuit breaker (per-server fail threshold + cooldown)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3.2</td>\n<td>opencode</td>\n<td>Per-server status enum + RFC 7591 dynamic OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3.3</td>\n<td>pi-mcp-adapter</td>\n<td>Single <code>mcp</code> meta-tool with action dispatch (progressive disclosure)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3.4</td>\n<td>Goose</td>\n<td>MCP-as-primary-extension validation in a Rust codebase</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3.5</td>\n<td>OpenHands</td>\n<td><code>filter_tools_regex</code> per-server tool scoping</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>3.1 Hermes Agent (mandatory reference)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Repo: <a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\">https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent</a> (Python, Apache 2.0)</li>\n<li>MCP module: ~5,175 LOC across 3 files (<code>mcp_tool.py</code> + 2 OAuth modules)</li>\n<li>SDK: official <code>mcp==1.26.0</code></li>\n<li>Transports: stdio + Streamable HTTP + SSE</li>\n<li>Tool naming: <code>mcp_{server}_{tool}</code> (single-underscore separators, no <code>__</code> boundary marker)</li>\n<li>Lifecycle: per-server long-lived <code>asyncio.Task</code> on dedicated background event loop</li>\n<li>Lazy loading: eager connect, but background-thread discovery with 0.75s join — non-blocking</li>\n<li>Hot reload: mtime-poll on <code>~/.hermes/config.yaml</code> + <code>/reload-mcp</code> slash command</li>\n<li>OAuth: mtime-based disk-watch for cross-process token refresh</li>\n<li><strong>Notable</strong>: ships a real circuit breaker — threshold 3 failures / 60s cooldown / half-open probe state. The only project surveyed that does so.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3.2 opencode (anomalyco/opencode, formerly sst/opencode)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Repo: <a href=\"https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode\">https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode</a> (TypeScript, MIT) — <code>sst/opencode</code> 301-redirects here after org transfer</li>\n<li><strong>Closest coding-agent comparison to openab-agent</strong></li>\n<li>MCP module: ~1,664 LOC across 5 files (<code>mcp/</code>, <code>auth.ts</code>, OAuth provider/callback, config)</li>\n<li>SDK: <code>@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.27.1</code></li>\n<li>Transports: stdio + Streamable HTTP + SSE</li>\n<li>Tool naming: <code>{sanitized_client}_{sanitized_tool}</code> (single underscore)</li>\n<li>Lifecycle: shared singleton service via Effect <code>Layer</code>; one <code>Client</code> per server</li>\n<li>Lazy loading: eager connect with <code>concurrency: &quot;unbounded&quot;</code>; per-server status union prevents one bad server from crashing others</li>\n<li>Hot reload: subscribes to MCP spec's <code>notifications/tools/list_changed</code>; <strong>no file watcher</strong> for config — config change still requires restart</li>\n<li>OAuth: RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, callback <code>http://127.0.0.1:19876/mcp/oauth/callback</code>, EffectFlock cross-process locking on token store</li>\n<li><strong>Known issues</strong> (cited as architectural cautionary tales): #11868 (113 GB virtual-memory leak, Windows v1.1.21), #7261 (heap not released + MCP orphan processes, v1.1.6), #13041 (per-session MCP+LSP duplication across concurrent sessions) — all rooted in child-process lifecycle, not protocol code</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3.3 pi-mcp-adapter</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Repo: <a href=\"https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter\">https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter</a> (TypeScript, MIT)</li>\n<li>An out-of-tree extension for the Pi coding agent (<code>pi.extensions</code>) — Pi itself has <strong>no native MCP</strong></li>\n<li>MCP module: ~3,661 LOC (server-manager, proxy-modes, direct-tools, OAuth)</li>\n<li>SDK: <code>@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.25.1</code> + <code>@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@^1.2.2</code></li>\n<li>Transports: stdio + Streamable HTTP + SSE</li>\n<li><strong>Notable — the reason this is cited</strong>: ships a <strong>single <code>mcp</code> meta-tool</strong> with sub-actions (<code>connect</code>, <code>describe</code>, <code>search</code>, <code>list</code>, <code>call</code>, <code>status</code>). All MCP capability is exposed through this one tool. Lazy connect happens inside <code>lazyConnect()</code> on first action that needs it. This is the <strong>progressive-disclosure pattern</strong> this ADR adopts.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3.4 Goose (block / aaif-goose)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Repo: <a href=\"https://github.com/block/goose\">https://github.com/block/goose</a> → <a href=\"https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose\">https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose</a> (Rust, Apache 2.0)</li>\n<li><strong>Most relevant precedent: a Rust coding agent built around MCP</strong></li>\n<li>Launched Jan 2025 with MCP as the <em>only</em> extension surface (no first-party plugin API to retrofit)</li>\n<li>Hand-rolled <code>mcp-client</code> crate (predated official Rust SDK)</li>\n<li>Per-session <code>Agent</code> owns an <code>ExtensionManager</code> that spawns MCP servers (stdio/SSE) as child processes</li>\n<li>Tools flattened into one namespace; extension name used as prefix to avoid collisions</li>\n<li>Supports <code>tools/list_changed</code> for hot reload</li>\n<li>Precedent for a Rust agent shipping MCP as the primary extension surface without WASM / cdylib / sidecar plumbing.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3.5 OpenHands (All-Hands-AI)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Repo: <a href=\"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands\">https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands</a> (Python, MIT)</li>\n<li>SDK: FastMCP (jlowin/fastmcp), not the reference SDK</li>\n<li><strong>Notable</strong>: per-agent <code>filter_tools_regex</code> config — subset a server's tools without modifying the server. OAuth tokens cached under <code>~/.fastmcp/oauth-mcp-client-cache/</code> with auto-refresh; explicit &quot;incompatible with headless&quot; caveat for browser-based auth.</li>\n<li>Cited for OAuth + tool-surface scoping patterns where Hermes/opencode/Pi are weaker.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3.6 Comparison matrix</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th></th>\n<th>Hermes</th>\n<th>opencode</th>\n<th>pi-mcp-adapter</th>\n<th>Goose</th>\n<th>OpenHands</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Language</td>\n<td>Python</td>\n<td>TS</td>\n<td>TS</td>\n<td>Rust</td>\n<td>Python</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>SDK</td>\n<td>mcp 1.26</td>\n<td>sdk 1.27</td>\n<td>sdk 1.25</td>\n<td>hand-rolled</td>\n<td>FastMCP</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Transports</td>\n<td>stdio+HTTP+SSE</td>\n<td>stdio+HTTP+SSE</td>\n<td>stdio+HTTP+SSE</td>\n<td>stdio+SSE</td>\n<td>stdio+HTTP</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Tool naming</td>\n<td><code>mcp_s_t</code></td>\n<td><code>s_t</code></td>\n<td>configurable</td>\n<td>ext-prefix</td>\n<td>filter</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Lifecycle</td>\n<td>per-srv task</td>\n<td>shared singleton</td>\n<td>per-ext + idle 10m</td>\n<td>per-session ExtensionMgr</td>\n<td>per-agent</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Lazy connect</td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td>✅ meta</td>\n<td>no (eager)</td>\n<td>no</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Hot reload</td>\n<td>mtime+cmd</td>\n<td><code>tools/list_changed</code></td>\n<td>session boundary</td>\n<td><code>tools/list_changed</code></td>\n<td>no</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n<td>mtime disk-watch</td>\n<td>RFC7591 + Flock</td>\n<td>PKCE+auto</td>\n<td>?</td>\n<td>FastMCP cache</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Circuit breaker</td>\n<td>✅ 3/60s</td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td>partial</td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td>no</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>LOC</td>\n<td>~5,175</td>\n<td>~1,664</td>\n<td>~3,661</td>\n<td>unmeasured</td>\n<td>unmeasured</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>3.7 Skills vs MCP — industry research</h3>\n<p>Anthropic positions the two as <strong>complementary</strong>, not competing. The 2025-2026 consensus across practitioner blogs (Simon Willison, Anthropic engineering, StackOne) converged on:</p>\n<pre><code>  Skills                                    MCP\n  ──────                                    ────\n  Procedural knowledge                      Live connectivity\n  Markdown + YAML frontmatter               Protocol spec + SDK\n  ~100 tokens/skill in prompt               10K-17K tokens/server in prompt\n  Body lazy-loaded via read tool            All tool schemas eagerly loaded\n  Local file                                Server (process or HTTP endpoint)\n  No auth, no lifecycle                     OAuth, lifecycle, transports\n  Open standard (Dec 2025)                  Linux Foundation steward (late 2025)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Adoption</strong>: no major OSS coding agent has rejected MCP in favor of Skills-only (or vice versa). All 11 surveyed agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Cline, Goose, opencode, Junie, Kiro, Roo, GitHub Copilot agent-mode) support both.</p>\n<p><strong>Cost data</strong>: large MCP server collections have been documented consuming substantial context budget — StackOne benchmarks Sonnet 4.6 at 42% tool-selection accuracy on the unmodified MCP surface vs 80% with their Code Mode wrapper, motivating the spec-level fix in MCP SEP-1576 (&quot;Mitigating Token Bloat in MCP&quot;) which proposes progressive disclosure (<strong>not yet ratified</strong>).</p>\n<p><strong>Implication for this ADR</strong>: progressive disclosure is not optional for openab-agent. The agent's design principle commits to a ~500-token system prompt; a naïve flat MCP integration would 30× that budget. Skills' descriptor-only injection pattern is the precedent.</p>\n<h3>3.8 Transport landscape &amp; SaaS MCP server adoption</h3>\n<p>MCP defines three transport profiles. Their 2026-Q2 status:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Transport</th>\n<th>Spec status</th>\n<th>Where it lives</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>stdio</strong></td>\n<td>Stable</td>\n<td>Local child process — Anthropic reference servers, npm/pypi community packages</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Streamable HTTP</strong></td>\n<td>Current (MCP spec 2025-11-25), supersedes HTTP+SSE</td>\n<td>Vendor-hosted SaaS endpoints</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>HTTP+SSE</strong></td>\n<td>Deprecated by spec 2025-11-25; vendor sunsets in progress</td>\n<td>Legacy fixtures — Atlassian sunsets SaaS, growing)     │     │\n   │   │                             │         │                                    │     │\n   │   │  Transport: stdio           │         │  Transport: Streamable HTTP HTTP+SSE                                                       │     │\n   │   │  e.g. Atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/sse (off 2026-06-30)          │     │\n   │
