└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Local stdio servers (representative sample)</h4>\n<p>Anthropic reference + community packages. All ship as <code>command + args</code>; no network endpoint.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Server</th>\n<th>Implementation</th>\n<th>Distribution</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-filesystem</code></td>\n<td>Node</td>\n<td><code>@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem</code> (npm)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-sqlite</code></td>\n<td>Python</td>\n<td><code>mcp-server-sqlite</code> (pypi)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-postgres</code></td>\n<td>Python</td>\n<td><code>mcp-server-postgres</code> (pypi) — local DB</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-puppeteer</code></td>\n<td>Node</td>\n<td><code>@modelcontextprotocol/server-puppeteer</code> (npm)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-github</code></td>\n<td>Go / Node</td>\n<td><code>github-mcp-server</code> (binary) / <code>@modelcontextprotocol/server-github</code> (npm)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-fetch</code></td>\n<td>Python</td>\n<td><code>mcp-server-fetch</code> (pypi)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-time</code></td>\n<td>Rust</td>\n<td><code>mcp-server-time</code> (cargo)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server-gitlab</code></td>\n<td>Node</td>\n<td><code>@modelcontextprotocol/server-gitlab</code> (npm)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Container-image caveat for headless deployments</strong>: Node/Python stdio servers require the corresponding interpreter (<code>node</code>, <code>python3</code>, <code>uvx</code>, <code>npx</code>) in the image. The openab base image ships none. Operators running openab-agent in headless environments (Fargate, Kubernetes pods, CI) must either bake the interpreter into a derived image or limit <code>mcpServers</code> to Go/Rust binaries (column above). A misconfigured server fails in isolation per §5.9.</p>\n<h4>Vendor-hosted SaaS servers — all Streamable HTTP</h4>\n<p>Survey of mainstream public endpoints (2026-Q2). Every active vendor endpoint surveyed is Streamable HTTP. The Atlassian SSE URL is the lone holdout and has a published sunset date.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Vendor</th>\n<th>Endpoint</th>\n<th>Transport</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Atlassian (Rovo)</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>Legacy SSE at <code>/v1/sse</code> sunset <strong>2026-06-30</strong></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Figma</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.figma.com/mcp</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth via Figma account</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Linear</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.linear.app/mcp</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Notion</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.notion.com/mcp</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Sentry</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Supabase</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>HubSpot</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.hubspot.com/anthropic</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Slack</td>\n<td>(vendor-hosted)</td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Stripe</td>\n<td>hosted (see Stripe MCP docs for current path)</td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>API key</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cloudflare</td>\n<td>multiple endpoints under <code>*.mcp.cloudflare.com</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth (workers/dns/r2/...)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Vercel</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.vercel.com/</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Neon</td>\n<td><code>https://mcp.neon.tech/</code></td>\n<td>Streamable HTTP</td>\n<td>OAuth</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Cover map</strong>: stdio + Streamable HTTP covers all mainstream public MCP endpoints surveyed as of 2026-Q2. SSE-only deployments are legacy fixtures with vendor sunsets in progress; deferred to a hypothetical v2.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Design Decision</h2>\n<h3>4.1 Architectural alternatives compared</h3>\n<p><strong>Alternative A — Naïve flat in-core.</strong> Every MCP tool from every connected server becomes a top-level entry in <code>tool_definitions()</code>. Surface explodes from 4 → 150+ tools; system prompt grows ~500 → ~17,000 tokens (5 servers × ~20 tools each, ~160 tokens per descriptor). Hermes Agent and opencode both pay this cost; StackOne benchmarks (§3.7) show tool-selection accuracy drops sharply under naïve flat surfaces.</p>\n<p><strong>Alternative B — Sidecar / plugin process.</strong> Spawn a separate <code>openab-mcp-bridge</code> binary; agent core has no <code>rmcp</code> dependency; communicate via stdio JSON-RPC. RAM saving is 1-2 MB on a 15-40 MB baseline — noise — but the bridge process itself adds ~15 MB and inherits opencode's documented sidecar failure modes (#11868 113 GB leak / #7261 orphan processes / #13041 per-session duplication). Cost ≫ benefit (see §7).</p>\n<p><strong>Alternative C — CHOSEN: in-core <code>rmcp</code> + progressive-disclosure meta-tool.</strong> <code>rmcp</code> enters <code>Cargo.toml</code>. Tool surface grows by exactly <strong>1 tool</strong>: <code>mcp</code>. All MCP capability (server enumeration, tool discovery, invocation, status) flows through that single tool's <code>action</code> field. System prompt grows ~500 → ~600 tokens (+100 for the meta-tool blurb).</p>\n<h3>4.2 Why C honors openab-agent design principles</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Principle (<code>docs/adr/openab-agent.md</code> §2)</th>\n<th align=\"center\">A (flat)</th>\n<th align=\"center\">B (sidecar)</th>\n<th align=\"center\"><strong>C (chosen)</strong></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Minimal tool surface (4 tools)</td>\n<td align=\"center\">⛔ 150+</td>\n<td align=\"center\">✅ 4</td>\n<td align=\"center\">✅ 5</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Tiny system prompt (~500 tokens)</td>\n<td align=\"center\">⛔ ~17K</td>\n<td align=\"center\">✅ ~500</td>\n<td align=\"center\">⚠️ ~600 (+100 over budget; accepted as smallest viable surface)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>No SDK dependency</td>\n<td align=\"center\">⛔ rmcp</td>\n<td align=\"center\">✅ none</td>\n<td align=\"center\">⚠️ rmcp (+1-2 MB binary, see §7)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-model</td>\n<td align=\"center\">✅</td>\n<td align=\"center\">✅</td>\n<td align=\"center\">✅</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>C concedes the &quot;no SDK dependency&quot; principle for a 1-2 MB binary cost. §7 shows that cost is dominated by child-process RAM (5-80 MB per server, depending on implementation language) regardless of architecture, so the concession is dwarfed by usage cost.</p>\n<h3>4.3 Symmetry with Skills (PR #955)</h3>\n<p>Skills is openab's existing &quot;first-tier-but-tiny&quot; extension. The mapping is exact:</p>\n<pre><code>┌────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Skills (224 LOC, in-core) │  MCP (proposed, in-core)            │\n├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Inject metadata only       │ Inject 1 meta-tool only             │\n│ (name + description)       │ (name + action sketch)              │\n├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Body load via `read` tool  │ Server connect via `mcp` tool       │\n│ on agent's demand          │ on agent's demand (lazy connect)    │\n├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ ~100 tokens / 10 skills    │ ~100 tokens / N servers             │\n├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ No new crate dep           │ Adds rmcp (1-2 MB binary delta)     │\n└────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>Skills' authors weighed &quot;simple in-core mechanism vs plugin abstraction&quot; and chose in-core. The same trade-off applies to MCP: plugin abstraction is ~10× the complexity for negligible RAM saving.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Detailed Design</h2>\n<h3>5.1 Tool surface (4 + 1)</h3>\n<pre><code>openab-agent/src/tools.rs::tool_definitions() returns 5 entries:\n\n  [ &quot;read&quot;  ] ─── existing, unchanged\n  [ &quot;write&quot; ] ─── existing, unchanged\n  [ &quot;edit&quot;  ] ─── existing, unchanged\n  [ &quot;bash&quot;  ] ─── existing, unchanged\n  [ &quot;mcp&quot;   ] ─── NEW\n</code></pre>\n<h3>5.2 The <code>mcp</code> meta-tool schema</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;mcp&quot;,\n  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Interact with configured MCP servers. Use action='help' for usage.&quot;,\n  &quot;input_schema&quot;: {\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;,\n    &quot;properties&quot;: {\n      &quot;action&quot;: {\n        &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot;,\n        &quot;enum&quot;: [&quot;help&quot;, &quot;list_servers&quot;, &quot;list_tools&quot;,\n                 &quot;describe_tool&quot;, &quot;call&quot;, &quot;status&quot;,\n                 &quot;login&quot;, &quot;complete_login&quot;]\n      },\n      &quot;server&quot;:       { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n      &quot;tool&quot;:         { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n      &quot;arguments&quot;:    { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot; },\n      &quot;redirect_url&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; }\n    },\n    &quot;required&quot;: [&quot;action&quot;]\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Per-action contract:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>action</th>\n<th>required fields</th>\n<th>returns</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>help</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>usage doc string</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>list_servers</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>[{ name, status, transport, tools_count }]</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>list_tools</code></td>\n<td><code>server</code></td>\n<td><code>[{ name, description }]</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>describe_tool</code></td>\n<td><code>server</code>, <code>tool</code></td>\n<td><code>{ name, description, input_schema }</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>call</code></td>\n<td><code>server</code>, <code>tool</code>, <code>arguments</code></td>\n<td>tool's <code>CallToolResult</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>status</code></td>\n<td><code>server?</code></td>\n<td>per-server health / last error / OAuth state</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>login</code></td>\n<td><code>server</code></td>\n<td><code>{ flow: &quot;device&quot;, user_code, verification_url, ... }</code> or <code>{ flow: &quot;paste&quot;, authorize_url, state, ... }</code> — see §6.4</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>complete_login</code></td>\n<td><code>server</code>, <code>redirect_url</code></td>\n<td><code>{ ok: true }</code> or <code>{ error }</code> — paste flow only; device flow polls internally</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>5.3 Agent loop interaction</h3>\n<p>Typical multi-turn usage (lazy connect at first need, idle eviction after TTL):</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Turn 1</strong> — LLM calls <code>mcp(action: &quot;list_servers&quot;)</code>; no IO, served from config cache. Returns <code>[&quot;github (stdio)&quot;, ...]</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Turn 2</strong> — LLM calls <code>mcp(action: &quot;list_tools&quot;, server: &quot;github&quot;)</code>; <code>lazy_connect(&quot;github&quot;)</code> spawns child proc, <code>peer.list_all_tools()</code> fetches descriptors. Returns <code>[{name, description}, ...]</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Turn 3</strong> — LLM calls <code>mcp(action: &quot;call&quot;, server, tool, arguments)</code>; <code>peer.call_tool()</code> invokes. Returns <code>CallToolResult</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Idle (no MCP call for <code>idle_ttl</code>)</strong> — the background eviction loop shuts down the child proc and drops the Peer (only if not mid-call); config + descriptor cache retained for fast re-connect.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>5.4 Module layout</h3>\n<pre><code>openab-agent/src/\n├── agent.rs           (existing — add 1 match arm in execute_tool)\n├── auth.rs            (existing — TokenStore reused by mcp/oauth.rs)\n├── llm.rs             (existing — UNCHANGED, ToolDef is already generic)\n├── tools.rs           (existing — add `mcp` to tool_definitions())\n├── skills.rs          (existing — UNCHANGED)\n└── mcp/               (NEW module)\n    ├── mod.rs         (public: McpRuntimeManager, dispatch())\n    ├── config.rs      (mcpServers schema, ${env:VAR} interpolation)\n    ├── runtime.rs     (per-server lifecycle, lazy connect, idle TTL)\n    ├── meta_tool.rs   (action dispatch: list_servers / list_tools / ...)\n    ├── oauth.rs       (uses src/auth.rs TokenStore; built-in providers)\n    └── breaker.rs     (circuit breaker per server)\n</code></pre>\n<p>Estimated total: <strong>500-750 LOC</strong> (no <code>reload.rs</code>; per-session refresh handled by <code>McpRuntimeManager::new()</code> re-reading config at session start). <code>llm.rs</code> is unchanged because both Anthropic and OpenAI Responses providers consume the generic <code>ToolDef</code> abstraction.</p>\n<h4>5.4.1 Runtime activation &amp; isolation choices</h4>\n<p>Three intentional choices that surfaced in PR #959 review (chaodu F2 / F6 / F7) and are load-bearing enough to belong in the design contract:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Runtime activation = config presence (F6, always-on, no env switch).</strong> <code>load_runtime_or_warn()</code> returns <code>Some(manager)</code> whenever <code>mcp.json</code> declares ≥1 server, and <code>None</code> otherwise. MCP is a first-class, always-supported capability — there is no separate enable flag; declaring a server <em>is</em> the activation signal. (An earlier draft gated activation behind an <code>OPENAB_AGENT_MCP={1,true,yes,on}</code> env var so an incidentally-present <code>mcp.json</code> couldn't auto-spawn third-party child processes. That gate was dropped: MCP is always on, and the operator owns what ships in <code>mcp.json</code>. The stdio child env-scrubbing in choice 2 remains the standing mitigation against an untrusted server reading inherited secrets.) The CLI subcommands (<code>mcp list / status / connect / doctor</code>) call <code>load_config_or_exit</code> rather than <code>load_runtime_or_warn</code>, so they inspect a config without starting the long-running runtime.</li>\n<li><strong>Stdio child env scrubbing (F2, intentional security).</strong> <code>Dial::Stdio</code> calls <code>env_clear()</code> and passes only the 4-var baseline allowlist (<code>HOME</code>, <code>PATH</code>, <code>TERM</code>, <code>USER</code> on Unix; Windows equivalents) plus the explicit <code>env:</code> map from <code>mcp.json</code>. Reasoning: openab-agent inherits high-value secrets from its launcher (<code>DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code>, <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code>, AWS credentials, GitHub tokens) and stdio MCP servers are third-party binaries with no contractual constraint on what they read from their environment. Leaking those by default is a much larger risk than the convenience of inherited proxy/locale settings. Servers that genuinely need additional env (proxy, certs, locale, provider config) declare them per-server in the config — a future <code>inherit_env</code> opt-in list is tracked as follow-up if user demand surfaces.</li>\n<li><strong>Per-process shared <code>McpRuntimeManager</code> (F7).</strong> A single manager is <code>Arc</code>-cloned across all ACP sessions of the same process. Reasoning: MCP servers are expensive to spawn (stdio child fork, HTTP handshake + OAuth) and most are pure-state read-only tools where cross-session visibility is benign. Trade-off: a <code>mcp connect github</code> in session A makes the <code>github</code> server immediately available in session B. We accept this — per-session isolation would multiply child processes and break the breaker / TTL accounting in §5.7 / §5.9.</li>\n</ol>\n<h4>5.4.2 Discovery slice — bounded catalogue + idle semantics (F1)</h4>\n<p>The §5.1 / §5.2 single <code>mcp</code> meta-tool minimizes the LLM-facing tool surface, but it also <em>hides</em> the configured server names from the LLM. The F1 PoC reproduced the resulting failure mode: when a user said &quot;use mcp fs to list /workspace&quot;, the LLM called <code>mcp(action: &quot;status&quot;)</code>, saw <code>fs: disconnected</code>, read it as &quot;broken&quot;, and refused to retry. Two intentional choices remove that failure mode without re-flattening the tool surface:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Static server catalogue in the system prompt.</strong> <code>mcp::format_system_prompt_appendix(manager)</code> appends a <code>## MCP tool</code> section containing the tool intro plus <code>- **{name}** ({transport})</code> per configured server (with a <code>requires \\</code>mcp login <name>`<code>annotation when an</code>oauth<code>block is present). The list is built once at</code>Agent::new_boxed<code>time from a sync</code>manager.catalog()<code>snapshot frozen at</code>from_config<code>, so no async or lock coordination is needed inside </code>build_system_prompt<code>. Token-budget invariance is preserved: section size grows **O(server count)** — not O(server count × tool count) — because per-tool descriptors stay behind </code>mcp(action: &quot;list_tools&quot;, server)`. The PoC measured ≤100 tokens per server-side entry under this pattern; flattening tools per-server (≈ what the multi-tool alternative in §4.1 would expose) blows that budget by ~30× for a typical 30-tool github server.</p>\n<p>Mirror with the Skills catalogue (<code>skills::format_skills_prompt</code>): both advertise <em>names + headline metadata</em> in the always-present system prompt and force <em>body / contract</em> discovery through an explicit tool call (<code>mcp(action: &quot;list_tools&quot; | &quot;describe_tool&quot;)</code> here, <code>read(&quot;skills/&lt;name&gt;&quot;)</code> there). Same intent (the LLM knows the surface exists; details are lazy), same token-budget shape (linear in surface count, not in surface depth).</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Status label <code>idle</code> for lazy-connect servers.</strong> The meta-tool's <code>status_label</code> returns <code>idle</code> — not <code>disconnected</code> — when a server is in <code>ServerStatus::Disconnected</code> with no failure history. <code>disconnected</code> reads as &quot;broken&quot; to the LLM (PoC observation above); <code>idle</code> correctly signals &quot;ready, will dial on first call&quot;. The genuine failure case still maps to <code>status: &quot;failed&quot;</code> with the dial / handshake error in <code>last_error</code>, so the LLM can distinguish &quot;not tried yet&quot; from &quot;tried and broke&quot;. The system-prompt section also advertises these semantics explicitly so the LLM doesn't have to guess.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<p>These choices are wired into PR #959 (Phase 1) because the failure mode they fix is reachable as soon as <code>list_servers</code> and <code>status</code> ship — deferring to Phase 2/3 would mean shipping a known-broken discovery UX on the foundation slice.</p>\n<h3>5.5 <code>rmcp</code> dependency &amp; features</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># openab-agent/Cargo.toml\n[dependencies]\nrmcp = { version = &quot;1.7&quot;, default-features = false, features = [\n    &quot;client&quot;,\n    &quot;transport-child-process&quot;,\n    &quot;transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest&quot;,\n    &quot;auth&quot;,\n] }\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>client</code> only — we host nothing</li>\n<li><code>transport-child-process</code> — stdio servers (majority of registry, see §3.8)</li>\n<li><code>transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest</code> — vendor-hosted SaaS endpoints (reqwest is already a transitive dep)</li>\n<li><code>auth</code> — OAuth helpers</li>\n<li><code>default-features = false</code> — avoid pulling SSE / server features we don't need (SSE intentionally omitted per §3.8 — superseded by Streamable HTTP in MCP spec 2025-11-25, all surveyed vendors migrated or migrating)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Binary delta estimate: <strong>+1-2 MB</strong> (see §7).</p>\n<h3>5.6 Config schema</h3>\n<p>Single root key <code>mcpServers</code> to match Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Cline convention. Loaded from <code>.openab/agent/mcp.json</code> (project) and <code>~/.openab/agent/mcp.json</code> (global), project-local takes precedence on name collision.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;mcpServers&quot;: {\n    &quot;github&quot;: {\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;stdio&quot;,\n      &quot;command&quot;: &quot;github-mcp-server&quot;,\n      &quot;args&quot;: [&quot;--repo-token&quot;, &quot;${env:GITHUB_TOKEN}&quot;],\n      &quot;env&quot;: { &quot;GH_HOST&quot;: &quot;github.com&quot; }\n    },\n    &quot;linear&quot;: {\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;http&quot;,\n      &quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://mcp.linear.app/mcp&quot;,\n      &quot;oauth&quot;: { &quot;provider&quot;: &quot;linear&quot; }\n    },\n    &quot;fs&quot;: {\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;stdio&quot;,\n      &quot;command&quot;: &quot;mcp-server-filesystem&quot;,\n      &quot;args&quot;: [&quot;/workspace&quot;],\n      &quot;tool_filter&quot;: { &quot;include&quot;: [&quot;read_*&quot;, &quot;list_*&quot;] }\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>${env:VAR}</code> interpolation matches Cursor / Cline; missing var = startup error for that server (others continue)</li>\n<li><code>tool_filter</code> supports <code>include</code> / <code>exclude</code> glob lists (lifted from OpenHands' <code>filter_tools_regex</code>)</li>\n<li>Per-server failure isolated — one bad server does not block agent boot</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>5.7 Lifecycle</h3>\n<pre><code>                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐\n                    │ McpRuntimeManager  (1 per agent)    │\n                    │                                     │\n                    │  config:           Arc&lt;McpConfig&gt;   │\n                    │  servers:          Map&lt;name, Hdl&gt;   │\n                    │  idle_ttl:         Duration (10m)   │\n                    │  max_concurrent:   usize    (10)    │\n                    └─────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                    │\n                                    │ on first call needing server X:\n                                    ▼\n                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐\n                    │ ServerHandle (lazy)                 │\n                    │                                     │\n                    │  state: Disconnected | Connecting | │\n                    │         Connected(Peer) | Failed |  │\n                    │         NeedsAuth                   │\n                    │  last_used: Instant                 │\n                    │  breaker: CircuitBreaker            │\n                    │  tools_cache: Vec&lt;ToolDef&gt;          │\n                    └─────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                    │\n                  ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐\n                  │                                   │\n            ┌───────────┐                       ┌───────────┐\n            │ child proc│                       │ HTTP conn │\n            │ (stdio)   │                       │ (reqwest) │\n            └───────────┘                       └───────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Lazy connect</strong>: server is <code>Disconnected</code> at boot; transitions to <code>Connecting → Connected</code> on first action needing it</li>\n<li><strong>Idle eviction</strong>: a background eviction loop (started at agent run) evicts servers idle &gt; <code>idle_ttl</code> (default 10m, configurable) — but only when the server is not mid-call (<code>in_flight == 0</code>); a busy server is never torn out from under an in-flight call. State drops to <code>Disconnected</code> (surfaced to the LLM as <code>idle</code>); tools cache retained for fast re-connect</li>\n<li><strong>Concurrency cap</strong>: <code>max_concurrent_servers</code> bounds simultaneously-<code>Connected</code> servers (default 10; see §7 for constrained-env tuning). When connecting a new server would exceed the cap, the LRU <strong>idle</strong> (<code>in_flight == 0</code>) connected server is evicted first; if every connected server is busy, the cap is exceeded transiently rather than evicting an in-use server</li>\n<li><strong>Connection reuse</strong>: while connected, all <code>mcp call</code> actions reuse the same <code>Peer</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>5.8 Config refresh model</h3>\n<p>Rather than file-watching mid-session, openab-agent re-reads <code>mcp.json</code> at session boundaries:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>New ACP session</strong> → <code>McpRuntimeManager::new()</code> parses <code>mcp.json</code> from scratch; ~5 LOC of glue, zero hot-path code</li>\n<li><strong>Mid-session config edit</strong> → not visible until next session; users re-open the Discord/Slack thread (cheap in openab's per-thread session model)</li>\n<li><strong>Process restart</strong> → applies config changes globally; rarely needed because broker spawns short-lived agent processes per session</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This drops <code>notify</code> crate + lease counter + diff applier (~150 LOC, race-condition hotspot) for an 80% UX coverage. Hermes' <code>/reload-mcp</code> slash command (§3.1) is the precedent for &quot;explicit user-triggered reload &gt;&gt; implicit file watcher&quot; in a coding-agent context.</p>\n<h3>5.9 Error isolation &amp; circuit breaker</h3>\n<p>Adopted from Hermes Agent (the only surveyed project that ships one):</p>\n<pre><code>                  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n                  │ CircuitBreaker (per server)             │\n                  │                                         │\n                  │  state: Closed | Open | HalfOpen        │\n                  │  fail_threshold: 3 (configurable)       │\n                  │  cooldown: 60s (configurable)           │\n                  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                    │\n            ┌───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐\n            │                       │                       │\n            ▼                       ▼                       ▼\n       3 consecutive fails     60s elapsed             1 success\n       ─────────────►         ─────────────►          ─────────────►\n       Closed → Open          Open → HalfOpen         HalfOpen → Closed\n                              (allow 1 probe)\n                                                            │\n                                                            │ probe fails\n                                                            ▼\n                                                       HalfOpen → Open\n                                                       (reset cooldown)\n</code></pre>\n<p>While <code>Open</code>, <code>mcp call</code> returns <code>{&quot;error&quot;:&quot;server unavailable, cooldown 45s remaining&quot;}</code> immediately — no child-process resurrection attempts, no LLM hang.</p>\n<p><code>rmcp</code> error model maps cleanly:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th><code>rmcp</code> error</th>\n<th>meta-tool response</th>\n<th>Counts toward breaker?</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ServiceError::McpError</code> (protocol)</td>\n<td><code>{ error: msg, code }</code></td>\n<td>No (server-level intent)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ServiceError::TransportSend/Closed</code></td>\n<td><code>{ error: &quot;transport&quot;, server: ... }</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>CallToolResult { isError: true }</code></td>\n<td>passed through as result</td>\n<td>No (tool-level)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. OAuth</h2>\n<h3>6.1 Shared TokenStore</h3>\n<p><code>openab-agent/src/auth.rs</code> already implements hand-rolled PKCE for Codex (<code>CODEX_AUTHORIZE_URL</code>, port 1455). The TokenStore (<code>~/.openab/agent/auth.json</code>, 0o600) is reused — <code>mcp/oauth.rs</code> calls into the same store with namespaced keys (<code>mcp:&lt;server_name&gt;</code> vs <code>codex</code>).</p>\n<p><strong>Persistence assumption</strong>: TokenStore is treated as persistent state. Deployments must mount <code>~/.openab/</code> on durable storage — hostPath / PVC (k8s work-agents), volume + S3 sync (Fargate Mira), or developer-laptop home directory. Ephemeral container filesystems force a re-bootstrap on every restart and are not a supported configuration.</p>\n<p><strong>Cold-start refresh</strong>: on process start the runtime reads TokenStore lazily (on first <code>mcp call</code> per server). Expired access tokens trigger an in-process refresh via the stored refresh token; success updates the store and proceeds transparently. Refresh failure (revoked / expired refresh token) flips the server's state to <code>NeedsAuth</code> (§5.7); the next <code>mcp call</code> returns an error that prompts the LLM to re-run the §6.4 login flow. No human interaction is required as long as the refresh token remains valid.</p>\n<p><strong>Refresh-token rotation race with async persistence layers</strong>: OAuth 2.1 servers issue a new refresh token on every rotation and immediately revoke the previous one; reuse of a revoked refresh token is treated as a replay attack and cascade-revokes the entire token chain. Deployments where TokenStore persistence is asynchronous (Fargate S3 sidecar sync, eventually-consistent volumes) must flush new tokens to durable storage <em>before</em> the agent can be killed — otherwise a Spot interruption between local write and remote sync restores the revoked token from S3 on the next task and locks the user out. Contract:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Agent side</strong>: <code>TokenStore</code> calls <code>fsync(2)</code> after every write to <code>auth.json</code></li>\n<li><strong>Deployment side</strong>: the S3 / volume sync layer must trigger on <code>auth.json</code> mtime change (<code>inotify</code> / <code>fsnotify</code> event), not poll on a cron. Cron-driven sync (≥1 min interval) is incompatible with refresh-token rotation under Spot interruption</li>\n<li><strong>Reference deployment</strong>: Mira (openab-ecs Fargate Spot) <code>mira-home/</code> S3 sync configuration</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>6.2 Built-in providers (Phase 2)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Provider</th>\n<th>Auth URL</th>\n<th>Token URL</th>\n<th>Callback</th>\n<th>Scopes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>anthropic-mcp</code></td>\n<td><code>https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize</code></td>\n<td><code>https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token</code></td>\n<td><code>localhost:53692/callback</code></td>\n<td><code>org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference user:sessions:claude_code user:mcp_servers user:file_upload</code> (subset varies per use)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>github-copilot</code></td>\n<td>(existing pi/anthropic flow)</td>\n<td>existing</td>\n<td>existing</td>\n<td>existing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>generic</code></td>\n<td>from <code>mcpServers[name].oauth.authorize_url</code></td>\n<td>from <code>.oauth.token_url</code></td>\n<td>dynamically allocated port</td>\n<td>from <code>.oauth.scopes</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Callback values apply when the browser flow is engaged (<code>--browser</code> / <code>$DISPLAY</code> set), and when the agent-guided paste-back branch of §6.4 is selected (user copies the redirect URL from the browser URL bar). The device-code branch of §6.4 ignores the callback entirely.</p>\n<h3>6.3 Custom provider extension point</h3>\n<p>Config can declare <code>oauth: { authorize_url, token_url, client_id, scopes, device_authorization_endpoint?, redirect_uri?, discovery?, discovery_allowlist? }</code> for any server. The generic provider handles PKCE + callback + token persistence. No code change needed for new MCP servers that use standard OAuth 2.1. If <code>device_authorization_endpoint</code> is set, §6.4 device-code flow is preferred over paste-back. RFC 8414 dynamic discovery is opt-in only and requires an allowlist — see §6.4.</p>\n<p><code>oauth.redirect_uri</code> is required by the paste-back branch of §6.4 for custom providers — it must match the URL pre-registered with the provider's OAuth app, since custom paste-back doesn't bind a local listener (built-ins pin their callback in <code>ProviderSpec</code>; the device-code branch ignores it).</p>\n<h3>6.4 Agent-guided OAuth flow (default)</h3>\n<p>openab-agent's primary deployment surface is containerized (k8s pods, Fargate tasks) where <code>localhost:53692/callback</code> is unreachable and there is no display to open. Two non-browser flows are supported; the runtime picks per server based on capability. Browser-callback remains a laptop-only opt-in (<code>$DISPLAY</code> set, or <code>--browser</code> passed to <code>openab-agent mcp login</code>).</p>\n<p><strong>Selection logic</strong> (on <code>mcp(action: &quot;login&quot;, server: X)</code>):</p>\n<ol>\n<li>If <code>X</code> declares an <code>oauth.device_authorization_endpoint</code> in config (§6.3), runtime uses <strong>device-code flow</strong> (RFC 8628). Matches openab's existing CLI convention (<code>claude auth login</code>, <code>codex --device-auth</code>, <code>grok --device-auth</code>).</li>\n<li>Else runtime uses <strong>paste-back flow</strong> (standard auth-code + PKCE). Universal fallback for OAuth 2.1 servers without a device endpoint (Linear, Notion, Figma, Sentry, ...).</li>\n</ol>\n<p>RFC 8414 dynamic discovery (<code>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server</code>) is <strong>disabled by default</strong>. Operators opt in per-server via <code>oauth.discovery: true</code> plus an explicit <code>oauth.discovery_allowlist</code> of permitted domains (e.g. <code>[&quot;*.anthropic.com&quot;]</code>); boot rejects <code>discovery: true</code> without an allowlist. Rationale: awsvpc egress restrictions + SSRF surface in multi-tenant deployments.</p>\n<p><strong>Device-code flow</strong> (typically platform OAuth: Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI):</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>login</code> returns <code>{ flow: &quot;device&quot;, user_code, verification_url, expires_in }</code>. Agent relays to chat: &quot;Open <code>https://example.com/device</code>, enter code: <code>ABCD-EFGH</code>&quot;.</li>\n<li>Runtime polls the token endpoint in background (5s interval, RFC 8628 §3.5). On success, persists tokens under <code>mcp:X</code>, transitions server to <code>Disconnected</code> so the next <code>connect()</code> reads the cached token via the oauth-aware dial path and reaches <code>Connected</code> through the normal lifecycle. Keeping the rmcp handshake out of the polling task avoids spawning child processes from a detached <code>tokio::task</code>.</li>\n<li>LLM checks <code>mcp(action: &quot;status&quot;, server: X)</code> to learn when the polling loop completes (status leaves <code>Connecting</code>); <code>complete_login</code> is not required for this branch — the next <code>mcp call</code> triggers <code>connect()</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Paste-back flow</strong> (typically MCP SaaS: Linear, Notion, Figma, ...):</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>login</code> returns <code>{ flow: &quot;paste&quot;, authorize_url, state }</code>. Runtime persists transient <code>{verifier, state}</code> in TokenStore. Agent relays to chat: &quot;Open this link, sign in, paste the URL you land on back here&quot;.</li>\n<li>User pastes the URL as next chat message; LLM calls <code>mcp(action: &quot;complete_login&quot;, server: X, redirect_url: &quot;...&quot;)</code>.</li>\n<li>Runtime parses <code>code</code> + <code>state</code>, validates <code>state</code>, performs PKCE token exchange against <code>token_url</code>, persists tokens under <code>mcp:X</code>, drops transient state.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Security</strong> (both flows):</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Device-code <code>user_code</code> is short-lived (RFC 8628 §3.2, typically ≤10 min); an attacker who sees the code in chat must also race the polling loop and prove device ownership.</li>\n<li>Paste-back redirect URL carries only the authorization code (OAuth 2.1 PKCE; implicit/hybrid removed); code is single-use + ≤10 min; PKCE verifier held in-process makes intercepted codes unusable.</li>\n<li>Token exchange happens entirely inside the agent process; the chat channel never carries access or refresh tokens. Refresh rotation runs in-process per §6.1.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><code>openab-agent/src/auth.rs</code> already ships all three paths for Codex OAuth (browser L150-244, paste-back L165-201, device L328-440). This ADR generalizes that pattern across MCP servers and centralizes flow selection on per-server capability rather than per-CLI hard-coding. OpenHands notes the same headless-OAuth incompatibility (§3.5) without shipping a fix.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Memory Impact Analysis</h2>\n<p>Included because the sidecar alternative (§4.1 B) was motivated by memory.</p>\n<p><code>openab-agent</code> baseline is 15-40 MB RSS. <code>rmcp</code> with the §5.5 feature set adds +1-2 MB binary delta and +0 MB idle RSS (no servers configured). Once servers connect, child processes dominate: Go ~10-20 MB, Rust ~5-10 MB, Python/Node ~30-80 MB each.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>A. Naïve flat</th>\n<th>B. Sidecar</th>\n<th><strong>C. In-core + meta-tool</strong></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Idle RAM delta</td>\n<td>+1-2 MB</td>\n<td>+0 MB</td>\n<td>+1-2 MB</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Per-server RAM</td>\n<td>+5-80 MB (child)</td>\n<td>+15 MB bridge + 5-80 MB</td>\n<td>+5-80 MB</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>System prompt tokens</td>\n<td>+17,000</td>\n<td>+600 (if sidecar discloses lazily)</td>\n<td>+600</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Lifecycle complexity</td>\n<td>Medium</td>\n<td>High (2 procs, IPC, version skew)</td>\n<td>Medium</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Crash blast radius</td>\n<td>Bad server kills loop</td>\n<td>Bridge crash = all gone</td>\n<td>Bad server isolated</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>The 1-2 MB sidecar saving is dominated by per-server child RAM (identical across architectures) and by token cost (identical <em>as long as progressive disclosure is used</em>). Memory does not justify the sidecar.</p>\n<p><strong>Constrained-environment note (Fargate / small Kubernetes pods).</strong> Fargate Spot tasks at 512 MB / 1 GB have no swap; OOMKill is hard. Worst-case stack — agent baseline 40 MB + 5 Node/Python stdio servers at 80 MB each + LLM context buffers — sums to ~440-540 MB, which trips a 512 MB task before any prompt processing. Two mitigations: (a) lower <code>max_concurrent_servers</code> to 3 in <code>mcp.json</code> (§5.7), bounding worst case to ~280 MB; (b) prefer Go/Rust stdio servers (5-20 MB) or HTTP servers (0 MB local) over Node/Python interpreters. The <code>mcp doctor</code> CLI (§8) flags configurations whose worst-case sum exceeds the cgroup limit.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. CLI Surface</h2>\n<pre><code>openab-agent mcp list                       — show configured servers + status\nopenab-agent mcp status [server]            — health, last error, OAuth state\nopenab-agent mcp add &lt;name&gt; &lt;command&gt;       — append a stdio server to config\nopenab-agent mcp add &lt;name&gt; --url &lt;url&gt;     — append an http server\nopenab-agent mcp remove &lt;name&gt;              — remove a server from config\nopenab-agent mcp login &lt;name&gt; [--browser]   — run OAuth flow (see §6.4; --browser opts into localhost callback)\nopenab-agent mcp refresh &lt;name&gt;             — force-refresh OAuth token\nopenab-agent mcp test &lt;name&gt; &lt;tool&gt; [json]  — invoke a tool from CLI (debug)\nopenab-agent mcp doctor                     — diagnose config, network, auth\n</code></pre>\n<p>Subcommand placement under existing <code>openab-agent</code> binary — no new binary. CLI is a thin wrapper over <code>McpRuntimeManager</code> to keep the same code path validated by both LLM-driven and human-driven flows.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Rollout Plan</h2>\n<p>Delivered across three phases (all landed):</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Foundation</strong> — <code>rmcp</code> + stdio + meta-tool + minimal CLI</li>\n<li><strong>Network &amp; auth</strong> — Streamable HTTP transport + OAuth providers + <code>login</code>/<code>refresh</code> CLI</li>\n<li><strong>Resilience</strong> — per-server circuit breaker (§5.9), idle eviction + concurrency cap (§5.7), and <code>doctor</code> CLI</li>\n</ol>\n<p>The runtime's activation contract is described in §5.4.1 (the long-running ACP path calls <code>load_runtime_or_warn()</code>, the CLI subcommands use <code>load_config_or_exit</code>); there is no Cargo <code>--features mcp</code> build flag.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. Open Questions</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Should <code>mcp.json</code> live in the agent or the broker?</strong> Agent owns its own config today; broker's <code>[agent].inherit_cloud_mcp_servers</code> (issue #753) is a separate concern. Proposal: agent reads <code>mcp.json</code> directly; broker can layer additional servers via env or kubectl ConfigMap. <strong>Owner</strong>: needs broker-team alignment.</li>\n<li><strong>Native-agent feature parity with broker-forward path.</strong> PRs #329/#330/#345/#903 attempted broker-side MCP forwarding to backing CLIs. With native MCP in openab-agent, do we deprecate that path, keep it for non-native CLIs, or unify? Proposal: native agent uses its own MCP runtime; broker continues to forward to backing CLIs that lack native MCP (Cursor, Copilot). <strong>Owner</strong>: broker-team.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Resolved at design time (tracked in tracking issue, not open): tool-naming prefix (<code>&lt;server&gt;_&lt;tool&gt;</code> single-underscore, matching Hermes §3.1 / opencode §3.2 convention), <code>session/load</code> re-enumeration (process-local state, re-read), per-tool permission gates (post-Phase-3 opt-in flag), <code>resources</code>/<code>prompts</code> capabilities (v2).</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>11. References</h2>\n<h3>Internal</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>docs/adr/openab-agent.md</code> — agent charter, design principles cited in §4.2</li>\n<li><code>docs/adr/pr-contribution-guidelines.md</code> — prior-art requirements followed in §3</li>\n<li><code>openab-agent/src/skills.rs</code> (PR #955) — extension-pattern precedent cited in §4.3</li>\n<li><code>openab-agent/src/auth.rs</code> — TokenStore reused in §6.1</li>\n<li>PRs #329, #330, #345, #903 — closed broker-forward attempts, §1.3</li>\n<li>Issue #753 — broker-side MCP opt-out (out of scope)</li>\n<li>PR #951 — SessionPool persisted-mapping fix (informs §10 resolved-at-design-time list)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>External — projects</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Hermes Agent: <a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\">https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent</a></li>\n<li>opencode: <a href=\"https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode\">https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode</a> (formerly <a href=\"https://github.com/sst/opencode\">https://github.com/sst/opencode</a>)</li>\n<li>pi-mcp-adapter: <a href=\"https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter\">https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter</a></li>\n<li>Goose: <a href=\"https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose\">https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose</a> (formerly <a href=\"https://github.com/block/goose\">https://github.com/block/goose</a>)</li>\n<li>OpenHands: <a href=\"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands\">https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands</a></li>\n<li>rmcp: <a href=\"https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk\">https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk</a></li>\n<li>OpenClaw (evaluated per <code>pr-contribution-guidelines.md</code>, scope not applicable — see §3; canonical repo URL not publicly resolvable, internal reference via avasdream blog cited in guidelines)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>External — specs &amp; research</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>MCP spec: <a href=\"https://modelcontextprotocol.io\">https://modelcontextprotocol.io</a></li>\n<li>MCP spec changelog 2025-11-25 (Streamable HTTP supersedes HTTP+SSE): <a href=\"https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports\">https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports</a></li>\n<li>MCP SEP-1576 — Mitigating Token Bloat in MCP: <a href=\"https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/issues/1576\">https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/issues/1576</a></li>\n<li>Atlassian Rovo MCP SSE→Streamable HTTP migration notice (sunset 2026-06-30): <a href=\"https://community.atlassian.com/forums/Rovo-articles/Migrating-from-Atlassian-s-MCP-Server-SSE-to-Streamable-HTTP/ba-p/3092878\">https://community.atlassian.com/forums/Rovo-articles/Migrating-from-Atlassian-s-MCP-Server-SSE-to-Streamable-HTTP/ba-p/3092878</a></li>\n<li>Figma MCP server (Streamable HTTP): <a href=\"https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/32132100833559-Guide-to-the-Dev-Mode-MCP-Server\">https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/32132100833559-Guide-to-the-Dev-Mode-MCP-Server</a></li>\n<li>Anthropic — Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills: <a href=\"https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills\">https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills</a></li>\n<li>Anthropic — Code execution with MCP: <a href=\"https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp\">https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp</a></li>\n<li>Simon Willison — Claude Skills (2025-10-16): <a href=\"https://simonwillison.net/2025/Oct/16/claude-skills/\">https://simonwillison.net/2025/Oct/16/claude-skills/</a></li>\n<li>StackOne — MCP Token Optimization: <a href=\"https://www.stackone.com/blog/mcp-token-optimization/\">https://www.stackone.com/blog/mcp-token-optimization/</a></li>\n<li>opencode issues cited in §3.2, §4.1, §7: #11868, #7261,         "title": "ADR: openab-agent — MCP Client Support"
