    {
      "slug": "adr/openab-agent-oauth",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: openab-agent — Multi-Vendor LLM-Provider OAuth &amp; Credential Storage</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-24</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @brettchien</li>\n<li><strong>Related:</strong> <code>docs/adr/openab-agent.md</code> (charter), <code>docs/adr/openab-agent-mcp.md</code> §6 (MCP OAuth + §6.1 storage format), PR #1187 (Anthropic OAuth, first provider), PR #1185 (<code>/auth</code> device-flow relay), PR #1111 (<code>--no-browser</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Motivation</h2>\n<h3>1.1 Why now</h3>\n<p><code>openab-agent</code> reaches LLM providers in two ways: <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code> (pay-per-token) and an existing\nCodex subscription-OAuth tenant in <code>~/.openab/agent/auth.json</code>. <strong>PR #1187</strong> adds native <strong>Anthropic\n(Claude Pro/Max) OAuth</strong> as a second subscription tenant. This is the moment to set the pattern for <em>every</em>\nfuture provider rather than let each PR hand-roll its own flow.</p>\n<h3>1.2 What PR #1187 surfaced</h3>\n<p>Reviewing #1187 exposed a latent, <strong>release-blocker-class storage bug</strong> that is independent of any single\nprovider: <code>auth.json</code> is a shared multi-writer file with an <strong>unlocked read-modify-write</strong>, and openab-agent\nruns <strong>one process per Discord thread</strong> (<code>SessionPool</code> in <code>crates/openab-core/src/acp/pool.rs</code> → <code>crates/openab-core/src/acp/connection.rs</code>\nspawns one <code>openab-agent</code> child per thread). So ordinary concurrent multi-thread usage = concurrent\nprocesses refreshing the same OAuth token → refresh-token-rotation reuse → worst case OAuth 2.1 §10.4\n<strong>token-family revocation = fleet-wide logout</strong>. API-key users never hit this (no refresh); <strong>OAuth adoption\nis what activates the bug.</strong></p>\n<h3>1.3 The wider demand</h3>\n<p>openab packages 14 agent variants (<code>kiro, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, grok, hermes, mimocode, opencode, antigravity, pi, native, agentcore</code>). Several wrap a model vendor reachable by subscription OAuth.\nA coherent extension model lets openab-agent (the <code>native</code> variant) host these directly. PR #1185 already\nshipped a Discord <code>/auth</code> slash command that relays a device-flow login — the agreed near-term auth UX.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Goals &amp; Non-Goals</h2>\n<h3>In scope</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>A single <strong><code>OAuthVendor</code> adapter</strong> (auth axis) reused by all subscription-OAuth providers.</li>\n<li>Keeping the <strong>inference axis</strong> (per-provider request/response transport) <strong>separate</strong> from auth.</li>\n<li>A <strong>concurrency-safe credential store</strong>: all <code>auth.json</code> writes funnel through one locked\nread-modify-write helper (covers MCP <code>CredentialStore</code> + provider tenants).</li>\n<li>Support for the OAuth styles real vendors use: <strong>PKCE public</strong>, <strong>PKCE + bundled client_secret</strong>,\n<strong>device flow (RFC 8628)</strong>, and <strong>pre-provisioned long-lived token via env</strong> (<code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code>).</li>\n<li>Compatibility with PR #1185's <code>/auth</code> poll-and-exit relay model.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Out of scope</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Layer-3 auto-trigger</strong> (agent auto-launches login on a mid-turn 401). DEFERRED (Brett, 2026-06-24);\nthe manual <code>/auth</code> command is sufficient for now.</li>\n<li>Building every vendor at once. This ADR sets the model; vendors land incrementally.</li>\n<li>Non-OAuth backends: <code>agentcore</code> (AWS SigV4/IAM/Bedrock) is explicitly outside the OAuth surface.</li>\n<li>MCP-server OAuth internals — owned by <code>docs/adr/openab-agent-mcp.md</code>; this ADR only shares the storage\nlayer with it.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Prior Art Survey</h2>\n<p>(Per <code>docs/adr/pr-contribution-guidelines.md</code>, OpenClaw + Hermes are mandatory references.)</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Pi (<code>earendil-works/pi</code>)</strong> — primary source ported for #1187's Anthropic flow (PKCE endpoints, Claude\nCode identity headers, system block, tool-name casing). Also ships <code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code> support\n(pi #3591) and provider extensions for Kiro / Cursor / xAI — evidence the per-vendor adapter shape works.</li>\n<li><strong>OpenClaw</strong> — API keys + subscription OAuth. Anthropic via <strong>setup-token</strong> or <strong>reuse of local Claude\nCLI</strong> (no native PKCE login). Codex via full PKCE. Stores per-profile <code>{access,refresh,expires,accountId}</code>\nand treats the profile file as a <strong>token sink refreshed under a file lock</strong> — direct corroboration for the\nlocked-RMW decision (§5.4).</li>\n<li><strong>Hermes Agent (NousResearch)</strong> — <code>PROVIDER_REGISTRY</code> dataclasses declare each provider's auth type +\nURLs + env vars; one <code>resolve_runtime_provider()</code> entry point. Anthropic is <strong>API-key only</strong> (or reuse\n<code>~/.claude/.credentials.json</code>). <code>auth.json</code> guarded with <code>fcntl</code>/<code>msvcrt</code> file locks — again corroborates\n§5.4. The registry pattern is the spiritual model for <code>OAuthVendor</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Vendor CLIs (evidence for the matrix, §6):</strong> Gemini CLI (<code>code_assist/oauth2.ts</code>), Antigravity\n(<code>opencode-antigravity-auth</code> + <code>ANTIGRAVITY_API_SPEC.md</code>), GitHub Copilot CLI, Kiro CLI, xAI/Grok,\nXiaomi MiMo Code — surveyed 2026-06-24 (§6).</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>How this ADR differs:</strong> like OpenClaw/Hermes it keeps one namespaced multi-tenant credential file with\natomic writes + per-refresh rotation handling, and (unlike both) adds native PKCE logins. It adds two things\nneither documents cleanly: a <strong>two-axis</strong> auth/inference split, and an explicit <strong>cross-process</strong> locked-RMW\ninvariant (both flag file locks but for the simpler single-process case).</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Design Decision</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Adopt a two-axis model.</strong> Auth (how a credential is obtained/refreshed/stored) and inference (how a\nrequest is sent) are <strong>orthogonal</strong> and must not be coupled. A vendor that serves Claude over Google's\nCode Assist envelope (agy; see §6) reuses neither Anthropic's Messages-V1 transport nor its auth.\n<strong>Note — &quot;agy as a GO vendor&quot; ≠ running the agy CLI.</strong> This ADR adds agy as an <code>OAuthVendor</code> + Code-Assist\ninference <em>provider</em> consumed by the <strong>native</strong> openab-agent; it does <strong>not</strong> spawn the agy binary. That\nmatters because <strong>agy speaks no ACP</strong> — the existing <code>antigravity</code> <em>runtime variant</em> (Mira on ECS) only\nworks via a dedicated <code>agy-acp</code> adapter that shells out to the agy CLI per prompt and polls its SQLite\nconversation DB to synthesize ACP events. The vendor/provider path here <strong>sidesteps ACP entirely</strong> and\nsupersedes that CLI-wrapper for native use — agy's lack of ACP is irrelevant to it (see §6).</li>\n<li><strong>Auth axis = one <code>OAuthVendor</code> descriptor + a shared driver built on the official <code>oauth2</code> crate</strong> (§5.1;\nthe crate is already in-tree via the MCP side). New vendor = new descriptor; PKCE/CSRF/auth-code\nexchange/refresh come from the crate, <strong>not hand-rolled</strong>. The few vendor quirks (e.g. Anthropic's JSON\ntoken body) are applied through the crate's custom http-client hook, not by forking the flow.</li>\n<li><strong>Inference axis = one provider per wire format</strong> (§5.2). Four formats today; no reuse across them.</li>\n<li><strong>Credential storage = locked-RMW funnel + per-tenant refresh lock</strong> (§5.4). <em>Every</em> write to <code>auth.json</code>\ngoes through <code>with_auth_locked</code> (global lock — file integrity); <em>every</em> token refresh serializes on a\n<strong>per-tenant</strong> lock so concurrent processes perform exactly one network refresh per tenant and never\npresent a rotated <code>RT_old</code> twice (which would trigger OAuth 2.1 §10.4 token-family revocation). A\nConsequence of the multi-writer/cross-process reality, not an optional perf tweak.</li>\n<li><strong>Credential-source precedence:</strong> explicit API key → pre-provisioned long-lived OAuth token env\n(<code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code> and equivalents) → stored interactive OAuth tenant. Rationale + why the env\npath is the preferred fleet mode: §5.3.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Detailed Design</h2>\n<h3>5.1 <code>OAuthVendor</code> (auth axis)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">trait OAuthVendor {\n    fn namespace(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;str;                 // &quot;codex&quot; / &quot;anthropic-oauth&quot; / &quot;antigravity&quot; ...\n    fn client_id(&amp;self) -&gt; String;               // env override + default\n    fn client_secret(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; { None }    // Gemini = Some(bundled); agy TBD (§9 Q2); Anthropic/Codex = None\n    fn authorize_url(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;str;\n    fn token_url(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;str;\n    fn redirect(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;(u16, &amp;'static str)&gt; { None } // Some((port,path)) for loopback PKCE; None for device flow (no redirect endpoint)\n    fn scope(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;str;\n    fn extra_authorize_params(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;[(&amp;str,&amp;str)] { &amp;[] }       // Anthropic: (&quot;code&quot;,&quot;true&quot;)\n    fn token_body(&amp;self) -&gt; TokenBodyFormat { TokenBodyFormat::Form } // Anthropic = Json-no-scope\n    fn grant(&amp;self) -&gt; AuthGrant { AuthGrant::Pkce }                  // DeviceCode for copilot/kiro\n}\nenum TokenBodyFormat { Form, Json }\nenum AuthGrant { Pkce, DeviceCode }\n</code></pre>\n<p>The shared driver is built on the <strong>official <code>oauth2</code> crate</strong> (already a dependency via the MCP side): it\nsupplies PKCE, CSRF <code>state</code>, the authorization-code exchange, and refresh; the descriptor only feeds it\nper-vendor config. Hand-rolled code is limited to what the crate does not cover — the loopback/paste/\ndevice-code callback plumbing (fold the existing Codex flow into the shared <code>accept_callback_code</code> helper —\nits comment already says &quot;fold it in&quot;; unify the <code>127.0.0.1</code> vs <code>localhost</code> bind) and the single\nbody-encoding override (Anthropic's JSON-no-scope token request, applied via the crate's custom http-client\nhook rather than a separate flow).</p>\n<h3>5.2 Inference providers (inference axis — no reuse)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Provider</th>\n<th>Endpoint</th>\n<th>Wire format</th>\n<th>Vendors</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AnthropicProvider</code> (exists)</td>\n<td><code>api.anthropic.com/v1/messages</code></td>\n<td>Anthropic Messages V1</td>\n<td>claude; mimocode <code>/anthropic</code> mirror</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OpenAiProvider</code> (exists)</td>\n<td>OpenAI-style <code>/v1/chat/completions</code></td>\n<td>OpenAI Chat/Responses</td>\n<td>codex, grok, copilot, mimocode</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AntigravityProvider</code> (new)</td>\n<td><code>cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com</code></td>\n<td>Google Code Assist (<code>{project,model,request}</code>→<code>{candidates[]}</code>)</td>\n<td>gemini, agy</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AwsQProvider</code> (new, heaviest)</td>\n<td>AWS CodeWhisperer/Q</td>\n<td>AWS proprietary event-stream</td>\n<td>kiro</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>OAuth-mode request decoration (Bearer + identity headers/system-block/tool-name casing) stays in the\ninference provider; if shared, a small <code>decorate_request()</code> hook — never folded into <code>OAuthVendor</code>.</p>\n<h3>5.3 Credential-source precedence &amp; the env route</h3>\n<p>Anthropic offers a route that bypasses interactive login entirely: <code>claude setup-token</code> mints a long-lived\nsubscription OAuth token (~1-year per Anthropic's Claude Code docs) exposed as <strong><code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code></strong>. For pods, ops mints it once and injects\nit as a k8s secret — no interactive flow, no <code>auth.json</code> write, near-zero race exposure. openab-agent should\nread it as a Bearer subscription source, precedence: <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code> → <code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code> →\nstored <code>anthropic-oauth</code> tenant. This is the recommended fleet mode; interactive OAuth is for self-service.</p>\n<h3>5.4 Concurrency &amp; storage invariant (folds in the flock decision)</h3>\n<p><code>auth.json</code> is multi-tenant (<code>codex</code>, <code>anthropic-oauth</code>, <code>mcp:&lt;server&gt;</code>×N) and written by <strong>two independent\nread-modify-write call sites</strong> across <strong>multiple processes</strong> (one per Discord thread): provider tokens via\n<code>save_tokens</code> (<code>openab-agent/src/auth.rs:234</code>) and <strong>MCP</strong> OAuth creds via <code>McpCredentialStore::save</code>/<code>clear</code>\n(<code>auth.rs:284-328</code>), plus the MCP pending-login finalize path. <strong>Today there is <em>no</em> lock on <code>auth.json</code></strong> —\nonly an atomic <code>tmp+rename</code> in the shared low-level <code>write_auth_file</code>; the two RMW callers each do their own\nunlocked <code>read_auth_file → mutate map → write_auth_file</code>, so a concurrent provider-refresh and MCP-save\nlast-writer-wins the <em>entire</em> map (lost update). Two distinct hazards demand two locks — <strong>and the fix is not\nprovider-only: the MCP <code>CredentialStore</code> is a co-equal RMW caller that must be routed through the same\ninvariant</strong> (see §9 Q4). (<code>with_auth_locked</code> below is <em>new</em> — the thing this ADR introduces.)</p>\n<p><strong>(a) File integrity — one global lock.</strong> Every write funnels through a single locked RMW so concurrent\nwriters never lost-update the shared file:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">// ALL writers funnel through this. auth.rs storage layer.\nfn with_auth_locked&lt;R&gt;(path: &amp;Path, f: impl FnOnce(&amp;mut HashMap&lt;String, AuthEntry&gt;) -&gt; R) -&gt; Result&lt;R&gt; {\n    let _g = flock_exclusive(&quot;auth.json.global.lock&quot;)?;  // sidecar file (NOT auth.json — rename swaps its inode)\n    let mut map = read_auth_file(&amp;path)?;          // re-read inside lock (anti lost-update)\n    let r = f(&amp;mut map);\n    write_auth_file(&amp;path, &amp;map)?;                 // existing atomic tmp+rename\n    Ok(r)\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>(b) Refresh-token rotation — one lock per tenant.</strong> An earlier draft ran the refresh <em>outside</em> the lock\nand committed the result inside, claiming &quot;N processes do 1 real refresh.&quot; <strong>That is wrong</strong> (Mira review,\n2026-06-24): re-read-on-commit only prevents a lost <em>write</em> — every process has already <em>sent</em> a network\nrefresh carrying the same <code>RT_old</code> before it reaches the commit. Under OAuth 2.1 §10.4 refresh-token\nrotation, the second <code>RT_old</code> presentation reads as reuse and the AS <strong>revokes the whole token family</strong> =\nexactly the fleet-wide logout this ADR exists to prevent. Holding the <em>global</em> exclusive lock across the\nnetwork refresh would serialize it, but then a slow refresh for one tenant head-of-line-blocks every other\ntenant (MCP servers, Codex). So: <strong>one exclusive lock file per tenant</strong>, network I/O held under the tenant\nlock only — never under the global lock:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">fn get_or_refresh(tenant: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;String&gt; {\n    // 1. fast path — fresh token under a shared (read) global lock\n    if let Some(t) = read_fresh(tenant)? { return Ok(t); }\n    // 2. serialize refreshes for THIS tenant only (other tenants unaffected)\n    let _tg = flock_exclusive(&amp;format!(&quot;auth.json.refresh.{tenant}.lock&quot;))?;\n    // 3. double-check — another process may have refreshed while we waited on the tenant lock\n    if let Some(t) = read_fresh(tenant)? { return Ok(t); }\n    // 4. exactly one network refresh per tenant per expiry — tenant lock held, global lock NOT\n    let fresh = perform_network_refresh(tenant)?;\n    // 5. commit under the global lock (fast inode swap, no network I/O inside)\n    with_auth_locked(|m| m.insert(tenant.into(), fresh.clone()))?;\n    Ok(fresh.access_token)\n}\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>flock(2)</code>, not a sentinel lockfile</strong>: kernel auto-releases on fd close / process death → a hung or\nkilled refresher frees its tenant lock instantly. No stale lock, no manual timeout/orphan cleanup.</li>\n<li><strong>try-lock + timeout</strong> on the global lock so a wedged writer degrades to a graceful error, never a wedged\nworker.</li>\n<li><strong>Bounded refresh + fail-closed tenant-lock timeout.</strong> Each refresh round-trip is bounded by an explicit\nHTTP timeout (<code>REFRESH_HTTP_TIMEOUT</code> = 8s), and the lock-acquire deadline is <strong>sized above the worst-case\nlock-hold</strong>: <code>REFRESH_LOCK_TIMEOUT = MAX_REFRESH_ROUND_TRIPS × REFRESH_HTTP_TIMEOUT + margin = 20s</code>. The\nMCP path holds the lock across <strong>two</strong> sequential bounded calls (rmcp's <code>initialize_from_store()</code>\nauthorization-server discovery, then <code>get_access_token()</code> refresh); the codex path one. Combined with\n<code>flock(2)</code> auto-release on holder death, a live holder still progressing through its bounded refresh always\nfrees the tenant lock before any waiter's deadline. A lock-acquire timeout is therefore <em>abnormal</em>, and\nproceeding unserialised would re-present <code>RT_old</code> and risk the §10.4 family revocation this lock prevents —\nstrictly worse than a transient retry. So the waiter <strong>fails closed</strong>: <code>lock_tenant_refresh</code> returns\n<code>RefreshLock::TimedOut</code> (logged at <code>error!</code>), the codex path surfaces a retryable error, and the MCP path\nreturns a <em>transient</em> dial error that leaves the server retryable <strong>without</strong> forcing re-login (<code>NeedsAuth</code>)\nor tripping the circuit breaker. (A filesystem error opening the sidecar returns <code>RefreshLock::Unavailable</code>\nand degrades to a best-effort unserialised refresh rather than blocking every refresh on a broken lock dir.)\nThis bounded-refresh + fail-closed design supersedes the earlier fail-open draft, which reintroduced the\ndouble-refresh in exactly the contended case the lock exists for.</li>\n<li><strong>Crate:</strong> <code>libc::flock</code> directly (<code>rustix</code> is <strong>not</strong> in-tree — this ADR's earlier <code>rustix::fs::flock</code>\ntext was optimistic), wrapped in a small <code>unsafe</code> + RAII guard, gated <code>#[cfg(unix)]</code> with a non-unix\nno-op — mirroring the existing atomic-write cfg split. (openab-agent is de-facto unix-only: its\n<code>ci-openab-agent.yml</code> is linux, deploy is always container; Windows binaries are the broker only. The\nnon-unix <code>lock_global</code> no-op emits a one-time <code>tracing::warn!</code> so the unprotected state is never silent.)</li>\n<li>Each MCP <code>mcp:&lt;server&gt;</code> tenant takes its own tenant lock by the same rule, so the MCP <code>CredentialStore</code>\nrefreshes are serialized per server too — the invariant serves it directly (see <code>openab-agent-mcp.md</code>\n§6.1). rmcp owns the MCP refresh internally (no pre-refresh <code>CredentialStore</code> hook), but openab drives it\nexplicitly at <code>resolve_oauth_dial</code> (<code>mcp/runtime.rs</code>) via <code>client.get_access_token()</code>; the per-server\ntenant lock wraps that call, and rmcp's <code>initialize_from_store()</code> re-<code>load()</code>s <code>auth.json</code> from disk\n(after which <code>get_access_token</code> skips the network refresh when the loaded token is already fresh), so the\nlock-loser adopts the winner's token (cross-process single-flight) without a second <code>RT_old</code> presentation.</li>\n<li><strong>Until this lands</strong>, prefer the <code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code> env route (§5.3 — no refresh write, no race);\ntreat interactive Anthropic OAuth as not-yet-hardened for high concurrency.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Vendor feasibility matrix (surveyed 2026-06-24)</h2>\n<pre><code>Variant      OAuth style                Inference bucket               Native feasibility\n──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nclaude       PKCE public  (+env token)  Anthropic Messages V1         ✅ done (#1187) + add env route\ncodex        PKCE public / device       OpenAI                        ✅ done (has device flow)\ngrok (xAI)   xai-oauth (sub) / api-key  OpenAI-compatible             🟢 easy (reuse OpenAiProvider)\nmimocode     MiMo Platform OAuth/key    OpenAI-compat (+/anthropic)   🟢 easy (dual-bucket; OAuth low-ROI)\ncopilot      GitHub device flow         OpenAI-compat (githubcopilot) 🟡 token exchange + CC headers\ngemini       PKCE + bundled secret      Google Code Assist            🟡 new provider\nantigravity  PKCE + bundled secret      Google Code Assist            🟡 same provider; ToS-risk*\nkiro         AWS Builder ID device flow AWS Q/CodeWhisperer (propr.)  🔴 hard (event-stream)\ncursor       Cursor browser OAuth       Cursor proprietary proxy      🔴 reverse-eng, ToS-risk*\nhermes       API-key                    multi                         ⚪ agent shell, not a vendor\nopencode     BYO (per-auth plugins)     multi                         ⚪ agent shell\npi           BYO (provider extensions)  multi                         ⚪ agent shell\nnative       —                          —                             = openab-agent itself\nagentcore    AWS SigV4/IAM (not OAuth)  AWS Bedrock                   ❌ out of OAuth scope\n</code></pre>\n<p>Concrete values (verified): codex <code>app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann</code> (no secret, form); claude\n<code>9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e</code> (no secret, JSON no-scope); gemini\n<code>681255809395-oo8ft2oprdrnp9e3aqf6av3hmdib135j</code> (+ bundled <code>GOCSPX-…</code> — non-confidential by spec but <strong>not</strong> safe as raw repo text; storage decided in §9 Q2); agy\n<code>1071006060591-tmhssin2h21lcre235vtolojh4g403ep</code> (bundled secret <strong>CONFIRMED</strong> 2026-06-24 — the same public\n<code>GOCSPX-…</code> constant ≥20 antigravity-auth ecosystem repos hardcode verbatim, e.g. <code>NoeFabris/opencode-antigravity-auth</code>,\n<code>router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI</code>; <strong>deliberately not reproduced here</strong> — pasting the literal would trip the very\n§9 Q2 push-protection, so we dogfood the env/encode decision; redirect <code>localhost:51121/oauth-callback</code>,\nscopes add <code>cclog</code>/<code>experimentsandconfigs</code>; inference <code>cloudcode-pa</code>, needs GCP <code>project</code> field; one OAuth\nunlocks Claude+Gemini+GPT-OSS; agy ≠ Messages V1).</p>\n<p>* <strong>ToS-risk</strong> = relies on the vendor's official-client OAuth credentials + subscription quota from a\nthird-party application (openab-agent) rather than the vendor's own client — which may violate that vendor's\nTerms of Service.</p>\n<p><strong>Build decision (§9 Q3, Brett 2026-06-24):</strong> GO <code>gemini</code>/<code>grok</code> (first wave) and <code>agy</code> (experimental,\nopt-in, ToS caveat); No-Go <code>cursor</code>/<code>kiro</code>.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Auth-trigger UX (PR #1185)</h2>\n<p><code>/auth</code> is broker-side (<code>crates/openab-core/src/discord.rs</code>) — openab-agent advertises no slash commands;\nit exposes CLI subcommands the relay shells out to via <code>$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND</code>. The relay is\n<strong>poll-and-exit</strong>: print URL+code to stdout, poll the AS, exit 0.</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Anthropic has NO device flow</strong> (claude.ai = authorization_code only; RFC 8628 unshipped,\nanthropics/claude-code #22992) and #1187's <code>--no-browser</code> reads the code from <strong>stdin</strong>, which the relay\ncannot feed → undrivable by <code>/auth</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Resolution for interactive Claude self-service = two-step, code-as-CLI-arg:</strong> <code>/auth claude</code> persists\nthe PKCE verifier+state as a pending entry <strong>keyed by the initiating Discord user id</strong>\n(<code>pending:claude:&lt;discord_user_id&gt;</code>, reuse the existing <code>mcp-pending</code>/<code>AuthEntry::Pending</code> machinery) +\nprints the <code>code=true</code> URL (claude.ai shows a copyable code); <code>/auth claude &lt;code&gt;</code> forwards that same user\nid so <code>anthropic-oauth --code &lt;code&gt;</code> loads the matching verifier and completes. No stdin. <strong>Per-user\nkeying is required</strong> (Mira review, 2026-06-24): a single global pending entry lets a second concurrent\nuser's verifier overwrite the first's → PKCE mismatch on exchange, and worse, lets user B complete a flow\nuser A initiated (session hijack). (Fallback: broker pipes a follow-up DM/modal to child stdin — #1185 v2.)\nFor pods, the §5.3 env route avoids all of this.</li>\n<li><strong>Pending-entry GC</strong> (Mira review, 2026-06-24): stamp each <code>AuthEntry::Pending</code> with <code>created_at</code>;\n<code>with_auth_locked</code> opportunistically drops pending entries older than 15 min on every write, so abandoned\n<code>/auth</code> attempts (user never pastes a code) don't accumulate stale verifiers in <code>auth.json</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Rejected alternatives</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Per-vendor bespoke flows (status quo):</strong> rejected — N copies of PKCE/loopback/refresh; #1187 already\nduplicated the Codex flow. Doesn't scale to 5+ vendors.</li>\n<li><strong>Force everything through rmcp <code>CredentialStore</code>:</strong> rejected — lossy. <code>TokenStore</code> (provider) and rmcp\n<code>StoredCredentials</code> are different on-disk shapes (untagged <code>AuthEntry</code>); the translation drops fields\n(see <code>openab-agent-mcp.md</code> §6.1). The shared layer must sit <em>below</em> both (file RMW), not in one's trait.</li>\n<li><strong>Fully hand-rolled OAuth flow:</strong> rejected — it reimplements PKCE/CSRF/exchange/refresh that the official\n<code>oauth2</code> crate (already in-tree) provides. The crate is the chosen basis (§4 decision 2, §5.1); its one\nfriction — it defaults to RFC form-encoded token bodies while Anthropic needs JSON-no-scope — is handled\nvia the crate's custom http-client hook, not by abandoning it. (<code>oauth2</code> is stateless and does <strong>not</strong>\nsolve the auth.json race — that's the storage-layer's job, §5.4.)</li>\n<li><strong>In-process <code>Mutex</code> / tokio single-flight, or a sentinel lockfile (create→delete), for the race:</strong>\nrejected — see §5.4 (in-process locks are useless across the per-thread processes; a sentinel lockfile\ndeadlocks if a holder dies, whereas <code>flock(2)</code> auto-releases on death).</li>\n<li><strong>Device flow for Anthropic:</strong> not available (Anthropic ships no device endpoint). Hence the env route +\ntwo-step interactive (§7).</li>\n<li><strong>Layer-3 auto-trigger now:</strong> deferred — <code>/auth</code> manual is sufficient (Brett, 2026-06-24).</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Decisions &amp; open questions</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Default-model staleness — DECIDED (Brett 2026-06-24): no hardcoded default; require via config/env,\nfail-loud.</strong> Hardcoding <code>claude-opus-4-8</code> is a recurring 404 timebomb: this PR exists because the prior\ndated default 404'd on the subscription endpoint, and 4.6+ dateless IDs are <strong>fixed canonical IDs, not\nevergreen aliases</strong> — there is no floating &quot;-latest&quot; to lean on, and Messages V1 mandates a <code>model</code>.\nResolve model as ACP/CLI <code>model_override</code> → <code>OPENAB_AGENT_MODEL</code> → <strong>error</strong> (no hardcoded fallback);\ndrop the three duplicated default sites (<code>llm.rs:153</code>, <code>acp.rs:385/446</code>). Consequence: removes the\nzero-config default (deployments set model via values.yaml/env already; needs a clear error message +\nCHANGELOG note). Also eliminates the silent Opus cost bump for API-key users.\n<strong>Status — to be implemented in a follow-up PR.</strong> This PR lands the ADR + the §5.4 storage locking only;\nthe hardcoded default-model sites still exist in <code>llm.rs</code> / <code>acp.rs</code> and are intentionally untouched here\nto keep the locking change reviewable in isolation.</li>\n<li><strong>Bundled <code>client_secret</code> storage — DECIDED (Brett 2026-06-24): encode-at-rest default; env-injection\nalternative.</strong> Google Code-Assist vendors (gemini, agy) ship a <code>GOCSPX-…</code> desktop-app secret. By RFC 8252 and\nGoogle's own docs this value is <strong>non-confidential</strong> (installed-app secret, &quot;obviously not treated as a\nsecret&quot;) — there is no confidentiality to protect, so obscuring it adds zero cryptographic security. But it\nis <strong>not safe as raw text in a public repo for operational reasons</strong>: GitHub push-protection covers Google\nsecrets <strong>by default</strong> (changelog 2026-03), so a raw <code>GOCSPX-</code> literal blocks contributor <code>git push</code>, and\nGitHub↔Google partner token-scanning may <strong>auto-revoke</strong> the credential once it lands in a public commit.\nDecision: do <strong>not</strong> commit the raw literal —\n<ul>\n<li><strong>(a) encode-at-rest is the default</strong> (split/base64, decoded at runtime): keeps the bundled zero-config\nUX while dodging push-protection and partner auto-revoke. It is <strong>scanner-evasion for an already-public\nvalue, <em>not</em> a security control</strong> — label it as such inline so reviewers aren't misled into treating it\nas a real secret. Well-adopted pattern: <strong>rclone</strong> declares a <code>rcloneEncryptedClientSecret</code> constant and\ncalls <code>obscure.MustReveal()</code> at runtime for exactly this reason (bypass static scanners / partner\nauto-revoke, explicitly not encryption) — see §10.</li>\n<li><strong>(b) inject at runtime via env is the alternative</strong> (no secret in the repo at all): cleanest provenance,\nconsistent with the §5.3 env-route preference; preferred where a deployment already sets env (fleet/pod)\nand the bundled zero-config UX isn't needed.\nEmpirically the ecosystem overwhelmingly commits the literal plaintext (survey: 99/107 ≈ 93%; obscure 4,\nenv 1) and the shared secret is <strong>not</strong> being aggressively auto-revoked despite 100+ public copies — so the\nrisk we mitigate is mainly <strong>contributor push-protection friction on the <code>openabdev/openab</code> org repo</strong>, not\ncredential loss. Encode-at-rest buys that with zero UX cost, hence the default.\nagy secret requirement is now <strong>CONFIRMED</strong> (2026-06-24): agy <em>does</em> require a <code>GOCSPX-…</code> client_secret, a\npublic ecosystem constant (≥20 antigravity-auth repos hardcode it — §6); it ships encode-at-rest by default\nper this decision (or via env where (b) applies).</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Vendor go/no-go — DECIDED (Brett 2026-06-24).</strong>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>GO:</strong> <code>gemini</code>, <code>grok</code> (high value, clean APIs, low ToS risk) — first wave.</li>\n<li><strong>GO (experimental, opt-in):</strong> <code>agy</code>. Marginal eng cost is low — it shares gemini's Google Code-Assist\n<code>AntigravityProvider</code>, and one OAuth unlocks Claude+Gemini+GPT-OSS. Its one residual risk is <strong>ToS</strong>\n(drives Antigravity's official client + the user's subscription quota from a third-party app), which is\n<em>independent of</em> the now-solved secret-storage question and cannot be engineered away — so agy stays\nbehind an <strong>explicit opt-in flag with a documented ToS caveat</strong>, and the user accepts the risk on their\nown subscription. Watch for <code>429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED</code> (shared-quota exhaustion) and <code>cloudcode-pa</code>\nendpoint drift (semi-internal Google API; agy auto-updates). openab already runs agy in production via\nthe ECS <code>antigravity</code> variant, so the auth/quota behaviour is first-hand-known. <strong>Ecosystem evidence\n(GitHub survey 2026-06-24):</strong> agy OAuth is widely ported — ≥20 public repos hardcode the identical\nclient_id/secret (opencode/pi/hermes/openclaw plugins, standalone proxies) — so the integration is\nproven, <em>and</em> the same ecosystem is full of &quot;anti-ban&quot;, &quot;strict quota locking&quot; and &quot;multi-account\nrotation&quot; tooling, which empirically confirms the ToS-ban and <code>429</code> quota-exhaustion risks are real, not\ntheoretical — reinforcing the opt-in gate.</li>\n<li><strong>No-Go:</strong> <code>cursor</code> (reverse-engineered proprietary proxy + high ToS/account-ban risk), <code>kiro</code> (AWS Q\nevent-stream protocol — high maintenance cost). Revisit only on explicit demand.</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>MCP credential store must be revamped together — IN SCOPE (Brett 2026-06-24).</strong> The locked-RMW +\nper-tenant-lock invariant (§5.4) is <strong>not</strong> a provider-only change. <code>McpCredentialStore::save</code>/<code>clear</code>\n(<code>auth.rs:284-328</code>) is a co-equal unlocked RMW writer of <code>auth.json</code>, and the MCP pending-login finalize\npath writes it too. Introducing <code>with_auth_locked</code> therefore requires routing <strong>both</strong> the provider\n(<code>save_tokens</code>) and the MCP <code>CredentialStore</code> (+ pending finalize) through it — otherwise the lock is\nbypassed by half the writers and the race persists. Land them in the same change. (<code>McpCredentialStore</code>\nreuses the same <code>TokenStore</code>/<code>auth.json</code> storage that <code>openab-agent-mcp.md</code> §6.1 describes, so the lock\nlands once and serves both.) Connects to the pending OAuth-revamp follow-up flagged on the\n<code>feat/openab-agent-mcp-resilience</code> PR — itself driven by the rmcp/<code>reqwest</code> dependency-version conflict its\nOAuth adoption surfaced.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>10. References</h2>\n<h3>Internal</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>docs/adr/openab-agent.md</code> — agent charter (4 tools, no SDK, thin HTTP)</li>\n<li><code>docs/adr/openab-agent-mcp.md</code> — MCP client + §6 OAuth + §6.1 storage format</li>\n<li><code>docs/adr/pr-contribution-guidelines.md</code> — prior-art requirements</li>\n<li>PR #1187 (Anthropic OAuth), PR #1185 (<code>/auth</code>), PR #1111 (<code>--no-browser</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>External — projects</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Pi <code>earendil-works/pi</code> (ported flow; <code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code> #3591) · OpenClaw · Hermes Agent</li>\n<li>Gemini CLI <code>code_assist/oauth2.ts</code> · <code>NoeFabris/opencode-antigravity-auth</code> (+ <code>ANTIGRAVITY_API_SPEC.md</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Antigravity (agy) OAuth ecosystem</strong> (GitHub survey 2026-06-24, ≥20 repos hardcoding the same client_id/\nsecret) — <code>NoeFabris/opencode-antigravity-auth</code>, <code>router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI</code>, <code>andyvandaric/opencode-ag-auth</code>\n(quota-locking/anti-ban), <code>Meapri/hermes-google-antigravity-plugin</code>, <code>wbbtmusic/openclaw-antigravity-oauth</code>;\nevidence the integration is proven and that ToS-ban/quota mitigations are a real ecosystem concern (§9 Q3)</li>\n<li>GitHub <code>copilot-cli</code> · Kiro CLI / <code>pi-provider-kiro</code> / <code>kiro-gateway</code> · xAI API / <code>pi-xai-oauth</code></li>\n<li>Xiaomi <code>MiMo-Code</code></li>\n<li><strong>rclone <code>rclone/rclone</code></strong> — <code>rcloneEncryptedClientSecret</code> constant + runtime <code>obscure.MustReveal()</code>: the\ncanonical real-world precedent for §9 Q2 encode-at-rest (scanner-evasion of a non-confidential bundled\nOAuth secret, explicitly not encryption).</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>External — specs</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>RFC 8628 (Device Authorization Grant) · OAuth 2.1 §10.4 (refresh-token rotation/reuse)</li>\n<li>anthropics/claude-code #22992 (device-flow request), #20215 (MCP device flow)</li>\n<li>GitHub secret-scanning — Google secrets push-protected by default (changelog 2026-03-31); Google\ngoogle-auth-library-nodejs #959 (desktop client secret is non-confidential)</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions.html\">Documenting Architecture Decisions — Nygard (2011)</a></li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: openab-agent — Multi-Vendor LLM-Provider OAuth & Credential Storage"
      }
