For behavior, read the source.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">// Per-message buffered payload — the bool snapshot for other_bot_present (§2.6)\n// rides on each message; the consumer reads batch.last()'s value at dispatch.\npub struct BufferedMessage {\n    pub prompt: String,\n    pub extra_blocks: Vec&lt;ContentBlock&gt;,\n    pub sender_json: String,\n    pub trigger_msg: MessageRef,\n    pub arrived_at: Instant,\n    pub sender_name: String,\n    pub estimated_tokens: usize,\n    pub other_bot_present: bool,\n}\n\n// Per-thread (or per-lane, see §4.1) consumer registry entry.\nstruct ThreadHandle {\n    tx: mpsc::Sender&lt;BufferedMessage&gt;,\n    _consumer: tokio::task::JoinHandle&lt;()&gt;,\n    generation: u64,                // race-safe eviction (§2.5); read/written under per_thread lock\n    channel_id: String,\n    adapter_kind: String,\n}\n\npub struct Dispatcher {\n    // std::sync::Mutex — critical section has no .await; tokio::Mutex buys nothing.\n    per_thread: std::sync::Mutex&lt;HashMap&lt;String, ThreadHandle&gt;&gt;,\n    target: Arc&lt;dyn DispatchTarget&gt;,\n    grouping: BatchGrouping,        // Thread (per-message / per-thread) or Lane (per-lane) (§4.1)\n    max_buffered_messages: usize,\n    max_batch_tokens: usize,\n    idle_timeout: Duration,         // per-mode (§6.10)\n}\n\nimpl Dispatcher {\n    pub async fn submit(\n        &amp;self,\n        thread_key: String,\n        thread_channel: ChannelRef,\n        adapter: Arc&lt;dyn ChatAdapter&gt;,\n        msg: BufferedMessage,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;(), DispatchError&gt; { /* ... §2.3 + §2.5 ... */ }\n\n    pub fn cancel_buffered_thread(&amp;self, platform: &amp;str, thread_id: &amp;str) -&gt; usize { /* ... §4.4 ... */ }\n\n    pub fn sweep_stale(&amp;self) -&gt; usize { /* ... §6.10; returns evicted count ... */ }\n\n    pub fn shutdown(&amp;self) { /* ... §6.8 ... */ }\n\n    fn key(&amp;self, platform: &amp;str, thread_id: &amp;str, sender_id: &amp;str) -&gt; String { /* ... §4.1 ... */ }\n}\n\nasync fn consumer_loop(\n    thread_key: String,\n    thread_channel: ChannelRef,\n    rx: mpsc::Receiver&lt;BufferedMessage&gt;,\n    target: Arc&lt;dyn DispatchTarget&gt;,\n    adapter: Arc&lt;dyn ChatAdapter&gt;,\n    max_batch: usize,\n    max_tokens: usize,\n    idle_timeout: Duration,         // tokio::time::timeout(idle_timeout, rx.recv()) for self-eviction (§6.10)\n) { /* loop { greedy_drain → bot_present = batch.last().other_bot_present → reactions → dispatch_batch } */ }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Notable shape choices</strong> (rationale is in the cross-referenced sections):</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>target: Arc&lt;dyn DispatchTarget&gt;</code> rather than <code>Arc&lt;Router&gt;</code> — keeps the dispatcher independent of the router's full surface and decouples test mocks (§2.3).</li>\n<li><code>adapter: Arc&lt;dyn ChatAdapter&gt;</code> is passed per-call to <code>submit</code> (not stored on <code>Dispatcher</code>) because Discord's adapter is constructed inside serenity's <code>ready</code> callback via <code>OnceLock</code>, after the dispatcher is built in <code>main.rs</code>.</li>\n<li><code>other_bot_present</code> is <em>not</em> a <code>Dispatcher</code> field, <em>not</em> an <code>Arc&lt;AtomicBool&gt;</code> mirror — see §2.6 for why.</li>\n<li><code>grouping: BatchGrouping</code> selects mpsc identity: <code>Thread</code> keys by <code>(platform, thread_id)</code>; <code>Lane</code> adds <code>sender_id</code>. <code>per-message</code> mode uses <code>Thread</code> with <code>max_buffered_messages = 1</code> (§4.1).</li>\n<li><code>idle_timeout</code> is per-mode: <code>PER_MESSAGE_CONSUMER_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 10s</code>, <code>DEFAULT_CONSUMER_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 300s</code> (§6.10).</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Version:</strong> 0.6</li>\n<li><strong>Changelog:</strong>\n<ul>\n<li>0.6 (2026-05-05): Round-4 corrections, two threads.\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Design contract change (matches <code>feature/turn-boundary-batching-v2</code> @ <code>e119abf</code>).</strong> §2.5 SendError handling rewritten to match the post-<code>afd6fff</code> design — proactive <code>consumer.is_finished()</code> check at submit head + transparent retry once on <code>SendError</code>; ❌ + ⚠️ + <code>Err(ConsumerDead)</code> only if the retry also fails. Motivated by the first-message-after-idle race; one-attempt bound preserves the no-spin-loop property. §6.11 staging smoke matrix split into Path A (transparent retry happy path, <code>PANIC_ONCE</code>) and Path B (failing-retry surfaces error, <code>PANIC_ALWAYS</code>). §4.4 Phase 1 plan + test list updated to the new contract.</li>\n<li><strong>Anchor audit (relative to declared base v0.8.2-beta.1 / <code>52052b8</code>).</strong> Pre-existing drift fixed in <code>adapter.rs</code> references that had been wrong since the SHA pin was set in v0.2: <code>:131-152</code> → <code>:156-172</code> (content_blocks build), <code>:138-143</code> → <code>:158-162</code> (transcript prepend, 7 sites), <code>:148-152</code> → <code>:165-169</code> (image append), <code>:154-161</code> → <code>:173-180</code> (per-thread keying), <code>:181</code> → <code>:254</code> (<code>pool.with_connection</code> call site — was pointing at the wrong call), <code>:240</code> → <code>:260</code> (<code>session_prompt</code> invocation). All <code>acp/connection.rs</code> / <code>acp/pool.rs</code> / <code>discord.rs</code> / <code>slack.rs</code> anchors verified correct vs <code>52052b8</code>. Anchor-pinning preamble (line 9) expanded to also pin the implementation cross-check SHA so readers can distinguish &quot;released-base anchor&quot; from &quot;design-validated-against&quot; SHAs.</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>0.5 (2026-05-05): Second-pass corrections after fact-check against PR #686 source. §2.6 rewritten — <code>other_bot_present</code> rides on <code>BufferedMessage</code> and is read from <code>batch.last()</code> at dispatch, not via an <code>Arc&lt;AtomicBool&gt;</code> mirror (the mirror was an earlier draft; the implementation chose the simpler snapshot path). §2.3 struct shapes and <code>submit</code> signature corrected to match. Anchor paths swept: <code>pool.rs</code> → <code>acp/pool.rs</code>, <code>connection.rs</code> → <code>acp/connection.rs</code> (modules live under <code>src/acp/</code> in v0.8.2-beta.1). Appendix A replaced with a signatures-only skeleton plus pointer to <code>src/dispatch.rs</code> — drops the ~200-line body sketch that had drifted from the implementation; rationale moved into a short shape-choices list.</li>\n<li>0.4 (2026-05-05): Sync ADR with PR #686 Phase 1 implementation. <code>message_processing_mode</code> becomes 3-valued (<code>per-message</code> / <code>per-thread</code> / <code>per-lane</code>) — legacy <code>&quot;batched&quot;</code> alias is rejected. <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> is now a standalone ContentBlock (delimiter), separate from the <code>{prompt}</code> block; <code>pack_arrival_event</code> layout becomes <code>[delimiter] → [Text extras] → [{prompt}, omitted if empty] → [non-Text extras]</code>. Per-mode consumer idle timeout (§6.10) — <code>PER_MESSAGE_CONSUMER_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 10s</code>, <code>DEFAULT_CONSUMER_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 300s</code>; <code>Dispatcher::sweep_stale</code> added to bound <code>per_thread</code> HashMap on one-shot threads. SendError manual staging smoke matrix added (§6.11). §6.7 reactions clarified as sequential, not parallel. Configuration table (§4.1) and Phase 1 plan (§4.4) rewritten for the 3-mode model.</li>\n<li>0.3 (2026-04-30): Merge all RFC source documents and issue #580 comments into single ADR. Additions: §2.3 <code>generation: u64</code> + <code>channel_id</code>/<code>adapter_kind</code> on <code>ThreadHandle</code>; §2.5 race-safe eviction detail and action chain (T1.1); §2.7 axis-1/axis-2 analysis and related issue inventory (T1.2); §3.4 three-way comparison table (packing-adr §4); §4.4 Slack/Gateway Phase 1 wiring and canonical adapter integration pattern (tier2-roundup §4); §4.5 adapter integration pattern; §5.3 Prior Art detailed comparison table with Hermes/OpenClaw source-level analysis (rfc-turn-boundary.md); §6.5 semantic neutrality prohibited transformations (packing-adr §8.1); §6.6 observability three-metric spec with acceptance test (T2.a / masami #1); §6.7 batch reaction UX Phase 1 (T2.h); §6.8 graceful shutdown design (T2.g); §6.9 Scenario D smoke matrix (masami #2); Appendix A reference implementation (rfc-turn-boundary.md Appendix A, updated for final design).</li>\n<li>0.2 (2026-04-29): Restructure per maintainer feedback — collapse to 6 decision-focused sections; T1.x dispositions become inline rationale, no longer chapter spine; add §5.1 mechanism alternatives (debounce / Hermes overwrite / mid-turn interrupt / topic detection / cross-thread keying / mutex-coalescing); strip RFC-process narrative; anchor pinning simplified to v0.8.2-beta.1 (<code>52052b8</code>) for all file:line refs.</li>\n<li>0.1 (2026-04-29): Initial proposed version. Folds RFC #580 mechanism, T1.1 / T1.2 / T1.3 resolutions, and the standalone packing ADR (PR #598) into a single document.</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/580\">RFC #580: Turn-boundary message batching</a> — kept as historical discussion record.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/580#issuecomment-4338125509\">Triage T1.1 / T1.2 standalone comment (#issuecomment-4338125509)</a> — SendError + last_active disposition.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/580#issuecomment-4329250043\">Triage T1.3 standalone comment (#issuecomment-4329250043)</a> — <code>other_bot_present</code> freshness.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/580#issuecomment-4325645814\">Triage T1.4 + B1 packing comment (#issuecomment-4325645814)</a> — reformed packing proposal.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/580#issuecomment-4329511044\">Triage T2.c / <code>/cancel-all</code> standalone comment (#issuecomment-4329511044)</a> — Phase 1 timing rationale.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/580\">RFC #580 Tier 2 round-up + masami acceptance criteria</a> — observability spec, Slack/Gateway integration, graceful shutdown, batch reaction UX, Scenario D smoke matrix.</li>\n<li>ADR: <a href=\"/openab/adr/multi-platform-adapters\">Multi-Platform Adapter Architecture</a> — defines the <code>SenderContext</code> record this ADR extends.</li>\n<li>ADR: <a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway\">Custom Gateway for Webhook-Based Platform Integration</a> — establishes the ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 UTC timestamp convention this ADR extends to <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> JSON.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/sync/struct.Mutex.html\">Tokio <code>Mutex</code> documentation</a> — basis for the not-strictly-FIFO ordering claim.</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions.html\">Documenting Architecture Decisions — Michael Nygard (2011)</a>.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Turn-Boundary Message Batching"
      }

      "slug": "adr/unified-binary",
      "html": "<h1>ADR: Separate Binaries with Opt-In Unified Build</h1>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted</li>\n<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-15</li>\n<li><strong>Author:</strong> @pahud</li>\n<li><strong>Amends:</strong> Deployment model from <a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway\">ADR: Custom Gateway</a> — outbound-only + gateway sidecar remains the default; unified mode is an opt-in alternative path.</li>\n<li><strong>Implementation:</strong> <a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/pull/1146\">PR #1146</a></li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Context &amp; Problem</h2>\n<p>Today, supporting webhook-based platforms (Telegram, LINE, Feishu, Google Chat, WeCom, Teams) requires running <strong>two processes</strong> — <code>openab</code> core and <code>openab-gateway</code> — wired together via WebSocket, often in the same pod with a shared volume for colocate-mode media passing.</p>\n<p>This creates operational friction:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Two containers</strong> in a single pod (or two separate services)</li>\n<li><strong>Shared volume</strong> required for media colocate mode</li>\n<li><strong>WebSocket wiring</strong> between core and gateway (auth token, reconnect logic)</li>\n<li><strong>Version matrix</strong> — gateway releases independently, version mismatches cause subtle bugs</li>\n<li><strong>Double serialization</strong> — every message is serialized to JSON, sent over WS, then deserialized</li>\n</ul>\n<p>For most users who just want &quot;Discord + Telegram in one bot&quot;, the two-process model is unnecessary complexity.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Decision</h2>\n<p>Restructure the project as a <strong>Cargo workspace</strong> that keeps the two-binary model by default (core + standalone gateway), while allowing users to compile everything into a <strong>single unified binary</strong> via a feature flag — requiring zero code changes, only <code>--features unified</code> or a Cargo config toggle.</p>\n<h3>Workspace Layout</h3>\n<pre><code>openab/\n├── Cargo.toml              (workspace root + binary crate)\n├── src/                    (core modules — Discord, Slack, ACP, Dispatcher,\n│                            SessionPool, ChatAdapter trait)\n├── crates/\n│   └── openab-gateway/     (webhook adapters: Telegram, LINE, Feishu,\n│                             Google Chat, WeCom, Teams — impl ChatAdapter)\n└── gateway/                (standalone gateway binary — kept for backward compat)\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Extracting <code>openab-core</code> as a separate library crate was considered but deferred\nto Phase 2 — it would require changing visibility on 30+ internal modules. The current\napproach keeps core in the root crate and only extracts gateway adapters.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Feature Flags (on the root binary crate)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[features]\n# Default: core adapters (Discord + Slack) + infrastructure.\ndefault = [&quot;discord&quot;, &quot;slack&quot;, &quot;secrets-aws&quot;, &quot;agentcore&quot;]\n\n# Opt-in: compile all gateway adapters into a single unified binary\nunified = [&quot;telegram&quot;, &quot;line&quot;, &quot;feishu&quot;, &quot;googlechat&quot;, &quot;wecom&quot;, &quot;teams&quot;]\n\n# Core adapters (directly in root crate)\ndiscord    = [&quot;dep:serenity&quot;]\nslack      = []\n\n# Infrastructure\nsecrets-aws = [&quot;dep:aws-sdk-secretsmanager&quot;, &quot;dep:aws-config&quot;]\nagentcore   = [&quot;dep:aws-config&quot;, &quot;dep:aws-sigv4&quot;, ...]\n\n# Gateway adapters (each pulls in the gateway crate as optional dep)\ntelegram   = [&quot;dep:openab-gateway&quot;, &quot;openab-gateway/telegram&quot;]\nline       = [&quot;dep:openab-gateway&quot;, &quot;openab-gateway/line&quot;]\nfeishu     = [&quot;dep:openab-gateway&quot;, &quot;openab-gateway/feishu&quot;]\ngooglechat = [&quot;dep:openab-gateway&quot;, &quot;openab-gateway/googlechat&quot;]\nwecom      = [&quot;dep:openab-gateway&quot;, &quot;openab-gateway/wecom&quot;]\nteams      = [&quot;dep:openab-gateway&quot;, &quot;openab-gateway/teams&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>The <code>dep:openab-gateway</code> syntax requires the gateway crate as an optional dependency:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[dependencies]\nopenab-gateway = { path = &quot;crates/openab-gateway&quot;, default-features = false, optional = true }\n</code></pre>\n<p>Users who want the unified single-binary experience:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cargo build --features unified   # all adapters in one binary\n</code></pre>\n<p>Or pick specific adapters:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cargo build --features telegram,line   # just these two added to core\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Runtime Activation</h3>\n<p>Adapters start <strong>only if their config section is present and has required fields</strong> (e.g., <code>bot_token</code>). Compiled-in but unconfigured adapters have zero runtime overhead.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Only Discord and Telegram start — others dormant\n[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\nallowed_channels = [&quot;123456789&quot;]\n\n[telegram]\nbot_token = &quot;${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Architecture — Before &amp; After</h2>\n<h3>Before (two-process model)</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────┐     ┌───────────────────────────────────┐\n│  openab core                │     │  openab-gateway (sidecar)         │\n│                             │     │                                   │\n│  Discord ──┐                │     │  Telegram ──┐                     │\n│  Slack ────┤► Dispatcher    │◄─WS─┤  LINE ──────┤► axum → GatewayEvent│\n│            │                │     │  Feishu ────┘                     │\n│  GatewayAdapter (WS client) │     │                                   │\n└─────────────────────────────┘     └───────────────────────────────────┘\n        shared volume for media colocate\n</code></pre>\n<h3>After — Default (two binaries, same as today but workspace-structured)</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────┐     ┌───────────────────────────────────┐\n│  openab core                │     │  openab-gateway                   │\n│                             │     │                                   │\n│  Discord ──┐                │     │  Telegram ──┐                     │\n│  Slack ────┤► Dispatcher    │◄─WS─┤  LINE ──────┤► axum → GatewayEvent│\n│            │                │     │  Feishu ────┘                     │\n│  GatewayAdapter (WS client) │     │                                   │\n└─────────────────────────────┘     └───────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>After — Opt-in Unified (<code>--features unified</code>)</h3>\n<pre><code>┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  openab (single binary)                                        │\n│                                                                │\n│  Discord ────┐                                                 │\n│  Slack ──────┤                                                 │\n│  Telegram ───┤► Dispatcher → SessionPool → ACP (child process) │\n│  LINE ───────┤                                                 │\n│  Feishu ─────┘                                                 │\n│                                                                │\n│  axum HTTP (:9090) — only starts if webhook adapters active    │\n└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Message Flow Change</h2>\n<pre><code>BEFORE:\n  Platform → HTTP → gateway/telegram.rs → serialize GatewayEvent\n    → WebSocket → core/gateway.rs → deserialize → Dispatcher.submit()\n\nAFTER:\n  Platform → HTTP → src/telegram.rs → Dispatcher.submit() (direct call)\n</code></pre>\n<p>Reply path is similarly direct — the adapter calls the platform API in its <code>ChatAdapter</code> impl without WS round-trip.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Published Artifacts</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Image</th>\n<th>Contents</th>\n<th>Use case</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>openab:latest</code></td>\n<td>Discord + Slack only (core)</td>\n<td>Default — lightweight, same as today</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>openab-gateway:latest</code></td>\n<td>Standalone gateway (all webhook adapters)</td>\n<td>Default companion for webhook platforms</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>openab:unified</code></td>\n<td>All adapters in single binary</td>\n<td>Simplified deployment for users who want one container</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Custom builds via feature flags:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cargo build --features unified             # all-in-one binary\ncargo build --features telegram,line       # core + specific adapters only\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Dockerfile Build Arg</h3>\n<p>The root Dockerfile supports both modes via <code>BUILD_MODE</code> and <code>FEATURES</code> args:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-dockerfile\">ARG BUILD_MODE=default\nARG FEATURES=&quot;&quot;\n\nFROM rust:1-bookworm AS builder\nARG BUILD_MODE\nARG FEATURES\n\nWORKDIR /build\nCOPY . .\n\nRUN if [ &quot;$BUILD_MODE&quot; = &quot;unified&quot; ]; then \\\n      cargo build --release --features unified; \\\n    elif [ -n &quot;$FEATURES&quot; ]; then \\\n      cargo build --release --no-default-features --features &quot;$FEATURES&quot;; \\\n    else \\\n      cargo build --release; \\\n    fi\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Build semantics differ between root and agent Dockerfiles:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Dockerfile</th>\n<th><code>FEATURES</code> behavior</th>\n<th>Rationale</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Root (<code>Dockerfile</code>)</td>\n<td><code>--no-default-features --features &quot;$FEATURES&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Explicit control — user specifies exactly which adapters</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent (<code>Dockerfile.&lt;agent&gt;</code>)</td>\n<td><code>--features &quot;$FEATURES&quot;</code> (additive)</td>\n<td>Adds adapters on top of defaults (Discord + Slack)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Root Dockerfile examples:\ndocker build -t openab:latest .                                    # default\ndocker build --build-arg BUILD_MODE=unified -t openab:unified .    # all adapters\ndocker build --build-arg FEATURES=telegram,line -t openab:custom . # ONLY these (no Discord/Slack)\n\n# Agent Dockerfile examples (additive — Discord + Slack always included):\ndocker build -f Dockerfile.claude --build-arg FEATURES=telegram -t openab-claude:tg .\n</code></pre>\n<p>For image tagging conventions (<code>stable/beta/latest/semver/pr&lt;N&gt;</code>), see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">docs/image-tags.md</a>.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Migration Path</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 1</strong></td>\n<td>Restructure into workspace. Keep two-binary default. Add <code>unified</code> feature flag. Ship <code>openab:unified</code> image for early adopters.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 2</strong></td>\n<td>Gather feedback from unified adopters. Improve single-binary DX (combined health endpoint, unified log format).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Phase 3</strong></td>\n<td>If community consensus shifts toward unified-by-default, flip the default in a future major release.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Backward Compatibility</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Default behavior is <strong>unchanged</strong> — existing two-binary deployments continue to work with no migration</li>\n<li>The <code>unified</code> feature is purely additive — opting in requires only a build flag or image swap</li>\n<li>No breaking change to config schema — <code>[gateway]</code> section continues to work for users who keep the two-binary model</li>\n<li>Platform-specific config sections (<code>[telegram]</code>, <code>[line]</code>, etc.) are <strong>unified-mode additions</strong> — they are only read when the corresponding adapter is compiled in via feature flags</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>7. Trade-offs</h2>\n<h3>Advantages (of this approach)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Zero disruption</strong> — default behavior unchanged; existing deployments need no migration</li>\n<li><strong>Opt-in simplicity</strong> — users who want a single binary get it with one flag (<code>--features unified</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Smaller default binary</strong> — <code>openab:latest</code> stays ~12MB without webhook adapter deps</li>\n<li><strong>Independent release cadence</strong> — gateway can still release independently by default</li>\n<li><strong>Progressive adoption</strong> — community can move to unified at their own pace</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Advantages (of unified mode, when opted in)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>One container, one config, one release</strong> — dramatically simpler deployment</li>\n<li><strong>Lower latency</strong> — no WS serialization hop</li>\n<li><strong>One log stream</strong> — easier debugging</li>\n<li><strong>No shared volume</strong> — media passed in-process</li>\n<li><strong>Smaller attack surface</strong> — no exposed WS port between containers</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Disadvantages</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Two images to maintain</strong> — CI must build both default and unified variants</li>\n<li><strong>Unified binary is larger</strong> — ~25MB vs ~12MB. Acceptable as opt-in.</li>\n<li><strong>Feature flag complexity</strong> — conditional compilation adds <code>#[cfg]</code> gates. Mitigated by clean workspace boundary (all gateway code lives in <code>openab-gateway</code> crate).</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>8. Core Changes Required</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Area</th>\n<th>Change</th>\n<th>Scope</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>main.rs</code></td>\n<td>Start axum server + register adapter routes</td>\n<td>~50 lines</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>config.rs</code></td>\n<td>Add <code>TelegramConfig</code>, <code>LineConfig</code>, etc.</td>\n<td>~100 lines (additive)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Cargo.toml</code></td>\n<td>Workspace restructure + feature flags</td>\n<td>Medium</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Adapter code</td>\n<td>Move from <code>gateway/src/adapters/</code> → <code>crates/openab-gateway/src/</code></td>\n<td>Mechanical move</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Per-adapter glue</td>\n<td>Replace WS broadcast with <code>Dispatcher.submit()</code></td>\n<td>~10 lines each</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Existing modules</td>\n<td><strong>Zero changes</strong> — ACP, pool, dispatcher, discord, slack untouched</td>\n<td>None</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>9. Rejected Alternatives</h2>\n<h3>A. Unified binary as default</h3>\n<p>Ship all adapters compiled in by default; users opt out for slim builds. Rejected — forces a larger binary and more deps on users who don't need webhook adapters, and deprecates the standalone gateway prematurely.</p>\n<h3>B. Compile-time only (no pre-built unified image)</h3>\n<p>Users must <code>docker build</code> themselves with desired features. Poor UX — rejected. We publish <code>openab:unified</code> as a pre-built image.</p>\n<h3>C. Merge all code into one crate</h3>\n<p>Couples platform-specific complexity (Feishu AES-CBC, WeCom XML) with clean core abstractions. Rejected in favor of workspace separation.</p>\n<h3>D. Keep current architecture, no workspace restructure</h3>\n<p>The workspace restructure is needed regardless — it enables feature flags, cleaner builds, and the opt-in unified path. Rejected.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "ADR: Separate Binaries with Opt-In Unified Build"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "agent-installable-tools",
      "html": "<h1>Agent-Installable Tools</h1>\n<h2>How to Install Extra Tools</h2>\n<p>You don't need to read this doc yourself. Just ask your agent:</p>\n<pre><code>per docs/* from OpenAB GitHub repo, how to install &lt;TOOL_NAME&gt; for my OAB agent\n</code></pre>\n<p>Your agent will query the relevant docs under <code>docs/</code>, find the recommended approach, and guide you through the entire installation — or just do it for you. That's it. One prompt, done.</p>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<pre><code>  Human                        Agent                         OpenAB Pod\n  ┌─────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐          ┌──────────────────────────┐\n  │                  │         │                  │          │  Container (read-only)   │\n  │ &quot;install glab   │────────►│ reads docs/*     │          │  ┌────────────────────┐  │\n  │  for my OAB     │         │ from OpenAB repo │          │  │ curl, gh, rg, tini │  │\n  │  agent&quot;         │         │                  │          │  │ (built-in, minimal)│  │\n  │                  │         │ finds install    │          │  └────────────────────┘  │\n  │                  │         │ steps for glab   │          │                          │\n  │                  │         │                  │          │  PVC (persistent ~/):    │\n  │                  │         │ executes:        │          │  ┌────────────────────┐  │\n  │                  │         │  curl ─► extract │─────────►│  │ ~/bin/             │  │\n  │                  │         │  ─► ~/bin/glab   │          │  │  ├── glab    ✅ new│  │\n  │                  │         │  ─► verify       │          │  │  ├── aws          │  │\n  │                  │         │                  │          │  │  ├── ssh          │  │\n  │  &quot;done! glab    │◄────────│ &quot;glab v1.46      │          │  │  ├── terraform    │  │\n  │   ready to use&quot; │         │  installed ✅&quot;    │          │  │  └── kubectl      │  │\n  │                  │         │                  │          │  │                    │  │\n  └─────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘          │  │ ~/.ssh/  ~/.config/│  │\n                                                            │  │ ~/.kiro/ ~/aws-cli/│  │\n                                                            │  └────────────────────┘  │\n                                                            └──────────────────────────┘\n\n  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n  │  Migration: move PVC to new node / cluster / cloud                         │\n  │                                                                            │\n  │  Old Cluster              PVC                    New Cluster               │\n  │  ┌──────────┐     ┌────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐                 │\n  │  │ Pod ──────┼────►│ ~/bin/         │────►│ New Pod      │                 │\n  │  │ (delete)  │     │ ~/.ssh/        │     │ (attach PVC) │                 │\n  │  └──────────┘     │ ~/.config/     │     │              │                 │\n  │                    │ ~/.kiro/       │     │ Everything   │                 │\n  │                    │ ~/aws-cli/     │     │ just works™  │                 │\n  │                    └────────────────┘     └──────────────┘                 │\n  │                                                                            │\n  │  Zero reinstallation. All tools, configs, keys, and agent memory persist. │\n  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Why This Pattern</h2>\n<p>OpenAB keeps its Docker image minimal — only the essentials ship in the Dockerfile. Everything else is installed <strong>at runtime by the agent</strong> into the home directory (<code>~/bin/</code>). This is a deliberate design choice:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Lean image, infinite extensibility</strong> — the Dockerfile never grows. Need AWS CLI today, Terraform tomorrow, glab next week? Same image, same pattern. No rebuild, no redeploy.</li>\n<li><strong>Doc-driven, AI-first</strong> — documentation is written for agents to consume. Humans just say what they need; the agent reads the docs and executes.</li>\n<li><strong>No gatekeeping</strong> — adding a new tool doesn't require a PR to the Dockerfile, a new Docker build, or a Helm upgrade. Any agent can install any tool at any time.</li>\n<li><strong>Full persistence on PVC</strong> — everything installed to <code>~/bin/</code> and <code>~/</code> lives on the Persistent Volume Claim. This means:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Pod restart</strong> — tools are still there</li>\n<li><strong>Helm upgrade</strong> — tools are still there</li>\n<li><strong>Migrate the PVC to a new node / new cluster</strong> — tools, configs, credentials, SSH keys — everything moves with it. Your agent's entire environment is portable.</li>\n<li><strong>Upgrade a tool</strong> — just re-run the install. The old binary is overwritten in place.</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>No Dockerfile sprawl</strong> — if we baked GitLab CLI into the image, we'd have no reason to reject AWS CLI, gcloud, azure CLI, wrangler, kubectl, terraform... The image would bloat endlessly. This pattern keeps the core small and lets each deployment customize itself.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>What Ships in the Image</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tool</th>\n<th>Why it's built-in</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>curl</code>, <code>unzip</code></td>\n<td>Bootstrap — needed to download everything else</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>gh</code> (GitHub CLI)</td>\n<td>Core workflow — OpenAB repos are on GitHub; agents push reviews and PRs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ripgrep</code></td>\n<td>Core workflow — fast code search inside the pod</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>procps</code>, <code>tini</code></td>\n<td>Runtime — healthcheck and process management</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>kiro-cli</code></td>\n<td>Core workflow — the coding agent runtime</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Everything else is <strong>agent-installable</strong>.</p>\n<h2>Common Tools</h2>\n<p>The following tools are commonly installed by agents. This doc does <strong>not</strong> hardcode install commands — they change over time. Instead, the agent should look up the <strong>official upstream install instructions</strong> and adapt them to the <a href=\"#constraints-for-agents\">constraints</a> below.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tool</th>\n<th>Upstream Install Docs</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>OpenSSH</strong> (<code>ssh</code>, <code>scp</code>, <code>ssh-keygen</code>)</td>\n<td><a href=\"https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/amd64/openssh-client/download\">packages.debian.org/bookworm/openssh-client</a> — use <code>.deb</code> extract pattern. Also see <a href=\"/openab/refarch/remote-ssh-debugging\">remote-ssh-debugging.md</a> for SSH key setup.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>AWS CLI v2</strong> (<code>aws</code>)</td>\n<td><a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/install-cliv2-linux.html\">docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/install-cliv2-linux.html</a></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>GitLab CLI</strong> (<code>glab</code>)</td>\n<td><a href=\"https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases\">gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases</a></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Cloudflare Wrangler</strong> (<code>wrangler</code>)</td>\n<td><a href=\"https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/install-and-update/\">developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/install-and-update</a></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Terraform</strong> (<code>terraform</code>)</td>\n<td><a href=\"https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/install\">developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/install</a></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>kubectl</strong></td>\n<td><a href=\"https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/install-kubectl-linux/\">kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/install-kubectl-linux</a></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This is not an exhaustive list. Any tool with a prebuilt Linux binary can be installed using this pattern.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Constraints for Agents</h2>\n<p>When installing any tool, the agent <strong>must</strong> follow these rules:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>No <code>sudo</code></strong> — the container has no root access and a read-only root filesystem</li>\n<li><strong>Install to <code>~/bin/</code></strong> (binaries) or <code>~/</code> (larger installs like <code>~/aws-cli/</code>) — never write to <code>/usr/</code>, <code>/opt/</code>, or other system paths</li>\n<li><strong>Detect architecture</strong> — the pod may be ARM64 (<code>aarch64</code>) or AMD64 (<code>x86_64</code>). Always check <code>uname -m</code> and download the correct binary.</li>\n<li><strong>Use <code>/tmp/</code> for scratch</strong> — download and extract in <code>/tmp/</code>, copy the final binary to <code>~/bin/</code>, then clean up <code>/tmp/</code></li>\n<li><strong>Verify after install</strong> — run <code>&lt;tool&gt; --version</code> or equivalent to confirm it works</li>\n<li><strong><code>export PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;</code></strong> — ensure <code>~/bin/</code> is in PATH before verification</li>\n<li><strong>Look up the latest version from upstream</strong> — do not hardcode version numbers; always fetch the latest stable release</li>\n</ol>\n<h3><code>.deb</code> Package Pattern (for tools without standalone binaries)</h3>\n<p>Some tools (like OpenSSH) are only distributed as <code>.deb</code> packages. Extract without <code>sudo</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">mkdir -p ~/bin /tmp/deb-extract\ncurl -fsSL -o /tmp/package.deb &quot;&lt;deb-url&gt;&quot;\ndpkg-deb -x /tmp/package.deb /tmp/deb-extract\ncp /tmp/deb-extract/usr/bin/&lt;binary&gt; ~/bin/\nchmod +x ~/bin/&lt;binary&gt;\nrm -rf /tmp/package.deb /tmp/deb-extract\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Persistence &amp; Portability</h2>\n<p>Everything under <code>~/</code> is mounted on a PVC — see the migration diagram above. Key directories that persist:</p>\n<pre><code>~/bin/           → all installed tool binaries\n~/.aws/          → AWS CLI config and credentials\n~/npm-global/    → npm-installed tools (wrangler, etc.)\n~/.ssh/          → SSH keys and config\n~/.config/       → tool configs (glab, wrangler, etc.)\n~/.kiro/         → agent steering docs and memory\n~/.openab/       → OpenAB runtime data (cronjobs, etc.)\n</code></pre>\n<p>The only time tools are lost is if the PVC itself is deleted.</p>\n<h2>Adding a New Tool Doc</h2>\n<p>If you're contributing a doc for a new tool (e.g., <code>docs/gitlab.md</code>, <code>docs/cloudflare.md</code>):</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Keep it short</strong> — provide the install commands with architecture detection and a verification step</li>\n<li><strong>Reference this doc</strong> — link back here for the general pattern and philosophy</li>\n<li><strong>Test the prompt</strong> — verify that asking your agent <em>&quot;per docs/your-tool.md from OpenAB repo, install X for me&quot;</em> actually works end-to-end</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Advanced: Sidecars and Init Containers</h2>\n<p>For use cases that go beyond installing CLI tools — such as running a network tunnel, a database sidecar, or pre-installing a deterministic toolset via init containers — see <a href=\"/openab/sidecar\">docs/sidecar.md</a>.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Agent-Installable Tools"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "agentcore",
      "html": "<h1>AgentCore Runtime Backend</h1>\n<p>Run your coding agent (Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, etc.) remotely on <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime.html\">Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime</a> instead of bundling it inside the OAB container.</p>\n<h2>Why</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No coding CLI in your OAB image</strong> — smaller, faster pulls, simpler upgrades</li>\n<li><strong>True isolation</strong> — each agent session runs in its own Firecracker microVM</li>\n<li><strong>Persistent workspace</strong> — <code>/mnt/workspace</code> survives across turns (14-day retention)</li>\n<li><strong>Background execution</strong> — agents survive pod restarts</li>\n<li><strong>Multi-agent routing</strong> — one OAB routes to N runtimes by config</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># config.toml\n[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n\n[agentcore]\nruntime_arn = &quot;arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:123456789012:runtime/my-kiro-agent&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>That's it. OAB auto-spawns the native AgentCore bridge.</p>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>An AgentCore Runtime</strong> with your coding agent deployed (see <a href=\"#deploying-a-kiro-runtime\">Deploying a Kiro Runtime</a> below)</li>\n<li><strong>AWS credentials</strong> on the OAB pod with <code>bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell</code> permission</li>\n<li><strong>Runtime deployed after June 5, 2026</strong> (interactive shells support required)</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>┌─ ECS / Kubernetes Pod ────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  openab (PID 1)                                               │\n│    └─ openab agentcore-bridge (child process)                 │\n│         ├─ stdin  ◄── JSON-RPC from OAB                       │\n│         ├─ stdout ──► JSON-RPC to OAB                         │\n│         └─ WebSocket ──► AgentCore (SigV4 signed)             │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n          │ InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell (wss://)\n          ▼\n┌─ AgentCore MicroVM ───────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  PTY shell (persistent per shellId)                           │\n│    └─ kiro-cli acp --trust-all-tools (long-lived)             │\n│         ├─ stdin  ◄── JSON-RPC (initialize, session/prompt)   │\n│         └─ stdout ──► JSON-RPC (responses, notifications)     │\n│                                                               │\n│  /mnt/agent (14-day persistent storage)                       │\n│    └─ .local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3 (OAuth)              │\n│  /tmp/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3 (local copy — SQLite locks work)  │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Config Reference</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agentcore]\nruntime_arn = &quot;arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:123456789012:runtime/my-agent&quot;  # required\nshell_command = &quot;kiro-cli acp --trust-all-tools&quot;  # default; any ACP agent\ncancel_strategy = &quot;stop&quot;       # &quot;stop&quot; (default) or &quot;noop&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>runtime_arn</code></td>\n<td>yes</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>AgentCore Runtime ARN (region is extracted from it)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>shell_command</code></td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td><code>kiro-cli acp --trust-all-tools</code></td>\n<td>ACP agent command to run in the PTY</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cancel_strategy</code></td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td><code>stop</code></td>\n<td>What to do on cancel: <code>stop</code> terminates the session, <code>noop</code> ignores</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>If you need full control, use <code>[agent]</code> directly:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;openab&quot;\nargs = [&quot;agentcore-bridge&quot;, &quot;--runtime-arn&quot;, &quot;arn:aws:...&quot;, &quot;--region&quot;, &quot;us-east-1&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Priority rules</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Explicit <code>[agent]</code> with <code>command = &quot;...&quot;</code> always wins — <code>[agentcore]</code> is ignored</li>\n<li><code>OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND</code> env var alone does NOT count as explicit — <code>[agentcore]</code> overrides it</li>\n<li>If neither <code>[agent].command</code> nor <code>[agentcore]</code> is set, falls back to <code>OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND</code> or <code>openab-agent</code></li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<p>Use <code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-agentcore</code> — a minimal image (~20MB) with only the OAB binary. No Python, no coding CLI bundled.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker pull ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-agentcore\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Deploying a Kiro Runtime</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> AWS does not currently offer a pre-built managed Kiro runtime. You build and deploy the container yourself. This applies to all coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) — AgentCore hosts your container, it doesn't provide one. This may change as AgentCore evolves.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>1. Build the container (arm64 required)</h3>\n<p>A ready-to-build Kiro runtime is at <code>agentcore/runtimes/kiro/</code>. Or build your own:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-dockerfile\">FROM public.ecr.aws/amazonlinux/amazonlinux:2023\nRUN dnf install -y git curl python3 python3-pip unzip &amp;&amp; dnf clean all\nRUN useradd -m -d /home/agent -u 1000 agent\n\n# Install kiro-cli\nUSER agent\nRUN curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install | bash\nUSER root\n\nRUN pip3 install boto3\nCOPY healthcheck.py /app/healthcheck.py\nCOPY run.sh /app/run.sh\nRUN chmod +x /app/run.sh\n\nENV PATH=&quot;/home/agent/.local/bin:${PATH}&quot;\nWORKDIR /app\nEXPOSE 8080\nUSER agent\nCMD [&quot;python3&quot;, &quot;/app/healthcheck.py&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Push to ECR and create the runtime</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Push image\naws ecr create-repository --repository-name agentcore-kiro --region us-east-1\ndocker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 -t &lt;ACCOUNT&gt;.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/agentcore-kiro:latest . --push\n\n# Create runtime\naws bedrock-agentcore-control create-agent-runtime \\\n  --agent-runtime-name kiro_agent \\\n  --agent-runtime-artifact '{&quot;containerConfiguration&quot;:{&quot;containerUri&quot;:&quot;&lt;ACCOUNT&gt;.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/agentcore-kiro:latest&quot;}}' \\\n  --role-arn &quot;arn:aws:iam::&lt;ACCOUNT&gt;:role/agentcore-execution-role&quot; \\\n  --network-configuration '{&quot;networkMode&quot;:&quot;PUBLIC&quot;}' \\\n  --protocol-configuration '{&quot;serverProtocol&quot;:&quot;HTTP&quot;}' \\\n  --region us-east-1\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Store API key in Token Vault</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">aws bedrock-agentcore-control create-workload-identity --name kiro-coding-agent --region us-east-1\naws bedrock-agentcore-control create-api-key-credential-provider \\\n  --name kiro-api-key --api-key &quot;$KIRO_API_KEY&quot; --region us-east-1\n</code></pre>\n<p>The runtime fetches the key at boot — no plaintext secrets in env vars or config.</p>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<pre><code>┌─────────┐       ┌─────────┐  ACP   ┌───────────────────┐  WebSocket  ┌─────────────────────┐\n│ Discord │──────▶│   OAB   │───────▶│ agentcore-bridge  │────────────▶│  AgentCore Runtime  │\n│  Slack  │       │         │ stdio  │  (Rust, in-tree)  │  (PTY/WS)  │  (Firecracker μVM)  │\n└─────────┘       └─────────┘        └───────────────────┘            │  ┌───────────────┐  │\n                                                                      │  │ kiro-cli acp  │  │\n                                                                      │  │ (long-lived)  │  │\n                                                                      │  └───────────────┘  │\n                                                                      └─────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<ol>\n<li>OAB spawns <code>openab agentcore-bridge</code> as a subprocess (ACP stdio protocol)</li>\n<li>Bridge opens a SigV4-signed WebSocket to AgentCore (<code>InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell</code>)</li>\n<li>Inside the persistent PTY shell, <code>kiro-cli acp --trust-all-tools</code> runs as a long-lived process</li>\n<li>JSON-RPC messages flow bidirectionally: OAB ↔ bridge ↔ WebSocket ↔ kiro-cli</li>\n<li>Same <code>shell_id</code> per thread ensures session continuity across messages</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Session Memory</h2>\n<p>Each Discord/Slack thread maps to a deterministic <code>runtimeSessionId</code>. AgentCore keeps the same microVM alive for 15 minutes (configurable up to 8 hours). The persistent filesystem means:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Kiro's conversation history survives across turns (via <code>--resume</code>)</li>\n<li>Git repos, node_modules, build caches all persist</li>\n<li>No re-clone on every message</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>IAM Policy</h2>\n<p>Minimum permissions for the OAB pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n  &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell&quot;],\n  &quot;Resource&quot;: [&quot;arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:&lt;ACCOUNT&gt;:runtime/*&quot;]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Comparison</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th></th>\n<th>Local ACP (default)</th>\n<th>AgentCore</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent location</td>\n<td>Same container</td>\n<td>Remote microVM</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Image size</td>\n<td>~500MB+</td>\n<td>~50MB (agentcore variant)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Session state</td>\n<td>In-memory (lost on restart)</td>\n<td>Persistent filesystem (14 days)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Parallelism</td>\n<td>Shared CPU</td>\n<td>Independent microVM per session</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cold start</td>\n<td>None</td>\n<td>~5-15s first invoke</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cost</td>\n<td>Always-on pod</td>\n<td>Pay per CPU-second</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "AgentCore"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "ai-install-upgrade",
      "html": "<h1>OpenAB Install &amp; Upgrade Guide</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>[AI Instruction]</strong> Follow this guide to install or upgrade an OpenAB Helm deployment. Execute each section in order. If any step fails, follow the ROLLBACK section. Do not skip the backup (for upgrades).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Goal</h2>\n<p>Enable an AI agent to fresh-install or upgrade OpenAB on Kubernetes. For upgrades: back up everything first, upgrade, validate, and automatically roll back if anything goes wrong.</p>\n<h2>How to Use</h2>\n<p>Tell your AI agent to follow this guide. Example prompts:</p>\n<pre><code># Fresh install with kiro on local k8s\nfresh install https://github.com/openabdev/openab v0.7.7 with kiro on my local k8s with all credentials in .env\n\n# Upgrade to latest stable\nupgrade to latest stable for my local openab k8s deployment per https://github.com/openabdev/openab/blob/main/docs/ai-install-upgrade.md\n\n# Upgrade to a specific version\nupgrade to v0.7.7 for my local openab k8s deployment per https://github.com/openabdev/openab/blob/main/docs/ai-install-upgrade.md\n\n# Upgrade to a beta\nupgrade to v0.7.7-beta.1 for my local openab k8s deployment per https://github.com/openabdev/openab/blob/main/docs/ai-install-upgrade.md\n\n# Rollback after a bad upgrade\nrollback openab per the upgrade SOP — the upgrade to v0.7.7 failed\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Flow</h2>\n<pre><code>  ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐\n  │  1. RESOLVE  │────►│  2. BACKUP  │────►│  3. UPGRADE │\n  │   versions   │     │   3 items   │     │ helm upgrade│\n  └─────────────┘     └──────┬──────┘     └──────┬──────┘\n                             │                    │\n                        fail │               ┌────┴────┐\n                             │             pass      fail\n                             │               │         │\n                             ▼               ▼         ▼\n                        ┌─────────┐    ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐\n                        │  ABORT  │    │6. CLEANUP│ │5. ROLLBACK│\n                        │         │    │  (ask    │ │          │\n                        └─────────┘    │  user)   │ │ uninstall│\n                                       └────┬─────┘ │ reinstall│\n                                            ▼       │ restore  │\n                                       ┌─────────┐  └──────────┘\n                                       │  DONE ✅ │\n                                       └─────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Invariant:</strong> At every point, the system is either running the current version, running the target version, or being restored to the current version. No data is lost.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Resolve Versions</h2>\n<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Determine current version, target version, and release name. If the user specifies a target (e.g. <code>0.7.7-beta.1</code>), use it. Otherwise resolve latest stable from the Helm repo.</p>\n<pre><code>  Helm Release          OCI / Helm Repo         User Override\n  ┌────────────┐       ┌────────────────┐      ┌────────────┐\n  │ CURRENT    │       │ LATEST STABLE  │      │ TARGET     │\n  │ = helm list│       │ = helm show    │  or  │ = user     │\n  │   chart ver│       │   chart version│      │   specified│\n  └─────┬──────┘       └───────┬────────┘      └─────┬──────┘\n        │                      │                      │\n        └──────────┬───────────┘──────────────────────┘\n                   ▼\n          CURRENT == TARGET? ──yes──► exit (nothing to do)\n                   │ no\n                   ▼\n            save to env file\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Success:</strong> <code>RELEASE</code>, <code>CURRENT</code>, and <code>TARGET</code> are resolved and saved.\n<strong>If same version:</strong> Exit — no upgrade needed.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Backup</h2>\n<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Capture everything needed to fully restore the current deployment.</p>\n<pre><code>  Current Cluster                           Local Disk\n  ┌──────────────┐    helm get values      ┌──────────────┐\n  │ Helm Release  │ ──────────────────►    │ values.yaml  │\n  ├──────────────┤    kubectl get secret   ├──────────────┤\n  │ K8s Secret    │ ──────────────────►    │ secret.yaml  │\n  ├──────────────┤    kubectl cp $HOME     ├──────────────┤\n  │ Pod /home/    │ ──────────────────►    │ home/        │\n  │    agent/     │                        │  (full snap) │\n  └──────────────┘                         └──────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Success:</strong> All 3 items exist and are non-empty.\n<strong>Failure:</strong> Do NOT proceed to upgrade.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Pod label selector:</strong> <code>app.kubernetes.io/instance=$RELEASE,app.kubernetes.io/component=kiro</code></p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Gateway config migration (one-time, if applicable):</strong> If you previously enabled a custom gateway by manually patching the ConfigMap (e.g. adding <code>[gateway]</code> to <code>config.toml</code> by hand), that block is not captured by <code>helm get values</code>. Before upgrading, copy the gateway settings into your <code>values.yaml</code> under <code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.gateway</code> and set <code>enabled: true</code> so they are preserved on every subsequent <code>helm upgrade</code>. See chart <code>values.yaml</code> for the field reference (<code>enabled</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>platform</code>, <code>token</code>, <code>botUsername</code>). After migrating, do not manually edit the ConfigMap again — manage gateway config through <code>values.yaml</code> only.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Usercron path migration (v0.8.2+):</strong> The usercron <code>cronjob.toml</code> path resolution changed from <code>$HOME/</code> to <code>$HOME/.openab/</code>. If you have an existing <code>cronjob.toml</code> in the agent's home directory, move it before upgrading:</p>\n<pre><code>mkdir -p $HOME/.openab\nmv $HOME/cronjob.toml $HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml\n</code></pre>\n<p>The scheduler will not pick up the file from the old location. Hot-reload (polling every 60s) will detect the file once it is in the correct path.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Upgrade</h2>\n<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Deploy the target version using the backed-up values.</p>\n<pre><code>  Local Disk                    Helm Repo                  Cluster\n  ┌──────────────┐             ┌──────────┐              ┌──────────┐\n  │ values.yaml  │──-f────────►│ helm     │──upgrade────►│ New Pod  │\n  └──────────────┘             │ upgrade  │              │ (TARGET) │\n                               │ --version│              └──────────┘\n                               │  $TARGET │\n                               └──────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Important:</strong> Use <code>-f values.yaml</code> (not <code>--reuse-values</code>) so new chart defaults are merged correctly.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Smoke Test</h2>\n<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Verify the upgraded deployment is healthy.</p>\n<pre><code>  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n  │                  SMOKE TEST                      │\n  │                                                  │\n  │  ✓ deployment rolled out successfully            │\n  │  ✓ pod is Ready                                  │\n  │  ✓ openab process alive (pgrep)                  │\n  │  ✓ no panic/fatal in logs                        │\n  │  ✓ &quot;bot connected&quot; in logs                       │\n  │  ✓ helm chart version matches TARGET             │\n  │  ✓ (if gateway enabled) no gateway disconnect    │\n  │    errors in logs; verify Cloudflare tunnel URL  │\n  │    is still reachable and update values.yaml if  │\n  │    the URL has rotated                           │\n  │  ✓ (if usercron enabled) cronjob.toml loaded     │\n  │    — check for &quot;loaded usercron jobs&quot; in logs;   │\n  │    if you see &quot;no cronjobs yet&quot; instead, verify  │\n  │    file is at $HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml         │\n  │                                                  │\n  │  ALL PASS ──► proceed to 6. CLEANUP            │\n  │  ANY FAIL ──► proceed to 5. ROLLBACK             │\n  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Rollback</h2>\n<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Restore the previous working state — uninstall, fresh install, restore data.</p>\n<pre><code>  Step ①  Uninstall failed deployment\n  ┌──────────┐\n  │ helm     │──► release gone\n  │ uninstall│──► chart PVCs are retained\n  └────┬─────┘\n       ▼\n  Step ②  Reinstall previous version\n  ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────────┐\n  │ helm     │◄───│ values.yaml  │\n  │ install  │    └──────────────┘\n  │ $CURRENT │──► new empty pod running\n  └────┬─────┘\n       ▼\n  Step ③  Restore data\n  ┌──────────────┐    kubectl cp     ┌──────────┐\n  │ backup/home/ │ ─────────────────►│ Pod $HOME│\n  ├──────────────┤    kubectl apply  ├──────────┤\n  │ secret.yaml  │ ─────────────────►│ K8s      │\n  └──────────────┘                   │ Secret   │\n                                     └────┬─────┘\n       ▼                                  │\n  Step ④  Restart + verify                │\n  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┘\n  │ rollout restart → wait Ready → pgrep openab\n  │\n  │ ✅ Rollback complete\n  └──────────────────────────────────────────────\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>PVC retention:</strong> OpenAB chart-created PVCs are kept on <code>helm uninstall</code> to protect auth/session data. Delete a retained PVC manually only when you intentionally want to discard that state. <code>persistence.existingClaim</code> PVCs are owned outside the chart and are never created or deleted by OpenAB.</p>\n<p><strong>Upgrade path:</strong> Existing installations will gain the <code>helm.sh/resource-policy: keep</code> annotation on their PVCs upon the next <code>helm upgrade</code>. This is an additive-only change — it does not alter runtime behavior and only takes effect on a subsequent <code>helm uninstall</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. Cleanup (post-upgrade)</h2>\n<p><strong>Goal:</strong> After a successful upgrade, evaluate old backups and let the user decide what to keep.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>[AI Instruction]</strong> This phase is advisory. List what you find and ask the user — do NOT auto-delete anything.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<pre><code>  Local Disk\n  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n  │  ~/openab-backups/                           │\n  │  ├── 0.7.5_20260401/  (1.2 GB)              │\n  │  ├── 0.7.6_20260415/  (1.4 GB)              │\n  │  └── 0.7.7_20260501/  (1.5 GB)  ◄── current │\n  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\n  Step ①  List all backup directories with size and date\n  Step ②  Show total disk usage\n  Step ③  Ask the user which backups to remove (if any)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>What to report:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Item</th>\n<th>Command</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Backup dirs</td>\n<td><code>du -sh ~/openab-backups/*/</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Total size</td>\n<td><code>du -sh ~/openab-backups/</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Then ask the user:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Which old backups to delete (if any)</li>\n<li>Whether to keep the most recent N backups as a policy going forward</li>\n<li>Recommend keeping at least the latest stable backup as a safety net</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Do NOT</strong> delete anything without explicit user confirmation.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Quick Reference</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Action</th>\n<th>Key info</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Release name</td>\n<td><code>helm list | grep openab</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Pod selector</td>\n<td><code>app.kubernetes.io/instance=$RELEASE,app.kubernetes.io/component=kiro</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Check logs</td>\n<td><code>kubectl logs deployment/${RELEASE}-kiro --tail=50</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Restart pod</td>\n<td><code>kubectl rollout restart deployment/${RELEASE}-kiro</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Auth kiro-cli</td>\n<td><code>kubectl exec -it deployment/${RELEASE}-kiro -- kiro-cli login --use-device-flow</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "OpenAB Install & Upgrade Guide"
      }
    },

      "slug": "ambient",
      "html": "<h1>Ambient Mode</h1>\n<p>Ambient mode allows your bot to passively listen to all messages in configured channels and autonomously decide whether to respond. Unlike the default @mention mode, the bot observes the full conversation flow and only speaks up when it has something valuable to add.</p>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Messages in configured channels (that are <strong>not</strong> @mentions) are buffered per-channel.</li>\n<li>When a <strong>time trigger</strong> (<code>flush_interval_seconds</code>) or <strong>count trigger</strong> (<code>flush_max_messages</code>) fires, the batch is sent to the LLM.</li>\n<li>The LLM evaluates the conversation and either:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Replies</strong> with a helpful response → posted to the channel.</li>\n<li><strong>Returns <code>[NO_REPLY]</code></strong> → silently suppressed, nothing is posted.</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>If someone <strong>@mentions</strong> the bot in an ambient channel, the buffer is discarded and the mention is handled normally (immediate response).</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[ambient]\nenabled = true\nflush_interval_seconds = 60      # Time trigger (±20% jitter applied)\nflush_max_messages = 10           # Count trigger\nflush_hard_cap = 50               # Safety cap on buffer size\nmax_concurrent_flushes = 3        # Global LLM concurrency limit\nflush_timeout_seconds = 120       # Safety timeout per flush\ninstructions_file = &quot;~/.openab/config/ambient.md&quot;  # Custom system prompt (optional)\ndebug = false                     # ⚠️ Only enable in test channels (exposes prompt + messages)\n\n[ambient.discord]\nchannels = [&quot;1234567890&quot;]         # Channel IDs to monitor (and their threads)\nallow_bot_messages = true         # Include other bots' messages in buffer (default)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Custom Instructions</h3>\n<p>The <code>instructions_file</code> field points to a Markdown file whose content is used as the ambient system prompt. This works like a user-defined <code>.cursorrules</code> or <code>CLAUDE.md</code> — you control how the bot behaves in ambient mode by editing one file.</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Default path:</strong> <code>~/.openab/config/ambient.md</code></li>\n<li><strong>Max length:</strong> First 2000 characters are used; content beyond that is truncated.</li>\n<li><strong>Fallback:</strong> If the file does not exist, the built-in default instructions are used.</li>\n<li><strong>Restart required:</strong> The file is read once at startup. To apply changes, restart the bot.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Example <code>~/.openab/config/ambient.md</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-markdown\">You are passively observing a Discord channel.\n\n- Reply EXACTLY `[NO_REPLY]` if you have nothing to add\n- Only speak up for technical corrections or when directly asked\n- Keep replies concise\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Configuration fields</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>enabled</code></td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Master switch. Must be explicitly enabled.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>debug</code></td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>When true, posts system prompt + transcript to channel on each flush and lets <code>[NO_REPLY]</code> responses through (not suppressed). ⚠️ <strong>Only use in private/test channels</strong> — exposes system prompt and buffered messages.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>flush_interval_seconds</code></td>\n<td><code>60</code></td>\n<td>Seconds between time-based flushes. ±20% jitter prevents thundering herd. Min: 1.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>flush_max_messages</code></td>\n<td><code>10</code></td>\n<td>Flush when this many messages accumulate. Min: 1.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>flush_hard_cap</code></td>\n<td><code>50</code></td>\n<td>Maximum buffer size. Messages beyond this are dropped. Min: 1.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_concurrent_flushes</code></td>\n<td><code>3</code></td>\n<td>Max simultaneous LLM calls across all ambient channels. Min: 1.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>flush_timeout_seconds</code></td>\n<td><code>120</code></td>\n<td>Safety timeout — resets flushing state if exceeded. Clamped to [5, 600].</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>instructions_file</code></td>\n<td><code>~/.openab/config/ambient.md</code></td>\n<td>Path to custom instructions file. First 2000 chars used as system prompt. Falls back to built-in default if missing.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>channels</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Explicit channel allowlist (required). Empty = ambient disabled.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_bot_messages</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Whether other bots' messages enter the ambient buffer.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Threads are observed by default.</strong> Messages in <strong>threads</strong> whose parent is a configured channel are buffered too (most OpenAB conversation happens in auto-created threads, not the parent channel). <strong>Both</strong> bot-owned and non-owned threads are observed — the bot passively follows all thread conversation under an ambient channel. An @mention in any thread discards its buffer and triggers immediate dispatch, so there is no double-reply. Each thread batches independently (keyed by the thread ID).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong><code>[ambient.discord].channels</code> vs <code>[discord].allowed_channels</code></strong> — these are independent allowlists with an OR relationship:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Config</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Effect</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[discord].allowed_channels</code></td>\n<td>Normal dispatch</td>\n<td>Bot responds to @mentions and direct messages in these channels/threads</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[ambient.discord].channels</code></td>\n<td>Passive observation</td>\n<td>Bot silently buffers messages (no @mention required) and decides whether to reply</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>A channel can appear in one or both. Ambient observation does <strong>not</strong> require the channel to also be in <code>allowed_channels</code>.</p>\n<p><strong>@mention always works in ambient channels.</strong> Even if a channel is only in <code>[ambient.discord].channels</code> (not in <code>allowed_channels</code>), an @mention still triggers immediate normal dispatch — the ambient buffer is discarded and the bot responds directly. The only difference between the two configs is behavior <strong>without</strong> a mention: <code>allowed_channels</code> ignores unmentioned messages entirely, while <code>ambient.discord.channels</code> passively observes them.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Reserved fields (v2, not yet enforced)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>context_window</code></td>\n<td><code>20</code></td>\n<td>Historical messages to fetch before each batch (not yet implemented).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pool.max_sessions</code></td>\n<td><code>5</code></td>\n<td>Max concurrent ambient sessions (not yet enforced).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pool.session_ttl_minutes</code></td>\n<td><code>60</code></td>\n<td>Session inactivity timeout (not yet enforced).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pool.context_flushes</code></td>\n<td><code>3</code></td>\n<td>Rolling flush history window (not yet enforced).</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Behavior</h2>\n<h3>@mention priority</h3>\n<p>When someone @mentions the bot in an ambient channel:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>The ambient buffer is immediately invalidated (current batch discarded).</li>\n<li>The mention is handled via normal dispatch (immediate response).</li>\n<li>After the mention is handled, ambient buffering resumes for new messages.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Buffered messages that arrived before the mention are <strong>not lost</strong> — they carry into the next ambient cycle.</p>\n<h3>[NO_REPLY] filtering</h3>\n<p>The bot uses a system prompt that instructs it to respond with <code>[NO_REPLY]</code> when it has nothing to add. This sentinel is intercepted <strong>before delivery</strong> — it never appears in the channel. The filtering uses a capture adapter that forces non-streaming mode to ensure the full response is evaluated before any message is sent.</p>\n<h3>Session isolation</h3>\n<p>Ambient sessions use the namespace <code>ambient:discord:&lt;channel_id&gt;</code>, separate from normal dispatch sessions. There is no collision with @mention sessions.</p>\n<h3>Cost control</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Jittered intervals</strong> prevent all channels from flushing simultaneously.</li>\n<li><strong>Global semaphore</strong> caps concurrent LLM calls (default: 3).</li>\n<li><strong><code>[NO_REPLY]</code></strong> means most flushes produce no visible output (only one LLM call, no channel message).</li>\n<li><strong><code>enabled = false</code></strong> default means zero cost until explicitly opted in.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Limitations (v1)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Limitation</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Planned fix</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Tool access</td>\n<td>Ambient flushes have full tool access (same as @mention).</td>\n<td>v2: restricted dispatch target</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>In-flight cancel</td>\n<td>A @mention during LLM generation cannot stop the ambient response mid-stream.</td>\n<td>v2: <code>tokio::select!</code> preemption</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Consumer supervision</td>\n<td>If a consumer task panics, that channel's ambient is permanently disabled until restart.</td>\n<td>v2: health check + respawn</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>No history fetch</td>\n<td><code>context_window</code> (Discord API history before batch) is not yet implemented.</td>\n<td>v2</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>No cooldown</td>\n<td>No minimum interval between consecutive flushes for a single channel.</td>\n<td>v2</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Example</h2>\n<p>Minimal config to enable ambient mode on one channel:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[ambient]\nenabled = true\n\n[ambient.discord]\nchannels = [&quot;1490282656913559673&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>This uses all defaults: 60s flush interval, max 10 messages per batch, 3 concurrent flushes.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Ambient Mode"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "antigravity",
      "html": "<h1>Google Antigravity CLI (agy)</h1>\n<p>OpenAB supports <a href=\"https://antigravity.google/\">Google Antigravity CLI</a> via the <code>agy-acp</code> adapter — a thin Rust binary that translates ACP JSON-RPC into <code>agy -p</code> invocations.</p>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<pre><code>openab ──ACP JSON-RPC──► agy-acp ──spawns──► agy --add-dir /home/agent -p &quot;prompt&quot;\n                                              agy --add-dir /home/agent --conversation &lt;ID&gt; -p &quot;follow-up&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>First prompt in a session: <code>agy -p &quot;text&quot;</code>, then discovers the conversation ID</li>\n<li>Subsequent prompts: <code>agy --conversation &lt;ID&gt; -p &quot;text&quot;</code> (resumes specific conversation)</li>\n<li>Only the <strong>delta</strong> (new response) is sent back — previous turns are not repeated</li>\n<li>Full <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> metadata is passed through to agy</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;agy-acp&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Environment Variables</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AGY_WORKING_DIR</code></td>\n<td>Working directory for agy invocations</td>\n<td><code>/tmp</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AGY_EXTRA_ARGS</code></td>\n<td>Extra arguments prepended to every <code>agy</code> invocation (optional)</td>\n<td>(none)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_TOOL_DISPLAY</code></td>\n<td>Controls filtering of intermediate thinking narration (&quot;I will...&quot;). <code>full</code> or unset keeps all output; <code>compact</code>/<code>none</code>/<code>off</code> drops leading narration-only parts.</td>\n<td><code>full</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Steering Files</h2>\n<p>agy reads <code>AGENTS.md</code> and <code>GEMINI.md</code> when it considers a directory a workspace:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>AGENTS.md</code> and <code>GEMINI.md</code> are loaded first and injected into the system prompt</li>\n<li>agy does not disclose how it determines HOME as a workspace, but <code>--add-dir</code> explicitly adds a directory</li>\n<li>agy-acp <strong>automatically</strong> passes <code>--add-dir &lt;working_dir&gt;</code> on every invocation — no configuration needed</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Place your steering instructions in <code>/home/agent/AGENTS.md</code> or <code>/home/agent/GEMINI.md</code> — they will be read on every prompt as long as <code>working_dir</code> points to that directory.</p>\n<h2>Docker</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.antigravity -t openab-antigravity .\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Antigravity CLI uses Google Sign-In (OAuth). Authenticate inside the container:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-antigravity -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Complete the device flow in your browser. Auth tokens persist in the PVC at <code>~/.gemini/</code>.</p>\n<h2>Helm</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  antigravity:\n    discord:\n      botToken: &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n      allowedChannels: [&quot;123456789&quot;]\n    agent:\n      command: &quot;agy-acp&quot;\n      args: []\n      workingDir: &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n    # image: leave empty — chart auto-resolves to openab:&lt;tag&gt;-antigravity\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No streaming</strong>: <code>agy -p</code> returns the full response at once; the adapter sends it as a single <code>agent_message_chunk</code> notification.</li>\n<li><strong>Cancel is a no-op</strong>: <code>agy -p</code> runs to completion; <code>session/cancel</code> acknowledges but cannot interrupt.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Antigravity"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "claude-code",
      "html": "<h1>Claude Code</h1>\n<p>Claude Code uses the <a href=\"https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp\">@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp</a> adapter for ACP support.</p>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.claude -t openab-claude:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<p>The image installs <code>@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp</code> and <code>@anthropic-ai/claude-code</code> globally via npm.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.claude.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.claude.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.claude.command=claude-agent-acp \\\n  --set agents.claude.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Set <code>agents.kiro.enabled=false</code> to disable the default Kiro agent.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-claude</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-claude</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-claude</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-claude</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.claude.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-claude\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Manual config.toml</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;claude&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Sign in interactively using the OAuth device flow. Credentials are stored on disk (persisted via PVC across pod restarts):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-claude -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>After authenticating, restart the pod so the bot process loads the new credentials:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-claude\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> <code>claude setup-token</code> is a different command — it generates a long-lived token for CI/scripts and prints it without saving locally. For container-based deployments, <code>claude auth login</code> is the correct approach as it persists credentials to the filesystem.</p>\n</blockquote>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Claude Code"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "codex",
      "html": "<h1>Codex</h1>\n<p>Codex uses the <a href=\"https://github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp\">@zed-industries/codex-acp</a> adapter for ACP support.\nThe recommended working directory for the Codex image is <code>/home/node</code>; this is\nalso the container <code>HOME</code>, so Codex auth, sessions, generated images, and skills\nlive under <code>/home/node/.codex/</code>.</p>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.codex -t openab-codex:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<p>The image installs <code>@zed-industries/codex-acp</code> and <code>@openai/codex</code> globally via npm.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.codex.discord.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.codex.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot;
