\\\n  --set-string 'agents.codex.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.codex.command=codex-acp \\\n  --set agents.codex.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Set <code>agents.kiro.enabled=false</code> to disable the default Kiro agent.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-codex</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-codex</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-codex</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-codex</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.codex.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-codex\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Manual config.toml</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;codex&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-codex -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Follow the device code flow in your browser, then restart the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-codex\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Persisted Paths (PVC)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Path</th>\n<th>Contents</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/home/node/.codex/auth.json</code></td>\n<td>Codex login credentials</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/home/node/.codex/config.toml</code></td>\n<td>Codex CLI settings and feature flags</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/home/node/.codex/sessions/</code></td>\n<td>Session history</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/home/node/.codex/generated_images/</code></td>\n<td>Built-in image generation outputs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/home/node/.codex/skills/</code></td>\n<td>User-created Codex skills</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Image Generation</h2>\n<p>Codex built-in image generation uses the <strong><code>gpt-image-2</code></strong> model under the hood.\nIt is controlled by the Codex CLI feature flag <code>image_generation</code>. Enable it\nonce inside the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-codex -- \\\n  codex features enable image_generation\n</code></pre>\n<p>This writes the following to <code>/home/node/.codex/config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[features]\nimage_generation = true\n</code></pre>\n<p>You can verify it with:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-codex -- \\\n  codex features list | grep image_generation\n</code></pre>\n<p>Generated images are saved by Codex under\n<code>/home/node/.codex/generated_images/...</code>. If the user needs a stable path, ask\nCodex to copy the selected output into <code>/home/node</code>, for example\n<code>/home/node/sky-birds.png</code>.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Note: Codex image generation may return a model-native size rather than the\nexact dimensions requested in the prompt. If exact dimensions matter, resize\nonly when the user explicitly asks for it.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Quick Imagegen Smoke Test</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-codex -- \\\n  codex exec \\\n    --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox \\\n    --enable image_generation \\\n    --skip-git-repo-check \\\n    -C /home/node \\\n    &quot;Use the imagegen skill and the built-in image_gen tool. Generate a simple image of birds flying across a bright sky. Save or copy the final PNG to /home/node/sky-birds.png. Report the output path and dimensions.&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then check for output:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-codex -- \\\n  sh -lc 'ls -lh /home/node/sky-birds.png /home/node/.codex/generated_images/*/* 2&gt;/dev/null | tail'\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Sending Generated Images Back to Discord</h2>\n<p>OpenAB streams text over ACP only. It does <strong>not</strong> relay image attachments from\nCodex back to Discord. To send a generated image, Codex must call the Discord\nREST API directly. See <a href=\"/openab/sendimages\">sendimages.md</a> for the full protocol.</p>\n<p>The agent should:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Read <code>thread_id</code> from OpenAB's <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> and use it as the Discord\ntarget channel. If <code>thread_id</code> is absent, fall back to <code>channel_id</code>.</li>\n<li>Upload the file with <code>POST /channels/{id}/messages</code> using multipart form\ndata.</li>\n<li>Read the token from <code>DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN</code> if available, otherwise\n<code>DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code>.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Example upload from inside the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">THREAD_ID=&quot;1499442140172910654&quot;\nIMAGE=&quot;/home/node/sky-birds.png&quot;\n\ncurl -X POST &quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/${THREAD_ID}/messages&quot; \\\n  -H &quot;Authorization: Bot ${DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN:-$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;content=Here is the generated image&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;files[0]=@${IMAGE}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Agent Environment for Uploads</h3>\n<p>The Discord bot token configured under <code>[discord]</code> is consumed by OpenAB itself.\nFor safety, OpenAB clears the inherited environment before spawning the agent and\nonly passes variables listed in <code>[agent].env</code>. If Codex should upload images\nitself, explicitly expose an upload token to the agent:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;codex&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\nenv = { DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN = &quot;${DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p>For production, prefer a dedicated &quot;File Deliverer&quot; Discord bot with only\n<code>Send Messages</code>, <code>Send Messages in Threads</code>, and <code>Attach Files</code> permissions.\nFor small personal deployments, using the same bot token is simpler but gives\nthe agent the same Discord permissions as the main OpenAB bot.</p>\n<h2>Recommended Skill</h2>\n<p>For repeated image requests, save the imagegen + Discord upload workflow as a\nCodex skill under <code>/home/node/.codex/skills/</code>, for example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">/home/node/.codex/skills/discord-imagegen-deliver/\n+-- SKILL.md\n`-- scripts/\n    `-- send-discord-image.sh\n</code></pre>\n<p>The skill should instruct Codex to:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Use the built-in <code>imagegen</code> skill and <code>image_gen</code> tool for raster images.</li>\n<li>Keep the generated image size as-is unless the user explicitly asks for\nresizing.</li>\n<li>Copy the selected file from <code>/home/node/.codex/generated_images/...</code> to a\nstable path under <code>/home/node</code>.</li>\n<li>Upload it to <code>thread_id</code> or <code>channel_id</code> using the Discord REST API.</li>\n<li>Avoid printing token values.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Example user prompt after creating such a skill:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">Use $discord-imagegen-deliver to generate a warm hand-painted sky with birds and send it back to this Discord thread.\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Approval Policy &amp; Auto-review</h2>\n<p>Codex separates <strong>when</strong> to ask for approval (<code>approval_policy</code>) from <strong>who</strong>\nreviews the request (<code>approvals_reviewer</code>):</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Valid values</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>approval_policy</code></td>\n<td><code>untrusted</code>, <code>on-failure</code> (deprecated), <code>on-request</code>, <code>granular</code>, <code>never</code></td>\n<td>When Codex must request approval before acting</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>approvals_reviewer</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;user&quot;</code> (default), <code>&quot;auto_review&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Who handles the approval — human or GPT-5.4 Thinking reviewer</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>For OpenAB deployments, <strong>Auto-review is the recommended mode</strong>. OpenAB agents\nrun as long-lived background processes with no human watching the terminal, so\nmanual approval is impractical and <code>&quot;never&quot;</code> removes all guardrails.</p>\n<p>Enable Auto-review in <code>/home/node/.codex/config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Full recommended config for OpenAB agents\nsandbox_mode = &quot;danger-full-access&quot;\napproval_policy = &quot;on-request&quot;\napprovals_reviewer = &quot;auto_review&quot;\n\n[features]\nimage_generation = true\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><code>sandbox_mode</code>, <code>approval_policy</code>, and <code>approvals_reviewer</code> are <strong>top-level</strong>\nkeys in <code>config.toml</code>, not under a <code>[sandbox]</code> section. Codex silently ignores\nthem if nested.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Or seed the config into the running pod's PVC with <code>kubectl cp</code> (writable,\npersists across restarts):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl cp config.toml &lt;pod-name&gt;:/home/node/.codex/config.toml\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-codex\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Do not mount a ConfigMap directly to <code>/home/node/.codex/config.toml</code>.</strong>\nConfigMap mounts are read-only — Codex cannot write back to them (e.g.\n<code>codex features enable</code> will fail with permission denied). Always use\n<code>kubectl cp</code> to seed config onto the PVC, which remains writable at runtime.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>What Auto-review does</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Approves ~99% of legitimate out-of-sandbox actions automatically.</li>\n<li>Blocks actions that could exfiltrate data, expose secrets, delete data, or\nweaken security settings.</li>\n<li>When it rejects an action, it gives the agent a rationale so Codex can find a\nsafer alternative (succeeds &gt;50% of the time without human input).</li>\n<li>Stops the trajectory after repeated denials to prevent gaming.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Limitations</h3>\n<p>Auto-review is <strong>not</strong> a security guarantee. It can be misled by adversarial\ninputs and cannot detect a model that hides malicious intent within the sandbox.\nTreat it as a strong default, not a replacement for network-level controls and\nsecret management.</p>\n<p>For more details, see the <a href=\"https://alignment.openai.com/auto-review\">OpenAI Alignment Blog post on Auto-review</a>.</p>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3><code>bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace</code></h3>\n<p>Some Kubernetes environments do not allow unprivileged user namespaces, which can\nblock Codex's default sandbox when running nested <code>codex exec</code> commands. For\nmanual smoke tests inside an already isolated pod, use:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox ...\n</code></pre>\n<p>Do not use this flag on an untrusted host.</p>\n<h3><code>bubblewrap is unavailable: no system bwrap was found on PATH</code></h3>\n<p>Codex's Linux sandbox modes (read-only / workspace-write) rely on <code>bwrap</code>\n(bubblewrap) to create an inner sandbox. If the runtime image does not include\nbubblewrap, even basic commands like <code>pwd</code> or <code>ls</code> will fail before execution\nwith this error.</p>\n<p>This commonly happens in OpenAB deployments where Codex already runs inside an\nisolated container or VM — the outer runtime provides the desired isolation, so\nthe inner sandbox is redundant.</p>\n<p><strong>Solution — Disable Codex's inner sandbox</strong> (recommended when the outer OpenAB\nruntime already provides isolation):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># /home/node/.codex/config.toml\nsandbox_mode = &quot;danger-full-access&quot;\napproval_policy = &quot;on-request&quot;\napprovals_reviewer = &quot;auto_review&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><code>sandbox_mode</code>, <code>approval_policy</code>, and <code>approvals_reviewer</code> are <strong>top-level</strong>\nkeys in <code>config.toml</code>. A <code>[sandbox]</code> section header is silently ignored by\nCodex 0.137+ — verified empirically: with the nested form in place, <code>codex exec</code> still fails with <code>bwrap: No permissions to create new namespace</code>; moving\nthe same keys to the top level makes <code>codex exec</code> report\n<code>sandbox: danger-full-access</code> and run.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Do NOT pair <code>danger-full-access</code> with <code>approval_policy = &quot;on-request&quot;</code> and\n<code>approvals_reviewer = &quot;user&quot;</code> on an OpenAB deployment.</strong> Without auto-review,\n<code>on-request</code> pauses each tool call to wait for an interactive human approval,\nand OpenAB agents have no terminal attached — every tool call hangs in\n<code>in_progress</code> until openab's 1800 s hard timeout fires. Use\n<code>approvals_reviewer = &quot;auto_review&quot;</code> (recommended, see\n<a href=\"#approval-policy--auto-review\">§Approval Policy</a>) or\n<code>approval_policy = &quot;never&quot;</code> for trusted and already-isolated pods (<code>&quot;never&quot;</code>\nremoves all per-call guardrails — the outer pod isolation is the only\nremaining boundary).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Or launch with:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">codex --sandbox danger-full-access\n</code></pre>\n<p>Or seed via <code>kubectl cp</code> (see <a href=\"#approval-policy--auto-review\">above</a> for why\nConfigMap mounts should not be used for <code>.codex/config.toml</code>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl cp config.toml &lt;pod-name&gt;:/home/node/.codex/config.toml\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-codex\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Important:</strong> <code>danger-full-access</code> disables only Codex's <em>inner</em> sandbox. It\ndoes <strong>not</strong> remove the outer OpenAB container/VM isolation. The agent remains\nconfined by the runtime's own security boundary. Ensure the outer runtime is a\nnon-privileged container (no <code>--privileged</code> flag or excessive capabilities) for\nthis security model to hold.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Imagegen appears to hang</h3>\n<p>Check whether an image was generated even if the CLI has not returned yet:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">find /home/node/.codex/generated_images -type f -name '*.png' -printf '%T@ %p %s\\n' | sort -n | tail\n</code></pre>\n<p>If a file exists, copy it to a stable path and upload it manually with the\nDiscord API command above.</p>\n<h3>No image upload appears in Discord</h3>\n<p>Verify the agent can see an upload token:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-codex -- \\\n  sh -lc 'test -n &quot;$DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; &amp;&amp; echo token-present || echo token-missing'\n</code></pre>\n<p>Also confirm the bot has <code>Send Messages</code>, <code>Send Messages in Threads</code>, and\n<code>Attach Files</code> permissions in the target channel or thread.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Codex"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "config-reference",
      "html": "<h1>Configuration Reference</h1>\n<p>OpenAB is configured via a TOML file (default: <code>config.toml</code>). Environment variables can be interpolated using <code>${VAR_NAME}</code> syntax.</p>\n<p>At least one adapter section (<code>[discord]</code> or <code>[slack]</code>) is required.</p>\n<h2>Loading Config</h2>\n<p>Specify the config source with <code>--config</code> / <code>-c</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Local file (default: config.toml when omitted)\nopenab run -c config.toml\n\n# Remote URL via HTTPS (recommended)\nopenab run -c https://example.com/config.toml\n\n# Remote URL via HTTP (warns — avoid in production; config contains secrets)\nopenab run -c http://internal.example.com/config.toml\n\n# Amazon S3 (or S3-compatible) object\nopenab run -c s3://my-bucket/path/to/config.toml\n</code></pre>\n<p>Remote config is fetched via HTTP GET with a 10-second timeout and a 1 MiB response size limit. Environment variable expansion (<code>${VAR}</code>) works identically on both local and remote config content.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Security best practice:</strong> Never hardcode secrets in remote config files. Use environment variable references like <code>bot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;</code> and inject the actual values via local environment variables or Kubernetes Secrets. For centralized secret management with rotation and audit, use <code>[secrets.refs]</code> with AWS Secrets Manager or an exec provider — see <a href=\"/openab/secrets-management\">secrets-management.md</a>. OpenAB expands <code>${VAR}</code> identically for both local and remote config.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3><code>s3://</code> config source</h3>\n<p><code>openab run -c s3://&lt;bucket&gt;/&lt;key&gt;</code> fetches the config object directly from Amazon S3\n(requires a build with the <code>config-s3</code> feature, which is on by default). The same\n1 MiB size cap, UTF-8 validation, and <code>${VAR}</code> expansion apply as for HTTP(S) sources.</p>\n<p><strong>Credential &amp; region resolution</strong> uses the standard AWS provider chain — the same\nmechanism as <code>aws-sm://</code> secret references:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>environment variables (<code>AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID</code>, <code>AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY</code>, <code>AWS_REGION</code>),</li>\n<li>shared config/credentials files (<code>~/.aws/...</code>),</li>\n<li>container/instance roles: <strong>IRSA / EKS Pod Identity</strong> (Kubernetes) or the <strong>ECS task role</strong> / EC2 instance role.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>There is no <code>[s3]</code> config section for this: the credentials needed to <em>fetch</em> the\nconfig cannot live <em>inside</em> the config you are fetching. Configure the bootstrap S3\naccess via the environment/role above.</p>\n<p><strong>Minimum IAM policy</strong> — scope the role to only the config prefix, never <code>Resource: &quot;*&quot;</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n  &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;s3:GetObject&quot;],\n  &quot;Resource&quot;: &quot;arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/path/to/*&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Secrets still never belong in the config object.</strong> The <code>s3://</code> loader does not\nresolve secrets — it only fetches text and expands <code>${VAR}</code>. Keep secrets out of the\nS3 object and inject them via env vars / <code>[secrets.refs]</code> as above.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>S3-compatible stores (Cloudflare R2, MinIO):</strong> R2 generally works by setting\n<code>AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3</code> (plus R2 keys and <code>AWS_REGION=auto</code>). MinIO and some others\nadditionally require path-style addressing, which the standard AWS env vars do not\ncover yet — explicit endpoint / path-style support is tracked as a follow-up. Only\npoint the endpoint at trusted hosts; a poisoned endpoint env var could redirect the\nfetch to a malicious server.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[discord]</code></h2>\n<p>Discord adapter. Requires a Discord bot token.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bot_token</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required</em></td>\n<td>Discord bot token. Use <code>${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}</code> for env var.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_channels</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td><code>true</code> = all channels; <code>false</code> = only <code>allowed_channels</code>. Omitted = inferred from list (non-empty → false, empty → true).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_channels</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Channel IDs to allow. Only checked when <code>allow_all_channels</code> resolves to false.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_users</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td><code>true</code> = any user; <code>false</code> = only <code>allowed_users</code>. Omitted = inferred from list.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_users</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>User IDs to allow. Only checked when <code>allow_all_users</code> resolves to false.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_bot_messages</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;off&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;off&quot;</code> — ignore all bot messages. <code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code> — only process bot messages that @mention this bot. <code>&quot;all&quot;</code> — process all bot messages (capped by <code>max_bot_turns</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>trusted_bot_ids</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>When non-empty, only these bot IDs pass the bot gate. Empty = any bot (mode permitting). <strong>Admission override:</strong> a trusted bot that @mentions this bot bypasses <code>allow_bot_messages</code> mode entirely (treated as human @mention, can pull bot into threads).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_user_messages</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code> — like <code>&quot;involved&quot;</code>, but require @mention once another bot has posted in the thread (recommended for multi-bot deployments). <code>&quot;involved&quot;</code> — reply in threads bot has participated in without @mention; channel messages require @mention; DMs always process. <code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code> — always require @mention.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_dm</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code> = respond to Discord DMs; <code>false</code> = ignore DMs. <code>allowed_users</code> still applies in DMs. Each DM user consumes one session slot.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_bot_turns</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>100</code></td>\n<td>Max consecutive bot turns per thread before throttling (soft limit). Human message resets the counter. A compiled-in hard cap of 1000 consecutive bot messages is always enforced.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>message_processing_mode</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;per-message&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Message dispatch mode: <code>&quot;per-message&quot;</code> (each message = own turn), <code>&quot;per-thread&quot;</code> (all messages in thread share one buffer), or <code>&quot;per-lane&quot;</code> (each sender gets own buffer). See <a href=\"/openab/message-dispatch-modes\">Message Dispatch Modes</a>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_buffered_messages</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>10</code></td>\n<td>Per-thread/lane mpsc channel capacity. Only applies to <code>per-thread</code> / <code>per-lane</code> modes.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_batch_tokens</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>24000</code></td>\n<td>Soft token cap per ACP turn. Only applies to <code>per-thread</code> / <code>per-lane</code> modes.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[slack]</code></h2>\n<p>Slack adapter using Socket Mode. Requires both a Bot User OAuth Token and an App-Level Token.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bot_token</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required</em></td>\n<td>Bot User OAuth Token (<code>xoxb-...</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>app_token</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required</em></td>\n<td>App-Level Token (<code>xapp-...</code>) for Socket Mode.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_channels</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td>Same behavior as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_channels</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Slack channel IDs (e.g. <code>C0123456789</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_users</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td>Same behavior as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_users</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Slack user IDs (e.g. <code>U0123456789</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_bot_messages</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;off&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>trusted_bot_ids</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Slack Bot User IDs (<code>U...</code>) or Bot IDs (<code>B...</code>). <code>U...</code> matching resolves event Bot IDs via Slack <code>bots.info</code>, so the bot token needs <code>users:read</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_user_messages</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_bot_turns</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>100</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>message_processing_mode</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;per-message&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord. See <a href=\"/openab/message-dispatch-modes\">Message Dispatch Modes</a>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_buffered_messages</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>10</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_batch_tokens</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>24000</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>assistant_mode</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Use <code>assistant.threads.setStatus</code> for status indicators instead of emoji reactions, and native content streaming via <code>chat.startStream</code>/<code>appendStream</code>/<code>stopStream</code> instead of the post+edit loop. Native streaming is suppressed when another bot is present in the thread. Requires an AI-app Slack app with <code>assistant:write</code> — set to <code>false</code> for non-AI Slack apps to keep emoji-reaction status. When native streaming is active, the <code>reply_to</code> output directive is bypassed — the streamed message is itself the in-thread reply.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[gateway]</code></h2>\n<p>Custom Gateway adapter for platforms like Telegram, LINE, Feishu/Lark, and Google Chat. Connects to the gateway via WebSocket.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required</em></td>\n<td>WebSocket URL of the gateway (e.g. <code>ws://openab-gateway:8080/ws</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;telegram&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Platform name for session key namespacing (e.g. <code>&quot;telegram&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;line&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;feishu&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;googlechat&quot;</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>token</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Shared token for WebSocket authentication (optional but recommended).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bot_username</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Bot username for @mention gating in groups.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_channels</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td><code>true</code> = all channels; <code>false</code> = only <code>allowed_channels</code>. Omitted = inferred from list (non-empty → false, empty → true).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_channels</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Chat/group IDs to allow. Only checked when <code>allow_all_channels</code> resolves to false.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_users</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td><code>true</code> = any user; <code>false</code> = only <code>allowed_users</code>. Omitted = inferred from list.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_users</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>User IDs to allow. Only checked when <code>allow_all_users</code> resolves to false.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_bot_messages</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Allow messages from bots. Unlike Discord/Slack (which use an enum with <code>&quot;off&quot;</code>/<code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code>/<code>&quot;all&quot;</code>), the gateway adapter uses a simple boolean: <code>true</code> = allow all bots, <code>false</code> = block (unless in <code>trusted_bot_ids</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>trusted_bot_ids</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Bot IDs that bypass the bot filter even when <code>allow_bot_messages = false</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>streaming</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Enable streaming (typewriter) mode — requires the gateway platform to support message editing.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>streaming_placeholder</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Show &quot;…&quot; placeholder at streaming start. Set <code>false</code> for platforms using drafts (e.g. Telegram Rich Messages).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>message_processing_mode</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;per-message&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord. See <a href=\"/openab/message-dispatch-modes\">Message Dispatch Modes</a>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_buffered_messages</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>10</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_batch_tokens</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>24000</code></td>\n<td>Same as Discord.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[agent]</code></h2>\n<p>The AI agent subprocess that OpenAB spawns to handle messages via ACP.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>This entire section is optional.</strong> If omitted, <code>command</code> and <code>args</code> default from <code>$OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND</code> (e.g. <code>&quot;opencode acp&quot;</code> — first token is command, rest are args). Each Docker image sets this env var so you typically don't need an <code>[agent]</code> block unless you want to override <code>env</code> or <code>args</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p><strong>Resolution priority:</strong> config <code>[agent].command</code>/<code>args</code> &gt; <code>$OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND</code> &gt; <code>&quot;openab-agent&quot;</code></p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Partial override rule:</strong> Setting <code>command</code> without <code>args</code> resets args to <code>[]</code>. This prevents a custom command from inheriting the env var's args. To keep env-var args with a custom command, set both fields explicitly.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>command</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>from <code>$OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND</code> or <code>&quot;openab-agent&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Agent binary. Optional — defaults from image env var.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>args</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td>from <code>$OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND</code> or <code>[]</code></td>\n<td>CLI arguments. Defaults to env var args only when <code>command</code> is also defaulted.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>working_dir</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>$HOME</code></td>\n<td>Working directory for the agent process. Optional — defaults to container's <code>$HOME</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>env</code></td>\n<td>map</td>\n<td><code>{}</code></td>\n<td>Extra environment variables (e.g. <code>{ OPENAI_API_KEY = &quot;${OPENAI_API_KEY}&quot; }</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>inherit_env</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Env var names to inherit from the OAB process (e.g. vars injected via K8s <code>envFrom</code>). Keys in <code>env</code> take precedence.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Default inherited vars:</strong> After <code>env_clear()</code>, the agent always receives <code>HOME</code>, <code>PATH</code>, and <code>USER</code> (on Windows: <code>USERPROFILE</code>, <code>USERNAME</code>, <code>PATH</code>, <code>SystemRoot</code>, <code>SystemDrive</code>). Use <code>inherit_env</code> to pass additional vars beyond this baseline.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Authentication</h3>\n<p>Each image sets <code>OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND</code> with the correct auth command. To authenticate any agent:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-&lt;name&gt; -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>This works for all agents regardless of backend — no need to remember the specific auth command.</p>\n<h3>Agent examples</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Kiro CLI\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;kiro-cli&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n\n# Claude Code\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;claude-agent-acp&quot;\nargs = []\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/node&quot;\n# Auth: kubectl exec -it deploy/openab-claude -- claude auth login\n# Credentials persist in HOME PVC across restarts. See docs/claude-code.md.\n\n# Codex\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;codex-acp&quot;\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/node&quot;\nenv = { OPENAI_API_KEY = &quot;${OPENAI_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n# Gemini CLI\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;gemini&quot;\nargs = [&quot;--acp&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/node&quot;\nenv = { GEMINI_API_KEY = &quot;${GEMINI_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n# GitHub Copilot\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;copilot&quot;\nargs = [&quot;--acp&quot;, &quot;--stdio&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/node&quot;\n\n# opencode\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;opencode&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/node&quot;\n\n# Pi Agent\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;pi-acp&quot;\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/node&quot;\n\n# Cursor Agent\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;cursor-agent&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--model&quot;, &quot;auto&quot;, &quot;--workspace&quot;, &quot;/home/agent&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n\n# Hermes Agent\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;hermes-acp&quot;\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[pool]</code></h2>\n<p>Session pool settings for managing concurrent agent sessions.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_sessions</code></td>\n<td>usize</td>\n<td><code>10</code></td>\n<td>Maximum number of concurrent agent sessions. When full, the oldest idle session is suspended (recoverable); if all sessions are busy, new requests are rejected.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>session_ttl_hours</code></td>\n<td>u64</td>\n<td><code>4</code></td>\n<td>Session time-to-live in hours. Idle sessions are reclaimed after this period. The example config uses <code>24</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[hooks]</code></h2>\n<p>Lifecycle hooks that run at specific points during the container lifecycle. See <a href=\"/openab/hooks\">hooks.md</a> for full documentation and examples.</p>\n<h3><code>[hooks.pre_seed]</code></h3>\n<p>Downloads and extracts archives from S3 before <code>pre_boot</code>. Seeds the agent environment with configs, tools, and shared memory without requiring AWS CLI in the image.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><code>pre-seed</code> is enabled by default. No feature flag needed.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sources</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>S3 URIs of archives (<code>.zip</code>, <code>.tar.gz</code>, <code>.tgz</code>). Max 5. Extracted in order; later layers overwrite earlier ones.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>target</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>$HOME</code></td>\n<td>Extraction target directory.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_bytes</code></td>\n<td>u64</td>\n<td><code>104857600</code></td>\n<td>Max compressed archive size in bytes (100 MiB). Rejects downloads exceeding this.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout_seconds</code></td>\n<td>u64</td>\n<td><code>300</code></td>\n<td>Per-source download+extract timeout in seconds.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>on_failure</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code> exits openab; <code>&quot;warn&quot;</code> logs and continues.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>region</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Override AWS region for S3 access.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>endpoint_url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Override S3 endpoint URL (for LocalStack, VPC endpoints).</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Credential resolution</strong> uses the standard AWS provider chain (same as <code>config-s3</code> and <code>secrets-aws</code>):\nenvironment variables, shared credentials, IRSA / EKS Pod Identity, ECS task role.</p>\n<p><strong>Integrity verification:</strong> If S3 objects are uploaded with <code>--checksum-algorithm SHA256</code>, OpenAB automatically verifies the checksum on download. No config needed — see <a href=\"/openab/hooks\">hooks.md</a> for details.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_seed]\nsources = [\n  &quot;s3://my-bucket/base-env.tar.gz&quot;,\n  &quot;s3://my-bucket/shared-memory.zip&quot;,\n  &quot;s3://my-bucket/agent-overrides.tgz&quot;,\n]\ntimeout_seconds = 300\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3><code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code></h3>\n<p>Runs <strong>before</strong> agent pool creation. Use for bootstrapping files, syncing from S3, installing CLIs.</p>\n<h3><code>[hooks.pre_shutdown]</code></h3>\n<p>Runs <strong>after</strong> pool shutdown on SIGTERM. Use for backing up state, syncing to S3.</p>\n<p>Both hooks share the same fields:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>script</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Absolute path to an executable script.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>inline</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Script content (written to temp file and executed).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Remote script URL (max 1 MiB).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sha256</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Required with <code>url</code> — hex-encoded SHA-256 checksum.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout_seconds</code></td>\n<td>u64</td>\n<td><code>60</code></td>\n<td>Max wall-clock seconds before the script is killed.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>on_failure</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code> exits openab; <code>&quot;warn&quot;</code> logs and continues.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Exactly one of <code>script</code>, <code>inline</code>, or <code>url</code> must be set. <code>script</code> must be an absolute path. <code>url</code> requires <code>sha256</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\nset -e\naws s3 sync &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_URI&quot; &quot;$HOME/&quot;\n'''\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\n\n[hooks.pre_shutdown]\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\naws s3 sync &quot;$HOME/&quot; &quot;s3://$STATE_BUCKET/$TASK_FAMILY/&quot; \\\n  --exclude &quot;aws-cli/*&quot; --quiet\n'''\ntimeout_seconds = 30\non_failure = &quot;warn&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[secrets]</code></h2>\n<p>External secrets management. Secrets are resolved at boot time (after <code>pre_boot</code> hooks) and held in memory only — never written to disk. See <a href=\"/openab/secrets-management\">secrets-management.md</a> for full documentation.</p>\n<h3><code>[secrets.refs]</code></h3>\n<p>Secret references. Each key maps to a provider URI. Resolved values are available as <code>${secrets.&lt;key&gt;}</code> in other config fields.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&lt;name&gt;</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>URI referencing an external secret. Supported schemes: <code>aws-sm://</code>, <code>exec://</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>URI formats:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>aws-sm://&lt;secret-id&gt;#&lt;json-key&gt;</code> — fetch from AWS Secrets Manager, extract JSON field</li>\n<li><code>exec://&lt;absolute-script-path&gt; &lt;key&gt; &lt;attribute&gt;</code> — run script with two arguments, read stdout</li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>[secrets.aws]</code></h3>\n<p>AWS Secrets Manager provider configuration (optional).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>region</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>auto</td>\n<td>Override AWS region. Defaults to SDK credential chain (env/IMDS/IRSA).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>endpoint_url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Override endpoint URL (for LocalStack or VPC endpoints).</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3><code>[secrets.exec]</code></h3>\n<p>Exec provider configuration (optional).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout_seconds</code></td>\n<td>u64</td>\n<td><code>10</code></td>\n<td>Max seconds per script invocation before kill.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.refs]\ndiscord_token = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#discord_bot_token&quot;\nopenai_key    = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#openai_api_key&quot;\ngithub_pat    = &quot;exec:///home/agent/.local/bin/get-secret.sh vault/openab github_pat&quot;\n\n[secrets.aws]\nregion = &quot;ap-northeast-1&quot;\n\n[secrets.exec]\ntimeout_seconds = 15\n\n[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${secrets.discord_token}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[reactions]</code></h2>\n<p>Emoji reaction feedback on messages to show agent processing status.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>enabled</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Enable/disable reaction feedback.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>remove_after_reply</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Remove the status reaction after the agent replies.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>tool_display</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;full&quot;</code></td>\n<td>How tool calls are rendered: <code>&quot;full&quot;</code> (complete title), <code>&quot;compact&quot;</code> (count summary, e.g. <code>✅ 3 · 🔧 1 tool(s)</code>), or <code>&quot;none&quot;</code> (hidden).</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3><code>[reactions.emojis]</code></h3>\n<p>Customize the emoji for each processing stage.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>queued</code></td>\n<td>👀</td>\n<td>Message received, queued for processing.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>thinking</code></td>\n<td>🤔</td>\n<td>Agent is thinking / generating.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>tool</code></td>\n<td>🔥</td>\n<td>Agent is calling a tool.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>coding</code></td>\n<td>👨‍💻</td>\n<td>Agent is writing code.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>web</code></td>\n<td>⚡</td>\n<td>Agent is doing web operations.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>done</code></td>\n<td>🆗</td>\n<td>Agent finished successfully.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>error</code></td>\n<td>😱</td>\n<td>Agent encountered an error.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3><code>[reactions.timing]</code></h3>\n<p>Fine-tune reaction timing behavior (milliseconds).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>debounce_ms</code></td>\n<td><code>700</code></td>\n<td>Debounce interval before updating the reaction emoji.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stall_soft_ms</code></td>\n<td><code>10000</code></td>\n<td>Soft stall threshold — warn if no progress.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stall_hard_ms</code></td>\n<td><code>30000</code></td>\n<td>Hard stall threshold — consider the agent stuck.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>done_hold_ms</code></td>\n<td><code>1500</code></td>\n<td>How long to show the done emoji before removing (if <code>remove_after_reply</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>error_hold_ms</code></td>\n<td><code>2500</code></td>\n<td>How long to show the error emoji before removing.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3><code>[reactions.mapping]</code></h3>\n<p>Map emoji reactions to text commands. When a user reacts with a configured emoji on any message in a monitored channel, the bot treats it as if the user sent the corresponding text message.</p>\n<p>Keys can be unicode emoji or Discord/GitHub shortcodes (e.g. <code>:thumbsup:</code>). Shortcodes are resolved to unicode at config load time.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[reactions.mapping]\n&quot;👍&quot; = &quot;OK&quot;\n&quot;:thumbsdown:&quot; = &quot;不行&quot;\n&quot;:arrows_counterclockwise:&quot; = &quot;重新 review&quot;\n&quot;:white_check_mark:&quot; = &quot;approve&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Requirements:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Enable the <code>GUILD_MESSAGE_REACTIONS</code> intent in the Discord Developer Portal.</li>\n<li>Only unicode emoji are supported (custom server emoji are ignored).</li>\n<li>The bot's own reactions are always ignored (prevents feedback loops).</li>\n<li>Channel/thread access control still applies — reactions in non-monitored channels are ignored.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[stt]</code></h2>\n<p>Speech-to-text transcription for voice messages. Uses an OpenAI-compatible <code>/audio/transcriptions</code> endpoint.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>enabled</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Enable voice message transcription.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>api_key</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td>\n<td>API key for the STT service. When empty and <code>base_url</code> contains <code>groq.com</code>, the <code>GROQ_API_KEY</code> environment variable is used automatically. For local servers, use <code>api_key = &quot;not-needed&quot;</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;whisper-large-v3-turbo&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Model name to use for transcription.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base_url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;https://api.groq.com/openai/v1&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Base URL of the STT API. Any OpenAI-compatible <code>/audio/transcriptions</code> endpoint works.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>echo_transcript</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>When set to <code>true</code> and STT runs, post a <code>&gt; 🎤 &lt;transcript&gt;</code> message to the thread before the agent reply so users can verify what was heard. Failures show <code>(transcription failed)</code> and add a ⚠️ reaction to the original message.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[workspace]</code></h2>\n<p>Workspace aliases for <a href=\"/openab/adr/control-directives\">Control Directives</a>. Users specify <code>[[ws:@alias]]</code> in their first message to set the session's working directory.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[workspace.aliases]\nopenab = &quot;~/projects/openab&quot;\ninfra  = &quot;~/projects/infra-cdk&quot;\nweb    = &quot;~/projects/frontend&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>aliases</code></td>\n<td>map</td>\n<td><code>{}</code></td>\n<td>Key-value map of alias name → path. Users reference with <code>@</code> prefix: <code>[[ws:@openab]]</code>. Paths starting with <code>~</code> expand to <code>$HOME</code>. All paths must be within the bot's home directory (security boundary).</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Security:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Relative paths are rejected</li>\n<li><code>~</code> expands to bot home (<code>$HOME</code>)</li>\n<li>Paths are canonicalized and must be within bot home subtree</li>\n<li>Symlink escapes are caught by canonicalization</li>\n<li>Target must be an existing directory (not a file)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[ambient]</code></h2>\n<p>Passive channel listening with batch flush. See <a href=\"/openab/ambient\">ambient.md</a> for full guide.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[ambient]\nenabled = false                   # Master switch\nflush_interval_seconds = 60       # Time trigger (±20% jitter)\nflush_max_messages = 10           # Count trigger\nflush_hard_cap = 50               # Max buffer size\nmax_concurrent_flushes = 3        # Global LLM concurrency limit\nflush_timeout_seconds = 120       # Safety timeout per flush\ncontext_window = 20               # (v2, not yet implemented)\n\n[ambient.pool]                    # (v2, not yet enforced)\nmax_sessions = 5\nsession_ttl_minutes = 60\ncontext_flushes = 3\n\n[ambient.discord]\nchannels = []                     # Channel ID allowlist — and their threads (required)\nallow_bot_messages = true\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2><code>[cron]</code></h2>\n<p>Everything cron-related lives under <code>[cron]</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[cron]\nusercron_enabled = true                      # enable hot-reload (default: false)\nusercron_path = &quot;cronjob.toml&quot;               # relative to $HOME/.openab/, or absolute\n\n[[cron.jobs]]\nenabled = true                               # optional, default: true\nschedule = &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;                    # cron expression (5-field POSIX)\nchannel = &quot;123456789&quot;                        # target channel/thread ID\nmessage = &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot; # message sent to agent\nplatform = &quot;discord&quot;                         # optional, default: &quot;discord&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;DailyOps&quot;                     # optional, default: &quot;openab-cron&quot;\ntimezone = &quot;America/New_York&quot;                # optional, default: &quot;UTC&quot;\nthread_id = &quot;&quot;                               # optional, post to existing thread\n\n[[cron.jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 0 * * 0&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789&quot;\nmessage = &quot;generate weekly status report&quot;\nplatform = &quot;discord&quot;\ntimezone = &quot;UTC&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3><code>[cron]</code> fields</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>usercron_enabled</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Enable usercron hot-reload. Must be explicitly set to <code>true</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>usercron_path</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Path to the external <code>cronjob.toml</code>. Relative paths resolve from <code>$HOME/.openab/</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3><code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> fields</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>enabled</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Set <code>false</code> to disable without removing the entry.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>schedule</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required</em></td>\n<td>Cron expression (minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>channel</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required</em></td>\n<td>Target Discord channel/thread ID or Slack channel ID.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>message</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required</em></td>\n<td>Message sent to the agent as a prompt.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;discord&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Target platform (<code>&quot;discord&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;slack&quot;</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sender_name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;openab-cron&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Sender attribution shown in the prompt context.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timezone</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;UTC&quot;</code></td>\n<td>IANA timezone for schedule evaluation (e.g. <code>&quot;America/New_York&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;Europe/Berlin&quot;</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>thread_id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Optional thread ID to post into an existing thread.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>The external <code>cronjob.toml</code> uses <code>[[jobs]]</code> (same fields). See <a href=\"/openab/cronjob#usercron--hot-reload-with-cronjobtoml\">Usercron docs</a> for details.</p>\n<h3>Usercron-only <code>[[jobs]]</code> fields</h3>\n<p>These fields are valid only in the external usercron file, for example <code>$HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml</code>. They are rejected in baseline <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> because OpenAB only writes state back to the user-managed cron file.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required with <code>disable_on_success</code></em></td>\n<td>Stable job ID used when the scheduler writes <code>enabled = false</code> or <code>thread_id</code> back to <code>cronjob.toml</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>disable_on_success</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Command to run before sending the scheduled prompt.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>disable_on_success_match</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><em>required with <code>disable_on_success</code></em></td>\n<td>Marker that must appear in stdout or stderr, in addition to exit code <code>0</code>, before the job is considered complete.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>disable_on_success_timeout_secs</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>60</code></td>\n<td>Timeout for the completion check command.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>disable_on_success_working_dir</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Working directory for the completion check command.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[jobs]]\nid = &quot;fix-unit-tests&quot;\nenabled = true\nschedule = &quot;*/10 * * * *&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789&quot;\nmessage = &quot;Unit tests are still failing. Continue fixing them.&quot;\ndisable_on_success = &quot;npm test &amp;&amp; echo OPENAB_GOAL_SUCCESS&quot;\ndisable_on_success_match = &quot;OPENAB_GOAL_SUCCESS&quot;\ndisable_on_success_timeout_secs = 120\ndisable_on_success_working_dir = &quot;/workspace/my-project&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Cron expression format:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>┌───────────── minute (0-59)\n│ ┌───────────── hour (0-23)\n│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1-31)\n│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1-12)\n│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0-7, 0 and 7 = Sunday)\n│ │ │ │ │\n* * * * *\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Behaviors:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Scheduler evaluates expressions once per minute</li>\n<li>If a previous execution is still running, the next tick is skipped (no overlap)</li>\n<li>Failed executions are logged but do not block other jobs or chat traffic</li>\n<li>Stateless — no persistence needed, re-evaluated from config on restart</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Customizing via Helm</h2>\n<p>When deploying with the Helm chart (<code>charts/openab</code>), the <code>config.toml</code> is generated from <code>values.yaml</code>. Each agent is defined under the <code>agents</code> map:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    command: kiro-cli\n    args: [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\n    discord:\n      enabled: true\n      allowedChannels: [&quot;1234567890&quot;]\n      allowBotMessages: &quot;mentions&quot;\n      trustedBotIds: [&quot;9876543210&quot;]\n    pool:\n      maxSessions: 10\n      sessionTtlHours: 24\n    reactions:\n      enabled: true\n    stt:\n      enabled: true\n      apiKey: &quot;your-groq-key&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Key mapping (<code>values.yaml</code> → <code>config.toml</code>):</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Helm value</th>\n<th>Config key</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord.allowedChannels</code></td>\n<td><code>[discord] allowed_channels</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord.allowBotMessages</code></td>\n<td><code>[discord] allow_bot_messages</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord.trustedBotIds</code></td>\n<td><code>[discord] trusted_bot_ids</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord.allowUserMessages</code></td>\n<td><code>[discord] allow_user_messages</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord.messageProcessingMode</code></td>\n<td><code>[discord] message_processing_mode</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord.maxBufferedMessages</code></td>\n<td><code>[discord] max_buffered_messages</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord.maxBatchTokens</code></td>\n<td><code>[discord] max_batch_tokens</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.slack.*</code></td>\n<td><code>[slack] *</code> (same pattern)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.pool.maxSessions</code></td>\n<td><code>[pool] max_sessions</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.pool.sessionTtlHours</code></td>\n<td><code>[pool] session_ttl_hours</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.workspace.aliases.&lt;alias&gt;</code></td>\n<td><code>[workspace.aliases] &lt;alias&gt;</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.reactions.enabled</code></td>\n<td><code>[reactions] enabled</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.reactions.toolDisplay</code></td>\n<td><code>[reactions] tool_display</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.stt.apiKey</code></td>\n<td><code>[stt] api_key</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].enabled</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] enabled</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].schedule</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] schedule</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].channel</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] channel</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].message</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] message</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].platform</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] platform</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].senderName</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] sender_name</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].timezone</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] timezone</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.cronjobs[].threadId</code></td>\n<td><code>[[cron.jobs]] thread_id</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ Use <code>--set-string</code> (not <code>--set</code>) for Discord/Slack IDs to avoid float64 precision loss:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade --install mybot charts/openab \\\n  --set-string agents.kiro.discord.allowedChannels[0]=&quot;1234567890&quot;\n</code></pre>\n</blockquote>\n<p>See <code>charts/openab/values.yaml</code> for the full list of Helm values including <code>persistence</code>, <code>image</code>, <code>resources</code>, and multi-agent examples.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Environment variable interpolation</h2>\n<p>Any value can reference environment variables with <code>${VAR_NAME}</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">bot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Undefined variables resolve to an empty string.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Unified Mode Environment Variables</h2>\n<p>When running with <code>BUILD_MODE=unified</code>, the binary embeds a webhook server for gateway platforms. These env vars control its behavior:</p>\n<h3>Server</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_LISTEN</code></td>\n<td><code>0.0.0.0:8080</code></td>\n<td>Bind address for the embedded webhook server</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Security Gating</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_CHANNELS</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Accept events from any channel. <strong>Set to <code>false</code> in production</strong> and use <code>GATEWAY_ALLOWED_CHANNELS</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_ALLOWED_CHANNELS</code></td>\n<td><em>(empty)</em></td>\n<td>Comma-separated channel IDs to allow (when <code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_CHANNELS=false</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Accept events from any user. <strong>Set to <code>false</code> in production</strong> and use <code>GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS</code></td>\n<td><em>(empty)</em></td>\n<td>Comma-separated user IDs to allow (when <code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=false</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_BOT_MESSAGES</code></td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Allow messages from all bots (for multi-agent scenarios)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_TRUSTED_BOT_IDS</code></td>\n<td><em>(empty)</em></td>\n<td>Comma-separated bot IDs to allow even when <code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_BOT_MESSAGES=false</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_BOT_USERNAME</code></td>\n<td><em>(empty)</em></td>\n<td>Bot's username for @mention detection in groups</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Platform Adapters</h3>\n<p>Each platform is auto-enabled when its env vars are present:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Required Env Var</th>\n<th>Optional</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Telegram</td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN</code>, <code>TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_PATH</code>, <code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>LINE</td>\n<td><code>LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET</code></td>\n<td><code>LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Feishu</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_APP_ID</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Google Chat</td>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true</code></td>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_JSON</code>, <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_FILE</code>, <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_ACCESS_TOKEN</code>, <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_AUDIENCE</code>, <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>WeCom</td>\n<td><code>WECOM_CORP_ID</code></td>\n<td><em>(see wecom config)</em></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Teams</td>\n<td><code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code></td>\n<td><code>TEAMS_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ <strong>Production checklist</strong>: Set <code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_CHANNELS=false</code> and <code>GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=false</code> with explicit allowlists. The defaults are permissive for development convenience.</p>\n<p>⚠️ <strong>Google Chat JWT</strong>: When <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_AUDIENCE</code> is unset, webhook requests are <strong>not</strong> verified via JWT. Set this to your Google Chat app's project number or service account email in production to enable request authentication. If <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_FILE</code> is set but the file cannot be read, the adapter starts without token authentication (warn logged).</p>\n</blockquote>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Configuration Reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "control-directives",
      "html": "<h1>Control Directives</h1>\n<h2>Overview</h2>\n<p>Users can configure session-level parameters by adding <code>[[key:value]]</code> directives to their first message. These are parsed and stripped before the prompt reaches the agent.</p>\n<h2>Format</h2>\n<pre><code>@Bot [[ws:@openab]] [[title:Fix CI workflow]]\nhelp me debug the smoke test failures\n</code></pre>\n<p>Rules:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Directives are only processed on the <strong>first message</strong> of a session</li>\n<li>Consecutive <code>[[key:value]]</code> tokens at the start = directive header</li>\n<li>First non-directive token/line = prompt content begins</li>\n<li>Later <code>[[key:value]]</code> text in the message body is preserved verbatim</li>\n<li>Duplicate keys: last value wins</li>\n<li>Unknown keys: silently ignored (forward compatible)</li>\n<li>Directives may span multiple lines:\n<pre><code>[[ws:@openab]]\n[[title:Review PR]]\nplease review this change\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Available Directives</h2>\n<h3><code>ws</code> — Workspace</h3>\n<p>Set the session's working directory. The agent starts with this path as cwd, loading steering files and skills from it.</p>\n<pre><code>[[ws:~/projects/myapp]]\n[[ws:@openab]]\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Alias syntax:</strong> Use <code>@name</code> to reference a configured alias (see <a href=\"/openab/workspaces\">Workspaces</a>).</p>\n<p><strong>Security:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Path must be absolute (<code>~</code> or <code>/</code> prefix)</li>\n<li><code>~</code> expands to bot home directory (<code>$HOME</code>)</li>\n<li>Path must exist and be a directory</li>\n<li>Path must be within bot home subtree (symlink escapes caught by canonicalization)</li>\n<li>Invalid paths abort the session with a user-visible error</li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>title</code> — Thread Title</h3>\n<p>Set the initial thread/channel title (max 100 characters, truncated silently).</p>\n<pre><code>[[title:Bug triage #42]]\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Empty value (<code>[[title:]]</code>) = use auto-generated title</li>\n<li>The agent may override this later per its own workflow</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Behavior</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Directives are <strong>immutable</strong> — once a session starts, parameters cannot be changed mid-conversation</li>\n<li>To change workspace or title, start a new session</li>\n<li>If no <code>[[ws:...]]</code> is specified, the session uses the bot's default working directory</li>\n<li>If workspace resolution fails on a new session, the session is not created. However, <code>[[title:...]]</code> is applied independently before workspace validation — the thread title may already be set even if the session aborts.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Relationship to Output Directives</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Output Directives</th>\n<th>Control Directives</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Direction</td>\n<td>Agent → Platform</td>\n<td>User → Bot</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Timing</td>\n<td>Every response</td>\n<td>First message only</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Syntax</td>\n<td><code>[[key:value]]</code></td>\n<td><code>[[key:value]]</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Future Directives (Phase 2+)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Directive</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[model:...]]</code></td>\n<td>Select model for the session</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[repo:owner/repo]]</code></td>\n<td>Bind GitHub repository context</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>[[timeout:300]]</code></td>\n<td>Session timeout in seconds</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>See Also</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/workspaces\">Workspaces</a> — configuring workspace aliases</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/output-directives\">Output Directives</a> — agent → platform directives</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/control-directives\">ADR: Control Directives</a> — design rationale</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Control Directives"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "copilot",
      "html": "<h1>GitHub Copilot CLI — Agent Backend Guide</h1>\n<p>How to run OpenAB with <a href=\"https://github.com/github/copilot-cli\">GitHub Copilot CLI</a> as the agent backend.</p>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>A paid <a href=\"https://github.com/features/copilot/plans\">GitHub Copilot</a> subscription (<strong>Pro, Pro+, Business, or Enterprise</strong> — Free tier does not include CLI/ACP access)</li>\n<li>Copilot CLI ACP support is in <a href=\"https://github.blog/changelog/2026-01-28-acp-support-in-copilot-cli-is-now-in-public-preview/\">public preview</a> since Jan 28, 2026</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>┌──────────────┐  Gateway WS   ┌──────────────┐  ACP stdio    ┌──────────────────────┐\n│   Discord    │◄─────────────►│ openab       │──────────────►│ copilot --acp --stdio │\n│   User       │               │   (Rust)     │◄── JSON-RPC ──│ (Copilot CLI)         │\n└──────────────┘               └──────────────┘               └──────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>OpenAB spawns <code>copilot --acp --stdio</code> as a child process and communicates via stdio JSON-RPC. No intermediate layers.</p>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command and args default from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;copilot --acp --stdio&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Docker</h2>\n<p>Build with the Copilot-specific Dockerfile:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.copilot -t openab-copilot .\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Copilot CLI has two independent auth layers that can use <strong>different</strong> GitHub accounts:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Copilot subscription auth</strong> — authenticates your Copilot subscription (model access)</li>\n<li><strong><code>gh</code> CLI auth</strong> — authenticates git operations (clone, push, PR creation)</li>\n</ol>\n<p>This separation lets you use a subscription owner's token for Copilot while scoping git operations to a different GitHub user (e.g. a bot account).</p>\n<h3>Step 1: Copilot Subscription (fine-grained PAT)</h3>\n<p>Generate a <a href=\"https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new\">fine-grained personal access token</a> from the GitHub account that owns the Copilot subscription:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Token name: e.g. <code>openab-copilot</code></li>\n<li>Expiration: as needed</li>\n<li><strong>Account permissions → Copilot Requests: Read-only</strong> (this is the only permission required)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Inject it as an env var in your Helm chart (add the last line):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab-copilot openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.copilot.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.copilot.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.copilot.discord.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.copilot.command=copilot \\\n  --set 'agents.copilot.args={--acp,--stdio}' \\\n  --set agents.copilot.persistence.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.copilot.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set 'agents.copilot.env.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE'  # optional\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: <code>COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN</code> is only required if you want to authenticate the Copilot subscription via a fine-grained PAT without running <code>copilot login</code>, or if you plan to use <code>gh auth login</code> with a different user for git operations. If you only have one GitHub account, you can skip this and use <code>copilot login</code> instead (see below).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Step 2: <code>gh</code> CLI Auth (scoped user)</h3>\n<p>After deployment, authenticate <code>gh</code> as a separate user for git operations:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-copilot-copilot -- gh auth login -p https -w\n</code></pre>\n<p>Follow the device flow in your browser, authorizing with the desired GitHub account (e.g. a bot user like <code>thepagent</code>).</p>\n<p>Verify:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-copilot-copilot -- gh auth status\n</code></pre>\n<p>The <code>gh</code> token is stored under <code>~/.config/gh/</code> on the PVC and persists across pod restarts.</p>\n<h3>Summary</h3>\n<pre><code>Scenario 1: Same user for both (simple)\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  copilot login (as @alice)                              │\n│    ├─ Copilot subscription ── @alice's plan ✅          │\n│    └─ gh operations ───────── @alice ✅                 │\n│                                                         │\n│  No env var needed. One login covers everything.        │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\nScenario 2: Different users (split auth)\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_... (from @alice)      │\n│    └─ Copilot subscription ── @alice's plan ✅          │\n│                                                         │\n│  gh auth login (as @bot-user)                           │\n│    └─ gh operations ───────── @bot-user ✅              │\n│                                                         │\n│  Use when subscription owner ≠ git operations user.     │\n│  e.g. @alice owns Copilot Pro, @bot-user pushes code.   │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Recommendation</strong>: If your Copilot subscription is on a privileged human account (e.g. org admin), we strongly recommend Scenario 2 — use a fine-grained PAT for the subscription and a scoped bot user for git operations. This limits the blast radius of the agent's git access.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Auth Layer</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Account</th>\n<th>Method</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>Copilot subscription (models)</td>\n<td>Subscription owner</td>\n<td>Fine-grained PAT env var</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>gh auth</code></td>\n<td>Git operations (clone, push)</td>\n<td>Bot / scoped user</td>\n<td>Device flow (<code>gh auth login</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: Classic personal access tokens (<code>ghp_</code>) are <strong>not supported</strong> for Copilot. Use a fine-grained PAT (<code>github_pat_</code>) with the &quot;Copilot Requests&quot; permission.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab-copilot openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.copilot.discord.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.copilot.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.copilot.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.copilot.command=copilot \\\n  --set 'agents.copilot.args={--acp,--stdio}' \\\n  --set agents.copilot.persistence.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.copilot.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set 'agents.copilot.env.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE' \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><code>COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN</code> is optional — see Authentication section below.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-copilot</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-copilot</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-copilot</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-copilot</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.copilot.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-copilot\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Model Selection</h2>\n<p>The default model is defined in <code>~/.copilot/settings.json</code>.</p>\n<p>To set <code>auto</code> as the default model, exec into the container and create the file:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-copilot-copilot -- bash -c '\ncat &lt;&lt; EOF &gt; ~/.copilot/settings.json\n{\n  &quot;model&quot;: &quot;auto&quot;\n}\nEOF'\n</code></pre>\n<p>The <code>auto</code> setting lets Copilot automatically select the best model for each request. This persists across pod restarts when <code>persistence.enabled=true</code> (the home directory is on a PVC).</p>\n<h2>Known Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>⚠️ ACP support is in <strong>public preview</strong> — behavior may change</li>\n<li>Classic personal access tokens (<code>ghp_</code>) are not supported — use fine-grained PATs (<code>github_pat_</code>)</li>\n<li>Copilot CLI requires an active Copilot subscription per user/org</li>\n<li>For Copilot Business/Enterprise, an admin must enable Copilot CLI from the Policies page</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "GitHub Copilot CLI — Agent Backend Guide"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "cronjob",
      "html": "<h1>Scheduled Messages (Config-Driven Cron)</h1>\n<p>Send recurring prompts to your agent on a schedule — daily summaries, weekly reports, periodic scans — without external infrastructure.</p>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Define <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> entries in <code>config.toml</code></li>\n<li>OpenAB's internal scheduler evaluates cron expressions once per minute</li>\n<li>When a schedule matches, the message is sent to the agent as if a user typed it</li>\n<li>The agent processes the message and replies to the target channel</li>\n</ol>\n<p>No external scheduler (K8s CronJob, GitHub Actions) is needed for simple use cases.</p>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<p>Add to your <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[cron.jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789012345678&quot;\nmessage = &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>This sends <code>summarize yesterday's merged PRs</code> to the agent every weekday at 09:00 UTC in the specified Discord channel.</p>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<p>Each <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> entry
