supports these fields:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[cron.jobs]]\nenabled = true                               # optional, default: true\nschedule = &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;                    # required: cron expression\nchannel = &quot;123456789012345678&quot;               # required: target channel ID\nmessage = &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot; # required: prompt for the agent\nplatform = &quot;discord&quot;                         # optional, default: &quot;discord&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;DailyOps&quot;                     # optional, default: &quot;openab-cron&quot;\ntimezone = &quot;America/New_York&quot;                     # optional, default: &quot;UTC&quot;\nthread_id = &quot;&quot;                               # optional: post to existing thread\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>enabled</code></td>\n<td></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Set <code>false</code> to disable without removing the entry</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>schedule</code></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>5-field POSIX cron expression</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>channel</code></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Discord channel/thread ID or Slack channel ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>message</code></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Message sent to the agent as a prompt</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform</code></td>\n<td></td>\n<td><code>&quot;discord&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;discord&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;slack&quot;</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sender_name</code></td>\n<td></td>\n<td><code>&quot;openab-cron&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Attribution shown in prompt context</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timezone</code></td>\n<td></td>\n<td><code>&quot;UTC&quot;</code></td>\n<td>IANA timezone (e.g. <code>&quot;America/New_York&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;Europe/Berlin&quot;</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>thread_id</code></td>\n<td></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Post into an existing thread instead of the channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Cron Expression Format</h2>\n<p>Standard 5-field POSIX cron, same as Linux crontab, K8s CronJob, and GitHub Actions:</p>\n<pre><code>┌───────────── minute (0-59)\n│ ┌───────────── hour (0-23)\n│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1-31)\n│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1-12)\n│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0-7, 0 and 7 = Sunday)\n│ │ │ │ │\n* * * * *\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Examples</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Expression</th>\n<th>Meaning</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0 9 * * 1-5</code></td>\n<td>Weekdays at 09:00</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0 0 * * 0</code></td>\n<td>Sundays at midnight</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>*/30 * * * *</code></td>\n<td>Every 30 minutes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0 18 * * 1-5</code></td>\n<td>Weekdays at 18:00</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0 9 1 * *</code></td>\n<td>First day of every month at 09:00</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Timezone Support</h2>\n<p>By default, schedules are evaluated in UTC. Set <code>timezone</code> to any IANA timezone:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[cron.jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789012345678&quot;\nmessage = &quot;good morning team, here's today's agenda&quot;\ntimezone = &quot;America/New_York&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>This fires at 09:00 New York time (13:00 or 14:00 UTC depending on DST).</p>\n<h2>Multiple Jobs</h2>\n<p>Define as many <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> entries as you need:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[cron.jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789012345678&quot;\nmessage = &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;DailyOps&quot;\ntimezone = &quot;America/New_York&quot;\n\n[[cron.jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 0 * * 0&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789012345678&quot;\nmessage = &quot;generate weekly status report&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;WeeklyReport&quot;\n\n[[cron.jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 18 * * 1-5&quot;\nchannel = &quot;C0123456789&quot;\nmessage = &quot;check for any critical alerts in the last 8 hours&quot;\nplatform = &quot;slack&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;OpsBot&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Helm Deployment</h2>\n<p>When using the Helm chart, define cronjobs under each agent in <code>values.yaml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    cronjobs:\n      - schedule: &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;\n        channel: &quot;123456789012345678&quot;\n        message: &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot;\n        platform: &quot;discord&quot;\n        senderName: &quot;DailyOps&quot;\n        timezone: &quot;America/New_York&quot;\n      - schedule: &quot;0 0 * * 0&quot;\n        channel: &quot;123456789012345678&quot;\n        message: &quot;generate weekly status report&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ Use <code>--set-string</code> for channel IDs to avoid float64 precision loss:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade mybot charts/openab \\\n  --set-string agents.kiro.cronjobs[0].channel=&quot;123456789012345678&quot;\n</code></pre>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Usercron — Hot-Reload with <code>cronjob.toml</code></h2>\n<p>Cronjobs defined in <code>config.toml</code> require a redeploy to change. <strong>Usercron</strong> lets you manage schedules in a separate <code>cronjob.toml</code> file that the scheduler hot-reloads automatically — no restart needed.</p>\n<h3>Enable Usercron</h3>\n<p>Add to your <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[cron]\nusercron_enabled = true\nusercron_path = &quot;cronjob.toml&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usercron is <strong>disabled by default</strong>. Both fields are required to activate it.</p>\n<h4>Minimal config.toml example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;kiro-cli&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n\n[cron]\nusercron_enabled = true\nusercron_path = &quot;cronjob.toml&quot;    # → $HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Note: Everything cron-related lives under <code>[cron]</code> — both usercron settings and baseline <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>The path is relative to <code>$HOME/.openab/</code> (e.g. <code>&quot;cronjob.toml&quot;</code> resolves to <code>$HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml</code>). Absolute paths are used as-is. The scheduler starts watching immediately, even if the file doesn't exist yet.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>New installations</strong>: If <code>~/.openab/</code> does not exist yet, the scheduler silently skips the file and continues running. Once you create the directory and place <code>cronjob.toml</code> inside, it will be picked up automatically on the next tick — no restart required.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p>[!CAUTION]\n<strong>Breaking Change (v0.8.2)</strong> — <code>usercron_path</code> relative path base changed from <code>$HOME</code> to <code>$HOME/.openab/</code>.\nIf you are upgrading from a previous version, move your existing file:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">mkdir -p ~/.openab\nmv ~/cronjob.toml ~/.openab/cronjob.toml\n</code></pre>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Create <code>cronjob.toml</code></h3>\n<p>Same format as <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> in config.toml, but uses <code>[[jobs]]</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;* * * * *&quot;\nchannel = &quot;1490282656913559673&quot;\nmessage = &quot;ping&quot;\nplatform = &quot;discord&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;usercron&quot;\ntimezone = &quot;Asia/Taipei&quot;\n\n[[jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;0 9 * * 1-5&quot;\nchannel = &quot;1490282656913559673&quot;\nmessage = &quot;summarize yesterday's merged PRs&quot;\nsender_name = &quot;DailyOps&quot;\ntimezone = &quot;Asia/Taipei&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<pre><code>                         config.toml                   $HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml\n                    ┌──────────────────┐                 ┌──────────────────────┐\n                    │ [cron]           │                 │ [[jobs]]             │\n                    │ usercron_enabled │                 │ schedule = &quot;* * * *&quot; │\n                    │   = true         │                 │ channel  = &quot;123...&quot;  │\n                    │ usercron_path    │                 │ message  = &quot;ping&quot;    │\n                    │   = &quot;cronjob.toml│&quot;                └──────────┬───────────┘\n                    │                  │                            │\n                    │ [[cron.jobs]]    │                   Agent writes here\n                    │ (baseline jobs)  │                   anytime (mobile/CLI)\n                    └────────┬─────────┘                           │\n                             │                                     │\n                    ┌────────▼─────────┐                           │\n                    │  OAB Scheduler   │◄──────────────────────────┘\n                    │  (ticks every    │   check mtime every tick\n                    │   1 minute)      │   reload if changed\n                    └────────┬─────────┘\n                             │\n              ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n              │              │              │\n     baseline jobs    usercron jobs    should_fire()?\n     (immutable)      (hot-reload)         │\n              │              │         ┌────▼────┐\n              └──────────────┘    no── │ match?  │ ──yes──► fire_cronjob()\n                                      └─────────┘          → send message\n                                                            → create thread\n                                                            → agent processes\n</code></pre>\n<ol>\n<li>Every scheduler tick (~1 minute), the file's modification time is checked</li>\n<li>If the file changed → re-parse and replace the dynamic job list</li>\n<li><code>config.toml</code> <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> are the <strong>immutable baseline</strong>; <code>cronjob.toml</code> jobs are the <strong>dynamic overlay</strong></li>\n<li>Invalid TOML or bad entries are logged and skipped — baseline jobs are never affected</li>\n<li>Deleting the file removes all dynamic jobs (baseline jobs continue)</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Agent-Managed Schedules</h3>\n<p>Because <code>cronjob.toml</code> is a plain file, your agent can write to it directly:</p>\n<pre><code>User: set up a cronjob that pings me every minute\nAgent: ✅ Written to cronjob.toml, takes effect within 1 minute\n</code></pre>\n<p>This enables mobile-friendly schedule management — talk to your agent from your phone, and it updates the cron file for you.</p>\n<h3>Goal-Driven Auto-Disable</h3>\n<p>Usercron jobs can stop themselves once a goal is complete. Add <code>disable_on_success</code> to run a command before the scheduled prompt is sent. The job is considered complete only when the command exits <code>0</code> <strong>and</strong> stdout or stderr contains <code>disable_on_success_match</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[jobs]]\nid = &quot;fix-unit-tests&quot;                       # required for scheduler writeback\nenabled = true\nschedule = &quot;*/10 * * * *&quot;\nchannel = &quot;1490282656913559673&quot;\nmessage = &quot;Unit tests are still failing. Continue fixing them and report progress.&quot;\n\ndisable_on_success = &quot;npm test &amp;&amp; echo OPENAB_GOAL_SUCCESS&quot;\ndisable_on_success_match = &quot;OPENAB_GOAL_SUCCESS&quot;\ndisable_on_success_timeout_secs = 120\ndisable_on_success_working_dir = &quot;/workspace/my-project&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Execution flow:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>The schedule matches.</li>\n<li>The scheduler runs <code>disable_on_success</code>.</li>\n<li>If the command exits <code>0</code> and output contains <code>disable_on_success_match</code>, OpenAB posts <code>✅ Goal achieved</code>, writes <code>enabled = false</code> back to <code>$HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml</code>, and skips the regular prompt.</li>\n<li>Otherwise, OpenAB sends the regular <code>message</code> and the agent continues working.</li>\n</ol>\n<p><code>disable_on_success</code> is supported only in usercron <code>[[jobs]]</code>, not baseline <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code>. This keeps scheduler writeback limited to the user-managed cron file.</p>\n<h3>Re-enabling a Disabled Job</h3>\n<p>Once a goal is achieved and the job is disabled, re-enable it by editing <code>$HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Flip back to true to restart the job\nenabled = true\n</code></pre>\n<p>This can be done manually, or by asking the AI agent (e.g. &quot;re-enable the fix-unit-tests cron job&quot;).</p>\n<h3>Kubernetes Deployment</h3>\n<p>Mount <code>cronjob.toml</code> on a PVC so it persists across pod restarts, and set <code>usercron_path</code> in your config.toml:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># config.toml\n[cron]\nusercron_enabled = true\n# Relative to $HOME/.openab/ — resolves to $HOME/.openab/cronjob.toml\nusercron_path = &quot;cronjob.toml&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Behaviors</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Minute-aligned</strong>: The scheduler aligns to minute boundaries (<code>:00</code>), so <code>0 9 * * *</code> fires at exactly 09:00:00, not at whatever second the process started.</li>\n<li><strong>Overlap protection</strong>: If a previous execution of the same job is still running, the next tick is skipped.</li>\n<li><strong>Isolation</strong>: Cron failures are logged but never block interactive chat traffic.</li>\n<li><strong>Usercron persistence</strong>: For usercron jobs, the scheduler may write <code>thread_id</code> and <code>enabled = false</code> back to <code>cronjob.toml</code>.</li>\n<li><strong>Graceful shutdown</strong>: In-flight cron tasks are waited on (up to 30 seconds) during shutdown.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Sender Identity</h2>\n<p>When a cron job fires, the agent sees a sender context like:</p>\n<pre><code>🕐 [DailyOps]: summarize yesterday's merged PRs\n</code></pre>\n<p>Use <code>sender_name</code> to distinguish different scheduled tasks in logs and thread titles. The agent can use this to tailor its response (e.g. &quot;DailyOps asked for a summary&quot; vs &quot;WeeklyReport asked for a report&quot;).</p>\n<h2>When to Use External Schedulers Instead</h2>\n<p>Config-driven cron covers the 80% use case: &quot;send this message at this time.&quot; For advanced needs, use external schedulers:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Need</th>\n<th>Recommendation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Simple recurring prompts</td>\n<td>✅ Config-driven cron (this feature)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Long-running jobs (&gt;5 min)</td>\n<td>K8s CronJob</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Conditional logic / retries</td>\n<td>GitHub Actions or Step Functions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-step workflows / DAGs</td>\n<td>GitHub Actions or Step Functions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Per-execution isolation</td>\n<td>K8s CronJob (separate Pod per run)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/refarch/cronjob_k8s_refarch\">Kubernetes CronJob Reference Architecture</a> for the external scheduler approach.</p>\n<h2>Known Limitations</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Limitation</th>\n<th>Details</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Mixed numeric/name day-of-week</td>\n<td><code>1,Mon</code> or <code>Mon,3</code> is not supported and will be rejected. Use either all numeric (<code>1-5</code>) or all name-based (<code>Mon-Fri</code>) notation.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Wrap-around day-of-week ranges</td>\n<td><code>5-2</code> (Fri through Tue) is not supported. Use explicit listing instead: <code>5,6,0,1,2</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Tip:</strong> Name-based notation (<code>Mon-Fri</code>, <code>Sun</code>, <code>Mon,Wed,Fri</code>) is always available as an alternative to numeric day-of-week values.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Symptom</th>\n<th>Cause</th>\n<th>Fix</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Job never fires</td>\n<td>Invalid cron expression</td>\n<td>Check logs for <code>invalid cron expression, skipping</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Job fires but no reply</td>\n<td>Agent error</td>\n<td>Check logs for <code>cron handle_message error</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Wrong time</td>\n<td>Timezone mismatch</td>\n<td>Set <code>timezone</code> explicitly (default is UTC)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Job skipped</td>\n<td>Previous execution still running</td>\n<td>Check logs for <code>skipping cronjob, previous execution still running</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Channel not found</td>\n<td>Bot not in channel</td>\n<td>Invite the bot to the target channel</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Usercron not reloading</td>\n<td>File not saved / wrong path</td>\n<td>Check logs for <code>usercron file changed, reloading</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Usercron parse error</td>\n<td>Invalid TOML syntax</td>\n<td>Check logs for <code>failed to parse usercron file</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Goal job does not auto-disable</td>\n<td>Command did not exit <code>0</code> or output did not include <code>disable_on_success_match</code></td>\n<td>Run the command manually and confirm both conditions</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Scheduled messages"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "cursor",
      "html": "<h1>Cursor Agent CLI — Agent Backend Guide</h1>\n<p>How to run OpenAB with <a href=\"https://www.cursor.com/\">Cursor Agent CLI</a> as the agent backend.</p>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>A paid <a href=\"https://www.cursor.com/pricing\">Cursor</a> subscription (<strong>Pro or Business</strong> — Free tier does not include Agent CLI access)</li>\n<li>Cursor Agent CLI with native ACP support</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>┌──────────────┐  Gateway WS   ┌──────────────┐  ACP stdio    ┌──────────────────────┐\n│   Discord    │◄─────────────►│ openab       │──────────────►│ cursor-agent acp      │\n│   User       │               │   (Rust)     │◄── JSON-RPC ──│ (Cursor Agent CLI)    │\n└──────────────┘               └──────────────┘               └──────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>OpenAB spawns <code>cursor-agent acp</code> as a child process and communicates via stdio JSON-RPC. No intermediate layers.</p>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command and args default from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;cursor-agent acp&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\n# Auth via: kubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- cursor-agent login\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Docker</h2>\n<p>Build with the Cursor-specific Dockerfile:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.cursor -t openab-cursor .\n</code></pre>\n<p>The Dockerfile installs a pinned version of Cursor Agent CLI via direct download from <code>downloads.cursor.com</code>. The version is controlled by the <code>CURSOR_VERSION</code> build arg.</p>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Cursor Agent CLI uses its own login flow. In a headless container:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># 1. Exec into the running pod/container\nkubectl exec -it deployment/openab-cursor -- bash\n\n# 2. Authenticate via device flow\ncursor-agent login\n\n# 3. Follow the device code flow in your browser\n\n# 4. Restart the pod (token is persisted via PVC)\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-cursor\n</code></pre>\n<p>The auth token is stored under <code>~/.cursor/</code> and persisted across pod restarts via PVC.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.cursor.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.cursor.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.cursor.command=cursor-agent \\\n  --set 'agents.cursor.args={acp}' \\\n  --set agents.cursor.persistence.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.cursor.workingDir=/home/agent \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-cursor</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-cursor</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-cursor</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-cursor</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.cursor.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-cursor\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Model Selection</h2>\n<p>List available models:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cursor-agent --list-models\n# or\ncursor-agent models\n</code></pre>\n<p>To specify a model, pass <code>--model</code> as an arg:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# Override args (command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;cursor-agent acp&quot;)\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--model&quot;, &quot;auto&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>In ACP mode, <code>--model</code> can be appended after <code>acp</code>. If omitted, the account default is used.</p>\n<p>To verify which model is active, ask the agent &quot;who are you&quot; — the underlying model will typically self-identify (e.g. &quot;I am Gemini, a large language model built by Google.&quot;).</p>\n<h2>MCP Usage (ACP mode caveats)</h2>\n<p>Cursor Agent CLI supports MCP servers configured via <code>.cursor/mcp.json</code> in the active workspace directory. <strong>Which directory counts as the workspace is determined by the <code>--workspace</code> flag</strong> — if omitted, cursor-agent auto-detects from <code>cwd</code>, which is usually <code>/home/agent</code> in OpenAB containers via the Dockerfile <code>WORKDIR</code> directive but can drift in interactive or local runs. For reproducible MCP loading, pass <code>--workspace</code> explicitly:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# Override args (command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;cursor-agent acp&quot;)\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--model&quot;, &quot;auto&quot;, &quot;--workspace&quot;, &quot;/home/agent&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>This anchors:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>MCP config lookup</strong>: <code>/home/agent/.cursor/mcp.json</code></li>\n<li><strong>Approval file path</strong>: <code>/home/agent/.cursor/projects/home-agent/mcp-approvals.json</code> (slug = URL-safe workspace path)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Without <code>--workspace</code>, a different cwd would produce a different slug and cursor-agent would not find previously saved approvals.</p>\n<h3>Example MCP config</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;mcpServers&quot;: {\n    &quot;playwright&quot;: {\n      &quot;command&quot;: &quot;/usr/bin/npx&quot;,\n      &quot;args&quot;: [&quot;-y&quot;, &quot;@playwright/mcp@latest&quot;]\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Approval quirk in ACP mode</h3>\n<p>Cursor's <code>--approve-mcps</code> flag <strong>does not apply in ACP mode</strong> — it only affects the interactive CLI. In ACP mode, MCP servers are gated by an approval file. Two options:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Pre-create the approvals file</strong> at <code>&lt;workspace&gt;/.cursor/projects/&lt;slug&gt;/mcp-approvals.json</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">[&quot;&lt;server-name&gt;-&lt;sha256_hash&gt;&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Hash is derived from workspace path + server config.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Approve once interactively</strong>, then let Cursor persist the approval:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-cursor -- cursor-agent\n# invoke an MCP tool, approve the prompt; approval is saved\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<p>OpenAB itself auto-responds to ACP <code>session/request_permission</code> with <code>allow_always</code> (see <code>src/acp/connection.rs</code>), so once an MCP server is <em>loaded</em>, subsequent tool calls pass without prompting. The approval file only gates the initial load.</p>\n<h3>Verifying MCP is loaded</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-cursor -- cursor-agent mcp list\n# Expected: &quot;&lt;server-name&gt;: ready&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Known Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Cursor Agent CLI is a separate distribution from Cursor Desktop — they are not the same binary</li>\n<li>No official apt/yum package; the Dockerfile downloads a pinned tarball directly</li>\n<li><code>cursor-agent login</code> requires an interactive terminal for the device flow</li>\n<li>Auth token persistence requires a PVC mount at the user home directory</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Cursor"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "devin",
      "html": "<h1>Devin CLI — Agent Backend Guide</h1>\n<p>How to run OpenAB with <a href=\"https://docs.devin.ai/cli\">Devin CLI</a> as the agent backend.</p>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>A <a href=\"https://devin.ai/\">Devin</a> subscription (Enterprise or individual plan) from Cognition AI</li>\n<li>Devin CLI with native ACP support (<code>devin acp</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>┌──────────────┐  Gateway WS   ┌──────────────┐  ACP stdio    ┌──────────────┐\n│   Discord    │◄─────────────►│ openab       │──────────────►│ devin acp    │\n│   User       │               │   (Rust)     │◄── JSON-RPC ──│ (Devin CLI)  │\n└──────────────┘               └──────────────┘               └──────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>OpenAB spawns <code>devin acp</code> as a child process and communicates via stdio JSON-RPC. No intermediate adapter needed — Devin CLI natively implements the Agent Client Protocol.</p>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;devin&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\nenv = { DEVIN_MODEL = &quot;glm-5.2&quot;, DEVIN_PERMISSION_MODE = &quot;dangerous&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Setting <code>DEVIN_PERMISSION_MODE = &quot;dangerous&quot;</code> is recommended for\nheadless/container deployments. Without it, Devin CLI may prompt for permission\nconfirmations on certain operations, causing the agent to get stuck in\nnon-interactive environments.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Docker</h2>\n<p>Build with the unified Dockerfile:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build --target devin -f Dockerfile.unified -t openab-devin .\n</code></pre>\n<p>Or via docker buildx bake:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker buildx bake devin\n</code></pre>\n<p>The Dockerfile installs a pinned version of Devin CLI from <code>static.devin.ai</code> with SHA256 checksum verification. The version is controlled by the <code>DEVIN_VERSION</code> build arg.</p>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Devin CLI requires authentication via a Devin account. In a headless container:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># 1. Exec into the running pod/container\nkubectl exec -it deployment/openab-devin -- bash\n\n# 2. Authenticate via manual token flow (headless-friendly)\ndevin auth login --force-manual-token-flow\n\n# 3. Follow the instructions to paste your token\n\n# 4. Restart the pod (credentials persist via PVC)\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-devin\n</code></pre>\n<p>Credentials are stored under <code>~/.local/share/devin/</code> and persist across pod restarts via PVC.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.devin.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.devin.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.devin.command=devin \\\n  --set 'agents.devin.args={acp}' \\\n  --set agents.devin.persistence.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.devin.workingDir=/home/agent \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-devin</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-devin</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Features</h2>\n<p>Devin CLI provides:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Native ACP</strong>: <code>devin acp</code> speaks JSON-RPC over stdio directly</li>\n<li><strong>AGENTS.md support</strong>: Reads <code>AGENTS.md</code> at project root automatically</li>\n<li><strong>MCP servers</strong>: Full MCP support (stdio + HTTP transports)</li>\n<li><strong>Subagents</strong>: Can spawn foreground/background subagents for parallel work</li>\n<li><strong>Session persistence</strong>: Conversation history saved and resumable</li>\n<li><strong>Models</strong>: SWE-1.6 series with adaptive routing</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Model Selection</h2>\n<p>Devin CLI uses its own model routing by default (SWE-1.6 series). To specify a model at startup:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;devin&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--model&quot;, &quot;opus&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Available models can be checked via the interactive CLI with <code>/model</code>. In ACP mode, the <code>--model</code> flag selects the model for the session.</p>\n<h2>MCP Usage</h2>\n<p>Devin CLI supports MCP servers configured via <code>.devin/config.json</code> or <code>devin mcp add</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Add an MCP server (persists in ~/.config/devin/)\nkubectl exec -it deployment/openab-devin -- devin mcp add github \\\n  -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github\n\n# List configured servers\nkubectl exec -it deployment/openab-devin -- devin mcp list\n</code></pre>\n<p>MCP configuration can also be placed in the project's <code>.devin/config.json</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;mcpServers&quot;: {\n    &quot;github&quot;: {\n      &quot;command&quot;: &quot;npx&quot;,\n      &quot;args&quot;: [&quot;-y&quot;, &quot;@modelcontextprotocol/server-github&quot;],\n      &quot;env&quot;: { &quot;GITHUB_TOKEN&quot;: &quot;ghp_xxx&quot; }\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Devin CLI supports both stdio and HTTP (Streamable HTTP + SSE fallback) transports.</p>\n<h2>AGENTS.md Compatibility</h2>\n<p>Devin CLI reads <code>AGENTS.md</code> from the project root — the same file OpenAB already uses. It also reads <code>CLAUDE.md</code> (for Claude Code compatibility) and rules from <code>.cursor/rules/</code> and <code>.windsurf/rules/</code>.</p>\n<h2>Known Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Requires a paid Devin subscription (Cognition AI); no free tier for CLI access</li>\n<li><code>devin auth login</code> requires interactive terminal for browser flow; use <code>--force-manual-token-flow</code> in headless environments</li>\n<li>Enterprise features (team settings, controls) require Devin Enterprise plan</li>\n<li>Config file must be mounted at <code>/etc/openab/config.toml</code> at runtime (not baked into image)</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Devin CLI — Agent Backend Guide"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "discord",
      "html": "<h1>Discord Guide</h1>\n<p>Complete guide to setting up, configuring, and running OpenAB with Discord.</p>\n<h2>Bot Setup</h2>\n<h3>1. Create a Discord Application</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to the <a href=\"https://discord.com/developers/applications\">Discord Developer Portal</a></li>\n<li>Click <strong>New Application</strong></li>\n<li>Give it a name (e.g. <code>AgentBroker</code>) and click <strong>Create</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<h3>2. Enable Gateway Intents</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>In your application, go to the <strong>Bot</strong> tab (left sidebar)</li>\n<li>Scroll down to <strong>Privileged Gateway Intents</strong></li>\n<li>Enable <strong>Message Content Intent</strong></li>\n<li>Enable <strong>Server Members Intent</strong> (recommended)</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Save Changes</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<h3>3. Get the Bot Token</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Still on the <strong>Bot</strong> tab, click <strong>Reset Token</strong></li>\n<li>Copy the token — you'll need this for <code>DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code></li>\n<li>Keep this token secret. If it leaks, reset it immediately</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>4. Set Bot Permissions</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>OAuth2</strong> → <strong>URL Generator</strong> (left sidebar)</li>\n<li>Under <strong>Scopes</strong>, check <code>bot</code></li>\n<li>Under <strong>Bot Permissions</strong>, check:\n<ul>\n<li>Send Messages</li>\n<li>Send Messages in Threads</li>\n<li>Create Public Threads</li>\n<li>Read Message History</li>\n<li>Add Reactions</li>\n<li>Manage Messages</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Copy the generated URL at the bottom</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>5. Invite the Bot to Your Server</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Open the URL from step 4 in your browser</li>\n<li>Select the server you want to add the bot to</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Authorize</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<h3>6. Get the Channel ID</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>In Discord, go to <strong>User Settings</strong> → <strong>Advanced</strong> → enable <strong>Developer Mode</strong></li>\n<li>Right-click the channel where you want the bot to respond</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Copy Channel ID</strong></li>\n<li>Use this ID in <code>allowed_channels</code> in your config</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>7. Get Your User ID (optional)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Make sure <strong>Developer Mode</strong> is enabled (see step 6)</li>\n<li>Right-click your own username (in a message or the member list)</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Copy User ID</strong></li>\n<li>Use this ID in <code>allowed_users</code> to restrict who can interact with the bot</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>Configuration Reference</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p>📖 Full config options with defaults: <a href=\"/openab/config-reference#discord\">docs/config-reference.md</a></p>\n</blockquote>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\nallowed_channels = [&quot;123456789&quot;]      # channel ID allowlist (empty = all)\nallowed_users = [&quot;987654321&quot;]         # user ID allowlist (empty = all)\nallow_bot_messages = &quot;off&quot;            # off | mentions | all\nallow_user_messages = &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;      # multibot-mentions | involved | mentions\ntrusted_bot_ids = []                  # bot user IDs allowed through (empty = any)\n</code></pre>\n<h3><code>allowed_channels</code> / <code>allowed_users</code></h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th><code>allowed_channels</code></th>\n<th><code>allowed_users</code></th>\n<th>Result</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>empty</td>\n<td>empty</td>\n<td>All users, all channels (default)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>set</td>\n<td>empty</td>\n<td>Only these channels, all users</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>empty</td>\n<td>set</td>\n<td>All channels, only these users</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>set</td>\n<td>set</td>\n<td><strong>AND</strong> — must be in allowed channel AND allowed user</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<ul>\n<li>Empty <code>allowed_users</code> (default) = no user filtering</li>\n<li>Denied users get a 🚫 reaction and no reply</li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>allow_bot_messages</code></h3>\n<p>Controls whether the bot processes messages from other Discord bots.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Value</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n<th>Loop risk</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;off&quot;</code> (default)</td>\n<td>Ignore all bot messages</td>\n<td>None</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Only process bot messages that @mention this bot</td>\n<td>Very low</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;all&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Process all bot messages (capped at 10 consecutive)</td>\n<td>Mitigated by turn cap</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>The bot's own messages are always ignored regardless of this setting.</p>\n<h3><code>allow_user_messages</code></h3>\n<p>Controls whether the bot requires @mention in threads.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Value</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;involved&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Respond in threads the bot owns or has participated in without @mention. Main channel always requires @mention.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Always require @mention, even in the bot's own threads.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code> (default)</td>\n<td>Same as <code>involved</code> in single-bot threads. In threads where other bots have also posted, requires @mention — prevents all bots from responding to every message.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Comparison</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th><code>involved</code></th>\n<th><code>mentions</code></th>\n<th><code>multibot-mentions</code></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Main channel (no @mention)</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Main channel (with @mention)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Single-bot thread (no @mention)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Single-bot thread (with @mention)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-bot thread (no @mention)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-bot thread (with @mention)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>When to use which</h4>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>involved</code></strong> — Single-bot setup, or you want all bots to respond freely in shared threads.</li>\n<li><strong><code>mentions</code></strong> — Strict control. Every message must explicitly @mention the bot. Best for high-traffic channels where accidental triggers are a concern.</li>\n<li><strong><code>multibot-mentions</code></strong> — Multi-bot setup. Natural conversation in single-bot threads, explicit @mention control in multi-bot threads. Recommended for most multi-bot deployments.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>trusted_bot_ids</code></h3>\n<p>When <code>allow_bot_messages</code> is <code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;all&quot;</code>, you can restrict which bots are allowed through:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">trusted_bot_ids = [&quot;123456789012345678&quot;]  # only this bot's messages pass through\n</code></pre>\n<p>Empty (default) = any bot can pass through (subject to the mode check).</p>\n<p><strong>Admission override:</strong> A trusted bot that explicitly @mentions this bot bypasses the <code>allow_bot_messages</code> mode entirely — the mention is treated the same as a human @mention. This allows trusted bots to pull this bot into threads even when <code>allow_bot_messages = &quot;off&quot;</code>. Messages from trusted bots <em>without</em> @mention still follow normal gating.</p>\n<h3><code>allowed_role_ids</code></h3>\n<p>Role IDs that trigger the bot, same as a direct @mention. This enables users to invoke multiple bots simultaneously with a single role mention (e.g. <code>@AllBots review this</code>).</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">allowed_role_ids = [&quot;123456789012345678&quot;]  # @mention this role = trigger the bot\n</code></pre>\n<p>Empty (default) = role mentions do not trigger the bot.</p>\n<p><strong>Setup:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li>Create a Discord role (e.g. <code>Bots</code> or <code>AllAgents</code>)</li>\n<li>Assign the role to all bots you want to trigger together</li>\n<li>Add the role's ID to each bot's <code>allowed_role_ids</code></li>\n<li>Users type <code>@RoleName &lt;prompt&gt;</code> to trigger all bots at once</li>\n</ol>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> If multiple bots share the same role, all will respond simultaneously. Use <code>multibot-mentions</code> mode if you want bots to require explicit @mention when other bots are already in the thread.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>Interaction with <code>multibot-mentions</code> mode</h4>\n<p>When <code>allow_user_messages = &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code> is set alongside <code>allowed_role_ids</code>:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Action</th>\n<th>Result</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>@Role review this</code> in a channel</td>\n<td>All bots trigger (role mention = explicit mention)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Follow-up in the thread without @mention</td>\n<td>Only the thread owner responds (multibot gate kicks in)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>@Role follow up</code> in the thread</td>\n<td>All bots respond again</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>This gives the best of both worlds: one role mention to summon all bots, but subsequent messages in the thread don't cause all bots to pile on.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>@Mention Behavior</h2>\n<p>The bot responds to:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Direct @mention</strong> (<code>@BotUser</code>) — always works</li>\n<li><strong>Role mention</strong> (<code>@RoleName</code>) — only if the role ID is in <code>allowed_role_ids</code></li>\n<li><strong>Thread reply</strong> — depends on <code>allow_user_messages</code> mode (no @mention needed in <code>involved</code> mode)</li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code>✅ @AgentBroker hello           ← user mention, bot responds\n✅ @AllBots hello               ← role mention, bot responds (if role in allowed_role_ids)\n❌ @SomeOtherRole hello         ← role not in allowed_role_ids, bot ignores\n</code></pre>\n<p>The triggering role mention is stripped from the prompt sent to the agent (same as the bot's own user mention).</p>\n<h3>User mention UIDs</h3>\n<p>When a user mentions another user (e.g. <code>@SomeUser</code>) in a message to the bot, the raw Discord mention <code>&lt;@UID&gt;</code> is preserved in the prompt sent to the LLM. This means:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>The LLM can copy <code>&lt;@UID&gt;</code> into its reply to produce a clickable Discord mention</li>\n<li>The bot's own mention is stripped (so the bot doesn't see itself being triggered)</li>\n<li>Triggering role mentions (in <code>allowed_role_ids</code>) are stripped</li>\n<li>Other role mentions are replaced with <code>@(role)</code> placeholder</li>\n</ul>\n<p>To help the LLM know who each UID refers to, provide a UID→name mapping via system prompt or context entry (see <a href=\"#multi-bot-setup\">Multi-Bot Setup</a> below).</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Thread Behavior</h2>\n<p>When you @mention the bot in a channel, it creates a <strong>thread</strong> from your message and responds there. After that:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>multibot-mentions</code> mode (default):</strong> just type in single-bot threads — no @mention needed; in multi-bot threads, @mention required</li>\n<li><strong><code>involved</code> mode:</strong> just type in the thread — no @mention needed</li>\n<li><strong><code>mentions</code> mode:</strong> @mention required for every message, even in threads</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Each thread gets its own agent session. Sessions are cleaned up after <code>session_ttl_hours</code> (default: 24h).</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Ambient Mode</h2>\n<p>Ambient mode allows the bot to passively listen to configured channels and respond only when it has something valuable to add — without requiring @mentions. See <a href=\"/openab/ambient\">ambient.md</a> for full details.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[ambient]\nenabled = true\n\n[ambient.discord]\nchannels = [&quot;1234567890&quot;]   # Channel IDs to monitor (and their threads)\n</code></pre>\n<p>When enabled:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Non-mention messages in listed channels are buffered and periodically sent to the LLM as a batch.</li>\n<li>If the LLM has nothing to add, it returns <code>[NO_REPLY]</code> (silently suppressed).</li>\n<li><strong>@mention always takes priority</strong> — the ambient buffer is discarded and the mention gets an immediate response.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Attachment Handling</h2>\n<p>OpenAB processes Discord file attachments and converts them into content blocks\nfor the agent. Supported types (checked in order):</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Detection</th>\n<th>Agent receives</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Audio</td>\n<td>MIME <code>audio/*</code></td>\n<td>Transcribed text via STT (if enabled)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Text files</td>\n<td>Extension list (<code>.txt</code>, <code>.md</code>, <code>.json</code>, etc.)</td>\n<td>File content inlined (up to 5 files, 1 MB total)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Images</td>\n<td>MIME <code>image/*</code> or image extensions</td>\n<td>Base64-encoded image block</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Video</td>\n<td>MIME <code>video/*</code> or extensions (<code>.mp4</code>, <code>.mov</code>, <code>.webm</code>, <code>.mkv</code>, <code>.m4v</code>, <code>.avi</code>)</td>\n<td>Text block with filename, content type, size, and Discord CDN URL</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Unsupported attachment types are silently ignored.</p>\n<h3>Video attachments</h3>\n<p>Video files are not downloaded or transcoded. The agent receives metadata and the\nDiscord CDN URL so it can fetch or inspect the file using tools like <code>ffprobe</code>.</p>\n<pre><code>[Video attachment]\nfilename: demo.mp4\ncontent_type: video/mp4\nsize_bytes: 8421376\nurl: https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../demo.mp4\n</code></pre>\n<p>No configuration is needed — video forwarding is always enabled.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Streaming</h2>\n<p>OpenAB uses <strong>edit-streaming</strong> on Discord — the bot sends a placeholder message and updates it every 1.5 seconds as tokens arrive, giving a live typing effect.</p>\n<p>Streaming is decided <strong>per-thread</strong>, not globally:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Thread state</th>\n<th>Streaming</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Single bot + human</td>\n<td>✅ ON — live edit updates</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2+ bots in thread</td>\n<td>❌ OFF — send-once to avoid edit interference</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>When a second bot posts in a thread, streaming automatically switches off for that thread. This prevents multiple bots from editing placeholder messages simultaneously, which causes visual glitches on Discord.</p>\n<p>No configuration needed — this is automatic based on multibot detection.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Multi-Bot Setup</h2>\n<p>Multiple bots can share the same Discord channel. Each bot only responds to its own @mentions.</p>\n<h3>Helm example</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.botToken=&quot;$BOT_A_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.kiro.discord.allowedChannels[0]=CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.dealer.discord.botToken=&quot;$BOT_B_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.dealer.discord.allowedChannels[0]=CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.dealer.discord.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.dealer.command=kiro-cli \\\n  --set 'agents.dealer.args={acp,--trust-all-tools}'\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Known limitations</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>One thread per message:</strong> when you @mention both bots in a single message, only the first bot creates a thread. The second bot's thread creation fails and the message is dropped. Workaround: @mention each bot in separate messages.</li>\n<li><strong>Thread ownership (involvement gate):</strong> a bot only responds in threads it owns or has participated in. See the Involvement Gate section below for full details.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Involvement Gate</h3>\n<p>In a multi-bot setup, every bot enforces an <strong>involvement gate</strong> before processing any message in a thread. This gate is evaluated before <code>allow_user_messages</code> or <code>allow_bot_messages</code> mode checks.</p>\n<p><strong>Rule:</strong> A bot must be <strong>involved</strong> (thread owner or has previously replied) before it will process any message in that thread.</p>\n<p><strong>Key constraint:</strong> Only a human @mention — or a @mention from a bot in <code>trusted_bot_ids</code> — can pull a bot into a thread for the first time. A @mention from an untrusted bot will be <strong>silently dropped</strong>.</p>\n<pre><code>Bot A's thread (Bot B not yet involved, Bot A NOT in Bot B's trusted_bot_ids):\n\n  Bot A: &quot;@Bot_B please review this&quot;     → ❌ dropped (Bot B not involved, Bot A untrusted)\n  Human: &quot;@Bot_B please review this&quot;     → ✅ Bot B replies, now involved\n  Bot A: &quot;@Bot_B any updates?&quot;           → ✅ processed (Bot B is involved)\n\nBot A's thread (Bot B not yet involved, Bot A IS in Bot B's trusted_bot_ids):\n\n  Bot A: &quot;@Bot_B please review this&quot;     → ✅ treated as human @mention, Bot B becomes involved\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Why:</strong> This prevents untrusted bots from pulling other bots into arbitrary threads without human consent, protects session pool resources, and eliminates cross-thread chain reactions. Trusted bots are explicitly authorized by the admin.</p>\n<p><strong>Workaround (without trusted_bot_ids):</strong> Pre-involve all needed bots at thread creation by @mentioning them (or using a shared role via <code>allowed_role_ids</code>).</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>📖 Full design details: <a href=\"/openab/messaging#involvement-gate\">docs/messaging.md — Involvement Gate</a></p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Recommended: <code>multibot-mentions</code> mode</h3>\n<p>In multi-bot channels, use <code>multibot-mentions</code> to get the best of both worlds:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nallow_user_messages = &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Single-bot threads:</strong> natural conversation, no @mention needed (same as <code>involved</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Multi-bot threads:</strong> requires @mention so only the addressed bot responds</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Bot-to-bot communication</h3>\n<p>To enable bots to collaborate (e.g. code review → deploy handoff):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Bot that receives bot messages\n[discord]\nallow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Bot turn limits</h3>\n<p>To prevent runaway bot-to-bot loops, OpenAB enforces two layers of protection:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Soft limit</strong> (<code>max_bot_turns</code>, default: 100) — total bot messages in a thread without human intervention. When reached, the bot sends a one-time warning and stops responding. A human message in the thread resets the counter.</li>\n<li><strong>Hard limit</strong> (1000, not configurable) — cap on consecutive bot messages in <code>allow_bot_messages = &quot;all&quot;</code> mode. When reached, bot-to-bot conversation stops until a human replies.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Both limits count <strong>all</strong> bot messages in the thread, including the bot's own replies. In a two-bot ping-pong with <code>max_bot_turns = 100</code>, each bot sends ~50 messages before the limit triggers.</p>\n<p>Warning messages are sent exactly once (on the exact threshold hit) to prevent warnings from ping-ponging between bots.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nmax_bot_turns = 200               # default is 100\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Ice-breaking: teaching bots who's in the room</h3>\n<p>Since user mentions are preserved as raw <code>&lt;@UID&gt;</code>, bots need a UID→name mapping to know who is who. Add an ice-breaking greeting to each bot's system prompt or context entry:</p>\n<pre><code>We have 3 participants in this room:\n\nMY_NICIKNAME    &lt;@MY_NAME&gt;\nBOT1_NICKNAME   &lt;@BOT1&gt;\nBOT2_NICKNAME   &lt;@BOT2&gt;\n\nAlways use &lt;@UID&gt; format to mention someone in your messages.\n</code></pre>\n<p>This lets each bot build the mapping in its own context from the start and correctly mention others using <code>&lt;@UID&gt;</code>.</p>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/multi-agent\">multi-agent.md</a> for detailed examples.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Helm Values</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.kiro.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.allowBotMessages=off \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.allowUserMessages=involved \\\n  --set-string 'agents.kiro.discord.allowedRoleIds[0]=YOUR_ROLE_ID'\n</code></pre>\n<p>⚠️ Use <code>--set-string</code> for channel/user/role IDs to avoid float64 precision loss.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3>Bot doesn't respond</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Check channel ID</strong> — make sure it's in <code>allowed_channels</code></li>\n<li><strong>Check permissions</strong> — bot needs Send Messages, Create Public Threads, Read Message History in the channel</li>\n<li><strong>Check intents</strong> — Message Content Intent must be enabled in Developer Portal</li>\n<li><strong>Check @mention type</strong> — use user mention or a role in <code>allowed_role_ids</code></li>\n<li><strong>Check if in a thread</strong> — with <code>mentions</code> mode, @mention is required even in threads</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Bot stops receiving messages after restart</h3>\n<p>Discord Gateway may throttle event delivery after rapid reconnects. Use <code>scale 0 → wait 5s → scale 1</code> instead of <code>rollout restart</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl scale deployment/openab-kiro --replicas=0 &amp;&amp; sleep 5 &amp;&amp; kubectl scale deployment/openab-kiro --replicas=1\n</code></pre>\n<p>See <a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/issues/455\">#455</a> for details.</p>\n<h3>&quot;Failed to create thread&quot;</h3>\n<p>Discord only allows one thread per message. If another bot already created a thread on the same message, this error appears. The message is dropped. This is a known limitation for multi-bot setups (#457).</p>\n<h3>&quot;Sent invalid authentication&quot;</h3>\n<p>The bot token is wrong or expired. Reset it in the Developer Portal and redeploy.</p>\n<h3>&quot;Failed to start agent&quot;</h3>\n<p>The agent CLI isn't authenticated. For kiro-cli:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-kiro -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-kiro\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Discord Guide"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "feishu",
      "html": "<h1>Feishu / Lark</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Unified Mode (v0.9.0+):</strong> The OAB binary now embeds the feishu adapter directly. Set <code>FEISHU_APP_ID</code> as an env var — no separate gateway container or <code>[gateway]</code> config needed. See <a href=\"/openab/telegram#unified-mode-recommended\">Telegram docs</a> for the pattern.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Unified Config (Kiro + feishu)</h3>\n<p><strong>Minimal:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Recommended:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;compact&quot;\n\n[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Set <code>FEISHU_APP_ID</code> (and related platform env vars) on the container. No <code>[gateway]</code> needed.</p>\n<p>Connect OpenAB to Feishu (China) or Lark (international) so users can chat with an AI agent in DMs or group chats.</p>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Create a Feishu/Lark app at <a href=\"https://open.feishu.cn/\">open.feishu.cn</a> or <a href=\"https://open.larksuite.com/\">open.larksuite.com</a>.</li>\n<li>Enable the <strong>Bot</strong> capability.</li>\n<li>In <strong>Event Subscriptions</strong>, select <strong>Long Connection</strong> (WebSocket) mode.</li>\n<li>Add the <code>im.message.receive_v1</code> event.</li>\n<li>Grant the following permission scopes:\n<ul>\n<li><code>im:message</code> — receive messages</li>\n<li><code>im:message:send_as_bot</code> — send messages as bot</li>\n<li><code>contact:user.base:readonly</code> — resolve sender display names (recommended; without it, senders show as <code>ou_xxx</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Copy the <strong>App ID</strong> and <strong>App Secret</strong> from <strong>Credentials &amp; Basic Info</strong>.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Quick Start (Helm)</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    gateway:\n      enabled: true\n      url: &quot;ws://openab-kiro-gateway:8080/ws&quot;\n      platform: &quot;feishu&quot;\n      botUsername: &quot;ou_YOUR_BOT_OPEN_ID&quot;  # bot's open_id for @mention gating\n      feishu:\n        appId: &quot;cli_xxx&quot;\n        appSecret: &quot;secret_xxx&quot;\n        domain: &quot;feishu&quot;           # &quot;feishu&quot; or &quot;lark&quot;\n        connectionMode: &quot;websocket&quot; # recommended\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade --install openab charts/openab \\\n  --set-literal agents.kiro.gateway.feishu.appSecret=&quot;your-secret&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Connection Modes</h2>\n<h3>WebSocket (default, recommended)</h3>\n<p>The gateway connects outbound to Feishu — no public URL, TLS, or Ingress required.</p>\n<p>Set <code>connectionMode: &quot;websocket&quot;</code> (default).</p>\n<h3>Webhook (fallback)</h3>\n<p>Use when outbound WebSocket is blocked by your network.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">feishu:\n  connectionMode: &quot;webhook&quot;\n  webhookPath: &quot;/webhook/feishu&quot;\n  verificationToken: &quot;your-token&quot;\n  encryptKey: &quot;your-key&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then configure the webhook URL in Feishu Open Platform → Event Subscriptions → Request URL:</p>\n<pre><code>https://your-gateway-host/webhook/feishu\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Configuration Reference</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Helm Value</th>\n<th>Env Var</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.appId</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_APP_ID</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>App ID (required)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.appSecret</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_APP_SECRET</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>App Secret (required, stored in K8s Secret)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.domain</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_DOMAIN</code></td>\n<td><code>feishu</code></td>\n<td><code>feishu</code> (China) or <code>lark</code> (international)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.connectionMode</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_CONNECTION_MODE</code></td>\n<td><code>websocket</code></td>\n<td><code>websocket</code> or <code>webhook</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.webhookPath</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n<td><code>/webhook/feishu</code></td>\n<td>Webhook endpoint path</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.verificationToken</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Webhook verification token (stored in K8s Secret)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.encryptKey</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Webhook encrypt key (stored in K8s Secret)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.allowedGroups</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_ALLOWED_GROUPS</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Comma-separated chat_id allowlist</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.allowedUsers</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_ALLOWED_USERS</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Comma-separated open_id allowlist</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>feishu.requireMention</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_REQUIRE_MENTION</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Require @mention in groups</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_DEDUPE_TTL_SECS</code></td>\n<td><code>300</code></td>\n<td>Event deduplication cache TTL (seconds)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_MESSAGE_LIMIT</code></td>\n<td><code>4000</code></td>\n<td>Max message length before auto-splitting (bytes)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS</code></td>\n<td><code>off</code></td>\n<td>Bot message handling: <code>off</code> / <code>mentions</code> / <code>all</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_TRUSTED_BOT_IDS</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Comma-separated open_id list of known bots</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_MAX_BOT_TURNS</code></td>\n<td><code>20</code></td>\n<td>Max consecutive bot replies per channel before suppression</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_SESSION_TTL_HOURS</code></td>\n<td><code>24</code></td>\n<td>How long the bot remembers thread participation (hours). After expiry, @mention is required again.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_ALLOW_USER_MESSAGES</code></td>\n<td><code>multibot-mentions</code></td>\n<td>Thread response mode: <code>multibot-mentions</code> / <code>involved</code> / <code>mentions</code>. See below.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>gateway.botUsername</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Set to bot's <code>open_id</code> for @mention gating</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>gateway.streaming</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Enable streaming (typewriter) mode</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cardStreaming.mode</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_CARD_STREAMING_MODE</code></td>\n<td><code>auto</code></td>\n<td>Card streaming mode: <code>auto</code> (short→post, long/code/table→card), <code>card</code> (always card), <code>post</code> (disable — kill-switch)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cardStreaming.fallbackToPost</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_CARD_FALLBACK_TO_POST</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Fall back to a post message if a card API call fails</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cardStreaming.promoteBytes</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_CARD_PROMOTE_BYTES</code></td>\n<td><code>4000</code></td>\n<td>Byte threshold for auto-promoting a plain-text reply to a card</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cardStreaming.idleFinalizeMs</code></td>\n<td><code>FEISHU_CARD_IDLE_FINALIZE_MS</code></td>\n<td><code>3000</code></td>\n<td>Idle window (ms) before a streaming card is finalized</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>@mention Gating</h2>\n<p>In group chats, the bot only responds when @mentioned (default). To find your bot's <code>open_id</code>:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Start the gateway — it logs the bot identity on startup:\n<pre><code>feishu bot identity resolved bot_open_id=ou_xxx\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>Set <code>gateway.botUsername</code> to this value.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>To disable mention gating: <code>feishu.requireMention: false</code>.</p>\n<h3>Thread Participation (Involved Mode)</h3>\n<p>Once the bot replies in a thread (topic), it remembers that thread and responds to subsequent messages <strong>without requiring @mention</strong> — similar to Discord's <code>allow_user_messages: &quot;involved&quot;</code> mode.</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Only applies to threads (messages with <code>root_id</code>). Main channel messages always require @mention.</li>\n<li>Participation is stored in memory. Gateway restart clears the cache; users need to @mention once to re-engage.</li>\n<li>TTL controlled by <code>FEISHU_SESSION_TTL_HOURS</code> (default 24h). After expiry, @mention is required again.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Multi-Bot Threads (multibot-mentions Mode)</h3>\n<p>When <code>FEISHU_ALLOW_USER_MESSAGES=multibot-mentions</code>, the bot detects when another bot is @mentioned in a participated thread and reverts to requiring @mention — preventing all bots from responding simultaneously.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mode</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>multibot-mentions</code> (default)</td>\n<td>Like <code>involved</code>, but requires @mention once another bot has posted in the thread.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>involved</code></td>\n<td>Bot responds in participated threads without @mention. All participated bots respond.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mentions</code></td>\n<td>Always require @mention, even in participated threads.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Multi-bot detection</strong> (how the gateway identifies &quot;another bot&quot;):</p>\n<ol>\n<li>If <code>FEISHU_TRUSTED_BOT_IDS</code> is set → exact match against configured IDs</li>\n<li>If only <code>FEISHU_ALLOWED_USERS</code> is set → any @mention that is not self and not in allowed_users is inferred as another bot (recommended, zero-config)</li>\n<li>If neither is set → no multibot detection</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Note: Detection only triggers in threads where the bot has already participated. This prevents premature marking of threads the bot hasn't joined.</p>\n<h2>Security Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><code>appSecret</code>, <code>verificationToken</code>, and <code>encryptKey</code> are stored in a Kubernetes Secret, not in ConfigMap.</li>\n<li>In webhook mode, always set both <code>verificationToken</code> and <code>encryptKey</code> for production.</li>\n<li>The gateway enforces a 1 MB body size limit and per-IP rate limiting (120 req/60s) on the webhook endpoint.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Slash Commands</h2>\n<p>The gateway intercepts slash commands before they reach the agent:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Command</th>\n<th>Action</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/reset</code></td>\n<td>Clears the conversation session.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/cancel</code></td>\n<td>Sends a cancel signal to the running agent.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/model list</code></td>\n<td>Numbered list of available models with ✅ current selection.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/model set &lt;name or number&gt;</code></td>\n<td>Switch model by exact name or list number.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/models</code></td>\n<td>Alias of <code>/model list</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/agent list</code></td>\n<td>Numbered list of available agents with ✅ current selection.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/agent set &lt;name or number&gt;</code></td>\n<td>Switch agent by exact name or list number.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/agents</code></td>\n<td>Alias of <code>/agent list</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><code>/model</code> and <code>/agent</code> commands require an active session — send a message first to start one. These work in both DMs and group chats, across all gateway platforms.</p>\n<h2>Rich Text (Post) Messages</h2>\n<p>Agent replies are sent as Feishu <strong>post</strong> (rich text) messages instead of plain text. This enables:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting</li>\n<li>Clickable hyperlinks</li>\n<li>Proper line breaks and paragraph structure</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Inline Markdown formatting (<code>**bold**</code>, <code>*italic*</code>, <code>`code`</code>, <code>~~strike~~</code>) is stripped to plain text because Feishu's post format does not support inline styles.</p>\n<h2>Image &amp; File Attachments</h2>\n<p>The gateway downloads and forwards image and text file attachments to the AI agent, matching Discord's attachment handling.</p>\n<p><strong>Supported message types:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Feishu msg_type</th>\n<th>Handling</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>text</code></td>\n<td>Text extracted, forwarded as prompt</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td>Image downloaded, resized (max 1200px), JPEG compressed, stored to <code>~/.openab/media/inbound/&lt;uuid&gt;</code> → <code>ContentBlock::Image</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>file</code></td>\n<td>Text files only (<code>.txt</code>, <code>.py</code>, <code>.rs</code>, <code>.md</code>, <code>.json</code>, etc., max 512KB). Non-text files (<code>.pdf</code>, <code>.zip</code>, etc.) are silently ignored.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>audio</code></td>\n<td>Voice message downloaded (opus/ogg, max 25MB), stored to filesystem, forwarded to core. If <code>[stt]</code> is enabled, core transcribes via Whisper API and injects <code>[Voice message transcript]: ...</code> into the prompt. If STT is disabled or fails, the message is silently skipped.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>post</code></td>\n<td>Rich text: text nodes extracted as prompt, <code>img</code> nodes downloaded as image attachments. This is the format Feishu uses when @mention + paste image in a group.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Group chat limitation:</strong> Feishu does not allow @mention and image upload in the same message. However, @mention + paste (Ctrl+V) an image works — Feishu sends this as a <code>post</code> message containing both the mention and the image. Direct image upload (via the attachment button) cannot include @mention, so the bot will not respond in groups.</p>\n<p><strong>Processing pipeline:</strong> Gateway downloads media using <code>GET /im/v1/messages/{message_id}/resources/{key}?type=image</code> with <code>tenant_access_token</code>, resizes to max 1200px, compresses to JPEG (quality 75), and stores to <code>~/.openab/media/inbound/&lt;uuid&gt;</code>. The file path is passed in <code>GatewayEvent.content.attachments[].path</code>. OAB core reads the file directly from disk and converts to <code>ContentBlock::Image</code> or <code>ContentBlock::Text</code> for the AI agent.</p>\n<h2>Streaming (Typewriter)</h2>\n<p>Agent replies stream incrementally — a placeholder message appears immediately, then updates every ~1.5 seconds as the agent generates content. This matches Discord's streaming behavior.</p>\n<p>To enable streaming, set <code>streaming = true</code> in the gateway config:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[gateway]\nurl = &quot;ws://127.0.0.1:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;feishu&quot;\nstreaming = true\n</code></pre>\n<p>The gateway platform must support message editing (Feishu/Lark do). Platforms that don't support editing should leave <code>streaming = false</code> (default).</p>\n<h2>Card Streaming</h2>\n<p>By default (<code>FEISHU_CARD_STREAMING_MODE=auto</code>), streaming replies render as\n<strong>interactive CardKit cards</strong> when the content warrants it. Cards have no\n20-edit cap (errcode 230072) and render markdown — including <strong>tables</strong> and code\nblocks — natively, which a <code>post</code> message cannot.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mode</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>auto</code> (default)</td>\n<td>Short replies stay as a <code>post</code> (native reply UI); long replies, or any reply containing a code fence or a markdown table, promote to a card.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>card</code></td>\n<td>Every reply is sent as a card from the first message.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>post</code></td>\n<td>Card streaming disabled — post-only behavior (the kill-switch).</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Notes:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Auto promotion is one-way</strong>: a reply starts as a post and, once promoted,\nstays a card. Promotion deletes the post placeholder (shown as &quot;message\nrecalled&quot; in Feishu) and re-sends as a card. In <code>card</code> mode the first reply is\na card from the start, so there is no placeholder and no recall.</li>\n<li><strong>Finalize</strong>: after ~<code>FEISHU_CARD_IDLE_FINALIZE_MS</code> ms with no further edits,\nthe card is rebuilt as a static card so the typewriter cursor settles and the\nmarkdown re-renders cleanly.</li>\n<li><strong>Fallback</strong>: if a card API call fails and <code>FEISHU_CARD_FALLBACK_TO_POST</code> is\n<code>true</code> (default), the gateway falls back to the post path (with the edit-cap\nrecovery), so a reply is never lost.</li>\n<li><strong>Tables wrapped in a code fence</strong>: agents sometimes wrap a markdown table in a\nbare ``` fence for monospace alignment in environments that don't render\ntables. On the card path the gateway unwraps a fence whose body is exactly one\ntable so it renders as a native table.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Thread (Topic) Replies</h2>\n<p>When a user replies to a bot message in a group chat, Feishu creates a thread (topic). The bot replies within the same thread, and each thread gets its own independent session.</p>\n<p>To start a threaded conversation: reply to any bot message in a group chat (long-press or hover → Reply). The bot's response will appear in the same thread. Subsequent messages in the thread still require @mention (same as group chat).</p>\n<p><strong>How it works:</strong> Feishu reply events include a <code>root_id</code> (the original message that started the thread). The gateway uses this as <code>thread_id</code> for session isolation. Replies are sent via <code>POST /im/v1/messages/{root_id}/reply</code> to stay in the thread.</p>\n<p><strong>Limitation:</strong> Messages sent directly in the Feishu thread panel (not via the &quot;Reply&quot; action) do not include <code>root_id</code> and will be treated as regular group messages. Use the &quot;Reply&quot; action to ensure thread context is preserved.</p>\n<p>Streaming (typewriter) mode works in threads — edits target the same message regardless of thread context.</p>\n<h2>Agent-Controlled Reply-To</h2>\n<p>Agents can reply to a specific message using the <code>[[reply_to:message_id]]</code> output directive (see <a href=\"/openab/output-directives\">docs/output-directives.md</a>). The gateway sends the reply via Feishu's native Reply API, showing a quote reference in the UI.</p>\n<pre><code>Agent output:\n  [[reply_to:om_xxx]]\n  This is my reply to that specific message.\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>How agents get message IDs:</strong> Every incoming message includes <code>message_id</code> in the <code>SenderContext</code> injected into the agent prompt. Agents can store and reference these IDs to reply to specific messages.</p>\n<p><strong>Fallback:</strong> If the specified message ID is invalid or the Reply API fails, the gateway automatically falls back to a plain send (no quote).</p>\n<p><strong>Use case:</strong> In multi-bot threads, each bot can reply to a different message, creating clear visual conversation threads within a Feishu thread.</p>\n<h2>Bot-to-Bot Collaboration (Gateway-Side Only)</h2>\n<p>The gateway adapter includes bot identification and filtering scaffolding (<code>AllowBots</code> enum, <code>FEISHU_TRUSTED_BOT_IDS</code>, <code>FEISHU_MAX_BOT_TURNS</code> with human-reset safety valve), matching Discord's <code>allow_bot_messages</code> design.</p>\n<p>Bot identification requires explicit configuration via <code>FEISHU_TRUSTED_BOT_IDS</code> because Feishu marks other bots as <code>sender_type=&quot;user&quot;</code> — they cannot be identified from the event alone.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Not yet functional.</strong> Two blockers remain:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Feishu platform limitation:</strong> Feishu does not deliver bot-sent messages to other bots' WebSocket connections.</li>\n<li><strong>OAB core limitation:</strong> <code>src/gateway.rs</code> unconditionally drops <code>is_bot</code> events before they reach the router. When blocker 1 is lifted, the core guard must become adapter-aware to let gateway-filtered bot events through.</li>\n</ol>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Problem</th>\n<th>Fix</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot doesn't respond</td>\n<td>Check <code>FEISHU_APP_ID</code>/<code>FEISHU_APP_SECRET</code> are correct. Check gateway logs for token errors.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot doesn't respond in groups</td>\n<td>Ensure bot is @mentioned, or set <code>requireMention: false</code>. Check <code>botUsername</code> matches bot's <code>open_id</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>WebSocket keeps reconnecting</td>\n<td>Check event subscription is set to <strong>Long Connection</strong> mode. Check app is published and approved.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Webhook verification fails</td>\n<td>Ensure <code>verificationToken</code> and <code>encryptKey</code> match Feishu app config.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Messages from Lark (international)</td>\n<td>Set <code>domain: &quot;lark&quot;</code> to use <code>open.larksuite.com</code> API endpoints.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Feishu / Lark"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "gemini",
      "html": "<h1>Gemini CLI</h1>\n<p>Gemini CLI supports ACP natively via the <code>--acp</code> flag — no adapter needed.</p>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.gemini -t openab-gemini:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<p>The image installs <code>@google/gemini-cli</code> globally via npm.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.gemini.discord.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.gemini.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.gemini.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.gemini.command=gemini \\\n  --set agents.gemini.args='{--acp}' \\\n  --set agents.gemini.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Set <code>agents.kiro.enabled=false</code> to disable the default Kiro agent.</p>\n<p>(Optional) <code>agents.gemini.args='{--acp}'</code> could be modified as <code>{--model,gemini-3-pro-preview,--acp}</code> if specific model is required. Otherwise, the default value will be 'Auto (Gemini 3)'.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-gemini</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-gemini</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-gemini</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-gemini</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.gemini.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-gemini\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Manual config.toml</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command and args default from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;gemini --acp&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\nenv = { GEMINI_API_KEY = &quot;${GEMINI_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Gemini supports Google OAuth or an API key:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>API key</strong>: Set <code>GEMINI_API_KEY</code> environment variable</li>\n<li><strong>OAuth</strong>: Run Google OAuth flow inside the pod</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Gemini CLI"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "gh-auth-device-flow",
