      "html": "<h1>GitHub CLI Authentication in Agent Environments</h1>\n<p>How to authenticate <code>gh</code> (GitHub CLI) when the agent runs in a headless container and the user may be on mobile.</p>\n<h2>Why <code>gh</code> auth matters</h2>\n<p><code>gh</code> is one of the most common tools agents use to interact with GitHub — reviewing PRs, creating issues, commenting, approving, merging, etc. Before the agent can do any of this, <code>gh</code> must be authenticated.</p>\n<h2>Challenges</h2>\n<p>This isn't a typical <code>gh login</code> scenario. Three things make it tricky:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>The agent runs in a K8s pod with no browser</strong> — <code>gh auth login --web</code> can't open a browser, so device flow (code + URL) is the only option</li>\n<li><strong>The user might be on mobile, not at a desktop</strong> — they're chatting via Discord on their phone, so the agent must send the URL and code as a clickable message</li>\n<li><strong>The user authorizes on their phone</strong> — they tap the link, enter the code in mobile Safari/Chrome, and the agent's background process picks up the token automatically</li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code>┌───────────┐  &quot;review PR #108&quot;  ┌───────────┐  gh pr view  ┌───────────┐\n│  Discord   │──────────────────►│  OpenAB    │────────────►│  GitHub   │\n│  User      │                   │  + Agent   │◄────────────│  API      │\n└───────────┘                    └─────┬─────┘  401 🚫      └───────────┘\n                                       │\n                                       │ needs gh auth login first!\n                                       ▼\n                                 ┌───────────┐  device flow  ┌───────────┐\n                                 │  Agent     │─────────────►│  GitHub   │\n                                 │  (nohup)   │  code+URL    │  /login/  │\n                                 └─────┬─────┘◄─────────────│  device   │\n                                       │                     └─────┬─────┘\n                                       │ sends code+URL            │\n                                       ▼                           │\n                                 ┌───────────┐  authorize    ┌─────▼─────┐\n                                 │  Discord   │─────────────►│  Browser  │\n                                 │  User      │  enters code │  (mobile) │\n                                 └───────────┘               └───────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h2>The problem with naive approaches</h2>\n<p><code>gh auth login --web</code> uses device flow: it prints a one-time code + URL, then polls GitHub until the user authorizes. In an agent environment the shell is synchronous — it blocks until the command finishes:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Approach</th>\n<th>What happens</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Run directly</td>\n<td>Blocks forever. User never sees the code.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout N gh auth login -w</code></td>\n<td>Code appears only after timeout kills the process — token is never saved.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Solution: <code>nohup</code> + background + read log</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">nohup gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https -p https -w &gt; /tmp/gh-login.log 2&gt;&amp;1 &amp;\nsleep 3 &amp;&amp; cat /tmp/gh-login.log\n</code></pre>\n<p>How it works:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>nohup ... &amp;</code> runs <code>gh</code> in the background so the shell returns immediately</li>\n<li><code>sleep 3 &amp;&amp; cat</code> reads the log after <code>gh</code> has printed the code + URL</li>\n<li>The agent sends the code + URL to the user (via Discord)</li>\n<li>The user opens the link (even on mobile), enters the code</li>\n<li><code>gh</code> detects the authorization and saves the token</li>\n<li>Done — <code>gh auth status</code> confirms login</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Verify</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh auth status\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Enable raw <code>git</code> operations</h2>\n<p><code>gh auth status</code> only proves that GitHub CLI can call the GitHub API. It does\nnot guarantee that raw Git commands can clone or fetch private repositories.\nMany coding agents call <code>git clone</code>, <code>git fetch</code>, or <code>git ls-remote</code> directly.\nIn a headless pod, raw Git cannot prompt for a username/password, so private\nrepo access can fail with:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address\n</code></pre>\n<p>After <code>gh auth login</code> succeeds, wire Git to use the GitHub CLI credential\nhelper:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then verify both layers:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh auth status --hostname github.com\ngit config --global --get-all credential.https://github.com.helper\ngit ls-remote https://github.com/OWNER/PRIVATE_REPO HEAD\n</code></pre>\n<p>Expected signal:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>gh auth status</code> shows an active GitHub account.</li>\n<li><code>git config</code> includes <code>gh auth git-credential</code>.</li>\n<li><code>git ls-remote</code> returns a commit hash for <code>HEAD</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>If <code>gh auth status</code> passes but <code>git ls-remote</code> fails, run\n<code>gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com</code> again. This is especially important\nfor Codex/ACP review workflows that need to fetch private forks or branches.</p>\n<h2>Steering / prompt snippet (Kiro CLI only)</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> This section applies only to <a href=\"https://kiro.dev\">Kiro CLI</a> agents. Other agent backends (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) have their own prompt/config mechanisms.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>To make your Kiro agent always handle <code>gh login</code> correctly, create <code>~/.kiro/steering/gh.md</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">mkdir -p ~/.kiro/steering\ncat &gt; ~/.kiro/steering/gh.md &lt;&lt; 'EOF'\n# GitHub CLI\n\n## Device Flow Login\n\nWhen asked to &quot;gh login&quot;, always use nohup + background + read log:\n\n```bash\nnohup gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https -p https -w &gt; /tmp/gh-login.log 2&gt;&amp;1 &amp;\nsleep 3 &amp;&amp; cat /tmp/gh-login.log\n</code></pre>\n<p>Never use <code>timeout</code>. The shell tool is synchronous — it blocks until the command finishes, so stdout won't be visible until then. <code>nohup</code> runs it in the background, <code>sleep 3 &amp;&amp; cat</code> grabs the code immediately.\nEOF</p>\n<pre><code>\nKiro CLI automatically picks up `~/.kiro/steering/*.md` files as persistent context, so the agent will remember this across all sessions.\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Auth device flow"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "github-token-setup",
      "html": "<h1>GitHub Token Setup for Agents</h1>\n<p>Step-by-step guide to give your agent secure access to GitHub via <code>gh</code> CLI.</p>\n<h2>Overview</h2>\n<p>Agents sometimes need to interact with GitHub — push branches, open PRs, comment on issues. The recommended approach is to store a GitHub fine-grained personal access token in a Kubernetes secret and inject it via the Helm chart's <code>envFrom</code>.</p>\n<h2>1. Create a Fine-Grained Personal Access Token</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <a href=\"https://github.com/settings/tokens?type=beta\">GitHub Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens</a></li>\n<li>Click <strong>Generate new token</strong></li>\n<li>Configure:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Token name</strong>: e.g. <code>openab-masami</code></li>\n<li><strong>Expiration</strong>: set a reasonable expiry (e.g. 90 days)</li>\n<li><strong>Repository access</strong>: select only the repos the agent needs</li>\n<li><strong>Permissions</strong>:\n<ul>\n<li>Contents: Read and write (push branches)</li>\n<li>Pull requests: Read and write (create/comment on PRs)</li>\n<li>Issues: Read and write (comment on issues)</li>\n<li>Workflows: Read and write (if the agent needs to modify workflows)</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Generate token</strong> and copy it immediately</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>2. Store the Token in a Kubernetes Secret</h2>\n<p>Create a dedicated secret for the GitHub token:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl create secret generic gh-token-secret \\\n  --from-literal=gh-token=&quot;&lt;YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>3. Inject via Helm Chart</h2>\n<p>Use <code>envFrom</code> in your Helm values to inject the token as <code>GH_TOKEN</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># values.yaml\nenvFrom:\n  - secretRef:\n      name: gh-token-secret\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Recommended</strong>: Use <code>envFrom</code> with a separate secret so the token doesn't appear in shell history or Helm release metadata.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>As a fallback, you can pass it directly during install — but note this exposes the token in shell history:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set env.GH_TOKEN=&quot;&lt;YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>The <code>gh</code> CLI automatically picks up <code>GH_TOKEN</code> — no additional auth setup needed.</p>\n<h2>4. Install <code>gh</code> CLI in the Agent Container</h2>\n<p>Ensure <code>gh</code> is available in your Dockerfile. Note: <code>gh</code> is not in the default Debian repos — you need to add the GitHub CLI apt repository first:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-dockerfile\">RUN apt-get update &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y curl gpg &amp;&amp; \\\n    curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \\\n      | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg &amp;&amp; \\\n    echo &quot;deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main&quot; \\\n      | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list &gt; /dev/null &amp;&amp; \\\n    apt-get update &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y gh &amp;&amp; \\\n    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n</code></pre>\n<p>See the <a href=\"https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/docs/install_linux.md\">official install docs</a> for other methods.</p>\n<h2>5. Verify</h2>\n<p>Once the agent pod is running:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Check auth status\ngh auth status\n\n# Should show:\n# ✓ Logged in to github.com as your-agent-user (GH_TOKEN)\n</code></pre>\n<p>The agent can now run <code>gh</code> commands: <code>gh pr create</code>, <code>gh issue comment</code>, <code>gh repo fork</code>, etc.</p>\n<h2>Security Best Practices</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Fine-grained tokens only</strong> — avoid classic tokens; fine-grained tokens limit access to specific repos and permissions</li>\n<li><strong>Least privilege</strong> — only grant the permissions the agent actually needs</li>\n<li><strong>Set expiration</strong> — rotate tokens regularly; don't use non-expiring tokens</li>\n<li><strong>One token per agent</strong> — if you run multiple agents, give each its own token with its own GitHub account</li>\n<li><strong>Never log tokens</strong> — ensure your agent doesn't echo <code>$GH_TOKEN</code> in responses or logs</li>\n<li><strong>Dedicated GitHub account</strong> — create a bot account (e.g. <code>masami-agent</code>) rather than using a personal account</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>gh auth status</code> fails</strong> — check that <code>GH_TOKEN</code> env var is set: <code>echo ${GH_TOKEN:+exists}</code></li>\n<li><strong>Permission denied on push</strong> — the token's repo access doesn't include the target repo, or write permission is missing</li>\n<li><strong>403 on PR create</strong> — the token needs Pull requests: Read and write permission</li>\n<li><strong>Token expired</strong> — generate a new one and update the k8s secret</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Token setup"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "github-webhook-integration",
      "html": "<h1>GitHub Webhook to Discord — Agent Trigger Pattern</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> This documents a v1 workaround using GitHub Actions + Discord webhooks.\nThe target architecture (v2+) is the <a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway\">Custom Gateway</a> with a\nnative GitHub adapter, which provides direct webhook reception, HMAC validation,\nand richer event context. See <a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway#5-what-this-enables-beyond-chat\">ADR: Custom Gateway — Section 5</a> for the GitHub integration example.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Overview</h2>\n<p>OpenAB only listens to Discord events. It does not accept external webhooks directly. To trigger agents from GitHub events (PR, Issue, etc.), we route through Discord as the single entry point.</p>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>GitHub (PR/Issue event)\n  → GitHub Actions workflow\n    → Discord Webhook (formatted message to channel)\n      → OpenAB detects message\n        → Routes to target agent\n          → Agent performs action (review, comment, notify)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Setup</h2>\n<h3>1. Discord Webhook</h3>\n<p>Create a webhook in your Discord server for the target channel/topic:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook</li>\n<li>Copy the webhook URL</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>2. GitHub Secret</h3>\n<p>Add the webhook URL as a repository secret:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions</li>\n<li>Name: <code>DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL</code></li>\n<li>Value: the webhook URL from step 1</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3. GitHub Actions Workflow</h3>\n<p>Add <code>.github/workflows/notify-discord.yml</code> to your repo:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">name: Notify Discord\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    types: [opened, reopened]\n  issues:\n    types: [opened]\n\njobs:\n  notify:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - name: Send to Discord\n        env:\n          DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL }}\n        run: |\n          if [ &quot;${{ github.event_name }}&quot; = &quot;pull_request&quot; ]; then\n            TITLE=&quot;${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}&quot;\n            URL=&quot;${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}&quot;\n            AUTHOR=&quot;${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}&quot;\n            NUM=&quot;${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}&quot;\n            TYPE=&quot;pr_opened&quot;\n            LABEL=&quot;PR #${NUM}&quot;\n          else\n            TITLE=&quot;${{ github.event.issue.title }}&quot;\n            URL=&quot;${{ github.event.issue.html_url }}&quot;\n            AUTHOR=&quot;${{ github.event.issue.user.login }}&quot;\n            NUM=&quot;${{ github.event.issue.number }}&quot;\n            TYPE=&quot;issue_opened&quot;\n            LABEL=&quot;Issue #${NUM}&quot;\n          fi\n\n          MSG=&quot;[GH-EVENT] repo:${{ github.repository }} action:${TYPE} ${LABEL}&quot;\n          MSG=&quot;${MSG}\\n**${TITLE}**\\nby ${AUTHOR}\\n${URL}&quot;\n          PAYLOAD=$(printf '%s' &quot;$MSG&quot; | jq -Rs '{content: .}')\n          curl -s -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; -d &quot;$PAYLOAD&quot; &quot;$DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Message Format Convention</h2>\n<p>Messages use a structured prefix so OpenAB can identify GitHub events:</p>\n<pre><code>[GH-EVENT] repo:{owner/repo} action:{event_type} {PR/Issue} #{number}\n**{title}**\nby {author}\n{url}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<pre><code>[GH-EVENT] repo:openabdev/openab action:pr_opened PR #42\n**Add webhook integration docs**\nby obrutjack\nhttps://github.com/openabdev/openab/pull/42\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Open Questions</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Bot message handling</strong>: Does OpenAB currently ignore messages from bots/webhooks? If so, webhook sources need to be allowlisted. Note: OpenAB uses <code>allowed_channels</code> and <code>allowed_users</code> in <code>config.toml</code> for filtering — webhook messages come from a bot user, so the bot's user ID may need to be added to <code>allowed_users</code>, or the filtering logic would need a <code>[GH-EVENT]</code> prefix check.</li>\n<li><strong>Routing</strong>: How does OpenAB determine which agent handles a <code>[GH-EVENT]</code> message?</li>\n<li><strong>Loop prevention</strong>: If an agent replies in the same channel, could it re-trigger events? Recommend using a dedicated channel and filtering by <code>[GH-EVENT]</code> prefix only.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Best Practices</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use a dedicated channel or thread for webhook events</li>\n<li>Stick to the <code>[GH-EVENT]</code> prefix convention for all GitHub-sourced messages</li>\n<li>Validate webhook sources on the Discord side (restrict channel permissions)</li>\n<li>Avoid agents posting back to the same webhook channel to prevent loops</li>\n<li>Start minimal (PR + Issue notifications), expand as needed</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Future Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Extend pattern to other sources: Jira, Slack, PagerDuty, etc.</li>\n<li>Agent-to-agent invocation during review workflows</li>\n<li>Event filtering and deduplication at the OpenAB level</li>\n<li>Richer payloads using Discord embeds instead of plain text</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Webhook integration"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "google-chat",
      "html": "<h1>Google Chat Setup</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Unified Mode (v0.9.0+):</strong> The OAB binary now embeds the google-chat adapter directly. Set <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true</code> as an env var — no separate gateway container or <code>[gateway]</code> config needed. See <a href=\"/openab/telegram#unified-mode-recommended\">Telegram docs</a> for the pattern.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Unified Config (Kiro + google-chat)</h3>\n<p><strong>Minimal:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Recommended:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;compact&quot;\n\n[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Set <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true</code> (and related platform env vars) on the container. No <code>[gateway]</code> needed.</p>\n<p>Connect a Google Chat app to OpenAB via the Custom Gateway.</p>\n<pre><code>Google Chat ──POST──▶ Gateway (:8080) ◀──WebSocket── OAB Pod\n                                          (OAB connects out)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>A Google Workspace (Business or Enterprise) account</strong> — required by Google to configure the Chat API. Regular <code>@gmail.com</code> consumer accounts cannot create Google Chat apps. Workspace Individual or Business Starter is the cheapest qualifying tier. See <a href=\"https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/configure-chat-api\">Configure the Google Chat API</a>.</li>\n<li>A running OAB instance (with kiro-cli or any ACP agent authenticated)</li>\n<li>The Custom Gateway deployed (<a href=\"../gateway/README.md\">gateway/README.md</a>)</li>\n<li>A Google Cloud project with the Google Chat API enabled</li>\n<li>A Google Cloud Service Account (JSON key recommended; no special IAM roles needed)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>1. Create a Google Chat App</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to the <a href=\"https://console.cloud.google.com/\">Google Cloud Console</a> and create or select a project.</li>\n<li>Enable the <strong>Google Chat API</strong> under <strong>APIs &amp; Services → Library</strong>.</li>\n<li>Go to <strong>APIs &amp; Services → Google Chat API → Configuration</strong>:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>App name</strong>: your bot name (e.g. &quot;OpenAB&quot;)</li>\n<li><strong>Avatar URL</strong>: any public image URL</li>\n<li><strong>Description</strong>: anything</li>\n<li><strong>Interactive features</strong>: Enable</li>\n<li><strong>Connection settings</strong>: select <strong>App URL</strong> and enter your gateway's webhook URL:\n<pre><code>https://your-gateway-host/webhook/googlechat\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Visibility</strong>: select the users or domains that can use the bot</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>2. Create a Service Account</h2>\n<p>Google Chat uses a service account to authenticate outbound API calls (bot replies).</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>IAM &amp; Admin → Service Accounts</strong> → <strong>Create Service Account</strong>.</li>\n<li>Name it (e.g. <code>openab-google-chat</code>) and grant it no special roles.</li>\n<li>After creation, click the service account → <strong>Keys</strong> → <strong>Add Key</strong> → <strong>Create New Key</strong> → JSON.</li>\n<li>Save the downloaded JSON file securely.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>3. Configure the Gateway</h2>\n<p>The gateway supports two authentication methods for sending replies:</p>\n<h3>Option A: Service Account Key (recommended — auto-refresh)</h3>\n<p>Pass the service account JSON key directly. The gateway handles JWT signing and token refresh automatically.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Via JSON string\ndocker run -d --name openab-gateway \\\n  -e GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true \\\n  -e GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_JSON='{&quot;type&quot;:&quot;service_account&quot;,&quot;client_email&quot;:&quot;...&quot;,&quot;private_key&quot;:&quot;...&quot;}' \\\n  -e GATEWAY_WS_TOKEN=&quot;your-ws-auth-token&quot; \\\n  -p 8080:8080 \\\n  ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:latest\n\n# Via file path\ndocker run -d --name openab-gateway \\\n  -e GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true \\\n  -e GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_FILE=&quot;/secrets/service-account.json&quot; \\\n  -v /path/to/service-account.json:/secrets/service-account.json:ro \\\n  -e GATEWAY_WS_TOKEN=&quot;your-ws-auth-token&quot; \\\n  -p 8080:8080 \\\n  ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:latest\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Option B: Static Access Token (for quick testing)</h3>\n<p>Generate a token manually. It expires after 1 hour.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker run -d --name openab-gateway \\\n  -e GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true \\\n  -e GOOGLE_CHAT_ACCESS_TOKEN=&quot;ya29.c...&quot; \\\n  -e GATEWAY_WS_TOKEN=&quot;your-ws-auth-token&quot; \\\n  -p 8080:8080 \\\n  ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:latest\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Local development</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true\nexport GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_FILE=&quot;/path/to/service-account.json&quot;\ncargo run --release\n</code></pre>\n<h2>4. Expose the Gateway (for local dev)</h2>\n<p>Google Chat requires a public HTTPS endpoint for webhooks.</p>\n<h3>Cloudflare Tunnel (quickest)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080\n# Copy the https://xxx.trycloudflare.com URL\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then update the webhook URL in the Google Chat API Configuration page:</p>\n<pre><code>https://xxx.trycloudflare.com/webhook/googlechat\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Reverse proxy (production)</h3>\n<p>Use nginx, Caddy, or a cloud load balancer with TLS termination pointing to the gateway's <code>:8080</code>.</p>\n<h2>5. Configure OAB</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[gateway]\nurl = &quot;ws://openab-gateway:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;googlechat&quot;\nallow_all_channels = true\nallow_all_users = true\n\n[agent]\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Features</h2>\n<h3>Supported</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>DM chat</strong> — send a direct message to the bot, get an AI agent response</li>\n<li><strong>Space chat</strong> — add the bot to a Google Chat Space, @mention it to start a conversation</li>\n<li><strong>Thread replies</strong> — in Spaces, bot replies are posted in the same thread as the user's message (note: @mention is required for every message in a Space, even within a thread — this is a Google Chat platform limitation)</li>\n<li><strong><code>argument_text</code> extraction</strong> — strips the @mention prefix to get the clean user message</li>\n<li><strong>Bot message filtering</strong> — bot messages (<code>user_type: &quot;BOT&quot;</code>) are filtered at the gateway level</li>\n<li><strong>Message splitting</strong> — long replies (&gt;4096 chars) are automatically split at newline/space boundaries</li>\n<li><strong>Token auto-refresh</strong> — service account JWT tokens are refreshed automatically before expiry</li>\n<li><strong>Markdown formatting</strong> — replies are converted via <code>markdown_to_gchat</code> to Google Chat's native formatting:\n<ul>\n<li>Bold: <code>**text**</code> / <code>__text__</code> → <code>*text*</code></li>\n<li>Italic: <code>*text*</code> → <code>_text_</code> (single-underscore <code>_text_</code> passes through)</li>\n<li>Strikethrough: <code>~~text~~</code> → <code>~text~</code></li>\n<li>Headings: <code># / ## / ###</code> → <code>*text*</code> (rendered as bold)</li>\n<li>Links: <code>[text](url)</code> → <code>&lt;url|text&gt;</code></li>\n<li>Inline code, fenced code blocks: pass through unchanged</li>\n<li>Tables and other unsupported syntax pass through as-is</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Streaming (edit_message)</strong> — when OAB streaming is enabled, the bot edits its initial reply in-place as tokens arrive (typewriter effect)</li>\n<li><strong>Inbound attachments</strong> — image, text file, and audio attachments are downloaded via Google Chat Media API and stored to <code>~/.openab/media/inbound/&lt;uuid&gt;</code> (colocate filesystem store):\n<ul>\n<li>Images: resized to ≤1200px JPEG (q75); GIFs preserved. Max 10 MB.</li>\n<li>Text files: only known text extensions (<code>.txt</code>, <code>.md</code>, <code>.json</code>, <code>.py</code>, <code>.rs</code>, etc.). Max 512 KB.</li>\n<li>Audio: forwarded as-is for STT processing by core. Max 25 MB.</li>\n<li>Drive-sourced attachments are skipped (require separate Drive API integration).</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Not Supported</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Reactions</strong> — Google Chat API does not support message reactions on behalf of bots</li>\n<li><strong>Outbound attachments</strong> — bot cannot send image/file attachments back to the user yet</li>\n<li><strong>Drive-linked attachments</strong> — only <code>UPLOADED_CONTENT</code> source is handled; <code>DRIVE_FILE</code> source skipped</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Environment Variables (Gateway)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Set to <code>true</code> or <code>1</code> to enable the adapter</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_AUDIENCE</code></td>\n<td>Recommended</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>JWT audience for webhook verification — set to your full webhook URL (e.g. <code>https://your-domain.com/webhook/googlechat</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_JSON</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Service account key JSON string (enables auto-refresh)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_FILE</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Path to service account key JSON file (alternative to <code>SA_KEY_JSON</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_ACCESS_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Static OAuth2 access token (fallback, expires in 1 hour)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>/webhook/googlechat</code></td>\n<td>Webhook endpoint path</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Security: Webhook Verification</h2>\n<p>Google Chat signs every webhook request with a JWT Bearer token. The gateway verifies this token to ensure requests come from Google Chat specifically (not just any Google service).</p>\n<p><strong>Setup:</strong></p>\n<p>In the Google Chat API <strong>Configuration</strong> page, leave <strong>Authentication Audience</strong> at its default — <strong>HTTP Endpoint URL</strong>. Then set <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_AUDIENCE</code> to your full webhook URL:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export GOOGLE_CHAT_AUDIENCE=&quot;https://your-domain.com/webhook/googlechat&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>The gateway will:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Reject requests without a valid <code>Authorization: Bearer &lt;jwt&gt;</code> header</li>\n<li>Verify the JWT signature against Google's public keys (JWKS, cached for 1 hour)</li>\n<li>Validate <code>iss == https://accounts.google.com</code> and <code>aud</code> matches the configured webhook URL</li>\n<li>Validate <code>email</code> ends with <code>@gcp-sa-gsuiteaddons.iam.gserviceaccount.com</code> (proves the token came from Google Chat, not another Google service)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>If <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_AUDIENCE</code> is not set, the gateway logs a warning and accepts all requests (insecure — for local development only).</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Only the &quot;HTTP Endpoint URL&quot; Authentication Audience mode is supported. The &quot;Project Number&quot; mode uses a different JWT flow that this adapter does not implement.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Problem</th>\n<th>Fix</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot doesn't respond</td>\n<td>Check <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_ENABLED=true</code> is set. Check gateway logs for parse errors.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>&quot;not responding&quot; in Google Chat</td>\n<td>Ensure the gateway returns a <code>200</code> with <code>{}</code> body. Check gateway is reachable via the webhook URL.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Replies not sent</td>\n<td>Use <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_JSON</code> or <code>GOOGLE_CHAT_SA_KEY_FILE</code> for auto-refresh. If using static token, check it hasn't expired (1-hour TTL).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Replies not in thread</td>\n<td>Verify the thread name is passed correctly. The gateway appends <code>?messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD</code> automatically.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot responds to its own messages</td>\n<td>Bot messages have <code>user_type: &quot;BOT&quot;</code> and are filtered out automatically.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Webhook returns 400</td>\n<td>Check the Google Chat API configuration uses <strong>App URL</strong> (not Dialogflow or Cloud Pub/Sub). The webhook expects the v2 envelope format with a <code>chat</code> wrapper.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/api/reference/rest\">Google Chat API Documentation</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/overview\">Google Chat App Setup</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/authenticate-authorize-chat-app\">Service Account Authentication</a></li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Google Chat Setup"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "grok",
      "html": "<h1>Grok Build (xAI)</h1>\n<p><a href=\"https://x.ai/news/grok-build-cli\">Grok Build</a> is xAI's official coding agent CLI. It speaks ACP natively via <code>grok agent stdio</code> — no wrapper required.</p>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.grok -t openab-grok:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<p>The image pulls a pinned <code>grok</code> binary from xAI's public artifacts bucket and verifies its SHA256 checksum. Bump <code>GROK_VERSION</code>, <code>GROK_SHA256_AMD64</code>, and <code>GROK_SHA256_ARM64</code> in <code>Dockerfile.grok</code> to upgrade.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.grok.discord.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.grok.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.grok.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.grok.command=grok \\\n  --set-string 'agents.grok.args[0]=agent' \\\n  --set-string 'agents.grok.args[1]=stdio' \\\n  --set agents.grok.workingDir=/home/agent \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Set <code>agents.kiro.enabled=false</code> to disable the default Kiro agent.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-grok</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-grok</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-grok</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-grok</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.grok.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-grok\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Manual config.toml</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command and args default from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;grok agent stdio&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior:\n# args = [&quot;agent&quot;, &quot;stdio&quot;, &quot;--model&quot;, &quot;grok-4.3&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Grok Build supports three credential sources. Pick whichever fits your deployment.</p>\n<h3>Option A: API key (simplest, recommended for CI / bot deployments)</h3>\n<p>Set the environment variable in the pod / task definition:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export GROK_CODE_XAI_API_KEY=&quot;xai-...&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Get a key from <a href=\"https://console.x.ai/\">https://console.x.ai/</a>. No interactive login needed.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ <strong>Security</strong>: env vars listed under <code>[agent].env</code> are visible to the agent and can be leaked via prompt injection. Prefer mounting them via the platform's secret manager.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Option B: Device-code OAuth (for SuperGrok subscriptions)</h3>\n<p>If you want to use a SuperGrok subscription instead of pay-per-token API billing:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>The CLI prints a short code and URL — open the URL on any device, enter the code, approve. The token is stored at <code>~/.grok/auth.json</code> inside the container.</p>\n<p>This works in any headless environment (K8s exec, ECS exec, plain SSH) <strong>without port-forwarding</strong> — unlike loopback OAuth flows.</p>\n<h3>Option C: Enterprise deployment key</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export GROK_DEPLOYMENT_KEY=&quot;...&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>A deployment key takes precedence over <code>auth.json</code>. The CLI fetches managed config from <code>cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/deployment/config</code> on startup. Available to xAI enterprise customers; contact xAI sales for details.</p>\n<h2>Credential Persistence</h2>\n<p><code>grok login</code> stores OAuth credentials at <code>~/.grok/auth.json</code> and runtime config at <code>~/.grok/config.toml</code>. The OpenAB Helm chart's default persistence covers <code>workingDir</code> automatically (PVC mounted at <code>/home/agent</code>).</p>\n<p>If deploying manually, mount persistent storage at <code>/home/agent/.grok</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">volumes:\n  - name: grok-credentials\n    persistentVolumeClaim:\n      claimName: grok-credentials-pvc\nvolumeMounts:\n  - name: grok-credentials\n    mountPath: /home/agent/.grok\n</code></pre>\n<p>API-key-only deployments don't need persistence.</p>\n<h2>Model Selection</h2>\n<p>The default model is whichever Grok Build CLI selects (currently <code>grok-code-fast-1</code> for the free tier; <code>grok-4.3</code> family for SuperGrok). To override:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# Override args to select a specific model (command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND)\nargs = [&quot;agent&quot;, &quot;stdio&quot;, &quot;--model&quot;, &quot;grok-4.3&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>List available models inside the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- grok models\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Updating</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Inside the container (one-shot upgrade):\nkubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- grok update\n\n# Or rebuild the image with a new pinned version:\ndocker build -f Dockerfile.grok \\\n  --build-arg GROK_VERSION=0.1.220 \\\n  --build-arg GROK_SHA256_AMD64=... \\\n  --build-arg GROK_SHA256_ARM64=... \\\n  -t openab-grok:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Comparison with Hermes</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Property</th>\n<th><code>Dockerfile.grok</code></th>\n<th><code>Dockerfile.hermes</code></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Provider</td>\n<td>xAI Grok only</td>\n<td>xAI + 30 others via Nous gateway</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>ACP</td>\n<td>Native (<code>grok agent stdio</code>)</td>\n<td>Via <code>hermes-acp</code> wrapper</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Headless auth</td>\n<td>API key env or device-code</td>\n<td>Loopback OAuth (needs port-forward / ECS curl trick)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Supply chain</td>\n<td>xAI only</td>\n<td>xAI + Nous Research install script</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Image size</td>\n<td>Smaller (single static binary, no Python venv)</td>\n<td>Larger (Python + uv + ffmpeg)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Pick <code>Dockerfile.grok</code> if Grok is the only model you need. Pick <code>Dockerfile.hermes</code> if you want multi-provider switching or fallback chains.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Grok"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "helm-publishing",
      "html": "<h1>Helm Chart Publishing</h1>\n<p>OpenAB publishes the Helm chart to two channels automatically via the <code>Release Charts</code> workflow (<code>.github/workflows/release.yml</code>).</p>\n<h2>Channels</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Channel</th>\n<th>URL</th>\n<th>Install command</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>GitHub Pages</td>\n<td><code>https://openabdev.github.io/openab</code></td>\n<td><code>helm repo add openab https://openabdev.github.io/openab &amp;&amp; helm install openab openab/openab</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>OCI (GHCR)</td>\n<td><code>oci://ghcr.io/openabdev/charts/openab</code></td>\n<td><code>helm install openab oci://ghcr.io/openabdev/charts/openab</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>How it works</h2>\n<pre><code>charts/openab/Chart.yaml changed on main\n        │\n        ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────┐\n│  Release Charts workflow    │\n│  .github/workflows/         │\n│  release.yml                │\n│                             │\n│  1. helm package            │\n│  2. helm push → OCI (GHCR)  │\n│  3. cr upload → GH Release  │\n│  4. cr index → gh-pages     │\n│  5. Update release notes    │\n└─────────────────────────────┘\n        │\n        ▼\n  Both channels updated\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Trigger</h3>\n<p>The workflow runs when <code>charts/openab/Chart.yaml</code> is pushed to <code>main</code>. This happens automatically when the <code>Build &amp; Release</code> workflow merges a chart bump PR.</p>\n<h3>OCI Registry</h3>\n<p><code>helm push</code> publishes the packaged chart to <code>oci://ghcr.io/openabdev/charts</code>. The GHCR packages must be <strong>public</strong> (configured at org level) for unauthenticated pulls.</p>\n<h3>GitHub Pages</h3>\n<p>The <a href=\"https://github.com/helm/chart-releaser\"><code>chart-releaser</code></a> (<code>cr</code>) tool uploads the <code>.tgz</code> as a GitHub Release asset, then updates <code>index.yaml</code> on the <code>gh-pages</code> branch. GitHub Pages serves this as a standard Helm repository.</p>\n<h2>Version flow</h2>\n<pre><code>PR merged to main (src/ or Dockerfile changes)\n  → Build &amp; Release workflow\n    → Builds Docker images (all 4 variants)\n    → Creates chart bump PR (patch/minor/major)\n    → App token merges the PR\n      → Chart.yaml change triggers Release Charts\n        → Publishes to OCI + GitHub Pages\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Stable vs beta</h2>\n<p>The <code>Build &amp; Release</code> workflow accepts two inputs via <code>workflow_dispatch</code>:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Input</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>chart_bump</code></td>\n<td><code>patch</code>, <code>minor</code>, or <code>major</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>release</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code> for stable (e.g. <code>0.5.1</code>), omit for beta (e.g. <code>0.5.1-beta.34</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Push-triggered builds always produce beta versions. Use <code>workflow_dispatch</code> with <code>release=true</code> for stable releases.</p>\n<p>Note: Helm hides beta versions by default. Use <code>--devel</code> to see them:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm search repo openab/openab --devel --versions\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Helm Chart Publishing"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "hermes",
      "html": "<h1>Hermes Agent</h1>\n<p><a href=\"https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent\">Hermes Agent</a> by Nous Research supports ACP natively via the <code>hermes acp</code> subcommand (or the <code>hermes-acp</code> binary).</p>\n<p>Hermes acts as a multi-provider inference gateway — it handles OAuth token lifecycle, credential storage, and provider routing so OAB agents don't need to manage auth directly.</p>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.hermes -t openab-hermes:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<p>The image installs Hermes Agent via the official install script.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.hermes.discord.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.hermes.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.hermes.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.hermes.command=hermes-acp \\\n  --set agents.hermes.workingDir=/home/agent \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Set <code>agents.kiro.enabled=false</code> to disable the default Kiro agent.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-hermes</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-hermes</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-hermes</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-hermes</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.hermes.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-hermes\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Manual config.toml</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;hermes-acp&quot;\n# working_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;  # optional — defaults to $HOME\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>Hermes supports 30+ providers. Authenticate inside the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- hermes auth add xai-oauth    # xAI Grok (SuperGrok $30/mo)\nkubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- hermes auth add nous         # Nous Portal\nkubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- hermes model                 # Interactive provider picker\n</code></pre>\n<h3>xAI Grok OAuth (Recommended)</h3>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ <strong>Requires an active <a href=\"https://x.ai/grok\">SuperGrok paid subscription</a> ($30/mo).</strong> Auth will succeed without one, but the API silently returns empty responses — the bot appears to work but never replies.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>xAI Grok OAuth uses a loopback redirect flow — the callback listener binds <code>127.0.0.1:56121</code> inside the pod/container.</p>\n<h4>Option A: Kubernetes (port-forward)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Terminal 1: port-forward\nkubectl port-forward deployment/&lt;your-deployment&gt; 56121:56121\n\n# Terminal 2: run auth\nkubectl exec -it deployment/&lt;your-deployment&gt; -- hermes auth add xai-oauth --no-browser\n</code></pre>\n<ol>\n<li>Copy the printed authorize URL → open in your local browser</li>\n<li>Approve access on accounts.x.ai</li>\n<li>Browser redirects to <code>127.0.0.1:56121/callback</code> → port-forward delivers it to the pod</li>\n<li>Terminal shows <code>Added xai-oauth OAuth credential #1: &quot;xai-oauth-oauth-1&quot;</code></li>\n</ol>\n<h4>Option B: ECS / Remote (curl-the-callback)</h4>\n<p>ECS Fargate doesn't support port-forward. Use two exec sessions instead:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Terminal 1: start the auth listener\naws ecs execute-command --cluster openab --task &lt;task-id&gt; --container openab --interactive --command bash\nhermes auth add xai-oauth --no-browser\n# → prints authorize URL with &amp;state=XXXXX in it\n# → &quot;Waiting for callback on http://127.0.0.1:56121/callback&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Open the authorize URL in your browser and approve. The browser will redirect to\n<code>http://127.0.0.1:56121/callback?code=...</code> and fail (&quot;Could not establish connection&quot;).\n<strong>Copy the <code>code</code> value</strong> from the page or URL bar. The <code>state</code> value comes from the\nauthorize URL printed in Terminal 1.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Terminal 2: exec into the SAME container\naws ecs execute-command --cluster openab --task &lt;task-id&gt; --container openab --interactive --command bash\ncurl &quot;http://127.0.0.1:56121/callback?code=&lt;THE_CODE&gt;&amp;state=&lt;THE_STATE&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Terminal 1 should print:</p>\n<pre><code>Added xai-oauth OAuth credential #1: &quot;xai-oauth-oauth-1&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ The code expires in seconds — be fast. If you get <code>invalid_grant</code>, re-run <code>hermes auth add</code> and try again.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>After auth: set the default model</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">hermes config set model.provider xai-oauth\nhermes config set model.default grok-4.3\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Fix file ownership (important for exec-based auth)</h4>\n<p>When running auth/config commands via <code>kubectl exec</code> or ECS exec (which runs as root),\nfix ownership so the <code>agent</code> user can read the files:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">chown -R agent:agent /home/agent/.hermes/\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Providers That Don't Need Port-Forward</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Provider</th>\n<th>Auth Method</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Anthropic (Claude Pro/Max)</td>\n<td>Paste-the-code flow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT Plus/Pro)</td>\n<td>Device code flow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>MiniMax, Nous Portal</td>\n<td>Device code flow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>xAI Grok, Spotify</td>\n<td>Loopback OAuth (port-forward required)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Supported Providers (via OAuth)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Provider</th>\n<th>Auth Command</th>\n<th>Cost Model</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>xAI Grok</td>\n<td><code>hermes auth add xai-oauth</code></td>\n<td>SuperGrok subscription ($30/mo)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>OpenAI Codex</td>\n<td><code>hermes model</code> → OpenAI Codex</td>\n<td>ChatGPT subscription</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>GitHub Copilot</td>\n<td><code>hermes model</code> → GitHub Copilot</td>\n<td>Copilot subscription</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Google Gemini</td>\n<td><code>hermes model</code> → Google Gemini (OAuth)</td>\n<td>Free tier available</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Anthropic</td>\n<td><code>hermes model</code> → Anthropic</td>\n<td>Claude Max + extra credits</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Nous Portal</td>\n<td><code>hermes auth add nous</code></td>\n<td>Nous subscription</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Supported Providers (via API Key)</h3>\n<p>Any provider can also be configured with an API key via environment variables:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;hermes-acp&quot;\n# working_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;  # optional — defaults to $HOME\nenv = { XAI_API_KEY = &quot;${XAI_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Provider Switching</h2>\n<p>Switch providers without restarting the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it &lt;pod&gt; -- hermes model\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Credential Persistence</h2>\n<p>Hermes stores OAuth tokens in <code>~/.hermes/</code>. The OpenAB Helm chart's default persistence covers this automatically (PVC mounted at <code>workingDir</code>).</p>\n<p>If deploying manually (without the Helm chart), mount persistent storage at <code>/home/agent</code> or <code>/home/agent/.hermes</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">volumes:\n  - name: hermes-credentials\n    persistentVolumeClaim:\n      claimName: hermes-credentials-pvc\nvolumeMounts:\n  - name: hermes-credentials\n    mountPath: /home/agent/.hermes\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Advantages</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Cost</strong>: SuperGrok $30/mo flat rate vs pay-per-token API pricing</li>\n<li><strong>Multi-provider</strong>: 30+ providers accessible through one agent</li>\n<li><strong>Zero auth complexity</strong>: Hermes handles OAuth + token refresh</li>\n<li><strong>Multi-modal</strong>: TTS, image gen, video gen via the same OAuth token</li>\n<li><strong>Fallback chains</strong>: Auto-switch providers on failure</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Hermes"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "hooks",
      "html": "<h1>Lifecycle Hooks</h1>\n<p>OpenAB supports lifecycle hooks that run at specific points during the container lifecycle. All lifecycle phases are configured in <code>config.toml</code> under the <code>[hooks]</code> table.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Platform support:</strong> Lifecycle hooks are <strong>Unix-only</strong> (Linux/macOS). They rely on Unix symlinks (<code>pre_seed</code> tarball extraction) and POSIX shell scripts (<code>pre_boot</code>/<code>pre_shutdown</code>), and are only ever exercised inside Linux containers. If any hook (<code>pre_seed</code>, <code>pre_boot</code>, or <code>pre_shutdown</code>) is configured while running on <strong>Windows</strong>, OpenAB <strong>fails fast at startup</strong> rather than misbehaving silently. Remove the <code>[hooks.*]</code> config to run on Windows.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Lifecycle Order</h2>\n<pre><code>hooks.pre_seed → hooks.pre_boot → (agent running) → hooks.pre_shutdown\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>When</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Config</th>\n<th>Action Type</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_seed</code></td>\n<td>First — before <code>pre_boot</code></td>\n<td>Download &amp; extract S3 archives to seed the environment</td>\n<td><code>[hooks.pre_seed]</code></td>\n<td>Built-in S3 download + extract</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_boot</code></td>\n<td>After seed, before agent pool starts</td>\n<td>Run custom setup scripts before agent pool creation</td>\n<td><code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code></td>\n<td>User script</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_shutdown</code></td>\n<td>After pool stops, before exit</td>\n<td>Run custom cleanup scripts after pool shutdown</td>\n<td><code>[hooks.pre_shutdown]</code></td>\n<td>User script</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Pre-Seed Phase</h2>\n<p>The <code>pre_seed</code> phase runs <strong>before</strong> <code>pre_boot</code>. It downloads archives from S3 and extracts them into the agent's home directory (or a custom target). Supported formats: <code>.zip</code>, <code>.tar.gz</code>, and <code>.tgz</code> (auto-detected via magic bytes). This eliminates the need for users to install AWS CLI and write download scripts in <code>pre_boot</code>.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><code>pre-seed</code> is enabled by default. No feature flag needed.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_seed]\nsources = [\n  &quot;s3://my-bucket/base-env.tar.gz&quot;,\n  &quot;s3://my-bucket/shared-memory.zip&quot;,\n  &quot;s3://my-bucket/agent-overrides.tgz&quot;,\n]\n# target = &quot;/home/agent&quot;                  # default: $HOME\n# max_bytes = 104857600                   # max compressed size per archive (default: 100 MiB)\n# timeout_seconds = 300                   # per-source timeout (default: 300)\n# on_failure = &quot;abort&quot;                    # &quot;abort&quot; or &quot;warn&quot; (default: &quot;abort&quot;)\n# region = &quot;us-west-2&quot;                    # optional: override AWS region\n# endpoint_url = &quot;http://localhost:4566&quot;  # optional: LocalStack / VPC endpoint\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Fields</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sources</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>S3 URIs of archives (<code>.zip</code>, <code>.tar.gz</code>, <code>.tgz</code>). Max 5. Extracted in order.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>target</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>$HOME</code></td>\n<td>Extraction target directory.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_bytes</code></td>\n<td>u64</td>\n<td><code>104857600</code></td>\n<td>Max compressed archive size in bytes (100 MiB).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout_seconds</code></td>\n<td>u64</td>\n<td><code>300</code></td>\n<td>Per-source download+extract timeout.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>on_failure</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code> exits openab; <code>&quot;warn&quot;</code> logs and continues.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>region</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Override AWS region.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>endpoint_url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Override S3 endpoint URL.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Layer Concept</h3>\n<p>Sources are extracted sequentially (first → last). Files from later archives overwrite earlier ones — like layers in a container image:</p>\n<pre><code>Layer 3 (last)   ─── highest priority, overwrites all below\nLayer 2          ─── overwrites layer 1\nLayer 1 (first)  ─── base layer\n─────────────────\n     $HOME\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Safety</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Integrity verification</strong>: two layers of protection:\n<ol>\n<li><strong>S3-native checksum (automatic)</strong>: if the object was uploaded with <code>--checksum-algorithm SHA256</code>, OpenAB automatically verifies it on download — no config needed</li>\n<li><strong>User-provided <code>sha256s</code> (optional)</strong>: explicit checksums in config for additional defense-in-depth</li>\n</ol>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Size cap</strong>: downloads exceeding <code>max_bytes</code> are rejected before extraction</li>\n<li><strong>Atomic extraction</strong>: archives are first extracted to a temp directory, then moved into target — if extraction fails, target is not corrupted. Note: the move phase is per-file; if it fails mid-way with <code>on_failure = &quot;warn&quot;</code>, the target may be partially updated.</li>\n<li><strong>Path traversal prevention</strong>: zip uses <code>enclosed_name()</code>; tarball uses <code>unpack_in()</code> which rejects <code>..</code> escapes</li>\n<li><strong>Permission hardening</strong>: suid/sgid/sticky bits are stripped from extracted files</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Constraints</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Maximum <strong>5</strong> sources</li>\n<li>Only <code>s3://</code> URIs supported</li>\n<li>Supported formats: <code>.zip</code>, <code>.tar.gz</code>, <code>.tgz</code> (auto-detected via gzip magic bytes)</li>\n<li>Uses the standard AWS credential chain (IRSA, ECS task role, env vars)</li>\n<li>Optional <code>region</code>/<code>endpoint_url</code> override for LocalStack or VPC endpoints</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>IAM Policy</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n  &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;s3:GetObject&quot;],\n  &quot;Resource&quot;: [\n    &quot;arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/base-env.zip&quot;,\n    &quot;arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/shared-memory.zip&quot;,\n    &quot;arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/agent-overrides.zip&quot;\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Recommended: Enable S3 Checksums on Upload</h3>\n<p>For automatic integrity verification without maintaining <code>sha256s</code> in config, upload zip archives with SHA-256 checksums enabled:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Upload with SHA-256 checksum (recommended)\naws s3 cp env.zip s3://my-bucket/env.zip --checksum-algorithm SHA256\n\n# Verify it was stored\naws s3api head-object --bucket my-bucket --key env.zip --checksum-mode ENABLED\n</code></pre>\n<p>When objects have S3-native SHA-256 checksums, OpenAB verifies them automatically on download — no <code>sha256s</code> config needed. This is the simplest path to integrity verification.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> If <code>sha256s</code> is also provided in config, both checks run. The S3-native check uses the base64-encoded checksum from the <code>x-amz-checksum-sha256</code> response header. If neither is available, download proceeds without integrity verification (relies on IAM + bucket policy for trust).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>Available Hooks</h2>\n<p>The hooks below are <strong>script-based</strong> (<code>pre_boot</code>, <code>pre_shutdown</code>) and share the <code>script</code> / <code>inline</code> / <code>url</code> configuration described in this section. <code>pre_seed</code> is configured separately — see <a href=\"#pre-seed-phase\">Pre-Seed Phase</a> above.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Hook</th>\n<th>Timing</th>\n<th>Use Case</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_boot</code></td>\n<td>Before agent pool creation</td>\n<td>Bootstrap files, sync from S3, install CLIs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pre_shutdown</code></td>\n<td>After pool shutdown, before exit</td>\n<td>Backup state, sync to S3</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<p>Each hook supports exactly <strong>one</strong> script source:</p>\n<h3>Option A: File path</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\nscript = &quot;/etc/openab/pre-boot.sh&quot;\ntimeout_seconds = 60\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Option B: Inline script</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\nset -e\naws s3 sync &quot;$BOOTSTRAP_URI&quot; &quot;$HOME/&quot;\n'''\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Option C: Remote URL (with SHA-256 verification)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\nurl = &quot;https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/config/main/pre-boot.sh&quot;\nsha256 = &quot;e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855&quot;\ntimeout_seconds = 60\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Fields</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>script</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Absolute path to an executable script</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>inline</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Script content (written to temp file and executed)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Remote script URL (max 1 MiB)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sha256</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Required with <code>url</code> — hex-encoded SHA-256 of the script</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout_seconds</code></td>\n<td><code>60</code></td>\n<td>Max wall-clock time before the script is killed</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>on_failure</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;abort&quot;</code> exits openab; <code>&quot;warn&quot;</code> logs and continues</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Validation Rules</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Exactly one of <code>script</code>, <code>inline</code>, or <code>url</code> must be set</li>\n<li><code>url</code> requires <code>sha256</code></li>\n<li><code>script</code> must be an absolute path</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Validation runs at startup — config errors are caught before any side effects.</p>\n<h2>Environment</h2>\n<p>Scripts run with a sanitized environment:</p>\n<p><strong>Always passed:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>HOME</code>, <code>PATH</code>, <code>USER</code> (unix) / <code>USERPROFILE</code>, <code>USERNAME</code>, <code>SystemRoot</code>, <code>SystemDrive</code> (windows)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cloud credentials (auto-detected and passed through):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>AWS_*</code>, <code>AMAZON_*</code>, <code>ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI*</code></li>\n<li><code>GOOGLE_*</code>, <code>GCLOUD_*</code>, <code>CLOUDSDK_*</code></li>\n<li><code>AZURE_*</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Bootstrap variables (passed if set):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>BOOTSTRAP_URI</code>, <code>BOOTSTRAP_BASE_URI</code>, <code>BOOTSTRAP_PERSONAL_URI</code></li>\n<li><code>STATE_BUCKET</code>, <code>TASK_FAMILY</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>OpenAB identity (passed if set):</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>OPENAB_AGENT_NAME</code> — the agent's configured name</li>\n<li><code>OPENAB_BACKEND_AGENT</code> — the backend agent type (e.g. <code>claude</code>, <code>codex</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> <code>DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code> and other openab secrets are NOT exposed to hook scripts.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Security</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Temp files are created atomically with <code>0700</code> permissions (unix)</li>\n<li>Remote scripts require SHA-256 verification — openab refuses to execute on mismatch</li>\n<li>Scripts run as the container's UID (not root, unless the container runs as root)</li>\n<li>Remote script size is capped at 1 MiB</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Examples</h2>\n<h3>Clone a config/steering repo on startup</h3>\n<p><code>pre_boot</code> is for <strong>running logic</strong> at boot — cloning a repo, installing a tool, rendering config from env. For pulling plain S3 archives into <code>$HOME</code>, prefer <a href=\"#pre-seed-phase\"><code>pre_seed</code></a> (path-traversal protection, size caps, and checksums built in — no script needed).</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\nset -e\n# Pull steering/config from a private git repo (something pre_seed can't do)\nif [ ! -d &quot;$HOME/.config/steering/.git&quot; ]; then\n  git clone --depth 1 &quot;$STEERING_REPO_URL&quot; &quot;$HOME/.config/steering&quot;\nelse\n  git -C &quot;$HOME/.config/steering&quot; pull --ff-only\nfi\n'''\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Auth ordering:</strong> cloning a <strong>private</strong> repo needs credentials. Because <code>pre_seed</code> runs <em>before</em> <code>pre_boot</code>, seed the GitHub auth there — include <code>~/.config/gh/</code> (the <code>gh</code> CLI OAuth token) or <code>~/.git-credentials</code> in one of your <code>pre_seed</code> archives. By the time this <code>pre_boot</code> script runs, <code>git</code>/<code>gh</code> is already authenticated and the clone succeeds. (Alternatively, inject a token via <code>[agent].env</code> and embed it in the clone URL — but seeding via <code>pre_seed</code> keeps the token out of config.)</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Backup state on shutdown (ECS Fargate)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_shutdown]\ntimeout_seconds = 30\non_failure = &quot;warn&quot;\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\naws s3 sync &quot;$HOME/&quot; &quot;s3://$STATE_BUCKET/$TASK_FAMILY/&quot; \\\n  --exclude &quot;aws-cli/*&quot; --exclude &quot;bin/*&quot; --quiet\n'''\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Conditional OAuth token refresh</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\nscript = &quot;/etc/openab/pre-boot.sh&quot;\ntimeout_seconds = 60\non_failure = &quot;warn&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">#!/bin/sh\n# /etc/openab/pre-boot.sh\nset -e\nif [ -f &quot;$HOME/.kiro/auth.json&quot; ]; then\n  EXPIRES=$(jq -r '.expires' &quot;$HOME/.kiro/auth.json&quot;)\n  NOW=$(date +%s)\n  if [ &quot;$NOW&quot; -gt &quot;$EXPIRES&quot; ]; then\n    kiro-cli auth refresh || true\n  fi\nfi\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Real-World Example: S3 restore + backup round-trip</h2>\n<p>A common pattern: bots run on stateless compute (ECS Fargate Spot, Kubernetes with <code>emptyDir</code>) where the home directory is wiped on every restart. To survive restarts, each bot:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Restores</strong> its home directory from S3 on boot via <code>pre_seed</code></li>\n<li><strong>Backs up</strong> its home directory to S3 on shutdown via <code>pre_shutdown</code></li>\n</ol>\n<p>The backup key written on shutdown is exactly the key restored on the next boot — a closed loop that gives persistent state without a PVC.</p>\n<pre><code>                     pre_seed (boot)\n   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   │   s3://$STATE_BUCKET/$OPENAB_AGENT_NAME-home.tar.gz\n   ▼                                                │\n $HOME  ◄── extract ◄── download                    │  upload ──► tar $HOME\n   │                                                ▲\n   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                  pre_shutdown (shutdown)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>1. Restore on boot (<code>pre_seed</code>)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_seed]\nsources = [\n  &quot;s3://${STATE_BUCKET}/${OPENAB_AGENT_NAME}-home.tar.gz&quot;,   # layer 1: this agent's saved home\n  &quot;s3://${STATE_BUCKET}/shared/default.tar.gz&quot;,              # layer 2: shared defaults / steering\n]\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\nmax_bytes = 629145600   # 600 MiB per archive\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Syntax matters.</strong> In <code>pre_seed.sources</code>, use <strong><code>${VAR}</code></strong> (with braces). OpenAB expands these from its <strong>own process environment at config-load time</strong> — they are <em>not</em> shell variables and are <em>not</em> expanded at download time. Sources are extracted first → last, so <code>shared/default.tar.gz</code> (layer 2) overwrites any same-path files from layer 1. Order them so the layer you want to win comes last.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p><code>${STATE_BUCKET}</code> and <code>${OPENAB_AGENT_NAME}</code> must be present in the OpenAB container's environment — you supply them at deployment time (see step 3).</p>\n<h3>2. Backup on shutdown (<code>pre_shutdown</code>)</h3>\n<p>This inlines a <a href=\"https://gist.github.com/chaodu-agent/ffc614ce670e79761c6c3c98d5472737\">reference <code>pre-shutdown.sh</code></a> — it tars <code>$HOME</code> (skipping caches and toolchains that bloat the archive) and uploads it to the exact key <code>pre_seed</code> restores from:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_shutdown]\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;warn&quot;\ninline = '''\n#!/bin/sh\n# Tar up $HOME and sync to S3 (preserves permissions, symlinks)\n# Env vars: OPENAB_AGENT_NAME, STATE_BUCKET\nexport PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;\n\ntar czf /tmp/home.tar.gz -C &quot;$HOME&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./.cache&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./.npm&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./node_modules&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./.rustup&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./.cargo&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./.local/share/uv&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./aws-cli&quot; \\\n  --exclude=&quot;./.local/aws-cli&quot; \\\n  . 2&gt;/dev/null\n\naws s3 cp /tmp/home.tar.gz &quot;s3://$STATE_BUCKET/$OPENAB_AGENT_NAME-home.tar.gz&quot; --quiet || true\nrm -f /tmp/home.tar.gz\n'''\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Syntax matters (the other way).</strong> Inside <code>inline</code> scripts use <strong><code>$VAR</code></strong> (no braces). The shell resolves them at runtime when the script runs. If you wrote <code>${VAR}</code> here, OpenAB's config loader would expand it at load time instead of leaving it for the shell. The exclude list keeps the archive small enough to stay under <code>max_bytes</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><code>on_failure = &quot;warn&quot;</code> is deliberate: a failed backup should log and let the container exit cleanly rather than block shutdown. The matching <code>pre_seed</code> uses <code>&quot;abort&quot;</code> so a missing/corrupt restore fails loudly at boot.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>3. Supply <code>STATE_BUCKET</code> and <code>OPENAB_AGENT_NAME</code> at deployment</h3>\n<p>These are plain environment variables — pass them however your platform injects env.</p>\n<p><strong>Helm (<code>--set</code>):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.kiro.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.kiro.env.STATE_BUCKET=&quot;my-openab-state&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.env.OPENAB_AGENT_NAME=&quot;bot1&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Helm (<code>values.yaml</code>):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    env:\n      STATE_BUCKET: my-openab-state\n      OPENAB_AGENT_NAME: bot1\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>ECS task definition (<code>environment</code>):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;containerDefinitions&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;name&quot;: &quot;openab&quot;,\n      &quot;image&quot;: &quot;ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:latest&quot;,\n      &quot;environment&quot;: [\n        { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;STATE_BUCKET&quot;, &quot;value&quot;: &quot;my-openab-state&quot; },\n        { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;OPENAB_AGENT_NAME&quot;, &quot;value&quot;: &quot;bot1&quot; }\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong><a href=\"https://github.com/oablab/ecsctl\">ecsctl</a> manifest</strong> (<code>ecsctl export &lt;service&gt;</code> renders the live service as YAML):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: ecsctl/v1\nkind: Service\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-bot1\n  cluster: openab\nspec:\n  image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-kiro\n  cpu: '2048'\n  memory: '4096'\n  arch: X86_64\n  capacity: FARGATE_SPOT\n  desiredCount: 1\n  execEnabled: true\n  env:\n    GHPOOL_URL: http://ghpool.openab.local:8080\n    OPENAB_BACKEND_AGENT: openab-kiro\n    RUST_LOG: openab=debug,openab_core=debug\n    OPENAB_AGENT_NAME: bot1\n    GITHUB_API_URL: http://ghpool.openab.local:8080\n    STATE_BUCKET: my-openab-state\n</code></pre>\n<p>The <code>spec.env</code> map carries <code>OPENAB_AGENT_NAME</code> and <code>STATE_BUCKET</code> into the container — <code>pre_seed</code> and <code>pre_shutdown</code> pick them up automatically. Apply with <code>ecsctl apply -f service.yaml</code>.</p>\n<p>Run a second bot by deploying another release/task with a different <code>OPENAB_AGENT_NAME</code> (e.g. <code>bot2</code>, <code>bot3</code>) — each gets its own <code>&lt;name&gt;-home.tar.gz</code> key while sharing the same <code>shared/default.tar.gz</code> base layer and <code>STATE_BUCKET</code>.</p>\n<h3>4. IAM policy</h3>\n<p>The container's role (IRSA on EKS, task role on ECS) needs read for restore and write for backup:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;Version&quot;: &quot;2012-10-17&quot;,\n  &quot;Statement&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;Sid&quot;: &quot;PreSeedRestore&quot;,\n      &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n      &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;s3:GetObject&quot;],\n      &quot;Resource&quot;: [\n        &quot;arn:aws:s3:::my-openab-state/bot1-home.tar.gz&quot;,\n        &quot;arn:aws:s3:::my-openab-state/shared/default.tar.gz&quot;\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      &quot;Sid&quot;: &quot;PreShutdownBackup&quot;,\n      &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n      &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;s3:PutObject&quot;],\n      &quot;Resource&quot;: &quot;arn:aws:s3:::my-openab-state/bot1-home.tar.gz&quot;\n    }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Platform Comparison</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Option</th>\n<th>Best for</th>\n<th>Requires redeploy?</th>\n<th>Network at boot?</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>script</code></td>\n<td>k8s (ConfigMap mount), EFS, image bake</td>\n<td>Only if image-baked</td>\n<td>No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>inline</code></td>\n<td>ECS, Docker Compose, bare metal</td>\n<td>Config change only</td>\n<td>No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code> + <code>sha256</code></td>\n<td>Central script repo, multi-cluster</td>\n<td>No (update sha256 to roll)</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Lifecycle Hooks"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "image-tags",
      "html": "<h1>Docker Image Tagging Convention</h1>\n<h2>Unified Image Repository (<code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab</code>)</h2>\n<p>All agent variants are published under a single image repository using tag-based variants.\n<strong>There is no default agent</strong> — every image tag must explicitly specify the agent:</p>\n<pre><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:&lt;version&gt;-&lt;agent&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Tag format</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n<th>Points to</th>\n<th>Updated when</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&lt;version&gt;-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.1-kiro</code></td>\n<td>Exact pre-release build</td>\n<td>Pre-release tag pushed</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-claude</code></td>\n<td>Latest pre-release</td>\n<td>Every pre-release build</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&lt;version&gt;-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-codex</code></td>\n<td>Promoted stable build</td>\n<td>Stable tag pushed</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&lt;major.minor&gt;-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-gemini</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor</td>\n<td>Stable promotion</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-grok</code></td>\n<td>Latest stable</td>\n<td>Stable promotion</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>No <code>latest</code> tag.</strong> Use <code>beta-&lt;agent&gt;</code> or <code>stable-&lt;agent&gt;</code> for floating tags,\nor pin to an exact version like <code>0.9.0-beta.1-kiro</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Available agents: <code>kiro</code>, <code>claude</code>, <code>codex</code>, <code>copilot</code>, <code>cursor</code>, <code>gemini</code>, <code>grok</code>, <code>hermes</code>, <code>mimocode</code>, <code>opencode</code>, <code>antigravity</code>, <code>pi</code>, <code>native</code>, <code>agentcore</code></p>\n<h3>Migration from per-repo images (deprecated)</h3>\n<p>Previously, each agent had its own image repository (<code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-codex:beta</code>).\nThese are now replaced by the unified tag format.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Old (deprecated)</th>\n<th>New</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta</code></td>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-kiro</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:latest</code></td>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:stable-kiro</code> (no more <code>latest</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-claude:beta</code></td>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-claude</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-codex:0.8.5-beta.13</code></td>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:0.8.5-beta.13-codex</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Gateway (<code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway</code>)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Points to</th>\n<th>Updated when</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.5.1</code></td>\n<td>Exact release</td>\n<td><code>gateway-v*</code> tag pushed</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>v0.5.1</code></td>\n<td>Same as above (v-prefixed alias)</td>\n<td>Same</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>latest</code></td>\n<td>Latest release</td>\n<td>Every release</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Which tag to use</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Use case</th>\n<th>Recommended tag</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Production (pinned)</td>\n<td>Exact version (<code>0.9.0-beta.1-claude</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Helm chart default</td>\n<td><code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code> — chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Local dev / quick test</td>\n<td><code>beta-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>CI</td>\n<td>Exact version or <code>&lt;sha&gt;-&lt;agent&gt;</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Release flow</h2>\n<pre><code>release PR merged → tag-on-merge → v0.9.0-beta.1\n                                         │\n                                         ▼\n                                  build-operator.yml\n                                         │\n                              ┌──────────┴──────────┐\n                              │ is_prerelease=true   │\n                              ▼                      │\n                    openab:0.9.0-beta.1-kiro         │\n                    openab:0.9.0-beta.1-claude       │\n                    openab:0.9.0-beta.1-codex        │\n                    openab:beta-kiro                 │\n                    openab:beta-claude               │\n                    openab:beta-codex                │\n                    ... (all agents)                 │\n                                                    │\n                              ┌──────────────────────┘\n                              │ is_prerelease=false (stable)\n                              ▼\n                    promote most recent beta images →\n                    openab:0.9.0-kiro\n                    openab:0.9.0-claude\n                    openab:0.9-kiro\n                    openab:0.9-claude\n                    openab:stable-kiro\n                    openab:stable-claude\n                    ... (all agents, no `latest`)\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Image tags"
      }
    },
