      "slug": "inbound-attachments",
      "html": "<h1>Inbound Attachments</h1>\n<p>How OAB handles images, audio, and files sent by users across all platforms.</p>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>User sends media (photo/voice/file)\n  → Platform webhook delivers to Gateway\n  → Gateway downloads via platform API (auth stays in Gateway)\n  → Image: resize ≤1200px, JPEG compress (GIF passthrough ≤5MB)\n  → Store to ~/.openab/media/inbound/&lt;uuid&gt;\n  → WS event includes file path in attachments[].path\n  → Core reads from disk (zero encoding overhead)\n  → Processes: image → LLM, audio → STT, text_file → code block\n  → File auto-evicted after 2 minutes\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Platform Support Matrix</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Images</th>\n<th>Audio/Voice</th>\n<th>Text Files</th>\n<th>Video</th>\n<th>Binary Files</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Discord</strong></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅ (STT)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>metadata only</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Telegram</strong></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅ (STT)</td>\n<td>✅ (whitelist)</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Feishu</strong></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅ (STT)</td>\n<td>✅ (whitelist)</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Google Chat</strong></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅ (STT)</td>\n<td>✅ (whitelist)</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n<td>Drive files skipped</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>WeCom</strong></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>✅ (whitelist)</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>LINE</strong></td>\n<td>✅ (LINE-hosted only)</td>\n<td>✅ (STT, 1:1 only, LINE-hosted only)</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>—</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Slack</strong></td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>✅ (STT)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>skipped</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Processing Pipeline</h2>\n<h3>Images</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Gateway downloads from platform API</li>\n<li><code>resize_and_compress()</code> — longest side ≤1200px, JPEG quality 75</li>\n<li>GIFs ≤5MB passed through unchanged (preserves animation)</li>\n<li>Stored to <code>~/.openab/media/inbound/&lt;uuid&gt;</code></li>\n<li>Core reads bytes → <code>ContentBlock::Image</code> → sent to LLM</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Downstream Image Requirements</h3>\n<p>OpenAB can create the ACP image block, but downstream coding agents and selected models must also support image input. For local <code>llama.cpp</code> examples, see <a href=\"/openab/local-vision-models\">Local OpenAI-Compatible Vision Models</a>.</p>\n<h3>Audio / Voice Messages</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Gateway downloads raw audio (ogg/m4a/mp3)</li>\n<li>Stored to filesystem (no transcoding)</li>\n<li>Core reads bytes → STT transcription (Whisper/Groq) → <code>[Voice message transcript]: ...</code></li>\n<li>If STT disabled: silently skipped</li>\n</ol>\n<p>LINE-specific note:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>LINE voice-message STT currently works in <strong>1:1 chats only</strong>.</li>\n<li>LINE group/room voice messages are still blocked by mention gating because LINE does not attach mention metadata to audio messages.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Text Files (Documents)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Gateway downloads file</li>\n<li>Extension whitelist check: <code>.txt</code>, <code>.csv</code>, <code>.md</code>, <code>.json</code>, <code>.yaml</code>, <code>.rs</code>, <code>.py</code>, <code>.js</code>, <code>.ts</code>, <code>.go</code>, <code>.java</code>, <code>.c</code>, <code>.cpp</code>, <code>.sh</code>, <code>.sql</code>, <code>.html</code>, <code>.css</code>, <code>.toml</code>, <code>.xml</code>, <code>.ini</code>, <code>.cfg</code>, <code>.conf</code>, etc.</li>\n<li>UTF-8 validation — non-UTF-8 files rejected</li>\n<li>Stored to filesystem</li>\n<li>Core reads → wraps in markdown code block: <code>```filename.ext\\n&lt;content&gt;\\n```</code></li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Unsupported Types</h3>\n<p>Binary files (zip, pdf, exe, docx), video, and stickers are <strong>rejected with a status reason</strong>. The agent receives a <code>[System: attachment &quot;...&quot; was not delivered — unsupported format: ...]</code> notification so it can inform the user.</p>\n<h2>Size Limits</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Max Size</th>\n<th>Enforced By</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Images</td>\n<td>10 MB</td>\n<td>Gateway (pre-download Content-Length + post-download bytes)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Audio</td>\n<td>20 MB</td>\n<td>Gateway</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Text files</td>\n<td>20 MB</td>\n<td>Gateway (same as store cap)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>GIF passthrough</td>\n<td>5 MB</td>\n<td><code>resize_and_compress()</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Store (defense-in-depth)</td>\n<td>20 MB</td>\n<td><code>store_media()</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Storage (Colocate Mode)</h2>\n<p>Media is stored at <code>~/.openab/media/inbound/&lt;uuid&gt;</code>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Filenames</strong>: Server-generated UUID v4, no extension (MIME type in event payload)</li>\n<li><strong>TTL</strong>: 2 minutes — background task evicts expired files every 30 seconds</li>\n<li><strong>Trust boundary</strong>: Gateway and Core share the same <code>$HOME</code> (same pod / sidecar)</li>\n<li><strong>No auth required</strong>: Core reads directly from filesystem, no HTTP/token needed</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Security</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Path traversal</strong>: Impossible — filenames are UUID only, never user-supplied</li>\n<li><strong>Token leakage</strong>: Platform auth tokens (Telegram bot token, LINE access token, Feishu tenant token) stay in Gateway, never reach Core or agent</li>\n<li><strong>Disk exhaustion</strong>: TTL eviction + size limits prevent unbounded growth</li>\n<li><strong>No executable content</strong>: Files are raw data, never executed</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Future: HTTP Proxy Mode</h3>\n<p>For separated deployments (Gateway ≠ Core pod), a future PR will add <code>GET /media/&lt;uuid&gt;</code> on the Gateway, allowing Core to fetch via internal HTTP. The <code>attachments[].path</code> field will be replaced by <code>attachments[].url</code> in that mode.</p>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<p>No additional configuration required. The filesystem store is always active when Gateway is running. Ensure Gateway and Core share the same <code>$HOME</code> (default in Helm colocate/sidecar mode).</p>\n<h2>Related</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/local-vision-models\">Local OpenAI-Compatible Vision Models</a> — Local vision model setup for Pi and OpenCode</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/telegram\">Telegram</a> — Telegram-specific behavior and limitations</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/feishu\">Feishu</a> — Feishu image/file/audio handling</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/google-chat\">Google Chat</a> — Google Chat attachment support</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/stt\">STT (Speech-to-Text)</a> — Audio transcription configuration</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/sendfiles\">Sending Files (Outbound)</a> — Agent → user file delivery (separate mechanism)</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Inbound Attachments"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "kiro",
      "html": "<h1>Kiro CLI (Default Agent)</h1>\n<p>Kiro CLI is the default agent backend for OpenAB. It supports ACP natively — no adapter needed.</p>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<p>The default <code>Dockerfile</code> bundles both <code>openab</code> and <code>kiro-cli</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -t openab:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm repo add openab https://openabdev.github.io/openab\nhelm repo update\n\nhelm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.kiro.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-kiro</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-kiro</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-kiro</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-kiro</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.kiro.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-kiro\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Manual config.toml</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command and args default from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;kiro-cli acp --trust-all-tools&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<h3>Recommended: API Key (No Login Required)</h3>\n<p>Kiro CLI supports API key authentication via the <code>KIRO_API_KEY</code> environment variable. This is the <strong>recommended</strong> approach — it requires no manual OAuth login and is fully managed by AWS Secrets Manager.</p>\n<h4>Setup Steps</h4>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Enable API Keys in AWS Console</strong> — Go to your AWS Console and search for &quot;Kiro&quot;. Enable the API Keys feature. This option is only available through the AWS Console.</li>\n<li><strong>Generate your API Key</strong> — Go to <a href=\"https://kiro.dev\">kiro.dev</a>, log in, and generate your API key.</li>\n<li><strong>Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager</strong> — Create a generic secret (e.g. secret name <code>kiro</code>) and store your API key as a key/value pair (e.g. key: <code>API_KEY</code>, value: your generated key).</li>\n<li><strong>Configure AWS credentials</strong> — Make sure your runtime environment has AWS CLI or AWS credentials configured so OpenAB can retrieve the secret.</li>\n<li><strong>Configure <code>config.toml</code></strong> — Add the secret reference and environment variable:</li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.refs]\nkiro_api_key = &quot;aws-sm://kiro#API_KEY&quot;\n\n[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${secrets.kiro_api_key}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p>That's it — you're all set. No OAuth login required.</p>\n<h4>Architecture</h4>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        One-time Setup                           │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                 │\n│  ┌───────────────┐      ┌───────────┐      ┌────────────────┐   │\n│  │  AWS Console  │      │ kiro.dev  │      │ AWS Secrets Mgr│   │\n│  │               │      │           │      │                │   │\n│  │ Enable Kiro   │      │ Generate  │      │ Secret: &quot;kiro&quot; │   │\n│  │ API Keys      │      │ API Key   │─────▶│ Key: API_KEY   │   │\n│  └───────────────┘      └───────────┘      │ Val: sk-xxxxx  │   │\n│        ①                      ②            └───────┬────────┘   │\n│                                                    │ ③          │\n└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────┘\n                                                     │\n┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────┐\n│                     Runtime (automatic)            │            │\n├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────┤\n│                                                    │            │\n│  ┌──────────────────────┐         ④ resolve        │            │\n│  │       OpenAB         │◀──────────────────-──────┘            │\n│  │                      │  aws-sm://kiro#API_KEY                │\n│  │  config.toml:        │                                       │\n│  │  env = { KIRO_API_KEY│                                       │\n│  │    = &quot;${secrets...}&quot;}│                                       │\n│  └──────────┬───────────┘                                       │\n│             │ ⑤ inject env                                      │\n│             ▼                                                   │\n│  ┌──────────────────────┐         ⑥ authenticate                │\n│  │     Kiro CLI         │────────────────────────▶ Kiro API     │\n│  │                      │      KIRO_API_KEY ✅                  │\n│  │  No login needed!    │                                       │\n│  └──────────────────────┘                                       │\n│                                                                 │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">sequenceDiagram\n    participant User as User (one-time setup)\n    participant Console as AWS Console\n    participant Kiro as kiro.dev\n    participant SM as AWS Secrets Manager\n    participant OAB as OpenAB\n    participant CLI as Kiro CLI\n\n    Note over User,SM: One-time setup\n    User-&gt;&gt;Console: 1. Enable Kiro API Keys\n    User-&gt;&gt;Kiro: 2. Generate API Key\n    User-&gt;&gt;SM: 3. Store key in secret &quot;kiro&quot; (key: API_KEY)\n\n    Note over OAB,CLI: Runtime (automatic)\n    OAB-&gt;&gt;SM: 4. Resolve aws-sm://kiro#API_KEY\n    SM--&gt;&gt;OAB: Return API key value\n    OAB-&gt;&gt;CLI: 5. Inject as KIRO_API_KEY env var\n    CLI-&gt;&gt;Kiro: 6. Authenticate with API key ✅\n</code></pre>\n<h4>How It Works</h4>\n<ol>\n<li>OpenAB starts and resolves <code>aws-sm://kiro#API_KEY</code> — fetches the <code>API_KEY</code> field from the AWS Secrets Manager secret named <code>kiro</code>.</li>\n<li>The resolved value is injected into the agent container as the <code>KIRO_API_KEY</code> environment variable.</li>\n<li>Kiro CLI detects <code>KIRO_API_KEY</code> and uses it directly — <strong>no OAuth flow, no device code, no manual intervention</strong>.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>This makes the entire Kiro deployment <strong>zero-touch</strong> — fully automated with no login step required.</p>\n<h3>Alternative: OAuth Device Flow (Legacy)</h3>\n<p>If you cannot use an API key, Kiro CLI falls back to the OAuth device code flow. The PVC persists tokens across pod restarts.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-kiro -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Follow the device code flow in your browser, then restart the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-kiro\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Persisted Paths (PVC)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Path</th>\n<th>Contents</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>~/.kiro/</code></td>\n<td>Settings, skills, sessions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>~/.local/share/kiro-cli/</code></td>\n<td>OAuth tokens (<code>data.sqlite3</code> → <code>auth_kv</code> table), conversation history</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Default Agent Resources</h2>\n<p>When Kiro CLI starts with the built-in <code>kiro_default</code> agent, it automatically reads the following resources into context:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Resource</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AGENTS.md</code></td>\n<td>Agent coordination file (if exists in working dir)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>README.md</code></td>\n<td>Project readme (if exists in working dir)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>.kiro/skills/*/SKILL.md</code></td>\n<td>Skill files (local and global <code>~/.kiro/skills/</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>.kiro/steering/**/*.md</code></td>\n<td>Steering docs (local and global, if exists)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AmazonQ.md</code></td>\n<td>Legacy prompt file (if exists in working dir)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Highly recommended:</strong> <code>AGENTS.md</code> and <code>.kiro/steering/**/*.md</code> are the primary ways to give Kiro persistent memory. If you need Kiro to &quot;memorize&quot; something — best practices, guidelines, operational procedures, or project conventions — always first consider these two locations:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>AGENTS.md</code></strong> — Place in the agent's working directory (default: <code>/home/agent</code>). Ideal for identity, role definition, and top-level instructions.</li>\n<li><strong><code>.kiro/steering/**/*.md</code></strong> — Organize guidelines by topic, e.g.:\n<ul>\n<li><code>.kiro/steering/operations/backup.md</code> — backup procedures</li>\n<li><code>.kiro/steering/coding/style.md</code> — code style rules</li>\n<li><code>.kiro/steering/security/secrets.md</code> — secret handling policy</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Both are read into context on every session start — no extra configuration needed.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Customizing the Default Agent</h3>\n<p>You can override the default agent by creating a custom agent config:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Inside the pod or on the PVC\ncat &gt; ~/.kiro/agents/my-agent.json &lt;&lt; 'EOF'\n{\n  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;my-agent&quot;,\n  &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;You are a helpful assistant.&quot;,\n  &quot;tools&quot;: [&quot;*&quot;],\n  &quot;resources&quot;: [\n    &quot;file://AGENTS.md&quot;,\n    &quot;file://README.md&quot;,\n    &quot;skill://.kiro/skills/**/SKILL.md&quot;\n  ]\n}\nEOF\n\n# Set as default\nkiro-cli settings chat.defaultAgent my-agent\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Slash Commands</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Command</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Status</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/models</code></td>\n<td>Switch AI model</td>\n<td>✅ Implemented</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/agents</code></td>\n<td>Switch agent mode</td>\n<td>✅ Implemented</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/cancel</code></td>\n<td>Cancel current generation</td>\n<td>✅ Implemented</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3><code>/models</code> — Switch AI Model</h3>\n<p>Kiro CLI returns available models via ACP <code>configOptions</code> (category: <code>&quot;model&quot;</code>) on session creation. User types <code>/models</code> in a thread → select menu appears → pick a model → OpenAB sends <code>session/set_config_option</code> (falls back to <code>/model &lt;value&gt;</code> prompt if not supported).</p>\n<h3><code>/agents</code> — Switch Agent Mode</h3>\n<p>Same mechanism as <code>/models</code> but for the <code>agent</code> category. Kiro CLI exposes modes like <code>kiro_default</code> and <code>kiro_planner</code> via <code>configOptions</code>.</p>\n<h3><code>/cancel</code> — Cancel Current Operation</h3>\n<p>Sends a <code>session/cancel</code> JSON-RPC notification to abort in-flight LLM requests and tool calls. Works immediately — no need to wait for the current response to finish.</p>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> All slash commands only work in threads where a conversation is already active. If no session exists, they will prompt the user to start one first.</p>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/slash-commands\">docs/slash-commands.md</a> for full details.</p>\n<h2>Built-in Kiro CLI Commands</h2>\n<p>All built-in kiro-cli slash commands can be passed directly after an @mention:</p>\n<pre><code>@MyBot /compact\n@MyBot /clear\n@MyBot /model claude-sonnet-4\n</code></pre>\n<p>These are forwarded as-is to the kiro-cli ACP session as a prompt. Any command that kiro-cli supports in its interactive mode works here.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Kiro"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "line",
      "html": "<h1>LINE Setup</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Unified Mode (v0.9.0+):</strong> The OAB binary now embeds the line adapter directly. Set <code>LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET</code> as an env var — no separate gateway container or <code>[gateway]</code> config needed. See <a href=\"/openab/telegram#unified-mode-recommended\">Telegram docs</a> for the pattern.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Unified Config (Kiro + line)</h3>\n<p><strong>Minimal:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Recommended:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;compact&quot;\n\n[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Set <code>LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET</code> (and related platform env vars) on the container. No <code>[gateway]</code> needed.</p>\n<p>Connect a LINE bot to OpenAB via the Custom Gateway.</p>\n<pre><code>LINE ──POST──▶ Gateway (:8080) ◀──WebSocket── OAB Pod\n                                   (OAB connects out)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>A running OAB instance (with kiro-cli or any ACP agent authenticated)</li>\n<li>The Custom Gateway deployed (<a href=\"../gateway/README.md\">gateway/README.md</a>)</li>\n<li>A LINE Official Account with Messaging API enabled</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>1. Create a LINE Official Account</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <a href=\"https://manager.line.biz\">LINE Official Account Manager</a> and create a new account</li>\n<li>After creation, go to <strong>Settings</strong> → <strong>Messaging API</strong> → <strong>Enable Messaging API</strong></li>\n<li>Select or create a Provider, then confirm</li>\n</ol>\n<p>The channel now appears in the <a href=\"https://developers.line.biz\">LINE Developers Console</a>.</p>\n<h2>2. Get Credentials</h2>\n<p>In the LINE Developers Console, open your channel:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Basic settings</strong> tab → <strong>Channel secret</strong> → copy (→ <code>LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Messaging API</strong> tab → scroll to bottom → <strong>Channel access token</strong> → Issue → copy (→ <code>LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>3. Configure the Gateway</h2>\n<p>Add the LINE env vars to your gateway deployment:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Docker\ndocker run -d --name openab-gateway \\\n  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=&quot;...&quot; \\\n  -e LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET=&quot;your-channel-secret&quot; \\\n  -e LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=&quot;your-channel-access-token&quot; \\\n  -p 8080:8080 \\\n  ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:0.3.0\n\n# Kubernetes\nkubectl set env deployment/openab-gateway \\\n  LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET=&quot;your-channel-secret&quot; \\\n  LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=&quot;your-channel-access-token&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>4. Set the Webhook URL</h2>\n<p>In the LINE Developers Console → <strong>Messaging API</strong> tab:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Webhook URL</strong> → Edit → enter: <code>https://gw.yourdomain.com/webhook/line</code></li>\n<li><strong>Use webhook</strong> → ON</li>\n<li><strong>Auto-reply messages</strong> → OFF (prevents LINE's default auto-reply from interfering)</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Verify</strong> to test the connection</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>5. Configure OAB</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[gateway]\nurl = &quot;ws://openab-gateway:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;line&quot;\n# allowed_users = [&quot;U1234567890abcdef&quot;]   # restrict to specific LINE user IDs\n# allowed_channels = [&quot;C1234567890abcdef&quot;] # restrict to specific chat/group IDs\n\n[agent]\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Tip:</strong> To find a LINE user ID, check the gateway logs — the sender ID is logged for each incoming message. By default all users and channels are allowed. Setting <code>allowed_users</code> or <code>allowed_channels</code> automatically restricts access to only those listed.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>6. Add the Bot as Friend</h2>\n<p>In the LINE Developers Console → <strong>Messaging API</strong> tab → scan the QR code with your LINE app, or search for the bot by its LINE ID.</p>\n<h2>Features</h2>\n<h3>Supported</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>1:1 chat</strong> — send a message to the bot, get an AI agent response</li>\n<li><strong>Inbound voice messages in 1:1 chat</strong> — LINE-hosted audio messages are downloaded through the LINE Content API and forwarded to OpenAB as <code>audio</code> attachments, so the existing STT flow can transcribe them. This requires <code>[stt] enabled = true</code> in OpenAB core. See <a href=\"/openab/stt\">STT (Speech-to-Text)</a>.</li>\n<li><strong>Group chat</strong> — add the bot to a group; it responds only when @-mentioned (see @mention gating below)</li>\n<li><strong>Inbound images</strong> — user-sent LINE images are downloaded through the LINE Content API and forwarded to OpenAB as image attachments</li>\n<li><strong>Webhook signature validation</strong> — HMAC-SHA256 via <code>LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET</code></li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Implementation tradeoff:</strong> OpenAB now acknowledges LINE webhooks before image download/processing so slow attachment work is less likely to trigger webhook redelivery. The follow-up image download and event emission happen asynchronously, which keeps the request path short but also means a crash after the HTTP 200 can still lose that in-flight work. This PR intentionally keeps scope small and does not add a separate background-task durability or duplicate-suppression layer on top of early-ack.\nBecause image processing now happens after the ACK, an earlier image webhook can also reach OpenAB after a later text webhook from the same chat if the image path is slower.\nOpenAB now also caps how many LINE payloads can enter that post-ACK path concurrently; once the cap is full, new webhooks wait for capacity instead of creating unbounded background backlog.\nIf a LINE-hosted image cannot be downloaded or decoded, OpenAB logs and skips that image event rather than synthesizing a fake text prompt.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Not Supported (LINE API limitations)</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Threads</strong> — LINE has no thread/topic concept. All messages in a chat share one agent session.</li>\n<li><strong>Reactions</strong> — LINE Bot API does not support message reactions.</li>\n<li><strong>@mention gating</strong> — Supported (zero-config). In group/room chats the gateway only forwards messages where the bot is explicitly @-mentioned (LINE's native <code>mentionees[].isSelf</code> signal). 1:1 DMs are always forwarded. No env var is needed.\n<ul>\n<li><em>Limitation — non-text messages</em>: LINE only attaches mention data to text messages. Images, videos, stickers, files, and location messages in groups are silently dropped because they cannot carry an @-mention.</li>\n<li><em>Limitation — group voice messages</em>: LINE voice/audio messages in groups and rooms are also dropped today because audio messages do not carry mention metadata. This PR only enables inbound voice STT for 1:1 chats.</li>\n<li><em>Limitation — <code>@All</code></em>: A group-wide <code>@All</code> mention does <strong>not</strong> trigger the bot; only a direct <code>@BotName</code> mention does.</li>\n<li><em>Breaking change</em>: This gating is always active. Deployments that previously relied on the bot responding to all group messages will need to @-mention the bot after upgrading.</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Markdown rendering</strong> — LINE uses its own text formatting. Agent replies are sent as plain text.</li>\n<li><strong>External-content images</strong> — LINE image messages backed by <code>contentProvider.type = &quot;external&quot;</code> are not downloaded yet.</li>\n<li><strong>External-content audio</strong> — LINE audio messages backed by <code>contentProvider.type = &quot;external&quot;</code> are not downloaded yet.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Environment Variables</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Channel secret for webhook signature validation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Channel access token for Reply/Push Message API and LINE-hosted image/audio downloads</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<p><strong>Bot doesn't respond:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Verify webhook URL is correct and shows ✅ in LINE Developers Console</li>\n<li>Check <strong>Use webhook</strong> is ON and <strong>Auto-reply messages</strong> is OFF</li>\n<li>Check gateway logs: <code>kubectl logs -l app=openab-gateway</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Voice message doesn't transcribe:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Confirm you sent the voice message in a <strong>1:1 chat</strong>, not a group or room</li>\n<li>Confirm <code>[stt] enabled = true</code> in your OpenAB config</li>\n<li>Confirm the STT provider is configured correctly; see <a href=\"/openab/stt\">STT (Speech-to-Text)</a></li>\n<li>Check gateway logs for <code>media stored</code> and OpenAB logs for downstream dispatch</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>&quot;Invalid signature&quot; in gateway logs:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Verify <code>LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET</code> matches the value in LINE Developers Console</li>\n<li>Make sure you're using the Channel secret (not the Channel access token)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Webhook verify fails:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Ensure the gateway is reachable at the webhook URL</li>\n<li>Check <code>curl https://your-gateway-host/health</code> returns <code>ok</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/\">LINE Messaging API Documentation</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://developers.line.biz\">LINE Developers Console</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/custom-gateway\">ADR: Custom Gateway</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/adr/line-adapter\">ADR: LINE Adapter</a></li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "LINE Setup"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "local-dev",
      "html": "<h1>Local Development</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ <strong>Security disclaimer:</strong> OpenAB is designed to run in Kubernetes with Pod-level isolation (NetworkPolicy, resource limits, read-only root filesystem). Native binaries — including Windows builds — are provided for <strong>temporary local development and debugging only</strong>, not for daily use. Running directly on a host without container isolation is <strong>not recommended for production</strong> — the agent subprocess inherits full host permissions and is not protected by any sandbox, which is a meaningful attack surface for a bot accepting messages from arbitrary users.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cp config.toml.example config.toml\n# Edit config.toml with your bot token and channel ID\n\nexport DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=&quot;your-token&quot;\ncargo run\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Remote Config</h2>\n<p>Config can be loaded from a local file or a remote URL via the <code>--config</code> / <code>-c</code> flag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Local file\nopenab run --config config.toml\nopenab run -c config.toml\n\n# Remote URL (http:// or https://)\nopenab run --config https://example.com/config.toml\nopenab run -c https://example.com/config.toml\n\n# Default (no flag → config.toml)\nopenab run\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is useful for containerized or multi-node deployments where config is hosted on a central server (e.g. S3, Git raw URL, internal HTTP service).</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Security best practice:</strong> Never hardcode secrets in remote config files. Use environment variable references like <code>bot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;</code> and inject the actual values via local environment variables or Kubernetes Secrets. OpenAB expands <code>${VAR}</code> identically for both local and remote config.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Build &amp; Push</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -t openab:latest .\ndocker tag openab:latest &lt;your-registry&gt;/openab:latest\ndocker push &lt;your-registry&gt;/openab:latest\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Project Structure</h2>\n<pre><code>├── Dockerfile          # multi-stage: rust build + debian-slim runtime with kiro-cli\n├── config.toml.example # example config with all agent backends\n├── k8s/                # Kubernetes manifests\n└── src/\n    ├── main.rs         # entrypoint: multi-adapter startup, cleanup, shutdown\n    ├── adapter.rs      # ChatAdapter trait, AdapterRouter (platform-agnostic)\n    ├── config.rs       # TOML config + ${ENV_VAR} expansion\n    ├── discord.rs      # DiscordAdapter: serenity EventHandler + ChatAdapter impl\n    ├── slack.rs        # SlackAdapter: Socket Mode + ChatAdapter impl\n    ├── media.rs        # shared image resize/compress + STT download\n    ├── format.rs       # message splitting, thread name shortening\n    ├── reactions.rs    # status reaction controller (debounce, stall detection)\n    └── acp/\n        ├── protocol.rs # JSON-RPC types + ACP event classification\n        ├── connection.rs # spawn CLI, stdio JSON-RPC communication\n        └── pool.rs     # session key → AcpConnection map\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Local Development"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "local-vision-models",
      "html": "<h1>Local OpenAI-Compatible Vision Models</h1>\n<p>OpenAB can pass inbound image attachments to ACP agents as image content blocks, but the downstream coding agent and selected local model must both support image input.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">User image\n  → OpenAB inbound attachment pipeline\n  → ACP ImageContent / ContentBlock::Image\n  → Pi/OpenCode model config that declares image input support\n  → local vision-capable inference endpoint\n</code></pre>\n<p>OpenAB can create the ACP image block, but it cannot make a text-only coding agent or text-only local model understand it. Use this guide for local OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as <code>llama-server</code>.</p>\n<h2>Requirements</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>The local inference server exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint that accepts <code>image_url</code> content parts with base64 data URLs.</li>\n<li>The selected model is a vision/multimodal model, not a text-only GGUF.</li>\n<li>The coding-agent model metadata declares image input support.</li>\n<li>The model can still emit reliable tool calls through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint if you want to use it as a coding agent.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Start a vision-capable <code>llama-server</code></h2>\n<p>Hosted GGUF from Hugging Face, when the repo includes a multimodal projector:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">llama-server \\\n  -hf ggml-org/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M \\\n  --alias local-vision \\\n  --host 0.0.0.0 \\\n  --port 8080 \\\n  -c 32768\n</code></pre>\n<p>In this mode, <code>llama.cpp</code> auto-loads the projector when the hosted GGUF repo provides one.</p>\n<p>Local GGUF files require both the text model and the multimodal projector:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">llama-server \\\n  -m /models/qwen2.5-vl-7b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf \\\n  --mmproj /models/mmproj-qwen2.5-vl-7b-instruct-f16.gguf \\\n  --alias local-vision \\\n  --host 0.0.0.0 \\\n  --port 8080 \\\n  -c 32768\n</code></pre>\n<p>Do <strong>not</strong> add <code>--no-mmproj</code> for image input. If <code>llama-server</code> runs in the same pod as OpenAB and the coding agent, use <code>http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1</code>. If it runs as a separate Kubernetes Service, use that Service URL instead.</p>\n<h2>Pi Configuration</h2>\n<p>Pi must declare image input support in <code>~/.pi/agent/models.json</code> with <code>input: [&quot;text&quot;, &quot;image&quot;]</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-pi -- mkdir -p /home/node/.pi/agent\nkubectl exec -i deployment/openab-pi -- sh -c 'cat &gt;/home/node/.pi/agent/models.json'&lt;&lt;'EOF'\n{\n  &quot;providers&quot;: {\n    &quot;local-vision&quot;: {\n      &quot;baseUrl&quot;: &quot;http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1&quot;,\n      &quot;api&quot;: &quot;openai-completions&quot;,\n      &quot;apiKey&quot;: &quot;not-needed&quot;,\n      &quot;compat&quot;: {\n        &quot;supportsDeveloperRole&quot;: false,\n        &quot;supportsReasoningEffort&quot;: false,\n        &quot;maxTokensField&quot;: &quot;max_tokens&quot;\n      },\n      &quot;models&quot;: [\n        {\n          &quot;id&quot;: &quot;local-vision&quot;,\n          &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Local Vision (llama.cpp)&quot;,\n          &quot;reasoning&quot;: false,\n          &quot;input&quot;: [&quot;text&quot;, &quot;image&quot;],\n          &quot;contextWindow&quot;: 32768,\n          &quot;maxTokens&quot;: 4096,\n          &quot;cost&quot;: { &quot;input&quot;: 0, &quot;output&quot;: 0, &quot;cacheRead&quot;: 0, &quot;cacheWrite&quot;: 0 }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\nEOF\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then select <code>local-vision/local-vision</code> in Pi with <code>/model</code>, or verify it with:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-pi -- pi --list-models local-vision\n</code></pre>\n<p>For OpenAB deployments, persist the Pi config on the PVC before starting the bot.</p>\n<h2>OpenCode Configuration</h2>\n<p>OpenCode must declare image input support in <code>opencode.json</code> with <code>modalities.input: [&quot;text&quot;, &quot;image&quot;]</code>.</p>\n<p>Create <code>opencode.json</code> in the working directory, usually <code>/home/node</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -i deployment/openab-opencode -- sh -c 'cat &gt;/home/node/opencode.json'&lt;&lt;'EOF'\n{\n  &quot;$schema&quot;: &quot;https://opencode.ai/config.json&quot;,\n  &quot;model&quot;: &quot;local-vision/local-vision&quot;,\n  &quot;provider&quot;: {\n    &quot;local-vision&quot;: {\n      &quot;npm&quot;: &quot;@ai-sdk/openai-compatible&quot;,\n      &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Local llama.cpp vision&quot;,\n      &quot;options&quot;: {\n        &quot;baseURL&quot;: &quot;http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1&quot;,\n        &quot;apiKey&quot;: &quot;not-needed&quot;\n      },\n      &quot;models&quot;: {\n        &quot;local-vision&quot;: {\n          &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Local Vision (llama.cpp)&quot;,\n          &quot;tool_call&quot;: true,\n          &quot;limit&quot;: {\n            &quot;context&quot;: 32768,\n            &quot;output&quot;: 4096\n          },\n          &quot;modalities&quot;: {\n            &quot;input&quot;: [&quot;text&quot;, &quot;image&quot;],\n            &quot;output&quot;: [&quot;text&quot;]\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\nEOF\n</code></pre>\n<p>Restart OpenAB/OpenCode after changing the config:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-opencode\nkubectl exec deployment/openab-opencode -- opencode models local-vision\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>tool_call: true</code> tells OpenCode the model can be used for coding-agent tool calls. Keep it only if the selected local model and server can reliably emit tool calls through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint.</p>\n<h2>Verify Image and Tool Support</h2>\n<p>Upload a screenshot and confirm the response references the image content. Then verify normal file-edit or shell-tool workflows still work. Image description alone is not enough for a coding agent.</p>\n<h2>Local Vision Pitfalls</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use a vision/multimodal GGUF from the <a href=\"https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/multimodal.md\"><code>llama.cpp</code> multimodal list</a>, not a text-only model.</li>\n<li>With local files, always provide the matching <code>--mmproj</code> file.</li>\n<li>Do not use <code>--no-mmproj</code>; it disables the projector needed for image input.</li>\n<li>Use enough context for image tokens plus coding-agent tools and repository context. Start around 16k-32k if the model and hardware allow it.</li>\n<li>Smoke-test tool calls. Some local vision models can describe images but are not reliable enough for coding-agent tool use.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Related</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/inbound-attachments\">Inbound Attachments</a> — how OpenAB converts uploaded images into ACP image content</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/pi\">Pi</a> — Pi coding agent setup</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/opencode\">OpenCode</a> — OpenCode setup</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Vision models"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "message-dispatch-modes",
      "html": "<h1>Message Dispatch Modes</h1>\n<p>OpenAB supports three message dispatch modes that control how incoming messages are batched before being sent to the AI agent as an ACP turn.</p>\n<h2>Modes</h2>\n<h3><code>per-message</code> (default)</h3>\n<p>Each message triggers its own ACP turn. This is the default behavior — simple, predictable, no batching. Existing deployments use this mode automatically without any configuration change.</p>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Zero added latency — every message dispatches immediately</li>\n<li>Simplest mental model (1 message = 1 agent response)</li>\n<li>No configuration needed</li>\n<li>No risk of messages being grouped with unrelated context</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Redundant context: if a user sends 3 messages quickly, the agent loads full context 3 times</li>\n<li>Higher token cost under burst traffic (N messages = N full context windows)</li>\n<li>Agent responds to each message independently — can't synthesize a coherent answer across rapid-fire messages</li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>per-thread</code></h3>\n<p>All messages in a thread share one buffer. Messages that arrive while the agent is processing are batched into a single ACP turn at the next turn boundary.</p>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Lowest token cost — one context window serves N messages</li>\n<li>Agent sees the full picture and can synthesize a single coherent response</li>\n<li>Reduces &quot;sorry I already answered that&quot; noise from sequential turns</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Silent-drop risk: if Alice and Bob both message, the agent may only address Alice</li>\n<li>Single response must cover all senders — harder for the agent to structure</li>\n<li>Slight latency for messages 2..N (they wait for the current turn to finish)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>per-lane</code></h3>\n<p>Each (thread, sender) pair gets its own buffer. Messages from the same sender batch together, but different senders get independent ACP turns.</p>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>No silent-drop risk — every sender gets their own dedicated turn and response</li>\n<li>Same-sender batching still reduces redundant context (rapid-fire messages consolidated)</li>\n<li>Best for multi-agent collaboration (each bot gets its own turn)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Higher token cost than <code>per-thread</code> (one turn per active sender per boundary)</li>\n<li>Turns serialize through the shared session — sender B waits for sender A's turn to complete</li>\n<li>More complex to reason about (ordering depends on arrival time)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Comparison Table</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th></th>\n<th><code>per-message</code></th>\n<th><code>per-thread</code></th>\n<th><code>per-lane</code></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Token cost</td>\n<td>Highest (N turns)</td>\n<td>Lowest (1 turn)</td>\n<td>Medium (1 per sender)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Latency</td>\n<td>Zero</td>\n<td>Wait for turn boundary</td>\n<td>Wait for turn boundary</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Silent-drop risk</td>\n<td>None</td>\n<td>Yes (multi-sender)</td>\n<td>None</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Rapid-fire handling</td>\n<td>Each separate</td>\n<td>All batched</td>\n<td>Same-sender batched</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Best for</td>\n<td>Single user, low traffic</td>\n<td>Cost-sensitive, single-reply</td>\n<td>Multi-user, multi-bot</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Configuration</td>\n<td>None (default)</td>\n<td>Opt-in</td>\n<td>Opt-in</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Decision Guide</h2>\n<pre><code>Is this a single-user bot (1 human per thread)?\n  → per-message (default, simplest)\n\nMultiple humans in the same thread?\n  ├─ Is it OK if the agent addresses everyone in one reply?\n  │    → per-thread (cheapest)\n  └─ Each person needs their own response?\n       → per-lane (safest)\n\nMulti-agent collaboration (bot-to-bot)?\n  → per-lane (each bot gets its own turn)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<h3>config.toml</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nmessage_processing_mode = &quot;per-lane&quot;   # &quot;per-message&quot; | &quot;per-thread&quot; | &quot;per-lane&quot;\nmax_buffered_messages = 10             # per-thread mpsc capacity (batched modes only)\nmax_batch_tokens = 24000               # soft token cap per ACP turn (batched modes only)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Helm values</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    discord:\n      messageProcessingMode: &quot;per-lane&quot;\n      maxBufferedMessages: 10\n      maxBatchTokens: 24000\n</code></pre>\n<p>The same fields are available under <code>slack:</code> and <code>gateway:</code> sections.</p>\n<h2>How It Works — ASCII Diagrams</h2>\n<h3>per-message (default)</h3>\n<pre><code>Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────►\n\nAlice: &quot;hi&quot;          Alice: &quot;also this&quot;       Bob: &quot;hey&quot;\n   │                      │                      │\n   ▼                      ▼                      ▼\n┌──────────┐         ┌──────────┐          ┌──────────┐\n│ ACP Turn │         │ ACP Turn │          │ ACP Turn │\n│ (1 msg)  │         │ (1 msg)  │          │ (1 msg)  │\n└────┬─────┘         └────┬─────┘          └────┬─────┘\n     ▼                    ▼                      ▼\n  Response 1           Response 2             Response 3\n\nEach message = its own turn. Simple. 3 messages → 3 responses.\n</code></pre>\n<h3>per-thread</h3>\n<pre><code>Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────►\n\nAlice: &quot;hi&quot;     Bob: &quot;hey&quot;   Alice: &quot;also this&quot;\n   │               │              │\n   ▼               │              │\n┌──────────┐       │              │\n│ ACP Turn │  (agent busy...)     │\n│ (1 msg)  │       │              │\n└────┬─────┘       ▼              ▼\n     │         ┌────────────────────────┐\n     ▼         │ Buffer (shared thread) │\n  Response 1   │  → Bob: &quot;hey&quot;         │\n               │  → Alice: &quot;also this&quot; │\n               └───────────┬────────────┘\n                           ▼  (turn boundary)\n                    ┌──────────────┐\n                    │  ACP Turn    │\n                    │  (2 msgs     │\n                    │   batched)   │\n                    └──────┬───────┘\n                           ▼\n                      Response 2\n                   (addresses both)\n\nAll senders share one buffer → one batched turn → one response.\n</code></pre>\n<h3>per-lane</h3>\n<pre><code>Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────►\n\nAlice: &quot;hi&quot;     Bob: &quot;hey&quot;   Alice: &quot;also this&quot;\n   │               │              │\n   ▼               │              │\n┌──────────┐       │              │\n│ ACP Turn │  (agent busy...)     │\n│ (Alice)  │       │              │\n└────┬─────┘       ▼              ▼\n     │      ┌─────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐\n     ▼      │ Bob's lane  │  │ Alice's lane     │\nResponse 1  │ → &quot;hey&quot;     │  │ → &quot;also this&quot;    │\n            └──────┬──────┘  └────────┬─────────┘\n                   ▼                  │\n            ┌──────────────┐          │  (waits for Bob's turn)\n            │  ACP Turn    │          │\n            │  (Bob, 1msg) │          │\n            └──────┬───────┘          │\n                   ▼                  ▼\n              Response 2       ┌──────────────┐\n              (for Bob)        │  ACP Turn    │\n                               │  (Alice,1msg)│\n                               └──────┬───────┘\n                                      ▼\n                                 Response 3\n                                 (for Alice)\n\nEach sender gets their own lane → own turn → own response. No silent drop.\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Batching internals (consumer loop)</h3>\n<pre><code>                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐\n                    │         Dispatcher (per thread)      │\n                    │                                     │\n  submit(msg) ─────►  mpsc channel (cap = max_buffered)  │\n                    │         │                           │\n                    │         ▼                           │\n                    │  ┌─────────────────────────┐       │\n                    │  │    consumer_loop         │       │\n                    │  │                         │       │\n                    │  │  1. Block on first msg  │       │  ← I1: zero latency\n                    │  │     (or idle timeout)   │       │\n                    │  │                         │       │\n                    │  │  2. Greedy drain:       │       │\n                    │  │     while try_recv()    │       │\n                    │  │       &amp;&amp; count &lt; cap    │       │\n                    │  │       &amp;&amp; tokens &lt; max   │       │\n                    │  │                         │       │\n                    │  │  3. Pack batch:         │       │\n                    │  │     [sender_ctx + msg]  │       │\n                    │  │     [sender_ctx + msg]  │       │\n                    │  │     ...                 │       │\n                    │  │                         │       │\n                    │  │  4. stream_prompt_blocks│       │  ← I2: one turn at a time\n                    │  │     (shared session)    │       │\n                    │  │                         │       │\n                    │  │  5. Loop back to 1      │       │\n                    │  └─────────────────────────┘       │\n                    └─────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Defaults</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Parameter</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>message_processing_mode</code></td>\n<td><code>per-message</code></td>\n<td>Backward compatible, no batching</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_buffered_messages</code></td>\n<td>10</td>\n<td>Only applies to <code>per-thread</code> / <code>per-lane</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_batch_tokens</code></td>\n<td>24000</td>\n<td>Rough estimate (~4 chars/token)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Message Dispatch Modes"
      }
    },

      "slug": "messaging",
      "html": "<h1>Messaging Model</h1>\n<p>This document explains the five messaging patterns in OpenAB, each building on the previous one:</p>\n<ol start=\"0\">\n<li><strong>Human → Bot in DM</strong> — Private 1:1 conversations (opt-in).</li>\n<li><strong>Human → Bot in Channel</strong> — How a conversation starts via @mention.</li>\n<li><strong>Human → Bot in Thread</strong> — How follow-up messages work without @mention.</li>\n<li><strong>Human → Multiple Bots in Thread</strong> — How multi-bot threads behave and how to control them.</li>\n<li><strong>Bot → Bot in Thread</strong> — How bots can talk to each other and how to prevent loops.</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>0. Human → Bot in DM</h2>\n<p>Users can interact with the bot privately via direct message. DMs are <strong>opt-in</strong> — disabled by default to prevent unexpected resource usage.</p>\n<p>When <code>allow_dm = true</code>, a DM is treated as an <strong>implicit @mention</strong> (mirrors Slack behavior). No thread is created — the bot replies directly in the DM channel.</p>\n<pre><code>User DMs BotA: help me with X\n  → BotA replies in DM (no thread, no @mention needed)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Key behaviors</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>allowed_users</code> still enforced</strong> — DMs are not a backdoor past user allowlists.</li>\n<li><strong>Bot turn tracking applies</strong> — <code>max_bot_turns</code> prevents loops in DM conversations.</li>\n<li><strong>Session pool shared</strong> — Each DM user consumes one session slot (<code>discord:{dm_channel_id}</code>). Existing TTL cleanup and eviction apply.</li>\n<li><strong>Discord only</strong> — Slack natively supports DMs without extra config. This setting applies to the Discord adapter only.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Relevant config</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_dm</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code> = respond to Discord DMs; <code>false</code> = ignore DMs.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_users</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>User IDs allowed to interact. Still enforced in DMs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Example config.toml</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\nallow_dm = true                      # opt-in to DM support\nallowed_users = [&quot;9876543210&quot;]       # restrict who can DM the bot\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Human → Bot in Channel</h2>\n<p>Bots <strong>never</strong> respond to regular channel messages. A conversation starts only when a human explicitly @mentions a bot.</p>\n<p>When you @mention a bot in a channel:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Ack</strong> — The bot reacts to your message with an emoji (e.g., 👀) to confirm receipt.</li>\n<li><strong>Thread creation</strong> — OAB automatically creates a dedicated thread.</li>\n<li><strong>Response</strong> — The bot responds inside that thread.</li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code>User in #general: @BotA help me with X\n  → BotA reacts 👀\n  → OAB creates thread &quot;help me with X&quot;\n  → BotA replies in thread\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Relevant config</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_channels</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td><code>true</code> = all channels; <code>false</code> = only <code>allowed_channels</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_channels</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Channel IDs where bots can be activated.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_users</code></td>\n<td>bool | omit</td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td><code>true</code> = any user; <code>false</code> = only <code>allowed_users</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_users</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>User IDs allowed to interact with bots.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>reactions.enabled</code></td>\n<td>bool</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Enable/disable emoji reaction feedback.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Example config.toml</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\nallowed_channels = [&quot;1234567890&quot;]    # restrict to specific channels\nallowed_users = [&quot;9876543210&quot;]       # restrict to specific users\n# By default, all channels and all users are allowed when these lists are empty.\n# Reactions are enabled by default with 👀 for ack.\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. Human → Bot in Thread</h2>\n<p>Once a thread is created, <strong>no @mention is needed</strong> for follow-up messages. All your messages in the thread are automatically routed to the bot.</p>\n<pre><code>User in thread: can you also do Y?\n  → BotA replies (no @mention required)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Relevant config</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_user_messages</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Controls when bots respond without @mention. See Layer 3 for all modes.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>In this single-bot scenario, the default <code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code> behaves the same as <code>&quot;involved&quot;</code> — the bot responds to all messages in threads it has participated in.</p>\n<h3>Example config.toml</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n# allow_user_messages defaults to &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;:\n# bot responds to all messages in single-bot threads it has participated in;\n# in multi-bot threads, @mention is required.\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Human → Multiple Bots in Thread</h2>\n<p>You can bring additional bots into a thread by @mentioning them. Once a bot responds, it becomes <strong>involved</strong> in the thread.</p>\n<p>How involved bots behave on subsequent messages is controlled by <code>allow_user_messages</code>:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mode</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>multibot-mentions</code> (default)</td>\n<td>Like <code>involved</code>, but once a second bot has posted in the thread, you must @mention the bot(s) you want to respond.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>involved</code></td>\n<td>All involved bots respond to every message — no @mention required.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mentions</code></td>\n<td>Always require an explicit @mention, even in threads.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code># allow_user_messages = &quot;multibot-mentions&quot; (default)\nUser in thread: @BotB what do you think?\n  → BotB replies, now &quot;involved&quot;\nUser in thread: any other ideas?\n  → No bot replies (need explicit @mention)\n\n# allow_user_messages = &quot;involved&quot;\nUser in thread: any other ideas?\n  → Both BotA and BotB reply\nUser in thread: @BotA any other ideas?\n  → Only BotA replies\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Relevant config</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_user_messages</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code> — require @mention once 2+ bots are in the thread. <code>&quot;involved&quot;</code> — reply without @mention in participated threads. <code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code> — always require @mention.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> This is a <strong>global setting</strong> — it cannot be changed per thread. Configure it in <code>config.toml</code> or via <code>values.yaml</code> for Helm.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Example config.toml</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n# Default is &quot;multibot-mentions&quot; — require @mention in multi-bot threads.\n# Use &quot;involved&quot; to let all bots respond without @mention.\nallow_user_messages = &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Bot → Bot in Thread</h2>\n<p>Bots can talk to each other within a thread. By default this is disabled.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mode</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>off</code> (default)</td>\n<td>Bots ignore all messages from other bots.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mentions</code></td>\n<td>A bot only processes messages from other bots that explicitly @mention it.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>all</code></td>\n<td>A bot processes all bot messages in threads it's involved in.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code># allow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;\nBotA in thread: @BotB can you review this?\n  → BotB processes and replies\n\n# allow_bot_messages = &quot;all&quot;\nBotA in thread: here's my analysis\n  → BotB automatically responds (no @mention needed)\n  → Continues until max_bot_turns is reached\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Relevant config</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_bot_messages</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;off&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;off&quot;</code> — ignore bot messages. <code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code> — only process bot messages that @mention this bot. <code>&quot;all&quot;</code> — process all bot messages (capped by <code>max_bot_turns</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>trusted_bot_ids</code></td>\n<td>string[]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Whitelist of bot IDs. For Slack, entries may be Bot User IDs (<code>U...</code>) or Bot IDs (<code>B...</code>); <code>U...</code> matching requires <code>users:read</code> so OpenAB can call <code>bots.info</code>. Empty = any bot (mode permitting). <strong>Admission override:</strong> a trusted bot that @mentions this bot bypasses <code>allow_bot_messages</code> mode entirely (treated as human @mention).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_bot_turns</code></td>\n<td>u32</td>\n<td><code>20</code></td>\n<td>Max consecutive bot turns per thread before throttling. A human message resets the counter.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Safety:</strong> When <code>allow_bot_messages = &quot;all&quot;</code>, a separate hardcoded cap of 10 consecutive bot turns applies regardless of <code>max_bot_turns</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Example config.toml</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\n# Default is &quot;off&quot; — bots ignore all messages from other bots.\n# Set to &quot;mentions&quot; to allow bot-to-bot via explicit @mentions.\nallow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;\n# Default is empty — any bot is allowed (mode permitting).\n# Set trusted_bot_ids to restrict which bots can interact.\ntrusted_bot_ids = [&quot;1111111111&quot;, &quot;2222222222&quot;]\n# Default is 20. Cap consecutive bot turns to prevent runaway loops.\nmax_bot_turns = 10\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Helm chart</h3>\n<p>Same keys are settable from chart values under <code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.discord</code> and\n<code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.slack</code> using camelCase (Helm convention):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  claude:\n    discord:\n      allowBotMessages: &quot;mentions&quot;\n      trustedBotIds: [&quot;1111111111&quot;, &quot;2222222222&quot;]\n      maxBotTurns: 50\n    slack:\n      allowBotMessages: &quot;mentions&quot;\n      trustedBotIds: [&quot;U1111111111&quot;, &quot;U2222222222&quot;]\n      maxBotTurns: 50\n</code></pre>\n<p>When <code>maxBotTurns</code> is omitted from values, the Rust default of 20\napplies. The hard cap of 100 is compiled-in\n(<code>HARD_BOT_TURN_LIMIT</code> in <code>src/bot_turns.rs</code>) and is not chart-tunable.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Quick Reference</h2>\n<pre><code>Layer 0 — Human → Bot (DM)\n  Config: allow_dm, allowed_users\n  DM to bot                     →  Bot replies directly (no thread, no @mention)\n\nLayer 1 — Human → Bot (Channel)\n  Config: allowed_channels, allowed_users, reactions\n  @BotA in channel              →  OAB creates thread, BotA responds\n\nLayer 2 — Human → Bot (Thread)\n  Config: allow_user_messages\n  Message in thread             →  BotA responds (no @mention needed)\n\nLayer 3 — Human → Multiple Bots (Thread)\n  Config: allow_user_messages\n    &quot;involved&quot;                  →  All involved bots respond\n    &quot;mentions&quot;                  →  Only @mentioned bot responds\n    &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;         →  Must @mention once 2+ bots are involved\n\nLayer 4 — Bot → Bot (Thread)\n  Config: allow_bot_messages, trusted_bot_ids, max_bot_turns\n    &quot;off&quot;                       →  Bots ignore other bots\n    &quot;mentions&quot;                  →  Only if explicitly @mentioned by a bot\n    &quot;all&quot;                       →  All involved bots respond (capped)\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Involvement Gate</h2>\n<p>All message routing in OpenAB is guarded by the <strong>involvement gate</strong> — a pre-dispatch check that determines whether a bot should process a message in a given thread. This gate runs <strong>before</strong> <code>allow_user_messages</code> and <code>allow_bot_messages</code> mode checks.</p>\n<h3>Design principle</h3>\n<p><strong>Humans are the gatekeepers.</strong> A bot cannot participate in a thread until a human explicitly pulls it in via @mention. Bots cannot pull other bots into threads — only humans can, <strong>unless</strong> the sending bot is in the target bot's <code>trusted_bot_ids</code> (see <a href=\"#trusted-bot-admission-override\">Trusted bot admission override</a> below).</p>\n<h3>How a bot becomes involved</h3>\n<p>A bot is considered <strong>involved</strong> in a thread if either condition is true:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Thread owner</strong> — the bot created the thread (human @mentioned it in a channel)</li>\n<li><strong>Has participated</strong> — the bot has previously replied in the thread</li>\n</ol>\n<p>A bot that has never posted in a thread is <strong>not involved</strong> and will not receive messages from that thread, regardless of <code>allow_bot_messages</code> or <code>allow_user_messages</code> settings.</p>\n<h3>Gate evaluation order</h3>\n<pre><code>Inbound message in thread\n  │\n  ├─ Is it the bot's own message? → ignore\n  │\n  ├─ Is the bot involved in this thread?\n  │     │\n  │     ├─ YES → proceed to mode checks:\n  │     │         • allow_user_messages (for human messages)\n  │     │         • allow_bot_messages (for bot messages)\n  │     │         • bot_turns cap\n  │     │         → dispatch to session\n  │     │\n  │     └─ NO → is there an explicit @mention of this bot?\n  │               │\n  │               ├─ From a human → pass (bot will reply and become involved)\n  │               │\n  │               └─ From another bot:\n  │                     │\n  │                     ├─ Sender in trusted_bot_ids → pass (same as human @mention)\n  │                     │\n  │                     └─ Otherwise → ❌ DROP (bot-to-bot cannot break the gate)\n  │\n  └─ Message dropped — never reaches Dispatcher or SessionPool\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Why bot-to-bot cannot break the involvement gate</h3>\n<p>This is an intentional safety constraint:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Resource control</strong> — each involved thread creates an agent session (subprocess). Allowing bots to pull other bots in would let a single bot consume session slots across many threads without human oversight.</li>\n<li><strong>Human authority</strong> — the human decides which bots participate in which conversations. This prevents unexpected bot pile-ups.</li>\n<li><strong>Loop prevention</strong> — without this gate, Bot A could @mention Bot B into a thread, Bot B could @mention Bot C, creating unbounded chain reactions across threads.</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Practical impact</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Result</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Human @mentions Bot B in Bot A's thread</td>\n<td>✅ Bot B replies, becomes involved</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot A @mentions Bot B (Bot B not yet involved)</td>\n<td>❌ Silently dropped</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot A @mentions Bot B (Bot B already involved)</td>\n<td>✅ Processed per <code>allow_bot_messages</code> mode</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Human @mentions Bot B, then Bot A @mentions Bot B</td>\n<td>✅ Works — Bot B is already involved</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Trusted</strong> Bot A @mentions Bot B (Bot A in Bot B's <code>trusted_bot_ids</code>)</td>\n<td>✅ Treated as human @mention — Bot B becomes involved</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Trusted bot admission override</h3>\n<p>When a bot is listed in another bot's <code>trusted_bot_ids</code> and explicitly @mentions that bot, the mention is treated identically to a human @mention:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>The target bot becomes <strong>involved</strong> in the thread</li>\n<li>The <code>allow_bot_messages</code> mode check is <strong>bypassed</strong> entirely</li>\n<li>The message is dispatched to the session</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This enables bot-to-bot coordination (e.g. a coordinator bot pulling reviewer bots into threads) without requiring human intervention for every thread.</p>\n<p><strong>Requirements:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>The sending bot must be in the target bot's <code>trusted_bot_ids</code> config</li>\n<li>The sending bot must explicitly @mention the target bot</li>\n<li>Messages from trusted bots <strong>without</strong> @mention still follow normal <code>allow_bot_messages</code> gating</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Safety:</strong> <code>trusted_bot_ids</code> defaults to empty — this feature is entirely opt-in. The <code>max_bot_turns</code> cap still applies after involvement to prevent runaway loops.</p>\n<h3>Workaround for bot-to-bot handoff (without trusted_bot_ids)</h3>\n<p>If you need Bot A to hand off to Bot B in a thread where Bot B is not yet involved:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Pre-involve all bots</strong> — have the human @mention all relevant bots at thread creation (e.g. via a shared role in <code>allowed_role_ids</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Use a shared channel</strong> — configure both bots in the same channel with <code>allow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;</code>, and have the human @mention both bots to start the thread</li>\n</ol>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Messaging Model"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "mimocode",
      "html": "<h1>MiMoCode (mimo)</h1>\n<p>MiMoCode is a fork of OpenCode. It supports ACP over stdio and can be used as an OpenAB agent backend.</p>\n<h2>Setup</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Image</td>\n<td><code>openab-mimocode</code> (or any image with <code>mimo</code> installed)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Command</td>\n<td><code>mimo</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Args</td>\n<td><code>[&quot;acp&quot;]</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Working dir</td>\n<td><code>/home/node</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<p>MiMoCode offers a free tier (<code>MiMo Auto</code>) that requires no API key — just a one-time device auth:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">mimo auth login --provider mimo --method &quot;MiMo Auto (free)&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is <strong>fully non-interactive</strong> and can be used in Dockerfiles, pre-boot hooks, or CI scripts. It sets <code>mimo/mimo-auto</code> as the default model (1M context, free).</p>\n<p>The token expires in ~1 hour but auto-refreshes on next ACP session start. For persistent deployments, run this in a <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> script to ensure fresh auth on every container start.</p>\n<h2>⚠️ Important: SQLite DB Locking</h2>\n<p>MiMoCode uses a SQLite database (<code>~/.local/share/mimocode/mimocode.db</code>) for state. <strong>Only one process can access it at a time.</strong></p>\n<p><strong>Do NOT</strong> run manual <code>mimo</code> commands (e.g. <code>mimo auth login</code>, <code>mimo debug config</code>, <code>mimo models</code>) while <code>mimo acp</code> is actively handling a request. This will corrupt or lock the database, causing all subsequent ACP requests to fail with empty responses or &quot;Connection Lost&quot;.</p>\n<h3>Safe workflow:</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Start the bot (openab spawns <code>mimo acp</code> on first message)</li>\n<li>Auth <strong>before</strong> the first message, or while the session is idle</li>\n<li>If the DB gets corrupted:\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># As root:\nrm -f ~/.local/share/mimocode/mimocode.db*\nchown -R node:node ~/.local/share/mimocode/\n# As node:\nmimo auth login\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>AWS/Bedrock Auto-Detection</h2>\n<p>When running on AWS (ECS, EC2), MiMoCode auto-detects AWS credentials and registers <code>amazon-bedrock</code> as a provider. Combined with its <code>Provider.sort()</code> logic, ACP mode picks the &quot;best&quot; (paid) model — which fails silently with 0 tokens if you don't have a paid Xiaomi account.</p>\n<h3>Solution: pre_boot hook</h3>\n<p>Add this to your <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> script:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Write mimo config — disables Bedrock, sets free model as default\nmkdir -p ~/.config/mimocode\necho '{&quot;disabled_providers&quot;:[&quot;amazon-bedrock&quot;],&quot;model&quot;:&quot;mimo/mimo-auto&quot;}' &gt; ~/.config/mimocode/config.json\n\n# Provision free-tier auth (non-interactive, token refreshes each boot)\nmimo auth login --provider mimo --method &quot;MiMo Auto (free)&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null || true\n</code></pre>\n<p>This ensures:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Bedrock is never auto-detected</li>\n<li><code>mimo/mimo-auto</code> is the default model (not <code>xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro-ultraspeed</code>)</li>\n<li>Fresh auth token every container start</li>\n</ol>\n<p>For paid Xiaomi accounts, replace <code>mimo/mimo-auto</code> with your preferred model (e.g. <code>xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro</code>).</p>\n<h2>Config (gist)</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;mimo&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;]\nenv = { GHPOOL_URL = &quot;http://ghpool.openab.local:8080&quot;, PATH = &quot;/home/node/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Known Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><code>mimo acp</code> does not accept <code>--model</code> flag (unlike the TUI)</li>\n<li>Default model is set during <code>mimo auth login</code> and stored in the DB</li>\n<li>No <code>config set</code> CLI command — model selection is via auth flow only</li>\n<li>The <code>-m/--model</code> flag only works for TUI/run modes, not ACP</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "MiMoCode (mimo)"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "msteams-enterprise",
      "html": "<h1>Microsoft Teams Enterprise Deployment</h1>\n<p>Deploy OpenAB with MS Teams in an enterprise Kubernetes environment. This guide covers Azure Entra ID configuration, Azure Bot Service setup, Teams app packaging, and Kubernetes deployment.</p>\n<pre><code>Teams Client → Bot Framework → K8s Ingress (HTTPS + TLS) → Gateway pod → OAB pod\n                                     ↑\n                        Company's existing infrastructure\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>An Azure subscription with permissions to create resources</li>\n<li>A Microsoft 365 tenant with Teams enabled (Commercial Cloud Trial works for testing)</li>\n<li>A Kubernetes cluster with an Ingress controller and TLS</li>\n<li><code>kubectl</code> CLI</li>\n<li>IT admin access to Teams Admin Center (for app approval)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Architecture Overview</h2>\n<p>The deployment consists of two components:</p>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Your Kubernetes Cluster                                    │\n│                                                             │\n│  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐  │\n│  │   Ingress    │───▶│   Gateway    │◀──▶│     OAB      │  │\n│  │  (HTTPS/TLS) │    │  (BYO deploy)│ WS │  (Helm chart)│  │\n│  └──────┬───────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘  │\n│         │                                                   │\n└─────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n          │ HTTPS\n┌─────────┴───────────┐\n│  Bot Framework      │\n│  (Microsoft Cloud)  │\n└─────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Component</th>\n<th>Deployed by</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Gateway</strong></td>\n<td>You (K8s Deployment or Docker)</td>\n<td>Receives Bot Framework webhooks, validates JWT, routes replies. Reads <code>TEAMS_*</code> env vars.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>OAB</strong></td>\n<td>Helm chart (<code>openab</code>)</td>\n<td>Connects outbound to Gateway via WebSocket. No inbound ports needed.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Step 1: Register an Azure Entra ID Application</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <a href=\"https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade\">Azure Portal → Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations</a></li>\n<li>Click <strong>New registration</strong></li>\n<li>Configure:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Name</strong>: <code>openab-teams-bot</code> (or your preferred name)</li>\n<li><strong>Supported account types</strong>: <strong>Single tenant</strong> (Accounts in this organizational directory only)</li>\n<li><strong>Redirect URI</strong>: leave empty</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Register</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<p>After creation, note from the <strong>Overview</strong> page:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Value</th>\n<th>Used As</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Application (client) ID</td>\n<td><code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Directory (tenant) ID</td>\n<td><code>&lt;YOUR_TENANT_ID&gt;</code> in OAuth endpoint</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Create a Client Secret</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>Certificates &amp; secrets</strong> → <strong>Client secrets</strong> → <strong>New client secret</strong></li>\n<li>Set a description and expiration (recommended: 12 or 24 months)</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Add</strong></li>\n<li><strong>Copy the Value immediately</strong> — it is only shown once → <code>TEAMS_APP_SECRET</code></li>\n</ol>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Security note</strong>: Store the client secret in a Kubernetes Secret. Never commit it to source control. Set a calendar reminder to rotate before expiration.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: Multi-tenant bot creation was deprecated by Microsoft on July 31, 2025. Single Tenant is the only supported path for new bots.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Step 2: Create an Azure Bot Resource</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <a href=\"https://portal.azure.com/#create/hub\">Azure Portal → Create a resource</a> → search <strong>Azure Bot</strong> → <strong>Create</strong></li>\n<li>Configure:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Bot handle</strong>: a unique name (e.g. <code>openab-prod</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Subscription / Resource group</strong>: your enterprise subscription</li>\n<li><strong>Pricing tier</strong>: F0 (free) for testing, S1 for production</li>\n<li><strong>Type of App</strong>: <strong>Single Tenant</strong></li>\n<li><strong>Creation type</strong>: <strong>Use existing app registration</strong></li>\n<li><strong>App ID</strong>: paste <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code> from Step 1</li>\n<li><strong>App tenant ID</strong>: paste your Directory (tenant) ID</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Review + Create</strong> → <strong>Create</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Configure the Messaging Endpoint</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to the Bot resource → <strong>Configuration</strong></li>\n<li>Set <strong>Messaging endpoint</strong> to your Kubernetes Ingress URL:\n<pre><code>https://&lt;YOUR_INGRESS_HOST&gt;/webhook/teams\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Enable the Teams Channel</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>Channels</strong> → click <strong>Microsoft Teams</strong></li>\n<li>Accept the terms of service → <strong>Save</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Testing tip</strong>: After enabling the Teams channel, use the <strong>Open in Teams</strong> link (Azure Bot → Channels → Teams) for quick testing without uploading an app package. This link only works for people who have it — it does not make the bot discoverable org-wide.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>⚠️ Do not use &quot;Test in Web Chat&quot;</strong> for outbound reply testing. Azure Portal's Web Chat uses <code>webchat.botframework.com</code> which returns 403 for Single Tenant bot replies. Only real Teams clients (<code>smba.trafficmanager.net</code>) work for outbound.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Step 3: Build a Teams App Manifest</h2>\n<p>Create a directory with three
