files:</p>\n<h3><code>manifest.json</code></h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;$schema&quot;: &quot;https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/json-schemas/teams/v1.25/MicrosoftTeams.schema.json&quot;,\n  &quot;manifestVersion&quot;: &quot;1.25&quot;,\n  &quot;version&quot;: &quot;1.0.0&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;&lt;GENERATE_A_UUID_V4&gt;&quot;,\n  &quot;developer&quot;: {\n    &quot;name&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_ORGANIZATION_NAME&gt;&quot;,\n    &quot;websiteUrl&quot;: &quot;https://&lt;YOUR_COMPANY_WEBSITE&gt;&quot;,\n    &quot;privacyUrl&quot;: &quot;https://&lt;YOUR_COMPANY_WEBSITE&gt;/privacy&quot;,\n    &quot;termsOfUseUrl&quot;: &quot;https://&lt;YOUR_COMPANY_WEBSITE&gt;/terms&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;name&quot;: {\n    &quot;short&quot;: &quot;OpenAB&quot;,\n    &quot;full&quot;: &quot;OpenAB AI Assistant&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;description&quot;: {\n    &quot;short&quot;: &quot;AI coding assistant powered by OpenAB&quot;,\n    &quot;full&quot;: &quot;Connect to an AI coding assistant through Microsoft Teams.&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;icons&quot;: {\n    &quot;outline&quot;: &quot;outline.png&quot;,\n    &quot;color&quot;: &quot;color.png&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;accentColor&quot;: &quot;#ffffff&quot;,\n  &quot;bots&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;botId&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_TEAMS_APP_ID&gt;&quot;,\n      &quot;scopes&quot;: [&quot;personal&quot;, &quot;team&quot;, &quot;groupChat&quot;],\n      &quot;isNotificationOnly&quot;: false,\n      &quot;supportsFiles&quot;: false\n    }\n  ],\n  &quot;validDomains&quot;: []\n}\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>id</code> — Teams app ID (generate a fresh UUID v4, not the same as <code>botId</code>)</li>\n<li><code>botId</code> — Azure Entra ID Application (client) ID from Step 1</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Icons</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>outline.png</code> — 32×32 transparent background, white icon</li>\n<li><code>color.png</code> — 192×192 full-color icon</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Package</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">zip openab-teams-app.zip manifest.json outline.png color.png\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Step 4: Deploy the Gateway</h2>\n<p>The Gateway is deployed separately from the OAB Helm chart. Use a standard Kubernetes Deployment:</p>\n<h3>Gateway Secret</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: v1\nkind: Secret\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-gateway-teams\ntype: Opaque\nstringData:\n  TEAMS_APP_ID: &quot;&lt;YOUR_APPLICATION_ID&gt;&quot;\n  TEAMS_APP_SECRET: &quot;&lt;YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET&gt;&quot;\n  TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT: &quot;https://login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;YOUR_TENANT_ID&gt;/oauth2/v2.0/token&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>⚠️ Single Tenant bots must set <code>TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT</code></strong> to the tenant-specific endpoint. The default (<code>botframework.com</code>) only works for Multi Tenant bots and will cause <code>401 Unauthorized</code> errors. This is the #1 setup pitfall.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Gateway Deployment</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: apps/v1\nkind: Deployment\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-gateway\nspec:\n  replicas: 1\n  selector:\n    matchLabels:\n      app: openab-gateway\n  template:\n    metadata:\n      labels:\n        app: openab-gateway\n    spec:\n      containers:\n        - name: gateway\n          image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:latest\n          ports:\n            - containerPort: 8080\n          envFrom:\n            - secretRef:\n                name: openab-gateway-teams\n          env:\n            - name: RUST_LOG\n              value: &quot;info&quot;\n          livenessProbe:\n            httpGet:\n              path: /health\n              port: 8080\n---\napiVersion: v1\nkind: Service\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-gateway\nspec:\n  selector:\n    app: openab-gateway\n  ports:\n    - port: 8080\n      targetPort: 8080\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Ingress</h3>\n<p>Route Bot Framework webhooks to the Gateway using your existing Ingress controller:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1\nkind: Ingress\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-gateway\n  annotations:\n    # Adjust for your Ingress controller (nginx, ALB, Traefik, etc.)\n    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: &quot;true&quot;\nspec:\n  tls:\n    - hosts:\n        - &lt;YOUR_INGRESS_HOST&gt;\n      secretName: &lt;YOUR_TLS_SECRET&gt;\n  rules:\n    - host: &lt;YOUR_INGRESS_HOST&gt;\n      http:\n        paths:\n          - path: /webhook/teams\n            pathType: Prefix\n            backend:\n              service:\n                name: openab-gateway\n                port:\n                  number: 8080\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Bot Framework requires HTTPS. Your Ingress controller handles TLS termination — the Gateway pod listens on plain HTTP (:8080).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Step 5: Deploy OAB with Helm</h2>\n<p>OAB connects outbound to the Gateway via WebSocket:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab oci://ghcr.io/openabdev/charts/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.url=&quot;ws://openab-gateway:8080/ws&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.platform=&quot;teams&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>The OAB pod does not need any Teams credentials — it only needs the Gateway WebSocket URL.</p>\n<h2>Step 6: IT Admin — Approve the Teams App</h2>\n<p>Enterprise tenants typically restrict custom app installation. An IT admin must approve the app.</p>\n<h3>Upload the App Package</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <a href=\"https://admin.teams.microsoft.com/\">Teams Admin Center</a> → <strong>Teams apps</strong> → <strong>Manage apps</strong></li>\n<li>Click <strong>Upload new app</strong> → select <code>openab-teams-app.zip</code></li>\n<li>The app appears with status <strong>Blocked</strong> (default for new custom apps)</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Configure Permission Policies</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>Teams apps</strong> → <strong>Permission policies</strong></li>\n<li>Edit the <strong>Global (Org-wide default)</strong> policy or create a new one:\n<ul>\n<li>Under <strong>Custom apps</strong>, allow the OpenAB app</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>If using a custom policy, assign it to target users or groups</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Configure Setup Policies (Optional)</h3>\n<p>To pin the app for users automatically:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>Teams apps</strong> → <strong>Setup policies</strong></li>\n<li>Edit the relevant policy → <strong>Installed apps</strong> → <strong>Add apps</strong> → select OpenAB</li>\n<li>Optionally add to <strong>Pinned apps</strong> for sidebar visibility</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Bot Discovery Methods</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Method</th>\n<th>Who can find it</th>\n<th>Best for</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Open in Teams link</strong></td>\n<td>Only people with the link</td>\n<td>Quick testing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Teams Admin Center upload</strong></td>\n<td>Everyone in the org</td>\n<td>Enterprise deployment</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>App Store publish</strong></td>\n<td>Everyone worldwide</td>\n<td>Commercial bots</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Verify</h3>\n<p>After policy propagation (may take up to 24 hours):</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Users go to <strong>Apps</strong> → <strong>Built for your org</strong> → find OpenAB → <strong>Add</strong></li>\n<li>For personal chat: open the app and start chatting</li>\n<li>For channels: add the app to a team → use <code>@OpenAB</code> to mention the bot</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Tenant Allowlist</h2>\n<p>Restrict which Azure AD tenants can interact with the bot by adding to the Gateway Secret:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">stringData:\n  TEAMS_ALLOWED_TENANTS: &quot;&lt;YOUR_TENANT_ID&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Multiple tenants: <code>&quot;&lt;TENANT_ID_1&gt;,&lt;TENANT_ID_2&gt;&quot;</code>. If not set, all tenants are allowed.</p>\n<h2>Sovereign Cloud Configuration</h2>\n<p>For Azure Government or Azure China deployments, add to the Gateway Secret:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Cloud</th>\n<th><code>TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT</code></th>\n<th><code>TEAMS_OPENID_METADATA</code></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Public (default)</td>\n<td><code>login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;TENANT&gt;/...</code></td>\n<td><code>login.botframework.com/...</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Azure Government</td>\n<td><code>login.microsoftonline.us/&lt;TENANT&gt;/...</code></td>\n<td><code>login.botframework.azure.us/...</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Azure China (21Vianet)</td>\n<td><code>login.partner.microsoftonline.cn/&lt;TENANT&gt;/...</code></td>\n<td><code>login.botframework.azure.cn/...</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Environment Variables Reference (Gateway)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Azure Entra ID application (client) ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_APP_SECRET</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Azure Entra ID client secret</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT</code></td>\n<td>Yes (Single Tenant)</td>\n<td><code>https://login.microsoftonline.com/botframework.com/oauth2/v2.0/token</code></td>\n<td>Tenant-specific OAuth endpoint</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_OPENID_METADATA</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/openidconfiguration</code></td>\n<td>OpenID metadata for JWT validation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_ALLOWED_TENANTS</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>(allow all)</td>\n<td>Comma-separated tenant IDs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>/webhook/teams</code></td>\n<td>Webhook endpoint path</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3>401 Unauthorized when bot tries to reply</h3>\n<p>OAuth endpoint mismatch. Single Tenant bots must use the tenant-specific endpoint.</p>\n<p><strong>Fix</strong>: Verify <code>TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT</code> is set to <code>https://login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;YOUR_TENANT_ID&gt;/oauth2/v2.0/token</code></p>\n<h3>&quot;Test in Web Chat&quot; works but Teams doesn't reply</h3>\n<p>Web Chat uses Direct Line (<code>webchat.botframework.com</code>), which has different auth than Teams (<code>smba.trafficmanager.net</code>). Web Chat may accept inbound but reject outbound for Single Tenant bots.</p>\n<p><strong>Fix</strong>: Always test with a real Teams client. Do not rely on Web Chat for outbound reply testing.</p>\n<h3>Bot doesn't appear in Teams</h3>\n<p>IT admin has not approved the custom app, or permission policy hasn't propagated.</p>\n<p><strong>Fix</strong>:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Verify the app is uploaded in Teams Admin Center → Manage apps</li>\n<li>Check Permission policies allow the custom app</li>\n<li>Wait up to 24 hours for policy propagation</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Gateway receives webhook but no reply in Teams</h3>\n<p>Check Gateway pod logs:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl logs deployment/openab-gateway --tail=50\n</code></pre>\n<p>Look for: <code>teams → gateway</code> (received) → <code>gateway → teams</code> (sent) → <code>teams activity sent</code> (success) or <code>teams send error</code> (failure).</p>\n<h3>JWT validation failed</h3>\n<p>The Gateway auto-refreshes JWKS on cache miss. If persistent, verify OpenID metadata is reachable:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-gateway -- curl -s https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/openidconfiguration\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Security Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Credentials in Kubernetes Secrets</strong> — never in ConfigMaps or Deployment manifests</li>\n<li><strong>Rotate client secrets</strong> before expiration — set a reminder based on the expiration chosen in Step 1</li>\n<li><strong>Use tenant allowlist</strong> in production — restrict <code>TEAMS_ALLOWED_TENANTS</code> to your organization's tenant ID</li>\n<li><strong>Network policies</strong> — consider restricting Gateway pod egress to Bot Framework endpoints</li>\n<li><strong>OAB pod has no inbound exposure</strong> — connects outbound to Gateway only</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/\">Azure Bot Service documentation</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/bot-service-quickstart-registration\">Register a bot with Azure</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-permission-policies\">Teams app permission policies</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-custom-app-policies-and-settings\">Teams custom app policies</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication\">Bot Framework authentication</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/resources/schema/manifest-schema\">Teams app manifest schema</a></li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "MS Teams (enterprise)"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "msteams-selfhosted",
      "html": "<h1>Microsoft Teams Setup (Self-Hosted)</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Unified Mode (v0.9.0+):</strong> The OAB binary now embeds the Teams adapter directly. Set <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code> as an env var — no separate gateway container or <code>[gateway]</code> config needed. See <a href=\"/openab/telegram#unified-mode-recommended\">Telegram docs</a> for the pattern.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Unified Config (Kiro + Teams)</h3>\n<p><strong>Minimal:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Recommended:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;compact&quot;\n\n[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Set <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code> and <code>TEAMS_APP_SECRET</code> on the container. No <code>[gateway]</code> needed.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Standalone Gateway Mode (Legacy)</h2>\n<p>Connect a Microsoft Teams bot to OpenAB via the Custom Gateway using a self-hosted Docker Compose stack.</p>\n<pre><code>Teams (Bot Framework) ──POST──▶ Gateway (:8080) ◀──WebSocket── OAB Pod\n                                                  (OAB connects out)\n                       ◀──REST──── (Bot Framework reply)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Docker and Docker Compose installed</li>\n<li>A Microsoft 365 / Azure AD account with permission to register apps and create Azure Bot resources</li>\n<li>A public HTTPS URL for the gateway (Cloudflare Tunnel, ngrok, Tailscale Funnel, etc.) — Bot Framework requires HTTPS endpoints</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>1. Register an Azure AD Application</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <a href=\"https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade\">Azure Portal → App registrations</a> → <strong>New registration</strong></li>\n<li>Name: <code>openab-teams-bot</code> (or anything you like)</li>\n<li><strong>Supported account types</strong>:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Single tenant</strong> — only your organization can use the bot (most common for internal use)</li>\n<li><strong>Multitenant</strong> — anyone with a Microsoft 365 account can install</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Leave <strong>Redirect URI</strong> empty → Register</li>\n</ol>\n<p>After creation, copy from the <strong>Overview</strong> page:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Application (client) ID</strong> → <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code></li>\n<li><strong>Directory (tenant) ID</strong> → needed for <code>TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT</code> if Single tenant</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Then go to <strong>Certificates &amp; secrets</strong> → <strong>New client secret</strong> → copy the <strong>Value</strong> (not the Secret ID) → <code>TEAMS_APP_SECRET</code>.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Client secrets are only shown once. Store it before leaving the page.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>2. Create an Azure Bot Resource</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Azure Portal → <strong>Create a resource</strong> → search <strong>Azure Bot</strong> → Create</li>\n<li><strong>Bot handle</strong>: pick a unique name (e.g. <code>openab</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Subscription / Resource group</strong>: pick yours</li>\n<li><strong>Pricing tier</strong>: F0 (free) is fine for testing</li>\n<li><strong>Microsoft App ID</strong>:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Type of App</strong>: must match what you picked in step 1 (<code>Single Tenant</code> or <code>Multi Tenant</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Creation type</strong>: <strong>Use existing app registration</strong></li>\n<li><strong>App ID</strong>: paste the <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code> from step 1</li>\n<li><strong>App tenant ID</strong> (Single tenant only): paste your tenant ID</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Review + Create</li>\n</ol>\n<p>After deployment, open the bot:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Configuration</strong> → <strong>Messaging endpoint</strong>: <code>https://&lt;YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST&gt;/webhook/teams</code></li>\n<li><strong>Channels</strong> → click <strong>Microsoft Teams</strong> → accept terms → save</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>3. Build a Teams App Manifest</h2>\n<p>Bot Framework only delivers messages once a Teams app installs your bot.</p>\n<h3>Option A — Teams Developer Portal (UI)</h3>\n<p>In <a href=\"https://dev.teams.microsoft.com\">Teams Developer Portal</a> → <strong>Apps</strong> → <strong>New app</strong>:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Basic information</strong> → fill name, description, developer info</li>\n<li><strong>App features</strong> → <strong>Bot</strong> → <strong>Create new bot</strong> → select <strong>Use existing bot ID</strong> → paste <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code></li>\n<li>Pick the scopes the bot needs:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Personal</strong> — 1:1 chat</li>\n<li><strong>Team</strong> — channel chat (must be @mentioned)</li>\n<li><strong>Group chat</strong> — multi-person DMs</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Publish</strong> → <strong>Publish to your org</strong> (single tenant) or sideload via <strong>Apps for your org</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Option B — Hand-rolled manifest.json</h3>\n<p>Create <code>manifest.json</code> next to two icons (<code>outline.png</code> — transparent 32×32 white, <code>color.png</code> — 192×192 colored), zip them, and in Teams: <strong>Apps → Manage your apps → Upload a custom app</strong>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;$schema&quot;: &quot;https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/json-schemas/teams/v1.25/MicrosoftTeams.schema.json&quot;,\n  &quot;manifestVersion&quot;: &quot;1.25&quot;,\n  &quot;version&quot;: &quot;1.0.0&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;&lt;GENERATE_A_UUID_V4&gt;&quot;,\n  &quot;developer&quot;: {\n    &quot;name&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_ORG&gt;&quot;,\n    &quot;websiteUrl&quot;: &quot;https://example.com&quot;,\n    &quot;privacyUrl&quot;: &quot;https://example.com/privacy&quot;,\n    &quot;termsOfUseUrl&quot;: &quot;https://example.com/terms&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;name&quot;: {\n    &quot;short&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_BOT_SHORT_NAME&gt;&quot;,\n    &quot;full&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_BOT_FULL_NAME&gt;&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;description&quot;: {\n    &quot;short&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_BOT_SHORT_DESCRIPTION&gt;&quot;,\n    &quot;full&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_BOT_FULL_DESCRIPTION&gt;&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;icons&quot;: {\n    &quot;outline&quot;: &quot;outline.png&quot;,\n    &quot;color&quot;: &quot;color.png&quot;\n  },\n  &quot;accentColor&quot;: &quot;#ffffff&quot;,\n  &quot;bots&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;botId&quot;: &quot;&lt;YOUR_TEAMS_APP_ID&gt;&quot;,\n      &quot;scopes&quot;: [&quot;personal&quot;, &quot;team&quot;, &quot;groupChat&quot;],\n      &quot;isNotificationOnly&quot;: false,\n      &quot;supportsFiles&quot;: false\n    }\n  ],\n  &quot;validDomains&quot;: []\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Notes:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>id</code> is the <strong>Teams app id</strong> — generate a fresh UUID v4 (<code>uuidgen</code>). It is <strong>not</strong> the same as <code>botId</code>.</li>\n<li><code>botId</code> is the <strong>Microsoft App (Bot) id</strong> from step 1 (the value you put in <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code>).</li>\n<li>The three <code>developer.*</code> URLs are required by the schema. They can point at your GitHub repo / privacy page / license — they just have to resolve.</li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote>\n<p>If your tenant requires admin approval, an admin must approve the published app in Teams Admin Center → Manage apps.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>4. Self-Hosted Deployment (Docker Compose)</h2>\n<p>Drop these three files into a project directory and run <code>docker compose up -d</code>.</p>\n<h3><code>.env</code></h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-env\"># From Azure AD app registration (step 1)\nTEAMS_APP_ID=&quot;&lt;YOUR_APPLICATION_ID&gt;&quot;\nTEAMS_APP_SECRET=&quot;&lt;YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET&gt;&quot;\n\n# Single tenant: must point at your tenant\n# Multi tenant: leave this line out (uses default)\nTEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT=&quot;https://login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;YOUR_TENANT_ID&gt;/oauth2/v2.0/token&quot;\n\n# Only needed if you use the Cloudflare Tunnel service below.\n# Skip this line if you expose the gateway via a different reverse proxy.\nTUNNEL_TOKEN=&quot;&lt;YOUR_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN&gt;&quot;\n\nRUST_LOG=info\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><code>.env</code> should be <code>.gitignore</code>d — it holds your bot secret.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3><code>docker-compose.yaml</code></h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">services:\n  gateway:\n    image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:latest\n    container_name: gateway\n    env_file:\n      - .env\n    ports:\n      - 8080:8080\n\n  openab:\n    image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:latest\n    container_name: openab\n    volumes:\n      - ./config.toml:/etc/openab/config.toml\n      - ./data:/home/agent\n    env_file:\n      - .env\n    depends_on:\n      - gateway\n\n  # Optional — only include this service if you want to use Cloudflare Tunnel.\n  # Drop this block if you reverse-proxy gateway:8080 some other way.\n  tunnels:\n    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest\n    command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run --token ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}\n    env_file:\n      - .env\n    depends_on:\n      - gateway\n      - openab\n</code></pre>\n<h3><code>config.toml</code></h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;kiro-cli&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 10\nsession_ttl_hours = 24\n\n[reactions]\nenabled = true\n\n[gateway]\nurl = &quot;ws://gateway:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;teams&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Start the stack</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker compose up -d\ndocker compose logs -f gateway openab\n</code></pre>\n<h2>5. Public HTTPS Exposure</h2>\n<p>Bot Framework needs to reach the gateway over HTTPS. Any reverse proxy works — pick whichever fits your setup.</p>\n<h3>Option A — Cloudflare Tunnel</h3>\n<p>In the <a href=\"https://one.dash.cloudflare.com/\">Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard</a>, open your tunnel and add a public hostname:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Subdomain / Hostname</td>\n<td><code>openab-bot</code> (or anything)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Path</td>\n<td><code>/webhook/teams</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Service type</td>\n<td><code>HTTP</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>URL</td>\n<td><code>gateway:8080</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Option B — ngrok / Tailscale Funnel / other reverse proxy</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># ngrok example\nngrok http 8080\n# → https://&lt;random&gt;.ngrok-free.app/webhook/teams\n</code></pre>\n<p>Drop the <code>tunnels</code> service and the <code>TUNNEL_TOKEN</code> line in <code>.env</code>; just expose <code>gateway:8080</code> to the internet however you prefer (k8s ingress, Caddy, nginx + Let's Encrypt, Tailscale Funnel, etc.).</p>\n<h3>Point Bot Framework at your endpoint</h3>\n<p>Azure Portal → your bot → <strong>Configuration</strong> → <strong>Messaging endpoint</strong>: <code>https://&lt;YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST&gt;/webhook/teams</code></p>\n<h2>6. Install the Bot in Teams</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Apps</strong> → <strong>Manage your apps</strong> → <strong>Built for your org</strong> → find your app → <strong>Add</strong></li>\n<li>For personal chat: open the app, start chatting</li>\n<li>For a channel: click the app → <strong>Add to a team</strong> → choose the team → use <code>@&lt;bot-name&gt;</code> in conversation</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Supported Features</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>1:1 personal chat</strong> — direct message the bot, get an agent response</li>\n<li><strong>Channel chat</strong> — bot responds when @mentioned</li>\n<li><strong>Group chat</strong> — same @mention gating</li>\n<li><strong>JWT validation</strong> — every webhook is verified against Microsoft's public JWKS</li>\n<li><strong>Markdown rendering</strong> — replies are sent with <code>textFormat: &quot;markdown&quot;</code></li>\n<li><strong>Tenant allowlist</strong> — set <code>TEAMS_ALLOWED_TENANTS=&lt;tenant-id-1&gt;,&lt;tenant-id-2&gt;</code> to restrict which tenants can talk to the bot</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Current Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Reactions</strong> — status reactions (👀 / 🤔 / ⚡ / 🆗) are silently dropped for Teams replies</li>\n<li><strong>Thread replies</strong> — all messages in a personal chat or channel share one agent session</li>\n<li><strong>Streaming edits</strong> — replies are sent as one final message, not progressively edited</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Environment Variables</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Azure AD application (client) ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_APP_SECRET</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Azure AD client secret value</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT</code></td>\n<td>Single tenant: Yes</td>\n<td><code>https://login.microsoftonline.com/botframework.com/oauth2/v2.0/token</code></td>\n<td>Override for single tenant bots</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_OPENID_METADATA</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/openidconfiguration</code></td>\n<td>OpenID metadata for JWT validation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_ALLOWED_TENANTS</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>(allow all)</td>\n<td>Comma-separated tenant IDs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TEAMS_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>/webhook/teams</code></td>\n<td>URL path the gateway listens on</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<p><strong>401 Unauthorized when bot tries to reply</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Almost always means OAuth endpoint vs. app type mismatch.</li>\n<li>Single tenant bot → set <code>TEAMS_OAUTH_ENDPOINT=https://login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;YOUR_TENANT_ID&gt;/oauth2/v2.0/token</code></li>\n<li>Multi tenant bot → leave default, but verify <code>TEAMS_APP_ID</code> and <code>TEAMS_APP_SECRET</code> are correct.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong><code>teams: no service_url for conversation</code> in gateway logs</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Gateway was restarted and the in-memory cache was cleared. Have the user send another message.</li>\n<li>Or the webhook never arrived — check Bot Framework webhook URL points at the right gateway.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong><code>teams JWT validation failed</code> in gateway logs</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>The gateway auto-refreshes JWKS on miss, so this usually resolves on retry.</li>\n<li>If it persists, check <code>TEAMS_OPENID_METADATA</code> is reachable from the gateway container.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Webhook returns 200 but no agent response</strong></p>\n<p>Check <code>docker compose logs gateway openab</code> and look for the trace:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>teams → gateway</code> (gateway received webhook)</li>\n<li><code>processing message channel_platform=teams</code> (OAB picked up the event)</li>\n<li><code>sending reply to gateway platform=teams</code> (OAB sent the reply over WS)</li>\n<li><code>gateway → teams</code> (gateway calling Bot Framework REST API)</li>\n<li><code>teams activity sent</code> (success) or <code>teams send error</code> (failure)</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Whichever step is missing tells you where the break is.</p>\n<p><strong>Bot doesn't appear when @mentioning in a channel</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>The Teams app must be installed in the team (Apps → Built for your org → Add to a team).</li>\n<li>If your tenant blocks third-party apps, an admin must approve in Teams Admin Center → Manage apps.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>References</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-api-reference\">Bot Framework REST API</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication\">Azure Bot Service authentication</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://dev.teams.microsoft.com\">Teams Developer Portal</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/resources/schema/manifest-schema\">Teams app manifest schema</a></li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "MS Teams (self-hosted)"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "multi-agent",
      "html": "<h1>Multi-Agent Setup</h1>\n<p>You can run multiple agents in a single Helm release. Each agent key in the <code>agents</code> map creates its own Deployment, ConfigMap, Secret, and PVC.</p>\n<h2>Example: Kiro + Claude Code</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.botToken=&quot;$KIRO_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.kiro.discord.allowedChannels[0]=KIRO_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.claude.discord.botToken=&quot;$CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.claude.discord.allowedChannels[0]=CLAUDE_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.claude.command=claude-agent-acp \\\n  --set agents.claude.workingDir=/home/node\n</code></pre>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Each <code>agents.&lt;name&gt;</code> entry creates an independent set of Kubernetes resources (Deployment, ConfigMap, Secret, PVC)</li>\n<li>Each agent gets its own Discord bot token and allowed channels</li>\n<li>Agents run in separate pods and don't share state</li>\n<li>Set <code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.enabled: false</code> to skip creating resources for an agent</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Example: All Four Agents</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.botToken=&quot;$KIRO_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.kiro.discord.allowedChannels[0]=KIRO_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.claude.discord.botToken=&quot;$CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.claude.discord.allowedChannels[0]=CLAUDE_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.claude.command=claude-agent-acp \\\n  --set agents.claude.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set agents.codex.discord.botToken=&quot;$CODEX_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.codex.discord.allowedChannels[0]=CODEX_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.codex.command=codex-acp \\\n  --set agents.codex.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set agents.gemini.discord.botToken=&quot;$GEMINI_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.gemini.discord.allowedChannels[0]=GEMINI_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.gemini.command=gemini \\\n  --set agents.gemini.args='{--acp}' \\\n  --set agents.gemini.workingDir=/home/node\n</code></pre>\n<p>See individual agent docs for authentication steps:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/kiro\">Kiro CLI</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/claude-code\">Claude Code</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/codex\">Codex</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/gemini\">Gemini</a></li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Bot-to-Bot Communication</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p>📖 Full config options: <a href=\"/openab/config-reference\">docs/config-reference.md</a></p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>By default, each agent ignores messages from other bots. To enable multi-agent collaboration in the same channel (e.g. a code review bot handing off to a deploy bot), configure <code>allow_bot_messages</code> in each agent's <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nallow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;  # recommended\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Modes</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Value</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n<th>Loop risk</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;off&quot;</code> (default)</td>\n<td>Ignore all bot messages</td>\n<td>None</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Only respond to bot messages that @mention this bot</td>\n<td>Very low — bots must explicitly @mention each other</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>&quot;all&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Respond to all bot messages</td>\n<td>Mitigated by turn cap (10 consecutive bot messages)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Which mode should I use?</h3>\n<p><strong><code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code> is recommended for most setups.</strong> It enables collaboration while acting as a natural loop breaker — Bot A only processes Bot B's message if Bot B explicitly @mentions Bot A. Two bots won't accidentally ping-pong.</p>\n<p>Use <code>&quot;all&quot;</code> only when bots need to react to each other's messages without explicit mentions (e.g. monitoring bots). A hard cap of 10 consecutive bot-to-bot turns prevents infinite loops.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>💡 User messages in multi-bot threads:</strong> The default <code>allow_user_messages = &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;</code> already handles the user→bot side — once multiple bots are in a thread, users must @mention the specific bot they want to respond. No extra config needed.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Example: Code Review → Deploy handoff</h3>\n<pre><code>┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ Discord Channel #dev                                     │\n│                                                          │\n│  👤 User: &quot;Review this PR and deploy if it looks good&quot;   │\n│       │                                                  │\n│       ▼                                                  │\n│  🤖 Kiro (allow_bot_messages = &quot;off&quot;):                   │\n│       &quot;LGTM — tests pass, no security issues.            │\n│        @DeployBot please deploy to staging.&quot;             │\n│       │                                                  │\n│       ▼                                                  │\n│  🤖 Deploy Bot (allow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;):        │\n│       &quot;Deploying to staging... ✅ Done.&quot;                  │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>Note: the review bot doesn't need <code>allow_bot_messages</code> enabled — only the bot that needs to <em>receive</em> bot messages does.</p>\n<h3>Helm values</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.botToken=&quot;$KIRO_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.allowBotMessages=&quot;off&quot; \\\n  --set agents.deploy.discord.botToken=&quot;$DEPLOY_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set agents.deploy.discord.allowBotMessages=&quot;mentions&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Safety</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>The bot's own messages are <strong>always</strong> ignored, regardless of setting</li>\n<li><code>&quot;mentions&quot;</code> mode is a natural loop breaker — no rate limiter needed</li>\n<li><code>&quot;all&quot;</code> mode has a hard cap of 10 consecutive bot-to-bot turns per channel</li>\n<li>Channel and user allowlists still apply to bot messages</li>\n<li><code>trusted_bot_ids</code> further restricts which bots are allowed through</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Restricting to specific bots</h3>\n<p>If you only want to accept messages from specific bots (e.g. your own deploy bot), add their Discord user IDs:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[discord]\nallow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;\ntrusted_bot_ids = [&quot;123456789012345678&quot;]  # only this bot's messages pass through\n</code></pre>\n<p>When <code>trusted_bot_ids</code> is empty (default), any bot can pass through (subject to the mode check). When set, only listed bots are accepted — all others are silently ignored.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Multi-Agent Setup"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "native-agent",
      "html": "<h1>Native Agent (openab-agent)</h1>\n<p>A lightweight, native Rust coding agent with built-in ACP support and ChatGPT subscription authentication. No Node.js, no Python, no adapter layer.</p>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Build\ncd openab-agent &amp;&amp; cargo build --release\n\n# Authenticate (browser flow — recommended)\nopenab-agent auth codex-oauth\n\n# Headless server (paste callback URL)\nopenab-agent auth codex-oauth --no-browser\n\n# Run as ACP server (used by openab core)\nopenab-agent\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;openab-agent&quot;\n# working_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;  # optional — defaults to $HOME\nenv = { OPENAB_AGENT_OPENAI_MODEL = &quot;gpt-5.4-mini&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Configuration file (config.json)</h3>\n<p>A small JSON file next to <code>auth.json</code> (default <code>&lt;auth dir&gt;/config.json</code>,\noverridable with <code>OPENAB_CONFIG_PATH</code>) declares the default model and params, so\na deployment can set them in a file instead of only via env vars. <strong>Secrets never\ngo here</strong> — credentials stay in the locked <code>auth.json</code> store.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;model&quot;: &quot;anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6&quot;,  // single provider/model string\n  &quot;max_tokens&quot;: 8192                         // optional\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Resolution is <strong>env-over-config</strong>: <code>OPENAB_AGENT_MODEL</code> / <code>OPENAB_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS</code>\noverride the file, so a pod's injected env stays authoritative over a baked\nconfig. A missing file is fine (empty config); a malformed file is logged and\nignored (the agent then falls back to env / built-in defaults). Unknown keys are\ntolerated for forward-compatibility.</p>\n<h2>Environment Variables</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_MODEL</code></td>\n<td>— (required for Anthropic)</td>\n<td>Anthropic model id, optionally <code>provider/</code>-qualified (e.g. <code>claude-opus-4-8</code>, <code>anthropic/claude-opus-4-8</code>). No hardcoded default — dateless 4.6+ IDs are fixed canonical IDs that retire each generation, so the agent fails loud if unset rather than pin a model that will eventually 404. Overrides <code>model</code> in <a href=\"#configuration-file-configjson\">config.json</a>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_OPENAI_MODEL</code></td>\n<td><code>gpt-5.4-mini</code></td>\n<td>Model to use (must be supported by your ChatGPT plan — see <a href=\"#supported-models-chatgpt-subscription\">Supported Models</a>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_OPENAI_BASE_URL</code></td>\n<td><code>https://chatgpt.com/backend-api</code></td>\n<td>API base URL</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_PROVIDER</code></td>\n<td>auto-detect</td>\n<td>Force provider (<code>anthropic</code>, <code>openai</code>, <code>codex</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS</code></td>\n<td><code>8192</code></td>\n<td>Max output tokens. Overrides <code>max_tokens</code> in config.json.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID</code></td>\n<td>Pi's client</td>\n<td>Custom Codex OAuth client ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_CLIENT_ID</code></td>\n<td>Claude Code's client</td>\n<td>Custom Anthropic OAuth client ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_LOOPS</code></td>\n<td><code>50</code></td>\n<td>Max tool-call iterations per prompt before the agent gives up</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Anthropic API key. Highest-precedence Anthropic credential (see <a href=\"#anthropic-credentials\">Anthropic credentials</a>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Pre-provisioned long-lived Claude Pro/Max subscription token (from <code>claude setup-token</code>). Fleet route — no interactive login, no <code>auth.json</code> write.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>OPENAB_CONFIG_PATH</code></td>\n<td><code>&lt;auth dir&gt;/config.json</code></td>\n<td>Override the config-file path.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<h3>Browser PKCE Flow (recommended)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openab-agent auth codex-oauth\n</code></pre>\n<p>Opens browser to authenticate with your ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription.</p>\n<h3>Headless Server (paste flow)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openab-agent auth codex-oauth --no-browser\n</code></pre>\n<ol>\n<li>Prints an authorization URL</li>\n<li>Open it in any browser and approve</li>\n<li>Browser redirects to <code>localhost:1455</code> (fails on remote server)</li>\n<li>Copy the full URL from the browser address bar</li>\n<li>Paste it back into the terminal</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Device Code Flow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openab-agent auth codex-device\n</code></pre>\n<p>Note: Device flow currently has limited scopes and may not work with all models.</p>\n<h3>Anthropic credentials</h3>\n<p>Three ways to authenticate Anthropic, resolved in this <strong>precedence</strong> (ADR §5.3):</p>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>API key</strong> — <code>export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...</code>. No login; auto-detected.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Pre-provisioned subscription token (fleet route)</strong> — <code>export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=...</code>\n(mint once with <code>claude setup-token</code>; ~1-year Claude Pro/Max token). Sent as a\n<code>Bearer</code> subscription token with the Claude Code identity headers — no\ninteractive login, no <code>auth.json</code> write, no refresh. Recommended for pods (inject\nas a k8s secret).</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Interactive Claude Pro/Max OAuth</strong> — browser PKCE login, refreshed from the\nstored <code>anthropic-oauth</code> tenant in <code>auth.json</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openab-agent auth anthropic-oauth            # browser\nopenab-agent auth anthropic-oauth --no-browser  # paste code#state\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<p>A higher-precedence source's own errors (e.g. a key set but no model) surface\nrather than silently falling through to a lower one.</p>\n<h3>Adding an OAuth vendor</h3>\n<p>Subscription-OAuth providers are declared as a single <code>OAuthVendor</code> descriptor\n(<code>auth.rs</code>, ADR §5.1) — namespace, client id, authorize/token URLs, redirect,\nscope, token-body encoding. The shared PKCE/device/refresh driver reads the\ndescriptor, so a new vendor is a new descriptor, not a new hand-rolled flow.</p>\n<h2>Custom System Prompt</h2>\n<p>Place an <code>AGENTS.md</code> file in the working directory (<code>cwd</code>). It will be prepended to the default system prompt at session creation.</p>\n<pre><code>/home/agent/\n├── AGENTS.md        ← read at session start\n├── .openab/\n│   └── agent/\n│       └── auth.json\n│   └── skills/      ← skill directories\n│       └── my-skill/\n│           └── SKILL.md\n└── (your project files)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Skills</h2>\n<p>openab-agent supports on-demand skills following the <a href=\"https://agentskills.io\">Agent Skills standard</a>. Skills are directories containing a <code>SKILL.md</code> with YAML frontmatter.</p>\n<h3>Skill Locations</h3>\n<p>Scanned in order (first occurrence of a name wins):</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>&lt;working_dir&gt;/.openab/skills/</code> — project-local skills</li>\n<li><code>~/.openab/agent/skills/</code> — global skills</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>SKILL.md Format</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-markdown\">---\nname: my-skill\ndescription: What this skill does and when to use it\n---\n\n# Instructions\n\nSteps the agent should follow when using this skill.\n</code></pre>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>At session start, openab-agent scans skill directories</li>\n<li>Skill names and descriptions are injected into the system prompt</li>\n<li>When a task matches, the agent uses <code>read</code> to load the full SKILL.md</li>\n<li>The agent follows the instructions using its built-in tools (bash, read, write, edit)</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Example</h3>\n<pre><code>.openab/skills/\n└── brave-search/\n    ├── SKILL.md\n    └── search.sh\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-markdown\">---\nname: brave-search\ndescription: Web search via Brave Search API. Use when the user needs current information from the web.\n---\n\n# Brave Search\n\n## Usage\n\n\\`\\`\\`bash\n./search.sh &quot;query&quot;\n\\`\\`\\`\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Compatibility</h3>\n<p>Skills written for Pi (<code>~/.pi/agent/skills/</code>) or Claude Code (<code>~/.claude/skills/</code>) use the same SKILL.md format. Copy or symlink them into <code>~/.openab/agent/skills/</code> to reuse.</p>\n<h2>Docker</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.native -t openab-native:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<p>Image is ~20MB (debian-slim + static Rust binaries). No runtime dependencies.</p>\n<h2>Memory Usage</h2>\n<p>~7MB per session — 28x lighter than Pi, 55x lighter than Kiro CLI.</p>\n<h2>Supported Models (ChatGPT Subscription)</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><code>gpt-5.2</code></li>\n<li><code>gpt-5.3-codex</code></li>\n<li><code>gpt-5.3-codex-spark</code></li>\n<li><code>gpt-5.4</code></li>\n<li><code>gpt-5.4-mini</code></li>\n<li><code>gpt-5.5</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Tools</h2>\n<p>4 built-in tools:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>read</code> — file contents or directory listing</li>\n<li><code>write</code> — create/overwrite file</li>\n<li><code>edit</code> — string replacement</li>\n<li><code>bash</code> — shell execution with process group isolation</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Native agent"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "opencode",
      "html": "<h1>OpenCode</h1>\n<p>OpenCode supports ACP natively via the <code>acp</code> subcommand — no adapter needed.</p>\n<p>OpenCode supports <a href=\"https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/\">75+ LLM providers</a> via the AI SDK, making it the most flexible backend for OpenAB. Users bring their own provider — no separate API keys per backend needed.</p>\n<pre><code>┌──────────┐  Discord  ┌────────┐ ACP stdio ┌──────────┐   ┌───────────────────┐\n│ Discord  │◄────────► │ OpenAB │◄────────► │ OpenCode │──►│  LLM Providers    │\n│ Users    │ Gateway   │ (Rust) │ JSON-RPC  │  (ACP)   │   │                   │\n└──────────┘           └────────┘           └──────────┘   │ ┌───────────────┐ │\n                                                 │         │ │ Ollama Cloud  │ │\n                                       opencode.json       │ │ OpenAI        │ │\n                                       sets model          │ │ Anthropic     │ │\n                                                           │ │ AWS Bedrock   │ │\n                                                           │ │ GitHub Copilot│ │\n                                                           │ │ Groq          │ │\n                                                           │ │ OpenRouter    │ │\n                                                           │ │ Ollama (local)│ │\n                                                           │ │ 75+ more...   │ │\n                                                           │ └───────────────┘ │\n                                                           └───────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Docker Image</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.opencode -t openab-opencode:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<p>The image installs <code>opencode-ai</code> globally via npm on <code>node:22-bookworm-slim</code>.</p>\n<h2>Helm Install</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.opencode.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.opencode.command=opencode \\\n  --set 'agents.opencode.args={acp}' \\\n  --set agents.opencode.discord.botToken=&quot;$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot; \\\n  --set-string 'agents.opencode.discord.allowedChannels[0]=YOUR_CHANNEL_ID' \\\n  --set agents.opencode.workingDir=/home/node \\\n  --set agents.opencode.pool.maxSessions=3 \\\n  --set image.tag=beta\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Set <code>agents.kiro.enabled=false</code> to disable the default Kiro agent.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Image Tag</h3>\n<p>Use <code>--set image.tag=&lt;version&gt;</code> to set the image version globally.\nThe chart auto-appends <code>-&lt;agent&gt;</code> to produce the final tag (see <a href=\"/openab/image-tags\">image-tags.md</a> for full details).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Tag</th>\n<th>Resolves to</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>beta</code></td>\n<td><code>beta-opencode</code></td>\n<td>Floating beta channel (latest pre-release)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9.0-beta.2-opencode</code></td>\n<td>Pinned to exact version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>0.9</code></td>\n<td><code>0.9-opencode</code></td>\n<td>Latest patch in minor (floating)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stable</code></td>\n<td><code>stable-opencode</code></td>\n<td>Floating stable channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To override a single agent's image instead of the global tag:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">--set agents.opencode.image=ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-opencode\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ There is no <code>latest</code> tag. Use <code>beta</code> or <code>stable</code>, or pin to an exact version.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Manual config.toml</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command and args default from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;opencode acp&quot;\n# Only override if you need non-default behavior\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-opencode -- sh -c &quot;$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Follow the browser OAuth flow, then restart the pod:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-opencode\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Providers</h2>\n<p>OpenCode supports multiple providers. Add any of them via <code>opencode auth login</code>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Ollama Cloud</strong> — free tier available, models like <code>gemini-3-flash-preview</code>, <code>qwen3-coder-next</code>, <code>deepseek-v3.2</code></li>\n<li><strong>OpenCode Zen / Go</strong> — tested and verified models provided by the OpenCode team (e.g. <code>opencode/big-pickle</code>, <code>opencode/gpt-5-nano</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, GitHub Copilot, Groq, OpenRouter</strong> — and <a href=\"https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/\">75+ more</a></li>\n</ul>\n<p>To list all available models across configured providers:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-opencode -- opencode models\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Local OpenAI-Compatible Vision Models</h2>\n<p>OpenAB can pass inbound image attachments to OpenCode as ACP image content blocks, but OpenCode must also select a model whose metadata declares image input support. For custom providers, that means <code>modalities.input: [&quot;text&quot;, &quot;image&quot;]</code> in <code>opencode.json</code>.</p>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/local-vision-models#opencode-configuration\">Local OpenAI-Compatible Vision Models</a> for the <code>llama-server</code> setup, <code>opencode.json</code> example, and local vision pitfalls.</p>\n<h2>Example: Ollama Cloud with gemini-3-flash-preview</h2>\n<h3>1. Authenticate Ollama Cloud</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-opencode -- opencode auth login -p &quot;ollama cloud&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Set default model</h3>\n<p>Create <code>opencode.json</code> in the working directory (<code>/home/node</code>). OpenCode reads it as project-level config:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-opencode -- sh -c \\\n  'echo &quot;{\\&quot;model\\&quot;: \\&quot;ollama-cloud/gemini-3-flash-preview\\&quot;}&quot; &gt; /home/node/opencode.json'\n</code></pre>\n<p>This file is on the PVC and persists across restarts.</p>\n<h3>3. Restart to pick up config</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-opencode\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4. Verify</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl logs deployment/openab-opencode --tail=5\n# Should show: discord bot connected\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>@mention</code> the bot in your Discord channel to start chatting.</p>\n<h2>Example: xAI Grok with SuperGrok OAuth</h2>\n<h3>1. Create the auth directory</h3>\n<p>OpenCode stores credentials at <code>~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json</code>. The directory must exist before login:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-opencode -- mkdir -p /home/node/.local/share/opencode\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Authenticate xAI (device-code flow)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-opencode -- opencode auth login -p xai\n</code></pre>\n<p>Select <strong>&quot;xAI Grok OAuth (Headless / Remote / VPS)&quot;</strong>. The CLI prints a URL and a short code:</p>\n<pre><code>Open https://x.ai/device on any device and enter code: ABCD-1234\n</code></pre>\n<p>Open the URL on any device with a browser, enter the code, and approve.</p>\n<h3>3. Verify auth file was created</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec deployment/openab-opencode -- cat /home/node/.local/share/opencode/auth.json\n</code></pre>\n<p>You should see a JSON object with <code>xai</code> credentials.</p>\n<h3>4. Set default model</h3>\n<p>Create <code>opencode.json</code> in the working directory (<code>/home/node</code>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-opencode -- bash -c 'cat &gt; /home/node/opencode.json &lt;&lt; &quot;EOF&quot;\n{\n  &quot;$schema&quot;: &quot;https://opencode.ai/config.json&quot;,\n  &quot;model&quot;: &quot;xai/grok-4.3&quot;\n}\nEOF'\n</code></pre>\n<h3>5. Restart to pick up config</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-opencode\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Important:</strong> Do NOT set a custom <code>baseURL</code> or provider override for xAI. The built-in xAI provider handles routing correctly. A stale <code>~/.config/opencode/opencode.json</code> with <code>baseURL: &quot;http://localhost:9090/v1&quot;</code> (from xai-proxy setups) will break xAI — delete it if present.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Example: API Key Providers</h2>\n<p>For providers that use API keys instead of OAuth (e.g. opencode-go, custom\nOpenAI-compatible endpoints), the config needs the full <code>provider</code> block with\n<code>options.apiKey</code>:</p>\n<h3>1. Set the model and API key</h3>\n<p>Create <code>opencode.json</code> in the working directory (<code>/home/node</code>). The key\ndifference from OAuth providers is the <code>provider.options.apiKey</code> field:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-opencode -- bash -c 'cat &gt; /home/node/opencode.json &lt;&lt; EOF\n{\n  &quot;provider&quot;: {\n    &quot;opencode-go&quot;: {\n      &quot;options&quot;: {\n        &quot;baseURL&quot;: &quot;https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1&quot;,\n        &quot;apiKey&quot;: &quot;{env:OPENCODE_API_KEY}&quot;\n      },\n      &quot;models&quot;: {\n        &quot;deepseek-v4-flash&quot;: {}\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  &quot;model&quot;: &quot;opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash&quot;\n}\nEOF'\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Inject <code>OPENCODE_API_KEY</code> via a Kubernetes Secret as an environment variable.</p>\n<p>Note: shell-style <code>${OPENCODE_API_KEY}</code> would also work in this specific\nheredoc (bash expands it before writing), but only here. <code>{env:VAR}</code> is the\nform that works everywhere.</p>\n<p>See the <a href=\"https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#env-vars\">opencode env var docs</a>\nfor the full <code>{env:VAR}</code> syntax and provider block schema.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>2. Restart to pick up config</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/openab-opencode\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Tool authorization</strong>: OpenCode handles tool authorization internally and never emits <code>session/request_permission</code> — all tools run without user confirmation, equivalent to <code>--trust-all-tools</code> on other backends.</li>\n<li><strong>Model selection</strong>: Set the default model via <code>opencode.json</code> in the working directory using the <code>provider/model</code> format (e.g. <code>ollama-cloud/gemini-3-flash-preview</code>).</li>\n<li><strong>Frequent releases</strong>: OpenCode releases very frequently (often daily). The pinned version in <code>Dockerfile.opencode</code> should be bumped via a dedicated PR when an update is needed.</li>\n<li><strong>Minimum version for OpenRouter reasoning models</strong>: Use <code>opencode-ai &gt;= 1.17.3</code>. OpenCode 1.16.x (and likely earlier) ships an ACP regression where OpenRouter reasoning models — e.g. <code>openrouter/google/gemini-3-flash</code> — produce a complete assistant <code>text</code> part in OpenCode's internal session storage (visible via <code>opencode export &lt;session_id&gt;</code>) but the ACP server never emits a corresponding <code>agent_message_chunk</code> notification. OpenAB's ACP loop then sees only <code>usage_update</code> + a final <code>stopReason: end_turn</code> and renders <code>(no response)</code> because there is no message content to display. Fixed upstream by <a href=\"https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/30332\">sst/opencode#30332</a> (&quot;generate reasoning variants for all OpenRouter models&quot;), released in OpenCode 1.17.0.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "OpenCode"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "openshell",
      "html": "<h1>OpenShell</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ <strong>NOT RECOMMENDED (June 2026)</strong></p>\n<p>OpenSHELL support is <strong>paused</strong> and not recommended for use at this time.</p>\n<p><strong>Reason:</strong> Recent OpenSHELL updates enforce mandatory Network Policy Enforcement\nand require all sandbox traffic to pass through an L7 proxy. This prevents direct\noutbound connections — including the WebSocket (WSS) connection to Discord Gateway\nthat OpenAB requires for real-time communication.</p>\n<p>Unless OAB's networking layer is refactored to be fully HTTP/HTTPS proxy-aware\n(tunneling WSS through OpenSHELL's L7 proxy), the integration cannot function.</p>\n<p><strong>Status:</strong> Blocked. We will re-evaluate when:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>OpenSHELL provides a relaxed policy option (e.g., outbound WSS allowlist), or</li>\n<li>OAB completes a proxy-aware networking refactor.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>See <a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/pull/1113\">PR #1113</a> for full context.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Run OAB inside an <a href=\"https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell\">NVIDIA OpenShell</a> sandbox for isolated, policy-enforced execution.</p>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Host (Linux with Docker)                                           │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  OpenShell Gateway (systemd user service :17670)              │  │\n│  │  • manages sandbox lifecycle                                  │  │\n│  │  • enforces network policy (default-deny egress)              │  │\n│  │  • injects provider credentials into sandbox env              │  │\n│  └──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                             │ creates &amp; policies                     │\n│                             ▼                                        │\n│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  Docker Container (sandbox: &quot;oab&quot;)                            │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  /home/sandbox/                                               │  │\n│  │  └── config.toml         ← bot token + agent config           │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  openab run ──stdio JSON-RPC──► openab-agent                  │  │\n│  │       │                              │                        │  │\n│  │       │ Discord WS                   │ ChatGPT API            │  │\n│  └───────┼──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┘  │\n│           │                              │                           │\n│  ┌────────┼──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────┐     │\n│  │ Network Policy (egress allowlist)     │                    │     │\n│  │  ✓ discord.com:443                    │                    │     │\n│  │  ✓ gateway.discord.gg:443            │                    │     │\n│  │  ✓ cdn.discordapp.com:443            │                    │     │\n│  │  ✓ chatgpt.com:443  ◄────────────────┘                    │     │\n│  │  ✓ auth0.openai.com:443                                   │     │\n│  │  ✗ everything else DENIED                                  │     │\n│  └────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │\n└───────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n            │\n            ▼\n┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐\n│  Discord API     │         │  ChatGPT API     │\n│  (bot gateway)   │         │  (chatgpt.com)   │\n└──────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Docker running on the host (user must be in the <code>docker</code> group)</li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell#install\">OpenShell CLI</a> installed</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/main/install.sh | sh\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> If the gateway fails with &quot;failed to query Docker daemon version&quot;, add your user to the <code>docker</code> group and re-login:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">sudo usermod -aG docker $USER\n# Log out and back in (or: loginctl terminate-user $USER)\n</code></pre>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<h3>1. Create credential provider</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openshell provider create --name discord --type generic \\\n  --credential &quot;DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=your-token-here&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Create sandbox</h3>\n<p>Using the pre-built image:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openshell sandbox create --name oab \\\n  --from ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-native-sandbox:latest \\\n  --provider discord \\\n  -- bash\n</code></pre>\n<p>Or build locally from <code>openshell/Dockerfile</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -t oab-sandbox openshell/\nopenshell sandbox create --name oab \\\n  --from oab-sandbox:latest \\\n  --provider discord \\\n  -- bash\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Set network policy (from host)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openshell policy update oab \\\n  --add-endpoint &quot;discord.com:443:read-write:rest:enforce&quot; \\\n  --add-endpoint &quot;gateway.discord.gg:443:read-write:websocket:enforce&quot; \\\n  --add-endpoint &quot;cdn.discordapp.com:443:read-write:rest:enforce&quot; \\\n  --add-endpoint &quot;chatgpt.com:443:read-write:rest:enforce&quot; \\\n  --add-endpoint &quot;auth0.openai.com:443:read-write:rest:enforce&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4. Authenticate (inside sandbox)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">sandbox$ openab-agent auth codex-oauth --no-browser\n</code></pre>\n<p>Open the printed URL in your browser, approve, then paste the <code>localhost:1455/auth/callback?...</code> URL back.</p>\n<h3>5. Create config and run</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">sandbox$ cat &gt; config.toml &lt;&lt;'EOF'\n[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;your-bot-token&quot;\nallow_all_channels = true\n\n[agent]\ncommand = &quot;openab-agent&quot;\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/sandbox&quot;\nenv = { OPENAB_AGENT_OPENAI_MODEL = &quot;gpt-5.4-mini&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\nenabled = true\nEOF\n\nsandbox$ openab run --config config.toml\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Network Policy</h2>\n<p>OpenShell sandboxes have <strong>default-deny egress</strong>. Required endpoints by backend:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Backend</th>\n<th>Endpoints</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>All</td>\n<td><code>discord.com:443</code>, <code>gateway.discord.gg:443</code>, <code>cdn.discordapp.com:443</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Native Agent (codex)</td>\n<td><code>chatgpt.com:443</code>, <code>auth0.openai.com:443</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Native Agent (anthropic)</td>\n<td><code>api.anthropic.com:443</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>GitHub access</td>\n<td><code>api.github.com:443</code>, <code>github.com:443</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Reconnecting</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openshell sandbox connect oab\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Cleanup</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">openshell sandbox delete oab\nopenshell provider delete discord\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "OpenShell"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "output-directives",
      "html": "<h1>Output Directives</h1>\n<h2>Overview</h2>\n<p>Agents can control platform-specific message delivery by prefixing their output with <code>[[key:value]]</code> directives. OAB parses and strips these before sending to the platform.</p>\n<h2>Format</h2>\n<pre><code>[[reply_to:1502606076451885136]]\n[[ephemeral:true]]              ← future\nActual message content starts here...\n</code></pre>\n<p>Rules:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Consecutive <code>[[key:value]]</code> lines at the start of output = directive header block</li>\n<li>First line that doesn't match <code>[[key:value]]</code> (with colon) = content begins</li>\n<li><code>[[X]]</code> without colon is NOT a directive — stops parsing, preserved as content</li>\n<li>Directives are stripped from the final message (never visible to users)</li>\n<li>Unknown keys are silently ignored (forward compatible, logged at debug level)</li>\n<li>If the same key appears multiple times, the last value wins</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Available Directives</h2>\n<h3><code>reply_to</code></h3>\n<p>Reply to a specific message by ID (Discord: <code>message_reference</code>).</p>\n<pre><code>[[reply_to:1502606076451885136]]\nHere is my reply to that specific message.\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Value</strong>: Platform message ID. Format depends on the target adapter — Discord requires a numeric snowflake; Slack accepts <code>ts</code> (e.g. <code>1234567890.123456</code>). The directive parser validates that the value is non-empty, ≤64 chars, and contains only ASCII alphanumeric characters plus <code>.</code>, <code>-</code>, <code>_</code>; per-platform format validation happens in each adapter.</p>\n<p><strong>Behavior</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Discord: sends with <code>message_reference</code>, showing the native &quot;replying to...&quot; UI</li>\n<li>Feishu: sends via Reply API (<code>POST /im/v1/messages/{id}/reply</code>), showing native quote UI</li>\n<li>Invalid/non-existent message ID: silently falls back to plain send</li>\n<li>Works in both streaming and send-once modes</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>How agents get message IDs</strong>: Every incoming message includes <code>message_id</code> in <code>SenderContext</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;schema&quot;: &quot;openab.sender.v1&quot;,\n  &quot;sender_id&quot;: &quot;845835116920307722&quot;,\n  &quot;sender_name&quot;: &quot;pahud.hsieh&quot;,\n  &quot;message_id&quot;: &quot;1502606076451885136&quot;,\n  &quot;channel&quot;: &quot;discord&quot;,\n  ...\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Multi-Agent Use Case</h2>\n<p>In a thread with multiple bots, agents can reply to each other's messages:</p>\n<pre><code>Human: &quot;Review this PR&quot; (message_id: 100)\nBot A: &quot;Found 3 issues&quot; (message_id: 101)\nBot B output:\n  [[reply_to:101]]\n  I agree with Bot A on F1, but F2 is actually fine because...\n</code></pre>\n<p>This creates clear visual conversation threads within a Discord thread — essential for multi-agent collaboration.</p>\n<h2>Comparison with Other Platforms</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Reply Mechanism</th>\n<th>Agent Control</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>OpenClaw</td>\n<td><code>replyToMode</code> config (<code>off</code>/<code>first</code>/<code>all</code>)</td>\n<td>❌ Platform decides, always to trigger msg</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Hermes Agent</td>\n<td><code>DISCORD_REPLY_TO_MODE</code> env var</td>\n<td>❌ Platform decides, always to trigger msg</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>OAB</strong></td>\n<td><code>[[reply_to:message_id]]</code> directive</td>\n<td>✅ Agent chooses any message</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> <code>reply_to</code> is currently implemented for Discord and Feishu (gateway). Slack behavior depends on <code>assistant_mode</code>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>assistant_mode = true</code> (default):</strong> When native streaming is active, the <code>reply_to</code> directive is <strong>bypassed</strong> — the streamed message is itself the in-thread reply and cannot target a different message. The directive is silently ignored (no error).</li>\n<li><strong><code>assistant_mode = false</code>:</strong> The Slack adapter does not implement <code>reply_to</code> — it falls back to plain send (same as previous behavior). Slack support for targeted replies can be added in a future PR.</li>\n</ul>\n</blockquote>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Output Directives"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "pi",
      "html": "<h1>Pi Coding Agent</h1>\n<p>OpenAB supports the <a href=\"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-coding-agent\">Pi coding agent</a> via the <code>pi-acp</code> adapter — a Node.js bridge that translates ACP JSON-RPC into Pi CLI invocations.</p>\n<h2>Advantages Over Other Native Coding Agents</h2>\n<p>Pi is a native coding agent that supports subscription-based authentication (like Codex, Cloud Code, and GitHub Copilot). Key advantages:</p>\n<h3>No Auth Proxy Required</h3>\n<p>Pi natively supports Anthropic (Claude Pro/Max) and ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscriptions via OAuth. Unlike agents that require an <code>openab-auth-proxy</code> sidecar for subscription forwarding, Pi handles subscription auth directly — reducing deployment complexity and eliminating a moving part.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Agent</th>\n<th>Subscription Auth</th>\n<th>Auth Proxy Needed?</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Pi</td>\n<td>Native OAuth (<code>pi /login</code>)</td>\n<td>❌ No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Codex</td>\n<td>Native device flow</td>\n<td>❌ No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>GitHub Copilot</td>\n<td>Native device flow</td>\n<td>❌ No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Claude Code</td>\n<td>Native OAuth</td>\n<td>❌ No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Kiro</td>\n<td>Native OAuth</td>\n<td>❌ No</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Minimal Tool Surface (Maximum Context Window)</h3>\n<p>Pi exposes only 4 core tools: <code>read</code>, <code>write</code>, <code>edit</code>, <code>bash</code>. Combined with a tiny system prompt, this drastically reduces prompt overhead and maximizes the available context window for actual project source files.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Agent</th>\n<th>Tool Count</th>\n<th>System Prompt Size</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Pi</td>\n<td>4</td>\n<td>Minimal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Claude Code</td>\n<td>10+</td>\n<td>Large</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Codex</td>\n<td>8+</td>\n<td>Medium</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Copilot</td>\n<td>10+</td>\n<td>Large</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Multi-Model Support</h3>\n<p>Pi is model-agnostic and supports 15+ LLM providers. Developers can switch models mid-session without restarting the agent or changing configuration.</p>\n<p>Supported providers include:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Anthropic (Claude) — via subscription or API key</li>\n<li>OpenAI (GPT/Codex) — via subscription or API key</li>\n<li>Google (Gemini) — via API key</li>\n<li>Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Branching Session Trees</h3>\n<p>Pi saves session history as trees, enabling clean branching of code exploration. This allows developers to explore multiple approaches from a single decision point without losing context.</p>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\n# command defaults from OPENAB_AGENT_COMMAND=&quot;openab-agent&quot;\n# working_dir = &quot;/home/node&quot;  # optional — defaults to $HOME\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Docker</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker build -f Dockerfile.pi -t openab-pi:latest .\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Helm</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  pi:\n    discord:\n      enabled: true\n      allowedChannels:\n        - &quot;YOUR_CHANNEL_ID&quot;\n    command: pi-acp\n    workingDir: /home/node\n    image: &quot;ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-pi&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Authentication</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-pi -- pi\n# Once inside the interactive interface, type /login to authenticate\n</code></pre>\n<p>Supported authentication methods:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Provider</th>\n<th>Auth Method</th>\n<th>Subscription</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Anthropic (Claude Pro/Max)</td>\n<td>OAuth via <code>pi /login</code></td>\n<td>Claude subscription</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>ChatGPT Plus/Pro</td>\n<td>OAuth via <code>pi /login</code></td>\n<td>ChatGPT subscription</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Any API key provider</td>\n<td><code>env = { OPENAI_API_KEY = &quot;...&quot; }</code></td>\n<td>Pay-per-token</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Local OpenAI-Compatible Vision Models</h2>\n<p>OpenAB can pass inbound image attachments to Pi as ACP image content blocks, but Pi must also select a model declared as image-capable. For custom OpenAI-compatible providers, add <code>input: [&quot;text&quot;, &quot;image&quot;]</code> to the model entry in <code>~/.pi/agent/models.json</code>.</p>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/local-vision-models#pi-configuration\">Local OpenAI-Compatible Vision Models</a> for the <code>llama-server</code> setup, <code>models.json</code> example, and local vision pitfalls.</p>\n<h2>Steering Files</h2>\n<p>Pi reads steering files in this order:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>.pi/SYSTEM.md</code> — replaces the default system prompt entirely</li>\n<li><code>.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md</code> — appends to the default system prompt</li>\n<li><code>AGENTS.md</code> — loaded hierarchically (project root → global) for context injection</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Place your steering instructions in <code>/home/node/AGENTS.md</code> or <code>/home/node/.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md</code>.</p>\n<h2>Persisted Paths (PVC)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Path</th>\n<th>Contents</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/home/node/.pi/</code></td>\n<td>Pi configuration and auth tokens</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/home/node/.pi/sessions/</code></td>\n<td>Session history trees</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No streaming</strong>: <code>pi-acp</code> returns the full response at once; streamed output is sent as a single <code>agent_message_chunk</code> notification.</li>\n<li><strong>Cancel is best-effort</strong>: Pi CLI runs to completion; <code>session/cancel</code> may not interrupt mid-generation.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Pi"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "python",
      "html": "<h1>Running Python Scripts in OpenAB</h1>\n<p>OpenAB Docker images do <strong>not</strong> ship a system Python or <code>uv</code>. This is by design — images are kept minimal for simplicity, and users are free to install anything they need into <code>$HOME</code>, which is fully persisted across restarts. The recommended way to run Python scripts is with <a href=\"https://docs.astral.sh/uv/\"><code>uv</code></a>.</p>\n<h2>Installing <code>uv</code></h2>\n<p>On first use, the AI agent will typically install <code>uv</code> automatically. You can also install it manually:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh\n</code></pre>\n<p>This installs <code>uv</code> to <code>~/.local/bin/</code>.</p>\n<p>To ensure <code>uv</code> is always available before the agent starts, add the install command to <code>hooks.pre_boot</code> in your <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks]\npre_boot = [&quot;curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/hooks\">Hooks</a> for details.</p>\n<p>Once installed, <code>uv run</code> handles everything else — downloading Python, managing dependencies, and executing your script.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> In OAB deployments, the entire <code>$HOME</code> directory is persisted (via PVC or volume mount). This means <code>uv</code> only downloads and installs a managed Python on the <strong>first run</strong> — subsequent runs reuse the cached interpreter from <code>~/.local/share/uv/python/</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">uv run script.py\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>uv run</code> automatically:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Detects the required Python version (from <code>.python-version</code> or <code>pyproject.toml</code>)</li>\n<li>Downloads and installs a managed Python if none is available</li>\n<li>Creates a virtual environment and installs dependencies</li>\n<li>Runs your script</li>\n</ol>\n<p>No manual <code>python</code> install needed.</p>\n<h2>Pin a Python Version</h2>\n<p>Create a <code>.python-version</code> file in your working directory:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">uv python pin 3.12\n</code></pre>\n<p>This writes <code>.python-version</code> with <code>3.12</code>, ensuring all <code>uv run</code> invocations use that version.</p>\n<h2>Scripts with Dependencies</h2>\n<p>For a standalone script that needs packages, add inline metadata:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\"># /// script\n# requires-python = &quot;&gt;=3.11&quot;\n# dependencies = [&quot;requests&quot;, &quot;beautifulsoup4&quot;]\n# ///\n\nimport requests\nfrom bs4 import BeautifulSoup\n\nresp = requests.get(&quot;https://example.com&quot;)\nsoup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, &quot;html.parser&quot;)\nprint(soup.title.string)\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then simply:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">uv run script.py\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>uv</code> resolves and installs the declared dependencies automatically.</p>\n<p>Alternatively, pass dependencies on the command line:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">uv run --with requests --with beautifulsoup4 script.py\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Project with <code>pyproject.toml</code></h2>\n<p>For multi-file projects, use a standard <code>pyproject.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code
