class=\"language-toml\">[project]\nname = &quot;my-tool&quot;\nversion = &quot;0.1.0&quot;\nrequires-python = &quot;&gt;=3.11&quot;\ndependencies = [&quot;httpx&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then run any module:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">uv run python -m my_tool\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>uv</code> syncs the environment automatically before execution.</p>\n<h2>How <code>uv run</code> Finds Python</h2>\n<p>Resolution order:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>.python-version</code> file (project root or parents)</li>\n<li>Existing virtual environment (<code>.venv</code> or <code>VIRTUAL_ENV</code>)</li>\n<li><code>requires-python</code> in <code>pyproject.toml</code></li>\n<li>uv-managed installs (<code>~/.local/share/uv/python/</code>)</li>\n<li>System <code>PATH</code> fallback</li>\n</ol>\n<p>If no suitable interpreter exists, <code>uv</code> downloads one automatically.</p>\n<h2>Example: Skill with Python Scripts</h2>\n<p>A typical skill directory structure:</p>\n<pre><code>twitter/\n├── scripts/\n│   ├── collect_timeline.py\n│   ├── collect_comments.py\n│   ├── filter_candidates.py\n│   └── upload.py\n└── SKILL.md\n</code></pre>\n<p>In your <code>SKILL.md</code>, instruct the agent to run scripts using <code>uv run</code> with the skill directory as the base path:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-markdown\">## Execution\n\n- **SKILL_DIR** = the directory containing this SKILL.md file.\n  Resolve all `scripts/` paths relative to it.\n\nTo upload, run:\n\n    uv run ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/upload.py\n\nTo collect timeline:\n\n    uv run ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/collect_timeline.py\n</code></pre>\n<p>The agent resolves <code>${SKILL_DIR}</code> to the actual skill path (e.g. <code>~/.kiro/skills/twitter/</code>) and runs the script directly. Each Python script can declare its own dependencies inline:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\"># /// script\n# requires-python = &quot;&gt;=3.11&quot;\n# dependencies = [&quot;tweepy&quot;, &quot;httpx&quot;]\n# ///\n\nimport tweepy\n# ... skill logic\n</code></pre>\n<p>No virtualenv setup, no <code>pip install</code> — <code>uv run</code> handles everything.</p>\n<h2>Tips</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>First run is slower</strong> — Python download + dependency install is cached for subsequent runs.</li>\n<li><strong>Offline environments</strong> — Pre-install Python with <code>uv python install 3.12</code> during image build if network is unavailable at runtime.</li>\n<li><strong>Force a version</strong> — <code>uv run --python 3.13 script.py</code> overrides all resolution.</li>\n<li><strong>See installed Pythons</strong> — <code>uv python list</code> shows all available interpreters.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Python scripts"
      }
    },

      "slug": "reactions",
      "html": "<h1>Emoji Reaction Mapping</h1>\n<p>Map emoji reactions to text commands. When a user reacts with a configured emoji on a message, OAB treats it as if the user sent the corresponding text message through the normal dispatch pipeline.</p>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<p>Add to your <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[reactions.mapping]\n&quot;:thumbsup:&quot; = &quot;OK&quot;\n&quot;:thumbsdown:&quot; = &quot;不行&quot;\n&quot;:arrows_counterclockwise:&quot; = &quot;重新 review&quot;\n&quot;:white_check_mark:&quot; = &quot;approve&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>That's it. Reacting with 👍 on any message in a monitored thread now behaves as if you typed &quot;OK&quot;.</p>\n<h2>Config Keys</h2>\n<p>Keys can be:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Unicode emoji</strong>: <code>&quot;👍&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;✅&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;🔄&quot;</code></li>\n<li><strong>Discord/GitHub shortcodes</strong>: <code>&quot;:thumbsup:&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;:white_check_mark:&quot;</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p>Shortcodes are resolved to unicode at config load time using the <a href=\"https://github.com/github/gemoji\">gemoji</a> database (same as GitHub and Discord). Unrecognized shortcodes are kept as-is and will never match a reaction.</p>\n<h2>Requirements</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong><code>GUILD_MESSAGE_REACTIONS</code> intent</strong> — must be enabled in the Discord Developer Portal. This is a standard (non-privileged) intent; no approval required.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Bot involvement</strong> — reactions are only processed in threads where the bot has already participated (posted at least one message). This follows the same <code>allow_user_messages</code> gating as text messages.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Gating &amp; Access Control</h2>\n<p>Reaction mapping respects all existing access control policies:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Policy</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_users</code> / <code>allow_all_users</code></td>\n<td>Denied users cannot trigger via reactions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_bot_messages</code></td>\n<td><code>off</code>/<code>mentions</code> → bot reactions ignored; <code>all</code> → allowed (respects <code>trusted_bot_ids</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_user_messages</code></td>\n<td><code>mentions</code> → reactions disabled entirely; <code>involved</code>/<code>multibot-mentions</code> → only in threads where bot has participated</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>multibot-mentions</code> + multibot thread</td>\n<td>Only responds if the reaction is on <strong>this bot's</strong> message (implicit targeting)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Channel/thread allowlist</td>\n<td>Same ACL as text messages</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Limitations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Bot's own reactions are always ignored</strong> — the bot's status emoji (👀, 🤔, 🆗, etc.) will never trigger mapping, even if they match a configured key. This prevents feedback loops.</li>\n<li><strong>Unicode emoji only</strong> — custom server emoji (<code>:custom_name:</code>) are silently ignored.</li>\n<li><strong>Thread-only</strong> (in <code>involved</code>/<code>multibot-mentions</code> mode) — reactions in non-thread channels are ignored unless <code>allow_user_messages</code> is set to a mode that allows them.</li>\n<li><strong>No reaction removal handling</strong> — only <code>reaction_add</code> events trigger mapping; removing a reaction has no effect.</li>\n<li><strong>One emoji = one dispatch</strong> — each mapped reaction dispatches independently through the pipeline.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Examples</h2>\n<h3>PR Review Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[reactions.mapping]\n&quot;:white_check_mark:&quot; = &quot;approve&quot;\n&quot;:x:&quot; = &quot;reject&quot;\n&quot;:arrows_counterclockwise:&quot; = &quot;重新 review&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Task Acknowledgment</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[reactions.mapping]\n&quot;:thumbsup:&quot; = &quot;OK&quot;\n&quot;:eyes:&quot; = &quot;looking into it&quot;\n&quot;:rocket:&quot; = &quot;deploying now&quot;\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Emoji Reaction Mapping"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "refarch/aws-ecs-fargate-spot",
      "html": "<h1>Reference Architecture: OpenAB on AWS ECS Fargate Spot</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>This doc is meant to be used with Kiro or any coding CLI.</strong> Prompt your AI agent with something like:</p>\n<pre><code>per https://github.com/openabdev/openab/blob/main/docs/refarch/aws-ecs-fargate-spot.md deploy an openab on ECS Fargate Spot for me in my AWS account\n</code></pre>\n<p>and it will guide you through (or handle) the full setup on AWS.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Deploy a single OpenAB bot on ECS Fargate Spot for ~$2.7/month with persistent auth via S3.</p>\n<h2>Why This Architecture</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Fully managed</strong> — Amazon ECS with Fargate eliminates cluster management. No EC2 instances, no patching, no capacity planning.</li>\n<li><strong>Enterprise-grade isolation</strong> — Fargate runs each task in a dedicated microVM powered by <a href=\"https://firecracker-microvm.github.io/\">Firecracker</a>. Hardware-level isolation between tenants — critical for enterprise workloads.</li>\n<li><strong>Cost effective</strong> — <code>FARGATE_SPOT</code> provides up to 70% savings over on-demand. Ideal for non-critical, interruptible workloads like AI agent bots (~$2.7/month for 0.25 vCPU).</li>\n<li><strong>Secrets &amp; IAM native</strong> — Bot tokens and API keys stored in AWS Secrets Manager, injected at runtime. Fine-grained IAM roles per task — no shared credentials.</li>\n<li><strong>Zero networking overhead</strong> — No NAT gateway, no load balancer needed. Public IP + egress-only security group keeps it simple and cheap.</li>\n<li><strong>Resilient</strong> — Spot interruptions auto-recover. Auth persists to S3 via hooks. ECS restarts tasks automatically.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>+-- AWS -------------------------------------------------------+\n|                                                              |\n|  +-- ECS Fargate Spot Task --------------------------------+ |\n|  |                                                         | |\n|  |  +----------------+                                     | |\n|  |  |    openab      |                                     | |\n|  |  |(main container)|                                     | |\n|  |  | kiro-cli acp   |                                     | |\n|  |  | Discord bot    |                                     | |\n|  |  +----------------+                                     | |\n|  |         |                                               | |\n|  +---------------------------------------------------------+ |\n|                                                              |\n|      |                     |                                 |\n|  S3 Bucket           Secrets Manager                         |\n|  (auth state)         (bot token)                            |\n|                                                              |\n+--------------------------------------------------------------+\n                            |               |\n                       Discord API   +-- GitHub ------+\n                      (bot gateway)  | Gist           |\n                                     | (config.toml)  |\n                                     +----------------+\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Cost</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Resource</th>\n<th>Spec</th>\n<th>Spot Price/mo</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Fargate Task</td>\n<td>0.25 vCPU + 512MB</td>\n<td>~$2.7</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>S3</td>\n<td>&lt; 1MB state</td>\n<td>~$0</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Secrets Manager</td>\n<td>1 secret</td>\n<td>$0.40</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>CloudWatch Logs</td>\n<td>minimal</td>\n<td>~$0</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Total</strong></td>\n<td></td>\n<td><strong>~$3.1/month</strong></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>AWS credentials</strong> — IAM user or IAM Identity Center (<code>aws sso login</code>)</li>\n<li><strong><a href=\"https://github.com/oablab/ecsctl\">ecsctl</a></strong> installed</li>\n<li><strong>Discord bot token</strong> — from <a href=\"https://discord.com/developers/applications\">Discord Developer Portal</a></li>\n<li><strong>Kiro CLI subscription</strong> — for the agent backend</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Install ecsctl</h3>\n<p><a href=\"https://github.com/oablab/ecsctl\">ecsctl</a> is an open-source CLI from the OpenAB Lab project that gives you a <code>kubectl</code>-like experience on Amazon ECS — deploy, exec, copy files, tail logs, and manage services declaratively.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># macOS (Apple Silicon)\ncurl -sL https://github.com/oablab/ecsctl/releases/latest/download/ecsctl-darwin-arm64.tar.gz | tar xz -O &gt; ~/.local/bin/ecsctl &amp;&amp; chmod +x ~/.local/bin/ecsctl\n\n# Linux (x86_64)\ncurl -sL https://github.com/oablab/ecsctl/releases/latest/download/ecsctl-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -O &gt; ~/.local/bin/ecsctl &amp;&amp; chmod +x ~/.local/bin/ecsctl\n\n# Linux (ARM64)\ncurl -sL https://github.com/oablab/ecsctl/releases/latest/download/ecsctl-linux-arm64.tar.gz | tar xz -O &gt; ~/.local/bin/ecsctl &amp;&amp; chmod +x ~/.local/bin/ecsctl\n</code></pre>\n<h2>One-Time Setup</h2>\n<p>Before your first deploy, create these AWS resources (once per account):</p>\n<h3>1. ECS Cluster</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">aws ecs create-cluster --cluster-name openab \\\n  --capacity-providers FARGATE_SPOT FARGATE \\\n  --region us-east-1\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. IAM Roles</h3>\n<p><strong>Execution role</strong> (<code>openab-ecs-execution-role</code>) — ECS uses this to pull images and inject secrets:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Trust: <code>ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com</code></li>\n<li>Attach: <code>AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy</code></li>\n<li>Inline: <code>secretsmanager:GetSecretValue</code> on your secret ARN</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Task role</strong> (<code>openab-ecs-task-role</code>) — the running container uses this:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Trust: <code>ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com</code></li>\n<li>Inline: S3 access (<code>s3:GetObject</code>, <code>s3:PutObject</code>, <code>s3:ListBucket</code>) for state persistence</li>\n<li>Inline: SSM for ECS Exec (<code>ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel</code>, <code>CreateDataChannel</code>, <code>OpenControlChannel</code>, <code>OpenDataChannel</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>3. Store Discord bot token</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">aws secretsmanager create-secret --name openab \\\n  --secret-string '{&quot;DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN&quot;:&quot;YOUR_BOT_TOKEN_HERE&quot;}' \\\n  --region us-east-1\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4. Supporting infra</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>S3 bucket</strong> for auth state (e.g. <code>openab-state-&lt;account-id&gt;</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>CloudWatch log group</strong> <code>/ecs/openab</code></li>\n<li><strong>Security group</strong> — egress-only (no inbound needed)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>5. Config gist</h3>\n<p>Host your <code>config.toml</code> as a GitHub Gist. OpenAB fetches it at startup.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh gist create --filename config.toml --desc &quot;OpenAB ECS config&quot; - &lt;&lt;'EOF'\n[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\nallow_all_channels = true\nallow_all_users = true\nallow_bot_messages = &quot;mentions&quot;\nallow_user_messages = &quot;multibot-mentions&quot;\nmessage_processing_mode = &quot;per-thread&quot;\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\nenabled = true\nremove_after_reply = false\nEOF\n</code></pre>\n<p>Note the raw gist URL for the next step.</p>\n<h2>Deploy</h2>\n<h3>Create <code>service.yaml</code></h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oablab/ecsctl/master/schemas/service.schema.json\napiVersion: ecsctl/v1\nkind: Service\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-mybot\n  cluster: openab\nspec:\n  image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:latest\n  cpu: &quot;256&quot;\n  memory: &quot;512&quot;\n  arch: ARM64\n  capacity: FARGATE_SPOT\n  desiredCount: 1\n  execEnabled: true\n  containerName: openab\n  executionRoleArn: arn:aws:iam::&lt;ACCOUNT_ID&gt;:role/openab-ecs-execution-role\n  taskRoleArn: arn:aws:iam::&lt;ACCOUNT_ID&gt;:role/openab-ecs-task-role\n  subnets: [subnet-xxx, subnet-yyy]\n  securityGroups: [sg-xxx]\n  assignPublicIp: true\n  logGroup: /ecs/openab\n  env:\n    OPENAB_AGENT_NAME: mybot\n    OPENAB_BACKEND_AGENT: openab\n    STATE_BUCKET: openab-state-&lt;ACCOUNT_ID&gt;\n  secrets:\n    DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN: arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:&lt;ACCOUNT_ID&gt;:secret:openab-XXXXXX:DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN::\n  command:\n    - sh\n    - -c\n    - &quot;exec /usr/local/bin/openab run -c https://gist.githubusercontent.com/&lt;user&gt;/&lt;gist_id&gt;/raw/config.toml&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Apply</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">ecsctl apply -f service.yaml --wait\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Authenticate (one-time)</h3>\n<p>After the task starts, exec in and run the auth command:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">ecsctl exec mybot -- sh -c '$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND'\n</code></pre>\n<p>Follow the device code flow in your browser. Auth is persisted via the <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> S3 sync configured in your gist.</p>\n<h3>Verify</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">ecsctl log mybot -f\n</code></pre>\n<p>Look for: <code>discord bot connected</code> → <code>spawning agent</code> → streaming response.</p>\n<p>Mention <code>@YourBot</code> in a Discord channel to confirm it responds.</p>\n<h2>Day-2 Operations</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Update config and redeploy\necsctl apply -f service.yaml --wait\n\n# Scale up for more capacity\necsctl apply -f service.yaml --set spec.cpu=512 --set spec.memory=1024 --wait\n\n# Clone to a second bot\necsctl apply -f service.yaml --set metadata.name=openab-mybot2\n\n# Force restart after auth refresh\necsctl restart mybot\n\n# Export current running state to YAML\necsctl export mybot -f service.yaml\n\n# Check task status\necsctl get mybot\n\n# Copy files to/from container\necsctl cp ./skills.tar.gz mybot:/tmp/\n\n# Remove the service\necsctl delete mybot\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Important Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Secrets Management</strong>: Store all credentials (bot tokens, API keys, OAuth tokens) in AWS Secrets Manager. Reference them in the <code>secrets:</code> block of your service YAML — they're injected as environment variables at runtime, never baked into images or gists.</li>\n<li><strong>Spot interruption</strong>: Task may be reclaimed with 2-min notice. Auth persists via S3; bot reconnects automatically on new task launch.</li>\n<li><strong>Config via URL</strong>: <code>openab run -c &lt;URL&gt;</code> fetches config over HTTPS. Use <code>${ENV_VAR}</code> for secrets — expanded at runtime from container environment.</li>\n<li><strong>No NAT needed</strong>: Public subnet + <code>assignPublicIp: ENABLED</code> gives direct internet access.</li>\n<li><strong>Memory</strong>: 512MB is tight (~370MB idle). Bump to 1024MB if sessions OOM.</li>\n<li><strong>Round-trip workflow</strong>: <code>ecsctl export</code> → edit YAML → <code>ecsctl apply</code> for iterative changes.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Advanced: Bootstrap &amp; Backup with Hooks</h2>\n<p>OpenAB supports <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code> and <code>[hooks.pre_shutdown]</code> in the config gist. These replace the need for sidecar containers.</p>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Task Lifecycle                                             │\n│                                                             │\n│  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌────────────────┐    │\n│  │  pre_boot    │───▶│  openab  │───▶│ pre_shutdown   │    │\n│  │              │    │  (main)  │    │                │    │\n│  │ • S3 → HOME │    │          │    │ • HOME → S3   │    │\n│  │ • install    │    │ agent    │    │ • cleanup     │    │\n│  │   tools      │    │ sessions │    │               │    │\n│  │ • restore    │    │          │    │               │    │\n│  │   auth       │    │          │    │               │    │\n│  └──────────────┘    └──────────┘    └────────────────┘    │\n│                                                             │\n│       ▲                                        │           │\n│       │            S3 Bucket                   │           │\n│       └────────── (state/auth) ◀───────────────┘           │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>pre_boot</strong> — runs before the agent starts:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Restore auth tokens and state from S3</li>\n<li>Install extra tools (AWS CLI, gh, custom binaries)</li>\n<li>Sync shared assets (AGENTS.md, skills)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>pre_shutdown</strong> — runs on graceful stop (Spot interruption, scale-down):</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Tar up HOME and push to S3</li>\n<li>Persist auth, conversation history, installed tools</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Add hooks to your config gist:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[hooks.pre_boot]\ntimeout_seconds = 120\non_failure = &quot;abort&quot;\nurl = &quot;https://gist.githubusercontent.com/&lt;user&gt;/&lt;id&gt;/raw/pre-boot.sh&quot;\n\n[hooks.pre_shutdown]\ntimeout_seconds = 120\nurl = &quot;https://gist.githubusercontent.com/&lt;user&gt;/&lt;id&gt;/raw/pre-shutdown.sh&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>This eliminates the init/sidecar container pattern — a single container handles everything.</p>\n<h2>Manual Deployment (without ecsctl)</h2>\n<details>\n<summary>Click to expand AWS CLI-based deployment</summary>\n<p>If you prefer to use the AWS CLI directly instead of ecsctl, replace Phase 5 with a manual task definition registration.</p>\n<p>Register a task definition with three containers:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Container</th>\n<th>Image</th>\n<th>Role</th>\n<th>Essential</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>s3-restore</code></td>\n<td><code>amazon/aws-cli</code></td>\n<td>Pull auth from S3 + <code>chown 1000:1000</code></td>\n<td>No (init)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>openab</code></td>\n<td><code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:latest</code></td>\n<td>Main bot process</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>s3-sync</code></td>\n<td><code>amazon/aws-cli</code></td>\n<td>Push auth to S3 every 5 min</td>\n<td>No (sidecar)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Key settings:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>CPU: 256 (0.25 vCPU), Memory: 512 MB</li>\n<li>Network mode: <code>awsvpc</code>, assign public IP</li>\n<li>Capacity provider: <code>FARGATE_SPOT</code></li>\n<li>Enable ECS Exec for interactive login</li>\n<li><code>openab</code> container depends on <code>s3-restore</code> (condition: SUCCESS)</li>\n<li><code>openab</code> entrypoint: restore auth from shared volume, then <code>exec openab run -c &lt;CONFIG_URL&gt;</code></li>\n<li>Inject <code>DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code> from Secrets Manager via container <code>secrets</code></li>\n<li>Shared volume (<code>agent-data</code>) mounted at <code>/data</code> across all containers</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Create an ECS service with <code>desiredCount: 1</code>.</p>\n<p>For auth, exec in manually:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">TASK_ID=$(aws ecs list-tasks --cluster openab --service-name openab-mybot \\\n  --desired-status RUNNING --query 'taskArns[0]' --output text | awk -F/ '{print $NF}')\n\naws ecs execute-command --cluster openab --task $TASK_ID \\\n  --container openab --interactive \\\n  --command &quot;kiro-cli login --use-device-flow&quot;\n</code></pre>\n</details>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Reference Architecture: OpenAB on AWS ECS Fargate Spot"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "refarch/ci-observability-discord",
      "html": "<h1>Reference Architecture: CI Observability via Discord</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>This doc is meant to be used with Kiro or any coding CLI.</strong> Prompt your AI agent with something like:</p>\n<pre><code>per https://github.com/openabdev/openab/blob/main/docs/refarch/ci-observability-discord.md set up CI notifications to my Discord channel\n</code></pre>\n<p>and it will guide you through the full setup.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Send GitHub Actions CI results (pass/fail) to a Discord channel or thread via webhook, with full CI metadata and user mentions.</p>\n<h2>Problem</h2>\n<p>When CI runs in GitHub Actions, the only way to know the result is to check the GitHub UI or wait for an email. For teams collaborating in Discord, this creates friction:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No visibility</strong> — CI failures go unnoticed until someone manually checks GitHub</li>\n<li><strong>Slow feedback loop</strong> — contributors wait without knowing their PR is broken</li>\n<li><strong>Context switching</strong> — developers must leave Discord to check CI status</li>\n<li><strong>No accountability</strong> — nobody gets pinged when CI breaks</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>What We Want</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>CI finishes (pass or fail) → automatically POST result to a specific Discord channel/thread</li>\n<li>Show who committed, how long CI took, and which step failed</li>\n<li>Include both PR URL and Run URL for quick navigation</li>\n<li>Mention a specific user so they get pinged</li>\n<li>Bot-readable content (not hidden in embeds) so mentioned bots can act on it</li>\n<li>Route notifications to the correct thread based on the PR description</li>\n<li>One reusable workflow that any CI job can call</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Two Approaches</h2>\n<h3>Approach 1: Polling Mode (Cronjob)</h3>\n<p>OpenAB has a built-in cron scheduler. You can schedule the agent to periodically check CI status and fix failures:</p>\n<pre><code>@bot can you schedule a cronjob for yourself to this thread and remind yourself to\n&quot;check https://github.com/owner/repo/actions and fix them if required&quot; every 10min?\n</code></pre>\n<p>This creates a <code>[[cron.jobs]]</code> entry:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[[cron.jobs]]\nschedule = &quot;*/10 * * * *&quot;\nchannel = &quot;123456789012345678&quot;\nthread_id = &quot;1505664791719710810&quot;\nmessage = &quot;check https://github.com/owner/repo/actions and fix them if required&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong> Holistic view — checks everything on your plate (all workflows, all branches, all repos). Agent can auto-fix issues. No webhook configuration needed.</p>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong> Up to N-minute delay, unnecessary API calls when nothing changed, burns compute on polling.</p>\n<h3>Approach 2: Notification Mode (Webhook Push) ← This Doc</h3>\n<p>CI pushes results to Discord the moment it finishes — zero delay, zero wasted calls. But it only tells you about <strong>this single CI run</strong>.</p>\n<pre><code>GitHub Actions ──finish──► HTTP POST ──► Discord thread\n                              (webhook)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong> Instant notification, no polling cost, precise metadata (duration, failed step, commit info) for the specific run.</p>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong> Narrow scope — only reports on the workflow that triggered it. Can't see the big picture. Can't auto-fix (notification only). Requires webhook setup.</p>\n<h3>Comparison</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th></th>\n<th>Polling (Cronjob)</th>\n<th>Notification (Webhook)</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Scope</strong></td>\n<td>Everything on your plate — all workflows, branches, repos</td>\n<td>Single CI run only</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Latency</strong></td>\n<td>Up to N minutes</td>\n<td>Instant (on completion)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Auto-fix</strong></td>\n<td>✅ Agent can push fixes</td>\n<td>❌ Notification only</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Setup</strong></td>\n<td>Just tell the bot</td>\n<td>Webhook + secrets + workflow changes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Cost</strong></td>\n<td>Burns compute even when idle</td>\n<td>Zero cost when nothing runs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Metadata</strong></td>\n<td>Whatever the agent can scrape</td>\n<td>Precise: duration, failed step, commit SHA</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Best for</strong></td>\n<td>&quot;Keep my CI green across all repos&quot;</td>\n<td>&quot;Tell me the moment this PR breaks&quot;</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Recommended</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>&quot;Tell me when CI breaks&quot;</td>\n<td>Notification mode (this doc)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>&quot;Check CI and fix it automatically&quot;</td>\n<td>Polling mode (cronjob)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Both — notify immediately + auto-fix</td>\n<td>Combine: webhook notifies, cronjob retries fixes</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Solution</h2>\n<p>A <strong>reusable workflow</strong> (<code>notify-discord.yml</code>) that any CI workflow calls as its final job. It posts CI results as plain-text content (bot-readable) with user mention — routing to the correct thread based on the PR description.</p>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>+-- GitHub Actions ----------------------------------------+\n|                                                          |\n|  +-- ci.yml ------------------------------------------+  |\n|  |                                                    |  |\n|  |  [check] ──► cargo fmt / clippy / test             |  |\n|  |     │                                              |  |\n|  |     │ outputs: status, duration, commit_msg,       |  |\n|  |     │          commit_author, failed_step          |  |\n|  |     ▼                                              |  |\n|  |  [notify] (if: always())                           |  |\n|  |     │  calls ──► notify-discord.yml (reusable)     |  |\n|  |     │                                              |  |\n|  +-----|----------------------------------------------+  |\n|        │                                                 |\n|        │  inputs: status, commit_msg, pr_body, ...       |\n|        │  secrets: DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL                    |\n|        │  vars: DISCORD_THREAD_ID, DISCORD_MENTION_UID   |\n|        │                                                 |\n+--------|─────────────────────────────────────────────────+\n         │\n         │ HTTP POST (webhook + ?thread_id=xxx)\n         ▼\n+-- Discord -----------------------------------------------+\n|                                                          |\n|  #channel or thread                                      |\n|  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     |\n|  │ ❌ CI failure — repo@main | PR #42              │     |\n|  │ 👤 author — commit message                      │     |\n|  │ ⏱️ 3m42s                                        │     |\n|  │ 💥 Failed at: Tests                             │     |\n|  │ https://github.com/.../pull/42                  │     |\n|  │ https://github.com/.../actions/runs/123         │     |\n|  │ @user-mention                                   │     |\n|  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     |\n|                                                          |\n+----------------------------------------------------------+\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Key Design Decisions</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Decision</th>\n<th>Rationale</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Reusable workflow (<code>workflow_call</code>)</td>\n<td>Any CI workflow can call it; single source of truth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>if: always()</code> on notify job</td>\n<td>Fires on success, failure, and cancellation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Plain-text content (not embed)</td>\n<td>Bots can read <code>message.content</code>; embeds are invisible to bots</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>printf</code> + <code>jq --rawfile</code></td>\n<td>Only reliable way to get real newlines into JSON payload</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Thread ID from PR body</td>\n<td>Dynamic routing — each PR notifies its own thread</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Fallback to repo variable</td>\n<td>Push-to-main events still get notified somewhere</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Both PR URL and Run URL</td>\n<td>PR for context, Run for debugging logs</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Setup</h2>\n<h3>1. Create a Discord Webhook</h3>\n<p>Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.</p>\n<h3>2. Configure Repository Secrets &amp; Variables</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Name</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Secret</strong></td>\n<td><code>DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL</code></td>\n<td>The webhook URL (contains token — keep secret)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Variable</strong></td>\n<td><code>DISCORD_THREAD_ID</code></td>\n<td>Default thread ID for fallback notifications</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Variable</strong></td>\n<td><code>DISCORD_MENTION_USER_ID</code></td>\n<td>Discord user ID to mention (e.g. <code>1234567890</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Set via CLI:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh secret set DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL --repo &lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt;\ngh variable set DISCORD_THREAD_ID --repo &lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt; --body &quot;&lt;thread_id&gt;&quot;\ngh variable set DISCORD_MENTION_USER_ID --repo &lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt; --body &quot;&lt;user_id&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Create the Reusable Workflow</h3>\n<p><code>.github/workflows/notify-discord.yml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">name: Discord Notify\n\non:\n  workflow_call:\n    inputs:\n      status:\n        required: true\n        type: string\n      failed_step:\n        required: false\n        type: string\n      duration:\n        required: false\n        type: string\n      commit_msg:\n        required: false\n        type: string\n      commit_author:\n        required: false\n        type: string\n      pr_body:\n        required: false\n        type: string\n    secrets:\n      DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL:\n        required: true\n\njobs:\n  notify:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - name: Send Discord notification\n        env:\n          WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL }}\n          DEFAULT_THREAD_ID: ${{ vars.DISCORD_THREAD_ID }}\n          MENTION_USER_ID: ${{ vars.DISCORD_MENTION_USER_ID }}\n          STATUS: ${{ inputs.status }}\n          FAILED_STEP: ${{ inputs.failed_step }}\n          DURATION: ${{ inputs.duration }}\n          COMMIT_MSG: ${{ inputs.commit_msg }}\n          COMMIT_AUTHOR: ${{ inputs.commit_author }}\n          PR_BODY: ${{ inputs.pr_body }}\n          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}\n          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}\n          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}\n          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}\n          SERVER_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}\n        run: |\n          # Extract Thread ID from PR body, fallback to variable\n          THREAD_ID=&quot;&quot;\n          if [ -n &quot;$PR_BODY&quot; ]; then\n            THREAD_ID=$(echo &quot;$PR_BODY&quot; | grep -ioP '^Thread:\\s*\\K[0-9]+' | head -1)\n          fi\n          [ -z &quot;$THREAD_ID&quot; ] &amp;&amp; THREAD_ID=&quot;$DEFAULT_THREAD_ID&quot;\n\n          if [ &quot;$STATUS&quot; = &quot;success&quot; ]; then\n            EMOJI=&quot;✅&quot;\n          else\n            EMOJI=&quot;❌&quot;\n          fi\n\n          # Build message into a temp file for proper newlines\n          {\n            printf '%s **CI %s** — `%s@%s`' &quot;$EMOJI&quot; &quot;$STATUS&quot; &quot;$REPO&quot; &quot;$REF&quot;\n            [ -n &quot;$PR&quot; ] &amp;&amp; printf ' | PR #%s' &quot;$PR&quot;\n            echo &quot;&quot;\n            [ -n &quot;$COMMIT_AUTHOR&quot; ] &amp;&amp; printf '👤 %s' &quot;$COMMIT_AUTHOR&quot;\n            [ -n &quot;$COMMIT_MSG&quot; ] &amp;&amp; printf ' — `%s`' &quot;$COMMIT_MSG&quot;\n            [ -n &quot;$COMMIT_AUTHOR&quot; ] &amp;&amp; echo &quot;&quot;\n            [ -n &quot;$DURATION&quot; ] &amp;&amp; echo &quot;⏱️ ${DURATION}&quot;\n            [ &quot;$STATUS&quot; != &quot;success&quot; ] &amp;&amp; [ -n &quot;$FAILED_STEP&quot; ] &amp;&amp; echo &quot;💥 Failed at: **${FAILED_STEP}**&quot;\n            [ -n &quot;$PR&quot; ] &amp;&amp; echo &quot;${SERVER_URL}/${REPO}/pull/${PR}&quot;\n            echo &quot;$RUN_URL&quot;\n            [ -n &quot;$MENTION_USER_ID&quot; ] &amp;&amp; echo &quot;&lt;@${MENTION_USER_ID}&gt;&quot;\n          } &gt; /tmp/msg.txt\n\n          # Use jq --rawfile to preserve real newlines in JSON\n          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --rawfile msg /tmp/msg.txt \\\n            '{content: $msg, allowed_mentions: {parse: [&quot;users&quot;]}}')\n\n          URL=&quot;${WEBHOOK_URL}&quot;\n          [ -n &quot;$THREAD_ID&quot; ] &amp;&amp; URL=&quot;${URL}?thread_id=${THREAD_ID}&quot;\n\n          curl -sf -X POST &quot;$URL&quot; \\\n            -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n            -d &quot;$PAYLOAD&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4. Wire Into Your CI Workflow</h3>\n<p>Add a <code>notify</code> job at the end of any workflow:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  check:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    outputs:\n      duration: ${{ steps.duration.outputs.value }}\n      commit_msg: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.commit_msg }}\n      commit_author: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.commit_author }}\n      failed_step: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.failed_step }}\n    steps:\n      - name: Record start time\n        id: start\n        run: echo &quot;ts=$(date +%s)&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$GITHUB_OUTPUT&quot;\n\n      # ... your build/test steps (give each an id) ...\n\n      - name: Collect metadata\n        id: meta\n        if: always()\n        run: |\n          echo &quot;commit_msg=$(git log -1 --pretty=%s)&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$GITHUB_OUTPUT&quot;\n          echo &quot;commit_author=$(git log -1 --pretty=%an)&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$GITHUB_OUTPUT&quot;\n          # Detect which step failed\n          FAILED=&quot;&quot;\n          # if [ &quot;${{ steps.test.outcome }}&quot; = &quot;failure&quot; ]; then FAILED=&quot;Tests&quot;; fi\n          echo &quot;failed_step=${FAILED}&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$GITHUB_OUTPUT&quot;\n\n      - name: Calculate duration\n        id: duration\n        if: always()\n        run: |\n          ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - ${{ steps.start.outputs.ts }} ))\n          echo &quot;value=$((ELAPSED/60))m$((ELAPSED%60))s&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$GITHUB_OUTPUT&quot;\n\n  notify:\n    needs: [check]\n    if: always()\n    uses: ./.github/workflows/notify-discord.yml\n    with:\n      status: ${{ needs.check.result }}\n      failed_step: ${{ needs.check.outputs.failed_step }}\n      duration: ${{ needs.check.outputs.duration }}\n      commit_msg: ${{ needs.check.outputs.commit_msg }}\n      commit_author: ${{ needs.check.outputs.commit_author }}\n      pr_body: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}\n    secrets:\n      DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL }}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>5. Dynamic Thread Routing via PR Description</h3>\n<p>Add a <code>Thread:</code> line anywhere in your PR description:</p>\n<pre><code>Thread: 1505664791719710810\n</code></pre>\n<p>The workflow extracts the first match and posts to that thread. If absent, it falls back to <code>DISCORD_THREAD_ID</code> variable.</p>\n<h2>Gotchas</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Issue</th>\n<th>Solution</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Embed content invisible to bots</td>\n<td>Use plain-text <code>content</code> field — bots only see <code>message.content</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>\\n</code> in <code>jq --arg</code> becomes literal <code>\\\\n</code></td>\n<td>Write to temp file, use <code>jq --rawfile</code> to preserve real newlines</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Duplicate YAML keys silently break workflows</td>\n<td>Validate with <code>actionlint</code> or check Actions run errors</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Webhook URL contains a token</td>\n<td>Always store as a <strong>secret</strong>, never in workflow files or docs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>if: always()</code> required on notify job</td>\n<td>Otherwise it's skipped when upstream jobs fail</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Mention requires numeric Discord user ID</td>\n<td>Use <code>&lt;@USER_ID&gt;</code> format in <code>content</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Webhook mentions don't trigger bots</td>\n<td>Webhook messages don't fire bot <code>MESSAGE_CREATE</code> — mention real users instead</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Reference Architecture: CI Observability via Discord"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "refarch/cronjob_k8s_refarch",
      "html": "<h1>Kubernetes CronJob Reference Architecture</h1>\n<p>This document is a reference architecture for how we set up the project-screening CronJob around <code>codex exec</code>, GitHub Projects, and Discord delivery.</p>\n<p>It is not meant to be framed as the one official OpenAB recommendation. The intent is narrower: when someone asks how to do scheduled screening work in Kubernetes, we can hand this document to their Kiro or Codex-style agent as a concrete starting point and let that agent adapt the pattern to their environment.</p>\n<h2>ASCII Flow</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">GitHub Project Board\n  Incoming\n     |\n     v\nKubernetes CronJob\n  schedule: every 30 minutes\n  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid\n     |\n     v\nEphemeral Job Pod\n  image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-codex\n  command: bash /opt/openab-project-screening/screen_once.sh\n     |\n     +--&gt; read GitHub Project state via gh\n     +--&gt; claim first Incoming item\n     +--&gt; build prompt from PR/issue metadata\n     +--&gt; run codex exec\n     +--&gt; post summary to Discord\n     +--&gt; create Discord thread\n     +--&gt; post full report\n     |\n     v\nProject Board\n  PR-Screening\n     |\n     v\nHuman or agent follow-up\n</code></pre>\n<h2>What This Document Covers</h2>\n<p>We deliberately chose a Kubernetes <code>CronJob</code> instead of:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>installing <code>cron</code> inside the app container</li>\n<li>running an always-on sleep loop in the main pod</li>\n<li>reusing a long-lived ACP session for scheduled screening</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This shape fits Kubernetes better:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>the scheduler is owned by the cluster</li>\n<li>each run gets a fresh pod</li>\n<li>failures are isolated per run</li>\n<li>logs are attached to each job</li>\n<li><code>concurrencyPolicy: Forbid</code> prevents overlapping claimers</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Credential Model</h2>\n<p>The job is intentionally stateless.</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>GH_TOKEN</code> comes from the <code>openab-project-screening</code> Secret</li>\n<li><code>auth.json</code> comes from the same Secret and is copied into <code>$HOME/.codex/auth.json</code></li>\n<li><code>DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code> comes from the existing <code>openab-kiro-codex</code> Secret</li>\n<li>the script and prompt are mounted from a ConfigMap</li>\n<li>the pod uses <code>/tmp</code> via <code>emptyDir</code></li>\n<li>no shared PVC is required</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This avoids coupling the scheduled workflow to a long-lived interactive pod.</p>\n<p>If another team wants the same behavior, they should treat the specific secret names, project names, and channel IDs in this document as implementation examples and swap in their own values.</p>\n<h2>CronJob Manifest</h2>\n<p>The CronJob shape we use looks like this:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: batch/v1\nkind: CronJob\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-project-screening\nspec:\n  schedule: &quot;*/30 * * * *&quot;\n  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid\n  jobTemplate:\n    spec:\n      # No retries — each run is one-shot. A failure should surface in job\n      # logs rather than silently re-claiming the same item.\n      backoffLimit: 0\n      template:\n        spec:\n          restartPolicy: Never\n          containers:\n            - name: project-screening\n              # Pin to a specific tag in production (e.g. :0.8.0) to ensure\n              # reproducible runs. :latest is used here for illustration only.\n              image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-codex\n              command:\n                - bash\n                - /opt/openab-project-screening/screen_once.sh\n              env:\n                - name: GH_TOKEN\n                  valueFrom:\n                    secretKeyRef:\n                      name: openab-project-screening\n                      key: gh-token\n                - name: CODEX_AUTH_JSON_SOURCE\n                  value: /opt/openab-project-screening-auth/auth.json\n                - name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN\n                  valueFrom:\n                    secretKeyRef:\n                      name: openab-kiro-codex\n                      key: discord-bot-token\n                - name: DISCORD_REPORT_CHANNEL_ID\n                  value: &quot;&lt;your_channel_id&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Security settings were kept tight on purpose:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">securityContext:\n  runAsNonRoot: true\n  runAsUser: 1000\n  runAsGroup: 1000\n  fsGroup: 1000\n  seccompProfile:\n    type: RuntimeDefault\n</code></pre>\n<p>Container hardening:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">securityContext:\n  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false\n  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true\n  capabilities:\n    drop:\n      - ALL\n</code></pre>\n<h2>ConfigMap And Script</h2>\n<p>The mounted ConfigMap carries:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>screen_once.sh</code></li>\n<li><code>screening_prompt.md</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p>The core runtime flow in <code>screen_once.sh</code> is:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">item_id=&quot;$(incoming_item_jq '.items[0].id // empty')&quot;\n\nif [[ -z &quot;$item_id&quot; ]]; then\n  log &quot;no Incoming items found&quot;\n  exit 0\nfi\n\ngh project item-edit \\\n  --id &quot;$item_id&quot; \\\n  --project-id &quot;$project_id&quot; \\\n  --field-id &quot;$status_field_id&quot; \\\n  --single-select-option-id &quot;$screening_option_id&quot; &gt;/dev/null\n\ngenerate_report &quot;$prompt_file&quot; &quot;$report_file&quot;\npost_report_to_discord &quot;$item_number&quot; &quot;$item_title&quot; &quot;$item_url&quot; &quot;$report_file&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>That gives us the exact one-shot behavior we want:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>no-op when <code>Incoming</code> is empty</li>\n<li>claim the first item when work exists</li>\n<li>generate the report once</li>\n<li>deliver it once</li>\n<li>exit</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Codex Execution</h2>\n<p>The report is generated with <code>codex exec</code>, not with a long-lived ACP daemon:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">codex exec \\\n  --skip-git-repo-check \\\n  --cd &quot;$WORK_DIR&quot; \\\n  --sandbox read-only \\\n  --ephemeral \\\n  --color never \\\n  --output-last-message &quot;$report_file&quot; \\\n  - &lt;&quot;$prompt_file&quot; &gt;/dev/null\n</code></pre>\n<p>Why <code>codex exec</code>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>this workflow is scheduled and one-shot</li>\n<li>each run should start clean</li>\n<li>we do not need a persistent interactive session</li>\n<li>job logs map naturally to one execution</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Discord Delivery</h2>\n<p>After the report is generated, the script posts a summary message, creates a thread on that message, and then sends the full report into the thread.</p>\n<p>Summary message:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">PR Screening - #&lt;number&gt;\n&lt;title&gt;\nStatus: moved to PR-Screening\n</code></pre>\n<p>Actual implementation:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">starter_content=&quot;🔍 **PR Screening** — [#${item_number}](${item_url})\n${item_title}\nStatus: moved to ${SCREENING_STATUS_NAME}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Thread naming (Node.js helper used by the script):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const base = `Screening: #${number}${title ? ` ${title}` : &quot;&quot;}`.trim();\nprocess.stdout.write(base.slice(0, 100) || `Screening: #${number}`);\n</code></pre>\n<p>Discord API flow:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># 1. post summary message\nPOST /channels/{channel_id}/messages\n\n# 2. create thread on that message\nPOST /channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/threads\n\n# 3. post report chunks\nPOST /channels/{thread_id}/messages\n</code></pre>\n<p>The script also retries on Discord <code>429</code> rate limits before continuing.</p>\n<h2>Secrets</h2>\n<p>The screening job secret contains:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">stringData:\n  gh-token: &quot;REPLACE_WITH_GITHUB_TOKEN_WITH_PROJECT_SCOPE&quot;\n  auth.json: |\n    REPLACE_WITH_CONTENTS_OF_CODEX_AUTH_JSON\n</code></pre>\n<p>Discord is intentionally not duplicated there. The CronJob reads the bot token from the existing:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">Secret name: openab-kiro-codex\nKey: discord-bot-token\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Raw Kubernetes Install</h2>\n<p>Create or update the screening secret:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl -n default create secret generic openab-project-screening \\\n  --from-literal=gh-token='YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN_WITH_PROJECT_SCOPE' \\\n  --from-file=auth.json=&quot;$HOME/.codex/auth.json&quot; \\\n  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -\n</code></pre>\n<p>Verify the shared Discord token secret exists:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl -n default get secret openab-kiro-codex\nkubectl -n default get secret openab-kiro-codex -o jsonpath='{.data.discord-bot-token}' | grep -q .\n</code></pre>\n<p>Apply the ConfigMap and CronJob manifests:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl -n default apply -f project-screening-configmap.yaml\nkubectl -n default apply -f project-screening-cronjob.yaml\n</code></pre>\n<p>Run one manual test:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl -n default create job \\\n  --from=cronjob/openab-project-screening \\\n  openab-project-screening-manual-$(date +%s)\n</code></pre>\n<p>Inspect the logs:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">LATEST_JOB=$(kubectl -n default get jobs \\\n  --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp \\\n  -o jsonpath='{.items[-1:].metadata.name}')\n\nkubectl -n default logs -f job/&quot;$LATEST_JOB&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Helm Values</h2>\n<p>A Helm chart can wire this under <code>projectScreening</code> values like:</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>⚠️ Security note:</strong> <code>githubToken</code> and <code>codexAuthJson</code> below are shown inline for illustration.\nIn practice, supply these via <code>--set</code> flags, environment variables, or an external secret manager\n(e.g. Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator). <strong>Do not commit credentials to version control.</strong></p>\n</blockquote>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">projectScreening:\n  enabled: true\n  schedule: &quot;*/30 * * * *&quot;\n  # Pin to a specific tag in production (e.g. :0.8.0)\n  image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab:beta-codex\n  githubToken: &quot;&lt;token with project scope&gt;&quot;\n  codexAuthJson: |\n    &lt;contents of ~/.codex/auth.json&gt;\n  discordReport:\n    enabled: true\n    secretName: &quot;openab-kiro-codex&quot;\n    secretKey: &quot;discord-bot-token&quot;\n    channelId: &quot;&lt;your_channel_id&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Operational Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>This pod cannot install the CronJob from inside itself without broader RBAC.</li>\n<li>The correct install path is a cluster-admin shell or CI/CD pipeline.</li>\n<li>Once the CronJob is live, stop any older in-pod watcher so only one claimer remains.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Design Summary</h2>\n<p>The elegant part of this setup is that each concern is separated cleanly:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Kubernetes owns the schedule</li>\n<li>GitHub Projects remains the source of truth</li>\n<li><code>codex exec</code> is used as a disposable analysis engine</li>\n<li>Discord is only the reporting surface</li>\n<li>the handoff queue is <code>PR-Screening</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p>That separation is why this design works well in Kubernetes.</p>\n<p>The more opinionated design discussion, including alternatives we considered and why we ultimately chose this route, should live in a separate architecture note. This document is intentionally the operational reference version.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Kubernetes CronJob Reference Architecture"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "refarch/gbrain",
      "html": "<h1>OpenAB + GBrain Reference Architecture</h1>\n<p>Shared persistent memory for OpenAB multi-agent deployments.</p>\n<h2>Background — The Isolation Problem</h2>\n<p>When running multiple AI agents through OpenAB (e.g. Kiro + Claude Code + Copilot), each agent pod operates in complete isolation:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No shared memory</strong> — Agent A discovers a critical finding, but Agent B has no way to access it.</li>\n<li><strong>No cross-agent context</strong> — Handing off a task means losing all the context the previous agent built up.</li>\n<li><strong>No persistent knowledge</strong> — Everything an agent learns is gone when the session ends. The next session starts from zero.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>In a single-agent setup this is tolerable. In a multi-agent deployment — which is the whole point of OpenAB — it becomes a serious bottleneck. Agents duplicate work, miss context, and cannot collaborate on anything beyond the current conversation.</p>\n<p>What we need is a <strong>shared brain</strong>: a persistent, queryable knowledge layer that all agents can read from and write to, in real time.</p>\n<h2>GBrain — A Shared Brain for AI Agents</h2>\n<p><a href=\"https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain\">GBrain</a> is an open-source persistent memory system built on PostgreSQL + pgvector. It was designed specifically for AI agent workflows.</p>\n<p>What makes it a good fit:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>MCP native</strong> — Exposes 30+ tools via the standard MCP protocol. Any ACP CLI that supports MCP (Kiro, Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode, etc.) can use it out of the box — no custom integration needed.</li>\n<li><strong>Hybrid search</strong> — Combines vector similarity, keyword matching, and knowledge graph traversal. Agents get high-quality retrieval, not just embedding cosine distance.</li>\n<li><strong>Structured knowledge</strong> — Pages with markdown + frontmatter + tags, typed links between entities (<code>assigned_to</code>, <code>depends_on</code>, …), and chronological timelines per entity.</li>\n<li><strong>Simple deployment</strong> — One PostgreSQL instance, one CLI binary. No external services, no API keys, no complex infrastructure.</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code>Capabilities:\n  • Pages        markdown + frontmatter + tags\n  • Search       hybrid (vector + keyword + graph)\n  • Links        typed edges (assigned_to, depends_on, …)\n  • Timeline     chronological events per entity\n  • 30+ tools    exposed via MCP (brain_write, brain_query, …)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>How GBrain Fits into OpenAB</h2>\n<p>The integration is straightforward: each OAB agent pod runs <code>gbrain serve</code> as a local MCP server, and all instances point to the same PostgreSQL database. One agent writes a page → all others can query it instantly.</p>\n<pre><code>  Discord / Slack / Telegram / LINE\n    │            │            │\n    ▼            ▼            ▼\n┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐\n│OAB Pod │ │OAB Pod │ │OAB Pod │   ← any ACP CLI (kiro, claude, copilot, …)\n│        │ │        │ │        │\n│ gbrain │ │ gbrain │ │ gbrain │   ← MCP server per pod (gbrain serve)\n│  serve │ │  serve │ │  serve │\n└───┬────┘ └───┬────┘ └───┬────┘\n    └──────────┼──────────┘\n               ▼\n     ┌───────────────────┐\n     │  gbrain-postgres  │   pgvector/pgvector:pg16 · 5Gi PVC\n     └───────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Zero coupling</strong> — GBrain is an add-on, not a dependency. OpenAB works fine without it. You opt in when you need cross-agent memory.</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>OpenAB</strong>: <a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab\">https://github.com/openabdev/openab</a></li>\n<li><strong>GBrain</strong>: <a href=\"https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain\">https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain</a></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Cross-Agent Workflow Example</h3>\n<pre><code>┌─ Agent A writes ──────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                           │\n│  gbrain put handoff/task-42   ← structured page           │\n│  gbrain link handoff/task-42 agent/B --type assigned_to   │\n│                                                           │\n├─ Agent B queries ─────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                           │\n│  gbrain query &quot;what tasks are assigned to me?&quot;            │\n│  gbrain get handoff/task-42   ← full context              │\n│                                                           │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Deployment</h2>\n<p>Currently, GBrain is set up manually alongside OpenAB. The Helm chart does not include built-in GBrain support yet, but the <code>extra*</code> escape hatches make automation possible.</p>\n<h3>Manual Setup</h3>\n<p>For existing OpenAB deployments. No Helm changes needed.</p>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ 1. Deploy PostgreSQL                                    │\n│                                                         │\n│    kubectl create secret ─► gbrain-postgres-secret      │\n│    kubectl apply          ─► Deployment + Service + PVC │\n│                                                         │\n│    Image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16                        │\n│    Env:   POSTGRES_DB=gbrain                            │\n│           POSTGRES_USER=gbrain                          │\n│           POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(from secret)               │\n│    PVC:   5Gi RWO                                       │\n│    Svc:   ClusterIP :5432                               │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ 2. For each OAB agent pod:                              │\n│                                                         │\n│    kubectl exec &lt;pod&gt; ──┐                               │\n│                         ├─► Install gbrain CLI          │\n│    curl install.sh      │   → ~/.local/bin/gbrain       │\n│                         ├─► Init database               │\n│    gbrain init --url    │   → ~/.gbrain/config.json     │\n│                         ├─► Write MCP config            │\n│                         │                               │\n│    ┌──────────┬─────────────────────────────┐           │\n│    │ CLI      │ MCP config path             │           │\n│    ├──────────┼─────────────────────────────┤           │\n│    │ kiro     │ ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json   │           │\n│    │ claude   │ ~/.claude/server.json       │           │\n│    │ copilot  │ ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json  │           │\n│    └──────────┴─────────────────────────────┘           │\n│                                                         │\n│    MCP config content:                                  │\n│    {&quot;mcpServers&quot;:{&quot;gbrain&quot;:{                            │\n│      &quot;command&quot;:&quot;~/.local/bin/gbrain&quot;,                   │\n│      &quot;args&quot;:[&quot;serve&quot;]}}}                                │\n│                                                         │\n│    ⚠ Note: ~ may not expand in all environments.        │\n│    Use $HOME or an absolute path if your MCP client     │\n│    or init container does not perform tilde expansion.   │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ 3. Verify                                               │\n│                                                         │\n│    kubectl exec &lt;pod&gt; -- gbrain stats                   │\n│    kubectl exec &lt;pod&gt; -- gbrain query &quot;test&quot;            │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>Data lives on PVC — survives pod restarts when <code>persistence.enabled: true</code> (OpenAB default).</p>\n<h3>Future: Helm Integration</h3>\n<p>The OpenAB Helm chart does not have first-class GBrain support today. For advanced users, the chart exposes <code>extraInitContainers</code>, <code>extraVolumes</code>, and <code>extraVolumeMounts</code> per agent — these can be used to automate the manual steps above at the pod level. A dedicated <code>gbrain.enabled</code> Helm value may be considered in a future release.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "OpenAB + GBrain Reference Architecture"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "refarch/remote-ssh-debugging",
      "html": "<h1>Debugging and Reproducing Issues via Remote SSH</h1>\n<p>This document describes how an OpenAB agent running inside a pod can debug, troubleshoot, and reproduce GitHub issues against a remote host over SSH — and validate proposed fixes before posting results.</p>\n<h2>Why This Matters</h2>\n<p>An AI agent that only reads code and speculates about bugs is limited. By giving the agent SSH access to a real environment, it can:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Reproduce issues end-to-end</strong> — deploy, configure, and observe the actual failure instead of guessing from source code</li>\n<li><strong>Validate fixes before posting</strong> — confirm the proposed solution works, not just that it looks correct</li>\n<li><strong>Provide evidence-based triage</strong> — post reproduction logs and fix verification to GitHub, giving maintainers confidence to act</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Use Cases</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Helm / Kubernetes issues</strong> — install a chart, inspect rendered manifests, check pod logs</li>\n<li><strong>Configuration bugs</strong> — apply a config, start a service, verify behavior</li>\n<li><strong>Infrastructure issues</strong> — test networking, DNS, storage, permissions on a real host</li>\n<li><strong>Documentation gaps</strong> — follow documented steps exactly and confirm they work (or don't)</li>\n<li><strong>Regression testing</strong> — deploy a specific version, trigger the reported bug, upgrade, confirm it's fixed</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>ASCII Flow</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Discord / Slack                                            │\n│                                                             │\n│  Maintainer: &quot;validate issue #N&quot;                            │\n│       │                                                     │\n│       ▼                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────┐                                               │\n│  │ OAB Bot  │  (OpenAB agent)                               │\n│  └────┬─────┘                                               │\n└───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n        │\n        ▼\n┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  OpenAB Pod                               │\n│                                           │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  Agent Runtime                      │  │\n│  │                                     │  │\n│  │  1. gh issue view &lt;N&gt;               │  │\n│  │  2. gh api → read source on main    │  │\n│  │  3. ssh k8s &quot;&lt;reproduce&gt;&quot;           │──┼──── SSH ────┐\n│  │  4. ssh k8s &quot;&lt;inspect logs/state&gt;&quot;  │──┼──── SSH ────┤\n│  │  5. ssh k8s &quot;&lt;apply fix&gt;&quot;           │──┼──── SSH ────┤\n│  │  6. gh issue comment &lt;N&gt;            │  │             │\n│  │                                     │  │             │\n│  │  Tools: gh, ssh (~/bin/), curl      │  │             │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────┘  │             │\n│                                           │             │\n│  No sudo · read-only rootfs               │             │\n│  SSH installed via dpkg-deb extract       │             │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────┘             │\n                                                          │\n                                                          ▼\n                                            ┌─────────────────────────┐\n                                            │  Remote Host            │\n                                            │                         │\n                                            │  Any environment:       │\n                                            │  • Kubernetes cluster   │\n                                            │  • Docker host          │\n                                            │  • Bare metal / VM      │\n                                            │                         │\n                                            │  Agent reproduces the   │\n                                            │  issue here, then       │\n                                            │  validates the fix.     │\n                                            └─────────────────────────┘\n\nFlow:\n  ① Maintainer triggers triage via chat message\n  ② Agent reads issue + relevant source code via GitHub API\n  ③ Agent SSHs into remote host to reproduce the reported problem\n  ④ Agent inspects logs, config, or state to confirm the error\n  ⑤ Agent applies the proposed fix and verifies it resolves the issue\n  ⑥ Agent posts structured results back to the GitHub issue\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Why This Pattern</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>The agent pod is sandboxed.</strong> It cannot run Kubernetes, Docker, or other infrastructure locally. SSH to a remote host gives the agent access to a real environment without requiring privileged containers.</li>\n<li><strong>GitHub API avoids cloning.</strong> The agent reads issue details, source code, and config files via <code>gh api</code> / <code>gh issue view</code>, then posts results with <code>gh issue comment</code>. No local clone needed for triage.</li>\n<li><strong>Reproducibility over speculation.</strong> The agent follows the exact steps a user would — deploy, configure, observe the error, apply the fix. This catches real-world gaps that code review alone misses.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<h3>SSH on the Agent Pod</h3>\n<p>The agent pod typically has no <code>sudo</code> and a read-only root filesystem. Install OpenSSH by extracting the official Debian deb package.</p>\n<p>Find the current <code>.deb</code> URL at <a href=\"https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/amd64/openssh-client/download\">https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/amd64/openssh-client/download</a>, then:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">mkdir -p ~/bin /tmp/ssh-extract\ncurl -fsSL -o /tmp/openssh-client.deb &quot;&lt;url from the download page&gt;&quot;\ndpkg-deb -x /tmp/openssh-client.deb /tmp/ssh-extract\ncp /tmp/ssh-extract/usr/bin/{ssh,ssh-keygen,scp} ~/bin/\nchmod +x ~/bin/{ssh,ssh-keygen,scp}\nexport PATH=&quot;$HOME/bin:$PATH&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>SSH Key and Config</h3>\n<p>Generate a key pair and configure the remote host:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -N &quot;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Add the public key to the remote host's <code>~/.ssh/authorized_keys</code>, then create <code>~/.ssh/config</code>:</p>\n<pre><code>Host k8s\n    HostName &lt;remote-ip&gt;\n    User &lt;user&gt;\n    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Remote Host</h3>\n<p>The remote host can be any environment relevant to the issue:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>A Kubernetes cluster (any distribution) with <code>kubectl</code> and <code>helm</code></li>\n<li>A Docker host</li>\n<li>A bare VM or EC2 instance</li>\n</ul>\n<p>The only requirement is that the SSH user has the permissions needed to reproduce the issue.</p>\n<h2>Triage Steps</h2>\n<h3>1. Read the Issue</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh issue view &lt;N&gt; --repo &lt;org&gt;/&lt;repo&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Understand the claim: what's broken, what error is reported, what fix is proposed.</p>\n<h3>2. Verify on Main</h3>\n<p>Read the relevant source code via GitHub API to confirm the claim before touching the remote host:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh api repos/&lt;org&gt;/&lt;repo&gt;/contents/&lt;path&gt; --jq '.content' | base64 -d\n</code></pre>\n<p>This step often reveals the root cause without deploying anything.</p>\n<h3>3. Reproduce</h3>\n<p>SSH into the remote host and follow the reporter's steps (or the documented steps) to trigger the error:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">ssh k8s &quot;&lt;commands to reproduce the issue&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Capture the error output — logs, config state, exit codes — as evidence.</p>\n<h3>4. Validate the Fix</h3>\n<p>Apply the proposed fix on the same host and confirm the error is resolved:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">ssh k8s &quot;&lt;commands to apply the fix&gt;&quot;\nssh k8s &quot;&lt;commands to verify the fix worked&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Capture the post-fix output as evidence.</p>\n<h3>5. Post Results to GitHub</h3>\n<p>Post a structured comment with the verdict up front and details collapsed:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh issue comment &lt;N&gt; --repo &lt;org&gt;/&lt;repo&gt; --body '\n## ✅ Bug validated — proposed fix verified\n\n### Bug confirmed\n&lt;one paragraph: what was tested, what error occurred, root cause&gt;\n\n### Proposed fix (validated)\n&lt;diff or command showing the fix + post-fix output&gt;\n\n&lt;details&gt;\n&lt;summary&gt;Full reproduction steps&lt;/summary&gt;\n&lt;step-by-step commands and outputs&gt;\n&lt;/details&gt;\n'\n</code></pre>\n<h3>6. Clean Up</h3>\n<p>Remove any test resources created on the remote host during reproduction.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Debugging and Reproducing Issues via Remote SSH"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "refarch/sidecar-proxy",
      "html": "<h1>Reference Architecture: OAuth Sidecar Proxy</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> For xAI/Grok models, OpenCode ≥1.15.0 supports native xAI OAuth.\nThe sidecar proxy is no longer required for OpenCode deployments.\nSee <a href=\"/openab/xai-proxy\">docs/xai-proxy.md</a> for the recommended approach.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>This document describes the <strong>sidecar proxy pattern</strong> implemented by\n<code>openab-auth-proxy</code> — a generic OAuth proxy that injects Bearer tokens into\nupstream API requests.</p>\n<h2>When to use this pattern</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Agents <strong>without</strong> built-in OAuth (Hermes, custom agents)</li>\n<li>Centralizing token management across multiple containers in a pod</li>\n<li>Proxying to any OAuth-protected API (not just xAI)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Architecture</h2>\n<pre><code>┌─ Kubernetes Pod ──────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                               │\n│  agent container (any OpenAI-compatible client)               │\n│               │  POST /v1/chat/completions                    │\n│               │  (no auth header needed)                      │\n│               ▼                                               │\n│         openab-auth-proxy :9090                               │\n│           • Reads OAuth token from disk                       │\n│           • Injects Authorization: Bearer header              │\n│           • Auto-refreshes 120s before expiry                 │\n│               │                                               │\n│  Token: ~/.openab-auth-proxy/&lt;provider&gt;/tokens.json           │\n└───────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                ▼\n        upstream API (configured via TOML or xAI default)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<p>Without a config file, <code>openab-auth-proxy</code> defaults to xAI/SuperGrok.</p>\n<p>For other providers, create <code>auth-proxy.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[provider]\nname = &quot;my-provider&quot;\ndiscovery_url = &quot;https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration&quot;\nclient_id = &quot;my-client-id&quot;\nscopes = &quot;openid offline_access api:access&quot;\nupstream_base_url = &quot;https://api.example.com&quot;\nredirect_port = 8080\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Helm deployment (xAI example)</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># 1. Login locally\nopenab-auth-proxy login-device\n\n# 2. Create K8s secret\nkubectl create secret generic auth-proxy-tokens \\\n  --from-file=tokens.json=$HOME/.openab-auth-proxy/xai/tokens.json\n\n# 3. Deploy with sidecar\nhelm install openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.mybot.command=opencode \\\n  --set-json 'agents.mybot.args=[&quot;acp&quot;]' \\\n  --set-json 'agents.mybot.extraContainers=[{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;auth-proxy&quot;,&quot;image&quot;:&quot;ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-auth-proxy:latest&quot;,&quot;args&quot;:[&quot;serve&quot;,&quot;--bind&quot;,&quot;0.0.0.0&quot;],&quot;ports&quot;:[{&quot;containerPort&quot;:9090}],&quot;volumeMounts&quot;:[{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;data&quot;,&quot;mountPath&quot;:&quot;/home/agent&quot;}]}]' \\\n  --set-json 'agents.mybot.extraInitContainers=[{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;copy-tokens&quot;,&quot;image&quot;:&quot;busybox&quot;,&quot;command&quot;:[&quot;sh&quot;,&quot;-c&quot;,&quot;mkdir -p /dest/.openab-auth-proxy/xai &amp;&amp; cp /src/tokens.json /dest/.openab-auth-proxy/xai/tokens.json&quot;],&quot;volumeMounts&quot;:[{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;tokens-src&quot;,&quot;mountPath&quot;:&quot;/src&quot;,&quot;readOnly&quot;:true},{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;data&quot;,&quot;mountPath&quot;:&quot;/dest&quot;}]}]' \\\n  --set-json 'agents.mybot.extraVolumes=[{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;tokens-src&quot;,&quot;secret&quot;:{&quot;secretName&quot;:&quot;auth-proxy-tokens&quot;}}]'\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Environment variables</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>AUTH_PROXY_TOKEN_PATH</code></td>\n<td><code>~/.openab-auth-proxy/&lt;provider&gt;/tokens.json</code></td>\n<td>Token file location</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>XAI_PROXY_TOKEN_PATH</code></td>\n<td>(legacy alias)</td>\n<td>Backward-compatible</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>RUST_LOG</code></td>\n<td><code>openab_auth_proxy=info</code></td>\n<td>Log verbosity</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>See also</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/linyiru/openab/tree/6ad4ef419dd131e3f718dfd9b224f3967387da94/openab-auth-proxy\">openab-auth-proxy source</a> — Rust implementation</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/xai-proxy\">docs/xai-proxy.md</a> — xAI-specific quick-start</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Reference Architecture: OAuth Sidecar Proxy"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "refarch/telegram-cloudflare-tunnel",
      "html": "<h1>Reference Architecture: Telegram via Cloudflare Tunnel</h1>\n<p>Deploy OpenAB on K3s with Telegram webhooks through a Cloudflare Tunnel — no public IP, no ingress controller, no TLS certificates required.</p>\n<h2>Deployment Modes</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mode</th>\n<th>Containers</th>\n<th>When to use</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Unified</strong> (recommended)</td>\n<td>2 (OAB + cloudflared)</td>\n<td>New deployments, simpler setup</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Standalone Gateway</strong> (legacy)</td>\n<td>3 (OAB + gateway + cloudflared)</td>\n<td>Custom routing, multi-gateway fan-out</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Unified Mode (Recommended)</h2>\n<p>The OAB binary embeds the Telegram adapter directly — no separate gateway container needed.</p>\n<h3>Architecture</h3>\n<pre><code>Telegram Cloud\n    │ HTTPS POST\n    ▼\nCloudflare Edge (bot.example.com)\n    │ Tunnel (QUIC)\n    ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ Single Pod                                          │\n│                                                     │\n│ ┌─────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────┐   │\n│ │ cloudflared │────▶│  OAB :8080               │   │\n│ │ (sidecar)   │     │  /webhook/telegram       │   │\n│ └─────────────┘     │  (embedded adapter)      │   │\n│    localhost         └──────────────────────────┘   │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>Two containers in the <strong>same pod</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>cloudflared</strong> — tunnel client, forwards Cloudflare traffic to <code>localhost:8080</code></li>\n<li><strong>OAB</strong> — embeds the webhook server + adapter + agent in one binary</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Prerequisites</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Requirement</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>K3s cluster</td>\n<td>Any single-node or multi-node K3s setup</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Helm 3</td>\n<td>Installed on the node or a workstation with kubeconfig access</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cloudflare account</td>\n<td>Free plan is sufficient</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Telegram Bot Token</td>\n<td>Create via <a href=\"https://t.me/BotFather\">@BotFather</a></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Domain on Cloudflare</td>\n<td>DNS managed by Cloudflare</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Step 1: Create a Cloudflare Tunnel</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Create a tunnel</strong></li>\n<li>Name it (e.g. <code>openab-telegram</code>)</li>\n<li>Copy the <strong>tunnel token</strong></li>\n<li>Add a <strong>public hostname</strong>:\n<ul>\n<li>Subdomain: your choice (e.g. <code>bot</code>)</li>\n<li>Domain: your Cloudflare-managed domain</li>\n<li>Service: <code>http://localhost:8080</code></li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Step 2: Deploy with Helm</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm install my-bot oci://ghcr.io/openabdev/charts/openab-telegram \\\n  --set telegramBotToken=&quot;&lt;token-from-botfather&gt;&quot; \\\n  --set cloudflareTunnelToken=&quot;$(cloudflared tunnel token my-telegram-bot)&quot; \\\n  --set webhookDomain=bot.example.com \\\n  --set platform.allowedUsers=&quot;{&lt;your-telegram-user-id&gt;}&quot; \\\n  --namespace openab --create-namespace\n</code></pre>\n<p>The unified image (<code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-unified</code>) embeds all platform adapters. No <code>[gateway]</code> config section needed — set <code>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</code> as env var and the embedded webhook server activates automatically.</p>\n<h3>Step 3: Authenticate the Agent</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/my-bot -n openab -c openab -- kiro-cli login --use-device-flow\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/my-bot -n openab\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Step 4: Set the Telegram Webhook</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl &quot;https://api.telegram.org/bot&lt;TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN&gt;/setWebhook&quot; \\\n  -d &quot;url=https://bot.example.com/webhook/telegram&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Resulting Resources</h3>\n<pre><code>$ kubectl get pods -n openab\nNAME                                    READY   STATUS    AGE\nmy-bot-xxxxx-yyyyy                      2/2     Running   ...\n</code></pre>\n<p>Two containers: <code>openab</code> (unified binary with embedded adapter) and <code>cloudflared</code>.</p>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<p>Minimal <code>config.toml</code> (no <code>[gateway]</code> needed):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;compact&quot;\n\n[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Standalone Gateway Mode (Legacy)</h2>\n<p>For deployments that need a separate gateway process (custom webhook routing, multi-gateway fan-out).</p>\n<h3>Architecture</h3>\n<pre><code>Telegram Cloud\n    │ HTTPS POST\n    ▼\nCloudflare Edge (your_custom.domain.com)\n    │ Tunnel (QUIC)\n    ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ Single Pod                                          │\n│                                                     │\n│ ┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐  │\n│ │ cloudflared │─▶│gateway :8080 │◀─│     OAB     │  │\n│ │ (sidecar)   │ │  (sidecar)   │ws│   (main)    │  │\n│ └─────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘  │\n│    localhost          localhost                      │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>All three components run as containers in the <strong>same pod</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>cloudflared</strong> — tunnel client, forwards Cloudflare traffic to <code>localhost:8080</code></li>\n<li><strong>gateway</strong> — receives Telegram webhooks, normalizes events, serves WebSocket on <code>:8080</code></li>\n<li><strong>OAB</strong> — connects to <code>ws://localhost:8080/ws</code>, runs the agent</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This keeps all communication on <code>localhost</code> — no K8s Services or cross-pod networking required.</p>\n<h3>Prerequisites</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Requirement</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>K3s cluster</td>\n<td>Any single-node or multi-node K3s setup</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Helm 3</td>\n<td>Installed on the node or a workstation with kubeconfig access</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cloudflare account</td>\n<td>Free plan
