is sufficient</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Telegram Bot Token</td>\n<td>Create via <a href=\"https://t.me/BotFather\">@BotFather</a></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Domain on Cloudflare</td>\n<td>DNS managed by Cloudflare</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Step 1: Create a Cloudflare Tunnel</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <strong>Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Create a tunnel</strong></li>\n<li>Name it (e.g. <code>openab-telegram</code>)</li>\n<li>Copy the <strong>tunnel token</strong></li>\n<li>Add a <strong>public hostname</strong>:\n<ul>\n<li>Subdomain: your choice (e.g. <code>bot</code>)</li>\n<li>Domain: your Cloudflare-managed domain</li>\n<li>Service: <code>http://localhost:8080</code></li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Step 2: Deploy with Helm</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cd openab\n\nRELEASE_NAME=&quot;my-openab&quot;\n\nhelm upgrade --install &quot;$RELEASE_NAME&quot; ./charts/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.discord.enabled=false \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.deploy=false \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.url=&quot;ws://localhost:8080/ws&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.platform=telegram \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[0].name=gateway \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[0].image=&quot;ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:0.4.0&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[0].env[0].name=TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN \\\n  --set-literal agents.kiro.extraContainers[0].env[0].value=&quot;&lt;TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN&gt;&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[1].name=cloudflared \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[1].image=&quot;cloudflare/cloudflared:latest&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[1].args[0]=&quot;tunnel&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[1].args[1]=&quot;--no-autoupdate&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[1].args[2]=&quot;run&quot; \\\n  --set agents.kiro.extraContainers[1].args[3]=&quot;--token&quot; \\\n  --set-literal agents.kiro.extraContainers[1].args[4]=&quot;&lt;CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN&gt;&quot; \\\n  --namespace openab --create-namespace\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Key difference:</strong> <code>gateway.deploy=false</code> skips the separate gateway Deployment/Service. Instead, gateway and cloudflared run as <code>extraContainers</code> sidecars in the OAB pod, communicating over <code>localhost</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Step 3: Authenticate the Agent</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl exec -it deployment/${RELEASE_NAME}-kiro -n openab -- kiro-cli login --use-device-flow\n</code></pre>\n<p>After login, restart the pod to pick up credentials:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">kubectl rollout restart deployment/${RELEASE_NAME}-kiro -n openab\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Step 4: Set the Telegram Webhook</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl &quot;https://api.telegram.org/bot&lt;TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN&gt;/setWebhook&quot; \\\n  -d &quot;url=https://your_custom.domain.com/webhook/telegram&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Verify:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl &quot;https://api.telegram.org/bot&lt;TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN&gt;/getWebhookInfo&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Resulting Resources</h3>\n<pre><code>$ kubectl get pods -n openab\nNAME                                    READY   STATUS    AGE\nmy-openab-kiro-xxxxx-yyyyy              3/3     Running   ...\n</code></pre>\n<p>The single pod runs 3 containers: <code>kiro</code> (OAB agent), <code>gateway</code>, and <code>cloudflared</code>.</p>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<p>The rendered <code>config.toml</code> for the OAB agent:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\ncommand = &quot;kiro-cli&quot;\nargs = [&quot;acp&quot;, &quot;--trust-all-tools&quot;]\nworking_dir = &quot;/home/agent&quot;\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 10\nsession_ttl_hours = 24\n\n[reactions]\nenabled = true\nremove_after_reply = false\n\n[gateway]\nurl = &quot;ws://localhost:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;telegram&quot;\nurl = &quot;ws://localhost:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;telegram&quot;\nallow_all_channels = true\nallowed_channels = []\n# ⚠️ Recommended: restrict to specific Telegram user IDs\nallow_all_users = false\nallowed_users = [&quot;&lt;YOUR_TELEGRAM_USER_ID&gt;&quot;]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Restricting Access</h3>\n<p>To limit which Telegram users can interact with the bot:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade $RELEASE_NAME ./charts/openab \\\n  ... \\\n  --set agents.kiro.gateway.allowAllUsers=false \\\n  --set-string agents.kiro.gateway.allowedUsers[0]=&quot;&lt;TELEGRAM_USER_ID&gt;&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Why Cloudflare Tunnel?</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No public IP required</strong> — the K3s node can be behind NAT or a firewall.</li>\n<li><strong>No TLS management</strong> — Cloudflare terminates TLS at the edge.</li>\n<li><strong>No ingress controller config</strong> — bypasses Traefik/nginx entirely.</li>\n<li><strong>Single-pod simplicity</strong> — all components share <code>localhost</code>, no cross-pod networking needed.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Reference Architecture: Telegram via Cloudflare Tunnel"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "secrets-management",
      "html": "<h1>Secrets Management</h1>\n<p>OpenAB supports resolving secrets from external providers at boot time. Credentials are held in memory only — never written to disk, never exposed in environment variables or logs.</p>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.refs]\ndiscord_token = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#discord_bot_token&quot;\n\n[discord]\nbot_token = &quot;${secrets.discord_token}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>That's it. OpenAB fetches the secret from AWS Secrets Manager on startup and injects it into the config.</p>\n<h2>Providers</h2>\n<h3>AWS Secrets Manager (<code>aws-sm://</code>)</h3>\n<pre><code>aws-sm://&lt;secret-id&gt;#&lt;json-key&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>&lt;secret-id&gt;</code> — Secret name or full ARN</li>\n<li><code>&lt;json-key&gt;</code> — Key within the JSON-structured secret value</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Authentication:</strong> Uses the default AWS credential chain (env vars → IMDS → IRSA → ECS task role). No extra credentials needed.</p>\n<p><strong>Example</strong> — one secret storing multiple keys:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;discord_bot_token&quot;: &quot;MTQ5...&quot;,\n  &quot;openai_api_key&quot;: &quot;sk-...&quot;,\n  &quot;github_pat&quot;: &quot;ghp_...&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.refs]\ndiscord_token = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#discord_bot_token&quot;\nopenai_key    = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#openai_api_key&quot;\ngithub_pat    = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#github_pat&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Optional configuration:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.aws]\nregion = &quot;ap-northeast-1&quot;          # override region\nendpoint_url = &quot;http://localhost:4566&quot;  # LocalStack\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Exec Provider (<code>exec://</code>)</h3>\n<pre><code>exec://&lt;script-path&gt; &lt;key&gt; &lt;attribute&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>&lt;script-path&gt;</code> — Absolute path to executable (must not contain spaces)</li>\n<li><code>&lt;key&gt;</code> — First argument: which secret to fetch</li>\n<li><code>&lt;attribute&gt;</code> — Second argument: which field within that secret</li>\n</ul>\n<p>The script must output the secret value to stdout (single line). Non-zero exit = failure.</p>\n<p><strong>Example:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.refs]\nvault_token = &quot;exec:///home/agent/.local/bin/get-secret.sh vault/openab token&quot;\n\n[secrets.exec]\ntimeout_seconds = 15\n</code></pre>\n<p>Where <code>get-secret.sh</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">#!/bin/sh\n# Usage: get-secret.sh &lt;path&gt; &lt;key&gt;\nvault kv get -field=&quot;$2&quot; &quot;$1&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Security:</strong> Exec scripts run with a sanitized environment (same as <code>[hooks.pre_boot]</code>). Only <code>HOME</code>, <code>PATH</code>, <code>USER</code>, and cloud credential vars (<code>AWS_*</code>, <code>GOOGLE_*</code>, <code>AZURE_*</code>) are passed through.</p>\n<h2>Boot Sequence</h2>\n<pre><code>1. Parse config.toml (env vars expanded)\n2. Run [hooks.pre_boot]          ← scripts provisioned here\n3. Resolve [secrets.refs]        ← fetch from AWS SM / exec\n4. Substitute ${secrets.*}       ← inject into config\n5. Re-parse config               ← final config with real values\n6. Start agent sessions\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Critical:</strong> Secrets resolution runs AFTER <code>pre_boot</code> hooks. If your <code>exec://</code> scripts are downloaded by a hook, they will be available.</p>\n<h2>Error Handling</h2>\n<p>OpenAB is <strong>fail-closed</strong> — if any secret cannot be resolved, the process exits with a non-zero code. This prevents starting with missing credentials.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>AWS API error</td>\n<td>Log error, exit 1</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Exec script not found</td>\n<td>Log hint about pre_boot hooks, exit 1</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Exec script timeout</td>\n<td>Kill process, log error, exit 1</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>JSON key not found</td>\n<td>Log error, exit 1</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Cost</h2>\n<p>AWS Secrets Manager: <strong>$0.40/secret/month</strong> + $0.05 per 10,000 API calls. Store all your credentials in one JSON secret to minimize cost.</p>\n<h2>EKS / IRSA Setup</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Create an IAM policy:</li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,\n  &quot;Action&quot;: [&quot;secretsmanager:GetSecretValue&quot;],\n  &quot;Resource&quot;: &quot;arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:openab/*&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<ol start=\"2\">\n<li>Attach to a ServiceAccount via IRSA:</li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">serviceAccount:\n  annotations:\n    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/openab-secrets-reader\n</code></pre>\n<ol start=\"3\">\n<li>Reference in config:</li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.refs]\ndiscord_token = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#discord_bot_token&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>No additional credentials needed — the pod's IRSA role handles authentication.</p>\n<h2>Feature Flags</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Provider</th>\n<th>Cargo Feature</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>AWS Secrets Manager</td>\n<td><code>secrets-aws</code></td>\n<td>✅ Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Exec (any provider)</td>\n<td>always built</td>\n<td>✅ Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>HashiCorp Vault</td>\n<td><code>secrets-vault</code></td>\n<td>❌ Opt-in</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>GCP Secret Manager</td>\n<td><code>secrets-gcp</code></td>\n<td>❌ Opt-in</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>To build with additional providers:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-dockerfile\">ARG FEATURES=&quot;default,secrets-vault&quot;\nRUN cargo build --release --features &quot;${FEATURES}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Secrets management"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "sendfiles",
      "html": "<h1>Sending Files Back to Discord</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>This doc is designed for your coding agent.</strong> Share it with your agent so it learns how to send files back to Discord.</p>\n<p>Example prompt:</p>\n<pre><code>Read docs/sendfiles.md from OpenAB GitHub and send the file back to my Discord thread.\n</code></pre>\n<p>💡 <strong>Tip:</strong> If it works the first time, ask your agent to save this as a <strong>SKILL</strong> so it remembers how to do it next time without re-reading the doc.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<p>OpenAB streams text only — it does <strong>not</strong> relay file attachments from the agent.\nTo send a file back to the user, the agent must call the Discord API directly.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>For image-specific guidance (formats, sidecar pattern), see <a href=\"/openab/sendimages\">sendimages.md</a>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<h3>Direct Upload (small files)</h3>\n<pre><code>┌──────────┐  text only   ┌──────────┐  ACP stdio   ┌──────────────┐\n│  Discord  │◄────────────│  OpenAB   │◄────────────│  Agent (CLI)  │\n│  Thread   │             └──────────┘              └──────┬───────┘\n│           │                                              │\n│           │         Discord REST API                     │\n│           │◄─────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n│           │  POST /channels/{thread_id}/messages\n│           │  + multipart file attachment\n└──────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Enterprise / Large Files (presigned URL)</h3>\n<pre><code>┌──────────┐  text only   ┌──────────┐  ACP stdio   ┌──────────────┐\n│  Discord  │◄────────────│  OpenAB   │◄────────────│  Agent (CLI)  │\n│  Thread   │             └──────────┘              └──────┬───────┘\n│           │                                              │\n│           │  send presigned URL as message                │  upload file\n│           │◄─────────────────────────────────────────────┤─────────────►┌─────┐\n│           │  POST /channels/{thread_id}/messages         │              │ S3  │\n└─────┬────┘                                               │              │ R2  │\n      │                                                    │              │ GCS │\n      │  user clicks link                                  │              └──┬──┘\n      └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►│\n                              presigned GET                                 │\n                              ◄─────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>OpenAB only streams text via ACP. To send a file, the agent calls the\nDiscord API directly using the <code>thread_id</code> from <code>sender_context</code>.</p>\n<h2>Step-by-Step</h2>\n<h3>1. Get the Target Channel from <code>sender_context</code></h3>\n<p>Every message includes a <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> JSON block:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;schema&quot;: &quot;openab.sender.v1&quot;,\n  &quot;channel&quot;: &quot;discord&quot;,\n  &quot;channel_id&quot;: &quot;1490282656913559673&quot;,\n  &quot;thread_id&quot;: &quot;1499442140172910654&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Use <strong><code>thread_id</code></strong> as the target. Fall back to <code>channel_id</code> if <code>thread_id</code> is absent.</p>\n<h3>2. Get the Bot Token</h3>\n<p>The agent needs a Discord Bot Token to call the API. Pass it via <code>[agent] env</code> in <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ The token in <code>[discord] bot_token</code> is consumed by OpenAB itself and is <strong>not</strong> automatically forwarded to the agent subprocess. You must explicitly pass it via <code>[agent] env</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>Security: dedicated bot recommended</h4>\n<p>For production, consider creating a <strong>dedicated &quot;File Deliverer&quot; bot</strong> with minimal permissions instead of sharing the main OAB bot token. See <a href=\"/openab/sendimages#security-dedicated-bot-recommended\">sendimages.md — Security: dedicated bot recommended</a> for the full architecture diagram and comparison table.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Production: dedicated file-upload bot (e.g. &quot;File Deliverer&quot;)\n[agent]\nenv = { DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN = &quot;${DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p>For personal use or small teams, sharing the same token is fine — you already trust your agent.</p>\n<h3>3. Upload the File</h3>\n<pre><code>POST https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/{thread_id}/messages\nAuthorization: Bot {DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}\nContent-Type: multipart/form-data\n</code></pre>\n<h4>curl example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST &quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/${THREAD_ID}/messages&quot; \\\n  -H &quot;Authorization: Bot ${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;content=Here is the report&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;files[0]=@/path/to/report.pdf&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Multiple files</h4>\n<p>Discord supports up to <strong>10 attachments</strong> per message:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST &quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/${THREAD_ID}/messages&quot; \\\n  -H &quot;Authorization: Bot ${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;content=Build artifacts&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;files[0]=@build.log&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;files[1]=@coverage.html&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Python example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import os, requests\n\ndef send_file(thread_id: str, file_path: str, message: str = &quot;&quot;):\n    url = f&quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/{thread_id}/messages&quot;\n    headers = {&quot;Authorization&quot;: f&quot;Bot {os.environ['DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN']}&quot;}\n    with open(file_path, &quot;rb&quot;) as f:\n        requests.post(url, headers=headers,\n                      data={&quot;content&quot;: message},\n                      files={&quot;files[0]&quot;: (os.path.basename(file_path), f)})\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Node.js example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const fs = require(&quot;fs&quot;);\nconst FormData = require(&quot;form-data&quot;);\n\nasync function sendFile(threadId, filePath, message = &quot;&quot;) {\n  const form = new FormData();\n  form.append(&quot;content&quot;, message);\n  form.append(&quot;files[0]&quot;, fs.createReadStream(filePath));\n\n  await fetch(`https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/${threadId}/messages`, {\n    method: &quot;POST&quot;,\n    headers: { Authorization: `Bot ${process.env.DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}` },\n    body: form,\n  });\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>File Size Limits</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Server Boost Level</th>\n<th>Max Upload</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>None</td>\n<td>25 MB</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Level 2</td>\n<td>50 MB</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Level 3</td>\n<td>100 MB</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Large Files &amp; Enterprise Best Practice</h2>\n<p>For enterprise use or files exceeding Discord's upload limit, the recommended pattern is:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Upload to external storage</strong> — Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Google Drive, etc. using your own credentials.</li>\n<li><strong>Generate a temporary link</strong> — e.g. an <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ShareObjectPresignedURL.html\">S3 presigned URL</a> with a short TTL.</li>\n<li><strong>Send the link back to Discord</strong> — post the URL as a regular message in the thread.</li>\n</ol>\n<blockquote>\n<p>See the <a href=\"#enterprise--large-files-presigned-url\">Enterprise / Large Files diagram</a> above for the full flow.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>Why this is better for enterprise</h4>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>No file size limit</strong> — S3/R2 handles files of any size.</li>\n<li><strong>Files stay off Discord</strong> — you control where data lives, important for compliance and data governance.</li>\n<li><strong>You control the TTL</strong> — the link expires on your terms; no permanent file sitting in a Discord CDN.</li>\n</ul>\n<h4>S3 presigned URL example (Python)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import boto3\n\ns3 = boto3.client(&quot;s3&quot;)\n\n# Upload\ns3.upload_file(&quot;/path/to/report.pdf&quot;, &quot;my-bucket&quot;, &quot;reports/report.pdf&quot;)\n\n# Generate presigned URL (expires in 1 hour)\nurl = s3.generate_presigned_url(\n    &quot;get_object&quot;,\n    Params={&quot;Bucket&quot;: &quot;my-bucket&quot;, &quot;Key&quot;: &quot;reports/report.pdf&quot;},\n    ExpiresIn=3600,\n)\n\n# Then send `url` as a Discord message via the API\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Common File Types</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Use Case</th>\n<th>Typical Format</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Code patches</td>\n<td><code>.diff</code>, <code>.patch</code></td>\n<td>Attach as file to avoid Discord's 2000-char limit</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Logs</td>\n<td><code>.log</code>, <code>.txt</code></td>\n<td>Truncate or compress large logs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Reports</td>\n<td><code>.pdf</code>, <code>.csv</code>, <code>.html</code></td>\n<td>PDF renders a preview in Discord</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Archives</td>\n<td><code>.zip</code>, <code>.tar.gz</code></td>\n<td>Bundle multiple files</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Security Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Never hardcode the bot token.</strong> Read from <code>$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code> or a mounted secret.</li>\n<li><strong>Validate file paths.</strong> Sanitize any dynamically constructed paths to prevent path traversal.</li>\n<li><strong>Check file size</strong> before uploading to avoid silent failures.</li>\n<li><strong>Sensitive content.</strong> Do not send files containing secrets, credentials, or PII unless the user explicitly requests it.</li>\n<li><strong>Rate limits.</strong> Discord enforces per-channel rate limits. Space uploads when sending multiple files.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Bot Permission Checklist</h2>\n<p>Ensure your bot has these permissions in the <a href=\"https://discord.com/developers/applications\">Discord Developer Portal</a>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><input checked=\"\" disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <code>Send Messages</code></li>\n<li><input checked=\"\" disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <code>Send Messages in Threads</code></li>\n<li><input checked=\"\" disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <code>Attach Files</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h2>FAQ</h2>\n<p><strong>Q: Can OpenAB relay files natively?</strong>\nA: Not currently. OpenAB streams text via ACP JSON-RPC. File sending is done out-of-band by the agent.</p>\n<p><strong>Q: What if the file is too large?</strong>\nA: Use the <a href=\"#large-files--enterprise-best-practice\">Large Files &amp; Enterprise Best Practice</a> pattern — upload to S3/R2/Google Drive, generate a temporary link, and send the URL in the message.</p>\n<p><strong>Q: Does this work with Slack / Telegram / LINE?</strong>\nA: Same concept — call the platform's file upload API using the channel ID from <code>sender_context</code>. API details differ per platform. For Slack, use <a href=\"https://api.slack.com/methods/files.upload\"><code>files.upload</code></a>. For Telegram, use <a href=\"https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#senddocument\"><code>sendDocument</code></a>.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Send files"
      }
    },

      "slug": "sendimages",
      "html": "<h1>Sending Images Back to Discord</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>This doc is designed for your coding agent.</strong> Share it with your agent so it learns how to send images back to Discord.</p>\n<p>Example prompt:</p>\n<pre><code>Read docs/sendimages.md from OpenAB GitHub and send the image back to my Discord thread.\n</code></pre>\n<p>💡 <strong>Tip:</strong> If it works the first time, ask your agent to save this as a <strong>SKILL</strong> so it remembers how to do it next time without re-reading the doc.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<p>OpenAB does <strong>not</strong> relay images from the agent to Discord — it only streams text.\nTo send an image back to the user, the agent must call the Discord API directly.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>For sending non-image files (PDF, CSV, logs, etc.), see <a href=\"/openab/sendfiles\">sendfiles.md</a>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<pre><code>┌──────────┐  text only   ┌──────────┐  ACP stdio   ┌──────────────┐\n│  Discord  │◄────────────│  OpenAB   │◄────────────│  Agent (CLI)  │\n│  Thread   │             └──────────┘              └──────┬───────┘\n│           │                                              │\n│           │         Discord REST API                     │\n│           │◄─────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n│           │  POST /channels/{thread_id}/messages\n│           │  + multipart file attachment\n└──────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>OpenAB only streams text via ACP. To send an image, the agent calls the\nDiscord API directly using the <code>thread_id</code> from <code>sender_context</code>.</p>\n<h2>Step-by-Step</h2>\n<h3>1. Get the Target Channel from <code>sender_context</code></h3>\n<p>Every message from OpenAB includes a <code>&lt;sender_context&gt;</code> JSON block:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;schema&quot;: &quot;openab.sender.v1&quot;,\n  &quot;sender_id&quot;: &quot;845835116920307722&quot;,\n  &quot;sender_name&quot;: &quot;pahud.hsieh&quot;,\n  &quot;display_name&quot;: &quot;pahud.hsieh&quot;,\n  &quot;channel&quot;: &quot;discord&quot;,\n  &quot;channel_id&quot;: &quot;1490282656913559673&quot;,\n  &quot;thread_id&quot;: &quot;1499442140172910654&quot;,\n  &quot;is_bot&quot;: false\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Use <strong><code>thread_id</code></strong> as the target channel. If <code>thread_id</code> is absent, fall back to <code>channel_id</code>.</p>\n<h3>2. Get the Bot Token</h3>\n<p>The agent needs a Discord Bot Token to call the API. Pass it via <code>[agent] env</code> in <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN = &quot;${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>⚠️ The token in <code>[discord] bot_token</code> is consumed by OpenAB itself and is <strong>not</strong> automatically forwarded to the agent subprocess. You must explicitly pass it via <code>[agent] env</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>Security: dedicated bot recommended</h4>\n<p>For production, consider creating a <strong>dedicated &quot;File Deliverer&quot; bot</strong> with minimal permissions instead of sharing the main OAB bot token:</p>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ Discord Server                                                  │\n│                                                                 │\n│  ┌─────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  OAB Bot         │         │  File Deliverer Bot          │   │\n│  │  (main bot)      │         │  (dedicated, minimal perms)  │   │\n│  │                  │         │                              │   │\n│  │  ✅ Read Messages │         │  ✅ Send Messages             │   │\n│  │  ✅ Manage Threads│         │  ✅ Send Messages in Threads  │   │\n│  │  ✅ Add Reactions │         │  ✅ Attach Files              │   │\n│  │  ✅ Send Messages │         │  ❌ Read Messages             │   │\n│  │  ✅ Attach Files  │         │  ❌ Manage Threads            │   │\n│  └────────┬────────┘         └──────────────┬───────────────┘   │\n│           │                                  │                   │\n│           │  ACP stdio                       │  REST API         │\n│           ▼                                  ▼                   │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  Agent (kiro-cli / claude / codex)                        │   │\n│  │                                                           │   │\n│  │  DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN ──► POST /channels/{id}/messages  │   │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>What users see in the thread:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>超渡法師:        好的，我幫你生成報告...\nFile Deliverer:  📎 report.pdf\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th></th>\n<th>Same token (simple)</th>\n<th>Dedicated bot (recommended)</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Setup</td>\n<td>One bot, one token</td>\n<td>Create a second bot in Discord Developer Portal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Agent permissions</td>\n<td>Everything the OAB bot can do</td>\n<td>Only <code>Send Messages</code> + <code>Attach Files</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Token leak impact</td>\n<td>Full bot access exposed</td>\n<td>Limited to file uploads</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Audit trail</td>\n<td>Cannot distinguish OAB vs agent messages</td>\n<td>Separate bot identity in logs</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\"># Production: dedicated file-upload bot (e.g. &quot;File Deliverer&quot;)\n[agent]\nenv = { DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN = &quot;${DISCORD_FILE_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p>For personal use or small teams, sharing the same token is fine — you already trust your agent.</p>\n<h3>3. Upload the Image</h3>\n<p>Use the Discord <a href=\"https://discord.com/developers/docs/resources/message#create-message\">Create Message</a> endpoint with a <code>multipart/form-data</code> body:</p>\n<pre><code>POST https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/{thread_id}/messages\nAuthorization: Bot {DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}\nContent-Type: multipart/form-data\n</code></pre>\n<h4>curl example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST &quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/${THREAD_ID}/messages&quot; \\\n  -H &quot;Authorization: Bot ${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;content=Here is the generated image&quot; \\\n  -F &quot;files[0]=@/path/to/image.png&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Python example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import os, requests\n\ndef send_image(thread_id: str, image_path: str, message: str = &quot;&quot;):\n    url = f&quot;https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/{thread_id}/messages&quot;\n    headers = {&quot;Authorization&quot;: f&quot;Bot {os.environ['DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN']}&quot;}\n    with open(image_path, &quot;rb&quot;) as f:\n        requests.post(url, headers=headers,\n                      data={&quot;content&quot;: message},\n                      files={&quot;files[0]&quot;: (os.path.basename(image_path), f)})\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Node.js example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const fs = require(&quot;fs&quot;);\nconst FormData = require(&quot;form-data&quot;);\n\nasync function sendImage(threadId, imagePath, message = &quot;&quot;) {\n  const form = new FormData();\n  form.append(&quot;content&quot;, message);\n  form.append(&quot;files[0]&quot;, fs.createReadStream(imagePath));\n\n  await fetch(`https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/${threadId}/messages`, {\n    method: &quot;POST&quot;,\n    headers: { Authorization: `Bot ${process.env.DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}` },\n    body: form,\n  });\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Automated Sidecar Pattern</h2>\n<p>If your agent generates images to a known directory (e.g. Codex writes to\n<code>~/.codex/generated_images/</code>), you can run a <strong>file-watcher sidecar</strong> that\nautomatically uploads new images:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Watch the output directory for new files.</li>\n<li>Read the session metadata to find the originating <code>thread_id</code>.</li>\n<li>Upload via the Discord API.</li>\n<li>Track uploaded files in a state file to avoid duplicates.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>This is the pattern used by the community <code>discord-image-uploader</code> sidecar.</p>\n<h2>Security Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Never hardcode the bot token.</strong> Read it from <code>$DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN</code> or a mounted secret.</li>\n<li><strong>Scope permissions.</strong> The bot only needs <code>Send Messages</code> and <code>Attach Files</code> in the target channels.</li>\n<li><strong>Validate file paths.</strong> If the agent constructs paths dynamically, sanitize them to prevent path traversal.</li>\n<li><strong>Rate limits.</strong> Discord enforces rate limits on message creation. Space uploads if sending multiple images.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Bot Permission Checklist</h2>\n<p>In the <a href=\"https://discord.com/developers/applications\">Discord Developer Portal</a>, ensure your bot has:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><input checked=\"\" disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <code>Send Messages</code></li>\n<li><input checked=\"\" disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <code>Send Messages in Threads</code></li>\n<li><input checked=\"\" disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <code>Attach Files</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p>These are typically already granted if your bot works with OpenAB.</p>\n<h2>FAQ</h2>\n<p><strong>Q: Can OpenAB relay images natively?</strong>\nA: Not currently. OpenAB streams text via ACP JSON-RPC. Image/file sending is done out-of-band by the agent.</p>\n<p><strong>Q: Does this work with Slack / Telegram / LINE?</strong>\nA: The same concept applies — call the platform's file upload API using the channel ID from <code>sender_context</code>. The API details differ per platform.</p>\n<p><strong>Q: What image formats are supported?</strong>\nA: Discord supports PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP. Max file size is 25 MB (or higher with Nitro boost).</p>\n",

        "title": "Send images"
      }

      "slug": "sidecar",
      "html": "<h1>Extending OpenAB with Sidecars and Init Containers</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This is an <strong>advanced</strong> pattern. For most tool installations, start with <a href=\"/openab/agent-installable-tools\">agent-installable tools</a> — one prompt, zero YAML.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Overview</h2>\n<p>OpenAB's Helm chart supports <strong>init containers</strong> and <strong>sidecar containers</strong> for cases where the agent-installable tools pattern isn't sufficient — when you need a long-running process, a deterministic pre-installed toolset, or a service running alongside the agent.</p>\n<pre><code>  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n  │  Pod                                                    │\n  │                                                         │\n  │  ┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────────────┐│\n  │  │  Init Container  │───►│  Main Container (openab)    ││\n  │  │                  │    │                              ││\n  │  │  Runs BEFORE the │    │  Agent runtime + tools from ││\n  │  │  main container. │    │  ~/bin/ (PVC)               ││\n  │  │  Pre-install     │    │                              ││\n  │  │  tools, seed     │    └─────────────────────────────┘│\n  │  │  configs, etc.   │                                   │\n  │  └─────────────────┘    ┌─────────────────────────────┐│\n  │                          │  Sidecar Container          ││\n  │                          │                              ││\n  │                          │  Runs ALONGSIDE the main    ││\n  │                          │  container. Proxies, tunnels,││\n  │                          │  log shippers, daemons, etc. ││\n  │                          └─────────────────────────────┘│\n  │                                                         │\n  │  Shared: volumes, network (localhost), PVC              │\n  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Common Scenarios</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>#</th>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Why a sidecar / init container?</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>1</td>\n<td><a href=\"#1-cloudflare-tunnel\">Expose agent via Cloudflare Tunnel</a></td>\n<td>Sidecar</td>\n<td>Long-running tunnel process that must stay alive alongside the agent</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2</td>\n<td><a href=\"#2-ngrok--tailscale\">Expose agent via ngrok / Tailscale</a></td>\n<td>Sidecar</td>\n<td>Same as above — persistent network tunnel</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>3</td>\n<td><a href=\"#3-pre-install-a-standard-toolset\">Pre-install a standard toolset</a></td>\n<td>Init</td>\n<td>Deterministic setup — tools are guaranteed before the agent starts</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>4</td>\n<td><a href=\"#4-local-database-or-cache\">Local database or cache</a></td>\n<td>Sidecar</td>\n<td>Agent needs a data store accessible via localhost</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>5</td>\n<td><a href=\"#5-log-shipping-and-observability\">Log shipping and observability</a></td>\n<td>Sidecar</td>\n<td>Continuous log/metric forwarding independent of the agent</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>6</td>\n<td><a href=\"#6-gpu--ml-model-serving\">GPU / ML model serving</a></td>\n<td>Sidecar</td>\n<td>Serve a model via HTTP on localhost; agent calls it as needed</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>1. Cloudflare Tunnel</h2>\n<p><strong>Problem:</strong> You want to expose your agent's webhook or API to the internet without a public IP or LoadBalancer.</p>\n<p><strong>Solution:</strong> Run <code>cloudflared</code> as a sidecar. It creates an outbound tunnel to Cloudflare's edge, making your agent reachable via a Cloudflare domain.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    extraContainers:\n      - name: cloudflared\n        image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest\n        args:\n          - tunnel\n          - --no-autoupdate\n          - run\n        env:\n          - name: TUNNEL_TOKEN\n            valueFrom:\n              secretKeyRef:\n                name: cloudflare-secret\n                key: tunnel-token\n        resources:\n          requests:\n            cpu: 50m\n            memory: 64Mi\n          limits:\n            memory: 128Mi\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>How it works:</strong> The tunnel connects outbound to Cloudflare. Incoming requests are routed to <code>localhost:&lt;port&gt;</code> inside the pod, where the agent (or gateway) is listening. No ingress, no LoadBalancer, no firewall rules needed.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2. ngrok / Tailscale</h2>\n<p><strong>Problem:</strong> Same as Cloudflare Tunnel, but you prefer ngrok or Tailscale for your network layer.</p>\n<h3>ngrok</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    extraContainers:\n      - name: ngrok\n        image: ngrok/ngrok:latest\n        args:\n          - http\n          - --authtoken=$(NGROK_AUTHTOKEN)\n          - &quot;8080&quot;\n        env:\n          - name: NGROK_AUTHTOKEN\n            valueFrom:\n              secretKeyRef:\n                name: ngrok-secret\n                key: authtoken\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Tailscale</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    extraContainers:\n      - name: tailscale\n        image: tailscale/tailscale:latest\n        env:\n          - name: TS_AUTHKEY\n            valueFrom:\n              secretKeyRef:\n                name: tailscale-secret\n                key: authkey\n          - name: TS_USERSPACE\n            value: &quot;true&quot;\n        securityContext:\n          runAsUser: 1000\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>When to choose which:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Cloudflare Tunnel</strong> — free, production-grade, custom domains, access policies</li>\n<li><strong>ngrok</strong> — quick dev/testing, instant public URL, built-in inspection UI</li>\n<li><strong>Tailscale</strong> — private mesh network, no public exposure, zero-config VPN between your devices and the agent</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3. Pre-install a Standard Toolset</h2>\n<p><strong>Problem:</strong> You want every agent pod to start with a specific set of tools already installed, without relying on the agent to install them at runtime.</p>\n<p><strong>Solution:</strong> Use an init container that writes to the agent's PVC before the main container starts.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    extraInitContainers:\n      - name: install-tools\n        image: curlimages/curl:latest\n        command:\n          - sh\n          - -c\n          - |\n            set -e\n            mkdir -p /home/agent/bin\n\n            # Skip if tools already exist (PVC is persistent)\n            if [ -f /home/agent/bin/.tools-installed ]; then\n              echo &quot;Tools already installed, skipping&quot;\n              exit 0\n            fi\n\n            ARCH=$(uname -m)\n            if [ &quot;$ARCH&quot; = &quot;aarch64&quot; ]; then ARCH=&quot;arm64&quot;; elif [ &quot;$ARCH&quot; = &quot;x86_64&quot; ]; then ARCH=&quot;amd64&quot;; fi\n\n            # Install kubectl\n            KUBECTL_VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)\n            curl -fsSL -o /home/agent/bin/kubectl \\\n              &quot;https://dl.k8s.io/release/${KUBECTL_VERSION}/bin/linux/${ARCH}/kubectl&quot;\n            chmod +x /home/agent/bin/kubectl\n\n            # Add more tools here...\n\n            touch /home/agent/bin/.tools-installed\n        volumeMounts:\n          - name: agent-home\n            mountPath: /home/agent\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Key detail:</strong> The init container checks for a marker file (<code>.tools-installed</code>) so it doesn't re-download on every pod restart — the PVC already has the tools.</p>\n<p><strong>When to use this over agent-installable tools:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Team standardization</strong> — every pod gets the same toolset, no variance</li>\n<li><strong>Offline / air-gapped</strong> — pre-bake tools from a private registry</li>\n<li><strong>Large tools</strong> — avoid the agent spending time downloading hundreds of MB on first run</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>4. Local Database or Cache</h2>\n<p><strong>Problem:</strong> Your agent needs a database or cache (Redis, SQLite server, DuckDB, etc.) accessible via localhost.</p>\n<p><strong>Solution:</strong> Run it as a sidecar. The agent connects to <code>localhost:&lt;port&gt;</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    extraContainers:\n      - name: redis\n        image: redis:7-alpine\n        ports:\n          - containerPort: 6379\n        resources:\n          requests:\n            cpu: 50m\n            memory: 64Mi\n          limits:\n            memory: 256Mi\n</code></pre>\n<p>The agent can then use <code>redis-cli -h localhost</code> or connect programmatically to <code>localhost:6379</code>.</p>\n<p><strong>Use cases:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Caching API responses or embeddings</li>\n<li>Session storage for multi-turn workflows</li>\n<li>Temporary data processing (agent writes data, queries it)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>5. Log Shipping and Observability</h2>\n<p><strong>Problem:</strong> You want to ship agent logs, metrics, or traces to an external system (Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch, etc.) without modifying the agent itself.</p>\n<p><strong>Solution:</strong> Run a log shipper as a sidecar that reads from shared volumes or stdout.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    extraContainers:\n      - name: fluent-bit\n        image: fluent/fluent-bit:latest\n        volumeMounts:\n          - name: agent-home\n            mountPath: /home/agent\n            readOnly: true\n        env:\n          - name: OUTPUT_HOST\n            value: &quot;your-log-endpoint.example.com&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Alternatives:</strong> Fluent Bit, Vector, OpenTelemetry Collector, Datadog Agent.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6. GPU / ML Model Serving</h2>\n<p><strong>Problem:</strong> Your agent needs access to a local ML model (e.g., for embeddings, classification, or code analysis) without calling an external API.</p>\n<p><strong>Solution:</strong> Run a model server as a sidecar. The agent calls it via <code>localhost</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    extraContainers:\n      - name: embedding-server\n        image: your-registry/embedding-server:latest\n        ports:\n          - containerPort: 8000\n        resources:\n          limits:\n            nvidia.com/gpu: 1\n</code></pre>\n<p>The agent calls <code>curl localhost:8000/embed -d '{&quot;text&quot;: &quot;...&quot;}'</code> to get embeddings locally.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Requires GPU-enabled nodes and the NVIDIA device plugin. This is a niche use case.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>Helm Values Reference</h2>\n<p>All fields are under <code>agents.&lt;name&gt;</code>:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>extraInitContainers</code></td>\n<td>list</td>\n<td>Init containers — run before the main container</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>extraContainers</code></td>\n<td>list</td>\n<td>Sidecar containers — run alongside the main container</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>extraVolumes</code></td>\n<td>list</td>\n<td>Additional volumes for the pod</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>extraVolumeMounts</code></td>\n<td>list</td>\n<td>Additional volume mounts for the main container</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>These accept standard Kubernetes container and volume specs. See the <a href=\"https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/init-containers/\">Kubernetes docs</a> for the full spec.</p>\n<h2>When to Use What</h2>\n<pre><code>  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n  │                                                              │\n  │  Agent-Installable Tools          Sidecars / Init Containers │\n  │  ─────────────────────            ──────────────────────────│\n  │  • CLI tools (aws, glab, ssh)     • Long-running daemons    │\n  │  • One prompt to install          • Network tunnels/proxies │\n  │  • Agent-driven, on-demand        • Pre-installed toolsets  │\n  │  • No Helm/YAML changes           • Requires values.yaml   │\n  │  • Persists on PVC                • Recreated each pod start│\n  │                                                              │\n  │  Start here ──────────────────►  Use when needed            │\n  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n</code></pre>\n<p>Most users will never need sidecars. Start with the <a href=\"/openab/agent-installable-tools\">agent-installable tools</a> pattern — it covers the vast majority of use cases with zero YAML.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Sidecars"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "slack",
      "html": "<h1>Slack Bot Setup Guide</h1>\n<p>Step-by-step guide to create and configure a Slack bot for openab.</p>\n<h2>1. Create a Slack App</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Go to <a href=\"https://api.slack.com/apps\">https://api.slack.com/apps</a></li>\n<li>Click <strong>Create New App</strong> → <strong>From scratch</strong></li>\n<li>Enter an app name (e.g. &quot;OpenAB&quot;) and select your workspace</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Create App</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<h2>2. Enable Socket Mode</h2>\n<p>Socket Mode uses a persistent WebSocket connection — no public URL or ingress needed.</p>\n<ol>\n<li>In the left sidebar, click <strong>Socket Mode</strong></li>\n<li>Toggle <strong>Enable Socket Mode</strong> to ON</li>\n<li>You'll be prompted to generate an <strong>App-Level Token</strong>:\n<ul>\n<li>Token name: <code>openab-socket</code> (or any name)</li>\n<li>Scope: <code>connections:write</code></li>\n<li>Click <strong>Generate</strong></li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Copy the token (<code>xapp-...</code>) — this is your <code>SLACK_APP_TOKEN</code></li>\n</ol>\n<h2>3. Subscribe to Events</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>In the left sidebar, click <strong>Event Subscriptions</strong></li>\n<li>Toggle <strong>Enable Events</strong> to ON</li>\n<li>Under <strong>Subscribe to bot events</strong>, add:\n<ul>\n<li><code>app_mention</code> — triggers when someone @mentions the bot</li>\n<li><code>message.channels</code> — receives messages in public channels (for thread follow-ups)</li>\n<li><code>message.groups</code> — receives messages in private channels (for thread follow-ups)</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Click <strong>Save Changes</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<h2>4. Add Bot Token Scopes</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>In the left sidebar, click <strong>OAuth &amp; Permissions</strong></li>\n<li>Under <strong>Bot Token Scopes</strong>, add:</li>\n</ol>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scope</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>app_mentions:read</code></td>\n<td>Receive @mention events</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>chat:write</code></td>\n<td>Send and edit messages</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>channels:history</code></td>\n<td>Read public channel messages (for thread context)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>groups:history</code></td>\n<td>Read private channel messages (for thread context)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>channels:read</code></td>\n<td>List public channels</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>groups:read</code></td>\n<td>List private channels</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>reactions:write</code></td>\n<td>Add/remove emoji reactions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>files:read</code></td>\n<td>Download file attachments (images, audio)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>users:read</code></td>\n<td>Resolve user display names</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>assistant:write</code></td>\n<td>Native streaming + assistant status line (required when <code>assistant_mode = true</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>5. Install to Workspace</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>In the left sidebar, click <strong>Install App</strong></li>\n<li>Click <strong>Install to Workspace</strong> (or <strong>Reinstall</strong> if you've changed scopes)</li>\n<li>Authorize the requested permissions</li>\n<li>Copy the <strong>Bot User OAuth Token</strong> (<code>xoxb-...</code>) — this is your <code>SLACK_BOT_TOKEN</code></li>\n</ol>\n<h2>6. Configure openab</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p>📖 Full config options with defaults: <a href=\"/openab/config-reference#slack\">docs/config-reference.md</a></p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Add the <code>[slack]</code> section to your <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[slack]\nbot_token = &quot;${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;\napp_token = &quot;${SLACK_APP_TOKEN}&quot;\nallowed_channels = []                # empty = allow all channels\n# allowed_users = [&quot;U0123456789&quot;]    # empty = allow all users\n</code></pre>\n<p>Set the environment variables:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=&quot;xoxb-...&quot;\nexport SLACK_APP_TOKEN=&quot;xapp-...&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Assistant Mode (default: enabled)</h3>\n<p><code>assistant_mode</code> is <strong>enabled by default</strong>. This uses Slack's native AI-app APIs for streaming (<code>chat.startStream</code>/<code>appendStream</code>/<code>stopStream</code>) and status indicators (<code>assistant.threads.setStatus</code>) instead of the legacy post+edit loop and emoji reactions.</p>\n<p><strong>Requirements:</strong> Your Slack app must be an <a href=\"https://api.slack.com/docs/apps/ai\">AI app</a> with the <code>assistant:write</code> scope. If your app already has <code>chat:write</code>, you only need to add <code>assistant:write</code> and reinstall.</p>\n<p><strong>Non-AI app compatibility:</strong> If your Slack app is <strong>not</strong> an AI app (or lacks <code>assistant:write</code>), set:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[slack]\nassistant_mode = false\n</code></pre>\n<p>This keeps the previous behavior: post+edit streaming with emoji reactions (👀 / ✅ / ❌) for status indicators. Without this opt-out, message delivery still works (native streaming degrades to post+edit automatically), but thinking/tool-use indicators will not be visible.</p>\n<h2>7. Invite the Bot</h2>\n<p>In each Slack channel where you want to use the bot:</p>\n<pre><code>/invite @OpenAB\n</code></pre>\n<h2>8. Test</h2>\n<p>In a channel where the bot is invited:</p>\n<pre><code>@OpenAB explain this code\n</code></pre>\n<p>The bot will reply in a thread. After that, just type in the thread — no @mention needed for follow-ups.</p>\n<h2>Slash commands are not supported on Slack</h2>\n<p>openab supports <code>/models</code>, <code>/agents</code>, and <code>/cancel</code> on <strong>Discord</strong>, but <strong>not on Slack</strong>. If you previously configured these commands in your Slack app's <strong>Slash Commands</strong> page, you can safely delete them — the Slack adapter ignores both <code>slash_commands</code> and <code>interactive</code> envelope types.</p>\n<p>The root cause is a combination of three Slack-specific platform constraints, none of which is fixable from openab's side:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Slack blocks third-party slash commands inside threads.</strong> Invoking <code>/models</code> from a thread's reply composer returns the Slack error <code>&quot;/models is not supported in threads. Sorry!&quot;</code>. This is enforced by the Slack client itself, not by any app setting — enabling Interactivity, Socket Mode, or reinstalling the app does not bypass it. Slack's built-in commands (<code>/remind</code>, <code>/shrug</code>, etc.) get special treatment that custom apps cannot.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Channel-level slash command payloads have no thread context.</strong> If the user types <code>/models</code> in the channel's main composer instead of a thread, Slack delivers the command but the payload carries no <code>thread_ts</code>. Since openab keys each ACP session by thread (<code>slack:&lt;thread_ts&gt;</code> or <code>slack:&lt;trigger_ts&gt;</code>), the command cannot be routed to the right session. Sessions are never keyed by <code>channel_id</code> alone, so there's no workaround on the adapter side.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Most ACP agents don't expose a model-switch surface.</strong> Even when routing succeeded, <code>/models</code> reads the session's <code>configOptions</code> from the ACP <code>initialize</code> response. Only <code>kiro-cli</code> emits these in the expected format (via its <code>models</code>/<code>modes</code> fallback). <code>claude-code</code>, <code>codex</code>, <code>gemini</code>, <code>cursor-agent</code>, and <code>opencode</code> do not, so the menu would be empty for those backends — the user would see <code>&quot;⚠️ No model options available&quot;</code> with no recourse.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<p>On Discord, none of these apply: slash commands work in thread-channels, the channel ID <em>is</em> the thread key, and users typically stay within a single agent per deployment anyway.</p>\n<h3>If you need to switch models or agents with a Slack deployment</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Change the agent</strong>: edit <code>[agent]</code> in <code>config.toml</code> (or the Helm chart values) and restart the pod / process</li>\n<li><strong>Change the Claude model</strong> (for <code>claude-code</code>): set <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL</code> (or equivalent env var depending on your claude-code-acp version) and restart — model selection happens at process start, not at runtime</li>\n<li><strong>Cancel an in-flight turn</strong>: there is no built-in way on Slack currently.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Finding Channel and User IDs</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Channel ID</strong>: Right-click the channel name → <strong>View channel details</strong> → ID at the bottom (starts with <code>C</code> for public, <code>G</code> for private)</li>\n<li><strong>User ID</strong>: Click a user's profile → <strong>...</strong> menu → <strong>Copy member ID</strong> (starts with <code>U</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3>Bot doesn't respond to @mentions</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Verify Socket Mode is enabled in your app settings</li>\n<li>Check that <code>app_mention</code> is subscribed under <strong>bot events</strong> (not user events)</li>\n<li>Ensure the app is reinstalled after adding new event subscriptions</li>\n<li>Check the bot is invited to the channel (<code>/invite @YourSlackAppName</code>)</li>\n<li>Run with <code>RUST_LOG=openab=debug cargo run</code> to see incoming events</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Bot doesn't respond to thread follow-ups</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Verify <code>message.channels</code> (and <code>message.groups</code> for private channels) are subscribed under <strong>bot events</strong></li>\n<li>Reinstall the app after adding these events</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>&quot;not_authed&quot; or &quot;invalid_auth&quot; errors</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Verify your <code>SLACK_BOT_TOKEN</code> starts with <code>xoxb-</code></li>\n<li>Verify your <code>SLACK_APP_TOKEN</code> starts with <code>xapp-</code></li>\n<li>Check the tokens haven't been revoked in your app settings</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Reactions not showing</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Verify <code>reactions:write</code> scope is added</li>\n<li>Reinstall the app after adding the scope</li>\n<li>If <code>assistant_mode = true</code> (the default), emoji reactions are intentionally suppressed — status is shown via the assistant status line instead. Set <code>assistant_mode = false</code> if you want emoji reactions back.</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Assistant status line not showing (&quot;Thinking…&quot; / &quot;Using tool…&quot;)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Verify your Slack app is configured as an <a href=\"https://api.slack.com/docs/apps/ai\">AI app</a></li>\n<li>Verify <code>assistant:write</code> scope is added under <strong>Bot Token Scopes</strong></li>\n<li>Reinstall the app after adding the scope</li>\n<li>If your app cannot be an AI app, set <code>assistant_mode = false</code> to use emoji reactions instead</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Native streaming not working (replies appear all at once)</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><code>chat.startStream</code> requires the <code>assistant:write</code> scope — the adapter automatically degrades to post+edit if the API call fails</li>\n<li>Native streaming is also suppressed when another bot is present in the thread (to avoid edit interference)</li>\n<li>Check logs for <code>warn</code> messages about <code>stream_begin</code> failures</li>\n</ol>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Slack"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "slash-commands",
      "html": "<h1>Slash Commands</h1>\n<p>OpenAB registers Discord slash commands for session control and agent management. Most work in both guild threads and DMs — the exception is <code>/auth</code>, which is <strong>DM-only</strong> for security (see <a href=\"#auth\"><code>/auth</code></a> below).</p>\n<h2>Commands</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Command</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Requires active session?</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/models</code></td>\n<td>Select the AI model via dropdown menu</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/agents</code></td>\n<td>Select the agent mode via dropdown menu</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/cancel</code></td>\n<td>Cancel the current in-flight operation</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/reset</code></td>\n<td>Reset the conversation session (clear history, start fresh)</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/auth</code></td>\n<td>Authenticate the backend agent via device flow (<strong>DM-only</strong>)</td>\n<td>No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/remind</code></td>\n<td>Set a one-shot delayed reminder to mention users/roles</td>\n<td>No</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>/export-thread</code></td>\n<td>Export thread/DM as <code>.txt</code> (default: last 100 messages)</td>\n<td>No</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>All responses are <strong>ephemeral</strong> — only the user who invoked the command sees the reply.</p>\n<h2>Platform Support</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Platform</th>\n<th>Supported</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Discord (guild threads)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Commands registered per-guild for instant availability</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Discord (DMs)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Commands registered globally; may take up to 1 hour to appear after first deploy</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Slack</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>Slack blocks third-party slash commands in threads; see <a href=\"/openab/slack#slash-commands-are-not-supported-on-slack\">slack.md</a></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>How They Work</h2>\n<h3><code>/models</code> and <code>/agents</code></h3>\n<p>These read <code>configOptions</code> from the ACP <code>initialize</code> / <code>session/new</code> response and present them as a Discord Select Menu.</p>\n<p>When the user picks an option, OpenAB sends <code>session/set_config_option</code> to the ACP backend.</p>\n<p><strong>Agent support varies:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Agent</th>\n<th><code>/models</code></th>\n<th><code>/agents</code></th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>openab-agent</td>\n<td>✅ Returns available models via <code>configOptions</code> in <code>session/new</code> response</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>kiro-cli</td>\n<td>✅ Returns available models via <code>models</code> fallback</td>\n<td>✅ Returns modes (<code>kiro_default</code>, <code>kiro_planner</code>) via <code>modes</code> fallback</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>claude-code</td>\n<td>❌ No <code>configOptions</code> emitted</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>codex</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>gemini</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>cursor-agent</td>\n<td>❌ (tracking: #493)</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>copilot</td>\n<td>❌ (tracking: #496)</td>\n<td>❌</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>If the agent doesn't expose options, the user sees: <code>⚠️ No model options available. Start a conversation first by @mentioning the bot.</code></p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Backward compatibility:</strong> <code>openab-agent</code> returns <code>configOptions</code> in the <code>session/new</code> response (alongside <code>sessionId</code>). ACP clients that only read <code>sessionId</code> will continue to work — <code>configOptions</code> is additive. Clients that support <code>/models</code> should read <code>configOptions[].options</code> to populate the model picker. Each model option includes a <code>provider</code> field (<code>&quot;anthropic&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;openai&quot;</code>) for routing.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Discord Select Menus are limited to 25 items. If the agent returns more, only the first 25 are shown with a count of how many were truncated.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3><code>/cancel</code></h3>\n<p>Sends a <code>session/cancel</code> JSON-RPC notification to the ACP backend. This aborts in-flight LLM requests and tool calls immediately — no need to wait for the current response to finish.</p>\n<h3><code>/reset</code></h3>\n<p>Cancels any in-flight operation, then removes the session from the pool. The ACP process terminates once the last reference is released. The next message in the thread or DM will automatically create a fresh session.</p>\n<p>This is equivalent to the <code>sessions close</code> + <code>sessions new</code> pattern used by <a href=\"https://github.com/openclaw/acpx\">OpenClaw ACPX</a>.</p>\n<p><strong>What gets cleared:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Conversation history</li>\n<li>ACP process and connection</li>\n<li>Suspended session state (no resume after reset)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>What is preserved:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Bot identity and system prompt (re-applied on next session creation)</li>\n<li>Config settings in <code>config.toml</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>/export-thread</code></h3>\n<p>Fetches the current Discord thread or DM history and returns a <code>.txt</code> file as an ephemeral follow-up. The transcript includes message timestamps, author names and IDs, message text, and attachment URLs.</p>\n<p><strong>Optional parameters</strong> (mutually exclusive — use at most one):</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Parameter</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>limit</code></td>\n<td>Integer</td>\n<td>Export only the most recent N messages (1–5000)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>since</code></td>\n<td>String</td>\n<td>Export messages after this message ID (right-click → Copy Message ID)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>days</code></td>\n<td>Integer</td>\n<td>Export messages from the last N days (1–365). Rolling N×24h window from now.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>all</code></td>\n<td>Boolean</td>\n<td>Export all messages (up to 5000)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>If no parameter is provided, the <strong>last 100 messages</strong> are exported.</p>\n<p><strong>Examples:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>/export-thread                              → last 100 messages (default)\n/export-thread limit:500                    → most recent 500 messages\n/export-thread since:1503744866100842698    → messages after this specific message\n/export-thread days:3                       → messages from the last 3 days (rolling 72h)\n/export-thread all:true                     → export all (cap 5000)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Constraints:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Only works in allowed Discord threads or enabled DMs.</li>\n<li>Specifying more than one filter returns an error.</li>\n<li>Very large exports may be truncated to fit Discord's attachment size limit.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Passing CLI Commands via @mention</h2>\n<p>In addition to slash commands, you can pass built-in CLI commands directly after an @mention:</p>\n<pre><code>@MyBot /compact\n@MyBot /clear\n@MyBot /model claude-sonnet-4\n</code></pre>\n<p>These are forwarded as-is to the ACP session as a prompt. Any command the underlying CLI supports in its interactive mode works here. This is the recommended workaround for agents that don't expose <code>configOptions</code>.</p>\n<h2><code>/remind</code></h2>\n<p>Set a one-shot delayed reminder that mentions users or roles in the channel after a specified delay.</p>\n<p><strong>Syntax:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>/remind targets:&lt;@user @role ...&gt; message:&lt;text&gt; delay:&lt;duration&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Parameters:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Parameter</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>targets</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Space-separated @mentions (users and/or roles)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>message</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Reminder text</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>delay</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Duration before firing: <code>1m</code> to <code>30d</code> (supports <code>m</code>, <code>h</code>, <code>d</code> and combinations like <code>1h30m</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Constraints:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Only humans can use <code>/remind</code> (bots are rejected)</li>\n<li>Minimum delay: 1 minute</li>\n<li>Maximum delay: 30 days</li>\n<li>Maximum message length: 1800 characters</li>\n<li>Maximum 5 active reminders per user</li>\n<li>Maximum 10 mention targets per reminder (use a @role for larger groups)</li>\n<li><code>@everyone</code> and <code>@here</code> in messages are automatically neutralized (will not trigger mass mentions)</li>\n<li>One-shot only (fires once, then removed)</li>\n<li>Reminders persist across bot restarts (stored in <code>$HOME/.openab/reminders.json</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Examples:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>/remind targets:@Alice @Bob message:Review PR #42 delay:2h\n/remind targets:@Reviewers message:Stand-up time delay:30m\n/remind targets:@Charlie message:Check deployment delay:1d\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>When fired, the bot posts:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>⏰ Reminder from @sender:\n&quot;Review PR #42&quot;\ncc @Alice @Bob\n</code></pre>\n<h2><code>/auth</code></h2>\n<p>Trigger the backend agent's device-flow authentication. OAB executes the command defined in <code>OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND</code>, captures the device code URL from stdout/stderr, and relays it to the user as an ephemeral Discord message.</p>\n<p><strong>Flow:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li>User runs <code>/auth</code></li>\n<li>OAB executes <code>$OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND</code> (e.g. <code>codex login --device-auth</code>)</li>\n<li>OAB captures the device URL + code from the command's output</li>\n<li>OAB sends an ephemeral reply with the URL and code</li>\n<li>User opens the URL in their browser, enters the code</li>\n<li>The auth command exits successfully → OAB confirms &quot;✅ Authentication successful!&quot;</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Requirements:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND</code> environment variable must be set</li>\n<li>The auth command must use OAuth device flow (print URL + code to stdout, then block until authorized)</li>\n<li>No interactive stdin input required (headless-compatible)</li>\n<li>Must be invoked in a <strong>DM</strong> with the bot (rejected in guild channels/threads for security)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Timeout:</strong> 14 minutes. If the user doesn't authorize within that window, the process is killed and the user is prompted to run <code>/auth</code> again. (Reduced from 15min to leave headroom for Discord's interaction token TTL.)</p>\n<p><strong>Behavior notes:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Only users in the <code>allowed_users</code> list can invoke <code>/auth</code></li>\n<li>Bot users are rejected — <code>/auth</code> is for human operators only</li>\n<li>A 30-second URL-collection window waits for the auth command to print its URL. Slow-starting CLIs that take longer may show &quot;no output&quot;.</li>\n<li>Only one <code>/auth</code> flow can run at a time (single-flight). A second concurrent invocation is rejected with &quot;already in progress&quot;.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Error cases:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>OPENAB_AGENT_AUTH_COMMAND</code> not set → immediate error message</li>\n<li>Invoked by a bot user → rejected</li>\n<li>Invoked outside a DM (in a guild channel/thread) → rejected for security</li>\n<li>Auth command fails to start → error message</li>\n<li>Auth command exits <strong>before</strong> printing a login URL (within the 30s window) → warning that no URL was produced, with a retry prompt</li>\n<li>Auth command exits with non-zero → failure message with exit code</li>\n<li>Timeout → process killed, retry prompt</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Slash Commands"
      }
    },
