      "slug": "steering-design-guide",
      "html": "<h1>Steering Design Guide</h1>\n<h2>Problem</h2>\n<p>AI coding agents load persistent instructions every session, but without deliberate organization:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Bloated instructions</strong> dilute attention — critical rules get buried in noise</li>\n<li><strong>Duplicated rules</strong> across files inevitably contradict each other when one is updated</li>\n<li><strong>Missing triggers</strong> mean mandatory behaviors live in docs the agent never reads</li>\n<li><strong>No shared standard</strong> across agents leads to each team reinventing the wheel</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This guide establishes a universal framework for organizing agent memory into layers, so rules are reliably followed, context budgets are respected, and teams can onboard new agents without starting from scratch.</p>\n<p>OpenAB is designed to be agent-agnostic — it supports Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, and Pi running side by side. This guide provides a shared memory architecture standard that allows all supported coding agents to maintain consistent behavior, collaborate effectively, and operate from a single source of truth regardless of their underlying platform differences.</p>\n<hr />\n<p>How to organize AI agent memory across three tiers: hot (always loaded), warm (triggered on demand), and cold (searched when needed).</p>\n<p>Applies to: Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, Pi — any agent that supports persistent instruction files.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Terminology</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Term</th>\n<th>Meaning</th>\n<th>Examples</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>🔥 <strong>Hot memory</strong></td>\n<td>Loaded every session, always in context</td>\n<td><code>AGENTS.md</code>, <code>.kiro/steering/</code>, <code>CLAUDE.md</code>, <code>GEMINI.md</code>, <code>.github/copilot-instructions.md</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>☕ <strong>Warm context</strong></td>\n<td>Not always loaded, but auto-triggered when conditions match</td>\n<td>Codex Skills (body), Copilot path-specific instructions, CC/Gemini individual memory files (pointed to by hot index), subdir instruction files</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>❄️ <strong>Cold storage</strong></td>\n<td>Searched or retrieved on demand, no automatic trigger</td>\n<td>Knowledge bases, <code>docs/</code>, project wikis, ADRs, historical records</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>What Goes in Hot Memory</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Criteria</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Every interaction might trigger it</td>\n<td>Output format spec, verdict logic</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Identity &amp; relationships</td>\n<td>Agent name, team members, contact IDs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>SOP trigger words</td>\n<td>&quot;review PRs&quot; → auto-execute workflow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Hard rules that are easy to get wrong</td>\n<td>&quot;NITs are blocking&quot;, &quot;never merge&quot;, &quot;English only on GitHub&quot;</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Tool usage patterns</td>\n<td>Login flows, API call patterns</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Constraints that override defaults</td>\n<td>&quot;Don't ask for confirmation on X&quot;, &quot;Always do Y before Z&quot;</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>What Stays in Cold Storage</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Criteria</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Historical records / case studies</td>\n<td>Past incident lessons, collaboration logs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>One-time reference</td>\n<td>Installation steps, migration guides</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Large data</td>\n<td>User profiles, conversation history</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Design proposals / RFCs</td>\n<td>Architecture decisions, feature specs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Lookup tables</td>\n<td>Feature flags, config reference, changelogs</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>What Goes in Warm Context</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Criteria</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Too large for hot, but has a reliable trigger</td>\n<td>Deployment SOP, release checklist</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Only relevant for specific file types or paths</td>\n<td>Gateway adapter checklist, Helm wiring rules</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Domain-specific expert knowledge</td>\n<td>Platform auth spec details, crypto implementation patterns</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Complex workflows with steps and scripts</td>\n<td>Incident triage playbook, skill bodies</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Rule of thumb:</strong> If it has a clear trigger condition and is &gt; 1KB, make it warm. Keep only the trigger (name + one-line description + path) in hot.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Design Principles</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Small and precise</strong> — Keep hot memory concise. Practical caps vary by agent (CC: ~200 lines for MEMORY.md, Codex: 32KB, Kiro: ~15KB recommended). Regardless of hard limits, attention dilution is the real constraint — less is more.</li>\n<li><strong>Behavior-oriented</strong> — Every line should change &quot;what the agent does next.&quot; Remove anything that's just &quot;nice to know.&quot;</li>\n<li><strong>Single source of truth</strong> — Define each rule in exactly one place. Duplication across files creates contradiction risk.</li>\n<li><strong>Testable</strong> — Each rule should be verifiable with a single prompt from a fresh session.</li>\n<li><strong>One file per responsibility</strong> — Separate concerns: identity, review process, workflow triggers. Avoid monolithic instruction files.</li>\n<li><strong>Hot/cold separation</strong> — If the agent can find it via search when needed, it doesn't need to be always-loaded.</li>\n<li><strong>Structure over prose</strong> — Use lists, tables, or key-value pairs in hot memory. LLMs follow structured constraints more reliably than natural language paragraphs.</li>\n<li><strong>WHAT and HOW only</strong> — Hot memory defines what to do and how. Put the WHY (historical context, incident backstory) in cold storage (ADRs, lessons learned).</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>Decision Flowchart</h2>\n<pre><code>&quot;If this rule is NOT loaded, will the next response be wrong?&quot;\n│\n├─ Yes → 🔥 Hot memory\n│\n├─ Only when doing a specific task/touching specific files\n│  → ☕ Warm context (put trigger in hot, body in warm)\n│\n└─ No, it's reference → ❄️ Cold storage\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Architecture Pattern</h2>\n<pre><code>┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    🔥 HOT — Always Loaded                        │\n│                                                                 │\n│  Identity, hard rules, collaboration protocol, trigger index    │\n│  AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / .kiro/steering/*           │\n│  .github/copilot-instructions.md / MEMORY.md index              │\n│                         &lt; 15KB                                  │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                 ☕ WARM — Progressive Exposure                    │\n│                                                                 │\n│  Auto-loaded when trigger condition matches                     │\n│  Skills (SKILL.md body), path-specific instructions,            │\n│  subdir instruction files, individual memory files,             │\n│  domain SOPs, deployment playbooks                              │\n│                                                                 │\n│  Triggers:  Rule-based (applyTo glob)                           │\n│             Semantic (agent reads index, decides to load)        │\n│             Explicit (activate_skill / read_file)               │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                 ❄️ COLD — Search on Demand                       │\n│                                                                 │\n│  No automatic trigger; requires explicit search/retrieval       │\n│  Knowledge bases, docs/*.md, wikis, ADRs, RFCs,                 │\n│  historical records, lessons learned, team trivia               │\n│                       Unlimited                                  │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\n         ▲ Smaller, precise, behavioral\n         │\n         ▼ Larger, reference, historical\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Key insight:</strong> The warm layer's <em>trigger metadata</em> lives in hot memory (skill names, index entries, applyTo globs). Only the <em>body</em> loads on demand. Pattern: <strong>put the table of contents in hot, put the chapters in warm.</strong></p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Trigger mechanisms vary by agent:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Rule-based:</strong> Copilot <code>applyTo</code> glob match, Codex skill metadata match</li>\n<li><strong>Semantic:</strong> CC/Gemini memory index — agent reads description and decides to load</li>\n<li><strong>Explicit:</strong> Agent calls <code>activate_skill</code> or <code>read_file</code> when task matches</li>\n</ul>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Real-world example:</strong> Claude Code's auto-memory system is a natural implementation of hot/warm separation — <code>MEMORY.md</code> index (hot, 200-line cap) points to individual <code>.md</code> memory files (warm, loaded when agent determines relevance from index description).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Common pattern:</strong> CC, Codex, and Gemini all use hierarchical loading (global → project → subdir). This naturally supports &quot;one file per responsibility&quot; by placing topic-specific rules in the relevant subdirectory's instruction file.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>Agent-Specific File Mapping</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Most agents are hybrid — they combine multiple loading models. The table below shows the primary mechanisms.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Loading Models</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Model</th>\n<th>Trigger</th>\n<th>Examples</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Always loaded</strong></td>\n<td>Every session/interaction in repo context</td>\n<td>Kiro <code>.kiro/steering/*</code>, CC/Codex/Gemini root instruction file, Copilot <code>.github/copilot-instructions.md</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Directory-scoped</strong></td>\n<td>Processing files within that directory tree</td>\n<td>CC/Codex/Gemini subdir instruction files, Copilot <code>AGENTS.md</code> (nearest-in-tree)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>File-scoped</strong></td>\n<td>Matching an <code>applyTo</code> glob pattern</td>\n<td>Copilot <code>.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Implication for hot memory design:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>&quot;Always loaded&quot; = put task-agnostic rules here (identity, verdict logic, workflow triggers)</li>\n<li>&quot;Directory-scoped&quot; = put domain-specific rules here (gateway checklist, docs standards)</li>\n<li>&quot;File-scoped&quot; = put file-type-specific review expectations here (only Copilot supports this natively)</li>\n</ul>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Agent</th>\n<th>Hot Memory Location</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Kiro</td>\n<td><code>AGENTS.md</code> + <code>.kiro/steering/*.md</code></td>\n<td>Multiple files, one per topic</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Claude Code</td>\n<td><code>CLAUDE.md</code> (project) + <code>~/.claude/CLAUDE.md</code> (global) + <code>MEMORY.md</code> index</td>\n<td>Hierarchical loading (global → project → subdir). Auto-memory index is hot (200-line cap); individual memory files are cold. <code>settings.json</code> is config, not instructions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Codex</td>\n<td><code>AGENTS.md</code> hierarchical (global → project root → subdir)</td>\n<td>Each directory loads at most one file. 32KB cap (<code>project_doc_max_bytes</code>). Use nested <code>AGENTS.md</code> for per-directory responsibility split. No multi-file topic split within same dir</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Gemini</td>\n<td><code>GEMINI.md</code> hierarchical (<code>~/.gemini/GEMINI.md</code> global → <code>./GEMINI.md</code> project → subdir) + <code>MEMORY.md</code> index</td>\n<td>Same hierarchical pattern as CC/Codex. Private project memory index is hot; individual memory files are cold</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Copilot</td>\n<td><code>.github/copilot-instructions.md</code> (repo-wide) + <code>.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md</code> (path-specific) + <code>AGENTS.md</code> (nearest-in-tree, where supported: cloud agent / CLI)</td>\n<td>Layered: Personal &gt; Path-specific &gt; Repo-wide &gt; Agent &gt; Organization. No documented hard size cap for Chat/Agent (code review reads first 4K chars only). Keep short (~2 pages recommended)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>OpenCode</td>\n<td><code>AGENTS.md</code> or equivalent</td>\n<td>Follows repo convention</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Pi</td>\n<td><code>AGENTS.md</code> hierarchical (project root → global) + <code>SYSTEM.md</code> or <code>APPEND_SYSTEM.md</code> in <code>.pi/</code></td>\n<td>Project or global <code>SYSTEM.md</code> replaces the default system prompt, while <code>APPEND_SYSTEM.md</code> appends to it. <code>AGENTS.md</code> is loaded hierarchically for context injection</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Validation Checklist</h2>\n<p>After adding or changing hot memory:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Start a fresh session</strong> (no prior context)</li>\n<li><strong>Ask a question that triggers the rule</strong> — e.g., &quot;what format should a review comment use?&quot;</li>\n<li><strong>Verify the response follows the rule exactly</strong></li>\n<li><strong>Test edge cases</strong> — e.g., &quot;what if there's only one 🟡 finding?&quot;</li>\n<li><strong>Check for contradictions</strong> — does the new rule conflict with anything else in hot memory?</li>\n</ol>\n<p>If the agent doesn't follow the rule → it's either not loaded, too buried in other content, or ambiguously worded.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Anti-Patterns</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Anti-Pattern</th>\n<th>Why It's Bad</th>\n<th>Fix</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Dumping everything into one file</td>\n<td>Critical rules get lost in noise</td>\n<td>Split by responsibility</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Duplicating rules across files</td>\n<td>Inevitable contradictions when one is updated</td>\n<td>Single source + pointer</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Putting case studies in hot memory</td>\n<td>Wastes context budget on history</td>\n<td>Move to docs, reference by lesson only</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Vague rules (&quot;be helpful&quot;)</td>\n<td>Untestable, no behavioral change</td>\n<td>Make specific and testable</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Hot memory &gt; 20KB</td>\n<td>Diminishing returns, attention dilution</td>\n<td>Audit and move cold items out</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Task-scoped rules in file/directory-scoped locations</td>\n<td>Review SOP, response format, collaboration protocol only load when certain files are touched — missing when needed most</td>\n<td>Put task-agnostic workflow rules in always-loaded layer, not path-specific</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Stale links in hot memory</td>\n<td>Index points to missing files; fresh session gets dead references</td>\n<td>Audit links quarterly; remove or create the target</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Mandatory behavior hidden in cold without trigger</td>\n<td>Agent must follow it but has no path to discover it</td>\n<td>Add trigger metadata to hot, or promote to warm with clear activation condition</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Maintenance</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Quarterly audit</strong>: Review hot memory files. Remove rules that are no longer relevant or have become default behavior.</li>\n<li><strong>After contradictions</strong>: When agent behavior contradicts a rule, check if it's a loading issue or a conflict with another rule.</li>\n<li><strong>After new capabilities</strong>: When adding new workflows, decide hot vs cold before writing the doc.</li>\n<li><strong>Adding a new agent</strong>: Document its loading model and precedence before adding file mappings. Don't assume it works like existing agents.</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Self-Reflection Prompt</h2>\n<p>Use this prompt from a fresh session to audit memory allocation against this guide:</p>\n<pre><code>Per the steering design guide in docs/steering-design-guide.md from OpenAB GitHub repo, review your current memory allocation:\n\n1. INVENTORY — List all loaded/discoverable instruction sources:\n   - File path\n   - Layer (Hot / Warm / Cold)\n   - Trigger model (always / directory / file-glob / semantic / explicit)\n   - Approximate size (lines or KB)\n\n2. CLASSIFY — For each item, what type of content is it?\n   - WHAT/HOW (behavior rule) vs WHY (history/rationale)\n   - Identity / hard rule / workflow / reference / trivia\n\n3. VIOLATIONS — Identify items that break the guide's principles:\n   - Not behavior-oriented (nice-to-know in hot)\n   - Duplicated or conflicting across files\n   - Stale links pointing to missing files\n   - Too large for its layer\n   - WHY/history in hot instead of cold\n   - Mandatory behavior in cold with no trigger path\n\n4. TRIGGER QUALITY — Review warm layer triggers:\n   - Are index descriptions precise enough to fire correctly?\n   - Where is the canonical source for each rule?\n   - Will the agent reliably see it when needed?\n\n5. OPTIMIZATION PLAN — Propose concrete moves:\n   - Remove (stale, duplicate, irrelevant)\n   - Keep in hot (behavioral, high-frequency)\n   - Promote cold → warm (add trigger)\n   - Demote hot → warm or cold (too large, low-frequency)\n   - Split (one file doing too many jobs)\n   - Add missing trigger/index entry\n\n6. VERIFY — Name one fresh-session test prompt that would confirm\n   the highest-risk rule still loads correctly.\n</code></pre>\n<p>Expected output: a before/after table with file paths, layer assignments, sizes, and rationale for each move.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Steering Design Guide"
      }
    },

      "slug": "steering/feature-request",
      "html": "<h1>Feature Request Guide for openabdev/openab</h1>\n<h2>Purpose</h2>\n<p>This document guides AI agents (and humans) in crafting well-structured\nfeature requests for the openabdev/openab project.</p>\n<p><strong>Usage — ask your AI:</strong></p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Per <a href=\"https://github.com/openabdev/openab/blob/main/docs/steering/feature-request.md\">https://github.com/openabdev/openab/blob/main/docs/steering/feature-request.md</a>,\nsubmit a feature request for me about our previous discussion.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>The AI will synthesize the conversation into a feature request and submit it.</p>\n<h2>Required Sections</h2>\n<p>Every feature request MUST include these headings with non-empty content:</p>\n<h3>1. Description</h3>\n<p>A clear, concise summary of the feature. Answer:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>What</strong> — What capability is being requested?</li>\n<li><strong>Where</strong> — Which component/area does it affect? (e.g. discord, slack, session, helm)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Keep it to 2–4 sentences. Lead with the outcome, not the implementation.</p>\n<h3>2. Use Case</h3>\n<p>Explain <strong>why</strong> this feature is needed. Answer:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>What problem does the user face today?</li>\n<li>What workflow or scenario triggers the need?</li>\n<li>Who benefits? (end users, operators, contributors)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Use concrete examples. &quot;As a server admin, I want X so that Y&quot; is better than\n&quot;it would be nice to have X.&quot;</p>\n<h3>3. Proposed Solution (optional but encouraged)</h3>\n<p>If the requester has ideas on implementation:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Describe the approach at a high level</li>\n<li>Reference relevant code paths or components</li>\n<li>Note any constraints or compatibility concerns</li>\n<li>Use ASCII diagrams for architecture/flow if helpful</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>4. Prior Art (optional)</h3>\n<p>Reference similar features in related projects or ecosystems:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>How does OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, or another project handle this?</li>\n<li>Link to relevant docs, issues, or implementations</li>\n<li>Note what worked well and what didn't</li>\n</ul>\n<p>This helps maintainers evaluate approaches and avoid known pitfalls.</p>\n<h3>5. Related Issues</h3>\n<p>Search existing issues and reference any that are related:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Duplicates or near-duplicates</li>\n<li>Issues that this feature would complement or depend on</li>\n<li>Issues that this feature could supersede</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Based on what already exists, consider whether the FR scope should be\nadjusted to better fit the product direction — narrower, broader, or\nreframed as an extension of existing work.</p>\n<h2>Submission Format</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">gh issue create --repo openabdev/openab \\\n  --title &quot;feat(&lt;scope&gt;): &lt;summary&gt;&quot; \\\n  --label &quot;feature,&lt;scope-label&gt;&quot; \\\n  --body '### Description\n\n&lt;description&gt;\n\n### Use Case\n\n&lt;use case&gt;\n\n### Proposed Solution\n\n&lt;proposed solution or remove section if none&gt;\n\n### Prior Art\n\n&lt;prior art or remove section if none&gt;\n\n### Related Issues\n\n&lt;related issues or &quot;None found.&quot;&gt;'\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Title Convention</h2>\n<p>Format: <code>feat(&lt;scope&gt;): &lt;short summary&gt;</code></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Scope must be one of: <code>discord</code>, <code>slack</code>, <code>session</code>, <code>helm</code>, <code>ci</code>, <code>docs</code></li>\n<li>Summary should be imperative mood, lowercase, no period (e.g. <code>add thread pinning support</code>)</li>\n<li>Keep under 72 characters total</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Quality Checklist</h2>\n<p>Before submitting, verify:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <strong>Title</strong> follows <code>feat(&lt;scope&gt;): summary</code> convention</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <strong>Description</strong> clearly states what the feature is</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <strong>Use Case</strong> explains why it's needed with a concrete scenario</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <strong>No duplicates</strong> — search existing issues first: <code>gh search issues &quot;&lt;keywords&gt;&quot; --repo openabdev/openab --label feature</code></li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <strong>Related issues reviewed</strong> — searched for related issues and considered whether the FR scope should be adjusted</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <strong>Scope label</strong> is included alongside <code>feature</code></li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> <strong>References</strong> — link related issues with <code>#number</code> if applicable</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>AI Agent Instructions</h2>\n<p>When an AI agent is asked to submit a feature request referencing this doc:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Synthesize</strong> — Distill the conversation into the required sections. Don't copy-paste raw chat; rewrite into clear, structured prose.</li>\n<li><strong>Infer scope</strong> — Determine the correct scope from the discussion context.</li>\n<li><strong>Search related issues</strong> — Search existing issues for duplicates and related work. List them in the Related Issues section.</li>\n<li><strong>Refine scope</strong> — Based on related issues found, consider whether the FR should be narrower, broader, or reframed to better fit the product. Suggest adjustments to the user.</li>\n<li><strong>Check prior art</strong> — Look for similar features in OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, or other related projects.</li>\n<li><strong>Draft and confirm</strong> — Show the user the formatted issue (title + body) and ask for confirmation before submitting.</li>\n<li><strong>Submit</strong> — Use <code>gh issue create</code> with the correct labels and format.</li>\n<li><strong>Report</strong> — Share the issue URL after creation.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Example</h2>\n<pre><code>Title: feat(discord): support per-channel session timeout override\n\nLabels: feature, discord\n\n### Description\n\nAllow server admins to configure different session timeout values\nper Discord channel, overriding the global default.\n\n### Use Case\n\nIn large servers, some channels are used for quick Q&amp;A (short timeout\npreferred) while others host long-running collaborative sessions\n(longer timeout needed). Currently the global timeout applies\neverywhere, forcing admins to pick a compromise value.\n\n### Proposed Solution\n\nAdd an optional `session_timeout` field to the per-channel config in\n`openab.yaml`. When set, it overrides the global `session.timeout`.\nFall back to global if unset.\n\n### Prior Art\n\nOpenClaw supports per-channel configuration overrides via its\n`channel_config` map. See openclaw/openclaw#142.\n\n### Related Issues\n\n- #210 — global session timeout configuration (this extends it)\n- #185 — per-channel bot personality (similar per-channel override pattern)\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Feature Request Guide for openabdev/openab"
      }
    },

      "slug": "steering/pr-review",
      "html": "<h1>PR Review Guide for openabdev/openab</h1>\n<h2>Review Framework</h2>\n<p>When reviewing a PR, always address these four questions:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>What problem does it solve</strong> — What pain point or requirement does this PR address? Explain the background in plain language.</li>\n<li><strong>How does it solve it</strong> — The specific technical approach, architecture decisions, and key implementation details.</li>\n<li><strong>Were alternatives considered</strong> — Does the PR description explain why this approach was chosen over alternatives? If not, suggest the author clarify.</li>\n<li><strong>Is this the best approach</strong> — Evaluate whether the current approach is optimal. Point out areas for improvement and potential risks.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Severity Levels</h2>\n<p>Use emoji + color to classify each review comment:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Level</th>\n<th>Emoji</th>\n<th>Meaning</th>\n<th>Action Required</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>🔴 Critical</td>\n<td><code>## 🔴 Critical:</code></td>\n<td>Correctness bug, security issue, data loss risk</td>\n<td>Must fix before merge</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>🟡 Minor</td>\n<td><code>## 🟡 Minor:</code></td>\n<td>Style inconsistency, missing defense-in-depth, non-blocking improvement</td>\n<td>Should fix, not really a blocker but nice to have</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>🟢 Info</td>\n<td><code>## 🟢 Info:</code></td>\n<td>Knowledge sharing, future consideration, design tradeoff note</td>\n<td>No action needed</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Comment Format</h2>\n<p>Each review comment should include:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>What's wrong</strong> — describe the issue clearly</li>\n<li><strong>Where</strong> — file path and line number</li>\n<li><strong>Why it matters</strong> — what breaks or what risk it introduces</li>\n<li><strong>Fix</strong> — provide a concrete code suggestion</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Example (from PR #210)</h3>\n<pre><code>## 🔴 Critical: resize() distorts aspect ratio\n\n**File:** `src/discord.rs`, line ~320\n\n`image::Image::resize(w, h, filter)` resizes the image to the exact\ngiven dimensions — it does not preserve aspect ratio automatically.\nA 4000×2000 landscape image gets squashed into 1200×1200.\n\n### Fix\n\n```rust\nlet ratio = f64::from(IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION_PX) / f64::max(w, h);\nlet new_w = (f64::from(w) * ratio) as u32;\nlet new_h = (f64::from(h) * ratio) as u32;\nimg.resize(new_w, new_h, image::imageops::FilterType::Lanczos3)\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code>\n## Self-Review Checklist (before opening PR)\n\nAuthors should check these before requesting review:\n\n- [ ] **API behavior verified** — read the docs for any new library/function used\n- [ ] **Safety checks preserved** — if refactoring, confirm all original validation/security checks are still present\n- [ ] **Code style consistent** — logging, error handling, naming match the existing codebase\n- [ ] **Tests test the right thing** — assertions reflect actual expected behavior, not just &quot;passes&quot;\n\n## Review Etiquette\n\n- **Be specific** — &quot;this is wrong&quot; is not helpful; show what's wrong and how to fix it\n- **Classify severity** — not everything is a blocker; use 🔴🟡🟢 so the author knows what to prioritize\n- **Acknowledge good work** — if something is well done, say so\n- **One round if possible** — batch all feedback in one review pass to avoid back-and-forth\n\n## Output Format — Traffic Light\n\nAfter the review, structure the output using this format:\n\n🟢 **INFO** — Things that look good, patterns followed correctly, positive observations.\n\n🟡 **NIT** — Minor suggestions, documentation improvements, nice-to-haves. Not blockers.\n\n🔴 **SUGGESTED CHANGES** — Significant concerns, DX footguns, missing pieces that should be addressed. Frame as suggestions for maintainers to consider (we are triagers, not maintainers).\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "PR Review Guide for openabdev/openab"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "steering/triage",
      "html": "<h1>Issue Triage Guide for openabdev/openab</h1>\n<h2>Steps</h2>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Confirm type</strong> — ensure one of: <code>bug</code>, <code>feature</code>, <code>guidance</code></li>\n<li><strong>Verify claims</strong> — be skeptical; find source code or official docs to confirm before accepting a bug report as valid</li>\n<li><strong>Set priority</strong> — add exactly one:\n<ul>\n<li><code>p0</code> 🔴 Critical — drop everything</li>\n<li><code>p1</code> 🟠 High — address this sprint</li>\n<li><code>p2</code> 🟡 Medium — planned work</li>\n<li><code>p3</code> 🟤 Low — nice to have</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Remove <code>needs-triage</code></strong> — triage complete</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Priority Guidelines</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Priority</th>\n<th>Criteria</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>p0</td>\n<td>Security vulnerability, data loss, entire system down</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>p1</td>\n<td>Major feature broken for a class of users (e.g. all Claude Code / Cursor users)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>p2</td>\n<td>Bug with workaround, or planned feature work</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>p3</td>\n<td>Minor improvement, cosmetic, nice to have</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Response Template</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Issue at a Glance</strong> — always include an ASCII diagram showing the flow and where things break</li>\n<li>Acknowledge the issue by investigating the relevant source code or official docs</li>\n<li>Confirm root cause or ask clarifying questions</li>\n<li>Link relevant spec/doc references when available</li>\n<li>Invite PR or state next steps</li>\n<li><strong>Draft response for human approval before posting to the issue comment</strong></li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Issue at a Glance Example</h2>\n<pre><code>Discord User ──► openab ──► Claude Code / Cursor agent\n                   │\n                   ▼\n          session/request_permission\n          (agent asks: &quot;can I run this tool?&quot;)\n                   │\n                   ▼\n          openab auto-reply (WRONG shape):\n          ┌─────────────────────────────────┐\n          │ { &quot;optionId&quot;: &quot;allow_always&quot; }  │  ← flat, no wrapper\n          └─────────────────────────────────┘\n                   │\n                   ▼\n          SDK cannot find `outcome` field\n          → treats as REFUSAL ❌\n</code></pre>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Issue Triage Guide for openabdev/openab"
      }
    },

      "slug": "stt",
      "html": "<h1>Speech-to-Text (STT) for Voice Messages</h1>\n<p>openab can automatically transcribe voice message attachments (Discord, Feishu, LINE 1:1 chat, and other gateway platforms) and forward the transcript to your ACP agent as text.</p>\n<h2>Quick Start</h2>\n<blockquote>\n<p>📖 Full STT config options: <a href=\"/openab/config-reference#stt\">docs/config-reference.md</a></p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Add an <code>[stt]</code> section to your <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = true\n</code></pre>\n<p>If <code>GROQ_API_KEY</code> is set in your environment, that's all you need — openab will auto-detect it and use Groq's free tier. You can also set the key explicitly:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = true\napi_key = &quot;${GROQ_API_KEY}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>How It Works</h2>\n<pre><code>Voice message (Discord .ogg, Feishu opus/ogg, LINE .m4a/.ogg, etc.)\n       │\n       ▼\n  openab downloads the audio file\n       │\n       ▼\n  POST /audio/transcriptions  →  STT provider\n       │\n       ▼\n  transcript injected as:\n  &quot;[Voice message transcript]: &lt;transcribed text&gt;&quot;\n       │\n       ▼\n  ACP agent receives plain text\n</code></pre>\n<p>The transcript is prepended to the prompt as a <code>ContentBlock::Text</code>, so the downstream agent (Kiro CLI, Claude Code, etc.) sees it as regular text input.</p>\n<p>Platform note:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>LINE voice-message STT is currently supported in <strong>1:1 chat only</strong>. Group/room audio is still filtered out by LINE mention gating rules.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Configuration Reference</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = true                              # default: false\napi_key = &quot;${GROQ_API_KEY}&quot;                 # required for cloud providers\nmodel = &quot;whisper-large-v3-turbo&quot;            # default\nbase_url = &quot;https://api.groq.com/openai/v1&quot; # default\necho_transcript = true                      # default: false (opt-in)\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>enabled</code></td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Enable/disable STT. When disabled, audio attachments are silently skipped.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>api_key</code></td>\n<td>no*</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>API key for the STT provider. *Auto-detected from <code>GROQ_API_KEY</code> env var if not set. For local servers, use any non-empty string (e.g. <code>&quot;not-needed&quot;</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model</code></td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td><code>whisper-large-v3-turbo</code></td>\n<td>Whisper model name. Varies by provider.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base_url</code></td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td><code>https://api.groq.com/openai/v1</code></td>\n<td>OpenAI-compatible API base URL.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>echo_transcript</code></td>\n<td>no</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>When set to <code>true</code> and STT runs, post a <code>&gt; 🎤 &lt;transcript&gt;</code> message to the thread before the agent reply so users can verify what was heard. Failures show <code>(transcription failed)</code> and add a ⚠️ reaction to the original message.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Deployment Options</h2>\n<p>openab uses the standard OpenAI-compatible <code>/audio/transcriptions</code> endpoint. Any provider that implements this API works — just change <code>base_url</code>.</p>\n<h3>Option 1: Groq Cloud (recommended, free tier)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = true\napi_key = &quot;${GROQ_API_KEY}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Free tier with rate limits</li>\n<li>Model: <code>whisper-large-v3-turbo</code> (default)</li>\n<li>Sign up at <a href=\"https://console.groq.com\">https://console.groq.com</a></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Option 2: OpenAI</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = true\napi_key = &quot;${OPENAI_API_KEY}&quot;\nmodel = &quot;whisper-1&quot;\nbase_url = &quot;https://api.openai.com/v1&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>~$0.006 per minute of audio</li>\n<li>Model: <code>whisper-1</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Option 3: Local Whisper Server</h3>\n<p>For users running openab on a Mac Mini, home lab, or any machine with a local whisper server:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = true\napi_key = &quot;not-needed&quot;\nmodel = &quot;large-v3-turbo&quot;\nbase_url = &quot;http://localhost:8080/v1&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Audio stays local — never leaves your machine</li>\n<li>No API key or cloud account needed</li>\n<li>Apple Silicon users get hardware acceleration</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Compatible local whisper servers:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Server</th>\n<th>Install</th>\n<th>Apple Silicon</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><a href=\"https://github.com/fedirz/faster-whisper-server\">faster-whisper-server</a></td>\n<td><code>pip install faster-whisper-server</code></td>\n<td>✅ CoreML</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><a href=\"https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp\">whisper.cpp server</a></td>\n<td><code>brew install whisper-cpp</code></td>\n<td>✅ Metal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><a href=\"https://github.com/mudler/LocalAI\">LocalAI</a></td>\n<td>Docker or binary</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Option 4: LAN / Sidecar Server</h3>\n<p>Point to a whisper server running on another machine in your network:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = true\napi_key = &quot;not-needed&quot;\nbase_url = &quot;http://192.168.1.100:8080/v1&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Not Supported</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Ollama</strong> — does not expose an <code>/audio/transcriptions</code> endpoint.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Helm Chart (Kubernetes)</h2>\n<p>When deploying via the openab Helm chart, STT is a first-class config block — no manual configmap patching needed:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.apiKey=gsk_xxx\n</code></pre>\n<p>The API key is stored in a K8s Secret and injected as an env var (never in plaintext in the configmap). You can also customize model and endpoint:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.apiKey=gsk_xxx \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.model=whisper-large-v3-turbo \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.baseUrl=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">helm upgrade openab openab/openab \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.enabled=true \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.apiKey=gsk_xxx \\\n  --set agents.kiro.stt.echoTranscript=true    # opt in to transcript echo\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Disabling STT</h2>\n<p>Omit the <code>[stt]</code> section entirely, or set:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[stt]\nenabled = false\n</code></pre>\n<p>When disabled, audio attachments are silently skipped with no impact on existing functionality.</p>\n<h2>Technical Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>openab sends <code>response_format=json</code> in the transcription request to ensure the response is always parseable JSON. Some local whisper servers default to plain text output without this parameter.</li>\n<li>The actual MIME type from the platform attachment is passed through to the STT API (e.g. <code>audio/ogg</code> for Discord and Feishu voice messages, <code>audio/mp4</code>, <code>audio/wav</code>).</li>\n<li>Environment variables in config values are expanded via <code>${VAR}</code> syntax (e.g. <code>api_key = &quot;${GROQ_API_KEY}&quot;</code>).</li>\n<li>The <code>api_key</code> field is auto-detected from the <code>GROQ_API_KEY</code> environment variable when using the default Groq endpoint. If you set a custom <code>base_url</code> (e.g. local server), auto-detect is disabled to avoid leaking the Groq key to unrelated endpoints — you must set <code>api_key</code> explicitly.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Speech-to-text"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "telegram",
      "html": "<h1>Telegram Setup</h1>\n<p>Connect a Telegram bot to OpenAB.</p>\n<h2>Deployment Modes</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Mode</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>When to use</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Unified</strong> (recommended)</td>\n<td>Single OAB binary with embedded webhook server</td>\n<td>New deployments, ECS, k8s, Zeabur</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Standalone Gateway</strong></td>\n<td>Separate gateway process, OAB connects via WebSocket</td>\n<td>Legacy deployments, custom routing</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Unified Mode (Recommended)</h2>\n<p>The OAB binary embeds the Telegram adapter directly. No separate gateway container needed.</p>\n<pre><code>Telegram ──POST──▶ OAB (:8080/webhook/telegram) ──▶ Agent (stdio)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Prerequisites</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>OAB image with unified features compiled in (default since v0.9.0-beta.4)</li>\n<li>A Telegram bot token (from <a href=\"https://t.me/BotFather\">@BotFather</a>)</li>\n<li>A public HTTPS URL for the webhook</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<p>Set environment variables:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Bot API token from @BotFather</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Webhook signature validation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Bot username for @mention gating</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>true</code> (default) for rich formatting</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_STREAMING</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>follows <code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_LISTEN</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Listen address (default: <code>0.0.0.0:8080</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>OAB config (<code>config.toml</code>):</p>\n<p><strong>Minimal</strong> — just pass the API key to the agent:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Recommended</strong> — with tuned pool, streaming, and native table rendering:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;compact&quot;\n\n[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Streaming is enabled by default when Rich Messages are active — replies are streamed live via <code>sendRichMessageDraft</code> with rich formatting, then finalized with <code>sendRichMessage</code>. If <code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES=false</code>, streaming is also disabled by default. To override, set <code>TELEGRAM_STREAMING=true</code> or <code>TELEGRAM_STREAMING=false</code> explicitly.</p>\n<p>No <code>[gateway]</code> section needed — the unified adapter activates automatically when <code>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</code> is set, or when the <code>[telegram]</code> section is configured in <code>config.toml</code>.</p>\n<h3>First-class <code>[telegram]</code> config (optional)</h3>\n<p>Instead of (or in addition to) the <code>TELEGRAM_*</code> env vars, you can configure Telegram as a first-class section in <code>config.toml</code> — symmetric with <code>[discord]</code> / <code>[slack]</code>:</p>\n<p><strong>Minimal required</strong> — only <code>bot_token</code> is needed to activate the adapter:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[telegram]\nbot_token = &quot;${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;    # or use aws-sm:// secret ref (see below)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Full example</strong> with all available fields:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[telegram]\nbot_token           = &quot;${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}&quot;   # ${} env expansion supported\nsecret_token        = &quot;${TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN}&quot; # webhook signature validation\ntrusted_source_only = true     # reject requests outside Telegram's IP subnets\nrich_messages       = true     # sendRichMessage rendering (default true)\nstreaming           = true     # override; defaults to follow rich_messages\nwebhook_path        = &quot;/webhook/telegram&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Precedence (per field):</strong> <code>[telegram]</code> value (with <code>${}</code> expansion) → <code>TELEGRAM_*</code> env var → built-in default. This is config-authoritative and matches <code>[discord]</code>/<code>[slack]</code>. Any field you omit falls back to its env var, so existing env-only deployments keep working unchanged.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th><code>[telegram]</code> field</th>\n<th>Env fallback</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bot_token</code></td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>secret_token</code></td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>—</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>trusted_source_only</code></td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_TRUSTED_SOURCE_ONLY</code></td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>rich_messages</code></td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>streaming</code></td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_STREAMING</code></td>\n<td>follows <code>rich_messages</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>webhook_path</code></td>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n<td><code>/webhook/telegram</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Tip</strong>: You can run a pure config-only deployment — no <code>TELEGRAM_*</code> env vars needed. Just set <code>bot_token = &quot;your-token&quot;</code> directly in <code>[telegram]</code> and the adapter will activate from config alone.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Security hardening</strong>: For production deployments, we highly recommend using <code>aws-sm://</code> secret references instead of hardcoding tokens in <code>config.toml</code>. This keeps secrets out of version control and enables rotation and audit:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[secrets.refs]\ntg_token  = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#telegram_bot_token&quot;\ntg_secret = &quot;aws-sm://openab/prod#telegram_secret_token&quot;\n\n[telegram]\nbot_token    = &quot;${secrets.tg_token}&quot;\nsecret_token = &quot;${secrets.tg_secret}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/secrets-management\">secrets-management.md</a> for full documentation.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Set the Webhook</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export BOT_TOKEN=&quot;your-bot-token&quot;\nexport WEBHOOK_URL=&quot;https://your-public-url&quot;\nexport SECRET=&quot;your-webhook-secret&quot;\n\ncurl &quot;https://api.telegram.org/bot${BOT_TOKEN}/setWebhook?url=${WEBHOOK_URL}/webhook/telegram&amp;secret_token=${SECRET}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Standalone Gateway Mode (Legacy)</h2>\n<p>For deployments that need a separate gateway process (e.g., custom webhook routing, multi-gateway fan-out).</p>\n<pre><code>Telegram ──POST──▶ Gateway (:8080) ◀──WebSocket── OAB Pod\n                                       (OAB connects out)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>A running OAB instance (with kiro-cli or any ACP agent authenticated)</li>\n<li>Docker or a Kubernetes cluster</li>\n<li>A Telegram bot token (from <a href=\"https://t.me/BotFather\">@BotFather</a>)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>1. Create a Telegram Bot</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Open <a href=\"https://t.me/BotFather\">@BotFather</a> in Telegram</li>\n<li>Send <code>/newbot</code>, follow the prompts</li>\n<li>Copy the bot token (e.g. <code>123456:ABC-DEF...</code>)</li>\n<li>Optional: send <code>/setprivacy</code> → <code>Disable</code> so the bot can see all group messages (required for @mention gating in groups)</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>2. Run the Gateway</h2>\n<h3>Docker</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker run -d --name openab-gateway \\\n  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=&quot;your-bot-token&quot; \\\n  -e TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN=&quot;your-webhook-secret&quot; \\\n  -e GATEWAY_WS_TOKEN=&quot;your-ws-auth-token&quot; \\\n  -p 8080:8080 \\\n  ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:0.1.0\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Kubernetes</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">apiVersion: apps/v1\nkind: Deployment\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-gateway\nspec:\n  replicas: 1\n  selector:\n    matchLabels:\n      app: openab-gateway\n  template:\n    metadata:\n      labels:\n        app: openab-gateway\n    spec:\n      containers:\n        - name: gateway\n          image: ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:0.1.0\n          ports:\n            - containerPort: 8080\n          env:\n            - name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN\n              valueFrom:\n                secretKeyRef:\n                  name: openab-gateway\n                  key: telegram-bot-token\n            - name: TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN\n              valueFrom:\n                secretKeyRef:\n                  name: openab-gateway\n                  key: telegram-secret-token\n            - name: GATEWAY_WS_TOKEN\n              valueFrom:\n                secretKeyRef:\n                  name: openab-gateway\n                  key: ws-token\n            - name: GATEWAY_LISTEN\n              value: &quot;0.0.0.0:8080&quot;\n---\napiVersion: v1\nkind: Service\nmetadata:\n  name: openab-gateway\nspec:\n  selector:\n    app: openab-gateway\n  ports:\n    - port: 8080\n      targetPort: 8080\n</code></pre>\n<h2>3. Configure OAB</h2>\n<p>Add a <code>[gateway]</code> section to your OAB <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[gateway]\nurl = &quot;ws://openab-gateway:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;telegram&quot;\ntoken = &quot;${GATEWAY_WS_TOKEN}&quot;\nbot_username = &quot;your_bot_username&quot;\n# allowed_users = [&quot;123456789&quot;]          # restrict to specific Telegram user IDs\n# allowed_channels = [&quot;-1001234567890&quot;]  # restrict to specific chat/group IDs\n\n[agent]\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>WebSocket URL of the gateway</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Session key namespace (default: <code>telegram</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>token</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Shared WS auth token (recommended)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bot_username</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Bot username for @mention gating in groups</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_users</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Restrict to listed user IDs (empty = allow all)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allowed_channels</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Restrict to listed chat IDs (empty = allow all)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>4. Set the Telegram Webhook</h2>\n<p>The gateway needs a public HTTPS URL for Telegram to send updates to.</p>\n<h3>Option A: Cloudflare Tunnel (quickest for dev/testing)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080\n# Copy the https://xxx.trycloudflare.com URL\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Option B: Reverse proxy (production)</h3>\n<p>Use nginx, Caddy, or a cloud load balancer with TLS termination pointing to the gateway's <code>:8080</code>.</p>\n<h3>Register the webhook</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export BOT_TOKEN=&quot;your-bot-token&quot;\nexport WEBHOOK_URL=&quot;https://your-gateway-host&quot;\nexport SECRET=&quot;your-webhook-secret&quot;\n\ncurl &quot;https://api.telegram.org/bot${BOT_TOKEN}/setWebhook?url=${WEBHOOK_URL}/webhook/telegram&amp;secret_token=${SECRET}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Verify:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl &quot;https://api.telegram.org/bot${BOT_TOKEN}/getWebhookInfo&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h2>5. Bot Permissions for Supergroups</h2>\n<p>For forum topic creation (thread isolation like Discord):</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Open the supergroup → Settings → Administrators</li>\n<li>Find the bot → Edit</li>\n<li>Enable <strong>Manage Topics</strong></li>\n</ol>\n<p>Without this permission, the bot replies in the main chat instead of creating topics.</p>\n<h2>Features</h2>\n<h3>@mention gating</h3>\n<p>In groups and supergroups, the bot only responds when @mentioned:</p>\n<pre><code>@your_bot explain VPC peering    ← triggers agent\nexplain VPC peering              ← ignored in groups\n</code></pre>\n<p>DMs and replies within forum topics always trigger the agent (no @mention needed).</p>\n<h3>File Attachments (Inbound)</h3>\n<p>The gateway downloads media from Telegram and stores it locally (<code>~/.openab/media/inbound/&lt;uuid&gt;</code>). Core reads directly from disk — no base64 encoding overhead.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Handling</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Images</strong></td>\n<td>Downloaded, resized (max 1200px), JPEG compressed, stored to filesystem. Agent sees the image.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Documents</strong></td>\n<td>Text-based files (<code>.txt</code>, <code>.csv</code>, <code>.rs</code>, <code>.py</code>, etc.) up to 20MB read as UTF-8 and passed to agent. Binary files silently skipped.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Audio/Voice</strong></td>\n<td>Downloaded and stored. If STT is enabled in Core, automatically transcribed and passed as text.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Not supported (inbound):</strong> video, stickers, animations (silently skipped).\n<strong>Not supported (outbound):</strong> bot cannot send images/files back to the user yet.</p>\n<h3>Emoji reactions</h3>\n<p>The bot shows status reactions on your message as the agent works:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Stage</th>\n<th>Emoji</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Queued</td>\n<td>👀</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Thinking</td>\n<td>🤔</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Tool use</td>\n<td>🔥 (general), 👨‍💻 (coding), ⚡ (web)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Done</td>\n<td>👍</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Error</td>\n<td>😱</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Forum topics</h3>\n<p>In supergroups with topics enabled, each new conversation auto-creates a forum topic (like Discord threads). Follow-up messages in the same topic reuse the same agent session.</p>\n<h3>Markdown rendering</h3>\n<p>Agent replies are rendered with Telegram Markdown: <strong>bold</strong>, <code>code</code>, and code blocks work natively.</p>\n<p>With <strong>Rich Messages</strong> enabled (default, requires Bot API 10.1+), headings (<code>##</code>) and tables render with full formatting via <code>sendRichMessage</code>. Code blocks remain on the legacy path for syntax highlighting and copy-button support. Content exceeding 4096 characters is automatically handled via rich messages (up to 32768 chars).</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Important:</strong> OAB's default table mode wraps markdown tables in code blocks before they reach the gateway. To allow native Telegram table rendering via Rich Messages, disable this conversion in your <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Rich Messages requires gateway version <strong>v0.6.0-rc.1</strong> or above (<code>ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:v0.6.0-rc.1</code>+).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>Set <code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES=false</code> to disable rich messages and use legacy <code>sendMessage</code> for all replies.</p>\n<h2>Environment Variables (Gateway)</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Bot API token from @BotFather</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>Webhook signature validation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Use <code>sendRichMessage</code> for tables/headings/long content (Bot API 10.1+). Set <code>false</code> to opt out.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_STREAMING</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>follows <code>TELEGRAM_RICH_MESSAGES</code></td>\n<td>Stream replies live via <code>sendRichMessageDraft</code>. Defaults to <code>true</code> when rich messages are enabled, <code>false</code> otherwise. Set <code>false</code> for send-once mode (single final message).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_WS_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>—</td>\n<td>WebSocket auth token</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>GATEWAY_LISTEN</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>0.0.0.0:8080</code></td>\n<td>Listen address</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>/webhook/telegram</code></td>\n<td>Webhook endpoint path</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<p><strong>Bot doesn't respond in groups:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Check bot privacy mode: <code>/setprivacy</code> → <code>Disable</code> in @BotFather</li>\n<li>Verify <code>bot_username</code> in OAB config matches the bot's actual username</li>\n<li>Check the bot is @mentioned in the message</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>&quot;not enough rights to create a topic&quot;:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Give the bot <strong>Manage Topics</strong> permission in supergroup admin settings</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Webhook returns 502/530:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Check the Cloudflare Tunnel or reverse proxy is running</li>\n<li>Verify <code>curl http://localhost:8080/health</code> returns <code>ok</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Agent spawns but immediately closes:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Run <code>kubectl exec -it deployment/openab-telegram -- kiro-cli login --use-device-flow</code></li>\n<li>Ensure auth is persisted on a PVC, not an emptyDir</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Telegram Setup"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "tool-display",
      "html": "<h1>Tool Display Configuration</h1>\n<p>Control how tool calls are rendered in chat messages during agent responses.</p>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;full&quot;   # full | compact | none\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Helm</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">agents:\n  kiro:\n    reactions:\n      toolDisplay: &quot;full&quot;   # full | compact | none\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Modes</h2>\n<h3><code>full</code> (default)</h3>\n<p>Shows each tool call with its complete title. When more than 3 tools finish, they collapse into a count summary automatically.</p>\n<pre><code>✅ `curl -s &quot;https://ghcr.io/v2/openabdev/charts/openab/tags/list&quot;`\n✅ `grep -r &quot;pattern&quot; src/`\n🔧 `npm install`...\n\nAgent response text here...\n</code></pre>\n<p>Best for: debugging, understanding what the agent is doing step by step.</p>\n<h3><code>compact</code></h3>\n<p>Shows a single-line count summary. No tool names, commands, or arguments are displayed.</p>\n<pre><code>✅ 3 · 🔧 1 tool(s)\n\nAgent response text here...\n</code></pre>\n<p>Best for: everyday use, public channels, mobile.</p>\n<h3><code>none</code></h3>\n<p>Hides tool lines entirely. Only the final agent response is shown. Reaction emojis (🔧→✅) still work, so you can tell the agent is busy.</p>\n<pre><code>Agent response text here...\n</code></pre>\n<p>Best for: clean output when you only care about the final answer.</p>\n<h2>Icons</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Icon</th>\n<th>Meaning</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>🔧</td>\n<td>Tool is running</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>✅</td>\n<td>Tool completed successfully</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>❌</td>\n<td>Tool failed</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>full</code> shows complete tool titles. Use <code>tool_display = &quot;compact&quot;</code> for a cleaner count-only summary, or <code>&quot;none&quot;</code> to hide tools entirely.</li>\n<li><strong>Reaction emojis are independent</strong>: The emoji reactions on messages (👀→🤔→🔧→🆗) work regardless of <code>tool_display</code> setting.</li>\n<li><strong>Streaming behavior</strong>: In <code>compact</code> mode, the count updates in real-time as tools start and finish. In <code>full</code> mode, individual tool lines appear and update during streaming.</li>\n</ul>\n",

      "slug": "wecom",
      "html": "<h1>WeCom (企业微信) Setup</h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Unified Mode (v0.9.0+):</strong> The OAB binary now embeds the wecom adapter directly. Set <code>WECOM_CORP_ID</code> as an env var — no separate gateway container or <code>[gateway]</code> config needed. See <a href=\"/openab/telegram#unified-mode-recommended\">Telegram docs</a> for the pattern.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Unified Config (Kiro + wecom)</h3>\n<p><strong>Minimal:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Recommended:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[agent]\nenv = { KIRO_API_KEY = &quot;${KIRO_API_KEY}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 3\nsession_ttl_hours = 1\n\n[reactions]\ntool_display = &quot;compact&quot;\n\n[markdown]\ntables = &quot;off&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Set <code>WECOM_CORP_ID</code> (and related platform env vars) on the container. No <code>[gateway]</code> needed.</p>\n<p>Connect a WeCom (Enterprise WeChat) bot to OpenAB via the Custom Gateway.</p>\n<pre><code>WeCom ──POST──▶ Gateway (:8080) ◀──WebSocket── OAB Pod\n                                   (OAB connects out)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>A running OAB instance (with any ACP agent authenticated)</li>\n<li>The Custom Gateway deployed (<a href=\"../gateway/README.md\">gateway/README.md</a>)</li>\n<li>A WeCom enterprise account with admin access</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>1. Create a WeCom App</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Log in to <a href=\"https://work.weixin.qq.com/wework_admin/frame\">WeCom Admin Console</a></li>\n<li>Go to <strong>应用管理</strong> (App Management) → <strong>自建</strong> (Self-built) → <strong>创建应用</strong> (Create App)</li>\n<li>Fill in the app name and description, select visible scope</li>\n<li>After creation, note down:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>AgentId</strong> — on the app detail page</li>\n<li><strong>Secret</strong> — click to view/copy on the app detail page</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Go to <strong>我的企业</strong> (My Enterprise) → copy the <strong>企业ID</strong> (Corp ID)</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>2. Configure the Callback URL</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>In the app detail page, scroll to <strong>接收消息</strong> (Receive Messages)</li>\n<li>Click <strong>设置API接收</strong> (Set API Receive)</li>\n<li>Fill in:\n<ul>\n<li><strong>URL</strong>: <code>https://your-gateway-host/webhook/wecom</code> (must be HTTPS)</li>\n<li><strong>Token</strong>: click &quot;随机获取&quot; (Random Generate) or set your own</li>\n<li><strong>EncodingAESKey</strong>: click &quot;随机获取&quot; (Random Generate) or set your own</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Do NOT click Save yet</strong> — you need the gateway running first to verify the URL</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>3. Configure the Gateway</h2>\n<p>Set the following environment variables:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_CORP_ID</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Enterprise Corp ID (from My Enterprise page)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_AGENT_ID</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>App Agent ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_SECRET</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>App Secret</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_TOKEN</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Callback Token (from step 2)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_ENCODING_AES_KEY</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>Callback EncodingAESKey (43 characters)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_WEBHOOK_PATH</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Webhook path (default: <code>/webhook/wecom</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_STREAMING_ENABLED</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Stream replies via &quot;thinking&quot; placeholder + recall + resend (default: <code>false</code>). WeCom has no edit-message API; enabling this causes a brief client flicker during streaming.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WECOM_DEBOUNCE_SECS</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Quiet-period seconds before flushing buffered streamed text (default: <code>3</code>, minimum: <code>1</code> — <code>0</code> is silently ignored by Helm's truthy check and disables the buffer purpose)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">docker run -d --name openab-gateway \\\n  -e WECOM_CORP_ID=&quot;ww1234567890abcdef&quot; \\\n  -e WECOM_AGENT_ID=&quot;1000002&quot; \\\n  -e WECOM_SECRET=&quot;your-app-secret&quot; \\\n  -e WECOM_TOKEN=&quot;your-callback-token&quot; \\\n  -e WECOM_ENCODING_AES_KEY=&quot;your-43-char-encoding-aes-key&quot; \\\n  -p 8080:8080 \\\n  ghcr.io/openabdev/openab-gateway:latest\n</code></pre>\n<p>For Kubernetes with Helm, see <a href=\"https://github.com/linyiru/openab/blob/6ad4ef419dd131e3f718dfd9b224f3967387da94/charts/openab/values.yaml\"><code>charts/openab/values.yaml</code></a> — set values under <code>agents.&lt;name&gt;.gateway.wecom</code>.</p>\n<h2>4. Verify the Callback URL</h2>\n<p>Once the gateway is running with the correct env vars:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Go back to the WeCom Admin Console → App → 接收消息 → 设置API接收</li>\n<li>Click <strong>保存</strong> (Save)</li>\n<li>WeCom will send a verification request to your URL — if the gateway decrypts and responds correctly, you'll see &quot;保存成功&quot; (Save Successful)</li>\n</ol>\n<p>If verification fails:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Check that the gateway is reachable over HTTPS</li>\n<li>Verify <code>WECOM_TOKEN</code> and <code>WECOM_ENCODING_AES_KEY</code> match exactly what's shown in the WeCom console</li>\n<li>Check gateway logs for errors</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>5. Configure OAB</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[gateway]\nurl = &quot;ws://openab-gateway:8080/ws&quot;\nplatform = &quot;wecom&quot;\nallow_all_channels = true\nallow_all_users = true\n\n[agent]\nenv = { CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN = &quot;${OPENAB_AUTH_TOKEN}&quot; }\n\n[pool]\nmax_sessions = 10\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>WebSocket URL of the gateway</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>platform</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Session key namespace (default: <code>wecom</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_channels</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Allow messages from all channels (default: <code>false</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>allow_all_users</code></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Allow messages from all users (default: <code>false</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>6. Expose the Gateway (HTTPS)</h2>\n<p>WeCom requires a publicly accessible HTTPS URL for callbacks.</p>\n<h3>Option A: Zeabur (one-click HTTPS for quick testing)</h3>\n<p>Deploy the gateway to <a href=\"https://zeabur.com\">Zeabur</a> — HTTPS is automatically provisioned.</p>\n<h3>Option B: Cloudflare Tunnel</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Option C: Reverse proxy (production)</h3>\n<p>Use nginx, Caddy, or a cloud load balancer with TLS termination pointing to the gateway's <code>:8080</code>.</p>\n<h2>7. Set Trusted IP (Optional)</h2>\n<p>For production, restrict the callback to WeCom's IP ranges:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>In the WeCom Admin Console → App → <strong>企业可信IP</strong> (Trusted IP)</li>\n<li>Add your gateway's public IP</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Usage</h2>\n<p>Send a direct message to the bot in the WeCom mobile or desktop app:</p>\n<pre><code>你好，帮我解释一下这段代码\n</code></pre>\n<p>The bot will reply directly in the same conversation.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note on group chats:</strong> WeCom self-built enterprise apps only deliver <strong>1:1 direct messages</strong> to the callback URL. Group chat messages are not forwarded by this API path; group chat support would require the <code>appchat</code> API (not yet implemented). For group chat use cases, see the WeCom AI Bot WebSocket API as a future adapter.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Features</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Feature</th>\n<th>Status</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Direct message (1:1)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Text message receive/reply</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>AES-256-CBC message decryption</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Message deduplication</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Auto-split long replies (2048 bytes)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Access token auto-refresh</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Image receive</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Text file receive</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Streaming replies (thinking placeholder + debounce flush)</td>\n<td>✅</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Group chat</td>\n<td>❌ Not supported (callback API limitation)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Voice/video messages</td>\n<td>Planned</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Markdown card replies</td>\n<td>Planned</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Production Hardening</h2>\n<p>The gateway does no application-level rate limiting on <code>/webhook/wecom</code>. Each request triggers an XML envelope parse, a SHA1 signature computation, and (if signature passes) AES-256-CBC decryption. A 5-minute timestamp freshness check rejects stale callbacks before any crypto runs, so old replays are cheap to drop, but fresh-but-invalid requests still consume CPU.</p>\n<p>Run the gateway behind a reverse proxy or load balancer that enforces rate limits at the IP / connection level:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Layer</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Edge / CDN</td>\n<td>Cloudflare WAF rate limiting rules on <code>/webhook/wecom</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Cloud LB</td>\n<td>AWS ALB rate-based rules, GCP Cloud Armor</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Reverse proxy</td>\n<td>nginx <code>limit_req_zone</code>, Caddy <code>rate_limit</code> directive</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>In addition, restrict the callback URL to WeCom's published IP ranges via the <strong>企业可信IP</strong> (Trusted IP) list in the WeCom Admin Console. This is the most effective control because all legitimate callbacks originate from those ranges.</p>\n<h3>Redact <code>corpsecret</code> from access logs</h3>\n<p>WeCom's <code>gettoken</code> API mandates <code>corpsecret</code> as a query parameter (the protocol does not support a header alternative). The gateway itself does not log this URL, but if the gateway sits behind a reverse proxy with default access logging enabled, the secret will appear in access logs. Configure the proxy to redact query strings on <code>/cgi-bin/gettoken</code> outbound calls (or sanitize at log-shipping time).</p>\n<h3>Known limitations</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Streaming task lifetime on shutdown</strong> — the optional streaming mode (<code>WECOM_STREAMING_ENABLED=true</code>) spawns one debounce task per in-flight reply. On SIGTERM these tasks are dropped by the tokio runtime; any text buffered but not yet flushed is lost. The agent will typically re-emit on the next interaction. If you need flush-on-shutdown semantics, keep streaming off (default) so each reply is sent synchronously.</li>\n<li><strong>DedupeCache eviction is lazy</strong> — entries are TTL-checked on lookup and bulk-evicted only when the cache reaches <code>DEDUPE_MAX_SIZE</code> (10K). For low-traffic deployments the HashMap can sit just below the cap with stale entries; max memory is bounded (~500 KB) and the dedup window itself is honored, so this does not affect correctness.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Symptom</th>\n<th>Cause</th>\n<th>Fix</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Callback verification fails</td>\n<td>Token/EncodingAESKey mismatch</td>\n<td>Double-check values match WeCom console exactly</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Bot receives but doesn't reply</td>\n<td>Agent auth token not configured</td>\n<td>Set <code>env = { CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN = &quot;${OPENAB_AUTH_TOKEN}&quot; }</code> in OAB config</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Intermittent &quot;no response&quot;</td>\n<td>WeCom disabled callback after errors</td>\n<td>Re-save callback config in WeCom console to re-verify</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>&quot;IP not in whitelist&quot; on reply</td>\n<td>Trusted IP not set</td>\n<td>Add gateway IP to app's trusted IP list, or leave it empty for dev</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",

        "title": "WeCom (企业微信) Setup"
      }

      "slug": "workspaces",
      "html": "<h1>Workspaces</h1>\n<h2>Overview</h2>\n<p>A single OAB bot instance can serve multiple projects. Workspaces let users switch project context at session start using the <code>[[ws:...]]</code> <a href=\"/openab/control-directives\">control directive</a>.</p>\n<p>When a workspace is set, the agent:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Uses the workspace path as its working directory</li>\n<li>Loads steering rules from <code>AGENTS.md</code> and <code>.kiro/steering/</code></li>\n<li>Activates skills from <code>.kiro/skills/</code></li>\n<li>Has correct git context (branch, remote, history)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Configuration</h2>\n<p>Define workspace aliases in <code>config.toml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-toml\">[workspace.aliases]\nopenab = &quot;~/projects/openab&quot;\ninfra  = &quot;~/projects/infra-cdk&quot;\nweb    = &quot;~/projects/frontend&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p>Paths starting with <code>~</code> expand to the bot's home directory (<code>$HOME</code>).</p>\n<h2>Usage</h2>\n<p>Reference aliases with <code>@</code> prefix in the first message:</p>\n<pre><code>@Bot [[ws:@openab]] help me debug the smoke tests\n</code></pre>\n<p>Or use raw paths:</p>\n<pre><code>@Bot [[ws:~/projects/myapp]] investigate the build failure\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Security Boundary</h2>\n<p>All workspace paths are validated before use:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Must be absolute</strong> — relative paths (e.g., <code>../secrets</code>) are rejected</li>\n<li><strong><code>~</code> expands to bot home</strong> — not the requesting user's home</li>\n<li><strong>Canonicalized</strong> — symlinks, <code>..</code>, <code>.</code> are resolved</li>\n<li><strong>Must be within bot home subtree</strong> — paths outside are rejected</li>\n<li><strong>Must be a directory</strong> — file paths are rejected</li>\n<li><strong>Must exist</strong> — non-existent paths are rejected with a clear error showing the expanded path</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Session Behavior</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Workspace is set <strong>once</strong> at session creation and is immutable</li>\n<li>The workspace persists across session suspend/resume and eviction rebuilds</li>\n<li>To change workspace, start a new session</li>\n<li>If workspace resolution fails, no session is created (clean failure)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Error Messages</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Error</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Unknown alias</td>\n<td><code>Unknown workspace alias @foo. Available: openab, infra, web</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Relative path</td>\n<td><code>Workspace path must be absolute (start with ~ or /): relative/path</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Outside home</td>\n<td><code>Workspace path is outside allowed directory: /etc/passwd</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Not a directory</td>\n<td><code>Workspace path is not a directory: /home/bot/Cargo.toml</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Does not exist</td>\n<td><code>Workspace path does not exist: ~/nope (expanded to /home/bot/nope)</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>See Also</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/control-directives\">Control Directives</a> — full directive syntax and rules</li>\n<li><a href=\"/openab/config-reference#workspace\">Config Reference</a> — <code>[workspace.aliases]</code> configuration</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Workspaces"
      }
    },

      "slug": "xai-proxy",
      "html": "<h1>xAI / SuperGrok Integration</h1>\n<h2>Recommended: Native xAI OAuth (OpenCode ≥1.15.0)</h2>\n<p>OpenCode now has <strong>built-in xAI OAuth support</strong> — no sidecar proxy needed.</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Run <code>/connect</code> inside OpenCode → select <strong>xAI Grok OAuth (Headless / Remote / VPS)</strong></li>\n<li>Approve the device-code on any browser</li>\n<li>Select your model with <code>/models</code> (e.g. <code>grok-4.3</code>)</li>\n</ol>\n<p>OpenCode handles token storage and auto-refresh internally.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Alternative: openab-auth-proxy sidecar</h2>\n<p>For agents <strong>without</strong> native xAI OAuth (Hermes, custom agents), use\n<code>openab-auth-proxy</code> — a generic OAuth sidecar that defaults to xAI.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Login (one-time)\nopenab-auth-proxy login-device\n\n# Start proxy\nopenab-auth-proxy serve --port 9090\n\n# Point any OpenAI-compatible client at the proxy\nexport OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9090/v1\nexport OPENAI_API_KEY=dummy\n</code></pre>\n<p>See <a href=\"/openab/refarch/sidecar-proxy\">docs/refarch/sidecar-proxy.md</a> for the full\narchitecture, Helm deployment, and custom provider configuration.</p>\n<h2>Comparison</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th></th>\n<th>Native OAuth</th>\n<th>openab-auth-proxy sidecar</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Requires</strong></td>\n<td>OpenCode ≥1.15.0</td>\n<td>Any OpenAI-compatible agent</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Extra container</strong></td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Token management</strong></td>\n<td>Built into OpenCode</td>\n<td>Proxy handles refresh</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Multi-agent sharing</strong></td>\n<td>Each agent needs own auth</td>\n<td>Single proxy serves all</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Custom providers</strong></td>\n<td>xAI only</td>\n<td>Any OIDC provider via TOML config</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "xAI proxy"
      }
    }
  ]
}
